# AUDIT ROUND 7 — THE DESIGN AUDIT

**777 findings** (204 critical, 387 high, 114 medium, 0 low losses, plus 72 design wins) — grand total across rounds 1–7: **2702**.

Scope: design only — UI, UX, motion, sound, haptics, copy, brand, and the philosophy the design embodies. The comparison universe was unrestricted: Teenage Engineering, Braun/Rams, Grand Seiko, Nomos, Leica, Aicher, Vignelli, Müller-Brockmann, Kinneir/Calvert, Elektron, Moog, Tufte, Playdate, Aesop, Vitsoe, Tokyo transit, the Eames standard, and philosophies of attention and time (Seneca, Weil, van Gennep, Turner, Heidegger, Stiegler, Han, Pieper, Csikszentmihalyi, Alexander, Pirsig, kintsugi, wabi-sabi, Ma, Zen, Illich, McLuhan, Simon, Crawford, Williams, Bogost, Munari, Mari, Deterding) — judged against Monolith's actual screens, rendered faithfully from the Compose source before judging (design-renders/deck.html, shield.html, drawer.html, park.html, airlock.html, receipt.html). Wins are included, in their own section at the end — the design decisions worth protecting in any redesign. Store-presence and monetisation findings are excluded (the app is unpublished; that class is banned). Every finding is new against all 1,925 findings of rounds 1–6 and deduplicated within this round.

---

### Visual identity and brand — 36 findings (10 critical, 18 high, 8 medium, 0 low)

#### [CRITICAL] Launcher sells a Bauhaus triad the product abolished — two palettes, two brands, one name

ic_launcher_foreground.xml draws a Bauhaus triad that exists nowhere else in the product: ultramarine ring #1E40FF, canary sector #F5B800, crimson hub #E6332A on paper #FCF9F2. The app itself runs on one accent only — Color.kt:10,18 defines the system as warm stone #E4DFDA plus 'THE single accent' #F55314 hot orange, and grep finds #1E40FF/#F5B800/#E6332A in no Kotlin file and no other values file. Worse, values/colors.xml:28-30 keeps the Bauhaus names as lies: bauhaus_crimson and bauhaus_canary both resolve to #F55314, and bauhaus_ultramarine resolves to grey #FF615B5A. So the launcher promises a primary-colour instrument; the first screen delivers a warm monochrome appliance. Two brands share one name. Seen in deck.html: the Deck's ground and accent share no hue with the icon the user tapped.

Recommendation: Pick one identity and redraw the other side to match. Keep the in-app system (it is the lived product): redraw ic_launcher_foreground.xml in the real tokens — paper #FAF6F0 dial plate, ink #252323 ring and gnomon, single #F55314 sector for the committed quadrant — and delete or honestly revalue the bauhaus_* aliases in colors.xml. Follow Nothing OS, which carries one red accent and one dot-matrix mark unchanged from launcher icon through UI to packaging, so the icon is a truthful sample of the product, not a poster for a different one.

#### [CRITICAL] Monolith has two different app icons: recognition forks by Android version

Two unrelated marks ship in the same APK. Legacy densities (mipmap-xxxhdpi/ic_launcher.png, served to API 24-25 since app/build.gradle.kts:17 sets minSdk 24) are a near-black slab (dominant pixel 13,14,18) with a cream octagonal frame and a single orange-red (#FF4F18) power ring. The adaptive icon used on API 26+ (mipmap-anydpi-v26/ic_launcher.xml:3-4) points to drawable/ic_launcher_foreground.xml:7-22: an ultramarine #1E40FF ring, paper dial #FCF9F2, canary #F5B800 quarter-sector and crimson #E6332A hub on the cream field of drawable/ic_launcher_background.xml:8-13. No shared geometry, no shared silhouette, inverted value story (dark tile vs light tile). ic_launcher_round.xml reuses the same adaptive pair, so even the round shelf shows the sundial, never the slab.

Recommendation: Kill one mark and ship a single identity through every density and API level. Promote the legacy slab/power-ring: redraw it as the adaptive foreground/background pair (ink field, cream frame, orange ring), regenerate every mipmap PNG from that same vector source, and delete the Bauhaus sundial from the launcher entirely. One source file, one mark, every shelf - the way Forest and Opal each ship exactly one recognisable glyph across all densities.

#### [CRITICAL] Exam season has no visual register: the app owns exactly two looks (day studio, session night) and the Deck in exam week is pixel-identical to the Deck in week one

ui/theme/Color.kt:10-18 defines exactly one light identity (Warm Stone #E4DFDA ground, #FAF6F0 raised, single accent #F55314) and Color.kt:32-39 one night identity; ui/theme/Theme.kt:42 holds only those two schemes. design-renders/deck.html shows the result: the Deck a student sees in the first week of term — warm beige ground, orange slide cap, 'GUARD 4/4' header — is pixel-identical to the Deck on the night before their final exam. Shield's only loadouts are STUDY/WORK/SLEEP (ui/components/ShieldCapSelector.kt:62); nothing anywhere in the UI re-dresses for the highest-stakes weeks of the user's year.

Recommendation: Add a third, date-bounded 'season' scheme modelled on the OCR/Edexcel exam-paper cover: answer-booklet white ground, invigilation-blue ink replacing the orange accent everywhere except the slide cap, and the header band re-ruled as a candidate strip (SUBJECT · PAPER · D−n in the existing mono). The season scheme should be a token swap through the existing scheme plumbing — same layout, same type — so the app visibly changes uniform the way a paper changes dress, then reverts the morning after the last paper.

#### [CRITICAL] Six incompatible metaphor families share one app — there is no world, only a word-hoard

The rail alone prints four nouns from four different worlds — WORDS = listOf("DECK", "SHIELD", "TASKS", "LEDGER") (ui/views/MonolithRailView.kt:34) — and the rest of the app keeps adding families: industrial machine ("MONOLITH ML-01", "UNIT Nº 01 · BUILT FOR ONE USER · NOT FOR SALE", spec plate at ui/components/ParkDrawer.kt:105-124), spacecraft (AirlockInterceptOverlay, ui/components/AirlockAndDisarmOverlays.kt, render airlock.html), smithy ("FORGED — IT STANDS IN THE CABINET", ui/screens/DrawerScreen.kt:486), architecture ("STREAK TOWER • 7 BRICKS / FLOOR", ui/views/BlockitTowerFadersAndCatalogViews.kt:60), furniture (Drawer/CABINET/STORED, DrawerScreen.kt:224,348), gaming ("LOADOUT", ui/screens/ShieldMatrixScreen.kt:82). Monument, ship, shield, drawer, airlock, forge, tower and loadout never imply each other; nothing a user learns in one room transfers to the next. Forest — Monolith's most successful rival — runs its entire product on ONE metaphor: a seed grows into a tree while you focus and dies if you leave; home, reward, failure and history are all the same plant, so the vocabulary tax is zero. Monolith charges full price at every door.

Recommendation: Elect one governing world and evict the rest. The machine/instrument world is the only candidate that already owns the core interactions (wheel, slide, sled switches, spec plate, ML-01), so make it constitutional: every surface must be nameable as part of, or output of, the ML-01. Concretely: AIRLOCK becomes INTERCEPT (a machine state, not a spaceship room); FORGE/CABINET/TOY die and curios become numbered PLATES or STAMPS in the machine's log; TOWER/BRICKS become the WALL the code already believes in (data/WallAccrual.kt:53); LOADOUT becomes PRESET. Any noun that cannot be drawn as a part of the machine or a slip it prints gets a plain functional name instead — the way Braun under Rams gave controls their function names and let the object itself carry the identity.

#### [CRITICAL] 2030 has nothing to recognise: the only mark is a borrowed Bauhaus dial in off-brand colours, and the name is typeset, never drawn

res/drawable/ic_launcher_foreground.xml draws the only brand mark as a Bauhaus sundial — ring #1E40FF, sector #F5B800, gnomon #E6332A — three hues that appear nowhere in ui/theme/Color.kt:8-19, whose constitution is warm stone plus the single accent #F55314. In-app, the 'logo' is not drawn at all: deck.html and MainActivity.kt's header band set the word MONOLITH as Anonymous Pro Bold 10sp tracked 2sp — body telemetry type, not a wordmark. No glyph, slab silhouette or detent-mark asset exists in res/drawable beyond this icon. Nothing owns NDot dot-matrix letterforms and the Glyph light pattern — marks recognisable cropped, at 16px, or with the name removed; TE's OP-1 silhouette is identifiable from its encoder row alone.

Recommendation: Design the mark from the product's own geometry, not Bauhaus clip-art: a vertical slab whose face is the rotary wheel's reader dot at the 50-minute detent, drawn on the token grid in TokenColorPrimary with the single #F55314 dot — one shape that survives as launcher icon, notification small-icon, receipt masthead stamp and an engraved badge. Retire the blue/yellow/red dial entirely, redraw MONOLITH as a fixed wordmark lockup (letterspaced Sora Bold, never re-typeset per screen), and ship both as versioned vector assets in the repo.

#### [CRITICAL] The anti-Material identity is inherited, not designed: every control is a Canvas View built on a base class still named after the rival it clones

The entire interactive surface — rotary wheel, slide-to-arm, sled switches, rail, emergency valve — is 3,824 lines of imperative android.graphics.Canvas Views under app/src/main/java/com/example/ui/views/, all extending `abstract class BlockitCanvasView` (BlockitCoreViews.kt:60), bridged into Compose via AndroidView (TactileDeckScreen.kt:683, ShieldMatrixScreen.kt:1066, MainActivity.kt rail). A whole-tree import census of material3 returns only MaterialTheme, Text, HorizontalDivider and Scaffold: zero Button, Switch, Slider, NavigationBar or any other Material component exists in the app. Nothing OS — the canonical designed rebellion — does the opposite: it keeps near-stock Android structure and navigation logic and layers identity on top via NDot typography, a monochrome icon pack and 19 custom widgets, so its difference is a deliberate skin over a living platform. Monolith replaced the plumbing and kept nothing: its 'rebellion' is the architecture of the Blockit clone it was modelled on, file names included, never re-decided as a position.

Recommendation: Decide the position explicitly and rebuild to it, Nothing-style: keep Monolith's visuals but re-found them on the platform. Migrate the three highest-frequency controls (sled switch, rail, cap selector) to real Compose components using Material3 interaction/state APIs skinned with Monolith tokens, reserving Canvas only for the wheel and tower art where drawing is the point. Rename the view layer (BlockitCanvasView, BlockitCoreViews.kt) to Monolith names as part of the same pass — an identity that still carries the rival's name in its base class is not an identity yet.

#### [CRITICAL] Two unrelated front doors: adaptive sundial on modern phones, orange power-button mark on legacy fallback

AndroidManifest.xml:33-35 routes the icon to @mipmap/ic_launcher / ic_launcher_round. On API 26+ that resolves to the adaptive vector: ic_launcher_foreground.xml:9-25 draws an ultramarine #1E40FF ring, paper #FCF9F2 dial, canary #F5B800 sector and crimson #E6332A hub on a cream ground (ic_launcher_background.xml:9-14). The legacy PNGs in res/mipmap-xxxhdpi/ic_launcher.png and ic_launcher_round.png are a completely different drawing: pixel census shows a dominant near-black (13,14,18) field, a cream octagonal frame and a single orange (255,79,24) power-button glyph — no ring, no dial, no Bauhaus primaries at all. minSdk is 24 (app/build.gradle.kts:17), so API 24-25 devices and any launcher falling back to the raster set get the power mark while modern devices get the sundial: the same installed app presents two unrelated identities depending on the phone.

Recommendation: Pick one mark and generate every density and layer from that single source. The buried legacy mark is the right survivor: it is already on-token (near-black field ≈ TokenColorPrimary #252323, orange ≈ the single accent #F55314, cream frame ≈ #FAF6F0) and reads at 48dp where the sundial does not. Redraw the octagon-and-power glyph as the adaptive foreground vector on a near-black background layer, regenerate all legacy PNGs from that vector, and delete the Bauhaus sundial layers entirely — one drawing, every API level, like Nothing OS and Spotify ship one mark across every density and mask.

#### [CRITICAL] The launcher sells a Bauhaus primary-colour brand that the app inside has already deleted

res/drawable/ic_launcher_foreground.xml:9,17,21 builds the mark from ultramarine #1E40FF, canary #F5B800 and crimson #E6332A; none of those hues exists in the product — ui/theme/Color.kt:11-19 defines warm stone #E4DFDA, ink #252323 and a single accent #F55314. Worse, Color.kt:160-162 keeps the Bauhaus names as aliases that lie: BauhausRed and BauhausYellow both resolve to the orange accent, BauhausBlue to grey — the primary system survives only as erased labels. deck.html confirms the in-app world is entirely stone/ink/orange. Nothing runs the opposite discipline: one bespoke NDot logotype, black/white only, and a single red dot that recurs identically on hardware, OS and packaging; Opal's brand kit likewise locks wordmark and crest as-provided, never recoloured, on a pure black/white base.

Recommendation: Pick the in-app brand and kill the other one. Redraw the launcher foreground in the app's own tokens: an ink slab/wheel segment #252323 on porcelain #FAF6F0 with exactly one #F55314 commit sector — the same orange sector language as the slide cap. Delete or honestly rename the Bauhaus aliases in Color.kt so no token claims a palette the product does not use.

#### [CRITICAL] The launcher mark is a sundial for an app named Monolith: the symbol depicts time passing, not the slab that shuts

res/drawable/ic_launcher_foreground.xml:7-25 draws a Bauhaus clock face — ultramarine ring, paper dial plate, canary quarter sector, crimson hub and a black gnomon bar (pathData M52,29 L56,29 L56,54 L52,54 Z). Nothing in the five paths is a slab, a block or a shut surface. Bass's test (The Man with the Golden Arm's single jagged arm) is that the symbol must be the product's one act; Monolith's one act is sealing a phone shut, yet its only symbol is an instrument for watching time pass — the metaphor of every timer rival, and the opposite of the name over the door (res/values/strings.xml:2, app_name 'Monolith').

Recommendation: Kill the dial. Draw the mark as the product's act: one solid ink slab in portrait proportion with a single horizontal seam cut through it — the shut phone, the laid brick, the sealed slot in one gesture. One path, drawn once as a vector, used at launcher size and struck at the seal; the sundial's five parts do not survive into it.

#### [CRITICAL] No reducible core: the mark is six paths in five colours with no one-colour, small-size version anywhere in the project

ic_launcher_foreground.xml stacks six paths in #1E40FF, #FCF9F2, #F5B800, #E6332A and #141318; the identifying details are a gnomon 4 units wide and a hub of radius 10 inside a 108-unit viewport, so at a 48px launcher render the gnomon is under 2px and hub, sector and ring collapse into one coloured disc. res/ contains no monochrome or single-path variant of the mark — the only other use, MonolithShieldService.kt:224, reuses the full-colour foreground as the notification small icon, a slot Android renders as a silhouette the artwork was never drawn for. Rand's IBM stripes are the counter-proof: a mark reduced until it survives one-colour reproduction at any size.

Recommendation: Impose the reduction test as a build artefact: ship the mark as a single path in a single ink, verified legible at 16dp in pure black and pure white, and add that same path as a dedicated monochrome drawable for the notification small icon. Any element of the current dial that cannot survive the 16dp/1-bit render — hub, sector, gnomon — is deleted, not shrunk.

#### [HIGH] No logotype, three competing signatures — and the keepsake receipt signs nothing

Three surfaces, three different name treatments, none a designed lockup. Deck header: 'MONOLITH' set live as a Text in Anonymous Pro Bold 10sp, letterSpacing 2sp (MonolithCustomComponents.kt:269-277) — body-text machinery, not a logotype. Park spec plate: a different lockup entirely, 'MONOLITH ML-01' with 'UNIT Nº 01 · BUILT FOR ONE USER · NOT FOR SALE' (ParkDrawer.kt:106-107), introducing an ML-01 model-number sub-brand that appears on no icon, no header and no other screen. Receipt — the one surface designed to be kept and shown — has no wordmark at all: ReceiptSheet.kt:91-110 heads the slip with the session's own title and receipt number, so the artifact a user photographs carries no brand lockup. Seen in deck.html, park.html and receipt.html: the same product signs itself three ways, and on its keepsake not at all.

Recommendation: Commission the wordmark once, as a vector asset, and legislate its three uses: (1) one drawn MONOLITH logotype (fixed letterforms, not a Text style) at header size on Deck; (2) keep ML-01 only if it becomes a real system — model number on the icon's reverse surfaces, the spec plate and the receipt footer, the way Teenage Engineering prints TP-7 / OP-1 model designations identically on hardware, packaging and UI; otherwise strike ML-01 from ParkDrawer.kt. (3) Stamp the logotype plus the dial glyph as the receipt's letterhead at 15-18sp equivalent, following Paul Rand's IBM programme: one mark, specified sizes, no local improvisations.

#### [HIGH] Shelf camouflage: the primary-colour segmented disc sorts Monolith into the Google-utility cluster

The adaptive foreground (drawable/ic_launcher_foreground.xml:7-22) is a white-ground disc built from saturated primary segments: blue ring #1E40FF, yellow wedge #F5B800, red centre #E6332A, thin black needle. That is the visual grammar of Google's own utility icons - Chrome's segmented disc and the Photos pinwheel use the same white field + primary-colour segmented circle construction. Parked in a real home-screen grid next to Chrome, Clock and Photos, the eye files Monolith as another pre-installed system utility and slides past it; it wins no attention from the colourful neighbours and borrows none of the focus category's codes (no dark, calm or vegetal signal).

Recommendation: Leave the primary-disc grammar to Google. Rebuild the mark in Monolith's own shelf language - flat ink field, one paper/orange glyph, zero blue and zero yellow - so its nearest neighbours read as 'other people's apps' and Monolith reads as the dark, quiet object in the grid, the same shelf contrast Nothing OS exploits with its monochrome dot-matrix icons against Android's colourful defaults.

#### [HIGH] The one borrowed metaphor with a real emotional logic — packing a Suitcase for a journey — was renamed into a shooter term and stranded

The views still ship under their original names — ui/views/BlockitSuitcaseAndSwitchesViews.kt and BlockitTowerFadersAndCatalogViews.kt — but on screen the Suitcase became a 'LOADOUT': ShieldCapSelector is documented as 'discrete 3-position Loadout selection (STUDY / WORK / SLEEP)' (ui/screens/ShieldMatrixScreen.kt:82) and the default set is literally named 'Study Loadout' (ShieldMatrixScreen.kt:94, render shield.html). The original metaphor was a small story: you pack a bag of apps, you go somewhere, a parachute is how you bail out — packing explains why the set is chosen before departure and why leaving early needs special equipment. 'Loadout' keeps none of that logic and imports a different one: it is the word shooters use for weapon configuration, so on the same screen as SHIELD it reframes a study session as combat prep, and it clashes with the ML-01 instrument language everywhere else. Teenage Engineering's PO/OP naming shows the alternative discipline: even their playful names (PO-12 'rhythm', OP-1) stay inside one product-family grammar, so a new name still tells you which world you are in.

Recommendation: Either restore the journey or finish the machine conversion — do not leave a gaming noun floating on an instrument. Cheaper and truer to the ML-01 world: rename loadouts to PRESET 01/02/03 with the user's own label underneath ('PRESET 01 — STUDY'), matching the spec plate's 'UNIT Nº 01' numbering (ParkDrawer.kt:107). If the packing story is preferred, it must be restored whole — pack/unpack verbs, named bags, the emergency exit renamed back into the same trip — because a metaphor that survives in only one noun is not a metaphor, it is trivia the user must memorise.

#### [HIGH] The one manifesto in the app refuses nothing: the Park spec plate is operating instructions in manifesto type

ParkDrawer.kt:105-124, PLATE_HEAD/PLATE_BODY — the app's only manifesto-shaped text. Of its ten lines, eight are operating instructions or trivia: 'WHEEL SETS TIME · SLIDE ARMS · THE HOLD BREAKS', 'PEEK: 2 MINUTES, THEN SHUT AGAIN', 'COLOUR IS A VERB: …', 'SOUND: FLOAT-PCM, 4 PARTIALS · POWER: YOUR PHONE'. The two lines that gesture at a stance refuse nothing behavioural: 'BUILT FOR ONE USER · NOT FOR SALE' is a commercial fact nobody was asking about, and 'DATA: ON THIS PHONE ONLY' plus 'STUDY HOURS: IN YPT' are jurisdictions — one of them actually outsources a job to another app rather than refusing it. park.html shows it typeset as a hardware spec plate (Anonymous Pro 10sp, foot of the Guard sheet). Nothing in it declines a feed, a score, a social layer, a collectible, or an always-on mode — categories the app in fact ships or neighbours sell. Light's published position names the refused things themselves: social networking services, traditional web browsing, ad-driven content platforms — 'never' attached to behaviours.

Recommendation: Rewrite the plate's body as a never-list of at most five lines, each naming a refused behaviour or category in the plate's own terse register — e.g. 'NEVER A FEED', 'NEVER A SCORE', 'NEVER A SECOND USER LOOKING OVER THE FIRST', 'NEVER A REASON TO OPEN THIS APP BETWEEN SESSIONS' — and delete the mechanism trivia (wheel/hold/peek timings already print on the screens that perform them). Keep the ML-01 head line and the 10sp spec-plate setting; change only what the plate claims. A manifesto that lists only how the machine works is a manual; following Light, it must list what the machine will not do.

#### [HIGH] The complete vocabulary is carceral: the user is an inmate on a register, the app is the guard, the valve and the court

RoutineDerive.kt:53 defines the day's judgement enum as ATTENDED / PARTIAL / MISSED / HELD / LATE_FIRE / NOT_DELIVERED — school-register and delivery-court language. ReceiptState.kt:30-46 adds ELAPSED_CLEAN, VALVE_BROKE ('the token was spent and the session BROKE'), ENDED_EARLY. GuardLine.kt:39 prints 'GUARD 4/4' in the header of deck.html; MonolithCustomComponents.kt:477 prints apps as 'WILL SHUT' / 'HELD'; receipt.html Frame 3 is literally headed 'DETENTION — the Deck's frozen last frame' in the render's own caption of the heldFinish state. Across all six renders there is no word for making, building, growing or finishing — only for attending, being held, being guarded and breaking.

Recommendation: Recast the whole lexicon from custody to craft, using the metaphor the product name already owns: Forest makes the user a gardener who plants and grows, Monolith should make them a builder who lays stone. Rename the system, not just words: MISSED → 'NOT LAID', PARTIAL → 'LAID IN PART', ATTENDED → 'LAID', VALVE_BROKE → 'STEPPED AWAY', GUARD 4/4 → 'TOOLS READY 4/4', 'WILL SHUT' → 'WILL CLOSE'. Ship it as a single string-table pass over RoutineDerive.kt, ReceiptState.kt and GuardLine.kt so no screen keeps a prison word the others dropped.

#### [HIGH] Owning a curio is illegible at a glance: FORGED is one 10.5sp grey word on an otherwise pixel-identical row

DrawerScreen.kt:390-410 renders every cabinet row identically (serial, name, subtitle in the same type and colour whether owned or not); the only difference for a forged item is a conditional 10.5sp Anonymous Pro 'FORGED' label at the row's right edge. design-renders/drawer.html Frame 2 confirms it visually: Toy 02 and Toy 05 differ from the four unowned rows by that single small word alone — no fill, no colour shift, no opacity change, no mark. KineticArtifact (MonolithModels.kt:492-498) carries no visual state the row could use.

Recommendation: Give ownership a visual state, not a caption, using Monolith's own ghost language from the Deck: render unforged rows as outline/ghost plates (serial and name in onSurfaceVariant at reduced weight, subtitle suppressed) and forged rows in solid ink with the accent reserved for the serial plate. Forest makes living vs withered instantly legible by shape and colour at thumbnail distance, and Opal's gems are saturated 3D objects against muted locked states — Monolith should pass the same squint test: owned and unowned must be distinguishable from across the room, not by reading a 10.5sp word.

#### [HIGH] The screenshot has no frame and no name: bottom-anchored over the Deck, variable-height, and the word MONOLITH never appears on it

The slip is hosted BottomCenter over the live Deck behind a scrim of only 0.12 black, with 12dp padding (ui/components/ReceiptSheet.kt:69-72), so in render receipt.html frame 1 most of the phone screen is empty beige ground and Deck context, and the artefact occupies the bottom third at whatever height its deflection count happens to produce (deflections print one line each, ReceiptSheet.kt:141-146 — a quiet session and a tempted session yield differently-shaped 'artefacts'). Worse, the slip carries no brand: its header is the user's task title and the № (ReceiptSheet.kt:95-110); the word MONOLITH appears nowhere on it, and the only other line is a 9sp footer outsourcing the record to 'YPT'. A user who does screenshot it captures an unattributable, unrepeatable crop. Spotify Wrapped's cards are the reference discipline: every card is a self-contained full-frame vertical composition, brand and personal headline inside the frame, designed aspect-first on the assumption it will be posted within seconds. Monolith designs its one shareable object as an overlay on something else.

Recommendation: Compose the slip as a self-contained frame: at issuance, seat it centred on a solid ground (the Deck fully scrimmed to the night background token, not 0.12), print 'MONOLITH' as the receipt's shop masthead — centred Anonymous Pro tracked caps as the slip's first line, the way real receipts print the store name before the items — and give the slip a fixed minimum height (pad short receipts with blank paper above the perforation, as a printer would) so every receipt screenshot has the same silhouette and proportions. Brand, intention, verdict-stamp and № must all be inside the paper; nothing essential may live on the Deck behind it.

#### [HIGH] The rail mixes two naming systems with no rule — three metaphors and one literal word — so a new user cannot tell which labels to take literally

ui/views/MonolithRailView.kt:34 sets the four stops as WORDS = listOf('DECK', 'SHIELD', 'TASKS', 'LEDGER'), confirmed in design-renders/deck.html ('DECK SHIELD TASKS LEDGER'). DECK, SHIELD and LEDGER are metaphors whose referents must be memorised (home/arm screen, rules screen, history screen); TASKS is simply the thing itself. Nothing in the treatment — same type, same tracking, same cap — signals that one label is literal and the other three are figurative, so the rational new-user strategy (read labels literally) works for exactly one stop in four and actively misleads on DECK (no cards, no presentation) and LEDGER (the screen calls itself STORED: ui/screens/DrawerScreen.kt:224,522).

Recommendation: Adopt a single naming rule for navigation and state it by example, following Teenage Engineering's product panels and Kinneir/Calvert wayfinding, where every label is the literal function or destination: go all-literal — 'START', 'RULES', 'TASKS', 'HISTORY' — which costs the brand nothing it was actually collecting, since TASKS already proves a literal stop sits comfortably in the rail. If any metaphor is kept, it must be the only one and carry a literal subtitle for its first weeks of use.

#### [HIGH] On its own nameplate row the wordmark loses: MONOLITH at 10sp sits beside GUARD 4/4 at 15sp, in the same type as every label

ui/components/MonolithCustomComponents.kt:270 sets the only wordmark in the product — text "MONOLITH", Anonymous Pro Bold 10sp, letterSpacing 2 — while the Guard readout sharing its own 47dp header row is set in the same family and weight at 15sp. deck.html renders exactly this: .brand 10px against .guard 15px. Anonymous Pro Bold tracked uppercase is also the style of BLOCK, APPS, TIME and every other field label, so the name is typographically indistinguishable from a data caption and literally smaller than a status count. Nothing's logotype is a bespoke dot-matrix face (NDot 55) governed by explicit rules — never another typeface, never another weight, black/white only; Opal pairs wordmark and crest at matched optical height.

Recommendation: Design an actual lockup and reserve it: a slab glyph plus MONOLITH set in Sora 700 at 16-18sp (or custom-cut letterforms), used nowhere else in the UI, with the Guard line demoted to the 10sp label scale the wordmark currently occupies. The name must be the largest, most distinct object in its own header band, not the smallest.

#### [HIGH] The desk clock — the app's longest-lived, most public face — is completely anonymous

ui/components/AirlockAndDisarmOverlays.kt:154 — the desk clock's only text besides the time is the eyebrow "NIGHTSTAND DESK CLOCK • TAP ANYWHERE TO EXIT", which names a piece of furniture, not a maker; :166 sets the 96sp time in Anonymous Pro in cream NightColorPrimary. receipt.html Frame 4 confirms the full face: no wordmark, no glyph, no orange commit colour anywhere. This is the surface displayed longest and seen from furthest away — across a bedroom, by other people — and it could be any timer app ever shipped. Nothing keeps identity at exactly this scale: its clock faces and widgets keep NDot numerals and the red dot, so the time itself is recognisably Nothing's at a glance.

Recommendation: Brand the clock face without breaking its OLED discipline: print the MONOLITH lockup small at the top of the column in the same cream at 60% alpha, and make the progress bar's leading edge the single orange commit dot. Keep true black and the burn-in drift — add only the maker's mark the face currently lacks.

#### [HIGH] The signature form language is inherited, not authored: wheel, slide, sled and tower still carry another product's name in the source

Every surface Monolith is recognised by belongs to another product's form language, and the debt is still on the nameplates: the wheel and slide live in ui/views/BlockitCoreViews.kt (RotaryWheelView:371, SlideToStartView:1444), the sled and valve in ui/views/BlockitSuitcaseAndSwitchesViews.kt:32/532, the tower in ui/views/BlockitTowerFadersAndCatalogViews.kt, and the shared chip is BlockitActionChip in ui/components/MonolithCustomComponents.kt. Rams' first principle is that innovation develops in tandem with technology and can never be an end in itself — imitation is its opposite: a wheel transplanted from a hardware-era blocker onto glass, where the technology offers direct entry, is nostalgia executed as engineering. The app is called Monolith, a name claiming a form of its own, but no control in it was drawn from its own one original idea — the sealed, numbered receipt.

Recommendation: Author one form from the receipt and let it replace the most borrowed one: retire the rotary wheel and set duration on a ruled slip — a vertical column of printed duration lines (5/10/15/25/50/90) on the Deck card, the chosen line struck through in the single accent like a cashier marking a bill, so setting time already rehearses the session's paper record. Rename the surviving views for what they do (CommitSlideView, SledSwitchView may stay as plain description) and remove every 'Blockit' identifier from shipped class and file names, so the product's own inventory no longer credits another maker for its face.

#### [HIGH] Distortion is kept as a signature: knurl teeth 17 and 83 are hand-set 'visibly wrong' and the hero number is printed three times

BlockitCoreViews.kt:553-557: toothFlare is 'from a fixed seed - 0.84..1.16, teeth 17 and 83 hand-set low'; :672 'teeth 17 and 83 sit visibly wrong inside the bright zone'; :695 'flare (teeth 17/83 stay broken)'. The Deck render confirms the alternating dark/light knurl teeth around the rim. The hero readout repeats the move in type: TactileDeckScreen.kt:637 'two static ghosts at +-1dp behind the glyph', rendered at :655-675 as the full '1H 50M' printed three times (shadow ghost, catch ghost, glyph). Tanaka's third principle tolerates zero distortion in any reflection or face; Monolith manufactures distortion on purpose and protects it in comments against anyone who would fix it.

Recommendation: Remove the two hand-set defects: set teeth 17 and 83 to the same flare value the cos^3 curve assigns their neighbours so the bright zone is one continuous, distortion-free band, and cut the hero to a single printing of the numeral — if a catch-light is wanted, give the glyph one hard 1dp offset edge in the surfaceBright tone on the lamp side only, never a full second and third ghost of the whole number.

#### [HIGH] The Deck opens and closes with the app advertising and certifying itself — wordmark, GUARD score, BIND and PROOF strips — before and after the user's own content

MonolithCustomComponents.kt:235 documents the header as 'the brand — MONOLITH, Anonymous Pro 700 10sp tracked +2.0' and :270 prints it on the Deck; the deck.html render shows the home surface opening with MONOLITH and GUARD 4/4, and closing its arm strip with 'BIND HELD · THIS VISIT' and 'PROOF: LIVE BIND' above 'SLIDE OR TAP TO START', while the user's actual content — the NOW task line — sits below the 72sp hero numeral in 15sp (TactileDeckScreen.kt:791-800). The first and last things the Deck says are the app certifying itself.

Recommendation: Empty the Deck of self-reference: delete the MONOLITH wordmark and the BIND HELD / PROOF strip from the Deck entirely (machine self-certification belongs in the Park, where machine state is the subject), and promote the NOW task line into the space freed at the top. On the home surface the user's day should be the headline and the app should be the blank frame around it.

#### [HIGH] The one hand-drawable idea the product already owns — a single tower brick — is used only as a progress meter and never promoted to the mark

The app already mints a daily unit with a name and a physical form: the tower brick (ui/views/BlockitTowerFadersAndCatalogViews.kt and BlockitCoreViews.kt draw the stacked tower on the Vault/Deck surfaces), and the drawer's prize is literally 'The Monolith Cube' (data/MonolithModels.kt:846). A brick passes every Bass/Rand test the sundial fails: one rectangle, drawable by a child from memory, one colour, meaningful at favicon size, and it is the product's own noun — a day kept is a brick laid. Yet identity was imported from a Bauhaus dial kit while the brick stays a chart. The brand's drawable idea was in the building the whole time, filed under data visualisation.

Recommendation: Promote the brick: take the tower's own brick proportion and seam offset, isolate one brick as the identity path, and retire the dial to history. The tower then becomes the mark repeated — one brick is the logo, seventy are the user's record — which is the exact relationship Rand built between the IBM stripe unit and the striped letterforms.

#### [HIGH] Monochrome without a pattern language: no dither, hatch or stipple anywhere, so flat tone does all the work a 1-bit screen does with texture

A codebase-wide search of the Canvas views finds zero dither, hatch, stipple or checker pattern code — states are separated only by flat fills and alpha. The tower draws laid bricks as one solid ink and the newest as the single accent (BlockitTowerFadersAndCatalogViews.kt:111-126); the shield render (design-renders/shield.html) shows row after row of identical flat surfaceVariant; the wheel fakes its one shade with a painted specular highlight. Playdate's 1-bit screen has no grey at all, so its designers made pattern do the work of tone — dither density is its shading language, instantly legible and printable. Monolith, running on a full-colour display, renders flatter than a 400x240 1-bit device: its monochrome is a palette choice, not an invented visual grammar.

Recommendation: Build a three-pattern state language in the Canvas views and retire the fake specular highlight: coarse dot-grid for PEEK (perforated, temporary), 45° hatch for HELD (detained, cross-lined), solid ink for LOCKED. Apply the identical three patterns on Shield rows, the Airlock badge and the tower's crown brick, so a state can be read from its texture across a room and in a screenshot, the way a Playdate screen reads in pure black and white.

#### [HIGH] Five surfaces, five feelings — instrument, admin matrix, repair board, interrogation room and paperwork share a palette but no single sensation

The renders are five different products sharing only a palette: deck.html is a precision instrument (288px knurled wheel, 72sp Sora hero, proof strip); shield.html is a dense admin matrix (section headers, ADD/REMOVE site rows, loadout caps); park.html is a permission-repair board (GUARD rows, LAST PROVED, FIX queue, sleds); airlock.html is an interrogation card (88sp Anonymous Pro countdown '03', 'AIRLOCK INTERCEPTION'); ReceiptSheet.kt:118-131,176 closes the cycle as paperwork ('ARMED 18:42 - PLANNED 50 MIN', 'HELD 12 APPS - 3 SITES', 'YOUR STUDY RECORD LIVES IN YPT'). No motif from the Deck's seal — the imprint double-rule and lip (MonolithCustomComponents ImprintSlot, deck.html) — recurs on Shield, Park or the Airlock.

Recommendation: Impose the seal as the one cross-surface motif: put the ImprintSlot double-rule + lip at the head of Shield, Park, Drawer and the Airlock card, stamped only when a session is sealed, and restyle the Airlock countdown from 88sp to the Deck hero's Sora 72sp treatment so interception reads as the same instrument holding, not a different machine shouting. Cut the receipt footer to 'THE MACHINE KEEPS ITS OWN LOG' and move the YPT sentence to the Drawer, where records actually live.

#### [HIGH] Yugen outsourced to a legend: Park prints a colour-verb decoder key because the colours cannot speak

Yugen is meaning suggested by the object itself, never explained beside it. Monolith's colour semantics are so unguessable in use that the app ships its own decoder ring: the Park spec plate prints 'COLOUR IS A VERB: ORANGE = COMMIT · INK = SHUT · GREY = PEEK · PORCELAIN = OPEN' (ui/components/ParkDrawer.kt:113, PLATE_BODY :109-123), because the single accent #F55314 and the grey tiers (ui/theme/Color.kt:8,19 tokens) carry verb meanings no surface makes visible. A design that needs a printed legend in its settings drawer has admitted the meaning lives in the manual, not in the thing — the opposite of subtle profundity.

Recommendation: Delete the COLOUR IS A VERB line from the Park plate and make the states self-evident on Shield: give SHUT, PEEK and OPEN distinct shapes/positions (filled cap, half-height cap, empty outline) in ShieldCapSelector and the app rows, so tier is read from form, not from a memorised colour key.

#### [HIGH] Art-object aura without an art object: the spec plate claims 'NOT FOR SALE, UNIT Nº 01' then speaks only in datasheet units

ParkDrawer.kt:105-124, the app's only self-portrait, claims art-object aura — PLATE_HEAD 'MONOLITH ML-01 / UNIT Nº 01 · BUILT FOR ONE USER · NOT FOR SALE' — then describes itself in unverifiable engineering units: 'SOUND: FLOAT-PCM, 4 PARTIALS · POWER: YOUR PHONE'. Munari demolished the myth of the artist-star and held that an object communicates by being handled, not by its datasheet; an aura ('NOT FOR SALE', a serial number) with no handleable art behind it is branding wearing Munari's clothes. The park.html render shows this plate as the footer's longest text block — the most words in Park are spent on specifications no finger can test.

Recommendation: Make the plate earn its aura or drop it: delete the 'FLOAT-PCM, 4 PARTIALS · POWER: YOUR PHONE' lines and make the plate itself playable — tapping and holding PLATE_HEAD sounds the four partials as a slow chord the user can bend by dragging, labelled only 'SOUND: TOUCH THE PLATE'. If it will not be touched, remove 'NOT FOR SALE / Nº 01' and print the plate as a plain settings footer.

#### [MEDIUM] A catalogue number is not a collection: the six curios share no material, scale or family resemblance

data/MonolithModels.kt:806-851 — the six objects are a wave plot (Harmonic Loop), a brass instrument (Brass Gyroscope), an optics construction (String Prism), an astronomy model (Pocket Planetarium), a sand drawing (Sand Pendulum) and a geometry solid (The Monolith Cube): six unrelated metaphor families, with subtitles switching register from mechanism ('Four Concentric Rings') to poetry ('A Spiral Drawn In Sand'). Their serials promise a series — 'Toy 01' to 'Toy 06' — that the objects themselves never form. Pocket Operators earn collectibility the opposite way: every model shares one exposed-PCB form factor, one control layout and one wire stand, while function and LCD character vary, so the family resemblance is physical and the differences are content. LEGO Architecture does the same with a fixed black base, microscale and muted palette across 50+ sets. In Monolith the only shared trait is the row layout of the list they appear in.

Recommendation: Declare one material world and re-derive all six inside it — the code already leans toward brass-and-light instruments, so commit: every curio is a brass desktop instrument, drawn in the same ink weight, at the same implied scale ('no wider than a palm', as Toy 02's lore already puts it at MonolithModels.kt:820), with subtitles restricted to form-only descriptions. Keep the names; change the emblems and lore so a user can answer 'what kind of thing are these?' in one sentence, the way 'bare-PCB pocket synths' answers it for Teenage Engineering.

#### [MEDIUM] The icon's background frame is drawn for a square no launcher will ever show

ic_launcher_background.xml draws the brand's framing device as a square: a #EDE6D8 'Recessed Linen Geometric Grid Frame' inset at 18dp on the 108dp canvas (M18,18h72v72h-72z). Android adaptive masks (circle, squircle, rounded square, teardrop) crop that canvas differently on every launcher, so the square frame is amputated asymmetrically by every non-square mask — the one deliberate compositional element in the background is guaranteed to be cut. ic_launcher_round.xml is a byte-identical duplicate of ic_launcher.xml: the round variant makes no shape-specific adjustment at all. The foreground dial survives masking; the background's identity does not.

Recommendation: Design for the mask, not the square. Make the background a flat paper field (#F7F3EA, no frame) and move any frame device inboard so its corners sit inside the 66dp-diameter adaptive safe zone, or drop the frame entirely and let the dial carry the mark. Ship a genuinely recomposed round variant (dial centred and scaled for circular crop) instead of duplicating the square file. Forest and Opal both use a single centred glyph on a flat field, which is why their icons read identically on a Pixel circle and a Samsung squircle.

#### [MEDIUM] The spec plate brands the flaw: 'BUILT FOR ONE USER' is printed as the object's doctrine, and the plate specifies everything except how the object behaves toward the other people in the room

ParkDrawer.kt:105-107 hard-codes the app's only statement of what the object is: PLATE_HEAD 'MONOLITH ML-01 / UNIT Nº 01 · BUILT FOR ONE USER · NOT FOR SALE', rendered verbatim at the foot of Park (park.html spec plate). The plate then specifies wheel, hold, peek and colour — a complete spec of the owner's relationship with the machine — and says nothing about the machine's relationship with the room it sits in: no noise ceiling, no night luminance, no public face. Braun's product plates and Dieter Rams' 'less, but better' objects earn their place in shared domestic space by being quiet neighbours; Monolith's plate instead brands solitude as the specification, in a product whose actual deployment context — a student hostel — is the most shared living space there is. The doctrine is not decorative: it is the same one-user assumption that produced a bystander-illegible Airlock and a manners system of one sled.

Recommendation: Rewrite the plate as a two-part spec, keeping the ML-01 instrument voice: keep the owner's half (wheel, hold, peek, colour) and add a room half with enforceable numbers — e.g. 'IN A SHARED ROOM: NO SPEAKER AFTER 22:00 · SEAL FELT, NOT HEARD · FACE SHOWS TIME, NOT CONTENT'. Then treat those lines as acceptance tests for the QUIET ROOM bundle and public face above, the way the existing plate lines describe real mechanics. The brand claim changes from 'built for one user' to 'built for one user, in a room with others' — which is the actual product.

#### [MEDIUM] Inside the Drawer the metaphors nest like dolls: a drawer containing a cabinet of forged toys, next to a tower made of bricks

One tab (rail word: LEDGER; screen title: 'STORED', DrawerScreen.kt:224) contains four unrelated conceits stacked inside each other: the task ledger itself; day-words REST/ILL/FAMILY (data/DayWordStore.kt, render drawer.html); a 'CABINET' (DrawerScreen.kt:348) housing curios catalogued as 'TOY 01…TOY 06' (render drawer.html; data/MonolithModels.kt:799 CurioCatalog) whose state line reads 'FORGED — IT STANDS IN THE CABINET' / 'NOT YET FORGED' (DrawerScreen.kt:486-488); and the STREAK TOWER of bricks, whose accrual the data layer calls a WALL (data/WallAccrual.kt:53). A finished session 'forges' a 'toy' that 'stands' in a 'cabinet' inside a 'drawer' that the rail calls a 'ledger' — five containers/verdicts deep before the user reaches the fact 'I earned a collectible'. Muji's storage design (and Kenya Hara's emptiness principle behind it) holds a container system to one level of conceit precisely so the container disappears and the contents stay legible; Monolith's containers are louder than anything stored in them.

Recommendation: Collapse the Drawer to the paper family it already half-belongs to — the same family as the Deck's imprint and the numbered receipt. Delete CABINET, TOY and FORGE from user-facing copy: curios become IMPRINTS, stamped onto the receipt of the session that earned them (the Deck already has the machinery: ImprintSlot, ui/components/MonolithCustomComponents.kt:782), listed in the Drawer as a simple ruled index 'IMPRINT 01 — HARMONIC LOOP'. Rename the tower to the WALL the code uses, drawn as courses of ruled ledger lines filling — one container (the ledger), one reward form (the imprint), one progress form (the wall), no dolls inside dolls.

#### [MEDIUM] A fake machined-metal ornament system runs on every control — knurled rim with simulated lamplight, recess shading and lit thumb edges carry zero information

deck.html wheel: ~120 alternating black/white knurl teeth ring the dial, each with a computed specular highlight. BlockitCoreViews.kt:673-727 implements the knurl with a fixed-lamp cos³ specular curve, per-tooth flare table ('teeth 17 and 83 sit visibly wrong'), plus chamfer arcs at :630-642. The same fake machining repeats on every control: shield.html/park.html sled and rocker tracks carry recess shading lines (top rgba(0,0,0,.18), bottom rgba(255,255,255,.18)) and every thumb carries a lit top edge and contact shadow — BlockitCoreViews.kt:1813,1823 draws the slide thumb's highlight and marker lines. None of these marks encode a value, state or affordance; the detent ticks at BlockitCoreViews.kt:750+ do, and are visually drowned by the knurl.

Recommendation: Cut the material simulation, keep the information. Remove: the knurl teeth and their specular pass, the chamfer arcs, the recess shading lines on sled/rocker tracks, and the thumb highlight/marker lines. Keep: the flat disc, the 35 true detent ticks, the reader dot, one flat thumb fill per state. Reference: Rams' Braun work — surfaces are flat and honest; texture appears only where a finger needs grip feedback, and on a touchscreen there is no grip to fake.

#### [MEDIUM] The shipped example curriculum imagines exactly one user — a STEM undergraduate — and speaks to him as his tutor, not his tool

MonolithRepository.kt:347-392 seeds three tasks and nothing else: 'Finish Chapter 4 Problem Set (#1–6)' with free-body diagrams and equilibrium equations, 'Synthesize Lecture 9 Architecture Notes' with L1/L2 cache and page-table substeps, and 'Debug Dynamic Programming Memo Table' with 'Trace base case indices on paper first'. The intention default repeats the first verbatim (MonolithViewModel.kt:226, also rendered as the session intention in airlock.html). Every verb is assignment-completion (Finish / Synthesize / Debug), every substep prescribes study method in an instructor's imperative voice. No writing, making, work, care, admin or creative task exists in the app's imagination of a first day.

Recommendation: Replace the fixed curriculum with a blank intention field and rotating ghost-text examples spanning domains — 'Draft the proposal intro', 'Practise scales', 'Sort the visa paperwork', 'Write 500 words' — shown as placeholder, never as data, the way Duolingo and Headspace ask the user's own goal before presenting any content. If one worked example must remain, make it self-describing and neutral ('Example: plan a 50-minute session — tap to make it yours'), so the brand statement is 'this tool fits your work' instead of 'this tool is a classmate's phone, pre-loaded'.

#### [MEDIUM] The receipt — the one keepable, shareable artifact — carries no masthead and signs itself 'THE MACHINE'

grep of ui/components/ReceiptSheet.kt finds no occurrence of the word MONOLITH on the slip at all: the head is the user's task title plus a number (receipt.html Frame 1: "Revise thermodynamics / № 048"), and the only attribution is ReceiptSheet.kt:176 — "THE MACHINE KEEPS ITS OWN LOG · YOUR STUDY RECORD LIVES IN YPT" — which anonymises the maker as "THE MACHINE" and then credits the record to another product's initials. A real printed receipt, ticket or spec sheet carries its issuer as a masthead; Teenage Engineering repeats its logotype and model code on every face, sheet and box. This slip is the one deliberately print-styled artifact the app produces, and it is the one place a screenshot would travel — unsigned.

Recommendation: Give the slip a masthead: "MONOLITH" lockup left and the receipt number right in the slip head, above the task title. Rewrite the footer to sign the log line with the brand ("MONOLITH KEEPS ITS OWN LOG") and drop the YPT credit from the artifact entirely.

#### [MEDIUM] The only brand manifesto is fake hardware provenance buried at the bottom of a settings drawer

ui/components/ParkDrawer.kt:105-123 defines PLATE_HEAD/PLATE_BODY — "MONOLITH ML-01 / UNIT Nº 01 · BUILT FOR ONE USER · NOT FOR SALE" plus the colour system and operating rules — and ParkDrawer.kt:628-645 renders it at 10sp Anonymous Pro at the very foot of the Guard drawer, after a 32dp spacer and the last hairline (park.html spec plate). Two failures compound: the product's only brand exposition is filed where a user scrolls last and rarest, and its language is borrowed hardware provenance. Teenage Engineering's codes (OP-1, OB-4, TP-7) denote real manufactured units with real serials, printed on the object's face; Monolith is software with no unit, no serial and nothing that could be for sale, so "UNIT Nº 01 · NOT FOR SALE" is costume, not provenance.

Recommendation: Either earn the model code or cut the costume. If ML-01 stays, print it as a product designation where TE prints theirs — on the Deck nameplate, the desk-clock face and the receipt masthead — and delete "UNIT Nº 01 · NOT FOR SALE". Move the one genuinely explanatory line, "COLOUR IS A VERB: ORANGE = COMMIT · INK = SHUT · GREY = PEEK · PORCELAIN = OPEN", out of the drawer foot and onto the Deck imprint where that behaviour actually happens.

### Typography — 35 findings (6 critical, 23 high, 6 medium, 0 low)

#### [CRITICAL] Tracked capitals are used for whole sentences, not labels — there is no sentence-case voice anywhere

Type.kt:84-92 defines the only label style as Anonymous Pro Bold 10sp with letterSpacing 2.0sp, and it is applied indiscriminately to instructions: deck.html renders 'SLIDE OR TAP TO START' in that style inside the slide track, receipt.html frame 3 renders the seam phrases 'BIND HELD · THIS VISIT' / 'PROOF: LIVE BIND' in it, and AirlockAndDisarmOverlays.kt:155-161 sets the full instruction sentence 'NIGHTSTAND DESK CLOCK • TAP ANYWHERE TO EXIT' in tracked capitals at 11sp. The pattern extends to prose: ReceiptSheet.kt sets the fault sentences 'THE SHIELD WAS OFF FOR PART OF THAT SESSION' (~line 150) and 'SHIELD — STILL BLOCKED' (~line 162) in 12sp capitals, and the 62-character footer sentence at ReceiptSheet.kt:178 in 9sp tracked mono. Josef Müller-Brockmann's Swiss system reserves spaced capitals for short headings and labels and sets running text in lowercase precisely because all-caps destroys word shape over phrase length; Teenage Engineering's OP-1 manual makes the same split — terse caps for panel labels, sentence-case for anything the user must actually read and act on. Monolith has no second register, so its most important sentences (faults, exit instructions) are typeset in its least readable style.

Recommendation: Split the caps style into two registers: PillBadge tracked capitals may only carry strings of four words or fewer (labels, states, tallies). Every string longer than that — slide instruction, desk-clock exit hint, receipt fault lines, footer — moves to Atkinson Hyperlegible sentence case, 13sp, letterSpacing 0, regular weight, following the TE manual label/instruction split. Enforce it in code: make the badge composable reject or auto-demote strings over ~24 characters.

#### [CRITICAL] The declared six-size ladder is fiction — 19 sizes, ten of them within 5sp, so nothing reads as hierarchy

Type.kt:55-56 declares 'six sizes only - 104 / 72 / 50 / 22 / 15 / 10 - no two tiers within 1.4x'. A census of ui/**/*.kt finds 19 distinct fontSize values: 9, 10, 10.5, 11, 11.5, 12, 12.5, 13, 14, 15, 16, 17, 22, 24, 50, 72, 88, 96, 104sp — ten of them crammed between 10sp and 15sp in 0.5sp steps (33 uses of 11sp, 20 of 12sp, 19 of 13sp, 12 of 10.5sp). Visible in shield.html: section header 11.5sp, routine sub-line 12sp, chip label 12sp, domain 14sp, app name 14sp — five 'levels' the eye cannot rank. deck.html shows the same mush below the hero: eyebrow 10sp, keycap 11sp, queue 11sp, task title 15sp.

Recommendation: Enforce a real modular scale and delete the in-between sizes: Display 72, Headline 28, Title 18, Body 16/14, Label 12, Micro 11 — minimum ratio 1.25x between adjacent tiers, following Material 3's scale (display 57/45/36, headline 32/28/24, title 22/16/14, body 16/14/12, label 14/12/11) where no two neighbouring roles differ by less than ~1.14x in size AND differ in weight/role. Migrate every 10.5/11.5/12.5sp call site to the nearest token; add a lint rule rejecting literal fontSize outside Type.kt.

#### [CRITICAL] Three rival display faces for the same job: Sora 72 hero, mono 88 countdown, mono 96 desk clock

Time — the product's core datum — is set in three unrelated display voices: Deck hero Sora Bold 72sp ls -2 (Type.kt:63-71, deck.html hero); Airlock countdown Anonymous Pro Bold 88sp (AirlockAndDisarmOverlays.kt:636-639, airlock.html Frame 1); desk clock Anonymous Pro Bold 96sp ls -3 (AirlockAndDisarmOverlays.kt:164-166, receipt.html Frame 4) — bypassing DeskClockTextStyle, which defines Sora 104sp for exactly that surface (Type.kt:74-82) and is never used there. Same user, same minute-count, three typefaces, three sizes, within one session flow.

Recommendation: One numeral voice everywhere, following Braun under Rams/Lubs: the ET66 uses a single grotesk (Akzidenz-Grotesk) for every digit and lets size/colour — never a second typeface — mark importance. Make Sora the sole display-numeral face: hero 72sp, Airlock countdown 72sp, desk clock 104sp via DeskClockTextStyle; reserve Anonymous Pro strictly for ≤15sp telemetry. Delete the 88sp and 96sp one-off styles.

#### [CRITICAL] Wheel numerals are printed upright and off-register on a radial scale — every numeral except the top one disagrees with its own tick

Nomos Tangente positions its numerals and batons radially — each numeral's stem is its radius, tilted in the bottom half — so glyph, tick and centre form one line. Monolith's ticks are radial lines (BlockitCoreViews.kt:784-791, drawn rInner→rOuter at angle rad), but its numerals are drawn with canvas.drawText at cx+cos(a)*numeralR, cy+sin(a)*numeralR + sp(5f) with paintMono.textAlign=CENTER and no rotation anywhere in the loop (BlockitCoreViews.kt:793-810). The deck.html render confirms it on screen: all six numerals (30 at top-left through 180 at lower-right, x=193.7 y=231.1) sit screen-horizontal while their major ticks point diagonally. Worse, the +sp(5f) baseline fudge is a constant screen-vertical shift, not a radial one: at 90 (top) it drags the numeral 5sp toward the hub, at 180 it pushes it 5sp outward, and at 60/120 it slides the numeral sideways off its tick axis — the six numeral centres do not lie on a circle at all. This is the exact counterfeit tell on a Tangente: numerals whose placement is generic instead of measured.

Recommendation: Redraw the numeral ring as dial print: wrap each numeral in canvas.save/translate/rotate so its vertical axis coincides with its tick's radius (rotation = a + 90°), position its centre exactly on numeralR using measured text bounds (cap-height/2 along the radius), and delete the +sp(5f) screen-vertical fudge. Re-proof the ring by checking that a straightedge from hub centre through each major tick passes through the centre of its numeral.

#### [CRITICAL] The Airlock's hero is the wait, not the destination: the countdown outranks the app and the intention by 3.7x and 7x

Kinneir/Calvert's Worboys principles require the important message to be distinguishable at long range and clear at a glance, with only essential information on the sign. AirlockAndDisarmOverlays.kt sets the countdown at 88sp Anonymous Pro Bold (line 639), the intercepted app name — the actual subject of the decision — at 24sp (line 618), the badge at 11.5sp (line 610) and 'ACTIVE INTENTION: …' at 12.5sp at 80% alpha (line 648). The airlock.html render confirms the on-screen order: '03' fills the visual field while the reason the user armed the session reads as a footnote. A tempted user in one second absorbs a number with no unit and no verb, not 'Instagram — you are working on Chapter 4'.

Recommendation: Invert the hierarchy to sign order: app name becomes the hero at 44-50sp sentence case, intention second at 17sp full alpha directly under it, and the countdown demoted to a 20sp mono distance-plaque in the card's top corner reading '5 sec' with its unit — the way a road sign subordinates the distance plate to the destination it serves.

#### [CRITICAL] Uppercase is a costume, not an alphabet: Crouwel abolished case as structure, Monolith shouts in three inconsistent mechanisms while user data breaks the register

Crouwel dreamed of, and in New Alphabet built, a single-case alphabet — case removed as a structural simplification. Monolith performs the opposite: the machine voice is ALL-CAPS, but produced three different ways — pre-shouted string literals, render-time transforms (DrawerScreen.kt:111 and :390 .uppercase(Locale.US), AirlockAndDisarmOverlays.kt:607, MonolithViewModel.kt:2053 uppercasing app names into warnings), and not at all where a developer forgot. Meanwhile user strings enter the same screens in sentence case (task title 'Finish Chapter 4 Problem Set (#1–6)' on deck.html), so the supposedly caseless machine register changes grammar depending on who typed the string. At 10sp with 2sp tracking (Type.kt PillBadgeTextStyle) the caps also destroy word shape precisely where Crouwel's merger was meant to aid recognition.

Recommendation: Make case a data rule, not a style: create one PlateText composable that owns the mono register and applies the transform exactly once; delete every scattered .uppercase() call site and every pre-capped literal; and bar user-authored strings from the plate register entirely — task titles and app names always render in Atkinson sentence case, machine speech only in the plate.

#### [HIGH] The desk clock bypasses its own across-the-room type style and sets the hero numerals in cramped typewriter mono

Type.kt:73-82 defines DeskClockTextStyle — Sora Bold 104sp, lineHeight 100sp, letterSpacing -3sp — documented as 'H1 - across-the-room time. AOD only' and wired as displayLarge at Type.kt:140, yet no call site uses it. AlwaysOnDeskClockOverlay ignores it and hardcodes Anonymous Pro Bold 96sp at -3sp tracking (AirlockAndDisarmOverlays.kt:161-168; its own comment even claims 112sp). receipt.html frame 4 confirms the result: '24:36' set in a narrow typewriter mono whose uniform advance and crushed -3sp tracking read as telemetry/code, not as clock numerals. The DN40's fluorescent display and Braun's later BC21 use purpose-built, widely-proportioned digits designed to be parsed in one glance at distance.

Recommendation: Make the overlay actually consume DeskClockTextStyle (Sora Bold 104sp) — or, if mono must stay for identity, redraw the numerals in Anonymous Pro at 104sp with letterSpacing 0 and tabular lining figures, and delete the dead 96sp hardcode so the type token is the single source. Add a 3-metre glance test to the design checklist: the value must parse as a duration in under a second, with the colon unmistakable.

#### [HIGH] Repair order #3: un-alias the type scale — bodySmall and all three label roles are the same two styles, so no explanatory copy can ever be written

Type.kt:141-151 maps the Material type scale onto six real styles and aliases the gaps shut: bodySmall = bodyMedium = BodyTextStyle (15sp Atkinson, Type.kt:123), and labelLarge = labelMedium = labelSmall = the single 10sp mono PillBadgeTextStyle (Type.kt:85). The ladder comment at Type.kt (~line 55) admits only 104/72/50/22/15/10 exist. drawer.html confirms the consequence: history rows, day declarations, serials and section heads are forced into either 14-15sp Atkinson or 10.5sp mono — explanation, caption and metadata have no tier of their own, so teaching copy either shouts at body size or whispers in telemetry mono.

Recommendation: Priority 3 — add the two missing reading tiers before any onboarding, empty-state or help work is attempted, following Material 3's 15-role scale where body-small (12sp) and label styles are distinct roles, not aliases: add a 13sp Atkinson caption style for metadata/explanation and a 17sp Atkinson reading style for instructions, and un-alias bodySmall and labelMedium to use them. This outranks copy rewrites: today there is literally no style a rewritten sentence could be set in that is neither a headline nor a serial number.

#### [HIGH] Single lines are spliced from two typefaces — mono numerals stitched into Atkinson words

MonolithCustomComponents.kt:84-115 implements rememberMixedTypographyText, a helper whose entire purpose is splicing one line out of two families: Atkinson Bold word spans with an Anonymous Pro Bold numeral span inserted mid-line. shield.html shows the result in every section header ('3 ACTIVE', 'SHOWING 10', '2 SITES') and in the rules tally ('4 SHUT · 3 PEEK · 3 OPEN'), where the mono numerals sit on a different x-height and stroke texture from the Atkinson words at the identical 11.5sp. deck.html's proof strip does the same at value size: BLOCK's value 'ON' is Atkinson 15sp while APPS '12' and TIME 'ENDS 10:40' beside it are Anonymous Pro 15sp, so one instrument row speaks in two voices. Nothing's type system uses three families (N Type, Lettera Mono, Ndot) but assigns each to a separate register — display/body, labels, navigation — and never splices them inside a single line; Swiss poster typography likewise holds one grotesque texture per line so numerals and words share one rhythm.

Recommendation: Abolish mid-line splicing: delete the mixed-span helper and adopt a one-family-per-line rule. Tallies and header counts should be set entirely in Atkinson Bold using tabular figures so '4 SHUT · 3 PEEK' reads as one texture; where a line is genuinely telemetry (times, serials), set the whole line in Anonymous Pro, words included, as TE panel legends do. Apply the same rule to the proof strip: all three cell values in one family.

#### [HIGH] The identity is inverted: eccentric type at illegible size, generic type at display size

Type.kt:86-90 sets the micro-label workhorse at 10sp with 2.0sp tracking — a 20% expansion ratio. Nothing's published token discipline for its comparable mono label style (Lettera Mono) is 0.05em tracking (5%) at 12px, and even its dot-matrix Ndot navigation face — a face whose dotted construction needs air — is held to 0.08em (8%). Meanwhile Monolith's display moments carry no identity at all: the Deck hero total is Sora Bold 72sp (Type.kt:64-72) and section titles Sora 22sp, a generic geometric sans indistinguishable from any fintech app. Nothing inverts this correctly: the eccentric face (Ndot) appears at display and navigation sizes where its construction survives, and the functional small text is a quiet, lightly tracked mono. Monolith spends its character budget at the size where character is illegible and spends nothing where the user actually looks.

Recommendation: Invert the allocation. Cut PillBadge tracking to 0.5sp (5%, matching Nothing's label discipline) and raise it to 11sp so the mono survives at label size. Give the display tier the identity: set the Deck hero and desk-clock numerals in Anonymous Pro (or a dot-matrix-style cut if one is ever licensed) so the biggest type on screen is unmistakably Monolith's, and demote Sora to section titles only.

#### [HIGH] The desk clock — the largest type in the product — is specified three incompatible ways

Three sources describe the app's largest type three different ways. Type.kt:62-63 comments a six-size ladder (104/72/50/22/15/10) and Type.kt:74-81 defines DeskClockTextStyle as Sora Bold 104sp, letterSpacing -3sp. The actual desk clock in AirlockAndDisarmOverlays.kt:163-170 carries the comment 'Hero architectural Space Mono numerals (112sp)' above code that sets Anonymous Pro Bold at 96sp — a third family, a third size, and a comment naming a fourth (Space Mono, which is not bundled). receipt.html frame 4 faithfully renders the shipped truth: Anonymous Pro 96sp tracked -3. The AOD clock is the one surface meant to be read across a room, and its typographic identity was never decided — it drifted between a Material ladder entry, a stale comment and the call site.

Recommendation: Decide the clock's voice once and delete the other two claims: keep the rendered Anonymous Pro treatment (it is the most Monolith-like surface in the app), promote it into Type.kt as the real DeskClockTextStyle (Anonymous Pro Bold, 96sp, -3sp), remove the phantom Sora 104sp entry from the ladder, and fix the comment to name the bundled family. One style, one source, referenced by the overlay instead of re-declared inline.

#### [HIGH] The voice is rented and its constitution is missing: three stock fonts, a frozen six-size ladder, and the design guide is not in the repo

ui/theme/Type.kt:16-46 builds the entire voice from three stock Google fonts (Sora, Atkinson Hyperlegible, Anonymous Pro) that any competitor can ship tomorrow, and Type.kt:56-60 freezes the ladder at six sizes (104/72/50/22/15/10). The comments repeatedly cite an external 'DEVELOPER-GUIDE.pdf §1/§5/TYPE-RAMP-TABLE' as the constitution's source — that PDF is not in the repository, so the identity's rules live outside the only artifact that must carry them to 2030. Nothing shows the mature move: it built the proprietary NDot face, then in OS 5.0 deliberately demoted dot-matrix to accent areas and adopted Geist for heavy text — a signature it owned, edited and versioned in public. Monolith can perform no equivalent edit: it owns no letterforms and keeps no in-repo record of why these were chosen.

Recommendation: Make one letterform property: commission or cut a Monolith numeral set — Sora-derived digits with the wheel's detent tick cut into the 5 and 0 — used only for the Deck hero, Desk Clock and receipt totals, the three numbers the brand is remembered by; Atkinson and Anonymous Pro stay as the honest working faces underneath, exactly Nothing's signature-on-top/workhorse-below split. Move the type and colour constitution into the repo as DESIGN.md, versioned with the code, so the 2030 edit is a diff, not archaeology.

#### [HIGH] The Deck hero is printed three times out of register, so the first fixation lands on a fringed numeral

TactileDeckScreen.kt:655-677 composes the same heroAnnotated string three times in one Box: a shadow ghost in 0x99D8D1CB offset y=-1dp, a catch ghost in 0xB3FAF6F0 offset y=+1dp, then the true glyph. deck.html reproduces it as .hero .g1/.g2 ghosts behind .main. The type is DialClockTextStyle, Sora Bold 72sp at -2sp tracking (Type.kt:64-70), so the two fringes sit inside the letterforms of the largest, most-read numeral in the product — at arm's length it reads as defocus, not debossing.

Recommendation: Print the numeral once, the way Hans Hilfiker's Swiss Federal Railways clock and Braun's dial faces do: one black impression, legibility at a glance is the entire design. Delete the -1dp shadow-ghost layer entirely; if a press effect is wanted, keep a single ghost at +2dp below at no more than 35% alpha so it reads as a cast shadow on the card, and get the tactile depth from the instrument card's shading (already used on the wheel's recess lines), never from a second, lighter copy of the glyph floating above the baseline.

#### [HIGH] The hero number is printed three times to fake letterpress — and reads as a blurry misprint

TactileDeckScreen.kt:657-676 renders the 72sp hero three times in one Box: the full string at offset y=-1dp in Color(0x99D8D1CB), again at y=+1dp in Color(0xB3FAF6F0), then the real glyph on top (heroShadowGhost/heroCatchGhost, :655-656). deck.html reproduces it faithfully (.hero .g1/.g2 ghost spans behind .main). The code comment at TactileDeckScreen.kt:632-637 concedes it is 'print not rig' faking a press impression. At 72sp with -2sp tracking the offset copies do not read as letterpress depth; they read as misregistration — the single most important number on the screen looks slightly out of focus. At night the ghosts flip to 0x80000000 black and 0x594A423C brown (:655-656), so the same number carries a different, dirtier artefact after dark.

Recommendation: Delete both ghost Text layers and print the hero once, flat, in the glyph ink — the standard Josef Müller-Brockmann set for Swiss poster typography: one impression, perfectly registered, no simulated press error. If tactility is wanted, put real elevation on the instrument card that houses the number, never fake depth on the numeral itself; a focus timer's readout must be the crispest object on the screen, not the blurriest.

#### [HIGH] 20% tracking on the plate style is an expansion multiplier and a script breaker

PillBadgeTextStyle (Type.kt:85-91) — the style for the header, proof-strip labels, seam stamps, imprint and every PARK board name — is 10sp, lineHeight 12sp, letterSpacing 2.0sp: tracking is 20% of the glyph size and it scales with sp. Effective width per character is glyph + 2sp, so expansion compounds: NOTIFICATION LISTENER (WatchStore.kt:85, already the longest board name, 21 chars) pays ~42sp of pure tracking at 100% and ~84sp at 200% before any translation. A German rendering (~30-35% longer, the standard planning figure) plus tracking pushes the PARK row in park.html — name left, GRANTED/MISSING right in a 48dp row — past the 350dp inner width with no wrap. For Hindi the failure is typographic, not just metric: 1.2 line height and 2sp tracking applied to Devanagari break the plate model — matras need headroom above the baseline the 12sp line does not give, and inter-character tracking fractures conjunct/shaping assumptions. The style has no locale variant at all.

Recommendation: Split the plate into two tokens. Keep PillBadge-Latin (10sp, 2sp tracking) only for language-neutral print: serials, numbers, MONOLITH. Add PillBadge-Localized for every human word: letterSpacing 0.sp, lineHeight 1.5x font size, no uppercase transform, used for board names, strip labels and seam stamps — following the W3C i18n / Material 3 rule that letter-spacing is dropped for complex scripts and capped near zero for localized labels. Budget German at +35% in every layout test: if a label does not fit at 10sp +35% + fontScale 2.0 with 0 tracking, it wraps to a second line by design, not by clipping.

#### [HIGH] The live countdown is set in proportional figures: the hero clock changes width every second because Sora's tabular figures are never switched on

Running readout is String.format("%02d:%02d") (ui/screens/TactileDeckScreen.kt:319) rendered in DialClockTextStyle — Sora Bold 72sp (ui/theme/Type.kt:63-71; TactileDeckScreen.kt:640,660-672). Measured from the shipped sora.ttf/sora_bold.ttf hmtx tables: digit advances are proportional, not tabular — '1' = 420/428 units, '0' = 743/763, '6'/'9' = 659/687 (1000 upem). Sora ships a 'tnum' GSUB feature, but grep finds zero uses of fontFeatureSettings anywhere in app/src/main/java. So 24:59 -> 24:58 -> 11:11 changes total string width every second and the centred hero re-centres/jitters continuously; the three stacked ghost copies (TactileDeckScreen.kt:660-672) jitter in sync, reading as vibration, not print. The app already knows better elsewhere: the desk clock sets its time in Anonymous Pro mono 96sp (design-renders/receipt.html frame 4).

Recommendation: Make every live-changing numeral tabular: add fontFeatureSettings = "tnum" to DialClockTextStyle and DeskClockTextStyle (Sora's own tnum feature, zero asset change), and add a lint/test asserting any style used for ticking readouts carries tnum. Follow Apple's Clock timer and SF Pro: figures in a live timer are fixed-width by definition, proportional figures are for static display only. If tnum rendering disappoints, set the running readout in Anonymous Pro Bold like the desk clock already does, unifying the two clocks.

#### [HIGH] Anonymous Pro Regular and Bold are two different fonts: mismatched builds, a 215-vs-623 glyph split, and the receipt's № exists only in Bold

Binary inspection of res/font/: anonymous_pro.ttf is 38,884 bytes, 215 glyphs, OS/2 v3, no GSUB/GPOS; anonymous_pro_bold.ttf is 153,616 bytes, 623 glyphs, a different Macintosh-era build carrying EBDT/EBLC/EBSC embedded bitmap strikes at exactly 10, 11, 12 and 13 ppem plus LTSH/VDMX/hdmx tables the Regular lacks. Charset parity fails on the app's own signature glyphs: U+2116 NUMERO SIGN (the receipt's session number) exists ONLY in Bold (glyph 'afii61352'); U+2713 checkmark likewise Bold-only; U+2192 arrow exists in neither. The receipt survives only by accident: ReceiptSheet.kt:103-110 sets receipt.numberPrint in Anonymous Pro Bold 13sp. Any regular-weight string containing № or a serial glyph outside the 215-glyph subset silently falls back to a system face with a different advance width, breaking the mono grid mid-line. Renders confirm the exposure: deck.html and shield.html set dozens of labels in both weights interchangeably.

Recommendation: Replace the stitched pair with one matched mono release whose weights share an identical cmap (e.g. IBM Plex Mono 400/700 or JetBrains Mono from a single version), subset it to the app's actual charset explicitly including №, ·, — and any serial symbols, and add a build-time cmap-parity check between weights. Reference: IBM Plex Mono ships weights as one engineered family with identical coverage per weight — a weight change must never be a font change.

#### [HIGH] +2sp tracking on a 10sp mono destroys the only reason to use a mono: the receipt and shield columns never actually align

PillBadgeTextStyle sets Anonymous Pro Bold 10sp with letterSpacing 2.0.sp — tracking equal to 20% of the font size and ~37% of the face's 0.546em advance (ui/theme/Type.kt:85-92). The same face is then tracked inconsistently everywhere it carries data: receipt lines 1.sp at 11sp and footer 0.25.sp at 9sp (ui/components/ReceiptSheet.kt:179-199), Shield caps and filter words 1.sp at 11sp (design-renders/shield.html), Drawer serials 1.sp at 10.5/11sp (ui/screens/DrawerScreen.kt:390,450). Tracking is added after the final glyph too, so centred tracked labels sit optically off-centre by half the tracking. The casualty is the one thing mono is for: vertical alignment. 'ARMED 18:42' and 'ENDED 19:32' on the receipt (design-renders/receipt.html frame 1) and the Shield's dot-leader tally lines can never column-align across lines set at different sizes/trackings — each line is a slightly different grid.

Recommendation: Split the mono into two disciplined roles, as Teenage Engineering's labelling and real thermal-receipt typography do: data mono (receipt lines, serials, times, dot leaders) at letterSpacing 0 so columns actually align; display mono (single-line badges like MONOLITH, GUARD 4/4) may keep +2sp tracking but gets compensating end padding equal to the tracking so centred text is optically centred. One tracking value per role, defined once in Type.kt, no per-call-site 0.25/0.5/1/2.sp improvisation.

#### [HIGH] Material type roles are aliased away — hierarchy is faked with tracking and caps because size and weight cannot carry it

Type.kt:139-151 maps Material's 15 roles onto ~5 distinct styles: headlineLarge=headlineMedium (same 22sp DrawerHeader), bodyMedium=bodySmall (same 15/22 Atkinson), labelLarge=labelMedium=labelSmall (all PillBadgeTextStyle 10sp ls 2sp), displaySmall/headlineSmall/titleMedium/titleSmall/bodyLarge-as-body never defined (bodyLarge is actually AppTitleTextStyle, a bold 15sp title). With size/weight roles collapsed, screens fake hierarchy with case, 20% tracking and colour instead — e.g. shield.html renders LOADOUT, YOUR RULES and ALL APPS identically at 11.5sp bold, distinguishable only by position.

Recommendation: Populate the scale by role, not by alias: following Material 3, give each role a distinct size+weight+leading triple (e.g. headlineSmall 24sp Sora for screen titles, titleMedium 16sp Atkinson Bold for row titles, bodyMedium 14sp/20sp Atkinson for copy, labelMedium 12sp for controls, labelSmall 11sp for plates) and forbid two Typography slots sharing one TextStyle instance. Hierarchy must be carryable by type alone, in grayscale, with tracking removed.

#### [HIGH] Pairing is inverted: typewriter mono is set as prose while the legibility face and display face sit idle

Anonymous Pro — a typewriter face — carries running text: receipt body lines at 11sp ls 1sp (ReceiptSheet.kt:192-194, receipt.html Frame 1), the Park spec plate as multi-line prose at 10sp/16sp ls 1.2sp (ParkDrawer.kt:631-642), blocked domains at 14sp mono (shield.html).
