Meanwhile Sora, bought and bundled in four weights, appears at exactly one call site outside Type.kt (ShieldMatrixScreen.kt:694, routine names), and Atkinson Hyperlegible — drawn specifically for low-vision reading — is demoted to labels while mono does the reading. Count: 67 Anonymous Pro vs 5 Sora style definitions across ui/.

Recommendation: Invert the pairing, following Teenage Engineering's manuals and Braun instruction panels: a neutral grotesk carries all sentences, mono appears only for values that must align or be quoted verbatim. Set every sentence-length string (receipt lines, spec plate, explanations, price/cooldown lines) in Atkinson 14-15sp with 1.45 line-height and 0 tracking; keep Anonymous Pro only for timestamps, counts, serials (№ 048) and domains-as-data. Promote Sora to all screen/section titles so the display face is actually present.

#### [HIGH] Numerals have no figure discipline: proportional hero digits, split-size units, no tabular figures anywhere

The hero mixes two sizes on one baseline — digits Sora 72sp, units 'H '/'M'/' MIN' at 50sp ls -1.5 (TactileDeckScreen.kt:644-650, deck.html hero '1H 50M') — and no style in the app sets fontFeatureSettings/tabular figures (zero hits for fontFeature or tabular in ui/). Sora's proportional figures in a live-ticking 72sp readout (DialClockTextStyle, Type.kt:63-71) mean the Deck's central number changes width as digits change; the wheel's detent numerals, proof-strip values and receipt times each use different figure widths with no shared figure grid.

Recommendation: Adopt the Braun ET66 / instrument rule: digits are moulded, identical, interchangeable. Enable tabular figures (fontFeatureSettings 'tnum') on every live or columnar number, set hero units at one size only (72sp digits with 50sp units aligned on the cap-height in a fixed-width unit slot, or drop units to the eyebrow line), and use Anonymous Pro — inherently fixed-width — for any number that ticks once per second, so width never changes mid-session.

#### [HIGH] The dial's scale begins in silence: the origin stop (10) and the factory-default value (50) are the two positions with no numeral

Nomos numbers its origin without exception — the Tangente's 12 is its largest print, and the Metro rings its dial with every 5-minute numeral from 5 to 60 — because a scale that does not print its home position cannot be read back to zero. Monolith's numeral loop is `for (m in 30..180 step 30)` (BlockitCoreViews.kt:801): the first numeric stop after the FLOW strait, 10 at 126 degrees (minutesToAngle, BlockitCoreViews.kt:521), gets a major-length tick but no numeral, and neither does 50 — which is the shipped default dial value (deck.html render caption: ViewModel defaults dial 50, 2 blocks). The value the product is born set to is one the dial itself never states; the user must interpolate it between a printed 30 and a printed 60 on a scale whose other end, 180, is printed.

Recommendation: Print '10' at the 126-degree shore in primary ink as the scale's origin numeral, at the same 15sp as the other majors, and add '50' — or restructure the ring to the Metro solution: numerals at every 15-minute mid (10, 25, 40 … is wrong on a 5-minute detent scale, so use 10/30/60/90/120/150/180 plus a distinct origin treatment for 10). No stop the wheel opens on should be unnumbered.

#### [HIGH] The flagship numeral is out of register in three places at once: comment says 112sp Space Mono, code sets 96sp Anonymous Pro, and the ladder's own 104sp Sora desk-clock style is dead code

On a Nomos the same live quantity never changes digit drawing: the small-seconds subdial repeats the main dial's numeral hand, smaller. Monolith's running countdown is Sora Bold on the Deck (DialClockTextStyle, Type.kt:63-72, applied at TactileDeckScreen.kt:659-676), but the same running session on the desk clock is Anonymous Pro Bold at 96sp (AirlockAndDisarmOverlays.kt:164-166) under a comment claiming 'Hero architectural Space Mono numerals (112sp)' — a third figure, and a typeface (Space Mono) that exists nowhere in the app. Meanwhile Type.kt defines DeskClockTextStyle — Sora Bold 104sp (Type.kt:74-82), one of the six sanctioned ladder sizes (Type.kt:55-61) — and maps it to displayLarge, yet no call site in the app ever uses DeskClockTextStyle or displayLarge. 96sp is off the declared ladder entirely, so the app's largest numeral obeys no register: not the ladder, not its own comment, not the Deck's face.

Recommendation: Set the desk clock in the existing DeskClockTextStyle (Sora Bold 104sp, letterSpacing -3sp) so the running value keeps one digit drawing from Deck to nightstand, delete the 96sp hand-set style and correct the comment to name Anonymous Pro's actual replacement; or, if mono is the deliberate nightstand choice, redraw the Deck running readout in the same mono — but pick one drawing for one quantity and strike the dead 104sp style from the ladder if it is not used.

#### [HIGH] A baseline grid is mathematically precluded: the seven specified leadings share no common unit

Müller-Brockmann derives horizontal field heights from the type's leading, so every baseline in the document can fall on one grid. Type.kt specifies leadings of 72.sp (DialClock, Type.kt:67), 100.sp under a 104.sp face (DeskClock, Type.kt:78), 12.sp (PillBadge, Type.kt:89), 26.sp (DrawerHeader, Type.kt:99), 20.sp (PrimaryButton/AppTitle, Type.kt:109,119), 22.sp (Body, Type.kt:127) and 27.sp (TaskActiveTitle, Type.kt:135) — a set whose only common divisor is 1, so no baseline or flowline grid can pass through all seven. Call sites then abandon even those, setting raw sizes with no leading at all (routine name 16.sp at ShieldMatrixScreen.kt:690-695, sub-step 12.5.sp at FocusSequencerScreen.kt:618-622). Block heights inherit the chaos: header band 47.dp (MonolithCustomComponents.kt:266), pinned strip 53.dp (MonolithCustomComponents.kt:659), Shield search 40.dp (ShieldMatrixScreen.kt:445) vs Drawer search 48.dp (DrawerScreen.kt:537) for the same object on two destinations.

Recommendation: Fix one leading and derive everything from it: keep Body 15/22 as the document leading, set the row unit to 22.dp, and re-lead the ladder onto its multiples and halves — DrawerHeader 22/22, TaskActiveTitle 22/22, PrimaryButton 15/22 — deleting the 20, 26 and 27.sp leadings. Set every block height as a count of rows: header band 66.dp (3 rows), rail 44.dp (2 rows), both search boxes 44.dp (2 rows), pinned strip 66.dp (3 rows), slide zone 66.dp (3 rows), Deck wheel field 308.dp (14 rows). A screen is then a stack of whole fields, and two destinations can be overlaid without a single horizontal edge disagreeing.

#### [HIGH] Every Airlock legend is set Bold in light type on a dark ground — the exact polarity Transport reverses to stop halation

Transport ships two weights for one reason: Heavy for black letters on light grounds, Medium for white letters on dark grounds, because bold light letterforms bloom and close up at a glance. The Airlock does the opposite on its Night ground (#362C27 card): badge Bold 11.5sp, app name Bold 24sp, countdown Bold 88sp, chips Bold 12sp (AirlockAndDisarmOverlays.kt:610, 618, 639; MonolithCustomComponents.kt BlockitActionChip), and Atkinson Hyperlegible exists in the app only as 400/700 (ui/theme/Type.kt), so no medium cut is even available to the night surfaces. The smallest, most decision-relevant line — the intention at 12.5sp regular, 80% alpha — is the only non-bold text on the sign.

Recommendation: Register a true medium weight for the night scheme and set all cream-on-brown Airlock legends in it, reserving Bold exclusively for the app name; raise the intention to full alpha. Test the badge and session line at arm's length in motion — if a legend needs Bold to survive the dark ground, enlarge its x-height instead of thickening its stroke.

#### [HIGH] The day word — the one word the user authors — is typeset in the machine's stamp voice, so the user's content is absorbed into the brand instead of standing apart from it

DayWordStore.kt:54 fixes WORDS = REST/ILL/FAMILY and DrawerScreen.kt:851-852 prints the declared word fused into the date heading — '"${headingLabel(group.date)} · ${group.word}"' — in the same Anonymous Pro tracked capitals the app uses for its own stamps (ATTENDED, MISSED, FORGED). DrawerScreen.kt:865-875 offers the words as three tappable chips in that same type. The drawer.html render shows 'FRI 30 OCT · REST' reading as one machine-issued filing, indistinguishable in voice from the app's judgements around it.

Recommendation: Give the user's one authored word a different body from every machine stamp: print it in Atkinson Hyperlegible, sentence case, untracked, after the date heading on its own line — and set the three declaration chips in the same human type. Reserve tracked mono capitals exclusively for facts the machine measured; a word the user declared about their own day must never wear the machine's uniform.

#### [HIGH] The wordmark is a font setting, not drawn letterforms — and it exists in three mutually inconsistent lockups

MonolithCustomComponents.kt:269-277 sets the brand as a Text composable: 'MONOLITH', AnonymousProFamily Bold, 10sp, letterSpacing 2.sp — swap the bundled mono font and the logo is redrawn by accident. ParkDrawer.kt:106-109 prints a second lockup, 'MONOLITH ML-01 / UNIT Nº 01', as spec-plate copy; system surfaces use a third, title-case 'Monolith' from strings.xml app_name (receipt render frame 2: notification title 'Monolith • Revise thermodynamics'). Rand drew IBM's letters once and fixed them for decades; Monolith has no drawn letterforms, no fixed casing, and no lockup rule relating word to symbol — because there is no symbol to relate it to.

Recommendation: Fix one lockup and draw it: set MONOLITH as outlined vector letterforms in the Anonymous Pro proportions at exactly the header's +2 tracking, export as a single drawable, and make the header, the PARK plate head and the receipt head all render that drawable instead of typesetting the name. Retire 'ML-01' as a brand variant — it may live as plate body copy, never in the lockup.

#### [HIGH] New Alphabet's lesson inverted: optical care is lavished on the 104sp clock while the 9sp proof text is rendered off the pixel grid in a face never drawn for that size

Crouwel drew New Alphabet for the actual output device — letterforms containing only what a coarse CRT raster could render truthfully, snapped to a 5×7 unit grid. Monolith does the reverse. Its display numerals get true optical treatment (Type.kt DialClock/DeskClock: letterSpacing −2/−3sp, Trim.Both, includeFontPadding=false), but the smallest, most load-bearing text gets none: the receipt's log footer is set at 9sp in Anonymous Pro (ReceiptSheet.kt:177-180), a typewriter face with fine strokes OLED cannot hold at that size, and Canvas telemetry is placed off-grid — MonolithRailView.kt:266-272 sets paintMono at sp(10f) with letterSpacing 0.2f and a baseline computed as centerY + sp(10f) * 0.36f, a fractional-pixel row that guarantees grey smear on every rail label.

Recommendation: Draw the small cut Crouwel would have drawn: set a hard 11sp floor for all mono, re-set the receipt footer at 11sp/0.5sp across two lines instead of shrinking it to one 9sp line, and pixel-snap every Canvas drawText position — round baselines and label centres to whole device pixels in MonolithRailView and BlockitCoreViews so glyphs land on the raster instead of between pixels.

#### [HIGH] The work itself is the smallest type on every surface - duration and temptation get the hero size

Deck render (deck.html) and TactileDeckScreen.kt: the tool's own parameter is the hero - TOTAL in DialClockTextStyle 72sp (ui/theme/Type.kt:63-66) over a 288dp RotaryWheelView - while the actual object of attention, the work, is one 15sp single-line ellipsised row at TactileDeckScreen.kt:803 ('NOW Finish Chapter 4 Problem Set (#1-6)' beside DONE/QUEUE). The Airlock repeats the inversion: AirlockAndDisarmOverlays.kt:615-625 prints the intercepted app at 24sp bold, and :646-655 prints 'ACTIVE INTENTION: ...' at 12.5sp in cream at 80% opacity. In Weil's terms the thought is penetrated by the blocker and by the temptation, never by the object.

Recommendation: Invert both hierarchies. On the Deck, make the active task title the hero (Atkinson Hyperlegible bold, 28sp, up to two full lines, no ellipsis) and demote duration to the strip's existing 15sp mono TIME cell, shrinking the wheel below it. In the Airlock, demote the intercepted app name to the 11.5sp badge line and set the session intention at 20sp full-opacity cream as the card's largest text after the delay.

#### [MEDIUM] One card, two numeric voices: the wheel, the hero total and the strip tell time in different faces

Within the Deck's single instrument card (deck.html), the same quantity — minutes — is typeset in two unrelated faces: the hero total '1H 50M' in Sora Bold 72sp, and the rotary wheel's detent numerals 30/60/90/120/150/180 in Anonymous Pro Bold 15sp (the .num style in deck.html, drawn from RotaryWheelView), while the proof strip below adds a third rendering of time, 'ENDS 10:40' in Anonymous Pro 15sp. Sora's proportional, tightly tracked figures and Anonymous Pro's fixed-width figures have different digit widths and rhythms, so the eye cannot carry a number from the wheel to the total above it without re-reading. Teenage Engineering's instrument screens (OP-1, TP-7) hold one numeric voice per instrument precisely so a value read at the dial is the same value at the readout; Swiss information design does the same with a single tabular figure set per document.

Recommendation: Unify the numeric voice inside the instrument: set the wheel detent numerals in the same family as the hero (or, per the identity fix, move both to Anonymous Pro) and keep the proof-strip time in that same face, so dial, total and end-time are one continuous numeric system. Reserve the second family exclusively for non-numeric labels.

#### [MEDIUM] The register is inverted for correspondence: the week's story would be set in tracked mono ledger lines while the readable prose face is rationed to titles, and the only signature in the system is 'THE MACHINE' outsourcing the record to YPT

ReceiptSheet.kt:186-199 ReceiptMonoLine sets every record line in Anonymous Pro 11sp with 1sp letter-spacing; drawer.html shows the same register governing the whole archive — day headings 11sp mono uppercase, session meta 10.5sp mono — while Atkinson Hyperlegible, a face designed for sustained legibility, appears only as the 15sp receipt/task title (ReceiptSheet.kt title Text). The one footer the system signs with reads 'THE MACHINE KEEPS ITS OWN LOG · YOUR STUDY RECORD LIVES IN YPT' (ReceiptSheet.kt:176): the sender names itself a machine, addresses nobody, and directs the reader's own record to an external product. Fitbit's letter inverts all three choices: a named salutation in a friendly proportional face, stats demoted to a ruled table beneath the greeting, and the sender's name on the message.

Recommendation: Reassign the two faces by genre, keeping both: mono stays for the letter's furniture — dateline, week №, and the appendix aggregates table (ruled, 11sp, exactly as ReceiptMonoLine) — and Atkinson Hyperlegible 15sp/22sp becomes the letter's body for the 3–5 prose sentences selected under the other findings. Replace the YPT footer on the weekly artefact with a real letter closing drawn from Monolith's own seal vocabulary: body, then '— SEALED · MONOLITH' in mono 9sp as the signature line, with the week's receipts listed as enclosures ('ENC: RECEIPTS № 041–048'). No salutation by personal name (the app stores none); address the work instead — the opening line names the week's intention, which the data already holds.

#### [MEDIUM] Three families, three incompatible small-size rendering strategies — and the 10sp workhorse face switches rendering modes exactly at badge size

Measured from the shipped binaries: (1) Sora statics (sora*.ttf) contain no fpgm/cvt hinting bytecode at all (maxSizeOfInstructions = 0) — at the 15sp button size (ui/theme/Type.kt:105-112) its rendering is left entirely to each OEM renderer's autohinter. (2) Atkinson Hyperlegible is ttfautohint v1.8.3 output (name table version string) with a full 3,596-byte fpgm. (3) Anonymous Pro (2009, v1.003) gates its rendering through a gasp table {9ppem: grayscale-off/gridfit, 13ppem: gridfit, 65535: grayscale} — so the 10sp badge sits at 10ppem on an mdpi device, 15ppem on hdpi, 30ppem on xxhdpi, straddling the face's own mode switches, while its Bold additionally carries bitmap strikes only for 10-13ppem. Nothing in the repo renders or screenshots text at these ppem/density combinations to check the result; the smallest, most-repeated text in the app is the least verified.

Recommendation: Pick one small-size strategy and engineer for 10-13ppem explicitly: either adopt a mono with modern full hinting drawn for UI sizes (Roboto Mono / JetBrains Mono ship deliberate small-size hinting), or accept unhinted rendering and compensate with size — data labels at 11-12sp minimum where stems survive autohinting. Add golden screenshots at mdpi and xxhdpi for the Deck badge row and receipt slip to CI so the last millimetre is regression-tested, the way Nothing OS and Apple treat caption-size rendering as a tested surface, not an assumption.

#### [MEDIUM] Font loading is lazy, per-view and silently faked on failure: Canvas screens can typeset themselves in fallback system faces and nobody would ever know

The Canvas views load their faces lazily, per view, via ResourcesCompat.getFont with silent fallbacks: wordTypeface* falls back to Typeface.SANS_SERIF and monoTypeface* to Typeface.MONOSPACE on any failure (ui/views/BlockitCoreViews.kt:172-190), then draw with raw Paint (textSize set at lines 296-300, 796, 1793) — a second text engine beside Compose, with its own shaping and a hand-rolled paintMono.letterSpacing = 0.2f reset to 0f after one draw (BlockitCoreViews.kt:1793-1800; same pattern in MonolithRailView.kt:267). Compose's side declares FontFamily(R.font...) resources (ui/theme/Type.kt:20-47) with no preload anywhere in MainActivity. Consequences at the last millimetre: first frames can paint the wheel, slide label and rail in fallback metrics (different advances, different baselines) before the real faces arrive, and a permanent silent fallback would re-typeset whole screens in Droid Sans Mono with no log, no visual alarm, nobody knowing.

Recommendation: Load the three families once, before first composition: preload via Compose's FontFamilyResolver.preload or a splash-gated init, hand the resulting Typefaces to the Canvas views from that single source, and make fallback loud in debug builds (throw/log) instead of silently substituting SANS_SERIF/MONOSPACE. Follow Material 3's downloadable-fonts guidance and Apple's practice: the brand face is part of the first frame's contract, not an async hope, and a typesetting failure should be a bug report, not a different-looking app.

#### [MEDIUM] Hero units are interleaved into the numeral line at 69% size with their own tracking — dial signature text forced into the scale

Dial print keeps two registers that never mix: numerals at one size on the scale, and signature text ('NOMOS Glashütte', 'Made in Germany') far smaller, letterspaced, parked in the dial's dead space under 12 and above 6. Monolith's hero breaks the registers inside a single readout: digits ride DialClockTextStyle at 72sp with -2.0sp tracking (Type.kt:63-72) while the units are appended mid-string as SpanStyle spans at 50sp with -1.5sp tracking — append('H ') and append('M') at TactileDeckScreen.kt:648-650, append(' MIN') at 644. The deck.html render shows the result, '1H 50M': the hour digit stands full height, its unit shrinks, the minute digits return to full height, so the span reads as two numbers of different rank instead of one measured quantity, and the trailing space inside the small 'H ' span makes the gap after H smaller than the gap the digits' own tracking sets elsewhere.

Recommendation: Take the units out of the numeral line entirely: print the full span in one size and one tracking ('1 50' digits only), and move H/M to the eyebrow register the Deck already has — PillBadgeTextStyle, Anonymous Pro 10sp at +2sp tracking (Type.kt:85-92) — set on the hero's baseline after the digit group, the way a dial parks its signature under the 12 instead of inside the numerals.

#### [MEDIUM] The one typographic interval in the app is literally filled in: YOUR RULES pours 90 dot characters into the space between each app name and its ruling

ui/screens/ShieldMatrixScreen.kt:1023: the YOUR RULES slip renders the space between an app's name and its ruling as Text(text = " .".repeat(90)) — ninety literal dot characters poured into the interval (shield.html shows the leader running the full row width on every line). The file's own comment at :960-963 defends it as 'the ledger's mechanism for binding an entry to its figure'. Binding is exactly what Ma refuses: the interval between a name and its verdict is where the reader's eye rests and the decision gathers weight; filling it with texture turns a pause into noise and makes every row vibrate at the same density, decided and undecided alike.

Recommendation: In SlipLineRow (ShieldMatrixScreen.kt:1023) delete the dot-leader Text: name left, ruling word right, true empty space between them on the slip's surfaceBright ground. Keep the 40dp row height and the right-aligned ruling column — alignment, not filler, holds the column. If a binding mark is needed for print legibility, allow at most three centred dots at 40% alpha on SHUT rows only, so emptiness itself becomes the mark of an undecided app.

### Colour — 24 findings (8 critical, 15 high, 1 medium, 0 low)

#### [CRITICAL] The climax is the least coloured surface in the app: the accent is spent at arming, and the receipt that delivers the verdict spends none of it

receipt.html Frame 1: the finished slip is surfaceBright #FAF6F0, ink #2C2A29 and dim #5F5856 only — no accent anywhere. ReceiptSheet.kt:78 paints the slip scheme.surfaceBright and every line scheme.onBackground/onSurfaceVariant; the app's single hue, TokenColorPrimaryContainer #F55314 (ui/theme/Color.kt:18), is already spent before the outcome exists — on the Deck's slide-to-start cap (deck.html) and on the Tower crown brick. Forest runs the opposite script: colour accumulates with the organism, fullest and most saturated at maturity, draining to withered brown-grey on death, so hue itself is the emotional graph. Monolith's palette is literally named for the exclusion — DaylightZeroGreenTokens / NightZeroGreenTokens (Color.kt:52,74) — and because the one warm colour is branding spent at arming, the moment of triumph and the moment of failure arrive in identical stone grey.

Recommendation: Give the slip an outcome-graded colour script in Monolith's own stone-and-orange language, following Forest's maturity gradient: ELAPSED_CLEAN gets a full accent edge-bar and warm cream field (the #F55314 currently wasted on the start cap, moved to where the result is known); PARTIAL gets the accent desaturated to a half-step amber-grey; ELAPSED_SHIELD_GAP gets the existing TokenAlert #D63E06 (Color.kt:29) as a ruled band. Reserve the slide cap in neutral ink so the accent's first appearance in a session's life is its verdict.

#### [CRITICAL] One orange does every job: start, safety, danger and error are the same colour

Color.kt:18 TokenColorPrimaryContainer #F55314 is 'THE single accent'; Color.kt:29 TokenAlert #D63E06 is a barely darker step of the same hue; Theme.kt:61 night error = NightColorPrimaryContainer #F47442, literally identical to the accent. As rendered: deck.html slide cap #F55314 means START (inviting), airlock.html RETURN TO FOCUS chip and Emergency60sValve fill are both #F47442 — the safe action and the session-ending, token-spending action share a fill — and receipt.html notification icon is the same orange. No hue distinguishes commit from rescue from catastrophe.

Recommendation: Break the accent into a semantic triad, following Apple HIG's separation of tint from destructive red and Teenage Engineering OP-1's per-function colour coding: keep #F55314 only for arming/starting, give the valve, faulted receipt and error slot a distinct deep oxblood red (#A3160A light / #FF6B4A night, never used elsewhere), and give RETURN TO FOCUS / KEEP FOCUSING the cream ink fill (#FFE4CF on night, #252323 on day). Audit every #F55314/#F47442 call site against that table.

#### [CRITICAL] The zero-green, one-hue constitution is a dead end: colour is banned, not coded, so the palette can never learn a second meaning

ui/theme/Color.kt:3-6 declares 'Strictly Zero-Green: every single color satisfies green < maxOf(red, blue)' and line 19 forces alert to be 'the deepest step of the ONE orange hue'; Theme.kt:60 then wires error = the same accent family, and MainActivity.kt:105 hard-codes dynamicColor = false. So accent, alert, error and success-that-does-not-exist are one hue forever, and the user's own wallpaper colour is refused by law. TE's system matured oppositely: RAL colour used strictly as code (orange always means recording, per-product encoder colours stay consistent across the Field line) — a vocabulary that grows by assignment, not a ban. Nothing OS 5.0 likewise kept its structure while admitting an adaptive colour engine tinting from wallpaper. A constitution whose only colour law is a prohibition cannot add a second coded meaning (a partner's countersignature, a health state, a live-vs-held distinction) without breaking itself.

Recommendation: Rewrite the colour law from prohibition to code, TE-style: keep warm stone + #F55314 as the inherited base, but reserve and name exactly two future coded hues with fixed meanings that never decorate (e.g. a witness/verification colour used only on countersigned receipts, a recovery colour used only on repair/forgiveness surfaces), each with a night step, added to Color.kt as tokens 20-23. Let dynamicColor tint only the launcher icon background and rail cap — Nothing OS 5.0's compromise — so personalisation arrives without surrendering the ground palette.

#### [CRITICAL] Evening has no dusk: at 20:00 the palette jumps in one frame from warm stone #E4DFDA to vault black #171412, with no intermediate stage

Theme selection is a single boolean with no third state: Theme.kt:108 'val scheme = if (darkTheme || isFocusSessionActive) SealedVaultNightColorScheme else WarmTactileStudioColorScheme', and MainActivity.kt:256 'val effectiveNight = darkTheme || sealed'. The two endpoints are Color.kt TokenColorBackground #E4DFDA (warm stone) and NightColorBackground #171412 (near-black) — nothing exists between them, and no animateColorAsState/tween drives the scheme anywhere in the app. The SLEEP routine that triggers it is a hard window edge, MonolithRepository.kt:849-850 (startMinutes=1200, endMinutes=210). shield.html confirms the daytime face the user is torn out of: full light scheme, SLEEP listed as one ordinary row '20:00 → 03:30'. By contrast f.lux has three staged modes — daytime, sunset, bedtime — warming slowly over ~60 minutes so the change is barely noticed, and Philips SmartSleep's sunset simulation 'prepares your body to sleep by gradually decreasing light… to your set duration'. Monolith's own code once knew better in miniature: the rail steps at t=400ms (MainActivity.kt:708 comment) — a 400ms courtesy for a tab bar, zero seconds of courtesy for nightfall.

Recommendation: Add a real DUSK state, not a fade gimmick: for the 45 minutes before the SLEEP window, interpolate the colour scheme in three held steps (f.lux's daytime→sunset→bedtime staging) — ground #E4DFDA → a warm amber-grey intermediate (~#B8A99B, accent desaturated one step) at T-45, → a deep ember intermediate at T-15, → NightColorBackground only at window start. Implement as a third ColorScheme derived by lerping the existing 19 day/night tokens, driven by the same RoutineDerive window math, so Shield, Deck and the rail all descend together. Philips sets the duration precedent: a descent is a programme with a set length, not a cut.

#### [CRITICAL] The emergency valve is the only surface that fills with the reward colour as you do the wrong thing, while KEEP FOCUSING stays drab ink

ParkDrawer.kt:113 states the app's own law 'ORANGE = COMMIT · INK = SHUT'. Color.kt:18 and :39 reserve that orange (#F55314 / night #F47442) as 'THE single accent'. In the Disarm overlay the valve fill is tokAccent() solid for banked progress and translucent in-hand (BlockitSuitcaseAndSwitchesViews.kt:655-661), so the longer you hold to break the session the more saturated orange you earn, in 15s banked increments; airlock.html frame 3 shows the orange bar growing across a near-black track. The right action on the same card, KEEP FOCUSING, is BlockitActionChip(isPrimaryInk=true) at AirlockAndDisarmOverlays.kt:809 — MonolithCustomComponents.kt:187-194 maps that to muted inkControlFill, never the accent, while RETURN TO FOCUS elsewhere does get isAccentArmed.

Recommendation: Invert the palette on this card, following an industrial emergency-stop / iOS destructive-action convention where the dangerous control is alarming and visually costly, not branded and rewarding: make KEEP FOCUSING the isAccentArmed chip, render the valve fill in desaturated ash-grey with a hatched/cracked texture that widens as it fills, and reserve orange for a thin 'session still protected' rim around KEEP FOCUSING that visibly drains while the valve is held. Progress toward breaking must look like damage accumulating, not a reward bar completing.

#### [CRITICAL] The one correct on-accent pairing is defined in tokens and bypassed in every rendered accent fill — cream on orange at 3.08:1

Color.kt:20-21 defines the correct pair — dark ink #471602 on accent #F55314 (measured 4.43:1 light, 5.37:1 on night accent #F47442) — but real components ignore it and set cream on the accent: MonolithCustomComponents.kt:193 `isAccentArmed -> Color(0xFFFBF1EC)` on a primaryContainer fill, ShieldCapSelector.kt:64 marker #FBF1EC on accent, and the Shield ratchet-warning banner at ShieldMatrixScreen.kt:259-267 fills scheme.primaryContainer and prints bold 12sp text in #FBF1EC. Measured: cream on light accent = 3.08:1 — below WCAG AA 4.5:1 for that text size and below even the 3:1 large-text floor for a warning the user must read before weakening rules mid-session (visible in shield.html, where the accent is noted as the only saturated fill). The token pair exists; the rendered pair is a different, failing colour combination invented at each call site.

Recommendation: Make the pairing un-bypassable: delete every cream-on-accent literal, route all accent fills through one AccentButton/AccentBanner component that hard-pairs #F55314 with #471602 ink (and #F47442 with #471602 at night), and add a Robolectric/contrast test asserting every primaryContainer surface's foreground. Follow Material 3's colour-role contract — onPrimaryContainer exists precisely so this pairing cannot drift — and Nothing OS's discipline of one foreground (white or black) locked to its red, never a tint of the background.

#### [CRITICAL] Danger has no colour of its own: at night error IS the accent token, in light alert sits 1.35:1 from it at the same 16-17° hue

Theme.kt:61 sets the night scheme's `error = NightColorPrimaryContainer` — error is not a similar orange, it is literally the accent object #F47442, and Theme.kt:62-67 admits NightAlert #FF8A5C was evicted from the scheme for it. In light, Color.kt:20 accent #F55314 (hue 17°) vs Color.kt:29 TokenAlert #D63E06 (hue 16°) measure 1.35:1 against each other — adjacent oranges, separable only by a lightness step. The accent simultaneously means commit/ARM (MonolithCustomComponents.kt:187 isAccentArmed fill), UNDO (same file :192), START (FocusSequencerScreen.kt:686) and the ratchet warning banner (ShieldMatrixScreen.kt:259). No screen can show 'this is wrong/dangerous' in a colour the user has not already learned means 'go'.

Recommendation: Give danger its own hue, not a deeper step of the brand hue: restore a true red for error/alert only — the Nothing Red #E30613 the palette killed (Color.kt:29 comment) is the right reference, since Nothing OS reserves exactly that red for critical signals against a monochrome field — and reserve #F55314 exclusively for commit verbs. Error must never fill a commit-shaped button; render it as red outline + red text on ground (red on #E4DFDA ≈ 3.5:1, so pair it with an icon/label, never as small text alone).

#### [CRITICAL] Light is flooded, not admitted: the 'spent rarely' accent leads both hero surfaces and fills the valve whole

Ando's Church of the Light admits light through one cross-shaped slit cut in an otherwise unbroken concrete wall — scarcity is what makes it light. Monolith's own law says the opposite discipline: Color.kt:16 calls #F55314 'THE single accent — spent rarely', yet the Deck's largest saturated object is the 84x56dp accent slide cap (design-renders/deck.html, cap #F55314 radius 20), the Airlock's primary action is a full-width accent chip (design-renders/airlock.html, chip-accent #F47442), the emergency valve fills its entire 68dp bar with solid accent as seconds bank (airlock.html frame 3), and the same hue is also the wheel reader dot (BlockitCoreViews.kt:811), the tower crown brick (BlockitTowerFadersAndCatalogViews.kt:116-119) and the horizon bar's first task. Five openings, all open at once: the accent reads as branding paint, not as light through a slit, and no surface stays dark enough for any one of them to register as an event.

Recommendation: Cut the accent back to one slit per screen. On the Deck: make the slide cap ink #252323 and keep only its existing 1dp marker line, recoloured to #F55314 and thickened to 3dp on the cap's leading edge — light through the joint, not the block. In the Airlock: RETURN TO FOCUS becomes the ink chip (#4A423C fill), and the sole accent is a 3dp vertical bar left of the countdown numeral, height equal to the numeral. In the valve: banked seconds fill ink, only the live, unbanked segment burns accent. One opening per surface; everything else concrete.

#### [HIGH] Surface staircase is too shallow in both schemes — Opal's black/white staging reads instantly, Monolith's beige-on-beige layers only separate by hairline

ui/theme/Color.kt:12-16 (light: ground #E4DFDA, recess #D8D1CB, raised #FAF6F0 — three tones separated by roughly a dozen RGB steps each) and Color.kt:33-37 (night: ground #171412, raised #362C27, with the file's own comment admitting 'staircase step 1, 1.35:1 over ground', and the recess #100E0C placed BELOW the ground). deck.html and shield.html renders confirm it visually: the Deck's one raised card and Shield's recessed search/track fields separate from the ground almost only via the 1dp outlineVariant hairline at 46% alpha. Opal's published brand kit (brandkit.opal.so) specifies the opposite staircase: pure black #000000 ground, #3A3A3A surfaces, pure white #FFFFFF text — every layer change is unmissable at a glance, in a screenshot, and in sunlight.

Recommendation: Widen the staircase until layers read without their hairlines: drop the light ground two steps (toward #D8D2CB) or lift the raised card to true paper white and push the recess down a full step, and raise the night card from 1.35:1 to at least 1.8:1 over ground (a #40362F-class step). Test by deleting every border in a screenshot: if card, recess and ground still read as three planes, the polish is real; today they collapse into one beige/brown field.

#### [HIGH] Zero-Green dogma deletes the success colour, leaving SHUT / PEEK / OPEN achromatic and unglanceable

Color.kt:5-7 enshrines the rule: 'Strictly Zero-Green: Every single color satisfies green < maxOf(red, blue)'. As rendered in shield.html, the three tiers that are the app's whole decision are fills #252323 (SHUT), #615B5A (PEEK) and #FAF6F0 (OPEN) — black, grey-brown and off-white. The margin glyph repeats the same monochrome code (solid / hollow / none). Colour carries zero information; the user must read 10sp words on every row, and red-green colour-blind safety is bought by removing hue coding altogether.

Recommendation: Repeal Zero-Green as a design law, following Kinneir & Calvert's British road signs and the London Underground map, where hue is redundant with shape and label, never a substitute for them: keep SHUT as ink black, make PEEK a muted amber (#D98A00, warmed to fit the stone palette), and make OPEN a desaturated sage/olive green (#6B7F5E light / #9AB08A night) that also becomes the sole success colour for a clean receipt and a held deflection. Retain the solid/hollow/none glyphs as the non-colour channel.

#### [HIGH] The stone staircase is too shallow: ground, recess and raised card are three near-identical beiges

deck.html and shield.html as rendered: background #E4DFDA (Color.kt:11), surfaceVariant recess #D8D1CB (Color.kt:14) and surfaceBright card #FAF6F0 (Color.kt:15) sit within a few lightness points of each other; separation is done almost entirely by a 1dp outlineVariant hairline at 46% alpha. Night repeats the fault — Color.kt:36 admits NightColorSurfaceBright #362C27 is only 1.35:1 over ground #171412. Whole screens (drawer.html especially) read as one flat wash of warm grey, so hierarchy, tappability and grouping have to be inferred from spacing alone.

Recommendation: Widen the staircase to hardware contrast, following Braun's ET66 calculator and Dieter Rams' Vitsoe 606 system, where recess, body and key are unmistakably different values: darken the recess to ~#C9C0B8, keep ground #E4DFDA, raise the card to pure #FFFFFF-adjacent #FEFCF9, and at night lift the raised card to #4A423C (currently reserved for sheets, Color.kt:34) so card vs ground clears 1.8:1. Test by squinting at deck.html: the timer card, wheel well and rail must separate with the hairlines removed.

#### [HIGH] The receipt prints every verdict in the same ink: clean, broken and shield-off are chromatically identical

receipt.html frame 1: the slip is surfaceBright #FAF6F0 with all lines in onBackground #2C2A29 or dim onSurfaceVariant #5F5856, whatever happened. ReceiptSheet.kt confirms it in code: the outcome line (line 124), 'THE SHIELD WAS OFF FOR PART OF THAT SESSION' (lines ~145-152, color = scheme.onBackground) and the faulted line 'SHIELD — STILL BLOCKED' (lines ~155-165, color = scheme.onBackground) all use the identical colour as the title. TokenAlert is wired only to MaterialTheme error (Theme.kt:36) and never reaches the receipt, the one artefact that exists to judge a session.

Recommendation: Give the receipt a print-shop verdict stamp, following Japanese hanko seals and airline boarding-pass status printing, where the verdict is the one coloured mark on an otherwise monochrome document: a clean finish gets a small sage-green rule and outcome word (per the new OPEN green), a valve-broken or shield-off finish gets the oxblood red rule and outcome word, and nothing else on the slip changes colour. The slip must be judgeable from across a desk without reading it.

#### [HIGH] A two-colour day: the palette has no dawn or dusk grades, only full paper daylight and full vault night

Theme.kt:103-112 MyApplicationTheme selects exactly two schemes — 'if (darkTheme || isFocusSessionActive) SealedVaultNight else WarmTactileStudio'. Color.kt:11 TokenColorBackground is #E4DFDA and Color.kt:32 NightColorBackground is #171412, with no dawn or dusk token set between them anywhere in the palette. MonolithViewModel.kt:76-95 evaluateTheme can only return NIGHT (session/SLEEP-owned) or 'AUTO · DAY — NO ROUTINE OWNS IT'. So an idle phone at 06:45 in dim dawn light and at 22:45 before bed both render the full-brightness warm-paper day scheme; the palette has a staircase inside each scheme (Color.kt night steps at 1.35:1) but no steps between day and night themselves.

Recommendation: Design the missing middle grades, following Philips Wake-Up Light HF3520, whose sunrise runs soft red through orange to bright yellow over 20-30 minutes and whose sunset simulation runs the same ramp in reverse: add DAWN and DUSK token sets interpolated on the existing staircase (ground between #E4DFDA and #171412, accent held at the locked orange family), crossfaded over 45 minutes anchored to the two moments the app already owns — the 03:30 filing-day start for dawn and the SLEEP window start for dusk. Two palettes become a four-stop day arc; no new hues are introduced.

#### [HIGH] Shield gives refused apps the loudest rows: SHUT/PEEK names print bold in ink while OPEN apps recede in grey — the catalogue advertises what it blocks

BlockitSuitcaseAndSwitchesViews.kt:185-187 and 345-348 state the rule in code comments: name is 'bold in ink when decided, quiet when OPEN' — a decided app 'speaks bold in ink; an OPEN app is quiet'. Lines 398-399 give the rocker thumb tokSurfaceBright() (#FAF6F0, the palette's brightest raised surface, Color.kt:15) for OPEN and near-black ink for SHUT, with a solid 8x8 brick glyph for SHUT, hollow for PEEK, none for OPEN (lines 326-342). shield.html renders the result: Chrome/TikTok/YouTube (SHUT) are the darkest, boldest rows on the screen; WhatsApp/Phone/Spotify (OPEN) recede in regular-weight grey — in a list whose whole purpose is refusal, the refused apps get top billing and the kept apps look like an afterthought. Apple Screen Time makes the inverse decision: under Downtime, restricted apps appear dimmed with an hourglass badge while allowed apps keep their normal appearance — refusal visually demotes the refused object.

Recommendation: Invert the catalogue's emphasis to match Downtime's dimming law: OPEN rows print at full Atkinson Bold 14sp in onBackground (these are the apps the user chose to keep — they should look kept); SHUT rows drop to regular weight in onSurfaceVariant with the thumb rendered in the recessed surfaceVariant tone instead of ink black, keeping only the solid brick glyph as the refusal mark; PEEK sits between. The Shield list should read at a glance as 'these few things remain', not as a bold-printed honours board of everything that was banned.

#### [HIGH] A broken day and a triumphant day print on the identical slip: no colour, motion or hierarchy anywhere separates failure from success

ui/components/ReceiptSheet.kt:56-80 — every outcome enters with the same fadeIn(MonolithCurves.specC()) onto the same surfaceBright #FAF6F0 slip; the verdict is one word appended to an 11sp mono line, 'ENDED 19:32 · {outcomeWord}' (ReceiptSheet.kt:126-129; words from MonolithRepository.kt:1683-1689: ENDED, PARTIAL, ATTENDED, SLEPT THROUGH), in the same onBackground ink as a clean finish. The palette owns an alert tone — TokenAlert #D63E06 (ui/theme/Color.kt:29), wired only as Material's unused error token (ui/theme/Theme.kt:36) — and the receipt never spends it; even 'THE SHIELD WAS OFF FOR PART OF THAT SESSION' (ReceiptSheet.kt:148-157) prints in plain onBackground bold. Confirmed visually in design-renders/receipt.html frame 1: at arm's length a shield-gap failure is indistinguishable from a triumph. Forest separates the states chromatically and permanently — living green vs the brown withered tree — readable across the room and across months of history.

Recommendation: Spend the alert tone the palette already owns: a shield-gap or partial slip prints its outcome word and a 2dp top rule in TokenAlert #D63E06 (NightAlert #FF8A5C at night), and enters with a flat, instant settle instead of the success fade — failure should feel abrupt and read at a glance, the way Forest's brown stump reads against green without a single word.

#### [HIGH] Material You is refused silently through a dead parameter, and the app never states the refusal as a design position anywhere

Theme.kt:101-119 declares `dynamicColor: Boolean = false` in MyApplicationTheme and then never reads it — the body branches only on darkTheme/isFocusSessionActive, so the parameter is a lie the API tells every caller. MainActivity.kt:105 passes dynamicColor = false explicitly, as if a decision were being made at the call site. No code anywhere reads isSystemInDarkTheme or UiMode (zero matches in the tree); the scheme is decided by evaluateTheme (MonolithViewModel.kt:70-97) from session state and routines alone, and the only place the app ever explains its colour to the user is PARK's readout 'AUTO · DAY — NO ROUTINE OWNS IT' (MonolithViewModel.kt:95) — colour framed as routine ownership, never as identity. Nothing OS, by contrast, makes its monochrome a named, user-facing mode the owner can see and toggle. A Pixel user whose whole phone follows their wallpaper meets Monolith's refusal with no sentence acknowledging it exists.

Recommendation: Make the refusal a printed, choosable position, or stop refusing. Add a PARK board sled — 'COLOUR: MONOLITH FIXED / FOLLOW PHONE' — defaulting to FIXED, and wire the FOLLOW branch to dynamicDarkColorScheme/dynamicLightColorScheme with the ink (#252323) and accent (#F55314) slots overridden back to the fixed tokens, the hybrid Material You explicitly supports: wallpaper-derived neutrals, brand-locked accent. If the answer is fixed forever, the sled still ships, set to FIXED, so the position is stated on the board instead of hidden in a dead parameter — and delete the unused dynamicColor parameter until it does something.

#### [HIGH] Paper-on-paper: the icon's three 'archival' layers differ by 1.05:1 and collapse into one cream wash

The mark's supposed depth — a paper dial plate recessed in a vellum ground inside a linen frame — is built from three near-identical warm off-whites: ground #F7F3EA (ic_launcher_background.xml:9), frame #EDE6D8 (ic_launcher_background.xml:13) and dial #FCF9F2 (ic_launcher_foreground.xml:13). Measured contrast: dial vs ground 1.05:1, frame vs ground 1.12:1, frame vs dial 1.18:1. At launcher size, with anti-aliasing and launcher icon scaling, steps that small vanish: the plate and the frame do not render as layers at all. What survives is only the high-chroma trio (ultramarine ring at 5.87:1, canary sector at just 1.70:1 against the dial it sits on, crimson hub) — a flat blue-yellow-red target, stripped of the archival-paper material the comments in both files claim to be drawing.

Recommendation: Rebuild the layer stack with real tonal steps, Rams/Braun-style: adjacent layers must differ by a step a user can see at arm's length (target at least ~1.6:1 between neighbouring fills, and far more for the ground). The cheapest honest fix follows the legacy mark's lead: invert the stack — near-black ground (TokenColorPrimary #252323), cream dial plate on top of it, orange as the single chroma — so ground-to-plate separation is an order of magnitude instead of 5%. If the paper concept must stay, drop one of the three off-whites entirely; three papers is zero papers.

#### [HIGH] Zero-green confines the entire chromatic world to a 9-30° warm band — the exact axis that red-green colour blindness erases

Color.kt:5-7 states the law: 'Strictly Zero-Green: Every single color satisfies green < maxOf(red, blue)'. Measured hues of everything chromatic in both schemes fall in a 9-30° warm band: accent 17°, alert 16°, night accent 17°, night alert 17°, grounds and greys 9-30° at low saturation. The only distinctions the system ever asks colour to carry — accent vs alert vs brown-grey neutrals — all live on the red-orange-brown axis, which is precisely the axis that collapses for protan/deutan colour-vision deficiency (~8% of men, ~98% of CVD is red-green type): orange, red-brown and taupe drift together and separate only by lightness. Zero-green does not merely ban green; by the G < max(R,B) inequality it also bans every blue-dominant cool hue that could serve as the second axis.

Recommendation: Break the zero-green law for exactly one functional hue: adopt the Okabe-Ito solution — keep the vermilion/orange brand accent and add its blue #0072B2 (or sky #56B4E9) as the sole cool token, used only where a second category or a safe/kept state must separate from danger under CVD simulation. Blue survives red-green deficiency because blue-yellow perception is untouched by it. Verify every semantic pair in a deuteranopia/protanopia simulator before shipping, the way Okabe-Ito was constructed, instead of asserting harmony from the hex table.

#### [HIGH] Night is brown, not black: a 1.05-1.86:1 warm-brown staircase on a lit #171412 ground fails OLED dark-surface craft

Color.kt:31 night background #171412 is a warm brown (hue 24°), not black: on an OLED panel those pixels stay lit and the 'sealed vault' glows brown-grey in a dark room. The elevation staircase built on it is compressed past legibility — measured against the ground: recessed #100E0C (Color.kt:34) = 1.05:1 and sits BELOW ground, raised #362C27 (:33) = 1.35:1, sheet #4A423C (:32) = 1.86:1 — three depth levels inside a 1.9:1 envelope, which collapses further at the low brightness a lockdown screen is actually used at. Meanwhile the scrims ignore the brown-black entirely and use pure Color.Black at 0.65/0.7 alpha (AirlockAndDisarmOverlays.kt:315,489), so the app has two unrelated blacks. airlock.html renders exactly this: a stack of near-identical warm browns where card, sheet and ground are told apart by hairlines, not tone.

Recommendation: Rebuild night on a true-black ground the way Nothing OS does — pure #000000 background (OLED-off pixels, signature red/orange accent carries all chroma) — and rebuild elevation as a monotonic lightening staircase with at least ~1.4x luminance per step, never a recess darker than the ground; depth below ground should be shown by border, not by a blacker fill. Tint scrims with the ground hue (e.g. #171412 at alpha) if the warm ground is kept anywhere, so there is one black in the app, not two.

#### [HIGH] Colour is specified by recipe, not by colour: alpha-baked tokens and alpha text mean the rendered colour exists in no token

Two of the 19 tokens are not colours at all: TokenColorOutlineVariant = Color(0x75615B5A) (Color.kt:27) and its night twin Color(0x758F8888) (:48) bake 0x75 alpha into the token, so the hairline's rendered colour depends on whatever is underneath — over ground, sheet or raised card it is three different colours, none of them in the palette. The habit spreads: AirlockAndDisarmOverlays.kt alone renders NightColorPrimary at alpha 0.6 (:158), 0.75 (:804) and 0.8 (:630,651,681,696-708) and NightColorBackground at 0.94 (:748) — a family of ghost creams that exist in no token list and cannot be audited, screenshotted against a spec, or kept consistent between the Deck and the Airlock. A token system whose promise is 'the hex in the file is the colour on screen' is false for every alpha-built surface.

Recommendation: Ban alpha from tokens and from text: pre-composite every needed tint into an opaque token over its intended ground (hairline-on-ground, hairline-on-sheet as separate named tokens), following the Material 3 / Braun print-spec practice of naming flat spot colours, never recipes. Where translucency is genuinely the effect (scrims, the 0.94 airlock veil), keep it on backgrounds only, name it as an overlay token, and never let body or label text drop below full opacity — muted text gets its own opaque hex, as the night secondary #9C8E84 already proves is possible.

#### [HIGH] Tier is encoded as luminance shading in one list and as plain ink in the other — colour is decoration, not a code

BlockitSuitcaseAndSwitchesViews.kt:396-398 the catalogue thumb encodes tier by fill luminance — LOCKED tokControlFill() (near-black), PEEK tokSecondaryContainer() (#615B5A), OPEN near-white — on a #D8D1CB track in shield.html, while the slip above it encodes the identical ruling as uncoloured ink text with no fill at all (ShieldMatrixScreen.kt SlipLineRow). Colour in the subway diagram was a code: one flat colour per line, identical on map, sign and train. Here colour is shading that appears in one representation, vanishes in the other, and at night inverts (PEEK thumb becomes tokControlFill(), the day colour of SHUT), so the code actively changes meaning when the ground changes.

Recommendation: Make tier a flat, invariant code, identical in slip and catalogue, day and night: SHUT = solid black square glyph, PEEK = black outline square glyph, OPEN = no glyph — the margin-glyph system the rows already half-use — and strip all tier meaning from thumb fill, leaving the thumb a neutral ink cap in every state. The ruling must be readable in pure black-and-white photocopy form; if it is not, it is not a code yet.

#### [HIGH] The single accent is reserved for triumph only: no colour in the token system exists for repair

Color.kt:10,18: the palette has exactly 'Single Accent #F55314… spent rarely'; BlockitTowerFadersAndCatalogViews.kt:117 spends it on the 'Crown brick' (the newest success) and the slide cap/seal. No token exists for a repaired, partial or broken state — ReceiptSheet.kt prints shield-gap and fault lines in scheme.onBackground, the identical ink as success, so failure is chromatically indistinguishable from triumph except by reading the verdict word.

Recommendation: Add one seam token to Color.kt (a gold derived from the accent, reserved exclusively for repaired states) and spend the existing accent budget differently: crown/success keeps plain ink, while mended bricks, valve receipts and shield-gap rules take the seam colour. In Monolith's own economy the rarest colour should mark the repair, not the latest win.

#### [HIGH] Seijaku faked as midnight: arming at noon flips the whole app to a night costume

Seijaku is stillness, not darkness. Monolith performs tranquillity as a costume change: MyApplicationTheme selects the full SealedVaultNightColorScheme whenever isFocusSessionActive is true, regardless of the actual hour (ui/theme/Theme.kt:108-109), and the Airlock hard-codes Night tokens — NightColorBackground at ui/components/AirlockAndDisarmOverlays.kt:591, imports :55-59 — so a 2pm intercept renders as midnight (airlock.html render confirms night scheme 'throughout'). A noon session plunges the whole phone into a fake night; the calm is theatrical inversion, not quiet — the palette shouts 'locked down' precisely when the user is supposed to settle.

Recommendation: Decouple session state from the night palette: during daylight hours a sealed session should keep the day scheme and achieve stillness by subtraction — hide the Deck's strip/imprint telemetry and mute the single accent to ink — reserving SealedVaultNightColorScheme for sessions that actually run after dark. Change AirlockAndDisarmOverlays to take the ambient scheme instead of hard-coded Night tokens.

#### [MEDIUM] REST, ILL and FAMILY print in identical ink: the three most different kinds of day are chromatically indistinguishable when scanning

Both renderings of a word use the single shared colour logic: the filed word inherits the heading's onSurfaceVariant grey (DrawerScreen.kt:851-860) and the declaration row distinguishes state only by onBackground vs onSurfaceVariant (DrawerScreen.kt:868-874). REST, ILL and FAMILY therefore look exactly alike everywhere — scanning a month in drawer.html, 'WED 28 OCT · ILL' and 'MON 26 OCT · FAMILY' differ only in letterforms at 11sp. The Hobonichi Techo makes one disciplined chromatic exception — Sundays print in red — and that single exception is what makes a month scannable at arm's length; Braun/Rams-era print systems likewise reserve one signal colour for state, never decoration. Monolith's palette restraint is right, but it currently spends its zero exceptions on nothing, including the one surface where an exception would carry meaning.

Recommendation: Assign each word one fixed ink, used only for that word wherever it prints (declaration row, heading, month index): keep REST in the current neutral onBackground, give ILL a single muted signal red in the Hobonichi-Sunday tradition, and FAMILY a warm ochre — both desaturated to sit inside the existing warm-grey scheme (Color.kt light scheme is built on #E4DFDA/#2C2A29). Three inks total, never used for anything else in the app, so a month becomes scannable by colour before it is readable by text.

### Layout and spacing — 32 findings (5 critical, 18 high, 9 medium, 0 low)

#### [CRITICAL] Four screens, four different grammars for 'a new section starts here' — card, gap-plus-label, rule, and silence

Deck marks a section by containment: the instrument is a raised card — clip 24dp, 1dp border, surfaceBright fill, internal spacedBy(10dp) (app/src/main/java/com/example/ui/screens/TactileDeckScreen.kt:571-602; deck.html). Shield marks a section by air plus a label: a 16dp Spacer stacked on the column's 12dp gap before an 11.5sp grey header (ShieldMatrixScreen.kt:875-878, header used at :282; shield.html) — and breaks its own rule mid-screen, printing YOUR RULES in full ink while every other header is grey (ShieldMatrixScreen.kt:872-894). Drawer marks a section by typography alone: a day heading with 6dp top padding, rows separated by full 1dp HorizontalDividers (DrawerScreen.kt:861, :926; drawer.html). Park marks a section by silence: the permission/interceptor family break is '16dp, no hairline, no eyebrow — the family break is whitespace, not a heading' (ParkDrawer.kt:355-356; park.html). Four surfaces, four mutually unintelligible signals for 'something new starts here'.

Recommendation: Adopt Shield's gap-plus-label as the single canonical boundary and impose it everywhere, following Müller-Brockmann's Grid Systems (1981), where one publication uses one division logic so the reader learns it once: Deck's instrument loses its border and surfaceBright fill and sits on the same ground as everything else, its TOTAL eyebrow reformatted as the standard 11.5sp section header at the standard cadence; Drawer's day headings take the same header style and the same 28dp effective cadence instead of 6dp-plus-rule; Park's two families get printed labels (PERMISSIONS / INTERCEPTORS) instead of a silent gap. One boundary language, learned on the first screen, valid on all four.

#### [CRITICAL] The two in-the-moment decisions are centre-screen: the Airlock's exit chips and the 60-second valve hold sit at maximum thumb extension, while Monolith's own lesser sheets are bottom-anchored

airlock.html frames 1-3: both cards are vertically centred, the RETURN TO FOCUS and EMERGENCY PEEK chips and the 68dp emergency valve all sit around mid-screen. AirlockAndDisarmOverlays.kt:594 sets the Airlock Box to contentAlignment = Alignment.Center and AirlockAndDisarmOverlays.kt:751 does the same for the Disarm overlay, whose valve must be held continuously for 60 seconds. The same file proves the alternative is already in the codebase: CapturedNotificationsDigestSheet (AirlockAndDisarmOverlays.kt:318) and ShieldPermissionPrimerModal (AirlockAndDisarmOverlays.kt:492) both use Alignment.BottomCenter. A 60-second press-and-hold at full thumb extension, on a loosening one-handed grip, is the highest drop-risk gesture in the app, placed at the moment of maximum agitation.

Recommendation: Bottom-anchor both decision cards exactly as the digest sheet and primer modal already are: Alignment.BottomCenter with 16dp margin, so RETURN TO FOCUS, the peek chip and the valve all land in the bottom 300dp resting-thumb zone. Samsung One UI's guideline states the rule Monolith already follows twice and breaks twice: arrange dialogs that require user actions at the bottom of the screen. The countdown numeral can stay large and high on the card as viewing material; only the actionable rows move down. For the valve specifically, bottom-anchoring turns a stretched 60-second hold into a braced one, thumb pad resting against the phone's lower bezel edge.

#### [CRITICAL] Never-grows doctrine makes the proof surfaces mathematically uninhabitable at 200%

MonolithCustomComponents.kt header comment states the doctrine verbatim: 'it never grows, never wraps, never changes height: a 47dp row over a 1dp hairline' (MonolithCustomComponents.kt:231-233, height 47.dp at :266). Same lock repeats everywhere status lives: ProofStripBand is .height(53.dp) at :659 with its seam stamps trapped in a .height(12.dp) box at :672, ImprintSlot text is trapped in .height(20.dp) at :863, RefusalSentenceSlot — the slot that explains why arming was refused — is .height(22.dp) at :747 for 15sp/20sp text. deck.html render confirms the geometry: 53px strip, 20px imprint line. Math at 200%: PillBadgeTextStyle (Type.kt:85-90, 10sp/12sp) becomes 20sp/24sp and the strip value 15sp/20sp becomes 30sp/40sp — label + 1dp gap + value needs ~65dp inside a 53dp band whose seam already owns 12dp. German makes it worse horizontally: BLOCK/TIME heads stay short, values like ENDS 10:40 become ENDEN / ZEIT strings that no longer fit the 0.9f/1.3f cell weights. The strip does not degrade — it clips the proof itself.

Recommendation: Abolish the invariant. Change every status container from height() to heightIn(min=): header min 47dp, ProofStrip min 53dp, Imprint min 20dp, sentence slot min 22dp with maxLines=2. Move the proof seam stamps to their own row below the cells instead of sharing the 53dp, so growth pushes the Deck scroll instead of overwriting proof. Follow Apple Dynamic Type at accessibility sizes and Material 3 list/app-bar practice: minimum height is the spec, content height is the truth — at fontScale >1.3 the strip stacks TIME under BLOCK/APPS rather than shrinking type.

#### [CRITICAL] Split-screen study — Monolith beside the notes — separates the wheel from the task it is arming

TactileDeckScreen.kt:548-563 splits the Deck into a weight(1f) verticalScroll column plus a pinned commit bar beneath it, with the wheel fixed at height(288.dp) (TactileDeckScreen.kt:705) and the hero readout ~72dp above it inside 16/18dp card padding — the instrument alone is ~380dp before the NOW task row or FLOW row. Fixed chrome adds 48dp header + 52dp rail (MainActivity.kt:735). In the posture students actually study in — Monolith in split-screen beside notes/PDF, or a foldable half-window, giving a compact-height window under ~480dp — the wheel fills the entire scroll viewport, the task it is arming scrolls out of sight, yet the slide-to-start stays pinned and operable: you can seal a session whose intention you cannot see. deck.html confirms instrument and task row are one vertical stack with no side-by-side fallback. Material 3 defines height window classes (compact <480dp) precisely because width-only adaptation fails here, and Android's large-screen Tier 3 requires full function in multi-window.

Recommendation: Add a compact-height Deck variant keyed to height class, not device: when window height is compact, shrink the wheel to ~176dp and lay the instrument out as a Row — wheel left, hero readout + NOW task + FLOW keycap stacked right — so instrument, task and slide are co-visible with zero scrolling. The phone portrait layout stays untouched; this is a second arrangement of the same composables, following Material 3's height-class guidance.

#### [CRITICAL] No field is ever drawn first: every width is either fillMaxWidth or sized to its payload, so there is no grid to break or trust

Müller-Brockmann's method is generative: divide the format into fields first, then fit content into fields. Monolith inverts it everywhere. All four destinations are a single LazyColumn/Column at padding(horizontal=12.dp, vertical=8.dp) — TactileDeckScreen.kt:563, ShieldMatrixScreen.kt:245, DrawerScreen.kt:212, FocusSequencerScreen.kt:162 — whose children are fillMaxWidth stacks; inside them widths are dictated by content, e.g. the Shield routine toggle is a 48x32.dp box sized to the word ON/OFF (ShieldMatrixScreen.kt:710-711) and the Deck slide cap is 84x56.dp in deck.html (.slidezone/.cap). No composable anywhere takes its width from a division of the 390dp format: there is no column, field or span in the code, only containers and payloads. The renders confirm it visually — deck.html, shield.html, drawer.html are four undifferentiated full-bleed stacks in which nothing on one screen predicts where anything sits on the next.

Recommendation: Draw the grid before the screens: publish a Grid object beside RailGeometry with margin 20.dp (the value header and rail already use), type area 350.dp at the 390.dp reference width, 4 columns of 80.dp separated by 3 gutters of 10.dp (4x80+3x10=350). Then re-express existing widths as spans: app icon + name occupy columns 1-3, every toggle/tier control is exactly column 4 (80.dp wide, text centred in the field, not a 48.dp box hugging the word), the Deck wheel spans columns 1-4, the receipt label field is column 1 and its value field columns 2-4. Any element that cannot state its span is not placed yet.

#### [HIGH] A filed word gets no page: an ILL day renders as one orphaned 11sp line with literally nothing beneath it

DrawerScreen.kt:851-860 prints the word as a suffix of the date heading itself — "${headingLabel(...)} · ${group.word}" — in the same Anonymous Pro Bold 11sp, letterSpacing 1sp, onSurfaceVariant grey as an undeclared date. drawer.html confirms it visually: 'WED 28 OCT · ILL' and 'MON 26 OCT · FAMILY' are single heading lines with zero rows, zero whitespace territory, zero body under them, while a worked day gets heading plus task rows plus dividers. The most human days in the journal — sick, family — occupy the least space on the surface, less than one stored task. The Hobonichi Techo's founding decision is the opposite: one full page per day whether anything is written or not, headed by date, weekday and moon phase, so an empty day is still a page with presence, not a caption. Monolith's day word is conceptually a page ('his authored note for a date', DayWordStore.kt:6-9) but is laid out as a punctuation mark on someone else's heading.

Recommendation: Give a word-day a page body: when a day carries a word, promote the word out of the heading suffix into its own display line (Atkinson Bold ~20sp, onBackground ink) under the date, followed by a full-width hairline rule and a deliberate block of empty ruled space (e.g. 48dp) before the next day heading — the Hobonichi page-per-day move, scaled to a list. A word-only day should take MORE vertical room than a worked day, not less: the emptiness is the entry.

#### [HIGH] The 'Airlock' is drawn as a modal dialog, not a room: a bordered, raised card floating in a void is the visual grammar of chrome to be dismissed, where one sec's pause is a full-bleed environment

AirlockAndDisarmOverlays.kt:588-605 — a fillMaxSize Box on flat NightColorBackground with 20dp padding, centring a Column clipped to 24dp radius, filled with raised NightColorSurfaceBright #362C27 and stroked with a 1dp border (NightColorPrimary @20%). airlock.html frames 1-2 show the result: a dialog card hovering in blackness, with dead void on all four sides. A bordered card is the learned visual grammar of an alert — a temporary obstacle object interposed between the user and their content, something to clear. one sec's intervention has no card, no border and no container: the breath fills the entire display edge to edge, so for ten seconds the pause is not an object on the screen, it is the screen — an environment the user is inside, with nothing framed as dismissible. Monolith names the moment after a sealed chamber and then draws it as a pop-up

Recommendation: Drop the card, its border and the raised surface fill from the intercept: compose the badge, app name, pacing element and intention directly on the full-bleed NightColorBackground, using the full width for the pacing element, and let vertical whitespace — not a container edge — do the grouping. Reserve the 24dp bordered-card grammar for the genuinely dialogic Disarm overlay, so the two surfaces stop sharing one visual language and the intercept stops reading as dismissible chrome.

#### [HIGH] CUT 2 — Delete the Deck's imprint and reserved sentence slot: three status bands print the same facts in the pinned stack

TactileDeckScreen.kt:956-1104 stacks three status assemblies under the slide in the pinned (non-scrolling) zone: ProofStripBand (MonolithCustomComponents.kt:644, fixed 53dp: BLOCK/APPS/TIME cells plus a 12dp seam 'BIND HELD · THIS VISIT / PROOF: LIVE BIND'), RefusalSentenceSlot (MonolithCustomComponents.kt:716, fixed 22dp, code comment: 'reserved always… Healthy = nothing stands here'), and ImprintSlot (MonolithCustomComponents.kt:782, double rule + fixed 20dp tenant box + 4dp lip zone + 6dp tail). deck.html shows the result: APPS 12 in the strip and '9 WILL SHUT · 3 PEEK' in the imprint print the same split twice, under a header that already prints GUARD 4/4, with an empty 22dp sentence gap between them.

Recommendation: Delete ImprintSlot and the reserved RefusalSentenceSlot outright. Keep ProofStripBand as the Deck's only status band and fold the imprint's one unique fact into its APPS cell ('12 · 9 SHUT 3 PEEK'); let a refusal sentence appear as a transient line that pushes content only while it exists instead of holding 22dp hostage forever. This is Dieter Rams' tenth principle as published by Vitsoe — 'as little design as possible… not burdened with non-essentials' — and the Braun ABW 21 logic cited with it: a clock face carries only what the read needs. Gain: ~65dp of pinned height returned to the wheel/task area and exactly one place to look for session state.

#### [HIGH] Density is inverted: the emptiest screen carries the simplest decision, the densest screen carries the most consequential ones

The Deck spends its first screenful on one datum: a 72sp hero readout plus a 288dp-tall wheel (TactileDeckScreen.kt:705; deck.html) express a single duration, with roughly three decisions (duration, task, start) in 844dp of viewport. Shield's first screenful packs the loadout cap selector, three routine rows with toggles, an expanded routine carrying eleven 42dp chips, the standing tally and seven slip lines before the app catalogue even begins (shield.html; ShieldMatrixScreen.kt:245-250, :327) — 25+ live controls in the same viewport height. The screen where a stray tap re-rules what gets blocked all day is the most crowded surface in the app; the screen whose only question is 'how long?' is a monument with acres of empty ground.

Recommendation: Rebalance density toward consequence, following Kinneir and Calvert's British motorway signage: at the point of action one message is carried large and alone, and density is deferred to reference material you consult standing still. Invert Monolith's allocation: give Shield's catalogue the Deck's calm — one tier decision per row-group with the routines and slip collapsed behind their headers so a screenful holds ~8 decisions, not 25 — and let the Deck's wheel shrink to ~200dp so the task row and proof strip share the first screenful instead of queuing beneath a dial that answers a one-number question.

#### [HIGH] The mid-study verbs are print, not targets: DONE is a ~24dp keycap and QUEUE is bare 11sp text, both buried under the 288dp wheel card

deck.html task row and TactileDeckScreen.kt:832-858: DONE — the verb tapped every time a problem set or chapter is finished mid-session — is a keycap Box with padding(horizontal 10.dp, vertical 5.dp) around 11sp mono text, a target roughly 50x24dp, and QUEUE, the door to the next task, is bare clickable 11sp text with no box at all. Both sit in the scroll, underneath the instrument card whose hero and 288dp wheel (deck.html) push them toward the fold, so the two most frequent mid-study taps are the smallest, least padded targets on the Deck.

Recommendation: Promote the task row to a thumb bar: make DONE a 48dp-high ink keycap spanning at least a third of the row width, make the whole NOW row (title included) a 56dp tap target that completes or advances, and move the row out of the scroll into the pinned stack above the proof strip so it never scrolls away mid-session. Follow Things 3 / Todoist, where completing the current task is a full-row-height target, not a printed keycap.

#### [HIGH] At the moment of commitment the plan collapses to one truncated line and a queue count

deck.html: the Deck's entire plan at the moment of commitment is one row — 'NOW' + a single-line task title with white-space:nowrap / text-overflow:ellipsis ('Finish Chapter 4 Problem Set (#1–6)') + 'QUEUE 2' as a bare count. TactileDeckScreen.kt ~L783-853 confirms it in code: activeTask.title on one line, sub-steps only behind a stepsExpanded toggle, queued tasks represented solely by 'QUEUE ${queuedTasks.size}'. The student slides to arm a 1H 50M session (deck.html hero) without seeing what task 2 is, whether the queue fits the span, or what the active task's next step is. YPT's Home/Planner keeps today's subject to-do list visible beside the timer for exactly this glance, and a paper timetable left open on the desk shows the whole day while you work through one period of it.

Recommendation: Make the Deck's task row a compressed day-strip, not a headline: under NOW, print the active task's current sub-step as a second line (never truncated — wrap to 2 lines, shrink the wheel hero from 72sp if space is needed) and render the queue as named mini-leaves in order ('NEXT: Lecture 9 notes → DP memo table') in 11sp mono, tappable through to Tasks. If the queue's placed time exceeds the dialled span, the strip — not a later receipt — says so before the slide, in the accent: 'QUEUE RUNS 25M PAST END'.

#### [HIGH] Same hierarchy at 23:00 as 07:00: wheel hero and orange slide-to-start still shout 'arm another session' at bedtime

deck.html shows the identical composition at any hour: 288px rotary wheel as hero, then a 72dp slide track in near-black #2E2A26 with an 84x56dp hot-orange #F55314 cap and the words 'SLIDE OR TAP TO START' as the single dominant call to action. TactileDeckScreen.kt:208 effectiveNight = isDarkTheme || isSessionRunning — the only hour-adjacent branch in the screen changes colour tokens; no layout, ordering or affordance branch reads the clock. MonolithViewModel.kt:70-95 evaluateTheme likewise returns only DAY/NIGHT owned by a session or SLEEP routine, never an evening state. At 23:00, unarmed, the Deck therefore still leads with an invitation to arm another session, at full visual volume.

Recommendation: Add an evening form of the Deck, following iOS Wind Down (lock screen dims and its shortcuts are swapped for calming ones before bedtime) and Sunsama's shutdown (the evening surface inverts from choosing work to reviewing and rolling it forward): in the 60 minutes before the SLEEP window (or after 21:30 with no SLEEP routine), collapse the wheel to its proof strip, demote the slide cap to the recess tone #D8D1CB with copy 'SLIDE TO CLOSE THE DAY', and promote the day's totals and tomorrow's first queued task into the hero card where the wheel sat. Arming stays possible via TASKS; it stops being the loudest object in the room at night.

#### [HIGH] Hierarchy inversion on the Airlock: the 88sp hero numeral is the meaningless 5-second wait, while every price is 12.5sp prose at 80% opacity

airlock.html frames 1-2, from AirlockAndDisarmOverlays.kt:646-652: the card's hero is an 88sp Anonymous Pro numeral — the 5-second breathing countdown, the one number on the intercept with no consequence. Everything with a price is set smallest and faintest: the peek's cost is a single 12.5sp line at 80% cream under the chip (AirlockAndDisarmOverlays.kt:673-685, peekPriceText), and the peek chip itself (line 665) carries only a '2m' badge — what you get, never what it costs in the economy. On Zario's intercept the priced element is the interactive hero: the XP slider is the control you manipulate to buy your way out (apk-re/zario/EVIDENCE.md §4.1, screen_blocker_xp_slider). Monolith inverts that hierarchy: wait-time is monumental, price is a footnote.

Recommendation: Demote the countdown to a thin progress ring or a 15sp mono figure in the badge row, and promote the price to the hero slot the countdown vacates: under RETURN TO FOCUS, draw the peek offer as a priced row in 24sp — 'PEEK 2M — COSTS: THIS APP SHUT FOR 20 MIN' — and, for LOCKED apps, 'NO PEEK — EXIT COSTS YOUR 1 TOKEN'. The biggest numeral on an intercept must be a number the user is deciding about.

#### [HIGH] Shield's catalogue scans as a column of identical rockers, not as a list of apps

shield.html: every .approw is 54px tall with a 168px-wide .rocker at right printing SHUT/PEEK/OPEN at 10px on all ten rows, while .appname sits at left:28px in 14px and the margin .glyph is 8px. BlockitSuitcaseAndSwitchesViews.kt:363-365 fixes the rocker at 168dp x 34dp; :406-427 draws all three stop words on every row; :345-360 sets the app name at 14sp, ellipsised into whatever width the 168dp rocker leaves; :326-344 makes the scan glyph meant to be read 'without decoding the rocker' only 8dp. A column of ten identical 3-word controls is wider, darker (ink/grey/porcelain caps) and more repetitive than any name in the list.

Recommendation: Make the row name-led, the way iOS Settings app rows are: the identity (icon/name) owns the leading two-thirds, the control is a compact toggle carrying zero printed vocabulary, and state is read from position alone. Keep Monolith's sled hardware but print only the selected stop's word on its cap, reduce the other two stops to tick marks, shrink the rocker to ~104dp, give the freed width to the name at 15sp AppTitle, and grow the margin glyph to 12dp so the down-scan reads glyph + name, not vocabulary. The full SHUT/PEEK/OPEN words belong on the one row being touched, not on all ten simultaneously.

#### [HIGH] Deck's pinned stack states the app count twice in 80dp — strip APPS cell, seam stamps and imprint tenant are three voices for one fact

deck.html pinned stack (53dp strip + 12dp seam + imprint): strip reads BLOCK ON / APPS 12 / TIME ENDS 10:40, the seam underneath stamps 'BIND HELD · THIS VISIT' and 'PROOF: LIVE BIND', and the imprint directly below reads '9 WILL SHUT · 3 PEEK' — the APPS total restated as its split, ~80dp below itself. TactileDeckScreen.kt:956-965 wires ProofStripBand, TactileDeckScreen.kt:1094-1100 wires ImprintSlot with imprintTenantText; MonolithCustomComponents.kt:644-714 ProofStripBand, MonolithCustomComponents.kt:782+ ImprintSlot. The Deck's own comment at TactileDeckScreen.kt:632 claims 'The hero states the TOTAL, once (one fact, one rendering)' — a discipline the pinned stack violates for the app count.

Recommendation: Cut one of the two renderings. Keep the strip's APPS cell (it sits with BLOCK and TIME, the glanceable trio) and reduce the imprint to what only it can say — the seal state, e.g. 'SEALED № 048' or nothing when unsealed. Delete the seam's 'PROOF: LIVE BIND' stamp: proof language under a status strip is decoration, not information. Reference: Müller-Brockmann's Swiss grid discipline — one fact, one cell, one position in the grid; nothing earns a second cell by being important.

#### [HIGH] Single-line chips and a hand-tuned one-line footer clip the verbs first

BlockitActionChip (MonolithCustomComponents.kt:201 .height(42.dp), :224 maxLines=1, no overflow set so overflow is silent Clip) is the single body for every action, including the safety actions in airlock.html: RETURN TO FOCUS and EMERGENCY PEEK 2m inside a ~302dp card. German RETURN TO FOCUS → ZUM FOKUS ZURÜCK (16 chars plus wider glyphs) and Hindi multi-word equivalents cannot fit one line at 12sp, let alone 24sp at 200% — the verb is amputated with no ellipsis to signal loss.
