The same one-line fetish is tuned by hand on the receipt: ReceiptSheet.kt footer comment admits the 62-char English sentence was re-tracked to 0.25sp at 9sp to measure ~326dp against a 348dp inner width specifically to avoid wrapping and 'orphaning YPT' — any translation or any font scale above 100% defeats the measurement, yet receipt.html shows the footer has no designed second line to land on. Shield slip lines repeat it: .height(40.dp) fixed (ShieldMatrixScreen.kt:~1007) with softWrap=false leader at :1028.

Recommendation: Design the second line instead of fearing it. Change BlockitActionChip to heightIn(min=42.dp) with maxLines=2, centred, vertical padding 8dp — Material 3 button practice (minimum height, growth allowed) — and audit every chip call site at pseudo-German (+35%) and fontScale 2.0; the Airlock chips must pass first. Redesign the receipt footer as an intentional two-line lockup (line 1: THE MACHINE KEEPS ITS OWN LOG · line 2: YOUR STUDY RECORD LIVES IN YPT) at all sizes, so translation and scaling change nothing structurally. A wrapped action label is honest; a clipped verb on an emergency screen is a lie.

#### [HIGH] Shield's printed slip and app catalogue are one stretched column — the slip's dot leaders disintegrate at tablet width

ShieldMatrixScreen.kt:240 is one LazyColumn stacking five jobs serially — LOADOUT cap, ROUTINES, the YOUR RULES print slip, ALL APPS catalogue, BLOCKED WEBSITES (shield.html render shows all five in one scroll). The slip's SlipLineRow uses dot leaders between app name and ruling word: on a tablet those leaders stretch across ~800dp, destroying the printed-slip metaphor (in print, leaders work only inside a bounded measure of roughly 45-75 characters — Bringhurst's rule) and making the eye's journey name-to-verdict absurdly long. Simultaneously the catalogue rows carry a fixed 168dp-wide rocker (shield.html: .rocker width 168px), so in a narrow split-screen pane the same row crowds the app name out. One fixed geometry is wrong at both ends of the width range.

Recommendation: At expanded width split Shield into Material 3 list-detail: catalogue (search, filter words, sled rows) in the left pane; the YOUR RULES slip becomes a sticky right pane capped at ~420dp measure so its dot leaders return to print-plausible length and the tally updates live as sleds move — the slip finally behaves like the live receipt it imitates. In compact/split width, collapse the rocker to its selected stop plus a tap-to-cycle cap so the app name keeps its measure. Routines move above the catalogue only in the wide layout, where they fit without scrolling.

#### [HIGH] Shield's horizontal budget is inverted: dot leaders eat the middle while app names are starved by an oversized rocker

shield.html: every Standing Orders slip line devotes its flexible middle to a dot leader (ShieldMatrixScreen.kt SlipLineRow: leader Text " .".repeat(90), Modifier.weight(1f).padding(horizontal = 6.dp) at :1032) to bind a name to a word already repeated in the section header, while directly below, the catalogue row where the ruling is actually made gives the control 168dp and the identity what is left: BlockitSuitcaseAndSwitchesViews.kt:353-354 nameMaxWidth = (w - dp(168f)) - nameX - dp(10f), nameX = dp(28f); :360-361 rocker is 168dp wide x 34dp. On a 390dp phone inside 12dp page padding the app name gets roughly 160dp and is ellipsised by ellipsizeToWidth (:356), while the read-only slip wastes ~150dp per line on decorative dots.

Recommendation: Allocate columns by job, not by ornament, following the iOS Settings list discipline (compact trailing control, identity gets the flexible width) and Muller-Brockmann's rule that a column's width follows its content's rank: shrink the rocker to 126dp (42dp per stop, still above the 34dp height), guarantee the name a minimum 55% of row width, and cut the slip leader to a fixed 24dp rule segment instead of a full flexible field - the ruling word stays right-aligned, the dots become a hinge, not a desert.

#### [HIGH] Park's status column fractures on exactly one row: the SOCIAL SITES sled pushes its state word 88dp off the board's right edge

park.html: GRANTED / MISSING / RUNNING words form one flush-right column down the board, except SOCIAL SITES, whose RUNNING sits visibly indented left of every other word. Code: ParkDrawer.kt:653-659 ParkBoardRow is a 48.dp row, name left, Spacer(weight 1f), word flush right; ParkDrawer.kt:713 ParkSocialSitesRow keeps the same 48.dp row but appends Spacer(Modifier.width(12.dp)) plus a 76.dp x 34.dp SledSwitchView after the word, so that one word's right edge lands 88dp inside the column every other row establishes. The sled rows below the board (ParkDrawer.kt:475, :544, 52.dp) prove the sheet already has a separate grammar for word-plus-sled rows.

Recommendation: Restore the table: a status board lives or dies by one right edge, as in Tufte's data tables and British Rail departure boards where the status column never moves. Move the SOCIAL SITES sled out of the board row into the 52dp sled-row grammar already used for SOUND EFFECTS and SHORTS + REELS directly below the FIX key, and let the board row print only name and RUNNING like its eight siblings; if the sled must stay inline, delete the word on that row - never print the same fact twice at two different x-positions.

#### [HIGH] The Deck's pinned stack spends ~46dp of permanent height on slots that are empty in the healthy state, while live content is truncated to fit

deck.html and receipt.html frame 3: under the slide sit a visibly empty 22dp sentence band and an imprint assembly of rules and blank boxes. Code: MonolithCustomComponents.kt:747 RefusalSentenceSlot is Box(Modifier.fillMaxWidth().height(22.dp)) reserved always ('Healthy = nothing stands here'); :858-895 ImprintSlot is a fixed assembly - 1.dp rule, 2.dp spacer, 0.5.dp rule, 6.dp spacer, a 20.dp text box that exists 'in every state, tenant or none', a 4.dp lip zone 'reserved always', 6.dp spacer (~39.5dp total); the ProofStripBand seam adds a 12.dp stamp band inside the 53.dp strip (:672). In the pinned column of TactileDeckScreen.kt:954-1059 these fixed heights are paid on every frame, sealed or not, while the actual task in the scroll area above is a single ellipsised line (deck.html .tasktitle: white-space nowrap, overflow hidden).

Recommendation: Stop paying rent for ghosts, following the Playdate / Teenage Engineering pocket-operator discipline that a small screen holds no reserved voids: collapse RefusalSentenceSlot to 0dp when its sentence is null and expand to 22dp only on fault (the 90ms hand-back fade already exists to soften it), shrink the unsealed imprint text box to 8dp and restore 20dp only at the seal strike, and return the reclaimed ~30dp to the task row as a second line. Layout stability should be bought with the slide and strip, which genuinely must not jump - not with empty print furniture.

#### [HIGH] One panel, three control placements: one interceptor's switch sits on its stage line, one's is exiled below the board past the FIX key, and one stage has no switch and no explanation

Three interceptors, three different control grammars on one panel. SOCIAL SITES carries its sled on its own board line (ParkDrawer.kt:369, ParkSocialSitesRow at :699 — the code calls this the exception, 'ONE exception on the board itself'). SHORTS + REELS prints as a bare board line, and its actual sled sits below the board (ParkDrawer.kt:534), past the FIX key and the unrelated SOUND EFFECTS sled, so the control is separated from the stage it governs by two foreign objects. NOTIFICATIONS has no control anywhere: WatchStore.kt:167 records why only in a code comment — 'The notification capture has no setting — it is on by design'. On a Moog panel every stage's control sits inside its labelled section; here a user hunting the Shorts switch finds a state word, scrolls past a repair button and a sound switch, and finds a second, identical name plate.

Recommendation: Seat every interceptor's sled on its own board line, exactly as ParkSocialSitesRow already does — move the SHORTS + REELS sled up from ParkDrawer.kt:534 onto its board row and delete the duplicated row below the board. For NOTIFICATIONS, print a fixed plate where a sled would sit, engraved 'ALWAYS ON — NO SWITCH FITTED', so the absence of a control is a labelled design fact on the panel instead of a fact buried in a source comment.

#### [HIGH] The void is absent: even sealed, the Deck is a full instrument panel — there is no empty centre to rest in

The Deck has no void at any state. The deck.html render packs the 390px frame edge to edge: 72sp hero span, a 288px rotary wheel, FLOW keycap row, NOW task row, a three-cell proof strip (BLOCK / APPS / TIME) with its 'BIND HELD · THIS VISIT / PROOF: LIVE BIND' seam, the 72dp slide zone, an imprint line and the 52dp rail — the caption notes even the reserved sentence slot and imprint are accounted for. The wheel's centre, the one place a void could sit, is filled with an instrument: a 64px hub disc carrying 8 block wells (deck.html wheel SVG, centre circle r=64). During a sealed session the user who opens Monolith to check the time therefore meets a full dashboard of counts, proofs and controls competing for the attention the session exists to protect. There is no empty, luminous centre anywhere in the six rendered surfaces.

Recommendation: Give the sealed Deck a void: when a session is sealed, collapse the Deck surface to a near-empty centre — background field only, with 'ENDS 10:40' in 15sp mono at the hub's former position and the rail dimmed — and move the proof strip, task row and imprint behind the existing PARK grip for anyone who deliberately pulls them up. The unarmed Deck keeps its wheel and density; the contrast between the busy instrument before the seal and the calm emptiness after it becomes the seal's visible meaning.

#### [HIGH] No spatial Ma anywhere: the Deck fills all 844dp edge-to-edge on a uniform 10-12dp rhythm, so the seal threshold gets the same interval as a list gap

deck.html, faithful to TactileDeckScreen.kt: the 844dp frame is filled edge to edge — 48dp header, instrument card (72sp hero plus the wheel at .height(288.dp), TactileDeckScreen.kt:705), task row, then the pinned stack of 53dp proof strip, 72dp slide zone, 22dp sentence slot and imprint, then the 52dp rail. Vertical rhythm is a mechanical spacedBy(12.dp) / spacedBy(10.dp) (TactileDeckScreen.kt:564,602); no interval anywhere is larger than any other, so the gap before the seal carries the same weight as the gap between two list rows. Ma is spatial as well as temporal: the empty room is what makes the single object visible. An app named Monolith never gives its monolith an empty room — the wheel nearly touches its card on all sides and the screen has no resting place for the eye.

Recommendation: Create one real interval on the Deck: remove the task row's permanent residence under the instrument card (it moves behind the NOW tap it already supports) and let the freed ~90dp stand empty between the wheel card and the pinned strip — no hairline, no label, no tenant. Set that one gap apart in the spacing scale (a single 48dp threshold space used only above the slide zone, nowhere else in the app), so crossing into the arm controls is felt spatially as entering a different room.

#### [MEDIUM] Sequence 5 — Shield and Drawer last, despite being the messiest screens: they are inventories of Steps 1-3, not sources of anything

ShieldMatrixScreen.kt is 1,086 lines and DrawerScreen.kt 949 lines — the temptation is to start where the bulk is. But shield.html is a stack of Step-2 section headers, Step-3 chips and sleds and list rows with 12dp gaps and 100dp bottom padding for rail clearance; drawer.html is the same header/divider/row pattern with no totals, tower or streak anywhere. Nothing on Deck, Airlock, Park or Receipt imports a Shield or Drawer visual decision, while every Shield/Drawer row imports the token, type, header and control decisions above.

Recommendation: Last, rebuild Shield and Drawer as pure assemblies once Steps 1-4 freeze: Shield = FullBleedSectionHeader + Sled rows on an 8dp spacing scale (8/16/24 section gaps, replacing the current uniform 12dp), with the YOUR RULES slip promoted to the top as the summary; Drawer = the same row system plus one Step-4-derived week strip (7 day cells showing stored minutes as a bar, not just date headings). Following Müller-Brockmann's grid-first method for Swiss posters — grid and type system fixed, then pages fall out — this pass should take days, not weeks, precisely because it is sequenced last; done first, it is the most expensive rework in the app.

#### [MEDIUM] The hairline — the app's most repeated element — exists at two weights and three materials depending on the screen

Park rules its rows with a private hairline: 1dp of onBackground at 18% alpha, commented 'print ruling, not a depth line' (ParkDrawer.kt:776-781; park.html). Drawer and Shield rule theirs with outlineVariant — #615B5A at 46% effective alpha, more than twice the weight (DrawerScreen.kt:926; shield.html/drawer.html token notes). Shield then invents a third ruling material inside the same screen: the standing-orders slip binds name to ruling with a dot leader of repeated ' .' characters across a 40dp line (ShieldMatrixScreen.kt:945, :960-967; shield.html). The horizontal rule is the single most repeated graphic element in the app and it changes weight and material at every destination boundary.

Recommendation: Fix one hairline token for the whole product, following Emil Ruder's Typographie, where the Haarlinie is a constant of the system, not a per-page choice: adopt Park's 18% print ruling — it is the most refined of the three and the only one that reads as paper rather than UI chrome — apply it to Drawer's dividers and Shield's app rows, and retire the dot leader from Shield (keep leaders only on the Receipt, where they quote a printed document rather than decorate a settings list). Same paper stock on every screen.

#### [MEDIUM] The Deck's hero is centred in a product that is otherwise entirely flush-left — two alignment axes inside one card

Inside the Deck's own card, two alignment axes fight: the hero readout is centred (Box with Alignment.Center and TextAlign.Center at TactileDeckScreen.kt:657-673; deck.html shows the 72sp '1H 50M' on the card's centre axis) while the eyebrow row directly above it is flush-left/space-between (:603-606) and every element below — FLOW keycap, task row, proof-strip cells — is flush-left on the card's 16dp margin. Shield, Drawer and Park are strict flush-left ledgers with right-aligned values, so the centred hero is not even a Deck-wide system: it is one centred object marooned in a left-aligned product, and tabbing away from the Deck moves the eye's anchor from the centre axis to the left margin and back on every navigation.

Recommendation: Put the readout on the margin, following Ruder's functional typography rule of one alignment per document: keep the wheel graphic centred (it is a dial, and dials are round), but set the hero readout flush-left on the card's existing 16dp padding line, aligned with TOTAL above it and the FLOW row below it, so the card reads as one left-anchored instrument panel — the way a Braun readout sits on the same grid as its keypad labels — instead of a centred poster pasted over a ledger.

#### [MEDIUM] The rail spends its easiest coordinate on its rarest, blankest target: PARK sits under the resting thumb while DECK, the daily home, sits at the far diagonal

deck.html: the 52dp rail spans the full 390dp width with DECK under the cap at far left and a blank 48dp PARK span at far right. MonolithRailView.kt:19-22 files the geometry: recess 350dp, four 73.5dp segments, PARK zone 48dp at the track's end; MonolithRailView.kt:26 sets HEIGHT_DP = 52. For the right-handed one-hand grip Hoober maps, the bottom-right corner is the resting, zero-stretch position and the bottom-left is the far diagonal - so the easiest tap in the entire navigation system is reserved for PARK, the rare machine-state drawer that prints no word at all, while DECK, the daily home the user returns to dozens of times a day, occupies the hardest coordinate. Frequency and ease are perfectly inverted, and the prime position is also the only unlabelled one.

Recommendation: Centre-weight the rail around the thumb's rest position instead of spreading it edge to edge: cluster the daily stops (DECK, TASKS) in the two centre segments that both hands' arcs share, move SHIELD and LEDGER outward, and take PARK off the rail's prime end entirely - the Deck header already carries a GUARD readout at deck.html's header band, so make that the PARK entry and give the freed 48dp back as width to the four real stops. If the five-stop rail must survive unchanged, at minimum swap the order so DECK sits adjacent to the PARK end for right-hand mode and mirrors in left-hand mode.

#### [MEDIUM] Park's two families share one undifferentiated list — a 16dp gap is the only boundary in a nine-row scan

ParkDrawer.kt:338-356 renders WatchItemId.PERMISSIONS (6 rows) then WatchItemId.INTERCEPTORS (3 rows) in one board with the comment at :353-355: 'The doubled gap: 16dp, no hairline, no eyebrow — the family break is whitespace, not a heading.' ParkBoardRow (:653+) gives every row the identical grammar: 10sp PillBadge name plate left, 15sp state word right, 48dp tall. park.html shows .family-gap at 16px against .brow at 48px. So the scan column runs GRANTED / GRANTED / GRANTED / MISSING / GRANTED / GRANTED / OFF / RUNNING / RUNNING, mixing a permission vocabulary with a service vocabulary, separated by a gap one-third the height of the rows it is meant to divide.

Recommendation: Give each family its printed subhead, as Android's own permission manager does with explicit 'Allowed / Not allowed' group headers: print PERMISSIONS and INTERCEPTORS as 10sp ink PillBadge eyebrows at the break, and widen the gap to 32dp with the hairline omitted only there. Per Muller-Brockmann's grid discipline, a group separation must be a clear multiple of the internal leading — here at least 2x the 12dp inter-section rhythm — or proximity groups the nine rows into one list and the two state vocabularies get compared as if they were one scale.

#### [MEDIUM] The foot is ~48dp of invisible furniture: an empty 22dp slot, two sub-visible rules and a tenant that restates APPS as 9+3

The pinned foot reserves height for states the idle user is not in. RefusalSentenceSlot is a fixed 22dp box (MonolithCustomComponents.kt:716, height at :747) that in the healthy state shown in deck.html renders literally nothing (.sentence is an empty 22px div). Below it, ImprintSlot (MonolithCustomComponents.kt:782) stacks a double rule — in deck.html .r1 at rgba(97,91,90,.10) and .r2 at .06, i.e. two hairlines no eye can separate from the background — plus a 6dp spacer, a 20dp tenant box (:863) and a 4dp 'lip zone' that is empty until a session seals. The one line the foot actually shows at idle, '9 WILL SHUT · 3 PEEK', restates the strip's APPS 12 cell (directly above it in the same pinned stack) split into two addends the user must sum to check against the 12.

Recommendation: Collapse the foot to a single 20dp line: keep the imprint tenant text, delete the double rule, the lip zone and the reserved sentence slot. Refusal sentences should replace the strip's BLOCK cell content in place when unhealthy — same address, no reserved dead air — the way a print colophon (Dieter Rams' Vitsoe catalogues) runs one rule and one line of type, total. If APPS is 12 in the strip, the foot must either say something the strip does not or say nothing; printing 9+3 underneath 12 is arithmetic homework, not information.

#### [MEDIUM] List rows take five near-miss heights - 40, 48, 52, 54dp - for the same job, so the finger never learns the rhythm

Same role, five heights: ShieldMatrixScreen.kt:945 SlipLineRow and SlipNoneLine are 40.dp; ParkDrawer.kt:659 ParkBoardRow is 48.dp; ParkDrawer.kt:475 and :544 the sled rows are 52.dp; ShieldMatrixScreen.kt:1083 CatalogueAppRow is 54.dp; DrawerScreen.kt:892 StoredRow is content-sized (~35-40dp from 6.dp vertical padding, 3.dp internal gap, two text lines). The worst offenders are the near-misses: 52 vs 54dp and 40 vs 48dp differ by less than a user can see as intentional, so moving from Shield's catalogue to Park's sled rows feels like the same list drifting off-beat. shield.html (54dp rows), park.html (48dp board, 52dp sleds) and drawer.html (short variable rows) show three different vertical tempos for 'scan a list and tap a row'.

Recommendation: Impose a two-height role system, as Material 3's list spec does (56dp one-line, 72dp two-line - height follows content role, never the screen): 48dp for single-line status and slip rows (raise the slip from 40dp, which is also below comfortable tap size), 56dp for two-line or control-bearing rows (catalogue, routines, stored tasks - retire 52 and 54dp). Every list in the app then beats at one of two tempos and a row's height alone tells the user what kind of row it is.

#### [MEDIUM] Margin generosity runs backwards: rare overlays get 20-24dp of air while the daily working lists are held at 12dp

The three screens used all day share a tight inset - TactileDeckScreen.kt:563, ShieldMatrixScreen.kt:245, DrawerScreen.kt:212 all use padding(horizontal = 12.dp, vertical = 8.dp) - while surfaces seen for seconds get luxury margins: ParkDrawer.kt:302 the Guard sheet scrolls at PaddingValues(start = 20.dp, end = 20.dp); AirlockAndDisarmOverlays.kt:592 the overlay pads 20.dp and its card a further 24.dp (:602), so Airlock body text starts 44dp from the screen edge; ReceiptSheet.kt:71-81 pads 12.dp outside and 20.dp inside the slip. Even the Deck's own header disagrees with its body: MonolithCustomComponents.kt:276 the brand starts at 20.dp while the scroll content below starts at 12.dp. Whitespace currently signals rarity, not importance.

Recommendation: Invert the budget to match Material 3's own logic (16dp standard content margin; larger insets reserved for focused dialogs, not smaller ones for lists): raise Deck, Shield and Drawer content to a single 20dp keyline that matches the header brand at 20.dp and Park's sheet, and pay for it by trimming the Airlock card's inner padding from 24dp to 20dp so its text lands on the same 40dp-effective inset family. One margin, everywhere, with overlays distinguished by elevation and scrim - not by being the only comfortable screens in the app.

#### [MEDIUM] The Drawer gives time no spatial unit: empty days collapse to a heading and missing days vanish, so a week has no readable shape

drawer.html: FRI 30 OCT with one stored task, THU 29 OCT with two, then WED 28 OCT - ILL and MON 26 OCT - FAMILY render as bare headings with nothing beneath, and the render's own note states a day with no stored rows and no declared word renders nothing at all - no heading, no mark. Code: DrawerScreen.kt:212-215 the LazyColumn spaces all items, day groups included, by a flat 12.dp; :849 DayHeading is a Column spacedBy 6.dp with the date text padded top 6.dp; :892 StoredRow adds ~35-40dp per task. A two-task day therefore occupies roughly 110dp, a declared rest day about 23dp, and an unrecorded day 0dp - vertical distance between date headings carries zero information about elapsed time.

Recommendation: Give the calendar a fixed temporal unit, as a paper diary page and Vignelli's calendar grids do - every day gets its block whether it was lived or not: set a 56dp minimum height per day group, print empty and word-only days with a 40dp NONE line at the same height the Shield slip already uses for empty sections (ShieldMatrixScreen.kt:945), and render unrecorded days as a muted heading inside their own block instead of omitting them. The Drawer's scroll then becomes a true picture of the month: dense where life happened, visibly empty where it did not.

### Iconography and illustration — 17 findings (5 critical, 9 high, 3 medium, 0 low)

#### [CRITICAL] Six curios, zero silhouettes: every object has the identical form, so identity is carried entirely by text

data/MonolithModels.kt:492-498 — KineticArtifact has exactly five fields (id, serialCode, name, subtitle, lore), all strings; there is no shape, glyph, colour or geometry field for any object to differ by. ui/screens/DrawerScreen.kt:154-160 admits it in its own comment: 'the kinetic toy VISUALS were never built as views in the shipped app and are not built here.' In design-renders/drawer.html Frame 2, all six cabinet rows are pixel-identical in layout: serial in 10.5sp grey mono, name in 14sp, subtitle in 10.5sp mono, 1px divider — cover the text and Toy 01 is Toy 06. Teenage Engineering's Pocket Operators share one PCB chassis yet each model (PO-12 rhythm, PO-14 sub, PO-20 arcade) carries its own animated LCD graphics that vary by model, so each unit is recognisable from across a desk; LEGO Architecture 21028 New York is recognisable in silhouette alone because each building gets a distinct profile. Monolith's lore even specifies silhouettes — 'Four Concentric Rings' (MonolithModels.kt:817-822), 'A Cube Within A Cube' (:845-850) — that are never drawn anywhere.

Recommendation: Give every curio a form before giving it anything else: add a glyph field to KineticArtifact and draw each object as a small monochrome line emblem (concentric rings for the gyroscope, nested squares for the cube, a decaying spiral for the pendulum) in the same Canvas idiom the tower already uses, shown at ~48dp at the left of each cabinet row and large on its detail page. Apply the silhouette test as the acceptance criterion: with all text masked, each of the six must be identifiable — the standard Pocket Operator LCD characters and LEGO Architecture profiles already meet.

#### [CRITICAL] Shield screenshot reads as a restaurant menu / stock ledger: dot-leader slip, text-only app names and unexplained SHUT/PEEK rulings hide that anything is being blocked

shield.html: the 'YOUR RULES' standing-orders slip (ShieldMatrixScreen.kt:342-384, header at :882) prints each app as an uppercase text name, a leader of roughly ninety literal '.' characters, and a ruling word — INSTAGRAM ........ PEEK, CHROME ........ SHUT — with no app icon, no phone imagery and no sentence saying these apps are blocked during focus. Above it, 'LOADOUT' offers STUDY/WORK/SLEEP caps (ShieldMatrixScreen.kt:282) and below, catalogue rows repeat the same text-only name plus a SHUT/PEEK/OPEN rocker whose three stop words are defined nowhere on screen (tier words at ShieldMatrixScreen.kt:833-834). At screenshot distance the dot leaders, caps and column of names are the visual grammar of a printed price list.

Recommendation: Rebuild the slip as wayfinding, following Otl Aicher's Munich 1972 / airport pictogram system — symbol first, word second, meaning survivable with no shared language: reinstate each app's real launcher icon at 32dp at the left of its rule line, delete the dot leaders, put a one-line header over the section in Atkinson 15sp ('Blocked while you focus'), and gloss the invented stops on their first appearance as 'SHUT = blocked', 'PEEK = 2 minutes only', 'OPEN = allowed', keeping SHUT/PEEK/OPEN as the short labels thereafter. A stranger should be able to point at the Instagram row and say what happens to Instagram.

#### [CRITICAL] Airlock erases the blocked app's icon at the one moment recognition must be instant

AirlockAndDisarmOverlays.kt:550 AirlockInterceptOverlay receives interceptedPackageName/AppName as strings only; at :~620-630 the blocked app is rendered as a single Text(state.interceptedAppName, Atkinson Bold 24sp) above an 88sp countdown — no icon is ever loaded anywhere in the app (zero Icon() composables and zero PackageManager getApplicationIcon calls in main source; CatalogueAppRow at ShieldMatrixScreen.kt:1068-1078 likewise passes only appName into AppRowSledToggleView). Render the blocked app's real launcher icon at 48dp directly above its name, but defused: desaturated to the night palette and over-stamped with the solid SHUT brick, following Nothing OS's monochrome icon treatment, which strips the dopamine colour from social icons while keeping them instantly recognisable. Keep the name, intention and countdown as words underneath. The user should feel 'that exact app, closed' in under half a second, without reading.

#### [CRITICAL] OPEN is encoded as nothing: the one pictogram family Monolith ships breaks Aicher's first law that a sign must be present to mean

BlockitSuitcaseAndSwitchesViews.kt:324-343 draws the catalogue margin glyph: LOCKED = 8dp filled rect (line 335), PEEK_2M = the same rect as a 1.4dp hollow stroke (line 340), OPEN = Unit — literally nothing drawn. The comment at lines 324-328 states the intent ('a shape a tired eye reads without decoding the rocker'), then the shipped reading surface abandons it: SlipLineRow in ShieldMatrixScreen.kt:1014-1055 renders name + ' .'.repeat(90) (line 1023) + the spelled word SHUT/PEEK, with no glyph at all — confirmed in design-renders/shield.html, where every slip line is dots and text while the catalogue rows below carry the brick.

On a 24dp module with a 3dp stroke: SHUT = filled square; PEEK = square outline with its top-right corner cut on the 45° diagonal (an opening, not just an absence of fill); OPEN = square outline completed by a 45° diagonal bar swung clear of the frame — three silhouettes that differ in outline, not only in fill, legible at 16dp and told apart without colour. Draw the same three marks at 16dp in SlipLineRow's margin (replacing nothing else; the word stays as caption) so the fast surface and the editing surface speak one language, and delete any state whose sign is 'nothing'.

#### [CRITICAL] The Airlock — the one surface that must work on a stranger in five seconds, in distress, possibly without the language — is a wall of English prose

AirlockAndDisarmOverlays.kt:606-648 composes the intercept as six stacked English texts: badge 'AIRLOCK INTERCEPTION • LOCKED' (11.5sp, line 606), app name (24sp), session-end line, an 88sp countdown numeral (line 636), 'ACTIVE INTENTION: …' (line 648), then word-chips RETURN TO FOCUS / EMERGENCY PEEK (lines 655-683) and a full price sentence via peekPriceText. design-renders/airlock.html confirms the on-screen result: a prose card whose only non-verbal element is the numeral. #### [HIGH] The Curio cabinet is illustration inverted into prose — six drawn-in-words objects, zero drawings

#### [HIGH] On a light shelf the icon has no silhouette: its edge is a near-white background

The in-app screens prove the brand owns the opposite value: deck.html renders on ink #252323 / #2C2A29 with paper #FAF6F0 text.

#### [HIGH] PARK, the most consequential door in the app, is labelled by two anonymous lines instead of its name

The rail's PARK zone — the only door to the Guard board, the FIX key and every permission state — is labelled by ornament alone: two vertical lines 4dp apart and 14dp tall (the 'notch grip'), whose ink merely deepens from 35% to 70% alpha as the cap enters (MonolithRailView.kt:228-245). The governing comment bans the alternative outright: the zone 'prints NO word ever, because PARK is where the machine's own state lives' (MonolithRailView.kt:76-88). In deck.html:257 the zone renders as the empty 48dp span after LEDGER. Kinneir & Calvert's UK wayfinding and every labelled tab bar (iOS, Material) share one rule the rail breaks: a destination is named in words; a symbol may accompany a name, never replace it for a place the user must find unaided.

Keep the alpha-deepening as a progress cue for the drag, but the word must be present at rest, before any cap movement teaches it.

#### [HIGH] Every 'witness' and 'guard' glyph in the design system counts machines: GUARD 4/4 tallies permissions and the proof seam certifies a bind, while the one presence-shaped visual Monolith owns — the hub's filled/hollow wells — is spent on study blocks

deck.html header and proof strip: the Deck's status language is 'GUARD 4/4' and the seam prints 'BIND HELD · THIS VISIT' / 'PROOF: LIVE BIND'. GuardLine.kt:13-14,39 defines that count precisely — GUARD {n}/4 counts four machine permissions ('WHOLE: GUARD 4/4'). Meanwhile the wheel hub already has a silent presence geometry — 8 wells, filled or hollow (deck.html hub: 2 of 8 filled) — that reads at a glance without a single word. No avatar, no status text, no last-seen timestamp: one dot that is either lit or not, in the visual language the Deck already speaks, matching Focusmate's speak-only-at-the-edges discipline.

#### [HIGH] The one glyph system Monolith has encodes its third state as nothing

BlockitSuitcaseAndSwitchesViews.kt:324-327 documents the app's only true glyph system verbatim: 'a solid brick for SHUT, the same brick hollow for PEEK, nothing for OPEN'; the drawing code at :330-345 draws a filled rect for LOCKED, a stroked rect for PEEK_2M and Unit (nothing) for OPEN. shield.html catalogue rows confirm it visually: OPEN apps (Phone, Spotify, WhatsApp) carry a blank margin indistinguishable from a row whose rule failed to load, was never decided, or is mid-sync.

Recommendation: Absence can never be a category — Otl Aicher's Munich 1972 pictogram system gives every class of thing its own mark precisely because a blank reads as 'no information', not as a state. Complete the brick family so fill AND shape both vary: SHUT stays the solid square, PEEK becomes the half-filled square (left half inked — literally half-open, and distinct from hollow at 8dp), OPEN becomes a hollow circle of the same 8dp footprint. Three shapes, scannable in peripheral vision down a 50-row catalogue, no new visual vocabulary invented.

#### [HIGH] Primary navigation is four jargon words with no symbol anchor to learn

MonolithRailView.kt:34 WORDS = listOf(DECK, SHIELD, TASKS, LEDGER) and :282 canvas.drawText(WORDS[i]) are the entire navigation iconography; deck.html rail shows four 10sp mono words in a 44dp recess plus a blank 48dp PARK zone. There is no mark a thumb or eye can learn — position is the only memory cue, and the words themselves are house jargon (a first-time user must read and decode 'LEDGER' to learn it means receipts/history).

Recommendation: Do not replace the words — anchor them. Add one 14dp geometric mark above/left of each word, drawn on an Aicher-style grid from shapes the app already owns: DECK = the wheel arc, SHIELD = the solid brick, TASKS = three ruled lines with one ticked, LEDGER = stacked ruled lines. Material 3's navigation bar pairs icon with label for exactly this reason: the icon carries repeat navigation pre-attentively, the label carries first-time meaning. After a week the marks alone should navigate; the words become captions, which is what Teenage Engineering's OP-1 screen icons do beside their labels.

#### [HIGH] Curios are written pictures: six objects described in prose and never drawn

MonolithModels.kt:799-848 CurioCatalog writes six purely visual objects — Harmonic Loop lore 'Two waves of different pitch, drawn against each other until the line closes into a knot of light' (:813), Brass Gyroscope 'Four brass rings nested one inside the next' (:820), String Prism (:827), Pocket Planetarium (:834), Sand Pendulum (:841), The Monolith Cube 'Sixteen vertices, two cubes, one held inside the other' (:848) — yet DrawerScreen.kt cabinet rows (:740, :778) render only serial, name, subtitle and the word FORGED. drawer.html frame 2 (Cabinet) confirms: six text rows and a rule line; the collectible the user earned is described, never shown.

Every curio in the catalogue is a geometric construction — concentric rings, a cube inside a cube, a decaying spiral, two orbiting points — drawable as a 40dp single-weight line diagram with the same Canvas primitives and ink tokens BlockitCoreViews.kt already uses for the wheel. Show the line drawing left of the name in the Cabinet, FORGED objects in full ink, unforged in outline-grey silhouette so the collection reads as a set to complete. This is the Playdate/Teenage Engineering lesson: a reward object must be an object. The lore then becomes a caption under a picture instead of a substitute for one.

#### [HIGH] SEAL, PEEK and HOLD have no signs: a concrete three-sign family, built from one ring, that the current text-only system needs

The three core state-words are currently carried by text alone everywhere they matter most: the receipt prints 'HELD 12 APPS · 3 SITES' as a mono text line (ReceiptSheet.kt:131) with no stamp or mark; the Airlock prints its three withheld-peek states as three full sentences — peekCooldownPrint, 'A PEEK IS ALREADY RUNNING', 'PEEK IS OFF' (AirlockAndDisarmOverlays.kt:692-708); the persistent shield notification reuses the full-colour launcher art as its small icon instead of a seal silhouette (MonolithShieldService.kt:224). SEAL, the verb the whole product is named around, has no glyph anywhere in the repo.

Recommendation: Draw the family from one primitive, the ring, on the 24-unit grid with a 3-unit stroke: SEALED = a continuous ring closed by a horizontal diameter bar (a gate shut and witnessed); PEEK = the identical ring broken by a 45° gap at upper-right, with a short diagonal sight-bar crossing the gap — same body, one structural break, so 'peek' reads as 'seal, opened a crack' without a word; HELD = the ring with a filled centre square (contents detained inside the vessel). All three differ in silhouette, survive pure monochrome, and stay distinct at 16dp. Ship them at exactly four addresses: 48dp hero in the Airlock, the notification small icon (seal ring), a 24dp stamp beside the receipt's HELD line, and the slip margin — nowhere else until each placement passes the cover-the-text test.

#### [HIGH] Every tower brick is drawn whole: the brick vocabulary has no cracked-and-mended brick, so partial and recovered days are forged as perfect

BlockitTowerFadersAndCatalogViews.kt:111-126: bricks have exactly two visual states — 'Solid laid brick in colorPrimary ink' and the accent 'Crown brick' for the newest. TowerStreakView takes only totalBricksCount (line 26), a bare count with no per-day outcome, so a PARTIAL day (MonolithRepository.kt:1034) or a day resumed after a miss lays either an identical perfect brick or none — the tower's history is survivorship-only and every brick pretends it was whole.

Recommendation: Give TowerStreakView a third brick type driven by per-day judgement: a mended brick drawn as two ink halves split by a 2dp accent seam, laid for PARTIAL days and for the first ATTENDED day after a MISSED day. The tower then visibly grows taller because of its cracks, and tapping a mended brick shows that day's receipt.

#### [MEDIUM] Full-bleed near-white tile has no edge: the icon dissolves into light wallpapers and light app drawers

ic_launcher_background.xml:9-10 fills the entire 108x108dp background layer edge-to-edge with #F7F3EA, a near-white warm cream (relative luminance ~0.90). The adaptive background is the tile itself: on a light wallpaper, a white app drawer, or a light launcher theme there is no darker edge, outline or shadow intrinsic to the artwork to separate tile from ground, so the icon's outer boundary dissolves and only the inner blue circle floats, apparently borderless and smaller than its neighbours. Every surrounding icon with a saturated or dark full-bleed ground keeps its silhouette in the same grid; Monolith's tile edge exists only when the wallpaper happens to be dark.

Recommendation: Give the front door a wallpaper-proof silhouette: make the background layer full-bleed near-black (NightColorBackground #171412 or TokenColorPrimary #252323, as the legacy PNG mark already does with its black field and cream frame), so the tile holds its edge on white, photographic and dark wallpapers alike — the discipline Nothing OS (black/red) and Spotify (black on saturated green) apply so the tile never depends on what is behind it. Test the final icon on pure-white, mid-grey and photographic wallpapers at 48dp before accepting it.

#### [MEDIUM] The gnomon is drawn over the hub, pierces the ring, and is a 1.8dp hairline at real launcher size

In ic_launcher_foreground.xml the black gnomon stem (lines 23-25: pathData M52,29 L56,29 L56,54 L52,54) is drawn last, on top of everything, and is geometrically wrong for a dial hand: it starts at y=29, above the dial plate's top edge (plate spans y=32-76, line 14), so it pierces the ultramarine ring band (y=26-32, line 10) and slices through the canary sector before ending exactly at the centre, half-buried in the crimson hub (hub spans y=44-64, line 22) which was drawn before it — the hub should cap the hand, not be cut by it. It is also 4dp wide on a 108dp canvas: ~1.8dp at a 48dp launcher rendering, an anti-aliased grey hairline rather than a black pointer, so the one element meant to say 'instrument' is the first element to disappear.

Recommendation: Redraw the hand to clockmaking rules, Braun wall-clock style: shorten the stem so it starts at the dial's inner edge (y=32) and never crosses the ring, widen it to at least 6dp so it survives at 48dp, counterweight or terminate it cleanly, and reverse the z-order so the hub disc is drawn last, capping the stem's base. If the stem cannot be made legible at launcher size, delete it and let the canary sector alone act as the pointer — one readable gesture beats a hairline that reads as a crack in the dial.

#### [MEDIUM] The Guard board's health can only be read, never seen

ParkDrawer.kt:342-382 prints every guard state as a word — PermPrint GRANTED/MISSING (:342-343) and InterceptorState RUNNING/OFF (:360) in Atkinson Bold 15sp, differentiated only by ink vs secondary grey. park.html shows the result: nine rows (ACCESSIBILITY…NOTIFICATIONS) that can only be audited by reading each word serially; from arm's length, in a hurry, or in peripheral vision the board's health is invisible — there is no shape or count of failures to catch the eye.

Recommendation: Give the board a pre-attentive layer using the catalogue's own brick language, the way Braun instruments and aircraft annunciator panels pair a lamp/shape with a caption: a 8dp solid square before each granted/running row, a hollow square with an ink diagonal before each missing/off row, aligned in one column. Keep the words as the precise record, but let health be a shape-scan: all solid = safe. Add the same two marks to the header's GUARD n/4 so the Deck's top band shows a broken shape, not just a smaller fraction, when a permission lapses.

### Motion and animation — 22 findings (3 critical, 14 high, 5 medium, 0 low)

#### [CRITICAL] The payoff frame is silent: the whole finish score plays during the frozen detention, and the receipt arrives mute 600-900ms after the last sound

MonolithViewModel.kt:1243-1260 fires the entire sonic score against E0 — seat knock at E0, completion pulse at E700, knock pair at E880 (+90ms) — while ReceiptState.kt:202-213 (Detention) does not issue the receipt until E1480-E1800, and emitReceipt() in MonolithViewModel.kt arms only the sled gate: no sound or haptic call exists at issuance. Worse, the issuance time is not a chosen beat: Detention.receiptAtMs derives it from pawlLiftMs, the frame the shield service happened to confirm stopped (ReceiptState.kt:209-213), so the reveal lands whenever plumbing finishes. receipt.html Frame 3 confirms the visual during all the sound: a frozen Deck frame, hero at 00:00. Apple Watch does the opposite: the ring-close sparkler/firework animation and its tone fire on the same frame the ring visually closes — sound and image are one event, scaled single-ring vs all-three.

Recommendation: Re-score the finish around issuance, not E0: keep one low settle knock at E0, then move the completion pulse to the exact receipt-issue frame and add a single haptic tick synchronised with the slip's first visible frame, so the payoff moment itself speaks. Pin issuance to a fixed dramatic offset (e.g. E1600) and let the shield-stop confirmation gate only the faulted branch, never the clean reveal's timing.

#### [CRITICAL] A 1.8-second engineered detention ends in a 280ms crossfade: the unveiling has no act in it

Detention is engineered to the millisecond: the Deck freezes on the session's last frame (ui/screens/TactileDeckScreen.kt:274 heldFinish) and the receipt cannot issue before E1480 and no later than E1800 (data/ReceiptState.kt:201-213). What that 1.5-1.8s of held breath buys is a plain crossfade: ReceiptSheet enters with fadeIn(MonolithCurves.specC()) — a 280ms tween (ui/components/ReceiptSheet.kt:60-63; ui/theme/MonolithCurves.kt:27,72) — of a slip that is, by its own header comment, 'settled and still: it never re-strikes, never animates its numbers' (ReceiptSheet.kt:43-44). Every line, the № and the verdict exist at full opacity from frame one; nothing feeds, prints, strikes or lands. The asymmetry is internal and damning: session START gets a named 1050ms three-phase cinematic (DEPARTURE/RECESSION/SETTLE vertigo, MonolithCurves.kt:32) while session COMPLETION — the moment the user earned — gets the same generic fade used for sheet dismissal anywhere. Render receipt.html frame 3 shows the frozen Deck and frame 1 the finished slip; there is no frame between them because the app designs none. Duolingo's lesson-complete sequence stages its reveal (ring draws itself, score ticks up, stars pop, 'NEW BEST!' badge drops, stat cards stagger in) so anticipation resolves in visible acts; Monolith builds the anticipation and skips the acts.

Recommendation: Spend the detention on a visible unveiling instead of a freeze: during E1200-E1480 keep the held frame but add one legible sign of manufacture (the slip's leading edge rising 12dp from the screen's bottom edge, printer-mouth style). At issuance, reveal the slip with a bottom-up clip wipe at printer speed (~90ms per line, lines appearing in print order: title/№, ARMED, ENDED, HELD, deflections, footer last), and let the outcome stamp (see stamp finding) strike 120ms after the last line. Keep the no-count-up, no-confetti discipline — the motion should be mechanical print, not celebration confetti — but a receipt must be seen to be printed.

#### [CRITICAL] The timing vocabulary is fiction: five durations on paper, twenty-plus in the product, three tokens nobody spends

MonolithCurves.kt:13-14 declares durations 'strictly chosen from {180, 260, 280, 420, 520} ms', but MonolithCurves.kt:22-32 itself defines nine values (110, 140, 180, 250, 260, 280, 420, 520, 1050) and MonolithKin in the same file (MonolithCurves.kt:85-103) adds 90, 120, 150, 160, 240 and 180+60-per-stop. Worse, DURATION_110, DURATION_250 and DURATION_520 have zero call sites anywhere in app/src/main/java — the 110ms value is spent as a raw literal instead (MonolithCustomComponents.kt:826, tween(110)). Off-book literals the registry never names: 340ms two-stop rocker throw (BlockitSuitcaseAndSwitchesViews.kt:294), 400ms ink settle (MonolithCustomComponents.kt:829 — 420 is the token, 400 is not), and a 650ms sled return whose own comment boasts it is 'never tokenised' (MonolithCurves.kt:44-47; spent at BlockitCoreViews.kt:1632). Choreography delays double as hidden durations: 300ms rest + 280ms exit in ShieldMatrixScreen.kt:983-1000, 500ms stability beat + 120ms hold in MonolithCustomComponents.kt:738-741.

Recommendation: Delete the fiction and enforce a real scale, following Material 3's token discipline (16 durations on a strict 50ms grid: short 50-200, medium 250-400, long 450-600 — the grid, not the count, is the point). Cut Monolith to five enforced tokens — micro 90, seat 180, travel 260, sheet 320, ceremony 1050 (seal only) — migrate every literal (340→travel scaled by stops, 400→sheet, 650→a named ceremony token or kill it), delete dead DURATION_250/520, spend DURATION_110 via its token, and add a lint/Detekt rule banning raw millisecond literals and bare tween() calls outside MonolithCurves.kt so the vocabulary cannot silently regrow.

#### [HIGH] Repair order #4: motion budget is inverted — 1050ms for the rare seal ceremony, 120ms and 14dp for the navigation performed dozens of times a day

MonolithCurves.kt:32 reserves the system's longest duration, DURATION_1050, for the seal-shot ceremony, while MonolithKin (MonolithCurves.kt:~90-100) gives everyday tab navigation a 120ms fade-out, a 240ms fade-in and a 14dp translation, and MonolithCurves.kt:66-73 defines all Compose motion as three tween specs (specA 260ms, specB 420ms, specC 280ms) with no spring and no shared-element transition anywhere. In the renders this reads as: screens swap almost invisibly dozens of times a day, and the one lavish animation is the transition the user watches least often and cannot act during.

Recommendation: Priority 4 — reallocate the motion budget from ceremony to continuity, following Material 3 motion guidance that duration and easing scale with how much of the screen moves and how often the transition repeats: cut the seal shot to ≤600ms, and spend the savings on (a) an emphasized-easing 300-350ms tab transition with the rail cap and content moving as one system, and (b) one shared-element move — the Deck wheel's chosen duration carrying into the session screen's elapsed numeral — so users can track where they are. This outranks new signature moments: a hundredth identical tab swap teaches the spatial model; a longer seal teaches nothing after the third viewing.

#### [HIGH] The finish is scored in sound but not in pictures: E0/E700/E880 beats play over a static freeze, then the receipt fades in off-beat

MonolithViewModel.kt onFinishE0 scores the finish in three audible beats fired against e0Mono: playSeatKnock at E0, playCompletionPulse at E700 (skipped only for shield-gap), playSeatKnock pair at E880/+90ms. No visual is keyed to any of them: TactileDeckScreen.kt heldFinish holds a static frame, and ReceiptSheet.kt:43-62 documents the reveal as 'the slip settled and still: it never re-strikes, never animates its numbers', entering via AnimatedVisibility(visible = true, enter = fadeIn(MonolithCurves.specC())) — a 280ms opacity fade (MonolithCurves.kt:72-73) of a bottom-anchored card with no rise, no travel from the Deck's imprint/proof-strip zone it supposedly prints from (receipt.html Frame 1 vs Frame 3: the slip appears at the bottom of a different, day-lit room).

Recommendation: Choreograph the picture to the score that already exists: at E0 the frozen hero locks (knock), at E700 the hero flips to the elapsed total / the imprint strikes (pulse), at E880 the slip rises 24dp from the pinned stack's address into place on specB as the knock pair lands — sound and image arriving as one event per beat. Following Duolingo's lesson-complete: the chime, the XP bar fill and the total tally are one synchronised gesture, so the ear and eye confirm the same achievement at the same instant.

#### [HIGH] The seal shot's blur is inverted depth of field: it blurs the subject and leaves the room sharp

The seal shot applies its blur to the hero card itself — the card containing the running readout and the wheel: blurDp = 6·4·blurT·(1−blurT) peaking at 6dp, on the same Modifier chain as the card's scale/translation (TactileDeckScreen.kt:584-597), driven by a separately eased blurT (TactileDeckScreen.kt:248-256; MonolithCurves.kt:57-62). Everything outside the card — rail, header, deck ground — stays pixel-sharp, so the claimed effect ('the room recedes') is spatially backwards: the subject smears while the room stays in focus. The blur is also double-shaped (a cubic-bezier easing fed into a parabola), so its peak lands early in the shot, not at the transform's mid-point the comment intends. Every reference use of blur in interface and cinema — iOS materials blurring the content behind a presented sheet, a rack focus throwing the background out — sharpens the subject by blurring its surroundings, never the reverse.

Recommendation: Invert the depth of field: keep the hero card tack-sharp through its scale-and-rise, and blur/dim everything behind it (deck ground, strip, rail) by up to 6dp over the same 1050ms, clearing at settle. If only one layer can afford the effect, drop the blur entirely — scale 0.94 + rise 10dp already reads as recession; a blurred subject only reads as a rendering fault.

#### [HIGH] The 'vertigo' shot is inverted: it blurs and shrinks the subject itself while the room stays sharp - the opposite of the Hitchcock shot it is named after

TactileDeckScreen.kt:584-596 attaches graphicsLayer scale (1 - 0.06*vt) and Modifier.blur to the hero card Column itself - the card that contains the 72sp hero readout and the wheel (the one-object composition visible in design-renders/deck.html). The blur term peaks at 6dp mid-shot (line 589: 6f * 4f * blurT * (1 - blurT)), i.e. for roughly the middle 500ms of the 1050ms shot the number the user just committed to is deliberately defocused, while everything outside the card - eyebrow ground, scroll column, rail - stays pixel-sharp. MonolithCurves.kt:57-62 names the easings 'Vertigo', after Hitchcock's dolly zoom, but that shot does the exact opposite on both axes: the subject holds its size and stays in focus while the background warps behind it. Monolith shrinks its subject by 6% and blurs it, and warps nothing behind it.

Recommendation: Invert the depth assignment to match the reference the code already cites: keep the hero card - readout and wheel - at full sharpness for the entire shot, and put the recession on the ground: apply the scale-down and a smaller blur (peak ~4dp) to the Deck content behind/around the card (the scroll column's non-hero sections and the rail), so the instrument reads as the fixed viewpoint and the room recedes, as in Vertigo (1958). If blurring live text is ever retained, cap it at 2dp and exclude the readout by splitting the card into two layers - ornament (wheel socket, borders) may blur, print (numerals, eyebrow) may not.

#### [HIGH] One seal shot, three clocks: continuous blur, 50ms-stepped cap shading and a single 400ms ground flip tick at different rates inside the same 1050ms

One 1050ms shot runs on three unrelated clocks. TactileDeckScreen.kt:245-263: vertigoT and blurT are recomputed continuously every frame via withFrameMillis, but exitPhase is quantised as (e / 50L).toInt() - four 50ms steps - and pushed to the slide view (line 259), where it drives the cap's accent shading as a 4-entry printed table (BlockitCoreViews.kt:1775, tokAccentShaded phases x1/x0.75/x0.50/terminal). A third element, the ground's night step, fires as a single binary jump at e >= 400 (line 255). On a 120Hz phone the blur is sampled ~126 times while the screen's one orange object changes colour exactly 4 times and the ground flips once: the eye reads the stepped elements as stutter inside an otherwise fluid shot, because the mismatch is inside one gesture, not between screens.

Recommendation: Put the whole shot on one clock, the way Apple drives iOS transitions: every property of a single transition is interpolated from the same display-link timestamp, so nothing inside one motion ticks at a different rate. Make the cap shading a continuous colour lerp between the same four table stops sampled by the shot's existing transform easing, and turn the 400ms ground step into a 200ms crossfade centred on 400ms using the same eased t. Keep the printed-table values as the lerp's keyframes so the colour decisions survive; only their sampling changes.

#### [HIGH] Slide-to-seal failure runs on fake physics: the success seat is a true spring integrator, the spring-back is a stock overshoot tween whose overshoot is clamped invisible

BlockitCoreViews.kt:1418-1443 documents the seat as a real physics integrator (accel = 400·(1−x) − 16·v, ω0=20, ζ=0.40, ≤5ms substeps, knock at 0.97 in-step). But the sub-catch release path at :2117-2121 admits in its own comment that 'the shipped spring-back survives for this path alone… and is not unified into the integrator': animateSpringBack (:2359-2380) is a 280ms ValueAnimator with MonolithCurves.MechanicalOvershoot (OvershootInterpolator(1.25), MonolithCurves.kt:49) whose update listener coerces displayed into 0f..1f (:2365) — an overshoot interpolator driving toward 0 overshoots below 0, so the one expressive part of the curve is clipped off and the cap simply decelerates into the wall and sticks. The refusal is stiffer still: startRefusal freezes the cap in REFUSAL_HOLD for a flat 300ms before returning it. deck.html:47-56 shows the resting cap with a hard 2.5px drop shadow — the object promises weight the failure motion never performs.

Recommendation: Delete animateSpringBack and run every return — sub-catch release, abort, refusal — through the same Choreographer integrator as the seat, seeded with the finger's actual release velocity and a lower stiffness (ω0≈14, ζ≈0.55) so failure reads as the same object losing energy, not a different animation. Replace the refusal's 300ms freeze with iOS Slide to Unlock's failure lesson: immediate elastic return plus one shimmer sweep across the 'SLIDE OR TAP TO START' track words as the retry hint. Failure is the teaching moment; it must get the best physics, not the leftover tween.

#### [HIGH] One verb, five bodies: 'go home uncommitted' bounces, glides, creeps or overshoots depending on which code path refuses you

One user meaning — 'this did not commit, go home' — is implemented four incompatible ways within a single file, BlockitCoreViews.kt. The seat spring integrates accel = 400·(1−x) − 16·v (ω0=20, ζ=0.40, deliberately bouncy) at BlockitCoreViews.kt:2308-2335 (stepSeat). The abort return in the same integrator uses ω0=22, ζ=0.90 (accel = 484·(0−x) − 39.6·v, BlockitCoreViews.kt:2243-2265) — almost critically damped, no bounce. The refusal return uses a third spring, stiffness 260 / damping 25.2 (ζ≈0.78, '~320ms', BlockitCoreViews.kt:2288-2305), explicitly called 'the app's one not-committed voice' — while the abort path, which means the same thing, does not use it. A fourth path abandons physics entirely: animateSpringBack runs a 280ms ValueAnimator on MechanicalOvershoot (OvershootInterpolator 1.25, MonolithCurves.kt:49) at BlockitCoreViews.kt:2359-2363. The finished session's sled return is a fifth feel: a 650ms bezier glide on ReturnHome (BlockitCoreViews.kt:1617-1633). The wheel adds a sixth: its well spring holds ζ=0.38 with ω0 switching 21 vs 23.5 by target (BlockitCoreViews.kt:1222-1228).

Recommendation: Give 'not committed' exactly one body, following Apple's Designing Fluid Interfaces rule: one spring family parameterised by damping + response, velocity inherited at handoff, damping 1.0 for functional returns and bounce reserved for genuine throws. Pick the refusal spring (stiffness 260, ζ≈0.78) as the canonical return spring, re-express the abort return, the MechanicalOvershoot spring-back and the 650ms ReturnHome glide as that same spring (the return-home case keeps a longer response, not a different curve species), and delete MechanicalOvershoot from the registry. The wheel's ζ=0.38 detent spring may stay — detents are a different verb — but document it as the sole exception.

#### [HIGH] Overlay entrances are a 280-vs-420 lottery and every exit ignores the enter/exit pairing the curves were stolen from

Five full-screen overlays in one file split into two entrance speeds with no stated rule: the desk clock and the Airlock intercept enter with fadeIn(specB()) = 420ms (AirlockAndDisarmOverlays.kt:80, :559) while the held-notifications digest, the permission primer and the disarm challenge enter with fadeIn(specC()) = 280ms (AirlockAndDisarmOverlays.kt:308, :482, :742) — yet all five exit identically with fadeOut(specA()) = 260ms (AirlockAndDisarmOverlays.kt:81, :309, :483, :560, :743), and ReceiptSheet.kt:62-63 repeats the 280-in / 260-out pairing. The pairing is also inverted against the source the curves were copied from: MonolithCurves.kt:55-64 lifts Material 3's values verbatim — EasingB (0.05, 0.7, 0.1, 1.0) is M3 emphasized-decelerate (for entrances) and EasingC (0.3, 0.0, 0.8, 0.15) is M3 emphasized-accelerate (for exits) — but Monolith spends the accelerate curve on entrances (specC fadeIns above) and the plain standard curve, not the accelerate curve, on every exit. PARK's FIX key completes the chaos: it enters using the CLOSE duration, expandVertically(tween(DRAWER_CLOSE_MS, EasingSeat)) at ParkDrawer.kt:417, so an appearance is timed by a constant named for disappearance.

Recommendation: Impose M3's actual pairing law instead of just its numbers: entrances decelerate and may be longer, exits accelerate and must be shorter. One overlay spec for all five surfaces plus the receipt: enter fadeIn 300ms on EasingB (emphasized-decelerate — its correct job), exit fadeOut 180ms on EasingC (emphasized-accelerate — its correct job); the Airlock intercept, the surface that must win a race against temptation, enters fastest of all at 200ms. Rename the PARK FIX-key entrance to use DRAWER_OPEN_MS so no entrance ever spends a close constant again, and forbid specA as an exit spec.

#### [HIGH] Single moments run on split clocks: the Strike lands at 110ms, 240ms and 400ms simultaneously, and the seal shot ticks in 50ms steps

The seal's imprint 'Strike' — perceptually one stamp — runs on three unsynchronised clocks with three different curves: scale settles in 110ms on a one-off CubicBezierEasing(0.9f, 0f, 1f, 0.4f) that exists nowhere else in the app (MonolithCustomComponents.kt:826), ink alpha settles in 400ms on EasingA from the same start frame (MonolithCustomComponents.kt:829, its own comment admits 'the settle ends at 400'), and the lip fades out over 240ms on tween(240) with no easing argument at all (MonolithCustomComponents.kt:843) — an omitted easing silently imports Compose's default FastOutSlowIn curve, a curve the Monolith registry never declares; the hand-back fade does the same at tween(90) (MonolithCustomComponents.kt:725-727). The 1050ms seal shot repeats the pattern at full-screen scale: transform and blur run the same 1050ms span on two unrelated beziers (VertigoTransformEasing vs VertigoBlurEasing, MonolithCurves.kt:61-62, driven at TactileDeckScreen.kt:247-253) while the ground colour steps as a hard cut at t=400 with no transition (TactileDeckScreen.kt:263-266) and the exit phase is quantised into 50ms steps (TactileDeckScreen.kt:255-257), so the app's signature moment visibly ticks in 50ms increments underneath two smooth curves.

Recommendation: One moment, one clock — the discipline Things 3 and Apple's keynote transitions apply: drive each choreographed moment from a single Animatable progress value and derive every property from it. Rebuild the Strike as one 240ms EasingA progress driving scale 1.04→1.0 in its first 45% and ink 0.82→0.88 across the full span, lip included; ban easing-less tween() outright (explicit easing on all three current default sites). For the seal shot, derive blur from the same eased progress as the transform (blur = f(vertigoT), not a second easing), replace the t=400 ground hard-cut with a 120ms crossfade inside the same clock, and drop the 50ms phase quantisation so exit phases interpolate continuously.

#### [HIGH] The filed motion system is a fiction: 15+ durations and 12 easings ship under a header claiming 5 durations and 3 curves

MonolithCurves.kt:14-18 declares durations 'strictly chosen from { 180, 260, 280, 420, 520 } ms', but the shipped app runs 45ms (hub dip, BlockitCoreViews.kt:465), 90ms (MonolithCustomComponents.kt:727), 110/400ms (imprint settle, MonolithCustomComponents.kt:826-829), 120ms (MainActivity.kt tab fade-out via MonolithKin.TAB_FADE_OUT_MS), 140/250ms (slide mesh, MonolithCurves.kt:24-27 amendments), 160ms (hub return, BlockitCoreViews.kt:483; drawer close, MonolithKin:91), 240ms (tab-in, MonolithKin:97; lip fade, MonolithCustomComponents.kt:843), 340ms (two-stop rocker throw, BlockitSuitcaseAndSwitchesViews.kt:294), 650ms (sled return, BlockitCoreViews.kt:1631) and 1050ms (seal shot). The 650 is worse than unlisted: MonolithCurves.kt:44-47 files it as 'a literal at the animator, never tokenised' — an anti-token by policy. Easings sprawl the same way: EasingA/B/C (MonolithCurves.kt:55-64), EasingThrow (MonolithCurves.kt:108), HubPressDip, HubSeatReturn, ReturnHome, VertigoTransformEasing, VertigoBlurEasing, MechanicalOvershoot, MechanicalAnticipateOvershoot, plus a one-off CubicBezierEasing(0.9f,0f,1f,0.4f) invented inline at MonolithCustomComponents.kt:826, plus bare tween() calls at MonolithCustomComponents.kt:727 and :843 that silently import the framework default easing as a twelfth curve. Each curve also exists twice — PathInterpolator for Views, CubicBezierEasing for Compose (MonolithCurves.kt:34-64) — hand-synced copies that can drift. The renders confirm the end state this produces: deck.html and shield.html are entirely static frames with no motion language visible between any two surfaces.

Recommendation: Collapse to a stateable system, the way Material 3's motion tokens fit on one card (one emphasized curve — which is literally Monolith's own EasingA, cubic-bezier(0.2,0,0,1) — plus a fixed duration scale): keep four named curves only (Seat = EasingA, Throw, Press, and Vertigo reserved solely for the seal), publish one duration scale {90, 160, 260, 280, 420, 650, 1050} with 650 tokenised as DURATION_650, delete EasingB/EasingC or write the one sentence each that justifies it, ban bare tween() and inline CubicBezierEasing in components, and generate the View PathInterpolator and Compose Easing from the same float constants so the two stacks cannot drift.

#### [HIGH] Two motion physics in one app: the Views integrate springs and mass, the Compose surfaces run distance-blind tweens

The custom Views run real physics: the wheel's well spring is integrated per unit mass with zeta held at 0.38 (BlockitCoreViews.kt:1222-1229) and its coast decays on a load-dependent tau (BlockitCoreViews.kt:538-539); the slide's seat is a Choreographer integrator, spring accel 400*(1-x) - 16*v, omega0=20, zeta=0.40 (BlockitCoreViews.kt:1420-1427). Every Compose surface instead runs fixed tweens with no velocity and no distance law: ShieldCapSelector.kt:85-88 animates the tier cap with specA(260) whether it crosses one cell or two, so a two-cell jump visibly glides at half the speed of a one-cell jump. Monolith's own View code proves the author knows the correct law and applies it there: the rail cap scales 180ms + 60ms per stop crossed (MonolithCurves.kt:85-87, used in MonolithRailView.kt:176) and the tier rocker scales 260ms for one stop, 340ms for two (BlockitSuitcaseAndSwitchesViews.kt:294). Same product, same 'mechanical' brand claim, two contradictory answers to how fast a cap may travel — and the Compose answer is the one on the Shield screen users configure most.

Recommendation: Give every travelling cap one speed law, following Material 3 Expressive's move to spring tokens (stiffness/damping pairs that carry velocity and retarget mid-flight instead of restarting a fixed tween): convert ShieldCapSelector's cap to a spring spec, or at minimum apply the rail's own distance law (base + per-stop) so one stop and two stops move at the same speed. Then state the law once in MonolithKin — stops-per-second for caps, zeta/stiffness for springs — and audit every animate*AsState in Compose against it.

#### [HIGH] All motion is spent on transitions and none on the session itself: the longest state in the app is a frozen frame

There is not one ambient animation in the app: grep finds zero rememberInfiniteTransition / infiniteTransition usages across app/src/main. During a running session — the state the app exists for, up to 180 minutes times 8 blocks — the Deck's readout is displaySeconds rendered as a formatted string (TactileDeckScreen.kt, primaryReadout derived from activeSession.remainingSeconds/elapsedSeconds), so the digits swap once per second with no transition, and progressFraction is recomputed from whole seconds, stepping silently. At the finish the design makes the stillness explicit: heldFinish renders 'the session's last frame — frozen readout, frozen progress… and nothing else moves' (TactileDeckScreen.kt held-frame block). Meanwhile the entire motion budget is spent on entering and leaving states: a 1050ms seal shot (TactileDeckScreen.kt:243-268) and a 650ms sled return (BlockitCoreViews.kt:1631). deck.html shows the consequence: a handsome static instrument panel with nothing that breathes. A user glancing at the phone mid-session cannot tell a live session from a screenshot of one.

Recommendation: Spend a small, deliberate ambient budget on the running state only, the way Teenage Engineering's OP-1 keeps its virtual tape reels turning while recording — motion as proof of life, not decoration: interpolate the session progress hairline continuously between seconds (sub-second, Seat curve, no bounce), and give the readout's colon a 1Hz opacity pulse synced to the second tick. Everything else stays print-still, which makes the two moving elements read as the session's heartbeat. Add nothing ambient to idle, setup or receipt states.

#### [HIGH] The motion rulebook exempts itself in its own header: 'strictly chosen' durations beside a 650ms literal that is 'never tokenised'

ui/theme/MonolithCurves.kt:14 declares durations 'strictly chosen from { 180, 260, 280, 420, 520 } ms', then the same file spends DURATION_1050 (:32) and, at :46, documents the sled return's 650ms as 'a literal at the animator, never tokenised, no Compose twin'; MonolithKin below it adds 90/120/150/160/240ms constants while its header (:80) insists 'No chrome motion exists outside these names'. Rams' eighth principle — thorough down to the last detail, nothing arbitrary or left to chance, care as respect for the user — is failed not by any single duration but by the pattern: the rulebook's exceptions are granted by comment, in the same breath as the rule, so the vocabulary is a plaque rather than a constraint and any future duration can join by writing itself an amendment.

Recommendation: Make the set enforceable or stop printing it: add a unit test that walks MonolithCurves and MonolithKin constants plus animator call sites and fails on any duration outside the token set; tokenise the sled return as DURATION_650 with a Compose tween twin, or change the animator to the existing 520 and delete the literal. Rewrite the MonolithCurves header to list the true closed set (including 1050 and 650) in one place — one rulebook, no amendments written as asides.

#### [HIGH] Closing gets no ceremony at all: the return home is engineered silence and the receipt exits as a swatted dialog

The Beosound 9000's motorised lid 'opens and closes in the same uniform movement' — closing receives the same engineering as opening. Monolith lavishes 1,050ms, a dedicated audio lane and a golden-hashed render on sealing, then designs its un-sealing as absence: BlockitCoreViews.kt:1560-1565 specifies the slide's return home as 'total silence by construction — no fireFeel, no knock, no engine token exists on its path', animated over 650ms in animateReturnHome() (BlockitCoreViews.kt:1617), and ReceiptSheet.kt:61-64 dismisses the slip with a plain fadeOut on any DOWN anywhere on the scrim. The object opens like a ceremony and closes like a dialog being swatted away.

Recommendation: Give the return a closing catch, quieter than the Throw by design: at the return animator's final 60ms, fire one seat-knock at 0.5 gain / 320Hz with the haptic waveform [0,12] at amplitude 110 as the cap seats home — the mirror of the latch knock, not silence. Give the receipt the reverse of its new entrance (slide down 24dp + fade over 260ms on specA) triggered only by a downward drag or the VAULT navigation, not by any stray tap on the scrim.

#### [MEDIUM] The cap comes home as a ghost: the ceremony's protagonist returns automatically, in designed silence, performed by nobody

BlockitCoreViews.kt:1560-1563 specifies the sled return as 'total silence by construction — no fireFeel, no knock, no engine token exists on its path'; animateReturnHome (BlockitCoreViews.kt:1617-1632) runs a fixed 650ms ValueAnimator, and TactileDeckScreen.kt's sled LaunchedEffect (~273-283) triggers it automatically 1,050ms after the receipt publishes — the user neither initiates nor accompanies the unsealing of the very control they drove to seal. Teenage Engineering's TP-7 rocker is symmetric by contrast: press its top edge to fast-forward, its bottom edge to rewind, and the reel answers audibly and visibly in both directions.

Recommendation: Give the return a performer and a voice at reduced rank: after the receipt, leave the cap seated until the user drags it home (the same travel, reversed, with the payload text re-covered as it retreats), ending in a soft dock — one 24ms haptic at amplitude ~120 and a latch click a fifth below the seal's pitch. If an automatic return must remain as a fallback after 30s untouched, it should be visibly labelled as the machine tidying up, not silently substituted for the closing half of the ritual.

#### [MEDIUM] The 3-stop rocker's flick throws away its momentum: velocity is a binary threshold, then a zero-velocity tween takes over

BlockitSuitcaseAndSwitchesViews.kt:470-491: on release the rocker's VelocityTracker output is reduced to a sign test against FLICK_DP_PER_SEC = 800dp/s (:511) — above it, jump to the far stop; below it, snap to nearest. commitTo (:289-300) then runs animateRockerTo, a fixed 260ms (one stop) or 340ms (two stops) CurveA ValueAnimator that starts from zero velocity regardless of how fast the finger was moving. A violent flick and a slow deliberate drag released at the same position produce byte-identical motion; the code comment at :225-230 records that the throw's overshoot keyframe was deliberately removed ('switches in this house seat, they don't bounce').

Recommendation: Seed, don't threshold, following iOS scroll/sheet physics and Teenage Engineering's OP-Z roller, where release velocity is the animation: project the landing stop from release position + velocity (standard deceleration projection, as in UIScrollView), then run a spring (ω0≈21 to match the wheel's well spring in the same codebase, ζ≈0.85) initialised with the finger's release velocity so a flick visibly carries and a nudge settles. Keep the no-overshoot seat as the spring's damping choice, not as a reason to amputate momentum.

#### [MEDIUM] Time is distance-blind everywhere except the two controls that prove the author knows better

The codebase proves twice that it understands distance-scaled time, then refuses to apply it. The rail prices travel as 180ms + 60ms per stop crossed (MonolithCurves.kt:85-87, spent at MonolithRailView.kt:177) and the app rocker charges 260ms for one stop but 340ms for two (BlockitSuitcaseAndSwitchesViews.kt:290-294). Everywhere else duration is a constant blind to distance and velocity: tab content always animates 240ms whether the user moves one stop or four (MainActivity.kt:449-466, TAB_IN_MS at MonolithCurves.kt:97); the Shield loadout cap always takes specA(260) for an adjacent hop or a two-stop STUDY→SLEEP jump alike (ShieldCapSelector.kt:85-88); the PARK drawer always opens in 280ms and closes in 160ms (ParkDrawer.kt:154-156), and when a drag is released the fraction re-tweens the full fixed duration from wherever the finger left it (ParkDrawer.kt:260-262) with the release velocity discarded — a slow drag released 90% closed and a flick released 10% closed take the same time to finish.

Recommendation: Generalise the rail's own law into the house rule, following Apple's fluid-interface model (springs with velocity handoff; duration emerges from distance, never a fixed tween for gesture-born motion): navDurationMs(stops) becomes the single pricing function for the cap selector (180+60/stop, capped at 360ms) and tab transitions scale their 14dp slide with stops crossed; convert the PARK drawer's release path from Animatable.animateTo(tween) to animateTo with the drag's measured end velocity as initial velocity (or Compose's spring with that velocity), so a flick finishes fast and a nudge settles slowly. Fixed durations remain lawful only for non-spatial fades.

#### [MEDIUM] Every overlay arrives as the identical fade: motion encodes no origin, so an emergency interception dissolves in like a settings sheet

Every overlay in AirlockAndDisarmOverlays.kt enters and exits as the same crossfade regardless of what it is or where it sits: desk clock fadeIn(specB 420)/fadeOut(specA 260) at :78, held digest fadeIn(specC 280)/fadeOut(specA) at :306, pre-flight at :480, the Airlock interception itself at :557, disarm challenge at :740 — and ReceiptSheet.kt:60-64 fades its bottom-anchored slip in place with fadeIn(specC())/fadeOut(specA()). The PARK drawer is the only surface in the app with real travel: it rises 280ms on EasingSeat and leaves 160ms on EasingThrow (ParkDrawer.kt:154-156, MonolithKin:90-91). So an emergency interception — the most spatially violent event in the product, another app being stopped mid-reach — materialises as a gentle dissolve identical to a settings sheet, and a receipt that physically should print upward from the bottom edge simply appears. Motion carries no information about origin, urgency or hierarchy anywhere except PARK.

Recommendation: Assign each surface class an origin motion, following Material 3's shared-axis/container logic that movement encodes where a thing came from: bottom-anchored sheets (receipt, held digest) rise 24dp with fade on the Seat curve, reusing PARK's KIN-DRAWER pair; centre overlays scale 0.96 to 1 with fade over 180ms; the Airlock alone gets a hard 120ms cut-in with no fade — an interruption should feel abrupt, because it is one. Write the three pairs into MonolithKin next to KIN-DRAWER and delete the per-file specA/specB/specC picks.

#### [MEDIUM] The filed press law is dead code and its own key breaks it: the FIX button teleports 1dp while the wheel hub gets a 45ms engineered dip

MonolithKin files a press law — PRESS_MS = 90 ('the FIX key answers on DOWN: dip within 90ms') and PRESS_BACK_MS = 150 (MonolithCurves.kt:100-103) — and nothing in the codebase uses either constant: grep finds zero call sites outside MonolithCurves.kt. The key it was written for doesn't follow it: PARK's FIX key 'dip' is .offset(y = if (fixPressed) 1.dp else 0.dp) at ParkDrawer.kt:429, an instant 1dp teleport with no animation at all, held for the entire settings round-trip and released just as instantly (ParkDrawer.kt:187-210). The hub in the custom Views, by contrast, gets a real 45ms animated dip on HubPressDip and a 160ms seat return (BlockitCoreViews.kt:464-495). So the app's most consequential button — the one that sends the user into system settings to repair a permission — presses like a light switch while a decorative wheel hub presses like a machine.

Recommendation: Wire the filed law or delete it: animate the FIX key's offset with a 90ms tween on the Press curve for the dip and 150ms on EasingSeat for the return, exactly as MonolithKin:100-103 already specifies, and give every other pressable Compose surface (chips, sled rows) the same dip depth and timing so 'pressed' feels identical everywhere. Then add a lint-style grep in review: any MonolithKin constant with zero call sites is either wired or removed at the next change — a vocabulary nobody speaks is not a system.

### Sound design — 28 findings (6 critical, 16 high, 6 medium, 0 low)
