#### [CRITICAL] Three rival minutes-to-pitch ladders and a voice-swap at every major make the dial's pitch unlearnable — there is no scale to own

Wheel Canvas maps minutes to pitch as 340 + ((value-5)/175)*540 Hz, linear in Hz (ui/views/BlockitCoreViews.kt:1172), but every 15-minute major abandons that pitch entirely and fires the canned latch via fireFeel(4L) — whose own contract admits the 4L/8L/10L branches 'play canned engine effects and ignore pitch' (BlockitCoreViews.kt:224-244, call at :1173). The same gesture driven from the ViewModel uses two further, incompatible ladders: setDialMinutes uses 440 + minutes*2.8 (ui/MonolithViewModel.kt:1474) and updateTaskDuration uses 480 + minutes*2.5 (MonolithViewModel.kt:2010). Linear-Hz spacing also compresses perceptually at the top of the range, since pitch is heard logarithmically. Playdate takes the opposite decision: one named sound designer (Simon Panrucker) authored a single consistent set of system clicks and beeps as feedback for inputs across the whole OS, so the ear learns the machine once.

Recommendation: Delete all three formulas and give TactileSoundEngine one owned pitch table: log-spaced (equal semitone steps) across 10-180 minutes, quantised so 15-minute majors are the same detent voice one octave/fifth step up plus the seat knock overlaid — never a different effect. ViewModel and Canvas both call playDetentForMinutes(m) and nothing else; add a golden test pinning the table the way the seal buffer is pinned.

#### [CRITICAL] The 20:00 sleep seal sounds bit-identically to the 05:00 fasted-block seal — the sound engine forbids an evening voice by design

TactileSoundEngine.kt:85 declares the seal 'ONE voice, bit-identical at every seal', and playSealThrow's contract at TactileSoundEngine.kt:756 is 'the one seal voice, zero parameters — no provenance, no duration, no clock can enter it, so two seals cannot differ'. RoutineHeartbeat.kt:155-159 enforces it for this exact case: 'the SLEEP 20:00 seal sounds, bit-identically'. So the user falling toward sleep hears the same 360Hz, 0.62-gain, 255-amplitude bolt Throw (TactileSoundEngine.kt renderSealBuffer, SEAL_THROW_AMPLITUDES) as a dawn study block. The engine header also bans the remedy in advance, TactileSoundEngine.kt:31: 'Zero ambient sound mixer loops', and the one softening mechanism ever designed was never built — TactileSoundEngine.kt:134-137: 'The bed catch (a later build, unassigned…) until it lands the Throw ships lawfully uncaught', i.e. the Throw's tail fades to nothing with no bed under it. Philips SmartSleep's sunset does the opposite on both axes: light AND 'optional sound' gradually decrease together to a set duration, plus RelaxBreathe light-guided wind-down rhythms.

Recommendation: Break the bit-identity law for exactly one provenance: a SLEEP-provenance seal variant rendered from the same recipe at ~180Hz fundamental, gain ~0.3, bolt layer removed, tail stretched past 900ms, and haptic amplitudes halved with the middle gap widened — a latch being laid down, not thrown. Then build the already-specced bed catch (TAIL_CATCH_SAMPLE) as a low, fading harmonic bed for the first minutes of the SLEEP window that decays to silence, so the evening seal lands on something soft instead of ending 'lawfully uncaught'.

#### [CRITICAL] Volume hierarchy is inverted across apps: a 6ms wheel tick ducks the user's own music, the seal gets the same duck

TactileSoundEngine.kt:458 calls requestTransientAudioFocus() for every dequeued SynthCommand, and :521-531 builds that request as AUDIOFOCUS_GAIN_TRANSIENT_MAY_DUCK on USAGE_ASSISTANCE_SONIFICATION; the smallest voice it protects this way is playRotaryDetent at TactileSoundEngine.kt:636-638 — 6ms at gain 0.38, fired per wheel detent from dozens of ViewModel call sites. Android's own audio-focus guidance reserves MAY_DUCK for brief, important prompts (its example is a fitness 'keep it up' cue / navigation direction), not UI ticks. There is no second, quieter focus class for ticks versus the seal.

Recommendation: Split the engine into two loudness classes the way a mixer splits channels: detents, clicks and latches request NO audio focus at all and sit ~18dB under the user's audio (system-sonification behaviour, as Pixel/Android system UI sounds do); only the 1-second Seal Throw may request MAY_DUCK, and it must abandon focus when its tail fade ends. Scrolling the wheel must never move another app's fader.

#### [CRITICAL] The Throw is bit-identical for every seal: the ceremony cannot register whether it locked away ten minutes or a whole day

TactileSoundEngine.kt:758-767 defines playSealThrow() as 'the one seal voice, zero parameters — no provenance, no duration, no clock can enter it, so two seals cannot differ'; the render is a fixed 44,100 samples (TactileSoundEngine.kt:95) at 360Hz with a pinned golden SHA-256 (TactileSoundEngine.kt:148-150), and its haptic twin is the constant SEAL_THROW_TIMINGS [0,24,38,16] / amplitudes [0,255,0,175] (TactileSoundEngine.kt:143-144). A BeoSound 9000's clamper sound encodes physical work — how far it travelled to reach the disc. A 10-minute FLOW seal, a 50-minute seal and an 8-block seal in Monolith are acoustically and haptically indistinguishable, down to the sample.

Recommendation: Keep the 360Hz body as the signature but parameterise the bolt layer by the commitment being sealed: shift BOLT_START_SAMPLE later and add one low bolt strike per study block (up to 8), and lengthen the haptic's final segment from 16ms in proportion to planned span (16ms under 30 min, 28ms at 180 min). Replace the single golden hash with a pinned family of hashes per block-count so variation is composed and testable, not accidental.

#### [CRITICAL] A supercomputer spent imitating a buzzer: the float-PCM synth inverts withered technology — maximum engineering for a click any mature part already makes

TactileSoundEngine.kt:29-41 specifies a float-PCM AudioTrack with 4 harmonic partials {0.6, 0.28, 0.37, 2.2} and dual exponential decays; TactileSoundEngine.kt:86-160 freezes a 44,100-sample Seal Throw with an xorshift32 bolt, one-pole lowpass, two comb filters and a pinned SHA-256 golden hash (SEAL_BUFFER_GOLDEN_SHA256) so the click is bit-identical on every device; TactileSoundEngine.kt:304-438 maintains separate legacy and seal AudioTracks plus writer threads polling queues at lines 350 and 449. The audible output of all 857 lines is a click, a knock and a clunk — indistinguishable in use from a 200-byte sample or the platform ToneGenerator.

Recommendation: Render the six transients (detent, click, knock, latch, seal, completion) once, offline, into small PCM16 buffers bundled as assets; delete the writer threads, command queues, comb-filter room and the golden-hash identity test; keep only the haptic waveform tables, which are the part the hand actually reads. Spend the freed complexity on nothing — that is the point.

#### [CRITICAL] 59 mechanical transients at a dozen pitches make a click soup — Balmuda tunes one timer tick to serve one bite; Monolith tunes everything, so nothing is the signature

MonolithViewModel.kt alone contains 46 playRotaryDetent/playMechanicalLatch/playFirmClick/playSeatKnock calls, at ad-hoc pitches 480Hz (:2010), 510Hz (:1761), 520Hz (:1608), 540Hz (:1420), 580Hz, 640Hz, 680Hz, 700Hz, 720Hz, 740Hz, 760Hz (:997) for actions as unlike as adding a blocked site (:1554), toggling a profile (:1489-1517) and moving a task (:1754). BlockitCoreViews.kt:236-244 adds a second dispatch table mapping gesture lengths 1L/4L/8L/10L to detent/latch/click. TactileSoundEngine.kt:20-40 promises 'one [pattern] per physical action' but in practice every action claims a mechanical transient.

Recommendation: Cut the vocabulary to three voices, printed as a closed table in TactileSoundEngine: (1) detent tick — wheel detents only, fixed 680Hz, no pitch arguments (delete the frequencyHz parameter); (2) seat knock — slide/sled seating only; (3) the Throw — seals only. Remove all latch/click transients from Shield, Sequencer and Park edits; those surfaces go silent, so silence itself becomes the background the Throw is heard against.

#### [HIGH] Feel is instant and sound is queued: the signature desynchronises and stale detents play back after the finger stops

In every play* method the haptic fires synchronously on the caller's thread and the sound is only enqueued afterwards: playRotaryDetent calls triggerWaveform then enqueueTransient (service/TactileSoundEngine.kt:629-637). The sound then waits in a 64-deep FIFO LinkedBlockingQueue (TactileSoundEngine.kt:293) to be rendered sample-by-sample and written by the single synth thread (runFloatPcmSynthLoop, TactileSoundEngine.kt:413). During a fast wheel spin, detents therefore sound late and keep clicking after the finger has stopped, in an order and tempo the finger never played. The codebase already proved this queue unfit for a signature moment: the seal needed a private pre-rendered lane, a sequence barrier and a queue purge (primeForSeal/playSealThrow, TactileSoundEngine.kt:767) precisely so queued backlog could never delay it. Teenage Engineering's OP-1 encoders and Panic's Playdate buttons make the click a property of the physical act itself — sound and feel are one event, with no queue in between.

Recommendation: Extend the seal lane's lesson to the whole vocabulary: pre-render the five core transients (detent, latch, firm click, seat knock, tear) into retained buffers at engine start and play them with a single non-blocking write at the haptic call site. Detents older than ~30ms must be dropped, never played late — a stale click is worse than a skipped one. Cap concurrent detent voices at two, newest wins.

#### [HIGH] An 857-line instrument with no tuning: every voice is an arbitrary Hz number, out of tune with the others and with itself

TactileSoundEngine.kt fixes voices at raw frequencies with no root, scale or temperament anywhere: completion 185 Hz (line 840), tear 240 Hz (line 824), seat knock 300 Hz clamped 160-420 Hz (lines 665, 674), seal body 360 Hz (renderSealBuffer), latch 520/760 Hz, detents scattered at 510/520/540/560/640/680/690/700/720/740/760 Hz across MonolithViewModel.kt call sites, and the duration dial maps pitch linearly as 440.0 + minutes*2.8 (MonolithViewModel.kt:1474). Measured against equal temperament these are inconsistently sour: 185 Hz is exactly F#3 (0 cents) but the seal's 360 Hz sits 47 cents flat of F#4 - so the seal is not even the octave of the completion - while 240 Hz is 49 cents flat of B3, 300 Hz is 37 cents sharp of D4, 680 Hz is 46 cents flat of F5 and 700 Hz is 4 cents from it, meaning two detents a screen apart disagree about what the same note is. The dial's linear-Hz glide also compresses pitch perceptually at the top of the range, the opposite of how pitch is heard.

Recommendation: Give the instrument a tuning, the way Teenage Engineering's Pocket Operators lock every voice to one key so any combination a user triggers is consonant: declare one root (e.g. build the ladder on the seal's existing body) and a small just-intonation or pentatonic set of ratios in the engine; quantize every call site's Hz to the nearest ladder degree, and change the dial mapping to logarithmic steps across those degrees so turning the wheel audibly climbs a scale. Pin the ladder with the same golden-hash discipline already used for the seal buffer.

#### [HIGH] The weightiest voices are pitched below what a phone speaker can reproduce, so the designed sound is never the heard sound

The events meant to feel heaviest carry the lowest fundamentals: completion at 185 Hz (TactileSoundEngine.kt:840), tear at 240 Hz (line 824), seat knock clamped down to 160 Hz (line 674), seal body at 360 Hz. Both AudioTracks render mono PCM float (lines 397, 434) destined for small phone loudspeakers whose output rolls off steeply below roughly 400-600 Hz; meanwhile the loudest single component of every voice is the inharmonic 4.7x partial with weight 2.2 against 0.6/0.28/0.37 for the rest (PARTIAL_WEIGHTS, line 79) - at 185 Hz that is an ~870 Hz ring the speaker reproduces easily. Net effect: on the actual device the low 'weight' the pitch was chosen to convey largely vanishes and what survives is the bright metallic partial, so completion and knock read as thin ticks rather than mass.

Recommendation: Voice the instrument for its transducer, as Panic and Teenage Engineering did for Playdate: its system sounds are composed inside the band its single small mono speaker actually reproduces well, so the designed and heard sounds match. Shift the body energy of the low voices up an octave, reinforce the low fundamentals with a strong 2nd/3rd harmonic pair so the missing-fundamental effect implies the weight the driver cannot emit, and add a device-playback check (render, play on a low-end phone, re-measure) to the existing golden-vector test discipline.

#### [HIGH] Failure sounds like nothing at all: the seal pulse is withheld from partial and shield-gap finishes, and no failure voice exists in the sound engine

data/ReceiptState.kt:110-118 — finishPulses() is an explicit withholding table: 'PARTIAL never pulses', death-booked (ELAPSED_SHIELD_GAP) finishes never pulse, only clean/attended/flow finishes sound the completion pulse. service/TactileSoundEngine.kt's whole vocabulary (playRotaryDetent:629, playFirmClick:644, playMechanicalLatch:683, playHarmonicSeal:707) contains no failure, refusal or low-register event — so the user who attended half a routine, or whose shield silently died, hears exactly what a crash or a dead app sounds like: nothing. The emotional message is that partial effort earns silence. Duolingo gives the wrong answer its own distinct low sound plus the mascot's visible reaction — failure is acknowledged in a different voice, never met with the absence of one; Forest likewise stages the withering as an event, not a non-event.

Recommendation: Compose a failure voice from the existing synth instead of withholding the success one: a single detuned, downward latch (playMechanicalLatch with engaged=false pitch/register dropped, ~0.4s, no shoulder/thunk) fired for PARTIAL and shield-gap finishes — audibly 'the machine noticed, and it is less than the seal', never silence. Silence should be reserved for nothing happening, not spent on the moment the user most needs acknowledgement.

#### [HIGH] The finish sequence is scored as a decrescendo and its one celebratory beat is best-effort — fire it late and it is silently deleted

TactileSoundEngine.kt:833-848 documents playCompletionPulse as 'three ticks that soften as they land — the machine winding down', with haptic amplitudes literally descending 175, 125, 80; MonolithViewModel.kt:1258-1260 then closes the sequence with a second knock at half amplitude (playSeatKnock(12, 0.5f)). After ~970ms the sequence is over; the remaining 500-800ms before issuance is silence. And the one celebratory element is disposable: MonolithViewModel.kt:1250-1254 only plays the pulse if the scheduler reaches it before E900 — miss the window and the finish gets knocks only, no error, no catch-up. Duolingo's lesson-complete screen escalates instead: XP counts up, then gems, then a claim animation — each reward louder than the last, ending on the high. Apple Watch likewise ends its ring celebration on the firework burst, not before it.

Recommendation: Invert the envelope: make the finish crescendo. Keep the E0 knock quiet (amplitude ~0.4), let the E700 pulse build rather than soften (ascending amplitudes, e.g. 90, 140, 200), and put the loudest, brightest event at issuance. Remove the E900 drop-deadline for the pulse — if the beat is late, play it at issuance; a celebration that can silently not happen teaches the user finishes are unreliable.

#### [HIGH] A milestone finish sounds exactly like the first finish — the sound engine's one-voice law leaves no sonic register for anniversaries

TactileSoundEngine.kt:85-92 enshrines the seal throw as 'ONE voice, bit-identical at every seal', and the finish side has a single fixed voice too: playCompletionPulse() (TactileSoundEngine.kt:831-845) is one waveform (0/10/24/10/24/14ms, amplitudes 175/125/80) plus one 64ms, 185Hz transient for every completion, with no variant keyed to session count, day count or receipt № anywhere in the engine. Session 1, day 7 and session 100 therefore close with the identical three softening ticks — the most crafted sense in the app is constitutionally barred from marking time.

Recommendation: Keep the daily voices bit-identical — that discipline is the brand — and add exactly one milestone voicing, following Apple Watch Activity awards, which pair the ordinary ring-close sound with a distinct award presentation (animated badge, its own chime and haptic flourish) only on award days. When the receipt being published is № 007/030/100/365, play a 'long throw': the completion pulse extended from three ticks to five with a final tick at chordRatio 2.0 (an octave above the 1.33 fifth-ish colour already used), and let the seal throw's tail run its full 1000ms uncut. One extra render path in TactileSoundEngine, triggered from the existing receipt-publish call — no new daily sounds.

#### [HIGH] A mechanical sound kit with no mechanics in it: every everyday voice is pure tuned sine, so latches, knocks and a paper tear all ring as bell pings

Every non-seal voice is rendered by the single loop in TactileSoundEngine.kt:458-478 from four sine partials with the fixed weights {0.6, 0.28, 0.37, 2.2} (TactileSoundEngine.kt:79) — the loudest component is the inharmonic 4.7x partial (line 472), which is what makes a bell or xylophone bar ring, not what makes a latch clack. There is no noise source anywhere in the legacy path: grep finds 'Random/noise' only in the seal lane. The reductio is playTearPulse (TactileSoundEngine.kt:817-830): a paper tear — in reality almost pure broadband noise — is voiced as a 240 Hz sine chord at ratio 1.21, so the receipt tear sounds like a low marimba note. The author demonstrably knows the fix: the seal's bolt layer (TactileSoundEngine.kt:104-190) is xorshift noise through a one-pole lowpass, and it is the one sound in the app that actually reads as a mechanism. iOS makes the opposite choice per voice — its keyboard click and lock sounds are built around short filtered noise bursts with a small resonant body, which is why they read as physical switches rather than tones.

Recommendation: Give each voice family a two-component recipe following the app's own bolt layer: a 2-5 ms noise-burst attack (reuse the xorshift32 generator and one-pole lowpass already in TactileSoundEngine.kt, with a per-voice cutoff — bright ~4 kHz for detent, dark ~900 Hz for seat knock) in front of the existing sine body, and cut the 4.7x partial's weight from 2.2 to under 0.8 for latch/knock/tear so the body reads as wood/metal mass instead of bell. Re-voice the tear as 40 ms of band-swept noise with three amplitude rips and no pitched partials at all. Keep the sine recipe only where a tone is honest: the seal body and the completion pulse.

#### [HIGH] The heavy voices are composed below what a phone speaker can play: completion at 185 Hz and seat knock at 160-420 Hz arrive thin, high and weightless

playCompletionPulse is voiced at 185 Hz fundamental (TactileSoundEngine.kt:833-847), playTearPulse at 240 Hz (line 817), and playSeatKnock's pitch is clamped to 160-420 Hz with 300-320 Hz at nearly every call site (TactileSoundEngine.kt:665-681; MonolithViewModel.kt:703, 1248, 2185). Handset loudspeakers roll off steeply below roughly 600-800 Hz, so on the device's own speaker those fundamentals are largely absent; what survives is the dominant 4.7x partial — meaning the 'weighted thock' is heard at ~1.4-1.5 kHz and the 'winding-down' completion at ~870 Hz, brighter and smaller than composed, while on headphones the same events arrive dark and heavy. The kit's central metaphor — pitch and weight fall as mass rises (playSeatKnock's own comment, TactileSoundEngine.kt:658-664) — inverts depending on the output transducer, and nothing in the engine compensates. Apple designs iOS system sounds against the built-in speaker's actual response and leans on upper harmonics to imply size; this kit was plainly tuned by the numbers in the code, not by listening on the target speaker.

Recommendation: Re-voice for the speaker first, following iOS's missing-fundamental practice: keep the low fundamental for headphones but build the perceived weight from a deliberate harmonic stack in the 800 Hz-3 kHz band (raise partials 2 and 3, add a short lowpassed noise 'thock' layer as in the bolt recipe) so a 300 Hz knock still reads heavy when its fundamental never reaches the ear. Then audition and sign off every voice on a mid-range handset speaker at arm's length — add that listening check to the golden-hash test's process so a future retune cannot again be approved from code constants alone.

#### [HIGH] The most-heard sound in the app is sample-identical forever: the synth has no variation mechanism at all, so the detent fatigues like a machine gun over 100 sessions

The detent is the app's highest-frequency sound — the wheel fires it per step and it has 24+ call sites across MonolithViewModel.kt and the views — yet SynthCommand carries only fundamentalHz, durationSamples, gain, chordRatio and a sequence stamp (TactileSoundEngine.kt:262-271): there is no variation field, no round-robin, no jitter anywhere in the engine, and renderSealBuffer's header boasts the render is 'input-free — no clock, no Random, no stored state' (line 197). A detent at 680 Hz on session 1 is bit-identical on session 100. Game-audio practice treats this as the cardinal UI-sound sin: Wwise/FMOD kits apply random container (round-robin) selection plus per-play pitch/volume randomization precisely because a mathematically identical repeated transient produces the 'machine gun effect' and listener fatigue within a single session, let alone a hundred. Monolith's determinism is a deliberate integrity aesthetic for the seal, but it has leaked into the disposable UI layer where identity buys nothing and repetition costs daily.

Recommendation: Add controlled variation to the legacy lane only, following the Wwise random-container model: give SynthCommand a variation draw — pitch jitter of ±4-7% and gain jitter of ±1.5 dB per play, plus 3 pre-computed detent grain variants (different noise seeds once the noise attack lands) cycled round-robin so the same variant never plays twice in a row. Keep the Seal Throw exempt and bit-identical: variation belongs to the sounds a user hears fifty times a day, never to the one that acts as a signature.

#### [HIGH] Gain ladder ranks a paper tear above the seal: tear and completion are the loudest sounds Monolith makes

Gains in TactileSoundEngine.kt: detent 0.38 (:638), firm click 0.50 (:653), seat knock 0.22-0.52 (:676), latch 0.54 (:700), harmonic seal 0.62 (:724) — but playTearPulse (:817-826, tearing the receipt counterfoil) and playCompletionPulse (:833-842) are both 0.68, the loudest voices in the app. Every voice also shares the same 4-partial recipe with the 4.7x partial weighted 2.2 (PARTIAL_WEIGHTS, :~90), so timbre cannot separate them; level was the only ranking signal available and it ranks paper above commitment.

Recommendation: Re-mix to a written dB ladder ranked by consequence, following Teenage Engineering's OP-1 field decision to give volume a per-patch setting and a higher-resolution dedicated volume encoder — level is authored per voice, not one frozen constant: detent -24dB, click -18dB, latch -14dB, tear -16dB (a detail sound, heard close), completion -10dB, Seal Throw -4dB as the sole climax. Then differentiate timbre per rank (tear loses the 2.2-weighted partial entirely) so rank survives on quiet speakers.

#### [HIGH] The seal's fake room is rendered in mono: comb-filter 'space' that turns to metallic ringing in headphones and double-room on speaker

Both AudioTracks are CHANNEL_OUT_MONO (TactileSoundEngine.kt:397 and :434), yet the Seal Throw's Layer C is a simulated room: two feedback combs (1310/1372 samples) plus an allpass at wet send -12dB (renderSealBuffer, :~210-260). Summed to mono, decorrelation is impossible, so in headphones the 'room' collapses into metallic comb coloration located inside the skull; through the phone speaker the listener's real room re-renders it a second time. The one signature sound therefore has no stable spatial identity in either of the two situations it is actually heard in.

Recommendation: Render the Throw in stereo following the OP-1 field's 'stereo throughout the whole signal chain' decision: keep body and bolt mono-compatible and centred, but decorrelate the two combs L/R so the room reads as space on headphones; on speaker output, cut the wet send by half and shorten the tail, because the physical room is already providing it. Test the seal as two authored mixes (headphone / speaker), not one mono compromise.

#### [HIGH] No negative space between sounds: every transient starts at full amplitude on sample 0 and detents machine-gun with no gap or thinning

renderSealBuffer's own spec states 'sample 0 = the attack, zero pre-silence' (TactileSoundEngine.kt:201-202), and the legacy synth loop likewise starts envBody/envTail at 1.0 on sample 0 for every command (:~465). Commands queue serially in a 64-deep LinkedBlockingQueue (:293) with no minimum inter-onset interval and no coalescing, so a fast wheel spin or sled throw fires full-attack transients back-to-back — a machine-gun rattle with no silence between events, in an app whose entire premise is the value of silence.

Recommendation: Compose the negative space: give every transient a 2-4ms raised-cosine attack (the bolt layer already proves the technique with its 88-sample onset), enforce a ~45ms minimum inter-onset gap, and coalesce detents during fast spins into one tick per 3-4 detents with pitch — not count — carrying the velocity, the way the Apple Watch Digital Crown's detent feel thins under speed instead of rattling. Silence between sounds is what makes each one read as mechanical rather than digital.

#### [HIGH] The wheel's physics hides its own best joke: a refused crossing is engineered to sound exactly like an ordinary arrival

The wheel's coast physics contains three physically distinct events — well capture, strait crossing, strait refusal — but the refusal is deliberately disguised: 'A coast arriving under 180 deg/s does not clear it: the spring for the shore it came from takes the wheel and seats it there, so a refusal sounds like an ordinary arrival, never an alarm. A faster coast crosses and pays the toll — 90 deg/s at the centreline, once.' (BlockitCoreViews.kt:1262-1264). The crossing pays a knock (fireWeightedKnock(10, 0.5f, 280f)) while the refusal is routed back through the same seat knock as a normal landing. Playdate's discipline is the opposite: every mechanic exaggerates its cause and effect — crank faster, the world visibly and audibly responds differently — so the player learns the toy by ear. Monolith engineered a joke (a toll, a strait, two shores) and then passed a law that it must never be noticed.

Recommendation: Give the strait refusal its own unmistakable voice: a two-step descending knock (300Hz then 210Hz, 14ms) fired only when a coast is turned back at the centreline, distinct from both the seat knock and the 280Hz toll knock, and flash the FLOW word once at the moment of refusal. Keep the physics identical; change only its legibility, so the wheel's three hidden events become three learnable sounds.

#### [HIGH] Sixty-eight sound calls: every trivial edit demands the ear attend to Monolith applauding itself

MonolithViewModel.kt contains 68 soundEngine.play* call sites: routine administration is sonified as insistently as commitment - playFirmClick() at :1525, playRotaryDetent() at :1542 and :1548, playMechanicalLatch(...) for toggles, sleds and site edits at :1460,1489,1496,1517,1554,1559,1564,1569,1600, all rendered by TactileSoundEngine.kt:629-833 (playRotaryDetent, playFirmClick, playSeatKnock, playMechanicalLatch, playHarmonicSeal). Weil's negative effort is quiet and receptive; Monolith's ear is summoned back to the tool for every toggle, so even a settings change becomes an event the tool performs for itself.

Recommendation: Impose a sound budget in MonolithViewModel/TactileSoundEngine: keep sound only for the two moments that are the user's own act - the seal throw on arm and the completion pulse on finish - and delete the detent, latch and firm-click calls from toggles, sleds, site add/remove, profile and routine edits, which become silent. Inside a running session, no sound at all except the finish. A tool that schools attention should stop applauding its own operation.

#### [HIGH] Sixty pitched sound calls tax the ear on every micro-action, with no auditory attention budget

MonolithViewModel.kt contains 60 soundEngine.play* call sites — playRotaryDetent at varying pitches (e.g. 480Hz + clamped*2.5, 520Hz + startHour*14), playMechanicalLatch on routine toggles, site adds and sled flips, playSeatKnock, playFirmClick, playHarmonicSeal — implemented in TactileSoundEngine.kt:629-850 as distinct detent/click/knock/latch/seal/completion voices. Almost every micro-action, including scrolling the wheel and flipping a settings sled, therefore emits an auditory information item the ear must process and, where pitch encodes value, decode. There is one binary soundEnabled toggle and no budget, no quiet tier, no distinction between a consequential seal and a trivial toggle. Simon applies to the ear exactly as to the eye: each emission consumes the recipient.

Recommendation: Cut the sound vocabulary to three paid-for events — seal/arm, Airlock intercept, session finish — and make wheel detents, tier taps, sled flips, site edits and navigation silent by default in TactileSoundEngine/MonolithViewModel. Add a PARK sled 'SOUNDS: SEAL ONLY / ALL / OFF' so the remaining auditory spend is an explicit allocation, defaulting to SEAL ONLY.

#### [HIGH] The completion pulse is a differential reward schedule: clean finishes get the E700 voice, PARTIAL and shield-gap finishes get silence

ReceiptState.kt:110-117 finishPulses: MANUAL_FINISH pulses except when ELAPSED_SHIELD_GAP, FLOW_FINISH and ROUTINE_ATTENDED pulse, 'PARTIAL never pulses'. MonolithViewModel.kt:1243-1256 fires the E700 completion pulse only when finishPulses allows — 'Death-booked: the E700 slot stands EMPTY.' The reward is delivered to the ear and body on a differential schedule keyed to the grade, below the level of anything the user can read, refuse or deliberate about: persuasion aimed at the nervous system, not at judgement.

Recommendation: Make the ending sound grade-blind: one identical neutral settle knock-pair (the existing E0/E880 seat knocks) for every honest ending — clean, partial, gap and stand-down alike — and delete the finishPulses gate. If a celebratory pulse is kept at all, surface it honestly in Park as a labelled toggle 'REWARD SOUND ON CLEAN FINISHES' defaulting off, so the conditioning is a disclosed, endorsed choice rather than a hidden schedule.

#### [MEDIUM] The seal's room is built from a stereo decorrelation pair, then summed to mono and thrown away

renderSealBuffer builds two feedback combs of deliberately unequal length - 1310 and 1372 samples (TactileSoundEngine.kt:232-233) with shared feedback COMB_G 0.836 (line 125) - then sums them 0.5 each into a single channel feeding one allpass, and both the seal track and the legacy track are hard-set to CHANNEL_OUT_MONO (lines 397, 434). Unequal comb lengths around 30 ms are the classic Schroeder/Moorer recipe precisely because the length difference decorrelates two channels into width; summed to mono the same difference buys almost nothing and can comb-filter the tail it was meant to enrich. The one sound the app treats as sacred is rendered with its spatial dimension designed in and then discarded.

Recommendation: Render the Throw in stereo: route comb1 to the left channel and comb2 to the right with the existing 18 ms pre-delay and -12 dB wet send unchanged, keep a mono fold-down audition as a test, and let the same stereo room serve the completion pulse so finishing a session feels like the same physical space opening, not a separate beep. On the mono-speaker majority the fold-down must be verified not to notch the tail.

#### [MEDIUM] A genuinely distinctive signature sound that is never promoted into an identity: it exists for one second, in private, and nowhere else

The seal Throw - 360 Hz four-partial body, xorshift-noise bolt lowpassed at 900 Hz entering at exactly +30 ms (BOLT_START_SAMPLE 1323), Schroeder room tail fading from -46 dB at 900 ms - is rendered only into an AudioTrack from an internal buffer (renderSealBuffer, TactileSoundEngine.kt) and fired from exactly one call site, SessionSealTransition.kt:142. It is never rendered to a shareable file, never used as a notification or alarm tone, never attached to a shared receipt, and no other surface repeats its body-plus-bolt motif, so nobody - including the user's friends - can ever learn to recognise Monolith by ear.

Recommendation: Do what Nintendo did with the Joy-Con click: one mechanical product sound, promoted unchanged into the logo sting of every trailer until the click alone meant Switch. Export the Throw render (the engine is procedural, so this is a file write, not a recording session), offer it as a system notification/alarm tone, attach its first 300 ms as the audio sting on shared receipts, and reuse the bolt interval as the motif for the completion voice so the product's sounds form one recognisable family with the seal as its full statement.

#### [MEDIUM] The soundtrack ends before the curtain: every completion sound fires during detention and the slip itself arrives in silence

The finish's entire soundtrack is scheduled against E0, the moment the session ends, not against the reveal: seat knock at E0, completion pulse at E700, knock pair at E880 and E970 (ui/MonolithViewModel.kt:1248-1260; the pulse itself is TactileSoundEngine.kt:833-845, a three-tick waveform with haptics). The slip it supposedly celebrates issues at E1480-E1800 (data/ReceiptState.kt:204-205) — so the music finishes, at minimum half a second of silence passes, and then the paper fades in mute: ReceiptSheet contains no sound or haptic call at all. The user hears a conclusion, looks up, and watches an unrelated silent card appear. Apple's WWDC19 audio-haptics session states the reference principle explicitly for the Apple Pay confirmation: the sound and haptics were designed to 'perfectly match the animation on screen, the checkmark' — one event in three channels, same frame. Monolith splits its one event across two moments a second apart and voices the wrong one.

Recommendation: Re-score the finish to the issuance frame, not to E0: keep the E0 seat knock as the detention's 'machine stopping' sound, delete the E880/E970 knock pair, and move the completion pulse so its first tick lands on the exact frame the slip's stamp strikes (issueOffsetMs in the ViewModel's detention loop is already computed — fire playCompletionPulse() in the same frame emitReceipt runs). Add one short paper tick (a 12ms low-amplitude seat knock variant) per printed line during the line-by-line reveal. Sound, haptic and image must describe the same instant: paper arriving.

#### [MEDIUM] Detent pitch is spent two ways that cancel out: a 6 ms window too short to hear pitch in, mapped to value on some screens and to nothing on others

playRotaryDetent renders just 6 ms of tone (TactileSoundEngine.kt:629-643) — about four cycles at its 680 Hz default, far under the ~20-30 ms a listener needs to resolve pitch as pitch; the elaborate per-call-site pitch choreography is therefore heard, at best, as a slight brightness difference. Worse, the mapping is inconsistent where it could be heard: pitch genuinely encodes value at the wheel (480.0 + clamped * 2.5, MonolithViewModel.kt:2010), the routine hour (520.0 + startHour * 14.0, line 2162) and reorder direction (740 Hz up / 560 Hz down, line 1754), but the same voice is fired at arbitrary fixed pitches — 480, 510, 520, 540, 580, 600, 640, 680, 690, 700, 720, 760 Hz — for unrelated toggles, navigation and edits across MonolithViewModel.kt, teaching the ear a grammar and then breaking it on the next screen. Nintendo's menu UI (Breath of the Wild, Switch system UI) does the opposite: cursor pitch is a strict ladder of position, identical in meaning on every screen, rendered long enough to sing. Monolith has accidentally invented the same language and then spoken it randomly.

Recommendation: Publish a pitch map and enforce it in the engine, following the Nintendo ladder: (1) lengthen the detent to ~25 ms (2 ms noise front + pitched body) so pitch is actually perceptible; (2) reserve detent pitch exclusively for continuous value — wheel position, hour, counts — quantised to steps of a single scale built on the seal's 360 Hz (e.g. its harmonics/simple ratios), so pitch always means 'where you are'; (3) collapse every discrete-event detent call site to one fixed pitch per semantic class (nav, toggle, edit), deleting the scattered 480-760 Hz literals in MonolithViewModel.kt.

#### [MEDIUM] Refusal has no voice of its own: the jam — the app's 'no' — is the affirmative seat knock played three times

The voice set covers detent, firm click, seat knock, latch, seal, tear and completion — every one affirmative or neutral. The one refusal event with sound, the arm-proving jam, is wired in MonolithViewModel.kt:700-707 to playSeatKnock(20, 1.0f, 320f) three times at 90 ms intervals: the exact voice and pitch used for successful tower seats and gate landings, at maximum amplitude. 'No' is expressed only as 'yes, yes, yes, louder' — repetition and force instead of timbre, so a user not looking at the screen hears effort being rewarded at the moment the seal was refused. The latch proves the engine can encode polarity when it tries: engaged vs released already split 760 Hz/sharp against 520 Hz/heavier (TactileSoundEngine.kt:683-705). Designed kits keep a spectrally distinct negative class — iOS and game UI error/back sounds are duller, lower and decaying where confirms are bright and resolving — because polarity is the one distinction a sound must carry eyes-free.

Recommendation: Compose a dedicated refusal voice in the latch's polarity language, not the knock's: a downward two-part sound — 300 Hz body dropping to ~210 Hz, noise layer lowpassed at 500 Hz, no 4.7x ring, ~90 ms — fired once for the jam and reused for every future denial (blocked save, refused disarm, invalid slide). One 'no' timbre, app-wide, at lower gain than any confirm: refusal should sound like mass settling against you, not like three successes.

#### [MEDIUM] Mute is designed as a blocker, not a listening state: identical sled to the app-killers, word flips 260ms late, and the state is invisible on every other screen

park.html / ParkDrawer.kt:479-520: the SOUND EFFECTS row is a 76x34 sled identical in grammar, weight and ON/OFF margin word to the SHORTS + REELS sniper sled and the SOCIAL SITES blocker sled directly around it — listening comfort is presented as another weapon to arm. The state word does not even flip with the throw: ParkDrawer.kt:484-488 delays displayedSound by 260ms. And the state exists nowhere else: deck.html and shield.html carry no sound-state mark at all, so a user muted in Park meets the dead-feeling seal on the Deck with no on-screen explanation.

Recommendation: Give sound its own grammar, distinct from the blockers: a speaker mark plus a 3-step level (QUIET / STANDARD / FULL) instead of a kill-sled, an audition tick played at the chosen level as the row is changed, and a persistent sound-state glyph in the Deck header (the iPhone hardware silent switch's orange exposure and Nothing's Glyph state marks both keep a mute state legible outside its settings). Flip the word with the throw; theatre that delays the truth is lying at 260ms scale.

### Haptics and feel — 14 findings (2 critical, 8 high, 4 medium, 0 low)

#### [CRITICAL] The seal clunk is spent on undoing a delete: the strongest feel in the app is inflated into a generic 'saved' sound

TactileSoundEngine.kt:707-721 playHarmonicSeal(arming=true) is timings [0,24,38,16] amplitudes [0,255,110,175]; TactileSoundEngine.kt:139-146 SEAL_THROW_TIMINGS is the identical [0,24,38,16] with amplitudes [0,255,0,175] - the sacred seal and the everyday seal differ by one middle segment (110 vs a true gap). MonolithViewModel.kt grep shows playHarmonicSeal called 13 times: :1799 undoDeleteTask (undoing a delete), :1968 splitActiveTaskAndReturn, :2002 autoSplitTaskIntoMicroSteps, :2020 cueTaskAndNavigateToFocus, :2099 applySmartLoadout, :2135 addCustomApp, :2142 selectAndApplyProfile, :2176 createCustomProfile, :2421/:2430 routine/profile plumbing. The finger receives the full-force 255-amplitude clunk for restoring a trashed task exactly as for committing to a lockdown.

Recommendation: Demote playHarmonicSeal to a reserved word: delete it from every CRUD/loadout/profile call site in MonolithViewModel.kt and replace those with playMechanicalLatch or playFirmClick (TactileSoundEngine.kt:644-682). Keep exactly two max-amplitude events in the app - playSealThrow at arm and playCompletionPulse at finish - the way Apple reserves its strongest Taptic patterns and a wax seal or a vault bolt is spent once per act, never as a generic 'saved' ding. Audit rule: no pattern with amplitude 255 may fire outside SessionSealTransition.kt:142 and the completion path.

#### [CRITICAL] The 60-second emergency hold - the longest, highest-stakes touch in the app - feels like standing next to a metronome, and losing it is silent

BlockitSuitcaseAndSwitchesViews.kt:604 the 60-second Emergency60sValveView hold fires fireFeel(if (sec % 5 == 0) 8L else 4L) once per second - the same latch/click stamps used for ordinary switch flips (BlockitCoreViews.kt:237-238 maps 4L to playMechanicalLatch, 8L to playFirmClick). At a bank boundary :598-599 fireFeel(1L, pitch) and fireFeel(8L) fire in the same frame, stacking two unrelated stamps. The drain path :622-645 is silent while held progress drains and fires a single fireFeel(8L) at :629 only when the loss is already complete. No waveform in TactileSoundEngine.kt exceeds 82ms total (longest: playCompletionPulse :833-845, 10+24+10+24+14ms); there is no continuous, ramping or sustained pattern anywhere in the engine.

Recommendation: Give the hold a continuous voice, following Apple Core Haptics, which separates HapticTransient clicks from HapticContinuous events whose intensity/sharpness follow parameter curves over time: replace the per-second stamps with one sustained waveform whose amplitude ramps as heldMs/totalMs rises (e.g. a repeating low-amplitude pulse train that shortens its interval 1000ms to 250ms approaching each 15s bank), make each bank a single descending seat knock, and make draining felt as a distinct rapid amplitude decay the moment the finger slips - losing progress must be feelable with eyes closed, not announced after it is gone.

#### [HIGH] The haptic language is written in sentences a shared table can read: 78ms full-amplitude seal thuds and six-segment completion pulses transmit through hostel furniture

TactileSoundEngine.kt:143-144 defines the seal's haptic as SEAL_THROW_TIMINGS [0, 24, 38, 16]ms at amplitudes [0, 255, 0, 175] — a 78ms double-thud with a full-amplitude first strike; :833-835 playCompletionPulse fires six segments [0, 10, 24, 10, 24, 14] — an 82ms triple pulse; every wheel detent (:631, [0, 7, 5] at amplitude 180) and sled flip repeats the pattern. On skin this is private; on the wooden desk, bunk frame or library table a hostel phone actually rests on, the furniture is the speaker and the pattern is legible — a roommate sharing the table can feel, and learn to read, the owner's seals, finishes and detent-spinning across an evening. Consumer wearables design against exactly this: Apple Watch haptics are short single/double taps meant for a wrist, and its Theater/DND modes exist because even wrist buzzes are room events in cinemas and lectures. Monolith composed haptic sentences with no concept of the surface the phone is lying on or the people sharing it.

Recommendation: Give haptics a room budget, the way typography has a size budget: cap any single event at two segments and ~30ms total, cap amplitude at 128 whenever QUIET ROOM (or the SLEEP routine) is active, and move the seal's ceremony into the visual throw animation at night instead of a third haptic segment. Keep the full 255-amplitude choreography only as the daytime, sound-on signature. Test it on the actual hostel surfaces — phone face-up on a shared study desk and on a bunk mattress — and publish the felt-at-30cm result as the acceptance criterion.

#### [HIGH] One screen, three clocks for a press: the hub's dip is finger-bound (45ms in, 160ms out, drag-off reverses), the slide cap's sink is a fixed 140ms wall-clock timer that expires under a still-holding finger, and the rail's press is a one-frame print with no release at all

Three elements on the Deck define 'pressed' three incompatible ways. (1) The wheel hub is pointer-bound and reversible: BlockitCoreViews.kt:461-473 dips over 45ms, lines 475-495 return over 160ms, and lines 1052-1065 reverse mid-press if the finger crosses 1.1x the hub radius. (2) The slide cap's brush sink is a wall-clock timer: BlockitCoreViews.kt:2071-2082 sets sinkUntilMs = now+140ms and postDelayed-invalidate at 150ms regardless of the finger, so a user who presses and holds for 500ms watches the cap pop back up under their still-planted thumb, then releases onto a cap that has already un-pressed itself. (3) The rail is a one-frame teleport: MonolithRailView.kt:88-91 specifies the pressed word 'strikes to full ink at once (a one-frame print, not a fade)', and lines 250-258 paint the selected cap's bottom 10dp one tone darker with no geometry change and no release transition. deck.html shows all three objects within one screen height of each other.

Recommendation: Publish one press token set and force all three (plus FIX and the Park grip, which currently grows 24dp→28dp wide on press, ParkDrawer.kt:302-312 — the app's only press that expands) to obey it: down-stroke ≤50ms, release 150-180ms on the existing HubSeatReturn curve, state owned by the pointer lifecycle end-to-end (DOWN sets, UP/CANCEL clears, drag-off reverses), and timers forbidden as press durations. Material 3 gets away with a single pressed state-layer/elevation response across every component for this reason: the finger learns one machine, not one per widget.

#### [HIGH] Haptic vocabulary collapses to duration: opposite sled throws feel identical, and pitched call sites are silently lying

BlockitCoreViews.kt:224-251: fireFeel's own contract comment concedes freqHz 'is honored ONLY by the 1L branch… The 4L/8L/10L branches play canned engine effects and ignore pitch', and the no-engine fallback is VibrationEffect.createOneShot(ms, DEFAULT_AMPLITUDE) — duration is the only variable. Consequence at the sled: SledSwitchView fires the identical fireFeel(8L) firm click for throw-to-ON and throw-to-OFF (BlockitSuitcaseAndSwitchesViews.kt:171); arming a blocker and disarming it feel exactly the same in the hand. The 3-stop rocker in the same file proves direction can be spoken — LOCKED gets a 4L latch, PEEK a 1L 520Hz detent, OPEN a latch-release (:276-286) — but the binary sled and the slide's gate never got that grammar: the slide's gate pitches its sound (620Hz up / 340Hz retreat) while the accompanying haptic stays a 1ms one-shot either way.

Recommendation: Give direction a body, following Apple's Core Haptics pattern library and the TE OP-1's encoder detents, where pitch, sharpness and intensity all move together: throw-to-ON = short ascending double-tick ending in a latch thud (waveform primitives CLICK then THUD, rising amplitude); throw-to-OFF = single descending release (THUD then TICK, falling amplitude); slide gate retreat must drop haptic sharpness with its 340Hz sound instead of reusing the up-crossing's 1ms tick. Retire DEFAULT_AMPLITUDE one-shots from every state-changing control; amplitude is information.

#### [HIGH] The seal clunk — the heaviest word in the vocabulary — is spent on undoing a task delete and adding sub-steps

playHarmonicSeal is documented as the 'Session seal clunk: full-force thunk' with the vocabulary's only 255-amplitude strike (TactileSoundEngine.kt:711-715, timings [0,24,38,16], amplitudes [0,255,110,175]). It is then fired from at least 13 ViewModel call sites, most of them clerical: undoDeleteTask (MonolithViewModel.kt:1799), splitActiveTaskAndReturn (:1968), addTaskSubStep / autoSplitTaskIntoMicroSteps (:2002), applySmartLoadout (:2099), createCustomProfile (:2176) and end2MinutePeekEarly (:2421). A user who edits tasks for a minute hears the sacred session-sealing thunk half a dozen times without sealing anything.

Recommendation: Ration the word. Reserve playHarmonicSeal exclusively for an actual session arm/disarm, and demote every bookkeeping call site to playMechanicalLatch or playFirmClick, which already exist for exactly that weight class. Apple's Human Interface Guidelines treat notification-success haptics as a reserved signal whose meaning collapses if fired for routine feedback; Monolith should apply the same scarcity law to its one 255 strike — a seal that also means 'sub-step added' soon means nothing.

#### [HIGH] The signature seal has a near-identical twin, so the one moment engineered to be unmistakable feels like everything else

Two seal patterns share the identical timing skeleton [0,24,38,16]: the Seal Throw (TactileSoundEngine.kt:145-146, SEAL_THROW_AMPLITUDES [0,255,0,175], fired once per real seal by SessionSealTransition.kt:142) and playHarmonicSeal arming ([0,255,110,175], TactileSoundEngine.kt:712-715). The only difference is the middle segment: amplitude 0 (a true gap) versus 110 (a settling shoulder) inside a 78ms event. The Throw's audio twin is engineered to bit-identity with a pinned SHA-256 golden hash (TactileSoundEngine.kt:149-154), yet its haptic twin differs from the everyday seal by one mid-amplitude value no fingertip can reliably parse — and the everyday version is the one heard far more often.

Recommendation: Make the Throw categorically, not incrementally, different: keep the [0,24,38,16] gap pattern for the Throw alone, and re-voice playHarmonicSeal into a clearly shorter, single-strike shape (e.g. [0,14] at 200) so the two can never be confused. Teenage Engineering's OP-1 and Apple's Taptic 'taptic time' patterns work because the signature event occupies its own rhythmic shape, not a remix of a common one — identity in haptics is rhythm first, amplitude second.

#### [HIGH] The pitch ladder is a sound, not a feel: every detent, tier and duration is the same 12ms stamp under the finger

TactileSoundEngine.kt:629-641 playRotaryDetent(frequencyHz) passes frequency only to enqueueTransient (sound); its haptic is the fixed waveform timings [0,7,5] amplitudes [0,180,70] for every call. Call sites encode real information in that pitch: MonolithViewModel.kt:2088-2093 maps AppBlockTier LOCKED to 320Hz, PEEK_2M to 560Hz, OPEN to 820Hz; :2010 maps task duration to 480.0 + clamped * 2.5; BlockitCoreViews.kt:1173 builds a 340-880Hz ladder across the wheel's minute range. With sound muted, on a noisy street, or for a deaf user, tier, duration and wheel position are haptically indistinguishable - one 12ms stamp for every value in the app.

Recommendation: Make the ladder felt, not just heard, following Nintendo's Joy-Con HD Rumble and Core Haptics' sharpness parameter, both of which vary the vibration itself (frequency/sharpness), not a paired tone: map tier and wheel position onto the waveform - LOCKED a long low-amplitude thud, PEEK a double tick, OPEN a short high-amplitude snap; on the wheel, grow detent amplitude/duration at 15-minute marks and at the 10-minute shore so position is readable eyes-free. Every pitch difference in MonolithViewModel.kt must have a timing or amplitude difference beside it.

#### [HIGH] Seven designed voices collapse to three at the Canvas boundary: fireFeel's millisecond ladder deletes the tear, the completion and latch direction

BlockitCoreViews.kt:224-247 fireFeel - the only haptic door for every Canvas control - maps 1L to playRotaryDetent, 4L to playMechanicalLatch(true), 8L to playFirmClick, and else also to playFirmClick; its own comment at :226-232 admits freqHz is honoured only by the 1L branch and the 4L/8L branches 'ignore pitch', and :240-244 admits the else branch used to spend the completion pulse and now spends the firm click. TactileSoundEngine.kt defines seven named voices (detent, firm click, seat knock, latch, seal, tear, completion at :629-845), but no Canvas surface can ever reach playTearPulse or playCompletionPulse through fireFeel, and latch direction is hardcoded to engaged=true at :237 even for release actions.

Recommendation: Replace the 1/4/8/10ms integer code - a leftover duration ladder, not a vocabulary - with named semantic calls at the Canvas layer (Feel.Detent, Feel.LatchEngage, Feel.LatchRelease, Feel.Seat, Feel.Tear, Feel.Complete), the way Material 3 and iOS name feedback by intention (selection, impact, notification) rather than by milliseconds. Wire the receipt tear in Canvas to playTearPulse and any Canvas finish state to playCompletionPulse, and pass latch direction through instead of hardcoding true.

#### [HIGH] Consequence is not encoded in control grammar: the emergency valve is the same chip as a −30 routine nudge

MonolithCustomComponents.kt:170 defines one BlockitActionChip grammar — 42dp, radius 12, one border, one label style — and it is spent indiscriminately: on routine −30/+30 nudges and day letters (ShieldMatrixScreen.kt:738-762), on REMOVE for a website, on DESK CLOCK, and, enlarged only to 58dp, on 'EMERGENCY BREAK VALVE (60S HOLD)' (TactileDeckScreen.kt:1050) and 'GRACE WINDOW ABORT' (TactileDeckScreen.kt:1039). On a Leica the controls are distinguishable blind: the shutter dial is large and knurled, the aperture ring thin, the advance a lever — size and texture ARE the hierarchy, and the most consequential control can never be mistaken for the least. In Monolith the finger cannot tell, by form, the difference between nudging a routine and breaking a sealed session.

Recommendation: Give the valve the slide's grammar, not the chip's: render EMERGENCY BREAK as a full-width 72dp hold-sled in the slide zone's own register (dark track, cap that must travel and be held), sharing no silhouette with any chip. Simultaneously demote all BlockitActionChips used for nudges and plumbing (−30, days, REMOVE, ADD) to bare text words with hairline rules, so chips survive only for DESK CLOCK and HELD. Three grammars total: sled for commitment and breach, cap/rocker for dials, print for plumbing.

#### [MEDIUM] The wheel's physics run on clamped time but its deadline runs on real time, so the instrument's feel changes under the load its own Canvas creates

BlockitCoreViews.kt:1215-1217: stepPhysics computes dt from real frame nanos but clamps it to 0.05f maximum, then integrates angle and spring from that clamped dt - while the fling's capture deadline at line 1283 (frameNanos - physStartNanos > 1_400_000_000L) is measured in unclamped real time. The wheel's own onDraw is the heaviest in the app (segmented socket/chamfer/tooth loops from BlockitCoreViews.kt:570 onward), so precisely when frames drop, physics time runs slower than real time but the deadline does not: a fling on a busy device travels less far and gets captured by a well earlier than the identical fling on an idle device. The same clamp pattern repeats in the slide view's integrator (line 2209). The instrument's feel - coast distance, capture, the seat knock's timing - is therefore a function of system load, not of the user's hand alone.

Recommendation: Adopt the fixed-timestep discipline game engines settled decades ago (Gaffer on Games, 'Fix Your Timestep'): accumulate real elapsed time and integrate the (theta, omega) model in fixed 1/240s substeps, rendering whatever the latest completed state is. The spring constants, zeta 0.38 tuning and 1400ms deadline all stay identical - they just stop being silently rewritten by frame drops. A Braun ET66-style instrument reference makes the design point: a dial's detents are a property of the object; Monolith's currently are a property of the object's workload.

#### [MEDIUM] No volume grammar: every primary strike lives between amplitude 160 and 255, so a wheel detent hits at 71% of the seal's force

Strike amplitudes in TactileSoundEngine.kt: rotary detent 180 with a 70 tail (:631-635), tear pulse 160 (:819-823), completion first tick 175 (:837-841), latch engage 215 (:691-695), firm click 225 (:647-651), seal 255 (:712-715). The smallest, most frequent gesture in the app — one wheel detent — strikes at 180/255, and a generic Canvas 'firm click' at 225 is 88% of the seal. No pattern's primary strike goes below 160; the vocabulary has eight words and one shouting register, so on the motor the distinctions the code names (tick vs click vs clunk) compress into a single buzz family differentiated mostly by duration.

Recommendation: Re-ladder the amplitudes into a perceptual staircase: detent strike to ~60 with a ~25 tail, tear ~90, latch ~130, firm click ~170, completion peaking ~150 and decaying, and leave 255 to the seal alone. Apple's UIImpactFeedbackGenerator ships five graded styles (light, medium, heavy, rigid, soft) precisely because intensity is the primary channel users read; Monolith's durations already vary well — give them amplitudes that spread across the motor's range instead of clustering in its top third.

#### [MEDIUM] Canvas controls speak a mistranslated dialect: every release says 'engage', the completion pulse is unreachable, and layered knocks cancel themselves

BlockitCoreViews.kt:235-245 routes all Canvas feel through a millisecond ladder: 1L → playRotaryDetent, 4L → playMechanicalLatch(true) — always the ENGAGE voice, even when the gesture releases or lowers something — 8L → playFirmClick, and the else branch (including 10L, the completion value) also → playFirmClick, with the comment at :240-244 admitting the completion pulse was withdrawn from generic use. The freqHz pitch argument is silently ignored by the 4/8/10 branches (:226-230). During the emergency-break hold, a bank crossing fires fireFeel(1L) and fireFeel(8L) back-to-back (BlockitSuitcaseAndSwitchesViews.kt:598-599): two vibrate() calls in the same frame, where the second preempts the first, so the intended two-layer knock collapses to the firm click alone. The same physical toggle therefore feels different depending on whether it lives on a Compose surface (MonolithViewModel.kt:1489 correctly calls playMechanicalLatch(newValue)) or a Canvas one.

Recommendation: Kill the millisecond ladder and route Canvas views through the same semantic calls the ViewModel uses: a small enum (Detent, Engage, Release, Commit, Complete) mapped once to engine patterns, so a release speaks playMechanicalLatch(false) everywhere. Where a layered knock is wanted, compose it as ONE VibrationEffect waveform with both segments (as playSeatKnock already does) instead of two competing vibrate() calls. Material 3's haptic guidance and Apple's Core Haptics both treat each feedback event as a single authored pattern; Monolith's engine already authors that way — only the Canvas adapter betrays it.

#### [MEDIUM] Finishing feels the same for 5 minutes as for 3 hours: the completion pulse is forbidden from knowing what was achieved

TactileSoundEngine.kt:759-766 documents playSealThrow as 'zero parameters - no provenance, no duration, no clock can enter it, so two seals cannot differ', and playCompletionPulse at :833-845 is one fixed three-tick softening pattern (amplitudes 175/125/80) called exactly once, at MonolithViewModel.kt:1253. A completed 5-minute session and a completed 3-hour session therefore end with the identical 82ms whisper; the receipt's numbers scale, the body's reward does not.

Recommendation: Keep the Throw bit-identical at ARM - sameness is right for a commitment - but scale the FINISH to the stake, the way Forest's grown tree literally gets bigger with session length and game feel scales its reward burst to the achievement: parameterise playCompletionPulse by elapsed time (e.g. under 25 min the current three ticks; 25-90 min add a fourth, stronger seat; over 90 min a full seal-weight clunk followed by the softening ticks). Finishing long must feel heavier than finishing short.

### Interaction and gestures — 43 findings (12 critical, 25 high, 6 medium, 0 low)

#### [CRITICAL] Airlock puts the safe verb mid-screen and the temptation verb nearer the thumb: centred card, both chips 42dp, PEEK stacked below RETURN

airlock.html frames 1-2 and AirlockAndDisarmOverlays.kt:592-603: the intercept is a Box with contentAlignment = Alignment.Center and 20dp padding, so the card sits at mid-screen, outside the bottom-third natural thumb arc. Inside it, RETURN TO FOCUS and (after the 5s countdown) EMERGENCY PEEK are both BlockitActionChip at height(42.dp) (MonolithCustomComponents.kt:201) with 12sp labels — below the 48dp Material 3 target floor. Because the chips stack in that order, the temptation verb ends up BELOW the safe verb, i.e. closer to where a one-handed thumb actually rests, and the countdown numeral that needs no action gets 88sp (AirlockAndDisarmOverlays.kt, countdown Text) while SESSION ENDS and ACTIVE INTENTION get 12.5sp at 80% alpha.

Recommendation: Rebuild the intercept as a bottom sheet, not a centred card: anchor the card to the bottom of the screen in the thumb arc, make RETURN TO FOCUS a 56dp full-width accent bar fixed at the very bottom, and move EMERGENCY PEEK above it with a deliberate gap once the countdown ends, so the safe verb is always the nearest, largest target and the risky verb always requires a reach. Keep the 88sp countdown, but demote it visually once it hits 00 instead of letting it remain the hero of a screen whose only job is one thumb tap.

#### [CRITICAL] The wheel demands a full circular trace the holding thumb cannot make: only its lower quadrant lies on the thumb arc, the rest is lift-and-replant

deck.html: the 288dp wheel sits inside the top instrument card, its hub at screen centre and its 90-minute detent at the card's top edge. TactileDeckScreen.kt:705 sets the wheel height(288.dp) inside the verticalScroll column at TactileDeckScreen.kt:562. BlockitCoreViews.kt:987-1073 (RotaryWheelView.onTouchEvent) computes rotation from atan2 around the wheel centre on every MOVE and hands the gesture to physics on ACTION_UP, so lifting the thumb mid-arc ends the drag; the hub's eight block wells are hit-tested to a dp(14f) tolerance around a dp(40f) ring inside that same centre. The thumb's pivot is the bottom corner of the grip: it can trace only the wheel's lower-right quadrant without lifting, so setting 90-180 minutes or tapping a far well means a full fingertip extension to the top of the card, a lift, and a replant that the code treats as release-and-coast.

Recommendation: Rebuild the instrument as Samsung One UI rebuilds its apps (2018, still its published guideline): top half is a viewing area, bottom half is the interaction area. Keep the 72sp hero number where it is as pure readout, but move the operable surface down: replace the full circle with a 120-degree arc scrubber seated directly above the pinned slide bar, its centre of rotation below the screen edge so every detent lies on the thumb's natural sweep, and move block-count selection onto that arc as large detents instead of 14dp wells in a hub. If the full wheel must stay, add a linear fine-scrub strip in the bottom interaction zone that drives the same minutesValue.

#### [CRITICAL] Friction is inverted on Shield: the most destructive mid-session gesture (one loadout-cap tap re-rules every app) is the lightest touch and gets the seal's celebratory sound

ShieldMatrixScreen.kt (LOADOUT section) wires ShieldCapSelector.onSelect straight to onApplySmartLoadout with no sealed-mode branch, no preview and no confirmation; shield.html shows it as a calm 84dp cap in the same grammar as every harmless selector. MonolithViewModel.kt:2098 applySmartLoadout opens with soundEngine.playHarmonicSeal(true) — the app's most affirmative, ceremonial sound — then bulk-rewrites every app's tier via repository.applySmartLoadout and flips the Shorts/Reels sniper and browser blocker. Compare the friction gradient inside the same screen: tightening ONE app takes a precise tap on one 54dp slot of a 168dp rocker (shield.html catalogue rows), while re-ruling EVERY app takes one casual cap tap. There is no diff ('SLEEP would open 9 apps'), no count, no undo, and the feedback rewards the act.

Recommendation: Invert the friction to match the blast radius, the way iOS bulk photo deletion confirms with a count before it commits: a cap tap while sealed must open a diff sheet in the slip's print grammar — 'WORK SPRINT: 6 APPS OPEN, 3 SHUT — SEALED RULES CANNOT WEAKEN' — with the loosening lines struck through and only the tightening subset applicable via a hold-to-apply sled. While unsealed, keep the one-tap cap but print the same diff as a 5-second undoable sentence ('LOADOUT WORK — 9 RULES CHANGED · UNDO'). Reserve playHarmonicSeal for the seal itself; a mid-session bulk change gets the flat latch, never the ceremony.

#### [CRITICAL] The slide-to-start is a one-thumb solo gesture and the session № is minted only at the end — Monolith's one joinable token faces backwards, issued when joining is impossible

deck.html: the start gesture is one 84×56dp orange cap in a 72dp track captioned 'SLIDE OR TAP TO START' (BlockitCoreViews.kt:2407 WORDS_START; class SlideToStartView at :1444) — a single-thumb, single-device gesture with no second participant slot. The session's only shareable-looking token faces backwards: ReceiptState.kt:187-189 formats numberPrint as '№ 048' but the № is minted by the seal transaction (ReceiptState.kt:131) and a broken session gets 'No receipt, no №, ever' (:40) — the number exists only after the session is over, when nobody can join it. Forest's Plant Together inverts this: the host creates a room, shares a room code before starting, others enter the code to join, and if anyone leaves, everyone's tree dies.

Recommendation: Issue the № at ARM time, not seal time, and make it a joining object in Forest's room-code sense: the Deck proof strip prints '№ 048 · OPEN TO PAIR' while armed; a partner enters that № on their own Deck and the slide becomes a co-arm — both caps must be slid within the same 60 seconds for the session to seal, and either phone breaking the session prints the fault on both receipts. No room list, no lobby, no chat: the number Monolith already prints is the entire social surface.

#### [CRITICAL] Two opposite shadow physics in one app: the hub's shadow stays planted while the slide cap's shadow rides down with it, so the commit cap's press produces zero depth change

BlockitCoreViews.kt:847-854 draws the wheel hub's contact shadow UNTRANSLATED at cy+2dp while the hub group translates down hubPressDepth*1dp, so the shadow gap provably closes 2dp→1dp under the finger. The slide cap in the same file does the opposite: BlockitCoreViews.kt:1765-1767 bakes the 1dp brush sink into thumbRect itself, and lines 1818-1821 then draw the cap's shadow at thumbRect.top+2.5dp — the shadow rides down with the cap, the gap never closes, so the sink is depth-neutral and reads as the whole sticker sliding 1dp. The sled and rocker thumbs never change at all: BlockitSuitcaseAndSwitchesViews.kt:141-146 and 382-388 paint an identical +2dp, 0x38 shadow at rest, mid-1:1-drag and mid-throw. deck.html and shield.html renders confirm every one of these shadows is a fixed hard offset in the static frame.

Recommendation: Adopt one contact-shadow law, the hub's, everywhere: shadows anchor to the track/ground and never translate with the part; a press closes the gap (2.5dp→1dp on the slide cap, as the hub already does), and a grabbed/dragging thumb lifts the way an iOS drag preview does — shadow offset grows to ~4dp and softens while held, settling back on release. Apply it to SlideToStartView, SledSwitchView and AppRowSledToggleView; delete the sink-from-thumbRect construction so sink and shadow are independent variables, as they already are in RotaryWheelView.

#### [CRITICAL] No clutch: the wheel reads absolute finger position, so it cannot be stroked, nudged or used eyes-free like a click wheel

BlockitCoreViews.kt:1131-1147 updateMinutesFromTouch() sets wheelAngleDeg directly from atan2(dy,dx) unwrapped and clamped to 108..432, and it is already called on ACTION_DOWN (BlockitCoreViews.kt:1051) and every MOVE (1069); the field that would enable delta tracking, lastTouchAngleDeg, is declared at BlockitCoreViews.kt:494 and never used anywhere. deck.html render confirms the consequence visually: 35 stops are printed at fixed positions around a 288dp disc, so the finger must travel to and aim at the target's location on the circle.

Recommendation: Rebuild drag as relative rotation, following the iPod click wheel: accumulate angular delta between successive touch points (wire up lastTouchAngleDeg), so a stroke anywhere on the annulus moves the value, lifting and re-stroking (clutching) accumulates, and a short stroke from the comfortable thumb arc nudges one detent without looking. Keep direct aiming only as an explicit tap on a printed tick, visually distinct from a stroke. This one change also makes long traversals 10->180 possible in several short strokes instead of one impossible 306-degree continuous drag.

#### [CRITICAL] 'SLIDE OR TAP TO START': the signature control prints its own redundancy on its face

The Deck's commit control prints its own redundancy on its face: WORDS_START = "SLIDE OR TAP TO START" (ui/views/BlockitCoreViews.kt:2407, described at :1434 as the plate text 'at rest and frozen through every' state; visible verbatim in design-renders/deck.html). The slide is the product's signature commitment ritual — a 72dp track, an 84x56 accent cap, and a driven-mesh integrator with its own duration vocabulary (MonolithCurves.kt Slice D amendment: 140/110/250ms) — yet the label concedes a plain tap on the same cap does the identical job. A control that needs two verbs has neither: if the tap is safe, the slide is decoration burdening every start; if the slide's travel is the deliberate friction that makes arming mean something, the tap is a hole in it. Rams' second principle (disregard anything that detracts from usefulness) and tenth (not burdened with non-essentials) cannot both be honoured by this label.

Recommendation: Pick one verb and redraw the plate to say only it. Keep the slide as the sole arm gesture — delete the tap path on the cap, set the plate to 'SLIDE TO START', and let the travel distance be the commitment. If reachability demands a tap fallback, then delete the slide instead: shrink the zone to a 56dp button labelled 'START' and spend the recovered 72dp and the mesh integrator on the task row. Do not ship a third state in which both exist.

#### [CRITICAL] The wheel hub is a FUNC key with no orange legend: three commands share one unlabelled press, chosen by invisible zones

On a Digitakt every key's secondary function is printed on the panel itself in orange beside the key; nothing a key does is unlabelled. The Deck's hub is one unlabelled key with three different semantics selected by invisible azimuth zones: a press on a well sets blocks directly to that well, a press in the upper arc at count >= 4 targets the tetrad closure 4, the lower arc targets 8 (BlockitCoreViews.kt:1038-1043), and on release a closure target fires onSetBlocksCount while any other hub press fires onCycleBlocksCount (BlockitCoreViews.kt:1092-1097). The code states the doctrine plainly: 'the count lives only as hub geometry — no numeral, no word' (BlockitCoreViews.kt:916). The deck.html render confirms the shipped panel: eight dots, two closure bars, zero printed words explaining that centre, well and bar are three different commands with jumps of +1, +N and straight-to-8.

Recommendation: Print the hub's grammar on the panel in the accent colour, as a fixed legend line directly under the wheel: 'HUB TAP +1 BLOCK · TAP A DOT = SET COUNT · TAP A BAR = 4 / 8'. Set the numerals 4 and 8 into the two closure bars themselves, and give the centre of the hub a printed '+' glyph, so each touch zone carries its own label at the point of touch.

#### [CRITICAL] The wheel breaks the winding hand at 6 o'clock: a 36-degree dead sector and an 18-degree valueless strait sit between FLOW and 10

BlockitCoreViews.kt:501-505 comment: 'FLOW seats at 108, the strait runs 108..126... the 6-o'clock dead sector is the 36 degrees between 72 and 108'; :516-530 minutesToAngle/valueForAngle place FLOW and 10 across that strait with the centreline at 117 as the only boundary; :677 'inside the break there is no grip, no tick, no value'; :745 'Inside the strait there is no tick at all'; :1136-1147 touches in the dead sector 'clamp to the nearer shore'; :1153-1154 'A strait crossing under the finger is 9 degrees of haptic silence'. deck.html render shows the resulting broken scale at the wheel's foot.

Recommendation: Abolish the strait and dead sector. Lay the scale as one continuous arc exactly as a timer dial does: FLOW as a single detent immediately anticlockwise of 10, then 10-180 at uniform 9 degrees per 5 minutes with no gap in teeth, ticks or haptics, and map every degree of finger travel to the scale so rotation angle and value never decouple. Delete the centreline-boundary logic in valueForAngle and the shore-clamping in updateMinutesFromTouch.

#### [CRITICAL] No approach beat: the machine never wakes for the hand — its only preparation is invisible and its theatre starts after the point of no return

B&O's proximity discipline (Beosound Edge controls light up on approach; Beosound Theatre's ultrasonic sensor wakes its glass panel within 60cm) puts a waking beat BEFORE touch. Monolith primes only invisibly: ArmProvingController.kt:342 calls transition.primeForSeal() inside the latch batch, and TactileSoundEngine.kt:738 primeForSeal() does audio-focus, queue purge and pre-render with no user-visible counterpart. SlideToStartView.onDraw in BlockitCoreViews.kt:1775-1830 reacts only to the post-DOWN displayed fraction — the cap has no hover, approach or press-awakening state, no marker brightening, no trail pre-light. The first thing the user can perceive is the seal shot, which starts after the commitment is already latched.

Recommendation: Add an approach beat in the 140ms between onPressStart and latch: raise the cap's marker (#FFE4CF) from 90% to full, light the track trail to the 0.25 fraction in accent at 55 alpha, and play the existing seat-knock at quarter gain — all reversed without trace if the press is released before latch. The prime already happens in this window; make the user see the machine wake for their hand instead of only learning it woke after it has seized them.

#### [CRITICAL] Thick boundaries fail: the seal, the receipt and the Airlock all share the same 1dp hairline — no threshold is a place

Every consequential crossing in the app is drawn with the identical membrane: the Deck header is a 1dp hairline (design-renders/deck.html: header .hairline height:1px), the Receipt slip is .border(1.dp, scheme.outlineVariant, RoundedCornerShape(24.dp)) at ui/components/ReceiptSheet.kt:79, and the Airlock card — the boundary between a sealed session and a distraction — is the same 1.dp border at 24.dp radius and 24.dp padding at ui/components/AirlockAndDisarmOverlays.kt:599-602. In the airlock.html render the crossing itself is instantaneous: a full-screen swap to a centred card with an 88sp countdown '03' → '00', after which RETURN TO FOCUS was already live and the peek simply appears. There is no threshold zone you inhabit, prepare in, or can linger at — only a line you are teleported across.

Recommendation: Make the Airlock a thick boundary, a place rather than a line: replace the instant full-screen swap with a three-zone threshold on the Airlock surface — outer zone naming the app and the cost, a middle breathing zone (the existing 5 seconds, rendered as a widening band the user stands in, with the session's intention engraved in it), and an inner zone where RETURN TO FOCUS lives. Give the seal crossing on the Deck the same thickness in reverse: the slide track should visibly thicken into a lintel as the cap crosses, so entering and being intercepted feel like passing through the same wall from opposite sides.

#### [CRITICAL] The Airlock is a hot medium: an 88sp countdown lecture about distraction that is itself five seconds of high-definition distraction content

AirlockAndDisarmOverlays.kt:607-648: badge 'AIRLOCK INTERCEPTION • LOCKED', app name at 24sp, 'SESSION ENDS…', an 88sp countdown numeral (line 636-639), then 'ACTIVE INTENTION: …' recited back (line 648); airlock.html frames 1-2 show all five elements stacked in one card. McLuhan's hot medium is high-definition and leaves nothing for the audience to complete — this intercept is a fully-produced lecture about the distraction, delivered at the moment of distraction.

Recommendation: Make the Airlock a cool, low-definition medium — a closed door, not a broadcast: true-black ground, the app name once at 15sp, no countdown numerals, no session-end line, no intention recitation, and RETURN TO FOCUS as the only chip. The 5 seconds become unfilled time the user must complete himself; that completion is the training the hot card currently does for him.

#### [HIGH] The slide is an unmeasured journey: a mixer-fader cap travelling a blank track with no scale, no detents and no end-gate to arrive at

BlockitCoreViews.kt onDraw (~1760-1830) draws only the dark track, a translucent trail at alpha 55 behind the cap, and the cap itself with a 1dp cream marker line; there are no tick marks, fractions or end geometry anywhere along the travel, and arrival is signalled only by sealExitPhase stepping the cap's accent shade at +50/+100/+150ms (BlockitCoreViews.kt:1567, 1775, 1807; deck.html slidezone: 72dp track, 84x56dp cap, words 'SLIDE OR TAP TO START'). The code itself names the cap a mixer fader (marker comment, BlockitCoreViews.kt onDraw), yet a real fader — e.g. Teenage Engineering's TX-6 channel faders — travels against a printed scale so position is a reading, not a guess.

Recommendation: Engrave the track like an instrument: hairline ticks at 25/50/75% printed on the track face, a physical end-gate notch in the last 8% of travel that the cap's marker line must align with a fixed SEAL index printed at the track end, and rising haptic density (ticks shortening from 12ms to 4ms spacing) through the final quarter so the hand feels the gate before the eye sees it. Replace the three-step shade change at arrival with the cap visibly dropping 1dp into its dock recess on the dock frame.

#### [HIGH] Sequence 3 — The shared control kit before the Deck: the same chip and sled already appear at incompatible sizes on different screens
