MonolithCustomComponents.kt (897 lines) holds the shared kit: FullBleedSectionHeader at :123, BlockitActionChip (42dp, r12) at :170, ProofStripBand at :644. The renders prove divergence, not reuse: shield.html uses the chip at 42dp and a 168x34dp three-stop rocker for SHUT/PEEK/OPEN, park.html uses a visually identical sled at 76x34dp for a two-state switch, airlock.html reuses the 42dp chip at full card width as the primary action. One gesture vocabulary, three geometries — a user learns the sled on Shield and meets a different-sized sled for a different job in Park.

Recommendation: Third, extract and redesign five controls only — ActionChip, Sled (one 3-stop and one 2-stop variant at one height, 48dp, one thumb geometry), SlideToStart, RotaryWheel, ProofStrip — with component tokens from Step 1, following Teenage Engineering's OP-1, whose four colour-coded encoders map to the same colours on screen in every mode so one learned control transfers everywhere. In Monolith terms: orange always means commit/arm, ink always means shut, grey always means peek, at identical size and haptic/sound response on Deck, Shield, Park and Airlock. No screen redesign starts until these five are signed off in isolation.

#### [HIGH] Shield's per-app rocker is a 34dp-high, 28dp-thumb precision strip repeated down the whole catalogue

shield.html catalogue rows and BlockitSuitcaseAndSwitchesViews.kt:361-380: the rocker is drawn 168dp wide x 34dp tall, pad 3dp, so each stop slot is 54dp wide but the moving thumb is only 28dp tall; ShieldMatrixScreen.kt:1083 gives the whole row height(54.dp), leaving roughly 10dp of vertical slack between one row's rocker and the next. The stop words inside are 10sp (shield.html .stops). A student re-tiering apps one-handed between classes must land repeated horizontal drags on a 34dp strip flush with the right screen edge, row after row, with the neighbouring app's identical strip a finger-slip away.

Recommendation: Grow the signature control to thumb scale instead of shrinking the thumb to it: rocker height 48dp minimum with a 42dp thumb, row height 64dp, and 12sp stop words, following Material 3's 48dp target floor and the full-height segmented controls in Apple Settings. Add a whole-row swipe (drag anywhere on the row moves its rocker) so the precise strip is a fallback, not the only grip, and give the first and last stops haptic detents strong enough to feel without looking down from a textbook.

#### [HIGH] The one exam object in the code is a dead enum with no seat on the wheel: EXAM_90 exists in the model but has no detent mark, no colour, no voice — selecting 90 minutes looks and feels exactly like selecting any other duration

data/MonolithModels.kt:71 defines EXAM_90('90m Exam', 90, 15, 4, 'Full Session') — even its badge copy refuses to say exam conditions. Worse, it is unreachable as a designed object: ui/screens/TactileDeckScreen.kt:569 records 'The preset tiles are gone: one value, one control — the wheel', TactileDeckScreen.kt:297-300 admits the engine 'never reads the preset', and the only preset control left on the Deck is the FLOW keycap (TactileDeckScreen.kt:722). In design-renders/deck.html the wheel's 90 is one plain Anonymous Pro numeral among 30/60/120/150/180 — no engraved mark, no distinct detent, no change of eyebrow, colour or sound when it seats.

Recommendation: Give the 90-minute seat a designed identity, following Texas Instruments' Press-to-Test: on the TI-84/TI-Nspire, exam mode recolours the status bar blue and blinks an LED so the device's exam state is unmissable at a glance, even across a room. Translate that: engrave the wheel's 90 detent with a PAPER glyph and a heavier detent haptic/click, and when the reader seats there the Deck re-voices — hero eyebrow switches to 'PAPER · 90 MIN', the header band takes the season blue, and the slide copy changes to 'SLIDE TO SIT PAPER'. One seat on the existing wheel, not a new screen.

#### [HIGH] The slide runs dead straight along the bottom edge for its full width - against the thumb's diagonal natural swipe and unmirrored for the other hand

deck.html: the slide zone is a 72dp straight horizontal track pinned at the bottom edge, cap 84x56 homed at left inset 8, printed SLIDE OR TAP TO START. BlockitCoreViews.kt:1318-1333 (SlideGestureMath) sets CATCH = 0.84 displayed, reached at finger p = 0.92 after the 2/3 damping gear past the 0.68 gate - a near-full-width straight sweep along the bottom fringe. Steven Hoober's thumb-zone research (49% of users hold one-handed, ~75% of interactions thumb-driven) found users swipe diagonally from the edge toward the middle, not in a straight line along the bottom edge: a straight bottom-fringe track forces the thumb to suppress its natural upward drift for ~280dp. The direction is also fixed left-to-right with the cap homed left: a right thumb begins the gesture at its point of greatest extension and a left thumb must finish it there, at the exact moment the damped final third demands the most precision. No hand or mirror setting exists.

Recommendation: Reshape the gesture to the arc instead of fighting it: (1) tilt the acceptance corridor - widen the track's effective hit height and let cap progress read the finger's x-projection while tolerating the natural diagonal rise, rather than one straight lane; (2) shorten the damped zone so the catch arrives at roughly p = 0.70 of travel, keeping the gear for weight but not for distance; (3) add a one-hand mode in settings that mirrors the slide (cap homes right, slides left) for left-handed grip, the way the rail and sled geometry should mirror with it. Keep the tap-to-start path, but stop making the longest, straightest, most handed sweep in the app its printed primary instruction.

#### [HIGH] Park's dismiss handle migrates to the top of the screen: the taller the Guard sheet grows, the farther its only drag grip sits from the thumb that opened it

park.html: the sheet is bottom-anchored but its only on-sheet handle, the 24x4 grip in a 48dp strip, is at the sheet's top edge, and in the rendered state (full Guard board plus sleds plus spec plate) that edge sits near the top of the 844dp screen. ParkDrawer.kt:242-292 confines dismissal dragging to that strip (detectVerticalDragGestures on the 48dp grab Box) and ParkDrawer.kt's 40% law requires the drag to carry fraction past 0.4 of the sheet's own height before it will dismiss - on a tall sheet, a long pull that must start at the least reachable point on the screen. The content rows between grip and thumb are inert to the dismiss gesture: a thumb resting at the bottom of the open sheet can scroll the board but cannot start closing it.

Recommendation: Make dismissal start where the thumb already is, following Apple's sheet behaviour: any downward drag that begins on a non-interactive row (board hairlines, spec plate, header) or a fast downward fling from the scroll position at its top should carry the sheet, with the grip strip kept as the visual affordance rather than the only sensor. Alternatively cap the sheet at roughly 75% screen height with the board scrolling inside it, so the grip never leaves the stretch zone. Either change keeps the 40% seat law; what changes is that the gesture's starting point stops migrating to the worst coordinate on the phone precisely when the sheet is fullest.

#### [HIGH] Today's REST / ILL / FAMILY judgement is a tappable word disguised as a printed tag — a guest scrolling the Drawer can rewrite the day's verdict in one casual tap

DrawerScreen.kt:835-846 documents the design in its own comment: on today's heading 'the declaration itself lives here: the three words, tappable, changeable all day — tapping the active word clears it'; :865-875 implements REST / ILL / FAMILY as bare 11sp bold Text with a plain clickable and no confirmation, consequence line or sheet. In drawer.html the declaration row is visually identical to the Drawer's shelf-label typography — it reads as a tag or filter, not as the control that re-judges today's routines. Any guest scrolling the history can declare the owner ILL, or clear a real declaration, with the same gesture used to read, and nothing on the surface says a judgement changed.

Recommendation: Take the verb out of the heading. History headings become print-only in all states (the word rides beside the date, as it already does for past days). Declaring moves to one explicit 'DECLARE TODAY' row that opens a small sheet: three full-width word rows, each with its consequence printed under it ('Routines today will be judged REST — no MISSED'), and a confirm key; changing or clearing an existing declaration requires the same sheet. This is Apple Health's logging decision — a health-relevant declaration is an editor flow with a date and a commit, never a tap-to-toggle chip sitting in the list it describes.

#### [HIGH] Two commit gestures with an order-of-magnitude effort gap buy the identical 110-minute seal, so the signature slide teaches nothing

BlockitCoreViews.kt:2407 WORDS_START='SLIDE OR TAP TO START' offers both on one control. The tap path (:1424-1427): a press >=90ms (SlideGestureMath BRUSH_FLOOR_MS, :1356) released on a LIVE wire runs a driven 140ms mesh to 0.92 plus the seat spring — roughly a quarter-second, near-zero travel. The drag path (:1336-1352): gear() is 1:1 only to the 0.68 gate, then damped at 2/3 gain, so the finger must reach p=0.92 for the displayed cap to cross the 0.84 catch, over a travel floor of 180dp (TRAVEL_FLOOR_DP). Same latch, same ArmProvingController cascade, same seal — one gesture is a ceremony, the other is a button wearing the ceremony's clothes. Apple Pay's double-click of the side button is the reference discipline: one canonical commit gesture, deliberately effortful, with no cheaper alias that bypasses it.

Recommendation: Pick one commit gesture and delete the other. Keep the slide as the sole arm: a tap on the cap (press >=90ms) should only latch the press preview — freeze the proof strip and imprint, as onPressStart already does in TactileDeckScreen.kt — and releasing without travel returns to rest with nothing dispatched. If a tap is genuinely wanted for repeat arms, delete the track entirely and design an honest press-and-hold cap (400ms fill) instead of keeping a 180dp ritual that its own label invites the user to skip.

#### [HIGH] Shield's rocker gives OPEN the porcelain prize material and presents SHUT, PEEK and OPEN as three equally pretty, equally effortless preference stops

shield.html's catalogue rows (from BlockitSuitcaseAndSwitchesViews.kt) use one identical 168x34dp rocker, three equal 54dp slots, for every app. The stop fills at BlockitSuitcaseAndSwitchesViews.kt:398-399 are SHUT = ink #252323, PEEK = grey #615B5A, OPEN = tokSurfaceBright() #FAF6F0 — porcelain, the same surfaceBright used for the Deck's raised instrument card and the receipt slip, i.e. the app's cleanest, most rewarded material is spent on the most permissive state. Unselected stop words are all the same Atkinson Bold 10sp grey, and sliding to OPEN takes exactly the same single tap/drag as sliding to SHUT, with no visual degradation, added travel, or confirmatory ugliness at the OPEN end.

Recommendation: Break the symmetry with a behavioural gradient, following Apple Screen Time, which greys a limited app's icon and badges it with an hourglass so the wrong state looks dead on sight: keep SHUT as the solid ink thumb, keep PEEK grey, but render OPEN as a hollow outline-only thumb on a faded track, drop the app name to 40% alpha with a diagonal hairline through its margin glyph position, and require a two-stage commit for OPEN only — slide to OPEN, then the thumb pulses once and must be tapped again on a chip reading 'LEAVE UNGUARDED'. SHUT and PEEK stay one gesture; OPEN becomes visibly the unprotected, unfinished state.

#### [HIGH] The signature wheel ignores the keyboard, mouse, trackpad and stylus that tablet study actually uses

RotaryWheelView is a raw Canvas View (BlockitCoreViews.kt:371) driven only by onTouchEvent (BlockitCoreViews.kt:987); grep of ui/views finds zero onGenericMotionEvent, onHoverEvent or onKeyEvent handling anywhere, and app/build.gradle.kts:86-118 pulls in no adaptive/window or input libraries. Tablets used for study routinely carry folio keyboards, trackpads, mice and styli — Android's large-screen guidelines (Tier 3 basic, Tier 1 differentiated) require keyboard/mouse/trackpad/stylus support with hover content and visible focus states, and Google Docs/Slides on tablet honour shortcuts, scroll and hover as first-class input. In Monolith a scroll-wheel resting on the duration wheel — the single most obvious desktop mapping in the whole app — does nothing; a mouse user must click-drag a pretend rotary knob, with no hover highlight on the rim, no focus ring, and arrow keys dead.

Recommendation: Give the wheel a peripheral dialect with parity of feel: mouse/trackpad scroll over the wheel steps detents (same tick sound and settle physics as a flick), ArrowUp/Down adjust by 5 minutes and Left/Right by one detent when the wheel is focused, hover draws the existing 1.3dp rim highlight, and a 2dp ink focus ring appears for keyboard focus with Enter moving focus to the slide. Apply the same hover/focus treatment to the Shield sleds and the rail. This is input design, not new features: every mapping lands on the existing onMinutesChanged path.

#### [HIGH] The FIX key's press is latched to an errand, not a finger: it stays sunk 1dp for the entire Settings trip (potentially minutes) and releases identically whether the repair worked or failed

ParkDrawer.kt:181-183 states the design in its own comment: the FIX key's dip is 'pressed on DOWN, held for the whole absence, resolved on the return'. The code does exactly that: onPress at ParkDrawer.kt:435-448 sets fixPressed=true and fires onFixClick (which leaves the app for a system Settings page), ignores tryAwaitRelease()'s result, and nothing resets the flag until the return effect at lines 195-214 waits for parkReturnTick, delays a further 800ms, and only then releases it — or until the drawer is hidden (lines 186-191). The visual itself is .offset(y = if (fixPressed) 1.dp else 0.dp) at line 431 over a flat inkControlFill with no shadow, border or clip change, so for minutes the key sits 1dp lower for no one — the user is in Settings — and on return the release is identical whether the permission was repaired or not (the only difference is a click sound, lines 205-209). park.html shows the key as an unshadowed ink slab: the 1dp offset has nothing to read against.

Recommendation: Make FIX a momentary key again: dip on DOWN, release on finger-up with the house 160ms return, exactly like the wheel hub (BlockitCoreViews.kt:475-495). If an 'errand in progress' state is wanted, invent one that is not a press — e.g. the key's label switches to the item name plus a hairline progress rule, or the key inverts to the surfaceVariant print treatment the app already uses for read-only-under-seal states. A latching, minutes-long dip follows no physical switch grammar: Braun/Rams push-keys and Moog panel buttons are either visibly latching toggles with a changed resting position, or momentary — never a momentary key frozen mid-press.

#### [HIGH] The 'mechanical sled' cannot be slid: the binary sled is a tap wearing a track, with no press state, no drag and no forgiveness

BlockitSuitcaseAndSwitchesViews.kt:168-177: SledSwitchView.onTouchEvent handles only ACTION_UP (fireFeel(8L) + onToggleRequested) and returns true for everything else — no ACTION_DOWN press pose, no ACTION_MOVE handling, no grab offset, no touch-slop or cancel path. The 'throw' is animateThrow() at :74-88: a 260ms ValueAnimator over MonolithCurves.CurveA, fired after the state has already flipped. The thumb is 54% of a 76dp track (travel ≈32dp, :134-141), yet none of that travel is touchable. park.html:83-92 renders it as a recessed mechanical track with pooled shadow and lit edges — a control that photographs as grabbable machinery and behaves as a checkbox. The in-house contradiction: the sibling AppRowSledToggleView in the same file (:432+) drags 1:1 with a VelocityTracker, so the house already owns the technique.

Recommendation: Make the binary sled a real sled, following Apple's UISwitch and iOS Slide to Unlock, both of which accept a drag as well as a tap and track the thumb under the finger with a midpoint commit: add DOWN grab with a 1dp sink and collapsed contact shadow, MOVE tracking 1:1 with commit decided by which half of the track the thumb is released in (releasing back across the midpoint cancels, firing nothing), and keep tap-to-toggle as the shortcut. One sled dialect across the app: the binary sled and the 3-stop rocker must share grab, travel and commit grammar.

#### [HIGH] The wheel never turns: knurl, ticks and numerals are screen-fixed and only a dot orbits, so the signature object is a gauge cosplaying as a dial

BlockitCoreViews.kt:673-676 states it in its own comment: 'The knurl is screen-fixed material... the swept integral lands the day the rim itself rotates.' The detent ticks are drawn at fixed minutesToAngle positions (748-795) and the rim numerals at fixed positions (793-810); the only element that moves with wheelAngleDeg is the 14dp reader dot (811-816) and the sweep arc. deck.html shows the result: a fully toothed, machined-looking disc whose teeth, including the deliberately 'broken' teeth 17 and 83, can never be seen or felt to move.

Recommendation: Choose honesty one way or the other. Preferred, following the Teenage Engineering OP-1 encoders and the original physically rotating iPod scroll wheel: make the disc a rigid rotating layer - knurl and tick ring rotate with wheelAngleDeg under a single fixed pointer at the top, numerals move off the disc into the hero readout (which already exists), so rotation, speed and direction are visible in the material itself. Or, if the fixed scale stays, strip the false affordance: delete the knurling and socket machining and present it plainly as a printed circular gauge in the Braun/Rams manner - texture that implies grip and rotation on a surface that does neither is the dishonest detail that undermines the whole instrument.

#### [HIGH] The wheel's feel secretly changes with block count: hidden 'mass' rewrites inertia, coast and capture, so the same flick lands differently on different days

BlockitCoreViews.kt:533-540 loadInertia() = 1 + 0.14 x (studyBlocksCount-1) and coastTau() rises with its square root; capture velocity is divided by sqrt(loadInertia()) at 1201 and again at 1278; the seat knock's duration, amplitude and pitch are all re-derived from block count at 543-551. Nothing on the wheel face states the current load as a number - the hub shows it only as well geometry - so the user experiences an unexplained change in how far a flick travels and how hard the wheel lands.

Recommendation: Freeze the gesture physics, following the OP-1's industrial encoders whose selling point is an indexing feel that stays consistent over the product's life: one inertia, one coast tau, one capture velocity, regardless of block count, so muscle memory learned on Monday is still true on Friday. Express 'weight' where it is visible and attributable instead - in the seat knock's pitch/volume and in the hero total - and print the block count as a numeral beside the hub so any remaining feel difference has a visible cause.

#### [HIGH] The hand is a faceless disc — and it goes dark at night, when a faceted hand should catch what light there is

BlockitCoreViews.kt:812-838: the current value is indicated by drawCircle — a 14dp flat disc with a 3dp 'dimple' and a 1dp leading line; it has no facet, no edge, no second tone, so nothing on it can catch light and split into bright/dark halves the way a dauphine hand does. At night it gets worse by design: 'at night the disc drops from the glyph tier to the sheet tone — a dark cap on the rim, not a cream slab' (paintAccent.color = tokSurfaceSheet() when isNightMode). Tanaka's multi-faceted hands exist so the pointer stays legible in the worst light; Monolith's pointer is at its least visible exactly in the armed night mode when the session is running.

Recommendation: Replace the disc with a faceted reader: a flat rectangular lozenge straddling the rim, split lengthwise into two planes — lamp-side half in the glyph tone, shadow-side half in the recess tone — in both day and night schemes, so the pointer reads by contrast within itself and never drops to the sheet tone at night.

#### [HIGH] The valve prints its only live instruction in the one place the user's thumb is guaranteed to cover

Emergency60sValveView.onDraw draws its sole status label — 'KEEP HOLDING VALVE • 42s' — centred at w*0.5f, h*0.5f at 11.5sp (BlockitSuitcaseAndSwitchesViews.kt:700-707, label built at line 683), while onTouchEvent requires the user's finger held on that same view for the full 60 seconds. Worboys principle (e) requires signs be placed so they are obscured as little as possible; here the sign is painted on the grip itself, so for the entire hold the remaining-seconds readout and the instruction sit under the thumb doing the holding, and the three label wordings (idle / holding / banked-resume, lines 683-695) swap unseen.

Recommendation: Move the readout off the grip: paint the remaining seconds as a large mono numeral fixed above the valve track (outside the touch surface) and reduce the in-bar text to a static 'HOLD' that never changes; keep the fill and its 15-second seams as the only in-bar signal, readable around a thumb.

#### [HIGH] Every app ruling is governed by two different dials in the same scroll — and the two dials have different ranges

ShieldMatrixScreen.kt:368-400 renders the YOUR RULES slip whose SlipLineRow (ShieldMatrixScreen.kt:968-1010) is a 40dp tap target that 'flips the ruling SHUT ↔ PEEK on the sled's commit path'; a few hundred dp below, the same apps appear again with AppRowSledToggleView 3-stop rockers (SHUT / PEEK / OPEN) as drawn in shield.html. The slip dial can never reach OPEN; the rocker can. One quantity, two controls, asymmetric ranges, stacked in a single column — the exact duplication a one-ring-per-function discipline exists to prevent, and a user who learns the slip's two-position grammar is miseducated for the rocker's three.

Recommendation: Strip the tap from SlipLineRow entirely: the slip becomes what its typography already claims to be — a printed standing-orders summary, read-only, dot leaders and ruling words with no commit path. The rocker remains the single dial that sets a ruling. If a fast SHUT↔PEEK flip is wanted, put it on the rocker as a long-press on its thumb, not on a second surface.

#### [HIGH] PARK is summoned by dragging into a deliberately blank stretch of rail — overscroll territory in every hand's experience

MonolithRailView.kt:20-23 'PARK is a zone the cap enters, not a stop it selects'; :30 PARK_ZONE_DP = 48f; :77-81 'at the track's end, the PARK zone — a flat 48dp stretch that prints NO word ever, because PARK is where the machine's own state lives, not a place he goes'; :63-65 stopForX returns PARK_INDEX for any x past parkStartDp, and :327-335 a drag into that blank, with resistance, seats the cap there and opens the sheet. deck.html render confirms the rail's right end is an unlabelled blank beside DECK/SHIELD/TASKS/LEDGER.

Recommendation: Print PARK in the zone in the rail's own Anonymous Pro 10sp voice, widen the zone to a full segment width so it reads as a fifth stop, and give its seat the same 4ms seat knock as the other stops. If a surface can be opened by travelling to it, its name must be written where the hand lands — no exceptions for 'machine state'.

#### [HIGH] The 'valve' is not a valve: it is a 60-second dead-man's press wearing a turn-mechanism's name

BlockitSuitcaseAndSwitchesViews.kt:532 Emergency60sValveView is a flat 68dp track filled by sustained finger pressure; :683 its holding label reads 'KEEP HOLDING VALVE'; AirlockAndDisarmOverlays.kt:801 instructs 'Hold to fill 60 seconds. Every 15 seconds banks. If your hand slips, what isn't banked drains away.' airlock.html frame 3 shows the result: a horizontal fill bar labelled as a valve. A real valve is turned or levered open and then stays open; a control that drains the moment the finger lifts is a dead-man's switch, the opposite machine.

Recommendation: Stop borrowing the valve's name for a press: redraw the control as what the hand is actually doing — a large recessed circular hold pad with a thumbprint ring that fills radially over 60 seconds — and rename every string from VALVE to 'HOLD FOR EMERGENCY BREAK', including the Deck chip and the rule line at AirlockAndDisarmOverlays.kt:801. Keep the banking/draining behaviour, which suits a dead-man's hold exactly; only the false valve costume goes.

#### [HIGH] The dial's one lateral idea — turning past the bottom until a timer becomes open-ended FLOW — is a value-less drift channel with no detent, tick or label

BlockitCoreViews.kt:525-531: valueForAngle's strait comment states 'Inside the channel there are no values at all — the nearest shore speaks' — angles below the 10-minute shore return 5 and become FLOW only by crossing; BlockitCoreViews.kt:742-743 confirms ticks/detents exist only every 5 minutes from 10 upward, so the FLOW zone has no stop, no tick and no label; BlockitCoreViews.kt:533-537 gives FLOW a real physical identity in code (loadInertia: 'FLOW rides unloaded — an open session is the lightest wheel') that the drawn scale never discloses.

Recommendation: Machine FLOW into the wheel as a first-class stop: a hard detent at the 108-degree end with its own deeper seat knock, a printed FLOW label on the scale beside the 10 stop, and a Deck eyebrow that reads 'FLOW — NO END SET' once it engages. One added stop converts a hidden crossing into the dial's signature move.

#### [HIGH] The Airlock's five seconds of forced boredom are spent watching an 88sp countdown — contemplation replaced by clock-watching

AirlockAndDisarmOverlays.kt:562-571 runs a 5-second countdown loop and :635-641 renders it as an 88sp 'Hero Architectural Countdown Numeral' — the single largest glyph on the intercept screen. The one interval in the product where the user is forced to do nothing is filled with a number to watch descend, so the urge is never actually sat with; attention is parked on a clock, the shallowest form of waiting. Han's deep attention is precisely the capacity to endure unfilled time, and Monolith fills its only empty room with a readout.

Recommendation: Empty the wall: remove the countdown numeral from the Airlock overlay — the screen shows the app name and the session intention on a still ground, and the RETURN/PEEK options simply appear when the interval ends, with no ticking, no numeral and no progress cue. Boredom that announces its own remaining seconds trains nothing.

#### [HIGH] The Airlock collects flow's own diagnostic — stuck, bored, habit — and treats all three with the same wall: the reason selector, the coaching tips and the micro-step split are all built and none are reachable

MonolithModels.kt:195-218 defines DistractionTriggerReason with exactly Csikszentmihalyi's two off-channel states plus habit — STUCK_ON_PROBLEM (challenge above skill, coachingTip: 'Break the current task into a 10-minute micro-step'), BORED_OR_TIRED (skill above challenge), MUSCLE_MEMORY — yet no UI ever renders a coachingTip (grep of ui/ finds none) and the Airlock body (AirlockAndDisarmOverlays.kt:605-720) never calls its own onSelectReason parameter (declared line 552, unused): every intercept, whatever its cause, gets the identical 5-second wall, RETURN TO FOCUS and EMERGENCY PEEK. The one recalibration the tips prescribe exists as MonolithViewModel.splitActiveTaskAndReturn (MonolithViewModel.kt:1967-1983, which records the intercept as STUCK_ON_PROBLEM and splits the task) but has no call site in any screen. The app wrote the diagnosis, wrote the treatment, and connected neither to the door where the patient arrives.

Recommendation: Turn the Airlock into a channel check with three reason chips under the countdown — STUCK / BORED / HABIT (the existing enum, its shortTags already stored on intercepts) — and branch the verbs on the answer: STUCK replaces EMERGENCY PEEK with 'SPLIT INTO A 10-MIN STEP' wired to the existing splitActiveTaskAndReturn, returning the user to a smaller goal; BORED offers 'TIGHTEN: LOCK PEEK FOR THIS BLOCK' instead of a peek; HABIT keeps today's breath-and-return. Print the matching coachingTip as the Airlock's body copy. Same door, three different treatments, chosen by the signal only the user can give at that second.

#### [HIGH] The emergency valve drains on a slipped grip — it taxes fine-motor error at the moment of least gumption

BlockitSuitcaseAndSwitchesViews.kt:560-563 implements a drain state (isDraining, drainStartMs, drainFromMs) that erodes unbanked hold progress whenever the grip slips, and AirlockAndDisarmOverlays.kt:801 states the terms to the user mid-emergency: 'If your hand slips, what isn't banked drains away.' Banking only lands every 15 seconds (bankIntervalMs = totalMs/4, :565), so a slip at 14.9s erases the whole segment. A genuine emergency — shaking hand, a child, a call that must be answered — is precisely the moment of lowest gumption in Pirsig's taxonomy, and that is the moment Monolith chooses to fine motor error with lost time.

Recommendation: Remove the drain from Emergency60sValveView: held time becomes monotonic within an Airlock visit — a slip pauses the fill, it never reverses it; the 60 seconds is accumulated grip time across slips. Update the :801 copy to say so: 'Hold to fill 60 seconds. Let go and it waits where it is. Nothing you have held is taken back.'

#### [HIGH] The only real play in the app — the wheel — is switched off at the seal, leaving the session itself with nothing to operate, only to endure

The one genuinely playable system in the app is the RotaryWheelView: detent ticks and synth clicks at every minute crossing (BlockitCoreViews.kt:369), load-dependent inertia where 'the block count has mass' (BlockitCoreViews.kt:533-538), coast, seat knocks weighted by count. Operating it is play in the strict sense — a system felt from inside its constraints. But at the seal its isLockedSession setter calls stopPhysics() and halts the wheel outright (BlockitCoreViews.kt:409-419), and nothing playable replaces it for the length of the session: the hours the product is actually about contain no system to operate, only a countdown to endure and counters that accrue. Play is used as the doorman and dismissed before the main event.

Recommendation: Give the sealed session a playable, scoreless instrument on the Shield/Deck: the same wheel, reborn as a free-spinning fidget during Safe Breaks and on the active Deck — full inertia, detents and seat knocks, changing nothing, counting nothing, unlocking nothing. Print one line under it: 'IT DOES NOTHING.' A focus app honest about play lets the hands play precisely where play buys nothing.

#### [HIGH] The user is never a maker: Munari's workshop is inverted into a lottery that hands him a finished object he did not create

Munari's workshops (Brera 1977, Giocare con l'arte) and his design method make the participant a maker: you learn a form by constructing it, not by receiving it finished. In Monolith the user authors nothing playful anywhere. The curio is chosen for him by lot (MonolithRepository.kt:2050 shuffled().first()), the Cabinet detail in DrawerScreen.kt ends at the record with explicitly no SELECT verb (comment DRW-06: 'no SELECT verb, no SELECTED state'), and even his one expressive act in the Drawer is picking from a closed word list — DayWordStore/MonolithRepository.kt:156 DAY_WORDS = REST / ILL / FAMILY only. He is a defendant who occasionally receives a toy he did not make, choose or configure.

Recommendation: Turn one Cabinet page into a workshop bench: on the Harmonic Loop detail, let the user set the two wave frequencies and phase with two plain sliders and watch his own figure close or fail to close; save his variant under his own title beside Toy 01, unscored, unjudged and never compared to a correct figure. Making, not receiving, becomes the app's one creative act.

#### [MEDIUM] The Deck's task row hides two of its three controls: the title and QUEUE are secret buttons dressed as print

TactileDeckScreen.kt:799-815: the NOW task title carries a Modifier.clickable that toggles stepsExpanded when subSteps exist — but it is rendered as plain 15sp Atkinson text, single-line ellipsis, with no chevron, no step count, nothing distinguishing it from a static label; a user whose task title is truncated cannot even read it in full, let alone discover it opens. TactileDeckScreen.kt:843-855: 'QUEUE ${queuedTasks.size}' is likewise clickable (onOpenTaskSequencer) while styled as a static 11sp mono count in onSurfaceVariant grey. Between them, DONE alone gets the raised keycap treatment (lines 828-842) — so on one row, the two navigation controls dress as print and the one verb dresses as a key. deck.html's task row shows exactly this: NOW + title + DONE keycap + QUEUE 2, with no affordance difference between the tappable title/queue and static text.

Recommendation: Spend the affordance the row already spends on DONE, twice more, in an afternoon: append a disclosure marker to the title when subSteps exist ('▾ 3 STEPS' in the existing 10.5sp mono plate style, rotating to ▴ when expanded, as in Things 3's checklist disclosure), and promote QUEUE to the same keycap grammar as DONE/FLOW with a trailing arrow ('QUEUE 2 ›'). Braun's rule applies literally: a control must look like a control — nothing on the app's home row should be a secret button.

#### [MEDIUM] FLOW is a lone keycap in a half-empty row duplicating a seat the wheel already has

TactileDeckScreen.kt:714-741: under the 288dp wheel sits a SpaceBetween row whose only content is a FLOW keycap (11sp, :728) that calls onSelectStudyPreset(STOPWATCH_FLOW) and onDialMinutesChanged(5) (:722-723). The row's right half is deliberately empty — the comment at :736 records 'the FINISHES line dies here', leaving a visibly orphaned pill floating at the card's left edge in deck.html (.flowrow with an empty second div). The control is also redundant twice over: dialMinutes < 10 already IS stopwatch mode in the engine (TactileDeckScreen.kt isStopwatchMode derivation), the hero already renames itself 'FLOW' in that state (:642), and the wheel itself already reserves a FLOW seat — BlockitCoreViews.kt:677 cuts the knurl 'across FLOW's basin (+/-13.5 of the FLOW seat)'.

Recommendation: Delete the FLOW keycap and its whole row (reclaiming the row height and the card's 10dp gap). Put FLOW where the wheel already seats it: label the wheel's sub-10 position 'FLOW' on the detent scale itself, the way a Leica/Fujifilm mode dial prints A and M on the same dial that selects everything else — one control, modes as its own detents, no satellite button restating a position the dial already has.

#### [MEDIUM] Detent hierarchy is arithmetic, not behavioural: the app's own default 50 and the canonical 25 are third-class minor ticks

BlockitCoreViews.kt:748-752 classifies stops purely by divisibility - majors every 30 min, mids every 15 - numerals are printed only for 30..180 step 30 (801-810), and the haptic ladder at 1173 gives the longer 4ms tick only when newValue % 15 == 0. So 50, the shipped default (minutesValue=50, BlockitCoreViews.kt:373), and 25, the Pomodoro length this product category runs on, receive the weakest tick, the shortest haptic and no numeral, while 30/60/90 - numbers nobody specifically aims for - get the landmarks. deck.html render shows 30/60/90/120/150/180 as the only printed numbers on the rim.

Recommendation: Re-tier the scale around behaviour, the way a watch bezel privileges 12/3/6/9 over the other numerals: give 25 and 50 a major-class tick, a printed numeral and the strong detent haptic, keep 100/120 as secondary landmarks, and demote the bare multiples of 30 to mid class. A user should be able to find 25 and 50 by feel and by landmark counting from the nearest printed number, without counting minor ticks.

#### [MEDIUM] Precision feedback sits exactly under the fingertip: the reader dot, its leading-edge pip and the passing ticks are occluded at the moment of aiming

The reader is a 14dp dot placed on rimR at the active angle (BlockitCoreViews.kt:811-816) - precisely the annulus a dragging fingertip (roughly 40dp+ of contact) covers - and its finest orientation cue, a 1dp leading-edge marker line and 6dp dimple, is drawn on that same dot. The major ticks and rim numerals it passes (748-810) lie on the same occluded ring, and there is no loupe, offset pointer or duplicated reader anywhere else on the surface; deck.html shows the dot and scale sharing the rim with no second readout of dial position besides the hero's total.

Recommendation: Borrow the offset-readout solution from the Galaxy Watch rotating bezel and the iOS text loupe: the finger works an edge, the reading happens somewhere it cannot cover. Either move the drag surface inward (relative strokes on the disc face, per the click-wheel redesign, leaving the rim scale permanently visible) or add a fixed needle at 12 o'clock plus a magnified callout of the three nearest detents that appears beside, not under, the touch point while dragging. The 1dp pip line should be deleted or enlarged - a direction cue that only exists when no finger is present is decoration, not feedback.

#### [MEDIUM] Session length is built to two incompatible modules: the hand dial stops at 180 minutes, routines run to 1080

The same dimension — how long a session runs — is manufactured to two incompatible modules. The hand dial clamps to 3..180 minutes (MonolithViewModel setDialMinutes: minutes.coerceIn(3, 180)), while the routine module clamps its window to 30..1080 minutes (RoutineSchedule.durationMinutes, MonolithModels.kt:578-586), and the shipped seed routines use spans far beyond the dial's reach (630-minute DAY BLOCKS-class windows, MonolithRepository.kt:842-850). The owner therefore cannot reproduce their own longest routine by hand — the part does not exist in the hand system's range — and cannot make a routine shorter than 30 minutes though the dial happily builds 5-minute sessions. 606 uprights accept every component along one continuous slot; Monolith's two editors measure the same quantity on two non-overlapping scales, so a configuration proven in one half of the product is inexpressible in the other.

Recommendation: Unify session length on one DurationSpec (3..1080 minutes, one stepping law) consumed by both the Deck wheel and the routine editor: the wheel gains a second, hours ring past 180 minutes instead of a hard stop, and the routine editor's start/end steppers accept the same 3-minute floor as the dial. Any length buildable in one editor must be buildable in the other, unchanged.

#### [MEDIUM] The Airlock doorway withholds the menu until the wait is over: the peek is not even composed during the 5-second countdown, so the guest cannot read its price or decide while standing there

AirlockAndDisarmOverlays.kt:562-569 runs the 5s countdown; line 636-639 renders it as an 88sp numeral; the EMERGENCY PEEK chip exists only under 'if (countdownSecs == 0 && state.canUse2MinutePeek)' (line 663) and the refusal text only under 'countdownSecs == 0 && !canUse2MinutePeek' (line 690). During the entire wait the only composed verb is RETURN TO FOCUS (line 656). A host who makes a guest wait at the door at least lets them read what is on offer; Monolith sequences the information after the penance — the guest spends five seconds unable to weigh the 2-minute peek against its 20-minute cooldown because neither the offer nor its price exists on screen yet.

Recommendation: Compose the full doorway at t=0: render the EMERGENCY PEEK chip from the first frame in a disabled state with its price line ('TAKING THE PEEK STARTS A 20 MINUTES COOLDOWN') already printed beneath it, and draw the countdown as a shrinking ring around the chip's badge instead of a standalone 88sp numeral. The five seconds become decision time the guest can use, not dead time served before the choices are revealed.

### Information architecture — 54 findings (21 critical, 26 high, 7 medium, 0 low)

#### [CRITICAL] Repair order #2: the Deck has six equal citizens and no first action — demote telemetry so duration + task + slide are the only above-fold elements

deck.html shows six competing blocks before the arm action: a 47dp header (MONOLITH / GUARD 4/4), the instrument card with a 72sp Sora hero (Type.kt:63 DialClockTextStyle), a 288px rotary wheel, a task row, a pinned telemetry strip whose cells are all PillBadgeTextStyle 10sp mono (Type.kt:85), and only then the 72dp slide-to-arm track. The duration is the largest type but the task — what the session is for — is a single 15sp row mid-screen, and guard status, totals and queue all carry the same 10sp plate treatment, so nothing tells a first-time user what to do first.

Recommendation: Priority 2 — rebuild the Deck as a single-decision screen, following the iOS Clock Timer tab: the picker IS the screen, the task is its subtitle, and one Start control is the only saturated element. Specifically: Deck above the fold becomes duration hero + active task title at DrawerHeaderTextStyle 22sp (Type.kt:95) + slide-to-arm; GUARD counts, totals and the pinned strip move to the Shield/PARK surfaces where they are acted on. This outranks icon, illustration and brand work because the home screen's job — arm the right session in under five seconds — currently fails before any of those are even seen.

#### [CRITICAL] CUT 1 — Delete the YOUR RULES slip: Shield prints its entire catalogue twice, in two different languages

ShieldMatrixScreen.kt:342-410 builds 'SECTION 3.5: YOUR RULES — THE STANDING ORDERS SLIP' as a full second list (SlipHeaderRow, StandingTallyLine, one 40dp SlipLineRow per SHUT/PEEK app, ShieldMatrixScreen.kt:968-1050, dot leader = ' .'.repeat(90)), then Sections 4-5 immediately re-list the same apps as CatalogueAppRow rockers (shield.html: the slip prints INSTAGRAM/REDDIT/X PEEK and CHROME/SNAPCHAT/TIKTOK/YOUTUBE SHUT, then ALL APPS prints the same 10 apps again with SHUT/PEEK/OPEN sleds). Two editable surfaces, two grammars (dot-leader ledger vs 168dp rocker) for one decision; the slip alone costs roughly 350dp of scroll before the real editor is reached.

Recommendation: Delete the slip section entirely — header, tally block, PEEK/SHUT subheads and SlipLineRow. Keep only its tally as the single right-hand count on the ALL APPS header ('10 APPS · 4 SHUT · 3 PEEK · 3 OPEN') and keep the rocker as the one place a ruling is made or revoked. This follows the iOS Focus settings decision: one alphabetical app list with one control per app, no summary ledger printed above the list it summarises. Gain: Shield's first screen becomes Loadout + Routines + the start of the actual catalogue, and no user ever has to learn that tapping a printed line secretly edits it.

#### [CRITICAL] Sequence 2 — The Scaffold chrome (header band + rail) before any destination: it is the only frame present on every screen

MainActivity.kt:409-421 creates one Scaffold hosting MonolithPullDownHeader for all destinations, MainActivity.kt:440-468 runs one AnimatedContent tab transition, and MainActivity.kt:~695-735 mounts one 52dp MonolithRailView (a Canvas AndroidView, MonolithRailView.kt:98, whose isNightMode is pumped in manually rather than inherited from Compose theme). deck.html and receipt.html frame 3 show the identical product of it: 47dp header with MONOLITH 10sp / GUARD 4/4 and the 52dp DECK/SHIELD/TASKS/LEDGER rail under unrelated content. Park rises under this header and above this rail (MainActivity.kt:~640-670), so even overlays inherit it.

Recommendation: Second, redesign only the frame as a wayfinding system, following Kinneir & Calvert's British road-sign system and the Transport typeface: one typeface/weight for all sign text, fixed sign positions, destinations named by function. Spec: header becomes a 56dp status sign (left: wordmark; right: guard state as shape + word, never number alone), rail becomes a 64dp labelled navigation bar with icon + word per stop in Atkinson 12sp sentence case, and the rail is rewritten in Compose so it consumes the Step-1 tokens directly instead of hand-pumped night flags. Freeze it; destinations redesigned later must fit inside it unchanged.

#### [CRITICAL] Deck screenshot reads as a safe dial / kitchen timer, not a focus session: the biggest object on the home screen explains nothing

deck.html: the frame's dominant area is a 288dp rotary wheel numbered 30/60/90/120/150/180 with no unit printed, under a 72sp hero '1H 50M' whose only label is the eyebrow 'TOTAL' (TactileDeckScreen.kt:618); the wheel's own mode word is 'FLOW' (TactileDeckScreen.kt:641,728) and the sole action sentence, 'SLIDE OR TAP TO START' (BlockitCoreViews.kt:2407), is 10sp mono centred inside a 72dp dark bar at the very bottom, below a strip reading 'BLOCK ON · APPS 12 · TIME ENDS 10:40 · BIND HELD · PROOF: LIVE BIND'. No word 'focus', 'study', 'block apps' or 'session' appears at readable size anywhere in the screenshot; 'MONOLITH' and 'GUARD 4/4' in the header are 10sp and 15sp mono.

Recommendation: Give the screenshot one plain-English sentence at hero scale, following Forest — whose home screenshot is a growing tree, a countdown and the line 'Put down your phone', so subject, verb and stake are read in one glance: replace the 'TOTAL' eyebrow with an Atkinson 17sp sentence that recomputes live, e.g. 'Focus for 1H 50M — 9 apps stay shut', print 'MINUTES' once under the wheel's 90 detent, and move the start instruction out of the slide track into a 15sp label directly above it ('Slide to start focusing'). Keep the wheel; make it the illustration of a sentence, not a substitute for one.

#### [CRITICAL] Guard board gives screen-reading, message-reading and battery exemption identical visual weight — no scope, no consequence, no difference

park.html renders nine identical ruled lines: 10sp Anonymous Pro name left, 15sp Atkinson GRANTED/MISSING right, no icon, no colour difference beyond lack printing in darker ink (ParkDrawer.kt:338-365, ParkBoardRow). ACCESSIBILITY sits in the same format as BATTERY, yet accessibility_service_config.xml:6 sets canRetrieveWindowContent=true and strings.xml:4 describes it only as detecting launches, while the notification listener in practice reads other apps' message title+body. WatchStore.kt:80-89 gives all six only a boardName string — the data model itself carries no scope, sensitivity or consequence field for the UI to print. Android's own system dialog for this grant warns the app can view and control the screen; one sec's setup names that capability in plain language before sending the user to that dialog. Monolith sends them via a bare FIX key with no equivalent framing.

Recommendation: Rebuild each board row as a two-line trust entry following Apple's Privacy Nutrition Label pattern (capability grouped, named in plain words, comparable at a glance): line 1 name + state, line 2 a fixed scope sentence — ACCESSIBILITY: 'Sees which app is in front and reads its window to catch Shorts/Reels and blocked sites'; NOTIFICATION LISTENER: 'Reads notification title and text on this phone to hold them until the session ends'; BATTERY: 'Stops Android putting the shield to sleep'. Group the six under two subheads — SEES YOUR SCREEN AND MESSAGES (accessibility, usage, notification listener) vs KEEPS ITSELF ALIVE (device admin, overlay, battery) — so visual weight follows actual sensitivity, and repeat the scope sentence on the FIX confirmation before the Settings trip.

#### [CRITICAL] The planner has no time plane: a serial tear-off pad where YPT and every paper timetable put tasks on a clock grid

FocusSequencerScreen.kt: the whole planner is a LazyColumn headed only 'HORIZON' (~L185) and 'QUEUE', followed by leaves numbered '#01 · #02' (TaskLeafItem ~L580) in tap order; no hour ruler, date header, start time or day column exists anywhere in the file. deck.html confirms the disconnect in the product: the Deck separately prints 'ENDS 10:40' in its proof strip, but no queue item is ever placed against that clock. YPT's Planner (per its Play listing and Planner sync descriptions) is the opposite decision: a vertical timeline in 10-minute cells where the todo is placed at a time, beside the calendar, so planned and recorded time share one ruler. A paper school timetable does the same in two dimensions — days across, periods down, cell height = duration — so collisions, gaps and overload are visible before the day starts.

Recommendation: Replace the order-only pad as the planner's primary view with a single-day time plane: a vertical 07:00–23:00 ruler in 10-minute rows following YPT's Planner, each leaf occupying the rows its session will take and anchored to a start time derived from the Deck wheel; keep the tear-off leaf as the row's content, not as the whole planner. Unscheduled tasks sit in a narrow 'UNPLACED' rail beside the ruler, visibly unplanned, until dragged onto a time. If a queue would end after 23:00 or overlap a routine window, the ruler shows it in the accent — that collision warning is the planner's job.

#### [CRITICAL] Dateless board: the first screen of the day never names the day, date or hour it is arming for

deck.html: header band is only 'MONOLITH' + 'GUARD 4/4', card eyebrow is only 'TOTAL', hero is the span '1H 50M', and the sole clock reference anywhere is the strip's 'ENDS 10:40'. TactileDeckScreen.kt:617-618 the idle eyebrow can only print TOTAL (or SESSION RUNNING / BREAK when running) — no date, weekday, or time-of-day branch exists. MainActivity.kt:420 the header band is specified as 'brand + Guard line' and nothing else. The data layer already knows the user's day precisely — DrawerDay.kt:8-23 files the day from 03:30 because 'he wakes at 03:30' — but no Deck code ever reads filingDate, so that knowledge never reaches the surface the user actually starts the day on.

Recommendation: Give the Deck a masthead, following the newspaper / iOS wake-up-screen decision that the first surface names its moment: add a second header line under MONOLITH in Anonymous Pro 10sp tracked 2sp printing the filing date and daypart from DrawerDay.filingDate — e.g. 'FRI 30 OCT · MORNING' before noon, '· EVENING' after 18:00 — and change the idle eyebrow from bare TOTAL to 'TODAY · TOTAL' on the first open after the 03:30 boundary. No new data is needed; the filing-day clock already exists.

#### [CRITICAL] Three denominations, three unrelated drawings, never co-present: the token is a chip badge, the brick lives in a view no screen composes, the curio is a text list

The token's only drawing anywhere is a mono badge on the Deck's disarm chip: TactileDeckScreen.kt:1048, monoBadge = "$weeklyEmergencyTokensRemaining/1 WEEK" on the 58dp EMERGENCY BREAK VALVE chip. The brick's only drawing is ui/views/BlockitTowerFadersAndCatalogViews.kt TowerStreakView (line 24) — imported at AirlockAndDisarmOverlays.kt:62 but never instantiated anywhere in the app, so its grid of laid/ghost bricks (lines 111-141) renders on no screen; the Drawer render's own caption confirms 'There is no tower, no bricks, no streak and no total anywhere on this screen.' The curio, the third denomination, is a text list in the Cabinet (drawer.html frame 2). No surface ever draws two denominations in the same row, so the user can never read total wealth or any exchange between token, brick and curio in one glance — unlike Duolingo's persistent top bar, which keeps gems, streak and hearts co-drawn in one wallet strip on every screen.

Recommendation: Give the economy one shared ledger line, drawn in the existing Anonymous Pro badge grammar, and seat it in three places: under the Deck header beside GUARD 4/4, at the top of the Airlock card, and as the Receipt's closing lines — 'TOKEN 1/1 · BRICKS 24' (curios stay in the Cabinet; they are collection, not currency). One component, one grammar, everywhere a decision is made; retire the lone badge on the disarm chip, which prices only the exit and only after the session has started.

#### [CRITICAL] Day 7 and day 30 are not merely uncelebrated — they are uncomputable: no start date is kept and the history screen's charter bans the counts an anniversary needs

No install date, first-session date or day-count is stored anywhere in data/ (grep of MonolithModels.kt / MonolithRepository.kt finds no such field; the only date anchors are per-session wall times and MonolithWeek.weekAnchorMillis for the emergency token, MonolithRepository.kt:2178). The one screen that holds history forbids the reckoning by charter: DrawerScreen.kt:58-65 — 'It is not a dashboard, report card or attendance book: no totals, no streaks, no percentages, no counts, no summons.' drawer.html confirms the consequence: days with no stored task and no declared word render literally nothing — no heading, no mark — so a 30-day relationship with the app has no continuous surface on which an anniversary could ever appear.

Recommendation: Break the charter once, narrowly, for anniversaries — the way Apple's Fitness Awards tab sits apart from the daily rings as a permanent gallery of dated milestone badges, and Duolingo's milestone screen knows the streak's start. Persist a single first-sealed-session date at the first receipt claim (ReceiptState claim path already exists). In the Drawer, render only three extra day-headings ever — 'DAY 7', 'DAY 30', 'DAY 100' — in the existing 11sp mono heading style beside that date, with the day's stored rows beneath as usual. No streak counter, no totals wall: one dated heading per threshold preserves the anti-dashboard stance while making the anniversary representable at all.

#### [CRITICAL] One warrant, four printings: GUARD, BLOCK, BIND and PROOF all announce the same fact in one viewport

deck.html: header prints 'GUARD 4/4' (MonolithCustomComponents.kt:251 MonolithPullDownHeader, guard text 15sp at line ~285), the pinned strip prints BLOCK 'ON' (ProofStripBand, MonolithCustomComponents.kt:644, 53dp at :659), its 12dp seam prints 'BIND HELD · THIS VISIT' / 'PROOF: LIVE BIND' (seamMarksFor, MonolithCustomComponents.kt:380), and the slide/imprint tense is judged off the same warrant in TactileDeckScreen.kt. Four vocabularies — GUARD, BLOCK, BIND, PROOF — for one boolean the user can summarise as 'blocking works'. Worse, the header's GUARD line only looks like print: MonolithCustomComponents.kt's header comment admits a tap on it is 'the third door into PARK', so a status readout is secretly navigation while the seam's BIND/PROOF telemetry offers no action at all.

Recommendation: Keep exactly one warrant rendering on the Deck: the strip's BLOCK cell. Delete the seam row entirely (the 53dp strip drops to ~41dp and loses its engineering-log vocabulary), and strip GUARD out of the header — the header becomes the 10sp MONOLITH nameplate alone, or the band is deleted and its PARK door gets an explicit labelled control in the rail's PARK zone. Follow Transport for London's line-status boards: each line carries exactly one status word in exactly one place, and nobody has to learn four synonyms to read it.

#### [CRITICAL] GUARD and SHIELD are synonyms assigned to two different things, so the readiness score teaches a false equivalence

deck.html and park.html show 'GUARD 4/4' as the headline readiness readout; ui/components/GuardLine.kt:13-14,39 defines that score purely as permission warrants ('GUARD 4/4', 'GUARD {n}/4 — {NAME}'). The SHIELD destination is something else entirely: ui/screens/ShieldMatrixScreen.kt:282 heads it 'LOADOUT' and ShieldMatrixScreen.kt:833-835 defines its tiers as SHUT/PEEK/OPEN app rules. A new user has no way to know GUARD (are the system's permissions granted?) and SHIELD (what have I chosen to block?) are different questions, because ordinary English treats them as the same word. GUARD 4/4 therefore reads as 'blocking is fully working' even on a Shield where every app is set OPEN.

Recommendation: Break the synonym pair, following Android Digital Wellbeing and iOS Screen Time, which never use two near-synonyms for permission state vs user rules: rename the GuardLine readout to 'PERMISSIONS 4/4' (or 'READY 4/4' when it is genuinely the arm gate) and rename the Shield destination to 'BLOCKING' or 'RULES'. Keep the word Shield, if at all, only for the live protection state during a session — one word, one referent, everywhere.

#### [CRITICAL] The Deck's fixed geometry reserves zero pixels for a second person — presence has nowhere to live

Deck render (design-renders/deck.html) shows the entire fixed geometry allocated to one operator: header is only 'MONOLITH' + 'GUARD 4/4', the instrument card is one hero readout + one rotary wheel, and the pinned zone is a 53dp proof strip + 72dp solo slide. In code, ProofStripBand is hard-built with exactly three cells — StripCell('BLOCK'), StripCell('APPS'), StripCell('TIME') — plus a 12dp seam for two machine stamps (ui/components/MonolithCustomComponents.kt:644-676), and TactileDeckScreen.kt:956-1094 wires that strip, the SlideToStartView and ImprintSlot with no other slot. There is no cell, seam, badge or margin anywhere on the home screen where a second human could appear, even as a single initial. Forest makes the opposite home-screen decision: Plant Together is a two-person icon on the main page opening Create Room / Join Room with a shareable room code, so the partner is a first-class object of the home surface before any timer starts.

Recommendation: Do not bolt a friends tab on — re-cut the proof strip, Monolith's own witness surface. Split it into two rows of fact: keep BLOCK/APPS/TIME, and strike a second 12dp seam directly under it in the same Anonymous Pro 10sp tracked style reading e.g. 'WITH A. · IN SESSION · ENDS 10:40' when paired, and 'ALONE — TAP TO INVITE' as a tappable empty state when not. The slide's centred words change from 'SLIDE OR TAP TO START' to 'SLIDE TO START WITH A.' once a partner has joined, following Forest's decision to put the room affordance on the home screen itself, translated into Monolith's strip-and-seam instrument language.

#### [CRITICAL] The archive's unit is a finished task, not an attended period — a witness cannot read a week or a lesson at a glance

drawer.html landing groups history only as calendar days of completed tasks; DrawerScreen.kt:886-930 StoredRow prints only title, categoryTag, clockTime(completedAtMillis) and spentLabel — no session, no ATTENDED/PARTIAL/MISSED verdict, no routine window. ReceiptSheet.kt is single-session only. ParkDrawer.kt:109-124 PLATE_BODY ends 'STUDY HOURS: IN YPT', exporting the aggregate elsewhere. Opal's managed model (apk-re/opal/EVIDENCE.md §5, §10.3) is built around distracting_usage_reports and a daily compliance report per managed rule/group — the witness's unit is the period, not the task.

Recommendation: Design a Witness period view with the period as the header, following Opal's daily-report unit: 'WEEK OF 27 OCT — Attended 4 · Partial 1 · Missed 1 · 6h 10m focused of 7h planned', then one plain row per session (date, intention, planned, focused, verdict word in full). Re-group the Drawer for this view by routine window / week, not by task-completion day; tasks become a secondary line under each session.

#### [CRITICAL] Arming is serialised across three tabs on a canvas wide enough to hold the whole decision at once

MainActivity.kt:442 hosts exactly one destination at a time in AnimatedContent (DECK/SHIELD/TASKS/VAULT are mutually exclusive), and TactileDeckScreen.kt:705 fixes the wheel at 288dp tall inside a single scroll column (deck.html render: wheel card, one NOW task row, then the pinned BLOCK/APPS/TIME proof strip — nothing beside anything). On an 840dp+ tablet the three facts that define a session — the task queue (Tasks), the duration/block plan (Deck wheel), and what will be shut (Shield tally) — can never be co-visible, so the student arms from memory after tab-hopping. Material 3's SupportingPaneScaffold exists precisely for this: dominant primary pane (~2/3) plus a permanently visible supporting pane (~1/3) for tools/context on expanded width. YPT's tablet surface likewise keeps the timer and the study material in one frame instead of serial screens.

Recommendation: At expanded width (>=840dp) rebuild the Deck as a supporting-pane layout: left pane keeps the instrument card (wheel + hero readout) at its natural ~420dp measure; right supporting pane (~360dp, hairline-divided, same paper tokens) shows the live task queue with NOW pinned, the proof strip (BLOCK/APPS/TIME) and the intention — all live while the wheel turns. The slide-to-start stays under the wheel pane only. Below 840dp collapse back to today's single column unchanged. No new data needed: every value already flows into MonolithRootApp in MainActivity.kt.

#### [CRITICAL] SHIELD is a junk-drawer destination: session config, scheduling, standing rules, the app catalogue and the website editor stacked in one six-section scroll

ShieldMatrixScreen.kt:282 (SECTION 1 LOADOUT cap), :299-303 (SECTION 3 ROUTINES), :342 (SECTION 3.5 YOUR RULES slip), :431 (SECTION 4 search/category), :505 (SECTION 5 app tier rows), :532-541 (SECTION 6 BLOCKED WEBSITES) — six numbered sections in one LazyColumn; shield.html shows the same single endless column. Routines are automation that fires when the user is absent; websites are a text list edited rarely; the catalogue is ~100 rows of per-app rules — three different visit frequencies forced into one scroll, with the most-edited thing (app tiers, section 5) below the least-edited (routines, section 3).

Recommendation: Split SHIELD by job, following iOS Screen Time's separation of Downtime (schedule), App Limits (rules) and Communication Limits into named sub-entries under one hub: make SHIELD a short hub index — LOADOUT stays as the session-config face, ROUTINES becomes its own screen reached from a hub row (and cross-linked from the Deck, where time is set), and the catalogue + websites become one RULES screen. Nothing on the hub scrolls; every job is one labelled row deep, the way Screen Time's settings list works.

#### [CRITICAL] No danger zone: protection-killing sleds and the cosmetic sound sled are the same object on the same panel

park.html and ParkDrawer.kt:79-82 state the law verbatim: 'one tone (the ground), everything print except the FIX key... orange zero.' The consequence is visible in park.html: SOUND EFFECTS (ParkDrawer.kt:479), SHORTS + REELS (ParkDrawer.kt:548) and the SOCIAL SITES sled inside ParkSocialSitesRow (ParkDrawer.kt:699) all use the identical 76x34dp chrome sled, identical 10sp plate label and identical ON/OFF margin word. Nothing in spacing, colour, border, grouping or copy distinguishes 'turning this off silences a click' from 'turning this off disables site blocking / the Shorts sniper'. WatchStore.kt:457-461 shows the protection sleds depend on accessibility/usage parents — they are load-bearing, the sound sled is not.

Recommendation: Create a real danger zone. Split Park below the board into two labelled, materially different groups: PROTECTION (Social Sites, Shorts + Reels sleds seated in a recessed, bordered well with a consequence line under each, e.g. 'OFF = INSTAGRAM.COM OPENS IN CHROME') and PREFERENCES (Sound, Theme). Give protection sleds a guarded treatment following cockpit practice — a two-step or press-and-hold throw, or at minimum a distinct thumb colour/shape — so a protection change can never be made with the same casual flick as a sound change.

#### [CRITICAL] Shield draws the same phone twice in two incompatible diagrams — no single schematic survives

ShieldMatrixScreen.kt:148 builds rules via groupedByRule(), :223-237 slipLines() re-sorts that set alphabetically, :362-410 prints it as PEEK-then-SHUT dot-leader lines, then :508ff prints the identical apps again as CatalogueAppRow sleds in filteredApps (search/category) order, with StandingTallyLine at :359 as a third rendering of the same facts. shield.html confirms it on screen: 10 apps appear as 7 slip lines plus 10 rocker rows plus a tally on one scroll. Vignelli's 1972 diagram rule was one dot per station, one line per route, geography discarded for sequence alone — two orders for one set teach two incompatible mental maps and neither can be learned.

Recommendation: Collapse Shield to ONE diagram. Keep the slip as the sole map: alphabetical, grouped, right-hand ruling column. Delete the catalogue rocker list as a separate geography; make tapping a slip line expand its SHUT/PEEK/OPEN control in place, in that same line, so an app exists in exactly one position on the screen. Search scrolls to and highlights the line in the diagram instead of swapping in a differently ordered list.

#### [CRITICAL] The drawers are crossed: the only pullable drawer in the app is called PARK, while the thing called Drawer is never pulled open

ParkDrawer.kt:241-291: PARK is a bottom sheet with a grab strip (32dp visual, 48dp touch) whose grip grows 24dp to 28dp on DOWN and whose onVerticalDrag carries the sheet 1:1 by fraction — a textbook drawer pull. By contrast DrawerScreen.kt is a LazyColumn of tappable rows and bare-Text BACK clickables with no pull, handle or drag-to-open anywhere, and it is not even reached under its own name: MonolithRailView.kt:34 WORDS = DECK, SHIELD, TASKS, LEDGER, so the 'Drawer' is entered by tapping LEDGER.

Recommendation: Uncross the two: give the archive the drawer grammar it is named for — open the Drawer as a pulled sheet from the rail with the same 48dp-touch grip PARK already implements, labelled DRAWER on the rail — and demote PARK to an ordinary labelled stop that opens with a tap, since its contents (sled settings) have no pulling behaviour of their own. One name, one motion, everywhere.

#### [CRITICAL] The Guard board is a parts bin, not a signal path: nine lines in inventory order with the stage break deliberately left as blank whitespace

ParkDrawer.kt:336 renders 'nine ruled lines, fixed order' straight from WatchItemId's enum order (WatchStore.kt board order: ACCESSIBILITY, USAGE ACCESS, DEVICE ADMIN, NOTIFICATION LISTENER, OVERLAY, BATTERY, then SHORTS + REELS, SOCIAL SITES, NOTIFICATIONS). ParkDrawer.kt:353-354 states the design law explicitly: 'The doubled gap: 16dp, no hairline, no eyebrow — the family break is whitespace, not a heading.' The park.html render confirms it on screen: two unlabelled groups separated by blank space, no arrows, no stage names, no flow cue of any kind. Yet the underlying system IS a chain — grants feed the accessibility/usage watch, the watch feeds three interceptors, the interceptors produce a verdict — and that chain exists only in WatchStore.kt's derivation code, never on the glass.

Recommendation: Redraw the board as a signal path, top to bottom in flow order: stage band 1 labelled GRANT (the six permissions), stage band 2 labelled WATCH (accessibility + usage as the sensing stage), stage band 3 labelled INTERCEPT (the three interceptors), stage band 4 labelled VERDICT. Print each stage name as a small engraved plate at the left of its band — the way a Minimoog panel prints OSCILLATOR BANK / MIXER / MODIFIERS / OUTPUT over its groups — and run a single hairline spine down the left margin connecting the bands so the eye travels the chain. Move BATTERY and OVERLAY out of the grant band into a side PLANT group (power and display are utilities, not signal stages).

#### [CRITICAL] The Deck's scale budget is spent on the tool's own variable: duration is the 72sp hero printed three times, the work it protects is a one-line caption

deck.html render of TactileDeckScreen: the hero card's centre is '1 H 50 M' in Sora Bold 72sp, printed three times in ghost layers (.g1/.g2 offset copies under .main), above a 288dp duration wheel (30–180) — together roughly 460dp of the 844dp frame devoted to choosing and displaying Monolith's parameter. The actual work appears once, as a single 15sp row: 'NOW Finish Chapter 4 Problem Set (#1–6) · QUEUE 2'. The pinned strip underneath reports the tool's standing ('BLOCK ON · APPS 12 · TIME ENDS 10:40') and the slide zone instructs the user in operating the apparatus ('SLIDE OR TAP TO START'). Every large thing on the home screen refers to Monolith; the only thing that refers beyond it — the chapter — is the smallest text on the card. That is the referential whole inverted: circumspection should rest on the work, with the tool transparent beneath it.

Recommendation: Swap the hierarchy on the unarmed Deck: the task takes the hero card — active task title at display size with its next substep under it — and duration demotes to the mono caption line the strip already uses ('1H 50M · ENDS 10:40'). Collapse the wheel to a ~96dp strip beneath the task card and delete the two ghost copies of the total. The slide's sentence slot prints the task title, not operating instructions.

#### [CRITICAL] The plan never shows its openings: OPEN apps exist only as a tally number, never as a readable list

The standing-orders slip — the one place the user's built rules are read back as a book — prints only two sections: PEEK lines (ShieldMatrixScreen.kt:362) and SHUT lines (line 383). OPEN exists solely as arithmetic: openCount = allApps.size - shutCount - peekCount (line 149), rendered as a tally number. Yet OPEN is the safety-critical set: SLEEP's exceptions are decided by a five-substring whitelist buried in the repository (MonolithRepository.kt:1152-1162: dialer/phone/clock/alarm/maps), and no surface ever lists, as a set, which apps a chosen loadout leaves reachable. Mari's drawing sheets showed every board, including the gaps; a maker who cannot see the holes in the wall they built cannot judge it — least of all the night loadout that decides whether an alarm or a parent's call app survives.

Recommendation: Complete the book: add an OPEN section to the slip under SHUT, listing every OPEN app by name in the same dot-leader grammar, and when the cap rests on SLEEP, head that section with the line 'THESE STAY REACHABLE ALL NIGHT'. Tapping an OPEN line flips it to SHUT on the same commit path as the other sections, so the exceptions are as buildable — and as visible — as the blocks.

#### [HIGH] No subject identity anywhere: exam season is five subjects and five papers, but Monolith's surfaces are subject-blind monochrome — tasks, routines and receipts never say which subject a block belongs to

Monolith has exactly one buried trace of subject thinking: data/MonolithModels.kt:180 gives category 'exam' a fixed 3-step sub-step template ('First pass without reference notes'…), but no surface ever prints a subject. design-renders/deck.html: the task is a single undifferentiated NOW line ('Finish Chapter 4 Problem Set (#1–6)') with 'QUEUE 2'; design-renders/shield.html: routines are FASTED BLOCK / DAY BLOCKS / SLEEP — named by time of day, never by subject — and every row, chip and rocker is the same stone monochrome. In exam season a student's day is five subjects with five papers; the app renders that day as one grey list where Physics and History are indistinguishable.

Recommendation: Adopt the exam paper's own coding system instead of colour confetti (which would break the one-accent law): every subject gets a paper code in the OCR style — 'PHY/2', 'HIS/1' — set in Anonymous Pro and printed in a fixed slot on the Deck task line, the Shield routine rows and the mark-sheet receipt, with per-subject separation in the Ledger done by code and rule, not hue. YPT proves students will track per-subject time (its planner is subject-first and its stats deepen in colour per subject); Monolith can answer with codes, which fit its print/instrument voice and cost no new colours.

#### [HIGH] Three time horizons share one screen and one chrome: live-sealed rules, standing rules and future routines are indistinguishable, and a routine edit never says which session it changes

One scroll (shield.html) holds three different time horizons in identical chrome: LOADOUT and YOUR RULES govern the live sealed session (ratcheted), the catalogue governs standing rules, and ROUTINES govern future windows — yet nothing on the screen labels which horizon a control belongs to. ShieldMatrixScreen.kt RoutineRow renders the same expanded −30/+30, day-letter and loadout chips whether or not that routine's window is live right now, and MonolithViewModel.kt persistRoutine (used by toggleRoutine/adjustRoutineTime/toggleRoutineDay) silently re-stamps scheduleEditedAtMillis and fires an immediate RoutineHeartbeat reconcile on every tap. A user who retimes DAY BLOCKS at 14:00, inside its 09:00–19:30 window, is never told whether they just changed the session they are in, the next window, or both — the design's answer is discoverable only by experiment.

Recommendation: Borrow the scope question every calendar app learned decades ago — Google Calendar editing a recurring event asks 'this event, or this and following events?' before saving. Split Shield into two labelled horizons while sealed: 'NOW — SEALED' (the live session's rules, tighten-only) pinned at top, and 'FROM THE NEXT SESSION' for routines and standing rules. Editing a routine whose window is currently live opens that scope sheet ('TODAY'S WINDOW IS LIVE — CHANGES APPLY FROM TOMORROW'), and the routine row itself carries a LIVE tag during its window so the horizon is visible before the tap, not inferred after it.

#### [HIGH] PARK: the surface that keeps the app alive is named with a word meaning 'leave it' — and the word is never even printed

PARK holds the permission board, the FIX keys and the guard status — the difference between a working shield and a dead one (render park.html: 'GUARD / LAST PROVED 21:47', 'NOTIFICATION LISTENER MISSING', 'FIX — NOTIFICATION LISTENER'). Yet its own rail code concedes it is unfindable by name: the PARK zone is 'a flat 48dp stretch that prints NO word ever, because PARK is where the machine's own state lives' (ui/views/MonolithRailView.kt:78-80). Worse, the chosen word fights its job: in ordinary English 'park' means set aside, leave unattended, come back later — the exact opposite of 'the checklist that must be green before anything else works'. Kalpana/Kinneir & Calvert's motorway signing principle is that a sign names its destination in the traveller's existing vocabulary; Monolith asks users to memorise that an unlabelled strip at the end of a track, named (only in code and comments) after leaving a car, is actually Permissions & Health.

Recommendation: Rename PARK to the word the app already shouts from its header band — GUARD (ui/components/GuardLine.kt:39 prints 'GUARD 4/4' on the Deck) — and print GUARD on the rail zone itself, so the thing you tap, the thing that reports 4/4, and the board that fixes a missing permission are one named object. Rule going forward: an invented noun is allowed only for something with no plain name; permissions, health and repair already have names, and borrowing 'park' from the driveway spends user trust for zero atmosphere.

#### [HIGH] The catalogue is numbered as a sequence but awarded as a lottery — Toy 06, the namesake grail, can drop in session one

CurioCatalog (MonolithModels.kt:807-850) numbers the set Toy 01 through Toy 06 in a deliberate order that culminates in Toy 06 'The Monolith Cube' — the brand's own namesake and obvious capstone. The forge ignores that order entirely: MonolithRepository.kt:2049-2051 picks CurioCatalog.artifacts.shuffled().first() per completed session. DrawerScreen.kt:431 prints the contradiction as the cabinet's standing line: 'A FINISHED SPAN FORGES ONE — THE FORGE CHOOSES WHICH.' Numbering promises a ladder the mechanism refuses to climb.

Recommendation: Make the numbering honest in one of two directions. Preferred: make order real — forge in catalogue sequence so Toy 01 is an initiation and Toy 06 The Monolith Cube is a true capstone earned last, the way Forest gates its Celestial Pine behind a 30-day streak and Opal reserves the Loyal Gem for 1,000 hours as a grail. Alternative: strip the numerals, present the six as unordered cabinet drawers, and stop implying progression the design does not deliver. Do not keep a sequence that is only a sort order.

#### [HIGH] Shield prints its entire catalogue twice on one screen — the YOUR RULES slip is a duplicate, not a summary

shield.html: the YOUR RULES slip prints 7 SlipLineRows (PEEK: Instagram/Reddit/X, SHUT: Chrome/Snapchat/TikTok/YouTube) directly above ALL APPS, where the same 7 apps reappear as catalogue rows with the same tiers. ShieldMatrixScreen.kt:342-410 builds the slip from slipLines(PEEK_2M) and slipLines(LOCKED); ShieldMatrixScreen.kt:968-1030 SlipLineRow prints name + ruling word per line; ShieldMatrixScreen.kt:882-960 adds a tally '4 SHUT · 3 PEEK · 3 OPEN' — the same counts a third time. The code comment at ShieldMatrixScreen.kt:1055 even admits the split: 'the slip above is where it is read, the catalogue is where a ruling is made' — one screen, two full renderings of one dataset.

Recommendation: Delete the slip as a list. Keep exactly one line — the tally — merged into the ALL APPS header ('ALL APPS — 4 SHUT · 3 PEEK · 3 OPEN'), and let the catalogue rows be the single place a tier is read or changed. If the ledger metaphor must survive, keep it only on the Receipt, where a session is actually closed. Follow Dieter Rams for Vitsoe: 'less, but better' — a fact printed twice on one scroll is not emphasis, it is a second maintenance surface that can disagree with the first.

#### [HIGH] PARK flattens three different categories — permission diagnostics, preferences, and a brand spec plate — into one headerless scroll, and its THEME row is a readout pretending to be a setting

ParkDrawer.kt: the sheet runs (3) the nine-row Watch permission board (~:307-460), (4) SOUND EFFECTS sled :468-478, (5) Shorts+Reels sled :534-547, (6) THEME :600-627, (7) the spec plate :627+ — park.html confirms one continuous sheet with hairlines but no group titles anywhere. Worse, THEME is not a control: ParkDrawer.kt:609-627 prints themeReadout as text, and MonolithViewModel.kt:212 records 'The manual theme is DEAD' — a row in the app's only settings surface that looks like a setting and accepts no input.

Recommendation: Give PARK the two-group structure Android Settings itself uses (system status separated from preferences): a titled SYSTEM group containing only the Watch board + FIX key, and a titled PREFERENCES group for Sound / Shorts+Reels / Social Sites sleds, with the spec plate moved out of the settings scroll entirely (it belongs on the Ledger's colophon or an About line). Make THEME either a real sled (DAY / AUTO / NIGHT, restoring the dead manual theme) or delete the row — a printed evaluation wearing a settings row's clothes teaches users that rows in PARK are not tappable, poisoning the sleds above it.

#### [HIGH] Every destination has two or three names and none of them agree: VAULT = 'Receipts' = LEDGER = 'STORED'

MonolithViewModel.kt:48-53: enum labels are DECK='Focus', SHIELD='Shield', TASKS='Tasks', VAULT='Receipts' — and grep shows destination.label is never rendered anywhere in the app. MonolithRailView.kt:33 prints a different set on the rail: DECK · SHIELD · TASKS · LEDGER. DrawerScreen.kt:224 and :522 then head the VAULT/LEDGER destination 'STORED'.
