So the fourth place is VAULT in code, 'Receipts' in the enum, LEDGER on the rail and STORED on its own masthead; the first is DECK on the rail but 'Focus' in the enum.

Recommendation: Pick one canonical name per destination and print it in all three places — rail word, destination masthead, and any cross-reference — the discipline Apple's HIG enforces by using the tab-bar label as the screen's title. Keep the rail words (DECK/SHIELD/TASKS/LEDGER are the brand voice) and change the destinations to match: DrawerScreen's masthead becomes LEDGER, the enum's dead label field is deleted or set to the rail words so a second vocabulary can never regrow. A user told 'check the Ledger' must find the word LEDGER when they arrive.

#### [HIGH] Inside LEDGER, four sub-places share one unchanging 'STORED' masthead — no running head, no breadcrumb, no way to tell INDEX from MONTH from CABINET

DrawerScreen.kt:72: private enum DrawerView { LANDING, INDEX, MONTH, CABINET } — four sub-places inside one rail stop, held in ephemeral remember state (:164). The masthead never changes: 'STORED' is printed identically at :224 (detail) and :522 (landing) regardless of view; INDEX (:620), MONTH (:652) and LANDING (:707) are entered via identical bare-text DrawerNavRows ('ALL MONTHS', 'CURIOS' :738/:776), and CABINET returns early at :330 as a separate composition with the same header. drawer.html shows the result: a screen whose only location signal is the content itself.

Recommendation: Add running-head wayfinding, the print convention Müller-Brockmann and Kinneir/Calvert both rely on: the masthead line becomes the current place — 'LEDGER · ALL MONTHS', 'LEDGER · OCT 2026', 'LEDGER · CURIOS' — set in the same 13sp mono as today's STORED, with the BACK row naming its destination ('BACK TO LEDGER') instead of the bare word BACK. No new chrome, no breadcrumb widget: just the running head every archive, timetable and ledger book has always used to answer 'where am I' at a glance.

#### [HIGH] Two different ontologies share one unlabelled board: the permission/interceptor family break is 16dp of whitespace and a silent vocabulary switch

ParkDrawer.kt:353-354 is explicit: 'The doubled gap: 16dp, no hairline, no eyebrow — the family break is whitespace, not a heading.' ParkDrawer.kt:339-391 therefore renders WatchStore.kt:93-102's two families — PERMISSIONS (ACCESSIBILITY...BATTERY) and INTERCEPTORS (SHORTS + REELS, SOCIAL SITES, NOTIFICATIONS) — as one continuous nine-line board under the single header GUARD (ParkDrawer.kt:308). park.html confirms it: the vocabulary silently switches mid-board from GRANTED/MISSING to RUNNING/OFF with no heading, legend or explanation that the second family is derived from the first (WatchStore.kt:440-476 deriveInterceptor: an interceptor reads OFF when a parent permission is MISSING or the setting is off — two completely different causes, one identical word OFF).

Recommendation: Name the groups and print the wiring, as a Neve 5088 console names its Input, Group and Monitor Master sections instead of running them together. Add engraved group heads — 'PERMISSIONS — GRANTED IN ANDROID SETTINGS' and 'INTERCEPTORS — LIVE STATE, DERIVED FROM THE ABOVE' — and under any OFF interceptor print its cause in the margin ('OFF — ACCESSIBILITY MISSING' vs 'OFF — YOU SWITCHED IT OFF'), so the board reads as a signal chain, not a list.

#### [HIGH] No master readout: a broken guard and a healthy guard look near-identical, and the FIX key hides its own queue

ParkBoardRow (ParkDrawer.kt:653-675) encodes health only as a shade swap: wordIsLack gets scheme.onBackground (#2C2A29), a granted/running word gets the dimmer onSurfaceVariant (#5F5856), both Atkinson Bold 15sp. The header above the board (ParkDrawer.kt:304-330) prints GUARD and a LAST PROVED clock time — never a count or verdict. The FIX key (ParkDrawer.kt:412-470) names only snapshot firstMissing, so with three permissions missing the panel says 'FIX — NOTIFICATION LISTENER' and hides that two more failures are queued behind it. park.html's broken board and a fully healthy board differ, at a glance, only in a few grey-vs-black words.

Recommendation: Add a master annunciator, the equivalent of a mixer's master meter/mute-group section and an aircraft master-caution light: make the header itself the verdict strip — 'GUARD — 2 MISSING' in full ink when anything lacks, 'GUARD — ALL PROVED' only when the counted set is complete — and make the FIX key carry its queue position: 'FIX 1 OF 3 — NOTIFICATION LISTENER'. One glance must answer 'am I protected?' before any line is read.

#### [HIGH] Shield has no master section: the global LOADOUT that rewrites every app tier gets the same 11.5sp grey header as a website count and scrolls away

ShieldMatrixScreen.kt:240 hosts everything in one flat LazyColumn, and every section — LOADOUT (ShieldMatrixScreen.kt:282), ROUTINES (ShieldMatrixScreen.kt:302), YOUR RULES (ShieldMatrixScreen.kt:342), ALL APPS (ShieldMatrixScreen.kt:434), BLOCKED WEBSITES (ShieldMatrixScreen.kt:541) — is introduced by the same FullBleedSectionHeader (MonolithCustomComponents.kt:123-148): Atkinson Bold 11.5sp, letterSpacing 0.6, onSurfaceVariant grey. Yet LOADOUT is the master control: its onSelect immediately calls onApplySmartLoadout (ShieldMatrixScreen.kt:285-296), rewriting the tier of the catalogue below. shield.html shows it scrolls away with the rest — a user editing app rockers screens later has no persistent readout of which loadout, or how many SHUT/PEEK rulings, are currently in force (that tally is buried mid-scroll in the YOUR RULES slip).

Recommendation: Give Shield a fixed master section, as a console's master strip never scrolls away from its channels: pin LOADOUT plus the standing tally ('STUDY · 4 SHUT · 3 PEEK · 3 OPEN') as a sticky header above the LazyColumn, in ink rather than the grey 11.5sp section label, and demote ROUTINES / ALL APPS / BLOCKED WEBSITES to subordinate, indented groups beneath it. The control that rewrites every other control must be visible while the others are touched.

#### [HIGH] The map's legend lies: Shield categories are false geography — name, label and code disagree

MonolithModels.kt:222-229 AppCategory: SHOPPING is labelled 'Other Apps' with code 'Tools', BROWSERS is labelled 'Web & News' with code 'Web', MESSAGING's code is 'Chat' while its label is 'Messaging' — the enum name, the printed label and the code are three different taxonomies for one station. Shield's filter row in shield.html therefore offers 'OTHER APPS' for shopping and 'SHORT VIDEO / SOCIAL / GAMES' beside it with no visible system. Schematisation only clarifies if the underlying classification is semantically correct first; Vignelli's test — semantically correct, syntactically consistent, pragmatically understandable — fails at the first word, before any drawing begins.

Recommendation: Rebuild the taxonomy as a closed, printed legend of exactly the categories the blocker enforces, with name = label = code: e.g. VIDEO, SOCIAL, GAMES, CHAT, WEB, SHOP. Rename SHOPPING to SHOP everywhere or delete the category and file those apps under OTHER with a printed definition on Shield ('OTHER = installed apps in no named line'). Print that legend once, fixed, at the head of the ALL APPS section so the map carries its own key like a transit diagram does.

#### [HIGH] The valve's operating instructions are sited after the machine they govern — the explanation sign stands past the junction

In DisarmChallengeOverlay the Emergency60sValveView is composed first and the rule sentence — 'Hold to fill 60 seconds. Every 15 seconds banks. If your hand slips, what isn't banked drains away. The banked part stays.' — is placed underneath it at 11sp, 75% alpha (AirlockAndDisarmOverlays.kt:801-803). A stressed user grips the valve on sight and only afterwards, if ever, reads the three-sentence banking/draining contract that determines whether releasing at 14 seconds loses everything. Worboys siting demands the sign be placed so the reader has the information before the action, not downstream of it.

Recommendation: Move the mechanics above the valve as three short stacked sign lines in 13sp full-alpha sentence case — 'Hold for 60 seconds.' / 'Every 15 seconds is banked for good.' / 'Let go and the unbanked part drains.' — and delete the paragraph under the valve entirely, so the hand starts only after the contract has been read.

#### [HIGH] Session sub-mode has no panel lamp: off the Deck, proving, running and Safe Break are indistinguishable

Elektron puts mode on the hardware: RECORD's LED is solid in GRID RECORDING, blinking in LIVE RECORDING, and MUTE/KEYBOARD modes light their own keys — the mode is readable from the panel whatever page is open. Monolith's session has at least five sub-modes (proving, running, Safe Break, grace, finish-held) but they are legible only in the Deck's eyebrow and hero. The global chrome never carries them: the header band prints only MONOLITH and GUARD x/4 in every state, the rail receives isSessionArmed as a single boolean (MainActivity.kt:710; MonolithRailView.kt:128-131) and draws it as one stroked circle on the DECK stop (MonolithRailView.kt:285-287), and Shield's only session signal is flipping to the night palette (ShieldMatrixScreen.kt:132: effectiveNight = isDarkTheme || isSessionActive). A user standing on Shield or Tasks during a Safe Break sees a dark screen and no word saying the machine is on break, in which block, or when it re-seals.

Recommendation: Add a permanent mode lamp to the header band, right of the brand, in Anonymous Pro: '◎ PROVING' during the cascade, '● SEALED · BLOCK 2 OF 3' while running, '◐ BREAK · RESEALS 14:20' during a Safe Break, '○ GRACE 0:07' during the grace window. Mirror the same state on the rail by changing the DECK stop's marker shape per sub-mode (ring for proving, filled disc for sealed, half-disc for break) so the mode survives on every screen, not just the Deck.

#### [HIGH] Shield has no parameter pages: five different scopes of edit are stacked in one scroll with no lit page key

Elektron survives density by paging: SRC, FLTR, AMP and MOD are separate PARAMETER pages, the active page key stays lit, and a knob only ever edits the page on screen — the operator always knows the scope of the edit. Shield is one unpaged scroll (shield.html) stacking five different scopes with no page key and no scope statement: LOADOUT (a global write to every app), ROUTINES (future scheduled writes), YOUR RULES (a derived print of current state), ALL APPS (single-row local edits) and BLOCKED WEBSITES. The section headers are typographically identical 11.5sp labels, so a global overwrite and a one-app edit present as the same class of act, and nothing at the top of the screen says which 'page' the user is standing in as they scroll from the loadout cap down into individual rockers.

Recommendation: Give Shield a fixed page-key row under the header — LOADOUT / ROUTINES / APPS / SITES — with the visible section's key ink-filled as the user scrolls, Elektron page-key style. Print a scope line under each section header in mono: under LOADOUT, 'APPLIES TO EVERY APP AT ONCE'; under ALL APPS, 'ONE APP · SURVIVES UNTIL A LOADOUT OR ROUTINE OVERWRITES IT'; under ROUTINES, 'FUTURE · FIRES ON SCHEDULE'.

#### [HIGH] Shield is a service panel worn as a taking surface: factory settings, search and site plumbing share the scroll with the daily dials

shield.html's single LazyColumn stacks, in order: the 3-stop Loadout selector, routine rows whose expanded state exposes −30/+30 chips, a loadout-cycle chip and 7 day chips per routine (ShieldMatrixScreen.kt:738-762), the YOUR RULES slip, a search field, 7 category filter words, 10 per-app rockers, and a blocked-websites editor with REMOVE chips and an add field. A Leica has no menu and no settings screen on the camera: operations performed once a month (loading film, setting the frame counter) live under the baseplate, physically separated from the dials used every exposure. Monolith performs no such separation — plumbing touched once (a site rule, a routine window) sits at the same depth and in the same grammar as rulings adjusted daily.

Recommendation: Split Shield at the Loadout selector. Above the split, the daily surface: Loadout cap, the slip, and the app rockers — nothing else. Everything else (search, category filters, routine editors, blocked websites) moves behind a single SERVICING entry at the bottom of the screen, opening one separate panel. The daily surface should be completable without ever scrolling past the last rocker.

#### [HIGH] A system for life that cannot grow: the loadout catalogue is a sealed enum of three, with no act anywhere for adding a part

A 606 installation grows for decades because the catalogue of parts is open: the owner buys a cabinet in year ten that hangs beside a shelf from year one. Monolith's central component is compile-time sealed. SmartLoadout is a closed enum of exactly three values (MonolithModels.kt:39-59), and a grep of every loadout verb in the app finds only applySmartLoadout and cycleRoutineLoadout (MonolithViewModel.kt:2098, 1521) — no create, edit, duplicate or delete for a loadout exists anywhere. The routine editor's only loadout gesture is cycling through the same three factory values (MonolithViewModel.kt:1521-1527). A user in year five of daily use owns precisely the parts shipped on day one; the system cannot gain a 'Library Exam Week' or 'Travel' configuration except by an app update recompiling the enum, and even the seeded routines only ever reference two of the three (STUDY and SLEEP, MonolithRepository.kt:842-850).

Recommendation: Promote loadouts from enum to data: a LoadoutEntity (id, name, per-category tier map plus per-app exceptions) with STUDY / WORK_SPRINT / SLEEP shipped as editable seed rows. Add one act to the Shield cap strip — SAVE CURRENT AS LOADOUT — which snapshots the hand-set tier wall as a named part, and let the routine editor pick any loadout row instead of cycling three constants. New parts then hang beside the factory ones on the same rail.

#### [HIGH] Shield reads its signal backwards: the YOUR RULES output slip is printed above the catalogue controls that create it, and the slip omits the OPEN range entirely

ShieldMatrixScreen.kt orders the panel: §1 LOADOUT (:274), §3 ROUTINES (:299), §3.5 YOUR RULES slip (:342), §4 search/filter (:431), §5 the app catalogue sleds that actually set the rulings (:505), §6 BLOCKED WEBSITES (:532). The shield.html render shows the consequence: the standing-orders slip — the readback of every tier decision — is printed above the controls that produce it, separated from them by a search box and filter strip. Worse, the output is incomplete: the slip renders a PEEK section and a SHUT section only (ShieldMatrixScreen.kt:363-404); OPEN apps appear in the tally ('4 SHUT · 3 PEEK · 3 OPEN') but get no lines, so a third of the panel's output range has no readout at all.

Recommendation: Move the YOUR RULES slip below the catalogue and the sites section, as the panel's OUTPUT readback — the last thing on the screen, summarising everything above it, the position the output section occupies on an instrument panel. Give OPEN its own printed section in the slip (name + dotted leader + OPEN), even though it is the resting state: an output meter that silently drops one of its three ranges teaches the user that unlisted means unruled.

#### [HIGH] Every visit opens with the house's lock report — 'GUARD 4/4' — the host greeting the guest with the state of his own security, not theirs

GuardLine.kt:13-14,39-45 defines the header band's permanent right-hand print as 'GUARD 4/4' or 'GUARD {n}/4 — {NAME}'; MainActivity.kt:422-432 seats this guard line in the header above every screen (deck.html and park.html both lead with it). The first fact Monolith offers a returning guest is never about the guest — not yesterday's session, not today's tower, not time reclaimed — but about whether the house's four warrants are intact. Housekeeping the host should absorb silently is worn as the welcome sign, and it only becomes information when it is bad news.

Recommendation: Demote the guard line: when the warrant is whole, the header band's right side carries the guest's own fact ('TODAY 1H 05M · TOWER 12') and GUARD appears only on lack (GUARD 3/4 — NOTIFICATION LISTENER) or inside Park. The locks report themselves when broken; a whole guard says nothing at the door.

#### [HIGH] A day lived without a finished task does not exist: the Drawer archives output, not life

In the Drawer a day exists only if it produced a stored task: the render's own source note states 'A day with no stored rows and no declared word renders NOTHING' (design-renders/drawer.html), the empty state is 'NOTHING STORED YET' (ui/screens/DrawerScreen.kt:712), and every rendered day is accounted in task units — 'ESTIMATE n MIN', 'SPENT' (DrawerScreen.kt:273, :280). A day spent walking, grieving, or doing nothing leaves literally no trace in the app's memory, while a day of six finished tasks is richly filed. Seneca's ledger is the reverse: a day is spent whether or not it was productive, and the unexamined days are precisely the theft. Monolith's archive silently defines a life as the sum of completed tasks.

Recommendation: Render every elapsed day in the Drawer month view, not only productive ones: days with no rows and no word print their date head with a single dim mono line 'NO RECORD — DAY LIVED ELSEWHERE' and tapping it offers the existing day-word declaration. Add a month footer counting 'DAYS ACCOUNTED n / DAYS LIVED 31' beside the existing month label (DrawerScreen.kt:641). No new data model — the calendar supplies the days; the Drawer merely stops deleting them.

#### [HIGH] The moment-to-moment goal is invisible: the running Deck shows a one-line truncated task title while the next concrete action sits collapsed behind an unlabelled tap on that title

On the running Deck the goal is one line: 'NOW' plus activeTask.title at 15sp with maxLines=1 and ellipsis (TactileDeckScreen.kt:795-815). The actionable decomposition — the sub-steps that say what to do in the next ten minutes — starts hidden: stepsExpanded is remember { mutableStateOf(false) } (line 784), revealed only by tapping the title itself (line 811), a gesture nothing labels. Inside the Airlock the goal is restated even more abstractly as 'ACTIVE INTENTION: <session title>' (AirlockAndDisarmOverlays.kt:662-671). Flow's clear-goals condition is not 'a title exists somewhere' — it is knowing, at every moment, what the next concrete action is; for the whole length of a session Monolith's default answer to 'what am I doing right now?' is a truncated noun phrase.

Recommendation: Promote the next action to the running Deck's permanent second line: under NOW <title>, always render 'NEXT · <first unchecked sub-step>' in Atkinson 13sp (falling back to 'NEXT · <title>' only when a task truly has no steps), and make the DONE key-cap complete that step — relabelled STEP DONE — advancing the NEXT line in place, with whole-task DONE demoted to the expanded list. The Airlock's intention line should print the same NEXT step under ACTIVE INTENTION, so the door argues with the user's actual next action, not the session's title.

#### [HIGH] Partial effort is already stamped — then buried in a machine log under a fake system package

MonolithRepository.kt:2311-2314 and 2346-2353: a session ended early with bankedElapsed >= 60 already computes a 'partial_stamp' and writes an InterceptLogEntity with packageName 'com.monolith.system' and appName 'Partial Stamp (Xm)' — Monolith does honour partial effort, then files the memorial inside the intercept log, disguised as a system app, where no record surface ever reads it back. ReceiptState.kt:97-106 finishKindOf confirms ENDED_EARLY / GRACE_CANCEL can never be a finish: no receipt, no Drawer trace (the Drawer stores tasks, not sessions). 'Nothing is finished' is wabi-sabi's third reality; Monolith computes the unfinished thing and buries it.

Recommendation: Promote the Partial Stamp into the Drawer as its own row kind: under the day it ended, an unnumbered, unruled row in onSurfaceVariant — the session's intention title plus 'ENDED EARLY — 23 MIN OF 60' — with no receipt №, no FORGED stamp and no verdict word. The 23 honest minutes become part of the kept record in a visibly lesser, unfinished form, instead of surviving only as a fake system entry in a machine log.

#### [HIGH] A priesthood of repair: PARK speaks only maker-jargon and counts every lesser mode as lack, so the user can never service their own tool

For Illich a convivial tool is intelligible to its user and usable without a specialist caste; a manipulative one can only be diagnosed in the priesthood's terms. PARK's board is nine lines of untranslated system jargon — ACCESSIBILITY, USAGE ACCESS, DEVICE ADMIN, NOTIFICATION LISTENER, OVERLAY, BATTERY, SHORTS + REELS, SOCIAL SITES, NOTIFICATIONS (service/WatchStore.kt:80-89) — each judged only GRANTED / MISSING / STALE / RUNNING / OFF (ui/components/ParkDrawer.kt:341-380), under a header reading 'LAST PROVED · SELF-REPORT' (ParkDrawer.kt:314-324): even the user's own check is framed as a report to the machine. No line says in plain words what the permission lets Monolith do, what concretely breaks without it, or that a lesser configuration is a legitimate way to use the app — DEVICE ADMIN missing simply makes GUARD x/4 a permanent accusation on every screen. The user cannot understand, choose or repair; they can only obey the FIX key.

Recommendation: Translate PARK into the vernacular and legitimise degraded modes: each board row gains a second line in Atkinson sentence case naming the consequence in the user's terms — e.g. under DEVICE ADMIN: 'Stops Monolith being deleted mid-session. Without it, everything else still works.' Add a selectable 'TIMER ONLY — NO GUARD' mode on the Deck: sessions run, receipts print stamped 'UNGUARDED', and GUARD prints 'GUARD — TIMER ONLY' as a whole state instead of a lack count, so choosing less apparatus is a lawful use of the tool, not a broken one.

#### [HIGH] Print logic imposed on attention: the Drawer files, indexes and makes searchable a past the user should be allowed to forget

DrawerScreen.kt:224 'STORED', :546 search field 'TYPE TO FIND A TASK', :621/:756 'ALL MONTHS' index, day headings filing each day under a declared word (REST/ILL/FAMILY, drawer.html frame 1). McLuhan on print: the printed word imposes linear, uniform, searchable, repeatable order on experience. Monolith applies exactly that order to attention — lived focus becomes paperwork, and the user's stance toward his own past becomes that of a records clerk auditing files.

Recommendation: Design forgetting into the Drawer, the opposite lesson of an archive: delete the task search field and the ALL MONTHS index; show only the current week as day entries, and collapse everything older into one unlabelled line per month ('OCTOBER — 31 SPANS') with no per-task rows to re-read. What cannot be searched cannot be audited, and the past stops being a second job.

#### [HIGH] The idle Deck spends attention on a hypothetical session: a dozen facts compete before the one decision to start

deck.html (from TactileDeckScreen.kt) in the unarmed state already demands parsing of at least twelve competing facts before the single decision 'start': header GUARD 4/4, eyebrow TOTAL, hero 1H 50M for a session not yet chosen, a 288dp rotary wheel with six detent numerals, FLOW keycap, NOW task title, DONE, QUEUE 2, ProofStripBand BLOCK/APPS/TIME (MonolithCustomComponents.kt:644-706), seam 'BIND HELD · THIS VISIT / PROOF: LIVE BIND', slide caption, and ImprintSlot tenant '9 WILL SHUT · 3 PEEK' (:782 onwards). Most of this is hypothetical (ENDS 10:40 for an 08:50 start that has not happened) or proof about a system the user is not doubting. Simon: designers who mistake the problem for information scarcity build systems that provide more and more information instead of filtering it.

Recommendation: Collapse the idle Deck to three emissions: intention/task, the wheel with its hero total, and the slide. Remove ProofStripBand, its seam stamps and ImprintSlot from the idle state entirely; show the strip only when the warrant is degraded or for 5 seconds after arming, and show 'WILL SHUT / PEEK' counts only on the Shield screen where tier decisions are actually made.

#### [HIGH] The in-session phone face is an altar to the countdown: 96sp session time is the hero of the desk clock while the work itself is a 14sp banner underneath

AirlockAndDisarmOverlays.kt:152-215: the desk clock's hero is timeText at 96sp Anonymous Pro Bold with -3sp tracking (163-170), above a full-width progress bar; the active task — the actual object of the session — is a 14sp banner in a surfaceBright pill below (196-215), and deskClockBannerText (225-226) reduces the work to a title string with no substep, no page, no next action. Crawford's ecology of attention asks what the environment solicits: a workshop clock is peripheral, a glance at the bench tells you where you are. Monolith's one sanctioned in-session face inverts this — the phone's remaining minutes are the monument, the work is the footnote.

Recommendation: Invert the desk clock's hierarchy: promote the current substep ('NOW — PROBLEM 4 · NEXT — PROBLEM 5') to the hero position in Atkinson Bold, and demote session time to a small mono line in the corner beside the 'TAP ANYWHERE TO EXIT' caption, keeping the progress strip as the only large time signal. A glance at the phone should answer 'what am I doing', with 'how long is left' available but peripheral — the clock recedes, the work solicits.

#### [MEDIUM] History is a ledger, not a place: Forest's past is a landscape you revisit, Monolith's Drawer is rows of text where empty days render as nothing at all

drawer.html Frame 1: history is a ledger — day headings in 11sp mono, task rows separated by 1dp hairlines, and a day with no stored rows and no declared word 'renders NOTHING — no heading, no missed mark… no tower, no bricks, no streak and no total anywhere on this screen' (render caption, from DrawerScreen.kt). Forest's history is a place: every session's tree stands on shared ground in chronological groves, so the past has spatial continuity — you revisit somewhere, and even an empty patch is ground you can see. Monolith's past is a filing system you query; effort evaporates into rows, and the gaps between good days are not even empty space, they are absent space.

Recommendation: Give the Drawer a ground line, following Forest's grove: a continuous horizontal 'ground' strip at the head of the month view on which each day occupies a fixed-width plot — a laid brick glyph for a kept day, a declared-word marker for REST/ILL/FAMILY, and visibly empty ground for an unkept day — so scrolling history feels like walking a plot the user owns, not paging a register. The existing rows stay beneath it as the index to that place.

#### [MEDIUM] Drawer erases empty days entirely: the week's rhythm has holes where a day should read as blank

DrawerScreen.kt:84-91: buildDayGroups groups only dates that have stored rows (plus declared day words) — a date with neither produces no group and no heading. drawer.html's own render note states it plainly: 'A day with no stored rows and no declared word renders NOTHING in the Drawer — no heading, no missed mark.' The rendered week jumps FRI 30 → THU 29 → WED 28 (word only) → TUE 27 → MON 26 (word only) → SUN 25: any day without a word simply does not exist in the archive, so a user reviewing their week cannot distinguish 'I rested and forgot to declare it' from 'the app lost Tuesday' from 'I never opened the app' — three very different facts rendered as the same absence.

Recommendation: For the current week only (7 headings, no new data model, no queries beyond the groups already built), print a heading for every day: days with no rows and no word get the date line plus one muted plate line '— NOTHING STORED' in the existing 10.5sp onSurfaceVariant mono. Older months keep today's sparse listing. This follows the printed-diary convention (a page per day, blank pages included — the continuity is what makes a gap legible as a gap) and Day One's calendar view, where an empty day is shown as empty rather than deleted from the week.

#### [MEDIUM] In the Drawer a day the user did nothing renders as literally nothing — failure is erased from history instead of being made visible and ugly

DrawerScreen.kt:84-91 buildDayGroups groups only stored completed-task rows by filing date, and the landing at DrawerScreen.kt:681-699 iterates those groups; a date with no rows produces no group, no heading and no mark. drawer.html's own caption confirms it: 'A day with no stored rows and no declared word renders NOTHING in the Drawer — no heading, no missed mark. There is no tower, no bricks, no streak and no total anywhere on this screen.' Scrolling a month therefore shows an unbroken run of productive days; the gaps where routines were missed are typographically identical to days before install or outside the month.

Recommendation: Render the full calendar, not just the harvest, following Forest's forest timeline where a withered tree stays standing in the grove as the visible cost of a broken session: emit a heading row for every day in the viewed month, and for a day with a missed routine and no stored work print a hollow brick glyph plus 'MISSED — {routine name}' in onSurfaceVariant with the date struck by a hairline. Kept days keep their current bold rows. Absence must become a designed, slightly ugly object the user scrolls past, not a silent omission.

#### [MEDIUM] The Drawer opens with its furniture, not its history — nav rows outrank every day heading

drawer.html landing order: .hdr 'STORED' (13px, grey #5F5856), a 48px filled .search slab, 'ALL MONTHS' and 'CURIOS' nav rows in bold ink 11-12px, and only then the day groups. DrawerScreen.kt:521-530 sets STORED at 13sp in onSurfaceVariant; :537-546 makes search a 48dp surfaceVariant box; DrawerNavRow (:815-831) prints nav labels in Atkinson Bold 12sp in full ink onBackground; DayHeading (:842-862) prints the dates a browsing user is scanning for at 11sp in the same grey as the page title. The anchors of the list are its palest elements; its doors are its darkest.

Recommendation: Invert the weights to match the job of a journal/ledger, the way Kinneir & Calvert's timetable typography makes the date/destination the strongest element in the scan column: print day headings in ink at 13sp, demote ALL MONTHS and CURIOS to a single footer row (or a quiet header-right word) below the current week, and slim the search field to a 40dp unfilled row under STORED. A returning user should fixate first on TODAY and yesterday's dates, not on a search slab and two doors.

#### [MEDIUM] The architecture is sealed against people in both axes — the rail admits 'no fifth rest position' and time is organised as perpetual DAILY routines and endless ALL MONTHS filing, so a finite shared season has no stop and no span to exist in

MonolithRailView.kt:21-34 is explicit: RailGeometry.WORDS = DECK, SHIELD, TASKS, LEDGER and 'There is no fifth rest position' — the chrome is a sealed four-room workshop, every stop a place or a thing. shield.html shows the same closure in time: every routine sub-line reads 'DAILY · STUDY', perpetual and unbounded, and DrawerScreen.kt:756 organises all history under 'ALL MONTHS' — filing time with no beginning or end. A seasonal cohort (the Inktober / NaNoWriMo pattern: a named, finite, shared period with an opening day and a closing day) has nowhere to live in either axis: no fifth stop to host it and no finite span of time to bound it.

Recommendation: Do not add a fifth stop — that restraint is correct. Give the cohort a season instead of a screen: a named 42-day season (e.g. 'WINTER TABLE · 42 DAYS') declared once, printed as a chapter divider in the Ledger in place of a month heading, during which a pair or small cohort arms under the same Deck and routines; on the closing day the season's receipts are bound as one Ledger chapter with a single closing slip listing each member's totals. When the season ends, the chapter closes and the rail returns to four solitary rooms — connection as a bounded rite the object hosts, not a permanent social layer bolted onto it.

#### [MEDIUM] The rail pretends four equals, but DECK is secretly home — and SHIELD (setup) outranks TASKS (daily work) in stop order

MainActivity.kt: BackHandler sends system Back from any non-DECK destination to DECK, and Deck entry alone triggers the watch sweep and residency stamp (LaunchedEffect on DECK) — DECK is functionally the home base. But MonolithRailView.kt:33 and the cap geometry (RailGeometry, MonolithRailView.kt:22-46) give all four stops identical segment width, type and weight, and the stop order seats SHIELD — pure configuration, visited rarely once set — second, ahead of TASKS, the destination a user visits daily to plan work. MainActivity.kt selectedTabIndex mapping (DECK 0, SHIELD 1, TASKS 2, VAULT 3) hard-codes that order.

Recommendation: Reorder the rail by journey frequency — DECK · TASKS · SHIELD · LEDGER — following the Material 3 navigation-bar guidance and Forest's home-then-plan ordering: the doing verbs left, the configuring and reviewing verbs right. Mark home without an icon: DECK's word alone takes the filled-centre armed-marker treatment permanently (the marker MonolithRailView.kt already draws for a running session), so the rail quietly says which stop is base camp. One word-order change in RailGeometry.WORDS and the stopIndexOf table; no new destinations, no new chrome.

#### [MEDIUM] Print and control share one material: read-only rows, live sleds and the sealed state are visually indistinguishable on the panel

Park uses one row grammar for three different kinds of thing: board rows are read-only measurements (ParkBoardRow, ParkDrawer.kt:653), sled rows are live controls (ParkDrawer.kt:479, 548), and the THEME row (ParkDrawer.kt:610) is a read-only evaluation ('AUTO · DAY — NO ROUTINE OWNS IT' in park.html) printed label-left/value-right over the same hairline. The only differentiators are the sled chrome and the FIX key. Under the seal the sleds become print via an invisible touch-blocking overlay (ParkDrawer.kt sealed overlays on the sound/shorts/social sleds) — the panel's appearance does not change at all when it stops being a control surface and becomes a display.

Recommendation: Separate display material from control material, as Teenage Engineering's OP-1 does — its OLED is a distinct recessed window while every control is a coloured physical encoder whose colour is matched on-screen. Put Park's read-only values (board words, THEME, LAST PROVED) in a visibly inset readout treatment (surfaceVariant field, mono type), keep bare print-and-sled only for live controls, and when sealed, print that state on the panel itself — sleds greyed with a 'SEALED — READ ONLY' plate — instead of an invisible overlay over an unchanged-looking switch.

### Flows and friction — 53 findings (19 critical, 29 high, 5 medium, 0 low)

#### [CRITICAL] Friction theatre: the decision is already on stage during the wait — RETURN TO FOCUS is composed and tappable from the first frame of the countdown, so the pause never exists as its own beat

AirlockAndDisarmOverlays.kt:655-661 — the accent BlockitActionChip 'RETURN TO FOCUS' is composed unconditionally, outside every countdown conditional; only the peek chip is gated on countdownSecs == 0 (:663). airlock.html frames 1-2 confirm it visually: at countdown 03 the full decision UI is already present. The user therefore spends the entire 5 seconds staring at the answer buttons — the wait is a lobby in front of a choice, not an experience. one sec sequences the two beats strictly: its intervention screen (dark full-screen, 'It's time to take a deep breath…', a gradient bar pacing the breath) contains no choices at all; only after the exercise ends does a separate decision screen appear. Monolith collapses one sec's two-act structure into one screen, and the act that does the psychological work — the pause with nothing to do but breathe — is the one that gets deleted

Recommendation: Split the Airlock into one sec's two beats. Beat one (the delay): no chips, no tappable elements at all — only the app name, the intention line and the pacing element, so there is literally nothing to decide or press while the nervous system settles. Beat two (composed only when the delay completes): the decision chips fade in as a distinct second state. If RETURN TO FOCUS must remain reachable during the wait for safety, demote it to a quiet text link at the bottom edge during beat one and promote it to the accent chip only in beat two.

#### [CRITICAL] No handover rendering exists: Monolith's read-only 'print' grammar is keyed to the session, never to whose hand holds the phone — so every guest gets the live editor

ParkDrawer.kt:80-97 states the app's own law — 'everything print except the FIX key… While sealed the drawer… is read-only: print and reading, no FIX, no sled' — but MainActivity.kt:651-654 wires that protection as isSealed = sealed (session state), never holder state. Unsealed, the handed-over phone is the full editor: ParkDrawer.kt:498-524 and 567-593 live sleds for SOUND EFFECTS and SHORTS + REELS, the 48dp ink FIX key at ParkDrawer.kt:412-458 launching a Settings trip, and ShieldMatrixScreen.kt:1068-1077 AppRowSledToggleView onTierSelected rewriting any app's tier on contact (renders: park.html sled/FIX rows, shield.html rocker rows). There is no third rendering between 'owner editing' and 'session sealed'.

Recommendation: Add a HAND OVER rendering that reuses the existing sealed print grammar socially, not just temporally: a rail long-press flips Deck/Shield/Drawer/Park to print-only (rockers and sleds render as the YOUR RULES slip renders tiers — words, no thumbs; FIX key absent; intentions shown as category only), bannered 'SHOWN — NOT EDITING', exited only by the owner's biometric/PIN. This is Samsung One UI 5 Maintenance Mode's decision — same hardware, a visibly distinct surface where personal data is concealed and exit requires the owner's lock credential — shrunk to an in-app mode Monolith's own print-vs-object language already knows how to draw.

#### [CRITICAL] Time-to-arm is two separate instruments with a translation intermission between them, not one choreographed start

deck.html: the Deck forces (1) rotate the 288dp wheel (TactileDeckScreen.kt:705), (2) set blocks in the wheel hub, (3) re-read the session in three different units before committing — hero total span in TactileDeckScreen.kt:325 totalSpanMinutes = dialMinutes*studyBlocksCount + (studyBlocksCount-1)*10, proof-strip TIME as a wall-clock ENDS 10:40, imprint as '9 WILL SHUT · 3 PEEK' — then (4) perform a second, unrelated slide/tap commit in a separate 72dp zone. Setting and committing share no motion, no surface and no vocabulary. A spring-wound mechanical countdown timer makes the opposite decision: one twist simultaneously winds the spring, sets the duration and starts it — set IS start, zero second commit. Apple Watch Timers makes the same decision digitally: tap one preset circle and the countdown begins immediately, custom values live behind a separate Custom door.

Recommendation: Collapse set and commit into one throw. Keep the wheel as the only setting instrument, and replace the mandatory slide travel with a single START cap whose face is printed live from the wheel's own state — 'START 1H 50M · ENDS 10:40 · 9 SHUT · 3 PEEK' — updating on every detent, so the verification the strip and imprint currently demand in three places happens on the control itself, in one reading, at the moment of the tap. One decision to set, one tap to arm, no intermission.

#### [CRITICAL] After the latch the choreography goes silent and then plays a fixed 1050ms film: minimum 1.26s from gesture to value, up to 2.5s with no verb offered

ArmProvingController.kt:686 DWELL_MS=210 (t=0 can never fire before latch+210ms), :695 DEADLINE_MS=500, :699 ANNUL_MS=1500, and :501-502 'The retry is the machine's, never his — no verb is offered.' MonolithCustomComponents.kt:537 states the design intent: 'PROVING's silence is the machine working' — jamSentenceFor only speaks once Jammed. TactileDeckScreen.kt:202-207 deliberately renders the Deck in its idle form while Proving/Jammed (isSessionRunning excludes provingThisSession), then at SealedRunning runs a fixed seal shot to e>=1050 at :258 with scroll disabled for exactly that span at :562 and task handlers removed. Healthy path: 210ms dwell + 1050ms shot = 1,260ms after the user's gesture has already succeeded. Apple Watch Workout also inserts a delay — a 3-second countdown — but it is numbered, its purpose (get ready) is legible, and tapping the screen skips it; Monolith's delay is unnumbered, unskippable and unexplained.

Recommendation: Make the post-latch interval legible and overlapping, following the Workout countdown's legibility without its length: fill the seated cap in three segments as the three ArmLinks (SESSION / SHIELD / ACCESS, ArmProvingController.kt ArmLink displayNames) confirm, run the vertigo/blur shot concurrently with proving instead of after it, and end input-death at t=0 rather than at shot settle. Cap total latch-to-running at the 210ms dwell on a healthy device; if a link jams, the cap itself — not a sentence slot 500ms later — shows which segment is unfilled.

#### [CRITICAL] The ratchet refuses in the wrong place, in silence, and lies about when it lifts — loosening looks identical to tightening until after the tap

ShieldMatrixScreen.kt:252-268 renders the ratchet warning as the FIRST item of the LazyColumn — a user who has scrolled to the catalogue rows at the bottom (100dp bottom padding, six sections above them, shield.html) attempts a loosening flip and the refusal appears off-screen, above the fold. MonolithViewModel.kt:300-312 auto-clears it after 3600ms and its own comment states 'The warning is a print; it sounds nothing' — while a successful tightening gets a pitched rotary detent (MonolithViewModel.kt setAppBlockTier, freq 320/560/820Hz). Worse, the cycle path's copy lies: MonolithViewModel.kt:2053 prints 'CANNOT UNLOCK X UNTIL 00:00' — a hard-coded midnight, not the session's real end (the Airlock itself prints 'SESSION ENDS 18:30', airlock.html). Three different refusal wordings exist (VAULT / LOCKDOWN / UNTIL 00:00) for one rule.

Recommendation: Move the refusal to the point of gesture, following AppBlock Strict Mode's principle that a sealed profile's settings are unchangeable in place, not scolded after the fact: in sealed mode render the sled with only its lawful stops — the OPEN (and PEEK, for a SHUT app) stop is removed from the track, the thumb physically halts at the ratchet detent with the seat-knock sound tightening already uses, and a line prints directly under that row: 'SEALED UNTIL 18:30 — TIGHTENING ONLY'. Delete the top-of-list banner and the 'UNTIL 00:00' string; one refusal sentence, sourced from the session's actual end time, everywhere.

#### [CRITICAL] Detention length is set by shield-service plumbing, not by ritual — a variable 1.48–1.8s invisible freeze that reads as a hang

ReceiptState.kt:201-213 Detention: receiptAtMs = min(max(1480, max(1200, pawlLiftMs)+280), 1800) — issue time is a function of pawlLiftMs, the frame MonolithShieldService.instance reads null. MonolithViewModel.kt onFinishE0 polls that instance every 25ms (delay(25L) loop, issueOffsetMs check) after stopShield(). TactileDeckScreen.kt:274 heldFinish = finishState != null && !finishState.issued freezes the last frame for the whole interval. receipt.html Frame 3 confirms what the user sees meanwhile: hero locked at 00:00, wheel as a still ghost, slide seated, utilities row absent — no progress bar, no countdown, no word explaining the hold.

Recommendation: Decouple ceremony time from service time. Fix detention at one authored duration (e.g. 1200ms) for every clean finish, run the shield-stop confirmation invisibly behind it, and make the hold legible while it runs: the proof strip's TIME cell counts the detention down or the hero breathes through a single scale settle on MonolithCurves.specB (420ms) then rests. If the pawl is late, extend the receipt's fade, never the freeze. Following Apple Watch Workout: ending shows a fixed, animated summary transition whose length never varies with whether the workout has finished saving to Health.

#### [CRITICAL] The intercept sells the refusal back as a menu: EMERGENCY PEEK is a full-width chip beside RETURN TO FOCUS

airlock.html frames 1-2 and AirlockAndDisarmOverlays.kt:562-569, 663-690: after a 5-second countdown (countdownSecs starts at 5), the composable adds a second full-width 42dp BlockitActionChip, 'EMERGENCY PEEK 2m', directly under the accent 'RETURN TO FOCUS' chip, with its price 'TAKING THE PEEK STARTS A 20 MINUTES COOLDOWN ON THIS APP' (line 268) set in the same Atkinson 12.5sp cream @80% as the session intention line. Two equal-geometry chips, stacked 16dp apart, is a choice menu, not a wall. one sec makes the opposite decision: its intercept is a breathing exercise that fills the screen — the pause itself is the entire content, and proceeding is only an outcome after the exercise, never a priced second button offered next to the exit. Opal's Deep Focus goes further: the bypass option does not exist on the screen at all.

Recommendation: Remove the peek chip from the first intercept entirely: frame 1's layout (badge, app name, end time, countdown, intention, single RETURN TO FOCUS chip) becomes the only layout. A peek may be requested only by re-attempting the open after returning — on that second intercept, replace both chips with a single text-only, unboxed line 'PEEK 2M — 20 MIN COOLDOWN' at the card's foot, no chip fill, no accent. Refusal must read as absence of an option, following one sec's single-content intercept and Opal Deep Focus's non-existent bypass.

#### [CRITICAL] Entry friction is costume, exit friction is real: the slide's visual weight lies about the price of starting

deck.html slidezone: 72dp track, 84x56dp orange cap (#F55314) reading 'SLIDE OR TAP TO START'; BlockitCoreViews.kt:2407 WORDS_START = "SLIDE OR TAP TO START" and :1424-1435 comment 'The tap is a first-class order' with a >=90ms tap running the commit mesh. Exit side: AirlockAndDisarmOverlays.kt:772 'It is the only break this week' behind a 60s hold (valve at :784-797).

Recommendation: Make entry cost real and say so: delete the tap commit path so only a full slide past the 0.92 catch plus a 600ms seated hold arms, and print the exit price on the Deck itself under the slide ('EXIT: 60S HOLD - ONE PER WEEK') before arming, following Opal's model of letting the user choose and see the difficulty (Deep Focus = cannot cancel) before the session starts, not discover it inside one.

#### [CRITICAL] Friction guards the door but not the rulebook: amending the law costs one tap, breaking it costs sixty seconds

ShieldMatrixScreen.kt:186-216 slipTap flips a ruling SHUT<->PEEK on a single line tap; :284-292 one cap tap calls onApplySmartLoadout and bulk-applies a whole loadout; RoutineRow toggles are single 48x32dp taps (shield.html). By contrast the session exit is a 68dp valve demanding 60 continuous seconds (airlock.html frame 3; AirlockAndDisarmOverlays.kt:784). The heaviest chrome in the app (88sp numeral, full-screen night takeover, AirlockAndDisarmOverlays.kt:636) guards a 2-minute peek; the lightest chrome (11sp filter words, 34dp sleds) guards rewriting the rules themselves.

Recommendation: Invert the chrome-to-consequence map: while a session is sealed, put Shield behind the same class of friction as the exit - loadout cap, routine toggles and any tier weakening require a 15s press-and-hold with the consequence printed inline ('THIS REWRITES THE LIVE SESSION'), following Freedom Locked Mode and Opal's passcode-locked Screen Time access, which both place friction on editing the blocklist during a session, not only on leaving it. Unsealed, keep Shield one-tap light as it is now.

#### [CRITICAL] The tap shortcut makes the slide's elaborate friction decorative — the hard gesture and the easy gesture seal the identical lock

BlockitCoreViews.kt:2407 WORDS_START='SLIDE OR TAP TO START' is printed on the track (deck.html: slidewords 'SLIDE OR TAP TO START', orange 84x56 cap in a 72dp zone). The drag path is heavily engineered friction: gear() at BlockitCoreViews.kt:1336 is 1:1 to GATE 0.68 (line 1312) then damped at 2/3 gain so CATCH 0.84 (line 1318) needs finger p=0.92. The tap path skips all of it: endDrag classifies any on-cap press >=90ms with <8dp slop as a tap and calls startMesh(target=0.92) at BlockitCoreViews.kt:2097/2132, a 140ms bezier (MonolithCurves.DURATION_140 in stepMachine) into the same seat spring and latch.

Recommendation: Delete tap-to-seal entirely. A tap should only prime the control: cap lifts, track words change to 'SLIDE TO SEAL', nothing dispatches. If a tap entry must survive for accessibility, make it a 1,200ms press-and-hold on the cap with a filling marker line and release-to-cancel, never a 140ms driven mesh. Follow iOS 'slide to power off': Apple gives that irreversible action no tap alternative at all — a long-press of two physical buttons summons the screen, then only the full slide commits.

#### [CRITICAL] The point of no return sits invisibly at 84% of the track — the cap finishes the seal by itself after the finger has stopped deciding

BlockitCoreViews.kt:1352 commits() fires when displayed >= CATCH 0.84 under contact, not at the end of travel; startSeat then sets seatFloor (line 2146) and stepSeat clamps it one-way at BlockitCoreViews.kt:2317-2318 ('the seat is one-way — displayed may never fall below it'), so from 84% the spring (400*(1-x)-16v) drives the cap to 1.0 on its own even if the finger lifts or reverses. Nothing on the surface marks that point: deck.html's track is a plain #2E2A26 bar with only the centred words and the cap's 1dp marker line — no tick, notch or colour break at 0.68 or 0.84, and the gate crossing is signalled only by a 1ms haptic (fireFeel 620Hz up / 340Hz retreat, BlockitCoreViews.kt:2009) with the track words explicitly frozen through every drag state.

Recommendation: Make the commitment point visible and located at the end of travel. Paint two permanent notches in the track face: a hairline tick at the gate (0.68) and a filled stop at the catch, move the catch to displayed 1.0 so 'end of track = sealed' is literally true, and at the gate change the cap fill from accent #F55314 to ink and swap the track words to the seal readback. Borrow the two-stage camera shutter (Canon/Leica pattern): half-press is a felt-and-shown detent that meters/focuses and can be released harmlessly, full-press past a second firmer detent fires — Monolith needs the same legible two detents instead of one invisible 84% tripwire.

#### [CRITICAL] The Airlock sign changes its message mid-read: the second exit is only erected after the driver has passed the decision point

AirlockInterceptOverlay composes the EMERGENCY PEEK chip and its price line only when countdownSecs == 0 (AirlockAndDisarmOverlays.kt:663 and 678), and the withheld-peek explanations likewise only at countdownSecs == 0 (line 690). For the full 5-second approach the sign advertises exactly one choice, RETURN TO FOCUS; then a new exit, its price sentence, and several lines of layout materialise and push the card's contents down — visible comparing frames 1 and 2 of airlock.html. Kinneir/Calvert advance direction signs exist precisely so every option and its consequence is legible before the junction, leaving time to act after reading (Worboys principle f).

Recommendation: Compose the complete sign from the first frame: RETURN TO FOCUS, the peek chip greyed with a live 'in 4 sec' mono badge, and the full price line all present at countdown 5, with only the chip's enabled state changing at zero. Reserve the final layout height from the start so nothing on the sign moves while it is being read.

#### [CRITICAL] No 5cc moment: the arm ritual measures only duration — there is no small, fixed, repeatable offering that makes the seal's feeling possible

deck.html render: the entire arm ritual is a duration — hero '1H 50M' (50min x 2 blocks + break), RotaryWheelView reader at the 50-minute detent, and SlideToStartView (TactileDeckScreen.kt:983) labelled 'SLIDE OR TAP TO START'. TactileDeckScreen.kt:107 receives intentionText but the rendered Deck contains no intention field, no offering step and no fixed quantity: the user measures only how long, never what they are putting in. Balmuda's feeling is impossible without its measured dose — exactly 5cc of water, poured from its own cup, every time.

Recommendation: Add the dose: before the wheel unlocks, require one fixed act — the user writes or confirms a single intention line in a dedicated 48dp 'measure' slot at the top of the Deck card (pre-filled from the NOW task, editable, never optional). The slide stays disabled until that line is placed. Print that exact line as the receipt's first line and as the Airlock's intention line, so the same measured offering opens, guards and closes every session.

#### [CRITICAL] The Airlock fills Weil's empty waiting with an 88sp number to seek

Weil: 'our thought should be empty, waiting, not seeking anything' (Waiting for God, 'Reflections'). The Airlock's 5-second 'breathing delay' fills that emptiness with the largest object in the app: AirlockAndDisarmOverlays.kt:562-569 ticks countdownSecs down each second and :636-639 renders it at 88sp Anonymous Pro ('0%d'/'00'), centred in the card (airlock.html frames 1-2: '03' dwarfs the 24sp app name and 12.5sp intention). The peek chip is withheld until the numeral reaches 00 (:663), so waiting is trained as watching a number and seeking its end - the precise seeking Weil excludes.

Recommendation: Delete the countdown numeral from AirlockInterceptOverlay entirely. Keep the 5-second delay, but render only the app name, the intention and RETURN TO FOCUS while the card background dims one step per second; compose EMERGENCY PEEK silently when the delay ends, with no '00', no tick sound and no number to chase. Waiting should be empty, not counted aloud.

#### [CRITICAL] Routine sessions abolish separation: the initiate never crosses — they are abducted into the limen and discover it by collision

Van Gennep (Les rites de passage, 1909): preliminal rites detach the initiate from the previous world before the limen is entered. Monolith's routines enter the limen with no crossing by the initiate at all: seeded routines auto-start live blocking sessions covering ~21h/day, and a routine firing performs the full seal (SessionSealTransition.kt executeSeal/playSealThrow) unattended. The user's first lived experience of a routine session is not a departure but a collision — an Airlock intercept when they open a blocked app (airlock.html frames 1-2: 'AIRLOCK INTERCEPTION • LOCKED'). Separation is not abbreviated; for the majority of hours it is absent, and the limen is something that happens to a person mid-life in another app.

Recommendation: Give every routine window a separation beat that precedes the seal: 60 seconds before a window, a full-screen preliminal card in the light scheme — window name, what will shut, the intention carried over — with CROSS (arms on time) and DEFER ONCE as the only verbs. The seal sound/Throw may only sound after that card has been shown; a window the user never saw begin must receipt as UNWITNESSED, never as a clean held session. No silent auto-seal.

#### [CRITICAL] Tomorrow arrives pre-judged: routines materialise and verdict the future with no moment where the present user re-authors it

MonolithRepository.materialiseRoutineSession (MonolithRepository.kt:1086) creates the session and raises the shield when a window arrives — no day-of consent step exists anywhere — and finaliseRoutineSession (MonolithRepository.kt:1030-1034) then stamps the window ATTENDED, PARTIAL or MISSED against a yardstick the user set once, possibly weeks ago. The user's past self, via a schedule, writes tomorrow's obligations and tomorrow's verdicts; the present self only discovers them by being blocked or judged.

Recommendation: Convert routines from orders into proposals: on the Deck each morning (and the night before after 20:00), show a 'TOMORROW'S WINDOWS' strip listing each routine window with CONFIRM and RELEASE actions. Only a confirmed window may materialise a session or be judged; a released or ignored window expires silently with no outcome stamp in the Drawer. The schedule proposes, the living user disposes.

#### [CRITICAL] In-session feedback measures time served, never work done: the computed sub-step progress fraction is wired to nothing

TactileDeckScreen.kt:336-347 derives the running progressFraction solely from elapsedSeconds/effectiveTargetSeconds (or elapsed/1200f in stopwatch mode); the 6dp track and % at TactileDeckScreen.kt:742-777 are that fraction and nothing else. FocusTaskEntity already computes the work signal — subStepProgressFraction and completedSubStepsCount at MonolithModels.kt:131-141 — but a search of the whole ui/ tree finds zero call sites for either: ticking a sub-step on the Deck (TactileDeckScreen.kt:853-882) changes only a numeral's colour and a strikethrough. A user who finishes every sub-step at minute 12 of 50 and a user who stares at the wall for 50 minutes receive byte-identical in-session feedback; the bar certifies attendance, not progress toward the goal.

Recommendation: Make work, not time, the running Deck's primary feedback: replace the hero progress track during a session with a two-part readout — the first unchecked sub-step's completion drives the fill (sub-steps done / total, animated with the existing seal sound and a firm haptic on each tick), and elapsed time demotes to the small mono % position. When the last sub-step is ticked before the block ends, the Deck must respond in the moment: print 'TASK CLEAR · 18 MIN LEFT' and offer EXTEND WITH NEXT TASK or FINISH BLOCK EARLY, instead of leaving the user to serve out a clock whose goal is already met.

#### [CRITICAL] The block boundary evicts the user at flow's most likely moment: the Safe Break fires on elapsed time alone, with no way to stay in a block that is working

MonolithRepository.kt:2020-2038: the tick that finds verifiedElapsed >= effectiveTarget unconditionally writes isInSafeBreak=true with safeBreakSecondsRemaining=SAFE_BREAK_DURATION_SECONDS (600s, MonolithRepository.kt:110) and fires the boundary knock — there is no state check for engagement, no intercept-free streak, no unfinished sub-step, no user confirmation. The only verb the break offers once it has started is END BREAK (TactileDeckScreen.kt:925-935); there is no STAY / DEFER verb at the boundary itself. The moment flow is most likely to have formed — deep into a block, sub-step mid-flight — is the exact moment the schedule evicts the user into a timed 10-minute exile, because the clock, not the state of attention, decides.

Recommendation: At a block boundary, insert a 15-second boundary offer on the Deck before the break flips: hero prints 'BLOCK CLEAR' with two chips — TAKE BREAK (default, fires if untouched) and STAY IN IT, which defers the Safe Break to the next boundary exactly once per session and prints 'BREAK HELD' in the eyebrow. Gate the offer on flow evidence the app already records: show STAY prominently only when the block had zero intercepts and an unfinished sub-step; a block full of deflections gets the break immediately, because that user needs recovery, not continuation.

#### [CRITICAL] At the moment of temptation the app fights for attention with a slogan, not with the work: the Airlock re-presents the intention as text to re-read while the task's actual next step never appears

AirlockAndDisarmOverlays.kt:607-678: the intercept card is badge ('AIRLOCK INTERCEPTION • LOCKED'), the blocked app's name at 24sp, an 88sp countdown numeral, then the intention demoted to a caption — 'ACTIVE INTENTION: …' (lines 644-648) — and two buttons that are both about the phone: RETURN TO FOCUS (656) and EMERGENCY PEEK (665). The work's next move exists in the data — FocusTaskEntity substeps with isDone flags (MonolithModels.kt:80-84, 128-137) — but no substep ever reaches this surface; the intercept state carries only sessionIntention. Crawford's skilled coping is not sustained by re-reading a representation of your goal inside your head; it is solicited by the resistant material itself. At the one moment attention is actually decided, Monolith offers a slogan and a negotiation with itself.

Recommendation: Rebuild the Airlock card around the work's next move: centre the active task's first undone substep in the intention slot's place ('PROBLEM 4 OF 6 — INTEGRATION BY PARTS', from TaskSubStep), shrink the countdown numeral to a small mono corner figure, and rename the primary chip from RETURN TO FOCUS to the substep itself ('BACK TO PROBLEM 4'). The intention string moves to a dim secondary line. The user should leave the intercept pulled toward a specific resistant thing, not re-convinced by a motto.

#### [HIGH] Three of the four text fields ignore the keyboard: no IME action, no clear button — the fourth field proves the house knows how

ShieldMatrixScreen.kt:459-475: the Shield app-search BasicTextField is declared with singleLine and a textStyle and nothing else — no keyboardOptions, no keyboardActions, no clear affordance. The same omission repeats at ShieldMatrixScreen.kt:591-610 (the blocked-site field: type a domain, press the keyboard's enter/done key and nothing happens; the only submit path is hunting the separate ADD chip) and DrawerScreen.kt:553-568 (Drawer search). The house standard already exists in-repo and proves this is a one-line-per-field fix: FocusSequencerScreen.kt's task composer sets KeyboardOptions(imeAction = ImeAction.Done) with KeyboardActions(onDone = { submitTask() }). Renders shield.html and drawer.html confirm all three fields are bare recessed boxes with no trailing clear control.

Recommendation: Bring the three neglected fields up to the composer's own standard, in under a day: Shield search gets imeAction=Search plus a trailing clear (x) keycap whenever the query is non-empty (Material 3 SearchBar pattern: clear affordance inside the field, keyboard action matches the field's job); the site field gets imeAction=Done wired to the exact onAddSite path the ADD chip calls, so keyboard and chip are one verb; Drawer search gets imeAction=Search and the same clear control. No new components — copy the KeyboardOptions/KeyboardActions block that already ships in FocusSequencerScreen.

#### [HIGH] Sequence 4 — The Deck before Receipt and Airlock: both are derivatives of the Deck's last frame and its intention text, so they cannot be designed first

MainActivity.kt:~775-785 only composes ReceiptSheet when currentDestination == DECK. receipt.html frame 3 is captioned in its own source as detention holding 'the session's last frame, frozen': same hero ghosts, ProofStrip (BLOCK ON / APPS / ENDS), slide and imprint as deck.html. airlock.html prints 'ACTIVE INTENTION: Finish Chapter 4 Problem Set' — the Deck's task/intention (TactileDeckScreen defaults in deck.html caption) — over its countdown. The receipt slip in receipt.html frame 1 then drops the elapsed duration entirely, printing only ARMED/ENDED wall times, because it inherits the Deck's wall-clock-first data, not a duration-first record.

Recommendation: Fourth, redesign the Deck's arm→run→finish flow as the source of truth (hero = time remaining in the current block, intention in Atkinson 22sp above the wheel, ProofStrip and imprint generated from the same state object), then derive the other two for free: Receipt becomes a print of that state object with a new first line 'ELAPSED 50 MIN — CLEAN' in Sora 22sp, and Airlock becomes the same intention + remaining time at night tokens, following Apple's Activity design where the workout summary reuses the live rings component rather than being a separately designed artefact. Designing Receipt or Airlock before this step designs a copy that the next Deck change breaks.

#### [HIGH] The blocks decision — the second-biggest lever on total time — is hidden as unlabelled dot geometry inside the wheel hub

deck.html caption, from source: 'hub wells 2 of 8 filled (study blocks live only as hub geometry — no numeral or word in code)'. BlockitCoreViews.kt:1014-1097: pressing the hub resolves to a well within 14dp of one of 8 dots on a 40dp ring (direct-set), a tap on a 'closed bar' arc (sets 4 or 8), or anywhere else in the hub (cycle +1, wrapping 8->1 via TactileDeckScreen.kt onCycleBlocksCount). No surface prints the count the user just chose; the only feedback is the hero total jumping by dial+10 minutes per block (TactileDeckScreen.kt:325). To verify '2 blocks of 50' the user must count filled 8dp wells, then reverse-engineer the arithmetic from 1H 50M. Apple Watch's Custom timer, turning the same kind of crown, prints the resulting hours/minutes/seconds numerals as you turn — the control's value is never encoded as geometry to be counted.

Recommendation: Print the decomposition the hero currently conceals, directly under it in the instrument card: '50 MIN x 2 BLOCKS + 10 MIN BREAK = 1H 50M', with the blocks numeral in the same Sora hero voice at reduced size. Demote the hub wells to a display of that numeral, and move block selection to a labelled 1-8 segmented row under the wheel (the Deck already speaks in keycaps — FLOW at TactileDeckScreen.kt is one). One glance verifies all three numbers; no counting, no reverse arithmetic.

#### [HIGH] The consequence line is printed below the commit control, so it is read after the hand is already moving

deck.html pinned stack, in visual order: proof strip, then the 72dp slidezone ('SLIDE OR TAP TO START'), then the empty sentence slot, then the imprint '9 WILL SHUT · 3 PEEK' at the very bottom of the screen. The one line that states what the seal will actually do to the user's apps sits after the control that does it, separated from it by the sentence slot. TactileDeckScreen.kt compounds it: the tenant is frozen into pressLatch at onPressStart (the DOWN frame) — the design itself treats the consequence as press-time information, then places it where a press-time eye, fixed on the cap and thumb, is not looking. Print contracts and order forms put the discipline the other way round: itemised totals stand above the signature line, so the signer reads the consequence before the hand reaches the committing mark.

Recommendation: Invert the stack: move the imprint tenant above the slide zone, directly under the proof strip, and duplicate it onto the moving cap at the point of no return — when displayed travel crosses the 0.68 gate (BlockitCoreViews.kt SlideGestureMath.GATE), flip the cap face from blank orange to '9 SHUT · 3 PEEK · ENDS 10:40' for the remaining travel to the 0.84 catch. The consequence is then read once before the gesture and again under the thumb inside it, instead of once, below it, after it.

#### [HIGH] The expedition's own map disagrees with its odometer: the header declares GUARD 4/4 — journey complete — while the board still lists two unvisited stops

WatchStore.kt:80-100 defines six PERMISSIONS but marks OVERLAY and BATTERY counted=false, leaving COUNTED at four; GuardLine.kt:39 prints 'GUARD 4/4' as the WHOLE state the moment those four are granted. The Park board (design-renders/park.html lines 122-127) prints all six rows in one undifferentiated ruled list — ACCESSIBILITY, USAGE ACCESS, DEVICE ADMIN, NOTIFICATION LISTENER, OVERLAY, BATTERY — with no visual family break between the counted four and the uncounted two. So the header band, the one status sign visible on every screen, can declare the journey complete while the board two taps away still shows OVERLAY MISSING and BATTERY MISSING, and nothing anywhere explains why those two rows don't count.

Recommendation: Make the map and the odometer the same document, the rule Kinneir & Calvert enforced on British Rail signage: one denominator everywhere. Either the header counts all six (GUARD n/6) until the board is fully GRANTED, or the board visually splits the families — the counted four under the warrant, OVERLAY and BATTERY set apart below the existing 16dp family gap with a printed reason on each line ('NOT COUNTED — NO SURFACE USES IT YET'). A traveller should never be told they have arrived while their own departure board still lists unvisited stops.

#### [HIGH] Every sign on the journey is written in Monolith's private vocabulary, not the vocabulary of the place the user is being sent to

WatchStore.kt:81-86 gives each grant an internal boardName — ACCESSIBILITY, USAGE ACCESS, DEVICE ADMIN, NOTIFICATION LISTENER, OVERLAY, BATTERY — and ParkDrawer.kt:458 prints that word verbatim on the only departure sign: 'FIX — NOTIFICATION LISTENER'. But Android's panes do not use these names: the listener pane is headed 'Notification access', the admin pane is 'Device admin apps', and the accessibility and listener panes list services by app name, so the destination the user must actually find and tap is 'Monolith', a word that appears nowhere on the FIX key or the board. one sec's published Android setup guide does the opposite: it names the exact rows in the destination's own vocabulary per Android version ('Scroll down and select one sec', 'select Installed Services'), and explicitly warns about a lookalike 'Accessibility Shortcut' toggle that must stay OFF — a wrong-switch warning Monolith never gives for any of its six panes.

Recommendation: Sign every departure in the destination's own words, the first rule of wayfinding from Kinneir/Calvert to airport signage: a sign that doesn't match the territory's labels is decoration. Before each trip, the FIX flow should print the full path in Settings' vocabulary — e.g. 'SETTINGS OPENS ON A LIST OF APPS. FIND MONOLITH. SWITCH IT ON.' — and where a lookalike toggle exists on the destination pane (the accessibility shortcut toggle one sec warns about), print the warning on the departure card. Rename the board rows to match the panes ('NOTIFICATION ACCESS', 'DEVICE ADMIN APPS') or print both names: Monolith's term as the label, the pane's term as the directions.

#### [HIGH] Two of the six trips are door-to-door and four are drop-offs at an unmarked directory — and the design treats them as the same journey

MainActivity.kt:362-411 (openFixPane) fires two different classes of journey with no design distinction. OVERLAY (lines 387-393) and BATTERY (lines 395-411) carry a package: Uri and land the user on Monolith's own detail page — door-to-door, one switch, done. ACCESSIBILITY (line 366), USAGE_ACCESS (line 368) and NOTIFICATION_LISTENER (lines 382-385) fire bare list intents that drop the user at the top of a system-wide directory of every installed app/service to search unaided. DEVICE_ADMIN (lines 372-380) tries a hardcoded com.android.settings.DeviceAdminSettings component and, if that fails, silently falls back to the root of Security settings — a different neighbourhood entirely, with no marker that the destination moved. The board and FIX key present all six as identical trips; the design never acknowledges that four of them abandon the user at a directory and one may abandon them at the wrong building.

Recommendation: Design the two journey classes differently, the way transit systems sign a direct service differently from one requiring a change. For the deep-linked trips (overlay, battery), keep the single FIX tap. For the directory trips, add a departure card before the intent fires: a monochrome thumbnail of the destination pane with the MONOLITH row and its switch marked — one sec publishes exactly these per-version screenshots in its setup guide — plus the instruction 'YOU LAND ON A LIST. FIND MONOLITH.' For the device-admin fallback, if the direct component fails, do not fire the Security-root intent silently: print that the direct door failed and give the path from Security root ('DEVICE ADMIN APPS IS UNDER SECURITY → OTHER SECURITY SETTINGS') before sending the user there.

#### [HIGH] The journey has no designed endpoints: departure is the app vanishing mid-press, and arrival is a sound with an explicit policy that no word ever prints

ParkDrawer.kt:437-447 fires onFixClick(item) inside the FIX key's onPress — the Settings intent launches on finger-DOWN, mid-press, so the app simply vanishes under the user's finger with no departure beat: nothing has said what the next screen will look like, what 'done' looks like there, or that they should come back. The return is equally undesigned as a visual event: ParkDrawer.kt:192-212 resolves the trip after an 800ms proving delay and, if the grant landed, plays one firm click through the sound engine — the code comment states the policy outright (line 204): 'no word prints, ever.' If sound is off, or the trip failed, the arrival is literally nothing; the board silently re-derives and the FIX key silently re-names itself to the next lack, so the traveller gets no position fix — no 'that stop is done', no count of stops remaining — and must re-read nine ruled lines to work out where they are. one sec's guide narrates the return as an explicit designed step ('go back until you reach the one sec main app again. Here you will be prompted to grant additional permissions') — the next ask is sequenced after a confirmed arrival, not silently swapped under the traveller.

Recommendation: Give the journey designed endpoints. Departure: a one-card interstitial between the FIX press and the intent — destination name in Settings' words, the single action to take there, and the return instruction ('THEN COME BACK HERE'). Arrival: on resume, the repaired board line should stamp GRANTED with a visible transition and the board header should print the expedition's position ('4 OF 6 GRANTED · LAST PROVED HH:mm' already exists as furniture at ParkDrawer.kt:311-335 — extend it to carry the count) before the FIX key re-arms for the next stop. Keep the firm click, but demote it to accompaniment: sound must never be the only arrival sign, because a muted phone currently makes a successful six-trip expedition visually indistinguishable from six failures.

#### [HIGH] The '+5 overtime' adjustment is wired to nothing and aimed at the wrong clock: it would lengthen the next session's dial, not the session that is running

The one adjustment a user in flow actually needs — more time — exists only as a phantom. MainActivity.kt:503 wires onExtendActiveTaskOvertime = { viewModel.extendActiveTaskOvertime(5) } into the Deck, but TactileDeckScreen.kt:124 declares the parameter and never invokes it anywhere in the composable — no chip, no verb, no surface. And the ViewModel function itself is addressed to the wrong clock: MonolithViewModel.kt:1814-1825 extendActiveTaskOvertime extends the TASK's estimate and then unconditionally adds the minutes to _dialMinutes — the idle arm-dial — while the running session's target (activeSession.effectiveTargetSeconds, read at TactileDeckScreen.kt:338) is never touched. Even if the button were rendered tomorrow, pressing '+5' mid-session would silently lengthen the NEXT session's dial and leave this one to expire on schedule.

Recommendation: Give the running Deck one honest time verb, following Forest's first-class in-session extension: in the slide's 72dp zone beside the valve chip, seat a '+10 MIN' chip (tightening-class, so no ratchet conflict) that extends the active session row's target, re-prints the strip's TIME cell to the new end, and stamps 'EXTENDED +10' on the receipt so the proof records the change. Keep task-estimate editing on the Tasks tab under its own name ('TASK ESTIMATE') — never let one control write to two clocks, and delete the dead Deck parameter until the chip exists.

#### [HIGH] The faulted finish is taxed with the longest detention: failure waits the full 1800ms ceiling, then gets a title-less slip

ReceiptState.kt:223-224 Detention.issueOffsetMs: 'if (isFaulted) return RECEIPT_CEILING_MS' — the faulted branch issues at E1800 exactly, the maximum the formula allows, and MonolithViewModel.kt's fallback loop also publishes faulted=true at RECEIPT_CEILING_MS+400. ReceiptSheet.kt then renders that slip with no title at all (faulted branch replaces the title with an empty Box) plus the single line 'SHIELD — STILL BLOCKED (SERVICE DIDN'T STOP)'. So the one finish where the machine, not the user, failed — and the phone may still be blocking — is the finish that detains longest and explains least, visually emptiest at the moment of maximum anxiety.

Recommendation: Invert the tax: a faulted finish should be the FASTEST exit, not the slowest. Issue the faulted slip at the 1480ms floor (or immediately on halt detection), keep the session title on it, and give the fault line the slip's one action — a RETRY RELEASE / OPEN SHIELD STATUS affordance in place of tap-anywhere dismissal. Following iOS/macOS installer and update failure design: when the system is at fault the error surfaces early, names itself, and puts the recovery verb on the failure card itself rather than after the longest wait.

#### [HIGH] The morning after a broken day, the app pretends nothing happened: no return surface, no repair offer, no smaller door back in

ui/screens/TactileDeckScreen.kt:612-632 — the Deck's hero states only the new session's TOTAL span; a grep of the whole screen finds no reference to yesterday, the last session, or any missed/broken state, and design-renders/deck.html confirms the unarmed Deck is byte-identical whether the previous day was kept, broken by the valve, or missed entirely. The user returning after failure is handed the full-size wheel and the full-size demand, with no acknowledgement, no reduced re-entry session and no way to mend the record. Duolingo designs this exact moment: a broken streak triggers a repair/restore offer at return (streak freezes auto-applied, later Streak Revival restoring a lost streak of 30+ days by completing three lessons) because it knows the return after failure is where users are lost; Blockit's tower likewise lets a parachute repair a missed day.

Recommendation: Add a return state to the Deck: when the last judged day was MISSED, PARTIAL or valve-broken, the Deck opens once with a slim 'YESTERDAY BROKE' band above the wheel offering a half-length RE-ENTRY session (pre-set on the wheel, one tap to arm), and completing it stamps the broken day REPAIRED in the Drawer — Duolingo's repair-at-return, rebuilt in Monolith's own receipt vocabulary instead of amnesia.

#### [HIGH] Access narrows as a cliff, not a slope: SLEEP assigns zero PEEK tiers, so messaging goes from 2-minute peek at 19:59 to fully locked at 20:00

MonolithRepository.kt:1152-1162, applySmartLoadout's SLEEP branch: every app whose name lacks 'dialer/phone/clock/alarm/maps' is set AppBlockTier.LOCKED — the PEEK_2M tier that STUDY and WORK_SPRINT both use (MonolithRepository.kt:1131-1151) is assigned to nothing. The loadout's own summary, MonolithRepository.kt:1124: 'Sleep Loadout: Locks everything except Phone, Clock, and Maps.'
