There is no twilight loadout, no staged narrowing, no intermediate state in SmartLoadout (MonolithModels.kt:39-59 has exactly three members). shield.html shows the resulting binary world: every catalogue row is SHUT/PEEK/OPEN by hand, with no evening gradient anywhere. Android's own Bedtime mode makes the opposite design decision — its goal is explicitly not to block apps but to make the phone less engaging (grayscale + DND), and Apple's Wind Down is a separate, earlier, softer period that precedes the Sleep window rather than being it.

Recommendation: Insert a TWILIGHT loadout auto-applied 45 minutes before the SLEEP window and swapped out at window start: SHORT_VIDEO/SOCIAL/GAMES → LOCKED (as now), everything else not already OPEN → PEEK_2M, MESSAGING stays PEEK_2M, Phone/Clock/Maps stay OPEN. The user experiences narrowing as a slope — feeds die first, conversations get a 2-minute knock, then the door closes — reusing the existing tier machinery and peek lease with no new enforcement code.

#### [HIGH] Airlock makes the countdown to temptation the 88sp hero and the user's own intention a 12.5sp footnote, with peek offered as an equal full-width menu chip

AirlockAndDisarmOverlays.kt:636-639 renders the breathing countdown at Anonymous Pro Bold 88sp, the largest type on any intercept surface; the intention that should cue the right action prints at 12.5sp in NightColorPrimary at 80% alpha in the same file around line 645, and the session-end line is the same size/alpha. When the count reaches 00, EMERGENCY PEEK appears as a second full-width 42dp BlockitActionChip directly under the accent RETURN TO FOCUS chip (AirlockAndDisarmOverlays.kt:663-676; MonolithCustomComponents.kt:170-205 gives both chips identical height, radius and border), differing only in fill darkness, with its price in the same 12.5sp/80% style as the intention. airlock.html frames 1-2 show the hierarchy plainly: 03/00 dominates, Instagram 24sp second, intention is body copy.

Recommendation: Rebuild the hierarchy the way one sec builds its intervention — the pause screen centres the breath and the act of reconsidering, not a jackpot timer unlocking the app (one sec's breathing intervention is the whole surface, and its PNAS-studied design reduced openings 57%). Demote the countdown to a 15sp mono readout in the badge line, promote 'ACTIVE INTENTION' to Atkinson Bold 24sp directly under the app name, render the blocked app's name desaturated and struck by a hairline, and demote EMERGENCY PEEK from a chip to a plain 11sp text link at the card's foot with its 20-minute price in the same line — same information, visibly a lesser, costlier door.

#### [HIGH] The arm gesture signs an unpriced contract: the slide itemises apps shut but never bricks earned or the token put at risk

deck.html: the arm surface itemises only the blocklist. The imprint tenant prints '9 WILL SHUT · 3 PEEK' (MonolithCustomComponents.kt splitTenantText), the proof strip's three cells are fixed as BLOCK / APPS / TIME, and the slide track reads 'SLIDE OR TAP TO START'. Nowhere in the press that commits the session does the surface state the session's economy: how many bricks completing it lays, or that the week's token stays at risk behind the valve for its whole duration. Forest's planting screen does state the yield before commitment — the tree species and the coins the completed session earns are printed on the confirm surface itself, so the stake and the reward are read in the same gesture as the plant.

Recommendation: Use the machinery already built for the press: the Deck's PressLatch already freezes the imprint tenant at DOWN (TactileDeckScreen.kt, PressLatch). Add a second tenant line latched the same way — 'EARNS 2 BRICKS · TOKEN 1/1 HELD AT RISK' for a two-block dial setting, computed from the same dial state that computes the hero span. The slide gesture then signs a priced contract, not just a blocklist.

#### [HIGH] The 5-second Airlock pays out in temptation: endurance is the price of the peek, not the space to refuse it

AirlockAndDisarmOverlays.kt:562-569 the 5s countdown is a passive delay loop; :636 the countdown renders at 88sp while the intention renders at 12.5sp at 80% alpha; RETURN TO FOCUS is composed immediately, but the EMERGENCY PEEK chip is only composed when countdownSecs == 0 (:663-678, confirmed in airlock.html frames 1 vs 2). The wait therefore buys exactly one thing - access to the craved app - and buys nothing for the user who turns back.

Recommendation: Stop paying out the peek for endured time: compose both choices at second 0, make the 5 seconds active - the numeral shrinks to 15sp, the intention becomes the hero line, and the peek chip only unlocks after the user taps a breath-pacer or re-taps their stated intention, following one sec, whose breathing pause plus attempt-count is the intervention a PNAS field study (Max Planck/Heidelberg) found cut target-app openings by 57% over six weeks. Waiting must rehearse the return, not purchase the lapse.

#### [HIGH] The emergency exit taxes the body, not the impulse: sixty seconds of grip is a regressive price that emergencies themselves make unpayable

AirlockAndDisarmOverlays.kt:801 rule line 'Hold to fill 60 seconds... If your hand slips, what isn't banked drains away'; BlockitSuitcaseAndSwitchesViews.kt:520-529 and :554-592 implement the price as sustained grip banked in 15s chambers with drain on release; park.html spec plate states the tariff as the product's law: 'HOLD: 60 SECONDS, BANKED EVERY 15 - ONE BREAK A WEEK'. No alternative modality (typing, waiting phone-down, voice) exists anywhere in the overlay.

Recommendation: Keep the 60 seconds but let the user pay it in mind instead of muscle: offer a second equal-price door on the same card - type the session's intention from memory plus hold the phone face-down for 60s (proximity/accelerometer verified) - following ScreenZen's switchable cognitive challenges (typing/math) and one sec's breath, both of which tax attention rather than grip. Print both doors at identical size so the choice of currency is the user's, not their body's.

#### [HIGH] On the Deck the consequence of starting prints below the slide, after the action it describes

TactileDeckScreen.kt:942-950 defines the pinned stack in this order: ProofStripBand (:956, BLOCK/APPS/TIME plus the seam 'BIND HELD - THIS VISIT / PROOF: LIVE BIND'), the 72dp slide (:971-1041), RefusalSentenceSlot (:1058, whose tenant is null in the healthy idle state), then ImprintSlot (:1094) printing '9 WILL SHUT - 3 PEEK'. deck.html shows the same order ending in .imprint .tenant below .slidezone, with .sentence an empty 22px reservation between them. The only line that tells the user what starting will actually do to their apps is the last line of the stack, underneath the control that does it.

Recommendation: Promote the imprint tenant to be the slide's own heading: print '9 WILL SHUT - 3 PEEK' directly above the slide track in ink, as the sentence the slide answers, and collapse the reserved sentence slot to zero height whenever it has no tenant so no blank rung sits in the eye path. This follows the GOV.UK pattern evidence: DWP/GDS user research found people do not read text placed under a start button, so consequence text is kept above the action it governs.

#### [HIGH] The steepest vocabulary lesson is set at the moment of craving, inside the Airlock intercept

design-renders/airlock.html: a user who has just impulsively opened Instagram mid-session is met with 'AIRLOCK INTERCEPTION • LOCKED', 'RETURN TO FOCUS' and, after the countdown, 'EMERGENCY PEEK 2m' plus 'TAKING THE PEEK STARTS A 20 MINUTES COOLDOWN ON THIS APP'. Source: ui/components/AirlockAndDisarmOverlays.kt:607 (badge), :656 (RETURN TO FOCUS), :665 (EMERGENCY PEEK), :235 ('PEEK COOLDOWN — AGAIN IN $minutes MIN'). None of AIRLOCK, PEEK or COOLDOWN has been defined at any earlier point in this user's journey that the intercept can rely on, and PEEK collides with the Shield tier of the same name, which is a standing rule, not this one-off 2-minute lease. The user must decode three coined terms, under time pressure and temptation, to understand the price of the button in front of them.

Recommendation: Crisis surfaces get the plainest language in the product — the principle behind Apple SOS and one sec's intercept, which names the action and its cost in ordinary words ('Open Instagram for 2 minutes? You can do this once, then not again for 20 minutes'). Rewrite the intercept in verbs and numbers only: header 'Instagram is blocked until 18:30', primary 'Go back', secondary 'Open for 2 minutes — once, then locked for 20 minutes'. Reserve coined terms, if any survive, for calm screens where the user has attention to spend learning them.

#### [HIGH] At the temptation moment the Airlock shows only you and the blocked app — the witness vanishes exactly when presence works

The Airlock — the exact second willpower fails — renders only the self and the temptation: badge 'AIRLOCK INTERCEPTION • LOCKED', the blocked app name at 24sp, an 88sp countdown, and 'ACTIVE INTENTION: {own task}' (ui/components/AirlockAndDisarmOverlays.kt:550, 644-656; design-renders/airlock.html frames 1-2). No partner name, no partner state, no 'someone is still in there' line exists in the composable. The lock-screen surface repeats the omission: MonolithShieldService.kt:138-144 builds title 'Monolith • {intention}' and text '{MM:SS} left • Block {i}/{n} • {n} urges stopped' — pure self-metrics. Focusmate makes the opposite decision: the partner's live video tile never leaves the screen for the whole 25/50/75-minute session, so presence is strongest precisely during the silent middle, not just at booking.

Recommendation: Add a witness line to the Airlock card in its existing type system — Atkinson 12.5sp cream at 80%, directly under the intention line: 'A. IS STILL IN · 24 MIN LEFT', driven by the partner's live session state, and give the RETURN TO FOCUS chip a mono badge with the partner's initial so the return action is addressed to someone. Mirror one clause in the shield notification text: '{MM:SS} left • With A. • {n} urges stopped'. No video, no chat — Focusmate's always-visible partner, reduced to the one line of type Monolith's night card can honestly carry.

#### [HIGH] All of Monolith's friction is motor and none is cognitive — the finger travels 92% of a track while the mind is never asked to verify anything

Every fact needed to verify a seal lives in a different place and none is assembled at the gesture: deck.html shows hero '1H 50M' inside the instrument card, the proof strip's 'TIME / ENDS 10:40' and 'APPS 12' in a separate pinned strip, the task 'Finish Chapter 4 Problem Set' in its own row, and the only consequence sentence — imprint '9 WILL SHUT · 3 PEEK' in 10sp mono — printed BELOW the slide zone, after the finger's path, from imprintTenantText in MonolithCustomComponents.kt:450. TactileDeckScreen.kt:1003 freezes that imprint at DOWN (PressLatch), i.e. it is a record of the press, not a check the user must pass before the latch at BlockitCoreViews.kt:2343 dispatches onArmSession.

Recommendation: Spend friction on reading, not just travelling. At the gate (displayed 0.68) arrest the cap and replace the track words with a single assembled readback plate in Atkinson 13sp: 'SEAL 1H 50M · ENDS 10:40 · 9 SHUT, 3 PEEK · FOR FINISH CHAPTER 4' — a second push past the gate, or a 600ms dwell on that plate, is what commits; releasing returns home. This is GitHub's delete-repository / IBM Carbon removal pattern applied to sealing: the friction is cognitive (you must produce/recognise the exact thing being destroyed or locked), not a motor ritual a thumb can perform on autopilot with its eyes elsewhere.

#### [HIGH] Intent is classified by a stopwatch alone — the 90ms floor reads no body, contact-shape or pocket signal that every pocket-mode system uses

SlideGestureMath.isBrush at BlockitCoreViews.kt:1356 is a one-variable classifier: pressDurationMs < BRUSH_FLOOR_MS (90L, line 1327) is a brush, anything else on the cap is an order. beginAttempt's hit test (BlockitCoreViews.kt, Rhea hit-test: drawn cap rect inflated 8dp in x, full track height in y) reads no touch major/size, no pressure, no proximity or ambient-light state, and no screen-wake source — the SlideToStartView contains no sensor read at all. A thigh-through-fabric contact, a bag strap press and a deliberate fingertip tap are indistinguishable to this classifier as long as they last 91ms and move less than the 8dp slop that defines isTap in endDrag.

Recommendation: Replace the clock-only classifier with a body-aware one, following Samsung Accidental Touch Protection and Xiaomi/OnePlus Pocket Mode, which fuse the proximity sensor with low ambient light (Samsung documents <10 lux) to decide a contact is in a pocket and ignore it. Concretely: while proximity is covered or light is pocket-dark, disable the tap path entirely and raise the drag requirement (movement must exceed 24dp with a changing touch-major typical of a fingertip); reject contacts whose touch major exceeds a fingertip band as fabric/palm regardless of duration. Duration should be the weakest signal in the classifier, not the only one.

#### [HIGH] Friction is a flat tariff — the identical 90ms tap and 0.92 throw seal a 5-minute FLOW and a multi-hour 12-app lockdown

GATE 0.68, CATCH 0.84, BRUSH_FLOOR_MS 90 and mesh target 0.92 are compile-time constants in SlideGestureMath (BlockitCoreViews.kt:1312-1327, 2132) with no input from what is being sealed. Yet the Deck's own range is enormous: deck.html's wheel is graduated 30-180 minutes, TactileDeckScreen.kt wires onCycleBlocksCount up to 8 blocks, the FLOW keycap sets the dial to 5 minutes, and the proof strip in the same render seals 12 apps. A 5-minute FLOW session with the same commit throw as a multi-hour, 12-app seal means the design prices a reversible trivial commitment and a phone-locking afternoon identically.

Recommendation: Make friction a priced material that scales with stakes (span x apps shut). Tier it: under 25 minutes and <=3 shut — current single slide; 25-90 minutes or 4-8 shut — slide plus a 600ms dwell on the gate readback; over 90 minutes, over 8 shut, or any seal whose ENDS time crosses midnight — slide, readback dwell of 1,200ms, and a second distinct push to latch. This follows the Carbon/GitHub principle that confirmation rigour scales with severity and irreversibility, instead of Monolith's flat tariff where the cheapest and the costliest seal cost the finger exactly the same.

#### [HIGH] Two assembly lines, no shared parts bin: routine sessions cannot use the Deck's blocks, hand sessions cannot reference a loadout

Sessions are built on two separate assembly lines that share an output row but no parts bin. A hand session is composed on the Deck from dial minutes, an intention and a block structure (blocks 1..8, MonolithViewModel setStudyBlocksCount; StudyModePreset.defaultBlocks up to 4, MonolithModels.kt:61-72), and a loadout reaches it only by destructively rewriting the global tier wall beforehand. A routine session is materialised by a different builder that hardcodes studyBlocksCount = 1 (MonolithRepository.kt:1090-1099, materialiseRoutineSession) — the block composition simply does not exist on that line — takes its intention from the routine's name and its identity from routineId (RoutineDerive.kt DesiredSession, lines 28-37). The finished FocusSessionEntity records routineId and window snapshot but no loadout reference at all (MonolithModels.kt:268-340): a hand session cannot say which tier configuration it ran under, and a routine session cannot carry the Deck's block structure. On one rail, any shelf, cabinet and desk combine in one installation; here the two ways of starting a session cannot exchange a single part.

Recommendation: Build one session assembler whose inputs are composable parts — source window (hand or routine), tier-configuration reference, block structure, intention/task bond — and have both the Deck arm path and materialiseRoutineSession call it. Add a blocks stepper to the routine editor writing into that assembler, and store the loadoutId on the session row so every receipt can name the exact configuration it ran under.

#### [HIGH] At the moment of commitment the Deck names only counts — '9 WILL SHUT · 3 PEEK' — never which apps the guest is about to lose

MonolithCustomComponents.kt:470-477: the imprint sentence is built purely from counts ('$shut WILL SHUT', '$peek PEEK'); TactileDeckScreen.kt:471-488 wires only shutCount/peekCount into the strip and imprint (deck.html shows '9 WILL SHUT · 3 PEEK' beside the slide). A thoughtful host tells the guest which rooms close tonight before they sit down; Monolith's guest must abandon the arming flow, travel to the Shield room, and audit the matrix by hand to learn who is on the list — or slide first and discover it at the first Airlock.

Recommendation: Make the imprint sentence expandable in place: tapping '9 WILL SHUT · 3 PEEK' on the Deck unfolds the actual names in two lines (SHUT: Instagram, TikTok… · PEEK: WhatsApp, YouTube…) inside the same hero card, above the slide, so the guest reads the guest list in the room where they commit — no trip to Shield required to know the terms of the evening.

#### [HIGH] The liminal middle has no internal time: hour three renders identically to minute one, so the ordeal is one undifferentiated duration

In rites of passage the limen is sequenced — ordeals, sacra and elders mark where the initiand is inside the transition; unmarked duration is precisely what turns a held threshold into mere waiting. Monolith's running hero is a single format from first second to last: displaySeconds = activeSession.remainingSeconds rendered as '%02d:%02d' (ui/screens/TactileDeckScreen.kt L312, L319-322), with only a progress fraction changing, and the eyebrow never advances beyond 'SESSION RUNNING' (L615). Worse, long spans are pre-chopped into identical cells — totalSpanMinutes = dialMinutes × blocks + (blocks − 1) × 10 (L325-329) — so a 3-hour session is three copies of the same 50 minutes with the same 10-minute break, structure imposed on the limen rather than phases unfolding within it. Nothing on screen at minute 100 tells the user they are deep, past halfway, or near return.

Recommendation: Give the limen phases and name them on the Deck eyebrow and hero: OPENING (first 10 minutes, countdown shown), DEEP (middle, countdown replaced by elapsed time and the wheel's progress track only — no numbers to watch), and CLOSING (final 10 minutes, hero switches to the ENDS clock time). A user who can tell where they are inside the threshold is held by it; a user staring at one undifferentiated countdown is just enduring it.

#### [HIGH] The emergency exit prints its own rulebook: mid-emergency, while holding a finger down for 60 seconds, the user must read three lines of banking law

ui/components/AirlockAndDisarmOverlays.kt:801, composed inside the DisarmChallengeOverlay under the valve: 'Hold to fill 60 seconds. Every 15 seconds banks. If your hand slips, what isn't banked drains away. The banked part stays.' — four clauses of mechanism (fill, banking interval, drain-on-slip, retention) rendered at 11sp in cream at 75% opacity (airlock.html frame 3), to be studied at the single moment the user is, by definition, in distress and already performing a sustained 60-second hold. This is obstinacy in Heidegger's precise sense: at breakdown the tool does not merely appear, it stands in the way demanding inspection of its rules before it will yield. A fire exit that required reading its hydraulic specification would fail the same test.

Recommendation: Delete the rule paragraph from DisarmChallengeOverlay. Put the whole law in the valve's own label, where the eye already is: idle 'HOLD 60s — BANKED EVERY 15s', holding 'KEEP HOLDING • 42s • 15s BANKED'. Move the drain rule to the one calm moment it can be learned — a single line under the valve description on Shield, where the emergency break is configured, not where it is used.

#### [HIGH] One wall for every gumption trap: the Airlock never asks whether the reach is boredom, anxiety or need

AirlockAndDisarmOverlays.kt:607 badges the intercept with the machine's own classification ('AIRLOCK INTERCEPTION • <reason>') and :648 shows 'ACTIVE INTENTION: …', but the surface never asks why this reach, now. Pirsig separates the value traps because each has a different cure: boredom is cured by stopping and changing the work, anxiety by learning more before acting, impatience by allowing more time, a genuine need by simply getting the thing. Monolith prescribes one remedy — wait, or return — for all of them, so the bored user is told to endure the exact condition that is draining his gumption, and the anxious user who needs one fact is treated as a relapsing addict.

Recommendation: Add a three-chip reason row to the Airlock intercept card — BORED / NEED ONE THING / JUST HABIT — and route each differently: BORED offers 'END CLEAN AND CHANGE THE WORK' (books a lawful early finish, no valve, no token); NEED ONE THING opens the timed peek directly; JUST HABIT starts the standard hold. Print the chosen word on the receipt's deflection line (ReceiptSheet.kt deflections list) so the log records causes, not just attempts.

#### [HIGH] The emergency token is counterfeit currency: Monolith mints one coin a week and charges it back for the user's own freedom

MonolithRepository.kt:2168-2185 derives the emergency exit as remaining = 1 − spends in an append-only ledger (MonolithModels.kt:433-434), and completeEmergencyBreak refuses at zero regardless of circumstance. The app first confiscates access to the user's own phone, then issues exactly one unit of a currency it invented, at zero cost to itself, with which the user buys their own freedom back — once a week. Bogost's counterfeit incentive is here inverted into a counterfeit price: the scarcity is entirely fictional, but the denial at zero tokens is real. The 60-second hold and the printed record already supply honest friction; the token adds only a mint.

Recommendation: Abolish the token as currency on the Airlock/valve surface: replace 'TOKENS REMAINING' with a declaration flow — the valve always exists, the 60s hold stays, and the user picks a printed reason (EMERGENCY / ILL / FAMILY — the day-words the Drawer already uses) that is stamped on the receipt and in the Drawer day record. Scarcity is replaced by testimony: exits are unlimited, unreusable as a lie, and permanently on the record instead of rationed by a fictional coin.

#### [HIGH] No bench, only legislation: every experimental tap is a live commit — and a routine fiddle re-stamps the judgement horizon

Every building gesture in Shield commits instantly to the live, enforced rule set. slipTap calls onSetAppTier directly on tap (ShieldMatrixScreen.kt, slipTap/slipLines region ~195-260); the cap tap bulk-applies a loadout in the same gesture (lines 285-294); every routine chip tap runs persistRoutine, which re-stamps scheduleEditedAtMillis and forces an immediate reconcile (MonolithViewModel.kt:1501-1518) — and that stamp is the legal horizon that decides whether past windows can be judged MISSED (MonolithModels.kt:562-568). There is no draft, sketch or discard state anywhere in the file. Mari's plans invited variation during making ('the designs have no measurements… you can make changes'); Monolith makes experimentation indistinguishable from legislation, so a user exploring a routine at the bench rewrites their own judgement history.

Recommendation: Add a bench mode to Shield: entering EDIT puts all cap, sled, site and routine changes into a DRAFT state (header prints 'DRAFT — NOT IN FORCE' with a changed-line count and a diff tally in the standing-orders grammar), with APPLY and DISCARD as the only exits. scheduleEditedAtMillis and the reconcile fire only on APPLY, so trying a window at the bench can never re-stamp the record or re-tier a single app.

#### [MEDIUM] CUT 5 — Delete the Airlock's 88sp countdown numeral: the wait is the hero, the decision is not

AirlockAndDisarmOverlays.kt:634-641 prints the breathing-delay countdown as an 88sp Anonymous Pro numeral ('0%d' / '00'), the largest type in the whole intercept, between 'SESSION ENDS 18:30' (AirlockAndDisarmOverlays.kt:625-633) and 'ACTIVE INTENTION: …' (:644-653). airlock.html Frames 1-2 show the consequence: '03' dominates a card whose only decision is RETURN TO FOCUS, and at expiry the card keeps a dead '00' hero while the EMERGENCY PEEK chip finally appears below it — the numeral teaches second-counting, then remains as spent decoration.

Recommendation: Delete the 88sp numeral entirely. Replace it with a 4dp hairline under the app name that drains over the 5 seconds (same information, no counting), and let the card start at its final height with RETURN TO FOCUS as its visual hero; the peek chip fades in at the same address when the line empties. Reference decision: Apple Watch's Breathe/Mindfulness session renders the wait as an expanding/contracting form rather than a giant seconds readout, because displaying the count makes the wait feel longer and more adversarial. Gain: the intercept card shrinks by ~100dp, the verb — not the punishment — becomes the biggest thing on the wall, and there is no '00' corpse left on screen.

#### [MEDIUM] The Safe Break is an adjustment the system makes to the user: it is never announced in advance, cannot be pulled forward or deferred, and its only verb is END

Breaks are the session's rhythm, but the user has no hand on them. MonolithRepository.kt:110 fixes SAFE_BREAK_DURATION_SECONDS at 10 minutes and the span math inserts breaks between blocks automatically; the running Deck (deck.html, TactileDeckScreen.kt) shows only remaining time — no 'next break' fact anywhere — until the break is already running, when the eyebrow flips to 'BREAK · N MIN' (TactileDeckScreen.kt:615-616). During the break the Deck's entire adjustment vocabulary is one verb, END BREAK (TactileDeckScreen.kt:930-936): a user two minutes from a block boundary who needs the break now cannot pull it forward, a user in flow cannot defer the incoming one, and neither choice is even shown as existing. Intent-to-value for 'I need to pause in 3 minutes, not 25' is: abandon via the 60-second valve, or wait.

Recommendation: Print the rhythm on the running Deck and make it negotiable within the seal, as Pomodoro timers like Flow do with a visible, skippable next break: under the hero, one mono line — 'NEXT BREAK 14:20 · 10 MIN' — tappable to open two lawful verbs, 'TAKE IT NOW' (starts the Safe Break early, total span unchanged) and 'WORK THROUGH IT' (skips this one break, once, and prints the skip on the receipt). Both are tighten-or-neutral moves, so they need no valve and no token — they simply return timing agency the seal currently confiscates along with the apps.

#### [MEDIUM] Same finish, opposite tempos: a watched end detains 1.8s with a sound score, a discovered end gets zero ceremony

MonolithViewModel.kt onFinishE0 has two issuance paths for the same finish kinds: witnessed finishes go through FinishState, the E-clock sounds and Detention's 1480–1800ms hold; the unwitnessed branch ('Branch U, late: claim + issue at discovery. No held frame, no pulse, no detention — the receipt simply stands when he next looks') calls repository.publishReceipt and emitReceipt immediately, and the public publishReceipt(sessionId) facade does the same. ReceiptState.restored slips likewise 'render settled, never re-Strike, and never arm E6'. The identical 50-minute achievement therefore ends in either a scored 1.8s ceremony or in paperwork already standing, depending purely on whether the app happened to be foreground at E0.

Recommendation: Give the discovered finish a compressed version of the same ceremony on first view, not none: when a receipt is first presented via the discovery/restore path, run a single-beat settle (hero already flipped to elapsed, slip rises on specB, one completion pulse if the kind pulses) before it becomes the settled, dismissible slip — subsequent views stay still. Following Apple Fitness/Strava: an activity you finished away from the phone still opens with its summary moment (rings closing / trophy beat) the first time you look; only repeat views are static history.

#### [MEDIUM] The app already has a weekly calendar event — the emergency-token renewal — and it turns over in total silence, wasting the natural scaffold for a day-7 moment

MonolithRepository.kt:2168-2178 derives the weekly emergency token from MonolithWeek.weekAnchorMillis(nowMillis) and ticks it via weekAnchorTickFlow() (lines 2189-2204): every seventh day the app's allowance silently resets. No surface marks the turn — deck.html shows the Deck's header ('GUARD 4/4'), proof strip ('BIND HELD · THIS VISIT') and imprint ('9 WILL SHUT · 3 PEEK') are all present-visit facts, identical on day 1, day 7 and day 70, and the token renewal produces no line, sound or state change anywhere a user looks.

Recommendation: Attach the week-turn to the furniture that already exists, following how Apple frames 'Ring in the New Year' — an ordinary weekly rhythm (close the rings seven days in January) presented as a named, dated award rather than a new mechanic. On the first Deck open after a week anchor where the prior week contained at least one clean sealed session, let the ImprintSlot tenant line (MonolithCustomComponents.kt ImprintSlot, currently 'N WILL SHUT · N PEEK') read 'WEEK 2 · TOKEN RENEWED · LAST WEEK HELD' for that visit only, then revert. No new screen, no counter wall — the anniversary rides the one weekly fact the system already computes.

#### [MEDIUM] There is no single cancel grammar — reversing cancels a drag, a secret second finger cancels the mesh, and nothing cancels the seat

Cancelling means three different things in three invisible machine modes. In DRAG, releasing below the catch springs home (animateSpringBack in endDrag). In MESH, only a SECOND touch anywhere aborts — onTouchEvent at BlockitCoreViews.kt:1847/1859 calls startAbortReturn on ACTION_DOWN/ACTION_POINTER_DOWN while mode==MESH, a second-finger gesture the track only advertises as 'TAP AGAIN TO UNDO' (WORDS_UNDO, line 2408, shown only while mode==MESH at line 1787, i.e. during the 140ms mesh). In SEAT there is no cancel at all: the seatFloor clamp at BlockitCoreViews.kt:2317-2318 forbids reversal and no touch branch reaches stepSeat. The user cannot see which mode they are in — deck.html/render track words are frozen as 'SLIDE OR TAP TO START' through every drag state.

Recommendation: Give the seal one cancel grammar that works in every mode until the latch knock at displayed 0.97: reversing direction and dragging back below GATE_RELEASE 0.66, or lifting the finger, cancels — including un-seating a seat that has not yet latched (drop the one-way seatFloor clamp before 0.97). Print that grammar on the track from the first movement: once displayed >0, the words become 'SLIDE BACK TO CANCEL' and stay until latch. Follow the virtual shutter in Camera FV-5 and iOS slide-to-cancel: hold/drag engages, dragging away or releasing before the endpoint cancels, with the same finger and the same motion that started it — never a secret second finger.

### Microcopy and voice — 38 findings (6 critical, 27 high, 5 medium, 0 low)

#### [CRITICAL] The clock face is permanently defaced by its own exit instructions — the room reads 'TAP ANYWHERE TO EXIT' before it reads the time

AirlockAndDisarmOverlays.kt:154 renders 'NIGHTSTAND DESK CLOCK • TAP ANYWHERE TO EXIT' as the top line of the face for the entire session (Atkinson Bold 11sp, NightColorPrimary at 0.6 alpha, AirlockAndDisarmOverlays.kt:153-159), and receipt.html frame 4 shows it sitting permanently above the 96sp numerals. The Braun DN40 (Rams/Lubs, 1976) puts every control on the back of the housing, shaped to be operated blind, precisely so the face carries nothing but time; Monolith instead prints its operating manual — and its escape hatch — on the face itself, so anyone glancing at the desk object reads an instruction to end the session before they read the session.

Recommendation: Remove the eyebrow from the sustained face entirely. Show the mode/exit line only as a 4-second entry caption that fades out when the clock arms, and move exit to a deliberate long-press on the bottom corner zone (with a small etched dot as its only marker). The standing face should contain exactly three things: numerals, progress bar, intention banner — nothing addressed to the owner's fingers.

#### [CRITICAL] The UI's only element named 'Refusal' never refuses anything: it reports machine faults, and health renders as 22dp of blank space

MonolithCustomComponents.kt:490-513 defines RefusalAction/RefusalSentence and refusalSentenceFor(): its complete vocabulary is 'BLOCKING IS OFF — TAP TO FIX', 'CAN'T CHECK BLOCKING — TAP TO RETRY', 'USAGE ACCESS IS OFF — TAP TO FIX' — every sentence is the machine reporting its own fault and asking for a repair tap. Healthy state returns null, commented 'the slot renders its reserved emptiness'; RefusalSentenceSlot (line 716) is a fixed 22dp Box that stays visibly blank, as deck.html and receipt.html frame 3 both render it — an empty .sentence strip under the slide on the healthy Deck. TactileDeckScreen.kt:1060-1075 wires the slot only to jam, annulment and warrant-fault sentences; a running session is explicitly silent. The word 'refusal' exists in this UI, but it is always aimed at a broken permission, never at a temptation, a category, or a product the app declines to be.

Recommendation: Give the slot a healthy tenant: when a session is sealed and the warrant is LIVE, print the session's own refusal in the same Atkinson Bold 15sp — e.g. '12 SHUT · 3 PEEK UNTIL 10:40 — NOTHING ELSE OPENS' — so the one line named Refusal speaks to the user at the moment of commitment, not only to the repairman when a permission dies. Reserve the fault sentences for Park's Guard board, which already lists GRANTED/MISSING per permission. Light Phone publishes its refusals ('will never support social networking, browsing or ad-driven platforms') as standing copy, not as an error state; Monolith's refusal line should likewise exist when nothing is wrong.

#### [CRITICAL] Valve copy speaks in scarcity and plumbing at the moment of emergency: 'only break this week', 'what isn't banked drains away' — no acknowledgement, no reassurance

AirlockAndDisarmOverlays.kt:762-774: title 'EMERGENCY BREAK', body (tokens>0) 'This ends the session early. It is the only break this week.'; rule at :800-801 'Hold to fill 60 seconds. Every 15 seconds banks. If your hand slips, what isn't banked drains away. The banked part stays.'; only exit chip :809 'KEEP FOCUSING'. Render airlock.html frame 3 shows the same three blocks and nothing else: no line naming why the user is here, what they keep if they proceed, or when the break renews.

Recommendation: Rewrite as a three-line humane pattern following Finch/GOV.UK: acknowledge, preserve, consequence. E.g. line 1: 'Something urgent came up — this break is here for that.' Line 2 (reassurance first): 'Your elapsed time and held count stay on the receipt.' Line 3 (consequence, dated not threatened): 'This uses this week's break; the next one arrives Monday.' Move the banking mechanics out of prose into the valve's own labels ('15s banked' ticks at each seam) so a distressed user reads zero metaphor. Rename the exit chip 'KEEP FOCUSING' to 'NOT NOW — BACK TO SESSION' so declining is a neutral choice, not a moral verdict.

#### [CRITICAL] The shield-gap receipt blames the session in the app's own failure: 'THE SHIELD WAS OFF' is a bold accusation with no apology, duration or reassurance

ReceiptSheet.kt:143-147 prints, bold 12sp onBackground, 'THE SHIELD WAS OFF FOR PART OF THAT SESSION'; MonolithRepository.kt:1688 sets the outcome word to 'ENDED · SHIELD GAP'; ReceiptSheet.kt:155-163 prints the faulted line 'SHIELD — STILL BLOCKED (SERVICE DIDN'T STOP)'. Render receipt.html frame 1 shows the slip's register: every other line is a neutral fact (ARMED/ENDED/HELD); the gap line is the only sentence, the only bold line, and it carries no duration, no cause, no reassurance that the held counts above it are still valid, and no next action.

Recommendation: Make the system the subject and give the Nielsen three parts — what happened, that it was the app's fault, what is still true. Replace with sentence case: 'Monolith stopped watching for part of this session — that's on the app, not you.' plus a quantified second line in the slip's mono register: 'UNWATCHED 04 MIN · HELD COUNTS BEFORE AND AFTER STILL COUNT'. Replace 'SHIELD — STILL BLOCKED (SERVICE DIDN'T STOP)' with 'Blocking didn't switch off cleanly. Force-stop Monolith in Settings if this repeats.' Never let 'SHIELD GAP' appear as the user's outcome word; keep it as an internal classification only.

#### [CRITICAL] The user is never the subject of a single sentence — sessions get verdicts, the person gets erased

receipt.html Frame 1: the slip's lines are 'ARMED 18:42 · PLANNED 50 MIN', 'ENDED 19:32 · ENDED', 'HELD 12 APPS · 3 SITES' — no pronoun, no human verb. MonolithRepository.kt:1683-1690 receiptOutcomeWord() returns only 'ATTENDED', 'PARTIAL', 'SLEPT THROUGH', 'FLOW ENDED', 'ENDED' — the session is the subject of every sentence. ReceiptSheet.kt:147 and :176 complete the voice: 'THE SHIELD WAS OFF FOR PART OF THAT SESSION' and 'THE MACHINE KEEPS ITS OWN LOG · YOUR STUDY RECORD LIVES IN YPT' — the only named actor on the artifact is THE MACHINE.

Recommendation: Rewrite the verdict line in second person with the user as subject, following James Clear's identity-vote framing in Atomic Habits and Forest's 'You planted…' receipt copy: replace 'ENDED 19:32 · ENDED' with 'YOU STAYED · 19:32' for clean finishes, 'YOU CAME BACK · PARTIAL' for partials, and change the footer to 'YOUR LOG · № 048 OF YOUR SESSIONS'. Add one identity line under the title, set in Atkinson 15sp bold like the title itself: 'Another session as the person who finishes Chapter 4.' Every outcome word in receiptOutcomeWord() must become a YOU-verb phrase, never a bare classification.

#### [CRITICAL] The app's only human voice is written and never spoken: four coaching sentences exist in code and the Airlock composes none of them

MonolithModels.kt:195-218 defines DistractionTriggerReason with four genuinely human, sentence-case, second-person coachingTip strings ('Your thumb tapped this on autopilot. Take one slow breath and return to your next micro-step.' :203; 'Doomscrolling drains working memory faster than resting…' :213). But AirlockAndDisarmOverlays.kt:552 accepts onSelectReason and the composed overlay (badge 'AIRLOCK INTERCEPTION • …', 88sp countdown, 'ACTIVE INTENTION:', RETURN TO FOCUS / EMERGENCY PEEK chips — confirmed in design-renders/airlock.html) never renders a reason selector or any coachingTip; MonolithViewModel.kt:2413/2438 only logs selectedReason.shortTag. The user in the hardest moment gets a number and telemetry, while the one warm voice the product ever wrote sits in an enum as dead code.

Recommendation: Compose the voice that already exists: under the countdown in the Airlock, print the selected reason's coachingTip verbatim in 13sp sentence-case Atkinson (the digest sheet already proves this register fits), and let the reason default from the intercept badge instead of a hidden MUSCLE_MEMORY default. Follow one sec, whose entire intervention is a spoken pause + a reflective prompt before 'continue or dismiss' — Monolith has the harder block AND the better sentences; it just has to put the sentence on the wall.

#### [HIGH] The decision chips speak in the warden's voice — second-person imperatives and system nouns — where one sec's choices are first-person declarations in the user's own voice, naming the app being decided about

AirlockAndDisarmOverlays.kt:656 'RETURN TO FOCUS' is an order issued to the user; :665 'EMERGENCY PEEK' is a system noun-phrase labelling a mechanism; neither string names the intercepted app, and the header at :607 ('AIRLOCK INTERCEPTION • LOCKED') describes the app's own machinery. airlock.html confirms every word on the screen is the system talking about itself or commanding. one sec's post-breath screen offers 'I don't want to open Instagram' and 'Continue to Instagram' — first-person statements, in the user's voice, naming the specific app. Tapping one is not obeying an instruction; it is the user declaring their own decision, which is what makes it a commitment device rather than a gate. Monolith's user taps a command; one sec's user makes a statement

Recommendation: Rewrite the two decision chips as first-person declarations that name the intercepted app, built from state.interceptedAppName: the return chip becomes e.g. 'I DON'T NEED INSTAGRAM RIGHT NOW' and the peek becomes 'OPEN INSTAGRAM ANYWAY — 2 MIN'. Keep the telemetry badge voice for logs and receipts where it belongs, but at the decision beat the only voice on screen should be the user's own, pre-written for them to stand behind.

#### [HIGH] FLOW is a lone, unexplained keycap that silently resets the dial to 5 — with no TIMED cap to tap back

TactileDeckScreen.kt:714-740: the only mode control on the Deck is a lone FLOW keycap whose click handler calls onSelectStudyPreset(STOPWATCH_FLOW) AND onDialMinutesChanged(5) — one curious tap silently destroys a dialled 50-minute setup, resetting it to 5. There is no TIMED counterpart cap to tap back, and at TactileDeckScreen.kt:641 the hero's reward for tapping is that the 72sp duration readout is replaced by the single word FLOW, with no line anywhere explaining that FLOW means an open-ended stopwatch with no set end (the proof strip's 'NO END' at line 379 is the closest, in 10sp plate type). deck.html shows the idle Deck: FLOW sits alone at the wheel's foot with an empty right-hand side of its row where its counterpart should be.

Recommendation: Replace the lone cap with the two-stop selector grammar the app already built for ShieldCapSelector (STUDY/WORK/SLEEP): a TIMED | FLOW track where both modes are named, both are visible, and the cap marks the current one. Stop resetting the dial: entering FLOW stores dialMinutes and leaving FLOW restores it, so the mode switch is reversible in one tap. Add one 11sp subline under FLOW when active — 'NO SET END · COUNTS UP' — following Apple Clock's Timer/Stopwatch segmented control, where both modes are labelled peers and neither tap is destructive.

#### [HIGH] Park screenshot reads as a device service menu: 'GUARD', a permission checklist and an ML-01 spec plate, with no sentence saying whether the user is protected

park.html: the sheet opens 'GUARD' (Sora 22sp), then 'LAST PROVED 21:47 · SELF-REPORT', then nine rows of system jargon with verdicts — ACCESSIBILITY GRANTED, USAGE ACCESS GRANTED, DEVICE ADMIN GRANTED, NOTIFICATION LISTENER MISSING, SHORTS + REELS OFF — and a single action key 'FIX — NOTIFICATION LISTENER' (ParkDrawer.kt:315,342-343). Below sits a spec plate in 10sp mono: 'MONOLITH ML-01 / UNIT Nº 01 · BUILT FOR ONE USER · NOT FOR SALE' and 'SOUND: FLOAT-PCM, 4 PARTIALS · POWER: YOUR PHONE' (ParkDrawer.kt:106-107,123). No row is grouped under a plain heading, no overall verdict sentence exists, and nothing in the screenshot connects this checklist to the user's focus being protected or unprotected.

Recommendation: Put the verdict before the checklist, following Android's own Security & privacy / Safety Check pattern — one plain status sentence ('No issues found' style) at the top, diagnostic detail underneath: replace the 'LAST PROVED' line with an Atkinson 16sp sentence that recomputes from the board, e.g. 'Protection is on except notifications — 8 of 9 checks working', group the rows under 'Permissions' and 'Blockers' in plain words with 'Device admin' glossed as 'Stops the app being deleted mid-session', and move the ML-01 spec plate off this sheet entirely to an About screen, where a collector's nameplate belongs. The FIX key should then read 'Fix notifications' with the technical name as its subtitle.

#### [HIGH] The one sentence that could earn the permissions — 'DATA: ON THIS PHONE ONLY' — is buried as spec-plate trivia

The app's only plain privacy promise, 'DATA: ON THIS PHONE ONLY', exists once: ParkDrawer.kt:121, inside PLATE_BODY, rendered at ParkDrawer.kt:637 in Anonymous Pro 400 10sp at the foot of the Park drawer, below the sound and theme sleds, in the identical style and list as 'SOUND: FLOAT-PCM, 4 PARTIALS' and 'POWER: YOUR PHONE' (park.html spec plate). It never appears on the Guard board it should reassure, on the FIX path, or in the permission primer copy at AirlockAndDisarmOverlays.kt:512, whose single sentence sells only benefit: 'Grant Accessibility & Usage Access so Monolith can intercept distracting apps, or arm the session immediately.' The claim is even backed in code — AndroidManifest.xml sets allowBackup=false so the sentence stays true — yet it is typeset as hi-fi trivia. Signal and DuckDuckGo put the equivalent on-device/no-collection claim at the decision point, in headline weight.

Recommendation: Promote the covenant from the spec plate to the decision surfaces, in Atkinson (the app's sentence face), not mono trivia. Put a three-line trust block directly under the GUARD header in Park, above the board: 'Reads your screen and notifications to block them. / Everything stays on this phone — backup is off, nothing is sent. / Revoke any line below in Android Settings and Monolith stops.' Repeat the middle line as the FIX key's subline and as the primer's second sentence, so the reassurance is present at the exact moment of granting, not discoverable only by scrolling past the sound settings. Keep the plate line; demote nothing else.

#### [HIGH] The product deleted its own wind-down: the routine named 'Night Wind-Down' was renamed 'SLEEP' and hardened, and the loadout now calls rest 'Full Lockdown / Strict Mode'

MonolithRepository.kt:885-893, reseed S2: the shipped seed 'Night Wind-Down' (startMinutes=1350 / 22:30, endMinutes=420 / 07:00) is migrated in place to name='SLEEP', startMinutes=1200 (20:00), endMinutes=210 (03:30) — the gentle name removed, the start moved 2.5 hours earlier, the end moved 3.5 hours earlier. The loadout it applies speaks pure carceral language, MonolithModels.kt:54-58: title 'Full Lockdown', badge 'Strict Mode', and a subtitle that tacks rest on as an afterthought — 'Blocks every distracting app except Phone, Clock, and Maps for total focus or wind-down' — claiming wind-down in prose while delivering lockdown in behaviour. No surface in the app uses the words wind-down, dusk, evening or rest for this window. Apple keeps the two concepts lexically and mechanically separate: 'Wind Down' is the named pre-bed period (15 min–3h, dimming, calming shortcuts) and 'Sleep' is what follows it; Philips names its function 'RelaxBreathe', not 'Lockdown'.

Recommendation: Restore the distinction in copy and in state: rename the pre-window period TWILIGHT / WIND-DOWN everywhere (Deck readout, Shield row sub-line, PARK theme readout in MonolithViewModel.kt evaluateTheme, which currently can only print 'AUTO · NIGHT — SLEEP 20:00'), retitle the SLEEP loadout from 'Full Lockdown / Strict Mode' to language of rest (e.g. title 'Night', badge 'Quiet'), and rewrite the subtitle to describe the descent honestly: what closes first, what stays on a knock, what stays open. Copy is the cheapest layer of this fix and the one the user reads every night.

#### [HIGH] The week's closing word is a stored enum, not a sentence: seven WindowJudgement codes, a one-word outcomeWord field, and UNKNOWN designed to print nothing

RoutineDerive.kt:53 enum class WindowJudgement { ATTENDED, PARTIAL, MISSED, HELD, LATE_FIRE, NOT_DELIVERED, UNKNOWN }, with the header comment at RoutineDerive.kt:50-52 stating UNKNOWN 'prints nothing, books nothing'. The receipt layer hard-codes the same ceiling: ReceiptState.kt:138 outcomeWord is a single String word, ReceiptSheet.kt renders it only as a suffix ('ENDED {hhmm} · {outcomeWord}'), and MonolithRepository.kt:1683-1689 receiptOutcomeWord maps every finish kind to one word ('ATTENDED', 'PARTIAL', 'SLEPT THROUGH'). There is no sentence template anywhere in the codebase — no second person, no cause, no consequence — so a week that contained illness, a shield failure and one kept session can only ever be filed as disconnected codes. Duolingo's weekly progress email is built on the opposite grammar: what you did, what it means versus last week, and one suggested next step, in sentences.

Recommendation: Design a code-to-sentence closing grammar and store its output, not the code, as the week's last line: judgement + witnessed cause + next-week consequence, set as Atkinson prose (the receipt title face, 15sp), never as a mono suffix. Worked forms: MISSED + ILL word declared → 'Wednesday was declared ILL. It is not counted as a miss.'; NOT_DELIVERED → 'Tuesday's session never reached your phone — that one is on the machine, not on you.'; UNKNOWN → a printed sentence is mandatory ('Thursday left no proof either way, so the letter says so') — silence about a day is banned as a design rule, replacing the 'prints nothing' law for the weekly surface.

#### [HIGH] A zero week and a kept week receive the identical artefact — three zeros — so the correspondence has no rhetoric for failure, absence or rest

compute7DayHistory (MonolithRepository.kt:2377-2402) returns the same DailyFocusStat shape for every week: a week of illness, travel or giving up is seven rows of totalMinutes=0, blocks25mCount=0, interceptionsCount=0, indistinguishable in form from the shape a good week fills with numbers, and no branch anywhere selects different words for an absent week. The humane risk is documented in Duolingo's own weekly report: sent unbranched to a lapsed learner it reads 'Amazing work this week / Your hard work is paying off' over zero activity — praise templated without regard to the week it describes lands as sarcasm. Monolith's version of the failure is colder: not false praise but a verdict trail (MISSED stamps, RoutineDerive.kt:53) with no accompanying letter at all.

Recommendation: Branch the weekly letter into three named forms with different rhetoric, selected from the week's own facts: KEPT (majority attended — report and superlative), BROKEN (sessions attempted, outcomes mixed — name what was kept first, verdicts only in the appendix table), ABSENT (no attended session — no MISSED/PARTIAL/ATTENDED words in the prose at all; the letter acknowledges the declared day words if any, states the record is blank without grading it, and closes with one concrete re-entry offer: the same intention re-armed at half the dialled duration). A week containing a REST declaration must never be rendered in the ABSENT form's failure register — rest is quoted as a decision, not an omission.

#### [HIGH] Miss, partial and late routines are judged in one tribunal word — MISSED, PARTIAL, LATE_FIRE — with no sentence, context or way back

MonolithRepository.kt:1683-1688 receiptOutcomeWord returns single bare words: 'ATTENDED', 'PARTIAL', 'MISSED' (via FinishKind), 'LATE_FIRE' rendered in the same family, 'FLOW ENDED'. MonolithModels.kt:313 documents the stamp vocabulary 'ATTENDED / PARTIAL / MISSED / LATE_FIRE. Stamps are immutable.' ReceiptSheet.kt prints that word as the entire second half of 'ENDED {time} · {word}' — a routine miss therefore gets exactly one word of copy in the whole app, no sentence, no reference to a declared REST/ILL/FAMILY day word, no next step.

Recommendation: Demote the stamp to metadata and add one humane sentence under it, generated from facts the app already holds. For MISSED with a declared word: 'Marked ILL that day — this miss isn't counted as a broken promise.' For MISSED with no declaration: 'No session ran in this window. Nothing else is recorded against it.' For PARTIAL: name what did happen first ('38 of 50 minutes ran') before the label. Follow Duolingo's recovery framing and Finch's rule that the bird never wilts: the first line after a miss must state what survives, the second may state the verdict word in the mono register.

#### [HIGH] At zero tokens the valve screen goes silent: one spent-sentence, no renewal date, no alternative, only 'KEEP FOCUSING'

AirlockAndDisarmOverlays.kt:771-774: when tokensRemaining == 0 the body becomes 'This week's break is already spent.' and the entire `if (tokensRemaining > 0)` block at :779-805 — valve and rule line — is not composed; airlock.html figcaption frame 3 confirms 'At 0 tokens the valve and rule line are not composed at all'. What remains is the dead-end sentence plus 'KEEP FOCUSING' (:809). No renewal date, no mention of alternatives the app itself offers elsewhere (peek, safe break), no acknowledgement that a second emergency in one week is precisely when wording matters most.

Recommendation: Never let the hardest state have the least copy. At 0 tokens print three lines: acknowledgement ('A second emergency in one week — that happens.'), the exact reset ('The weekly break returns Monday 00:00'), and the lawful alternatives that do exist ('A 2-minute peek is still available from the Airlock; a Safe Break still runs inside a session.'), each as its own chip. Keep 'KEEP FOCUSING' but add a second, equal-weight chip 'BACK TO DECK' so the user is returned somewhere rather than ordered to persist.

#### [HIGH] The private vocabulary is abandoned on system surfaces, proving it buys nothing outside the app's own rooms

Inside the app the user must learn DECK, SHIELD, HELD, WILL SHUT and PEEK (ui/components/MonolithCustomComponents.kt:470-477; design-renders/deck.html). The moment the session leaves the app, the author switches to plain English and none of those terms survive: service/MonolithShieldService.kt:65 posts 'Monolith Locked' / 'Protecting your focus session...' and MonolithShieldService.kt:138-144 reports '{mm:ss} left • Block {i}/{n}' and '{count} urges stopped' — 'Block' and 'urges', words the in-app UI never uses for those same facts (receipt.html render frame 2 confirms the wording). Learning the in-app language therefore transfers nowhere: not to the lock screen, not to explaining the app to a friend, not to searching for help.

Recommendation: Pick one language and use it on every surface, the way Apple Focus uses the identical words 'Focus' and 'Do Not Disturb' in Settings, Control Centre and the lock-screen banner. The notification's plain words are the better candidate: bring 'left', 'block' and a plain blocked-attempts count into the Deck strip, and retire HELD/WILL SHUT in favour of the phrasing the notification already proves the author trusts when clarity actually matters.

#### [HIGH] Auto-split writes the author's physics homework into any user's task: the fallback micro-steps are 'Sketch diagram & list known variables' and 'Check units & boundary conditions'

MonolithModels.kt:186-190: defaultSubStepsForCategory's else branch — the branch every uncategorised, non-Code/Writing/Exam task falls into — returns 'Sketch diagram & list known variables', 'Solve core problem set step-by-step', 'Check units & boundary conditions'. MonolithRepository.kt:2912-2919 autoSplitTaskIntoMicroSteps() overwrites a task's notesOrSubsteps with that generated set, and MainActivity.kt:619 wires it to a live UI callback (MonolithViewModel.kt:2000). A user who auto-splits 'Prepare investor update' or 'Plan mother's physiotherapy' receives statics-problem instructions in the app's authoritative voice, verbatim descendants of the seeded Chapter 4 example.

Recommendation: Make the fallback domain-neutral and non-destructive, following the blank-template principle of Word's Normal template and Google Docs' gallery (templates are chosen, never imposed, and a blank page is the default): fallback steps should be 'Name what done looks like', 'Take the first 10-minute step', 'Check the result against done' — and auto-split must append or offer-as-suggestion, never overwrite substeps the user already wrote.

#### [HIGH] Intention is printed like a log field, never designed as a declaration made to another person

Monolith's intention is formatted everywhere as a system log entry, never as words said to another person: the Deck task row is 'NOW' + title + 'DONE' (design-renders/deck.html), the Airlock prints it as 'ACTIVE INTENTION: Finish Chapter 4 Problem Set' (ui/components/AirlockAndDisarmOverlays.kt:648) — a field label, not a promise — and the Receipt uses the same string as a mere slip title (ui/components/ReceiptSheet.kt:96-105). No surface ever shows two intentions side by side, and no start or end ritual asks the user to declare or report anything. Focusmate's entire presence design is two copy rituals: at the start each partner states what they will work on, mics then mute for silent work, and at the end each reports what they actually accomplished — the declaration and the checkout are the product; the video is just their carrier.

Recommendation: Build the bookends in text, in Monolith's mono idiom, with no camera: before the slide arms, the Deck's empty sentence slot (RefusalSentenceSlot, TactileDeckScreen.kt:1060) becomes a paired declaration slip of two ruled ReceiptMonoLine-style lines — 'I WILL: FINISH CHAPTER 4' / 'A. WILL: REVISE THERMODYNAMICS' — exchanged and locked at seal, so arming is signing under a witness's stated intention as well as your own. The Airlock's log label is rewritten from 'ACTIVE INTENTION:' to the partner-addressed form 'YOU SAID: FINISH CHAPTER 4'. Focusmate's say-it-then-report-it ritual, carried by ruled paper lines instead of video.

#### [HIGH] REST / ILL / FAMILY is a finished low-bandwidth social protocol — a closed three-word lexicon with no photos, no names, no feed — typeset as a grey filing suffix nobody is meant to read as a message

DayWordStore.kt:20,56-58: the entire expressive vocabulary for a bad day is a closed list — WORDS = REST, ILL, FAMILY, 'never TEST'. DrawerScreen.kt:846-880 (DayHeading) typesets the chosen word as a suffix to the date heading — 'FRI 30 OCT · REST' in Anonymous Pro Bold 11sp, letterSpacing 1sp, onSurfaceVariant grey, identical in weight and colour to the date itself (drawer.html Frame 1) — and the declaration row renders only on today's heading while unsealed. It is a filing annotation, visually indistinguishable from metadata. Slowly proves a constrained, photo-free, name-free channel can carry real connection; a naval signal flag carries a complete message in one hoisted sign. Monolith already owns exactly such a one-word signal and prints it as a footnote.

Recommendation: Promote the day word from filing suffix to the pair's whole message — the only thing Monolith ever transmits socially: when a word is declared, the pair receives a single word-card typeset like a receipt slip (surfaceBright #FAF6F0, the word alone in Sora Bold, date beneath in 11sp mono), with no session data, no streak consequence and no reply affordance beyond declaring a word back. In the Drawer, the word leaves the date line and gets its own full-width line in onBackground so a REST day reads as a statement, not a suffix.

#### [HIGH] At the true emergency the voice turns into a ledger: 'This week's break is already spent.' and nothing the user can still do

AirlockAndDisarmOverlays.kt:766-776: title 'EMERGENCY BREAK', body when the token is gone is exactly 'This week's break is already spent.' — a ledger entry, full stop. No line names anything still possible (Phone/OPEN-tier apps, calling someone, the time the routine/session ends), and the available-token body 'This ends the session early. It is the only break this week.' (:772) is the same flat bookkeeping register. design-renders/airlock.html's disarm frame confirms the spent face is title + that one sentence + KEEP FOCUSING.

Recommendation: Keep the consequence-first structure but add a recourse line in the same plain register the valve instructions already use well ('Hold to fill 60 seconds. Every 15 seconds banks…'): spent face becomes 'This week's break is already spent. Calls and [OPEN apps] still work. This session ends at 21:00.' Model it on aviation/emergency-card copy (e.g. iOS Emergency SOS, which at the moment of distress names what will happen and what you can still do) — at a hard moment, copy must list affordances, not just refusals.

#### [HIGH] The spec plate is a glossary for a different app: it defines PORCELAIN, INK and COMMIT — words no screen ever prints — and specs the user cannot use

ParkDrawer.kt:105-123 (the spec plate, the app's only self-description): 'COLOUR IS A VERB: ORANGE = COMMIT · INK = SHUT · GREY = PEEK · PORCELAIN = OPEN' defines four colour-names, but no screen ever prints PORCELAIN, INK or COMMIT as a tier word — the Shield cap and tallies print the tier words themselves (OPEN/PEEK/SHUT). The same plate offers 'SOUND: FLOAT-PCM, 4 PARTIALS · POWER: YOUR PHONE' — an implementation detail no user can act on, plus a joke at the user's expense. design-renders/park.html shows the plate as 10sp mono at the foot of PARK.

Recommendation: Rewrite the plate so every line defines a word the UI actually prints, in the UI's own terms: 'SHUT = NO DOOR · PEEK = 2 MINUTES, THEN SHUT AGAIN · OPEN = ALWAYS YOURS'. Cut FLOAT-PCM and POWER entirely. Braun's ET66 / Teenage Engineering spec plates earn their poetry because every printed spec is one the owner can verify or use; a glossary for a vocabulary the product never speaks is brand cosplay, not a spec plate.

#### [HIGH] The lock-screen notification speaks a third voice — stock Title Case — and sends the user to a 'Break tab' and a 'desk toy' that exist nowhere in the app

MonolithShieldService.kt:65 buildNotification('Monolith Locked', 'Protecting your focus session...'); :116 updateNotification('Session Complete', 'Unlocked desk toy ready in your Break tab.'); :126-138 'Safe Break %02d:%02d • Block %d/%d', 'Stopwatch +%02d:%02d (20m floor)'. There is no 'Break tab' and nothing in the app is called a 'desk toy' — in-app destinations are DECK / SHIELD / DRAWER (design-renders/receipt.html frame 2 renders this notification). The most frequently read surface in the product uses Title Case template English and names a place that does not exist, while every in-app surface uses the caps instrument voice.

Recommendation: Rewrite all shield-notification strings in the app's own lexicon and register: title 'MONOLITH · 32 MIN LEFT', text 'BLOCK 2/4 · HELD 3', completion 'SESSION COMPLETE · RECEIPT № 048 ON THE DECK'. Delete 'desk toy' and 'Break tab'. Apple Focus and Nothing OS keep one vocabulary across the status surface and the app itself; the lock screen is Monolith's front door and currently speaks like a stock sample project.

#### [HIGH] No drawn boundary between sign and sentence: Monolith spells out states a pictogram should carry, while its conditional prose is the load-bearing part a pictogram must never be asked to carry

The sentences that must stay sentences are already in the code doing work no symbol can do: 'This ends the session early. It is the only break this week.' (AirlockAndDisarmOverlays.kt:771-775) and 'Hold to fill 60 seconds. Every 15 seconds banks. If your hand slips, what isn't banked drains away. The banked part stays.' (line 800) — both carry tense, uniqueness and a conditional. Conversely, pure states that a sign could carry are spelled out at full length: the three withheld-peek sentences at AirlockAndDisarmOverlays.kt:692-708 and the receipt's HELD count line at ReceiptSheet.kt:131.

Recommendation: Write the boundary into the design system as a rule with two lists. Never pictogram: the user's intention text, the day word, task titles, permission consequences, the emergency-break consequence and banking sentences, and receipt outcome reasoning — these keep Atkinson text, full sentences, no icon beside them competing for the glance. Always sign-plus-caption: tier rulings (SHUT/PEEK/OPEN), sealed vs peek-running vs cooldown, held-count, shield on/off. Eligibility test for any future string: if it names a state a photograph could show, it gets a sign; if it needs a verb tense, a negation beyond prohibition, or a number of conditions, it stays prose — and no sign may be drawn for it.

#### [HIGH] The Deck's only error voice is three subject-less telegrams: 'BLOCKING IS OFF — TAP TO FIX' never says what is off or what fixing restores

MonolithCustomComponents.kt:501-520 refusalSentenceFor() is the app's complete standing error vocabulary: 'BLOCKING IS OFF — TAP TO FIX', 'CAN'T CHECK BLOCKING — TAP TO RETRY', 'USAGE ACCESS IS OFF — TAP TO FIX'. Despite the type being named RefusalSentence, none is a sentence: no subject a person would recognise ('blocking' is the app's internal noun, not Android's), no naming of the actual setting (Accessibility, Usage access) as the system itself labels it, and no statement of consequence. A first-time user who has never opened Accessibility settings cannot act on this without guessing.

Recommendation: Rewrite the cause table as one sentence-case complete sentence per cause, naming the setting exactly as Android Settings names it and stating what the tap does: 'Monolith cannot block apps, because Accessibility is turned off for Monolith. Tap to open Accessibility settings.' / 'Android has not granted Monolith usage access, so it cannot see which app is open. Tap to grant it.' Keep the existing causal priority, single-sentence limit and tap target; only the words change.

#### [HIGH] At the exact moment of confrontation the Airlock addresses the user with a badge, not a sentence: 'AIRLOCK INTERCEPTION • LOCKED'

AirlockAndDisarmOverlays.kt:607 prints the intercept headline as "AIRLOCK INTERCEPTION • ${state.interceptReasonBadge.uppercase(Locale.US)}" at 11.5sp — the badge is a free string defaulted to "Locked" (MonolithViewModel.kt:157). Below it the overlay offers only fragments: the app name at 24sp, an 88sp countdown numeral, and airlockSessionLine() (AirlockAndDisarmOverlays.kt:244-248) returning 'SESSION ENDS 19:32' or 'SESSION RUNNING · NO SET END'. The state already holds interceptedAppName, sessionIntention and sessionEndsAtMillis — everything a sentence needs — and none of it is ever assembled into one. This is the surface where the user is mid-temptation, the one place the app speaks to him about his own decision, and it speaks in a rubber stamp.

Recommendation: Delete the badge line and replace it with one sentence composed from the state already present, set Atkinson 15sp sentence case above the app name: 'You asked Monolith to keep Instagram shut until 19:32, so you could revise thermodynamics.' For stopwatch sessions: 'You asked Monolith to keep Instagram shut, with no set end.' The countdown numeral stays beneath it as the label's measure, subordinate to the sentence instead of replacing it.

#### [HIGH] Monolith can write sentences — it demotes every one to fine print while codes get the headline type

The app contains genuine, well-written sentences, all set as disclaimers: the digest's 'Everything here is as of the time above. Nothing here opens. Anything newer waits until the session ends.' (AirlockAndDisarmOverlays.kt:377) at 13sp in onSurfaceVariant, and the valve's 'This ends the session early. It is the only break this week.' (AirlockAndDisarmOverlays.kt:772) as small print under a chip labelled 'EMERGENCY BREAK'. Meanwhile the headline positions are occupied by codes and fragments — the receipt's mono telegrams (ReceiptSheet.kt:117-141), the Deck's '12 WILL SHUT · 3 PEEK' imprint, 'HELD NOTIFICATIONS • n' digest header (AirlockAndDisarmOverlays.kt:362). The hierarchy is exactly inverted: the more a line matters, the less it is allowed to be prose.

Recommendation: Promote by rule: any line that carries a consequence becomes a full sentence at headline size and primary ink; codes and counts drop to the mono small print they are suited to. Concretely: the valve sheet's headline becomes 'This ends the session early, and it is the only break you have this week.' at 15sp onBackground, with 'EMERGENCY BREAK' demoted to the eyebrow; the digest note moves above the notification list at 13sp onBackground instead of trailing it in variant ink.

#### [HIGH] No deferral grammar anywhere: every public surface prohibits or grades, none names the legitimate time and place the way 'Please do it at home' does

Every verb on Monolith's contested surfaces is prohibition or verdict: 'AIRLOCK INTERCEPTION • LOCKED' (AirlockAndDisarmOverlays.kt:607), 'RETURN TO FOCUS' (:656), 'EMERGENCY PEEK' (:665), 'EMERGENCY BREAK — This ends the session early. It is the only break this week.' (:772-779), and receiptOutcomeWord mints ATTENDED / PARTIAL / SLEPT THROUGH (MonolithRepository.kt:1684-1688). The one deferral fact the app owns — the session end — is printed only as telemetry, 'SESSION ENDS 18:30' (airlockSessionLine, AirlockAndDisarmOverlays.kt:239-243), never as an offer. Yorifuji's 2008-2010 Tokyo Metro campaign ('Please do it at home') was built on the opposite grammar: never 'Don't', always a named legitimate place and time — do it there, do it then — which Yorifuji himself contrasted with posters that only say 'Don't do this'. The behaviour is legitimate; only its location in time is wrong, and the poster says where it belongs.

Recommendation: Rewrite the Airlock headline in deferral grammar using data already on the card: replace 'AIRLOCK INTERCEPTION • LOCKED' with '{App} again at {session end}' (e.g. 'Instagram again at 18:30') as the 24sp line, demote the countdown below it, and rename the peek chip's price line to state the same promise for the peek path. Apply the same grammar to the valve: 'This ends the session early' becomes 'Next break is yours on {next token date}' when tokens are spent. No new machinery — the end-time derivation (endsAtText) already exists; only the sentence changes from verdict to appointment.

#### [HIGH] 'Urges stopped' makes the user attend to himself resisting, all session long

Weil's attention empties the self out of the frame ('to empty ourselves of our false divinity, to deny ourselves, to give up being the centre of the world'). Monolith keeps the self centre-frame as a live score: MonolithShieldService.kt:144 appends '${phantomReachesBlocked} urges stopped' to the notification the user sees all session, MonolithRepository.kt:2104-2124 increments that counter on every intercept (recordIntercept), and ReceiptSheet.kt:149-154 then prints each reach back as a timed deflection list. Mid-work, a glance does not return the user to the task - it reports how many times he has already tried to leave it.

Recommendation: Remove the urges/deflection tally from every in-session surface: strip ' - {n} urges stopped' from the ShieldService notification subtitle, remove the HELD-style reach count from the running Deck, and on ReceiptSheet.kt replace the timed deflection list with a single unnumbered line 'YOU CAME BACK' only when a return actually happened. Keep the raw intercept count in the log the footer already claims ('THE MACHINE KEEPS ITS OWN LOG'), not in the user's face.

#### [HIGH] At breakdown, Park shows the user Monolith's autobiography — board state-words, a theme that narrates itself, a spec plate — instead of what the breakage does to their next session

Park is reached when something lacks, yet park.html / ui/components/ParkDrawer.kt answer in the tool's own ledger language: rows print 'ACCESSIBILITY GRANTED', 'NOTIFICATION LISTENER MISSING', 'SHORTS + REELS OFF', 'SOCIAL SITES RUNNING', headed 'LAST PROVED 21:47 · SELF-REPORT' (ParkDrawer.kt:315-324). Below the board the app narrates its internal state machine — the THEME row prints evaluateTheme's readout verbatim, 'AUTO · DAY — NO ROUTINE OWNS IT' (ParkDrawer.kt:616; MonolithViewModel.kt:68) — and the drawer ends in the manufacturer's plate: 'MONOLITH ML-01 / UNIT Nº 01 · BUILT FOR ONE USER · NOT FOR SALE' plus its own operating manual (ParkDrawer.kt:105-109, 628-637). Heidegger allows the tool to become conspicuous when it breaks; what should become visible is the broken relation to the work. Monolith instead presents itself for contemplation and offers exactly one verb: a FIX key exporting the user to Android Settings to perform the tool's maintenance.

Recommendation: Rewrite each Park board row as a consequence for the next session, not a system state: 'NOTIFICATION LISTENER MISSING' becomes 'Messages will ring through your next session'. Delete the THEME readout row entirely — the scheme is already visible on screen; a tool does not narrate its own evaluation. Move the ML-01 plate and manual lines out of Park to a single About page in the Drawer, and let Park's foot carry only 'LAST PROVED hh:mm' and a RETURN TO DECK key.

#### [HIGH] A dose with marketing but no leaflet: the 1-per-week scarcity badge borrows attention-economy grammar, and nothing anywhere discloses Monolith's own effects

The Deck's emergency chip prints monoBadge = "$weeklyEmergencyTokensRemaining/1 WEEK" (TactileDeckScreen.kt:1048) — an artificial-scarcity counter in the exact grammar of the attention economy (lives, energy, weekly drops) — and no surface in the app explains the dose: why one, why a week, what the valve costs, or what else Monolith does to the user (verdict stamps, indefinite notification storage, collectible forging). The medicine ships with dosage marketing on the label and no patient information leaflet anywhere.

Recommendation: Keep the scarcity, drop the game grammar and add the leaflet. Replace the 'n/1 WEEK' badge with plain words on the chip's second line: 'ONE A WEEK — THE EXIT STAYS RARE ON PURPOSE'. In PARK, add a fixed plate titled 'WHAT MONOLITH DOES' listing in plain sentences its verdicts, its one-token rule, what it stores and for how long, and the collectible forge — the side-effects disclosure every other pharmakon is required to carry.

#### [HIGH] A day may be named REST, ILL or FAMILY — but never simply nothing: the closed day-word list has no lawful word for boredom or an unplanned day

DayWordStore.kt:54 closes the lawful vocabulary of a day at WORDS = REST / ILL / FAMILY, and its header (:20-23) boasts 'never TEST. This app does not know test days.' A day can be excused only as recovery, sickness or family duty — all still defined against work. There is no word for a day that was deliberately nothing: no BORED, no WANDER, no UNPLANNED. An undeclared, unproductive day has no lawful name in the app and falls back into the space where routine windows are judged.

Recommendation: Add a fallow word to DayWordStore.WORDS (e.g. OPEN) with legal force, not just print: declaring OPEN on DrawerScreen's today heading suspends that day's routine judgements entirely (no ATTENDED/MISSED stamp is written) and the Drawer heading prints the date with the word and no session rows beneath it — a blank day the app certifies as legitimate.

#### [HIGH] The only unscheduled free time in the app is named an emergency and receipted as breakage: VALVE_BROKE

Spontaneous release exists only as catastrophe vocabulary: the overlay is titled EMERGENCY BREAK and explains 'This ends the session early. It is the only break this week.' (AirlockAndDisarmOverlays.kt:763-774), Park teaches 'ONE BREAK A WEEK' as a ration (ParkDrawer.kt:111), the supply is exactly 1 per Monday-anchored week (MonolithWeek.kt:37-40), and taking it stamps the session's permanent outcome as SessionOutcome.VALVE_BROKE (MonolithRepository.kt:2277, 2323) — the machine's metaphor for a person stopping is that something broke. Pieper's feast is the opposite framing: free time that is planned, affirmed and celebrated, not an escape hatch whose use is recorded as failure. A user who simply wants an unplanned hour must either lie about an emergency or accept a broken verdict on the record.

Recommendation: Add a lawful, unstigmatised release and rename the record: (1) A 'FEAST HOUR' verb on the Deck, available once a day outside routines, ends the session with outcome word RELEASED (new SessionOutcome, printed on the receipt as 'ENDED · RELEASED') and no token spend. (2) Retire VALVE_BROKE from every user-visible surface — the receipt and Drawer print 'ENDED EARLY' for the emergency path; the token keeps its scarcity but loses its verdict. (3) Change the Airlock overlay body copy from 'It is the only break this week.' to state the two paths plainly: 'A feast hour ends this cleanly, once a day. The emergency break is for the day that goes wrong.'

#### [HIGH] When the app itself dies mid-session, the receipt blames the session in the passive voice and withholds its completion pulse

ReceiptState.kt:36-38 brands a session whose shield service died as ELAPSED_SHIELD_GAP — 'the books are BROKEN' — and finishPulses in the same file withholds the completion pulse for that outcome ('Death-booked finishes never pulse'). ReceiptSheet.kt:147 then prints 'THE SHIELD WAS OFF FOR PART OF THAT SESSION' in agentless capitals. The sentence is identical whether the user killed the service or Monolith's own process was reaped by the OS; the user who sat out the full span gets no completion sound and a stained slip for the app's own death. Pirsig's ego trap is the refusal to see one's own fault when the facts show it; here the artifact structurally cannot record 'we failed', only 'the session failed'.

Recommendation: Split the gap verdict by cause in ReceiptState/ReceiptSheet: when the gap coincides with process death, reboot or update, the slip prints 'MONOLITH STOPPED FOR PART OF THAT SESSION — THE SPAN STILL COUNTS' in the fault-line slot, the finish pulse plays, and the outcome word carries no BROKEN branding; reserve the current wording for gaps with evidence of user action (service toggled, admin revoked).

#### [MEDIUM] The voice never sobers up: GUARD tallies, a FLOW keycap and playful imprint copy run unchanged through exam week, where every real exam artifact speaks in flat invigilator imperatives

design-renders/deck.html: the Deck speaks in its everyday register year-round — 'GUARD 4/4' in the header, 'FLOW' as a playful keycap, the imprint '9 WILL SHUT · 3 PEEK', and the RefusalSentenceSlot (ui/components/MonolithCustomComponents.kt) sitting empty. Nothing in the copy system has a second register. Exam halls run on the opposite voice: the OCR paper's INSTRUCTIONS TO CANDIDATES block — short, numbered, procedural imperatives ('Answer all questions', 'Write your answers in blue or black ink') — and invigilator announcements in the same flat procedural tone. Monolith's brand banter, charming in October, reads as unserious in the exam hall in May.

Recommendation: Add a season copy register for the arm flow and the Airlock, written as candidate instructions: numbered imperatives in the existing sentence slot and eyebrow positions — '1 · PHONE FACE DOWN. 2 · PAPER AND WATER ONLY. 3 · NO PEEK UNTIL THE BELL.' — replacing GUARD tallies and FLOW during season sessions, then reverting with the season scheme. No new voice needs inventing: borrow the exam paper's instructions block verbatim in structure, set in the app's existing mono uppercase.

#### [MEDIUM] The spec plate engraves factory lore no operator can use — FLOAT-PCM is trivia dressed as specification

At the foot of the PARK drawer, below the board the user came to read, sits a ten-line plate in 10sp Anonymous Pro at 1.2sp tracking (ParkDrawer.kt:102-120, rendered ParkDrawer.kt:623-645; park.html:165-176).
