Its closing line — 'SOUND: FLOAT-PCM, 4 PARTIALS · POWER: YOUR PHONE' — is factory-plate cosplay: an audio implementation detail and a joke about the battery, neither of which any user can act on. Real engraved plates earn their place because every datum is operator-usable: Leica's top-plate engravings are the shutter speeds and frame counters the photographer sets; Braun plates state the voltage the device needs. FLOAT-PCM denotes nothing a hand can do, and the plate does not even sit on the object's back — it sits inside a scrollable settings sheet, where its lore lines push nothing out only because they are last, and teach nothing the board above hasn't said better ('PEEK: 2 MINUTES' and the COLOUR IS A VERB line are the exceptions, and both duplicate facts printed elsewhere in the app).

Recommendation: Cut the plate to the three lines that pass the operator test — PEEK: 2 MINUTES, THEN SHUT AGAIN; HOLD: 60 SECONDS, BANKED EVERY 15; DATA: ON THIS PHONE ONLY — and delete the ML-01 serial lore, the FLOAT-PCM line and the POWER joke outright. Keep the plate typography and its foot-of-drawer seat; a plate with only usable facts reads as an instrument, a plate with trivia reads as a costume.

#### [MEDIUM] The brand voice certifies distrust: 'BUILT FOR ONE USER' and 'SELF-REPORT' make every screenshot look self-forged

ParkDrawer.kt:105-107 PLATE_HEAD prints 'UNIT Nº 01 · BUILT FOR ONE USER · NOT FOR SALE' at 10sp mono in PARK; park.html shows the Guard header as 'LAST PROVED 21:47 · SELF-REPORT' from ParkDrawer.kt:315-330 (SimpleDateFormat HH:mm + ' · SELF-REPORT'). ReceiptSheet.kt:176 footer completes the voice: 'THE MACHINE KEEPS ITS OWN LOG · YOUR STUDY RECORD LIVES IN YPT'. Opal's managed banners name the other authority instead — 'This is managed by your school' / 'This rule is managed by your family' (apk-re/opal/EVIDENCE.md §10.3) — so a screenshot carries its provenance. Monolith's screenshot carries a disclaimer that its proof is self-reported.

Recommendation: Rewrite the provenance voice for a second reader, following Opal's managed-banner pattern: spec plate becomes 'BUILT TO BE SHOWN — ONE USER, ONE WITNESS'; 'LAST PROVED · SELF-REPORT' becomes 'LAST CHECKED {time} · BLOCKING ACTIVE' on the Guard board, and the receipt footer gains a countersign line 'Shown to ________ · {date}' under the existing footer. If no witness is set, print 'No witness set' honestly rather than implying verification.

#### [MEDIUM] Input fields have no shared voice: one teaches by example, one whispers, one shouts 'TYPE TO FIND A TASK' in the plate register

Three text inputs, three unrelated voices: ShieldMatrixScreen.kt:453 placeholder 'Filter apps…' (sentence case, ellipsis), ShieldMatrixScreen.kt:585 'Add a site — e.g. news.ycombinator.com' (sentence case with a genuinely helpful example), FocusSequencerScreen.kt:224 'Add single-line focus task...' (sentence case, three dots), DrawerScreen.kt:546 'TYPE TO FIND A TASK' (Anonymous Pro caps — an instruction shouted in the plate register, with no example). The helpful example-led style already exists in the codebase; it is applied by accident, screen by screen.

Recommendation: Adopt one input voice and apply it everywhere: sentence-case Atkinson, action + example, e.g. Drawer search becomes 'Find a task — try “problem set”'. Reserve the caps mono plate register strictly for labels and readouts, never for addressing the user. This is the GOV.UK / Material 3 text-field convention — hint text speaks to the person, labels describe the machine — and Monolith's own site field (:585) is the in-house proof it works.

#### [MEDIUM] A stranger holding the phone can decode nothing: public surfaces speak initiate code and never state the one plain fact — busy until when

The surfaces a stranger actually encounters assume initiation. The ongoing notification's subtitle requires decoding 'Block 1/1' and 'urges stopped' (MonolithShieldService.kt:142-144); the Airlock badge reads 'AIRLOCK INTERCEPTION' (AirlockAndDisarmOverlays.kt:607); the receipt footer directs the record to an unexplained external noun, 'YOUR STUDY RECORD LIVES IN YPT' (ReceiptSheet.kt, reproduced in receipt.html frame 1). None of them answers the bystander's only real question — is this person busy, and until when — in plain words, even though the app computes the end instant continuously. Tokyo Metro posters are bilingual Japanese/English under a self-explanatory pictogram because shared space is full of people who share neither your language nor your context; the design target is the first-day stranger, not the regular. Monolith designs its public face for its own initiate and leaves family, teachers and colleagues holding an undecodable phone.

Recommendation: Add a plain-language public line as the notification's first text row, derived from the existing end-time code: 'Busy until 19:32' — no app vocabulary, no counts, no metaphor nouns. Audit the other two stranger surfaces against the same test: the Airlock badge becomes 'Not now — back at 18:30' and the receipt footer names what YPT is or drops the direction. Rule for the design system: any surface Android can show without unlock must pass the stranger test — understandable to someone who has never opened the app.

### Onboarding and teaching — 16 findings (5 critical, 8 high, 3 medium, 0 low)

#### [CRITICAL] Seconds 0–3 contain no brand at all: stock launch theme, then a compliance ledger is the first designed surface

app/src/main/res/values/themes.xml:4 defines the launch theme as a single line — parent="android:Theme.DeviceDefault.NoActionBar" — with no splash background, brand mark or held first frame anywhere in res. MainActivity.kt:313-318 then auto-opens PARK in a LaunchedEffect(Unit) at first composition, so the literal first designed pixels are the GUARD permission board in park.html: six rows of 10sp mono caps (ACCESSIBILITY / USAGE ACCESS / DEVICE ADMIN…) headed 'LAST PROVED'. The word MONOLITH exists only as 10sp header text (deck.html header band). Screensdesign's walkthrough of Opal documents a staged opening — a 'fist bump' commitment animation and a 'First Gem' unlocking animation as immediate reinforcement — and Forest's first frame is a seed centred in soil waiting to be planted.

Recommendation: Build a held first frame from assets the app already owns: on cold first launch, show the Deck's slab full-bleed with the spec-plate head engraved centre-frame ('MONOLITH ML-01 — UNIT Nº 01'), the rotary wheel drawing itself in over ~900ms with detent ticks from the existing TactileSoundEngine, then the wheel inviting the first turn. One image, one object, one verb — the way Forest's seed and Opal's gem each compress the whole product into the opening frame. PARK must not appear until after that frame has been touched.

#### [CRITICAL] The one hero object is served under a scrim: PARK covers the wheel for the whole first impression

MainActivity.kt:313-318 sets parkOpen = true at first composition whenever parkIntroPending() (MonolithRepository.kt:454-458), and park.html shows what that means visually: a 32%-black scrim over the underlying screen with the GUARD sheet seated on top. Behind that scrim sits deck.html — the 288dp engraved rotary wheel, the ghost-offset 72sp Sora hero numeral, the orange slide cap — the only surface in the app with the visual mass to be a Forest-seed equivalent. A new user spends their entire first impression reading MISSING rows through glass while the product's signature object sits dimmed and untouchable underneath; by the time the drawer is dismissed, the wheel is no longer a reveal, it is furniture they have already half-seen.

Recommendation: Reverse the sequence. Give the first 20 seconds to the Deck alone: let the new user turn the wheel (detents, hero numeral re-printing) and drag the slide cap in an unarmed rehearsal that commits nothing, THEN let PARK rise — summoned by the first real attempt to arm, so the permission board arrives as the price of a thing already desired. Forest plants the tree before any grant exists; Monolith should let the wheel be touched before the ledger is opened.

#### [CRITICAL] The birth state is a chimera no preset can reproduce: dial 50, blocks 2, preset '25m Sprint', task estimate 25, hero 1H 50M

MonolithViewModel.kt:217 sets _dialMinutes=50, :220 sets _studyBlocksCount=2, :223 sets _studyPreset=POMODORO_25_5. MonolithModels.kt:69-70 defines POMODORO_25_5 as 25 work / 5 break / 2 blocks and DEEP_50_10 as 50 / 10 / 3 blocks — so 50+2 matches neither. MonolithViewModel.kt:1460-1464 selectStudyPreset() overwrites dial and blocks from the preset, proving the shipped combination is unreachable by any user action. The seeded task carries estimatedMinutes=25 (MonolithRepository.kt:355) while TactileDeckScreen.kt:325 prices the hero as 50x2+10=110 min; deck.html renders exactly that: hero '1H 50M', wheel detent at 50, NOW task 'Finish Chapter 4 Problem Set (#1–6)'. Five numbers, no two sources agree.

Recommendation: Make the first-run state exactly one named preset, seeded from the enum alone: either ship POMODORO_25_5 honestly (dial 25, 2 blocks, hero 55M) or DEEP_50_10 honestly (dial 50, 3 blocks, hero 2H 50M) — following Francesco Cirillo's Pomodoro bundle and synthesizer preset recall (a Moog/Teenage Engineering preset recalls precisely the values its name stores). Print the preset name on the Deck ('50M DEEP · 3 BLOCKS') so the default reads as a chosen, reproducible recipe, never as three independent accidents.

#### [CRITICAL] The update is invisible: no version identity, no what's-new surface, PACKAGE_REPLACED only re-arms the shield in silence

app/build.gradle.kts:19-20 freezes versionCode=1 / versionName="1.0" and grep finds zero BuildConfig reads in app/src/main/java, so no build identity is ever available to the UI. service/MonolithBootReceiver.kt:31,42-46 handles ACTION_MY_PACKAGE_REPLACED by mapping it to RoutineHeartbeat.Source.PACKAGE_REPLACED, ticking silently and restarting the shield if a session is active — no flag, note or surface is set. design-renders/deck.html shows the Deck's only reserved announcement space is the empty RefusalSentenceSlot; there is no banner, strip or version line anywhere in deck.html or park.html.

Recommendation: Make the update a printed event in Monolith's own instrument voice: store lastSeenVersionCode, and on first Deck open after it changes show a one-time Deck strip in the existing one-time-strip grammar — 'UPDATED · ML-01 REV N — WHAT CHANGED' — expanding to 3-5 mono lines naming the changed screens/behaviours in before→after form, dismissed by an explicit tap and re-readable in PARK. Bump versionCode/versionName per build and print the revision on the PARK plate. Follow Linear's UI-refresh changelog, which names exactly what moved (headers/navigation consistent, icons redrawn) instead of saying 'improvements', and Apple TV's post-update What's New splash, which introduces the one changed feature on first launch after updating.

#### [CRITICAL] The first frame is a double exposure: an unseen Deck dimmed under a 32% scrim by a maintenance sheet, so the app introduces its underside before its face

MainActivity.kt:311-318 auto-opens PARK at first composition (parkIntroPending -> parkOpen=true) over whatever Deck frame exists; ParkDrawer.kt:74-90 hosts it as a bottom sheet under a black 32% scrim (park.html: .scrim rgba(0,0,0,0.32), sheet top corners 16dp), and res/values/themes.xml is a bare DeviceDefault theme with no splash or reveal state. The first legible word is GUARD (ParkDrawer.kt DrawerHeader, park.html .guard 22sp Sora). Opal instead sequences first contact one message at a time — greeting, name, what-matters (Focus better / Sleep better / Be more present), then a personalised projection and gem-crack reveal before any permission (apk-re/opal/EVIDENCE.md:190); one sec opens with a quantified promise and an art screen before setup (apk-re/onesec/EVIDENCE.md:144,167).

Recommendation: Stage the first frame as a full-screen object reveal, not a drawer accident: frame 1 is the Deck wheel at rest on porcelain with the plate head 'MONOLITH ML-01' at display size and one user-addressed sentence; frame 2 asks the Opal-style single question (what this phone steals time from); PARK auto-rise is demoted to step 3, after the user has seen the product it guards. Never let a scrimmed sheet be frame 1.

#### [HIGH] SPLIT fabricates the student's plan: one physics template printed as authored sub-steps for every subject

FocusSequencerScreen.kt: every composer task is created with category 'Study' (submitTask, ~L145). MonolithRepository.kt:2916 autoSplit calls FocusTaskEntity.defaultSubStepsForCategory(title, categoryTag), and MonolithModels.kt:168-195 shows that function: 'code'/'writing'/'exam' branches are unreachable from the composer, so every SPLIT falls to the else template — 'Sketch diagram & list known variables', 'Solve core problem set step-by-step', 'Check units & boundary conditions'. TaskLeafItem (~L620-650) then prints those lines in the same Atkinson 12.5sp, same strikethrough interaction, as steps the student wrote herself. An essay, a language vocab set and a history revision task all receive physics problem-solving steps, presented as their plan. YPT's Planner keeps the opposite discipline: its to-dos and 10-minute blocks are the student's own entries; the app supplies the grid, never the content.

Recommendation: Stop printing templates as authored steps. Redesign SPLIT as a labelled scaffold following the paper study-planner convention of a printed prompt the student overwrites: tapping SPLIT opens three empty ruled lines on the leaf headed 'SPLIT — YOUR THREE MOVES' with the template shown only as grey ghost examples that vanish on typing, and no leaf can be STARTed from ghost text alone. If a template is kept, name its technique on the leaf ('FIRST PASS / DRILL MISSES / RECALL' for exam tasks) in the 10.5sp mono plate voice, so the student learns a named method instead of receiving fake personal steps.

#### [HIGH] The one what's-new note ever built says almost nothing: a single 11sp line, no before/after, that deletes itself in 14 days

ui/screens/ShieldMatrixScreen.kt:313-326: the sole what's-new element ever shipped is one 11sp Anonymous Pro line in scheme.primary, 'SCHEDULE RESET TO YOUR DAY — TAP ANY ROW TO CHANGE IT', placed inside Shield's ROUTINES section. ui/MonolithViewModel.kt:506-527 (showRoutineResetNote) auto-hides it after 14 days or on any routine edit, and data/MonolithRepository.kt:855-865 describes its trigger as a 'Version-blind reseed' — explicitly not keyed to any app version, so it is a one-off, not a system.

Recommendation: Promote this strip into a reusable UpdateNote component driven by a stored lastSeenVersion: every release ships 1-5 note lines, each anchored on the screen it changed (routines notes on Shield, receipt changes on the Receipt, guard changes in PARK), each stating old→new ('DAY BLOCKS NOW 09:00–19:30 · WAS MORNING DEEP WORK 09:00–13:00'), persisting until explicitly dismissed — never time-expired. Follow Linear's changelog entries for its UI refresh, which enumerate the specific surfaces that changed so a returning user can rebuild their mental map in one read.

#### [HIGH] Behaviour-changing migrations land unannounced and un-re-taught: a new sniper default, renamed and retimed routines, new receipt fields — all discovered by accident

data/MonolithDatabase.kt:190-201 MIGRATION_11_12 adds shortsReelsSniperEnabled with 'DEFAULT 1 IS the truthful pre-v12 value: until this column the sniper fired unconditionally' — a new named, toggleable behaviour appears in PARK (design-renders/park.html board row 'SHORTS + REELS') with no announcement. data/MonolithRepository.kt:863-915 reseedRoutinesV1() renames and retimes the user's routines in place ('Morning Deep Work' 09:00-13:00 → 'DAY BLOCKS' 09:00-19:30; 'Night Wind-Down' → 'SLEEP' 20:00-03:30). No composable re-teaches a renamed routine, a new sled, or a changed receipt field at the moment the user first meets it.

Recommendation: Adopt a rule: no migration or reseed may change a name, a time, a default or a screen without shipping its re-teaching line in the same build. On first open of the affected surface, mark the changed control itself — a one-visit 'NEW' / 'CHANGED' plate tag beside the Shorts+Reels sled in PARK and beside renamed routine rows on Shield, clearing after the user interacts with that control. This is the in-context re-teaching Panic used for Playdate OS 3.1.2 — naming the exact version, the exact consequence and the exact Settings path — instead of Monolith's current pattern of letting the user discover the change by being blocked differently.

#### [HIGH] The spec plate teaches a four-colour language on the one screen that by law contains none of it — a legend with no specimens

ParkDrawer.kt:105-124 PLATE_BODY prints 'COLOUR IS A VERB: ORANGE = COMMIT · INK = SHUT · GREY = PEEK · PORCELAIN = OPEN' as 10sp Anonymous Pro text, while ParkDrawer.kt:79-82 states PARK's own material law is 'one tone (the ground)... orange zero' — park.html confirms the whole first screen renders in #E4DFDA / #2C2A29 / #5F5856 with no orange, grey-peek or porcelain specimen anywhere beside the legend that defines them. Teenage Engineering's colour coding works because the colour is printed on the control it names; a legend with no specimen is vocabulary without a referent.

Recommendation: Give the legend specimens or move it: add a four-chip specimen strip to the plate (8dp squares in the actual commit-orange, ink, peek-grey and porcelain tokens, each beside its verb), and repeat each single clause in situ where its colour actually fires — orange clause on the Deck's slide-to-arm, grey clause in the Airlock. A colour system taught only in monochrome text will never be learned.

#### [HIGH] The permission board counterfeits a Settings list: nine tappable-looking 48dp rows are dead print, and the only live key serves just the first failure

ParkDrawer.kt ParkBoardRow (~655-685) renders each of the nine WatchItemId rows (WatchStore.kt:80-102: ACCESSIBILITY...NOTIFICATIONS) as a 48dp ruled list row with name left and state word right, but the composable carries no clickable/tap handling at all; the board's only action is the single FIX key (ParkDrawer.kt:~418-490) naming only the first missing permission. park.html shows the result: a perfect imitation of a tappable Android Settings list in which every row is inert print. one sec's configuration flow makes each permission its own actionable dialog with a dedicated tutorial and a privacy pre-ask (apk-re/onesec/EVIDENCE.md:168); Opal's chat flow attaches a plain-language benefit sentence to each grant (apk-re/opal/EVIDENCE.md:191).

Recommendation: Resolve the affordance lie one way or the other: either make each MISSING row itself the button (full-row tap target, trailing chevron/FIX word, pressed dip like the FIX key) so the list behaves as it looks, or strip the list styling — remove the Settings-like row rhythm and present the board as an explicitly printed certificate. The per-row version is right for first run: a new user should be able to tap the exact line that is wrong.

#### [HIGH] Failure is the loudest ink on the board: MISSING prints in full-strength black, GRANTED in muted grey — success makes the first screen fade

In ParkBoardRow (ParkDrawer.kt:~655-685) the state word's colour is wordIsLack ? scheme.onBackground : scheme.onSurfaceVariant — park.html encodes it verbatim: .word.lack{color:#2C2A29} vs .word.ok{color:#5F5856}. So MISSING/OFF print in full-strength ink while GRANTED/RUNNING recede to muted grey, and the sheet's only filled object, the ink FIX key (park.html .fix, #2C2A29 fill), names a lack. Granting permissions one by one literally makes the first screen paler and quieter; the reward for progress is fading. Aviation and medical checklist design does the opposite: completed items gain the mark and the weight, open items stay visually pending.

Recommendation: Invert the salience: GRANTED/RUNNING earns full ink plus a filled tick glyph, MISSING drops to onSurfaceVariant outline style with its own small FIX pill, and a '3 / 6 PROVED' count in the GUARD header gains ink as it fills. Success should accumulate visual weight on the board the way a stamped checklist does; failure should look unfinished, not bolder.

#### [HIGH] The board hides its own wiring: an interceptor prints OFF for three different upstream causes and never names the parent stage that starved it

WatchStore.kt:443-476 (deriveInterceptor) encodes exact wiring: SHORTS + REELS rides ACCESSIBILITY alone; SOCIAL SITES rides ACCESSIBILITY + USAGE ACCESS; NOTIFICATIONS rides NOTIFICATION LISTENER alone — and returns the single word OFF for three different faults: 'setting off, or any parent MISSING or STALE' (WatchStore.kt:443). ParkDrawer.kt's ParkBoardRow prints only name + that one word. So when NOTIFICATION LISTENER reads MISSING (as in the park.html render) and NOTIFICATIONS consequently reads OFF, nothing on the board connects the two lines four rows apart; the user must already know the schematic to diagnose the panel that was supposed to teach it.

Recommendation: Print the wiring on the board. Indent each interceptor line under its parent stage and add a cause suffix to every non-RUNNING word, in the board's secondary ink: 'OFF — NO LISTENER', 'OFF — A11Y STALE', 'OFF — SWITCHED OFF BELOW'. When a parent is the cause, tapping the interceptor line should flash the parent row's hairline. One word per state was the parts-bin grammar; a stage that names its upstream fault is the instrument grammar.

#### [HIGH] The built thing is never test-fitted: a loadout's first lived experience is a real session or an unattended routine firing

A built configuration is first experienced when it is already law: a hand loadout applies the instant the cap is tapped (ShieldMatrixScreen.kt:285-294) and a routine's loadout fires unattended at its window via applySmartLoadout (MonolithRepository.kt:1087-1089). There is no rehearsal path — no short trial session launched from the builder, no post-trial verdict — and the loadouts' own recipe subtitles (MonolithModels.kt:46-59) are never rendered on any screen, so the user cannot even read the plan before living under it. Mari's maker sat on the chair while building it and felt the wobble in time to fix the joint; Monolith's maker discovers the wobble at 09:00 in a lecture, when the study app they need is on a 2-minute ration.

Recommendation: Add a test-fit to the builder: a TRY THIS LOADOUT FOR 10 MINUTES chip on the LOADOUT section that arms a short, clearly-labelled trial session under the current (or draft) rules, and on its end returns the user to Shield with a one-line verdict prompt — 'KEPT / TOO TIGHT / TOO LOOSE' — where TOO TIGHT reopens the slip with the trial's deflected apps pre-marked. Print the selected loadout's recipe as a checklist above the chip so the plan is read before it is lived.

#### [MEDIUM] Most of the first 30 seconds are designed by AOSP: the FIX key teleports the user into stock Settings, repeatedly

MainActivity.kt's openFixPane (~lines 363-410) maps every board lack to a raw OS intent — Settings.ACTION_ACCESSIBILITY_SETTINGS, ACTION_USAGE_ACCESS_SETTINGS, ACTION_NOTIFICATION_LISTENER_SETTINGS, ACTION_MANAGE_OVERLAY_PERMISSION and the battery-optimisation pane. A first run needing several grants therefore spends the majority of its first half-minute inside stock Android Settings: AOSP type, AOSP toggles, AOSP navigation, with Monolith reduced to an entry in a list. The 280ms drawer tween (ParkDrawer.kt:154) is the only Monolith-authored motion in the window, and each return is a cold re-entry with no recap of where the user is in the sequence. Opal's and Forest's openings never leave their own art direction — every second of the first 30 is spent inside the product being sold.

Recommendation: Stage the exits as a single authored journey instead of six raw teleports: before each FIX trip, a full-screen Monolith card in the Deck's language names the one grant, shows an engraved diagram of the exact Settings toggle to flip, and on return the card strikes that grant through in ink before advancing — so the Settings detour reads as a chapter inside Monolith's book, with the user's place held, rather than the app evaporating and Android taking over its own onboarding.

#### [MEDIUM] The plate is a manual for controls that are not in the room: WHEEL, SLIDE, HOLD and PEEK are explained on a screen that holds none of them

PLATE_BODY (ParkDrawer.kt:109-124) is a running manual — 'WHEEL SETS TIME · SLIDE ARMS · THE HOLD BREAKS', 'PEEK: 2 MINUTES, THEN SHUT AGAIN' — yet it is engraved at the foot of PARK (ParkDrawer.kt:623-646; park.html .plate-foot after all rows and sleds), a screen containing no wheel, no slide-to-arm and no peek; every clause points at a control on another surface. Braun/Rams panel lettering and Teenage Engineering's printed legends obey the opposite rule: the instruction sits adjacent to the control it governs, and a maker's plate certifies only model, power and origin. Monolith fuses the two genres and satisfies neither — the plate is too cryptic to teach and too instructional to be a plate.

Recommendation: Split the plate by genre: PARK keeps a true certification plate only (MONOLITH ML-01 · UNIT Nº 01 · DATA: ON THIS PHONE ONLY · SOUND/POWER lines), and each teaching clause migrates to the surface it names — 'WHEEL SETS TIME · SLIDE ARMS' engraved along the Deck rail, 'PEEK: 2 MINUTES, THEN SHUT AGAIN' printed inside the Airlock, the colour legend on the Deck. First-run teaching then happens at the moment and place of use, which is how one sec's per-permission tutorials and Opal's in-flow walkthrough demos work.

#### [MEDIUM] The pre-flight prepares the jail and never the bench: arming proves guards, permissions and bind, but no step arranges the physical work the session is supposedly for

The arm path's ritual vocabulary is entirely machine-facing: 'SYSTEM GUARD PRE-FLIGHT — Grant Accessibility & Usage Access so Monolith can intercept distracting apps' (AirlockAndDisarmOverlays.kt:505-512), and the Deck render shows GUARD 4/4, 'PROOF: LIVE BIND', '9 WILL SHUT · 3 PEEK' as the pre-start content. Crawford's practitioners build jigs — they prepare the bench (materials laid out, the work opened at the right page) so attention is scaffolded by the environment before willpower is needed. Monolith proves its jail exhaustively and never once asks about the bench: nothing in the arm flow records or prompts a single physical preparation of the actual work.

Recommendation: Split the pre-arm strip into two rows: GUARD (the existing machine proof) and BENCH — a per-task, user-authored preparation line set in Tasks ('BOOK OPEN AT PROBLEM SET 4 · PENCIL · WATER ON THE DESK'), printed under the wheel on the Deck and repeated as the desk clock's banner when no substep is active. Slide-to-start stays disabled-free (no new gate), but the bench line must be authored once per task before it can be bonded, making jig-building part of the ritual rather than an afterthought.

### States: empty error loading — 17 findings (1 critical, 11 high, 5 medium, 0 low)

#### [CRITICAL] The worst failure gets no surface at all: MISSED is designed as an absence, while success gets a numbered ceremony

data/ReceiptState.kt:86 states the law outright — 'MISSED / LATE_FIRE are never an E0' — and finishKindOf (ReceiptState.kt:88-107) returns null for them, so no PendingReceipt, no №, no slip is ever built for a missed or late-fired routine window. Success gets a numbered, sealed artifact (receipt.html frame 1: '№ 048', ARMED/ENDED/HELD lines, deflection list); the worst outcome gets literally no designed surface. The Drawer confirms the asymmetry visually: drawer.html's own caption notes a day with no stored rows 'renders NOTHING — no heading, no missed mark', so a missed day is indistinguishable from a day the app was never installed. The failure the user most needs explained — why the window never happened — is the only outcome with zero presentation.

Recommendation: Give MISSED its own artifact with the same ceremony as a finish: an un-numbered 'no-show slip' (or a Drawer day-heading mark) that prints the window ('WITHIN STUDY · 21:00–22:00'), the judgement in a sentence ('THE WINDOW CLOSED AND NO SESSION RAN'), and the one fact that matters — whether the routine will fire tomorrow unchanged. Follow Dark Souls' 'YOU DIED' and GOV.UK's error-summary pattern: the failure state gets the largest, plainest type on the surface, not absence. Concretely: add a MISSED branch to the receipt/Drawer rendering fed by WindowJudgement.MISSED (RoutineDerive.kt:53), styled as print, dismissed like the slip.

#### [HIGH] PARK's unmeasured board is a finished-looking table with its right column deleted — loading rendered as intentional minimalism

ParkDrawer.kt:387-407 renders the never-measured board as names only (word=null for every row) and ParkDrawer.kt:653 ParkBoardRow composes the state word only if word != null, keeping the full 48dp row and hairline; ParkDrawer.kt:304-315 leaves the LAST PROVED slot blank until a complete set lands and GuardLine.kt guardLineFor returns null for UNMEASURED so the header line vanishes too. park.html shows the measured board's disciplined two-column table — the unmeasured version keeps that table's rhythm with its entire right column deleted, so it reads as a finished spec plate, not as pending measurement.

Recommendation: Keep the column and print the pending state in it: render a designed placeholder in the exact 15sp Atkinson slot for every UNMEASURED row — e.g. '— — —' in onSurfaceVariant plus LAST PROVED '—:— · NOT YET PROVED' — following Apple's SwiftUI .redacted(reason: .placeholder) principle that a loading view preserves the real view's skeleton instead of deleting its content. The board must look unfinished in the same geometry it will look finished in.

#### [HIGH] Receipt builds every variant by deleting rows — faulted, zero-held and zero-deflection slips share no comparable skeleton

ReceiptSheet.kt:90-101 replaces the faulted receipt's title with an empty Box(weight=1f), leaving the № floating over a hole; ReceiptSheet.kt:129-139 composes HELD only when both counts are >=0, BREAK BANKED only when >0, and deflection lines only via forEach — so zero-held, zero-deflection, FLOW (no PLANNED segment) and faulted slips each delete different rows and share no fixed skeleton. receipt.html frame 1 shows the populated slip's tight 8dp stack; no variant preserves that stack's addresses. This contradicts the app's own Shield rule at ShieldMatrixScreen.kt:938-949 (SlipNoneLine) that an empty section prints NONE because 'a printed NONE is a fact'.

Recommendation: Give the slip a fixed field skeleton like a Swiss VAT invoice or an airline boarding pass, where every field prints even at zero: always print title (faulted slips print the intention with the fault line beneath, not a blank box), 'HELD 0 APPS · 0 SITES' or 'HELD — NOT COUNTED', 'BREAK BANKED 0 MIN', and 'DEFLECTIONS — NONE' when the list is empty. Receipts then align row-for-row across days and a missing line means a printing error, not a variant.

#### [HIGH] Deck deletes its NOW row at zero tasks while Tasks holds a 112dp blank leaf — the home screen has no empty-task address

TactileDeckScreen.kt:783 wraps the entire NOW task row — label, title, DONE keycap and 'QUEUE n' — in if (activeTask != null), so at zero tasks the row is not disabled or emptied, it is uncomposed and the Deck's vertical rhythm collapses. FocusSequencerScreen.kt:369-395 does the opposite on purpose: an empty queue holds a 112dp ruled blank leaf printed 'NOTHING QUEUED' so 'the address of what's next is learned once and kept'. deck.html shows the NOW row as the Deck's only task anchor under the wheel; with no task there is no anchor and no instruction at the exact moment a new user or a user who just finished everything needs one.

Recommendation: Apply the Sequencer's own blank-leaf law to the Deck: reserve the NOW row at fixed height in all states and print 'NOW — NOTHING QUEUED' in onSurfaceVariant with the QUEUE count still visible and tappable into the Sequencer, following Things 3's empty-Today treatment which keeps the list's headers and place while stating emptiness. Finishing the last task should land on a held blank, not on a screen that silently lost a row.

#### [HIGH] The empty state is staged as real work: the sample task sits in the NOW row in full ink with a live DONE keycap, indistinguishable from the user's own task

deck.html shows the seeded 'Finish Chapter 4 Problem Set (#1–6)' in the NOW row at full Atkinson 15sp weight with a DONE keycap beside it and 'QUEUE 2' — no SAMPLE tag, no ghost/placeholder treatment, no replace affordance. MonolithRepository.kt:345-356 seeds it as a real FocusTaskEntity with status ACTIVE, one substep already ticked ('Draw free-body diagrams for problems #1–3', done=true); MonolithViewModel.kt:343-363 repeats the same three titles as the checklist fallback when the task list is empty. The user's first meaningful tap is therefore either DONE on someone else's homework or deleting someone else's homework.

Recommendation: Adopt print design's greeking convention and Notion's template-gallery rule: sample content is visibly dummy and quarantined until adopted. Render the seed row in the Deck's existing ghost register (the hero's D8D1CB ghost layer in deck.html), tagged 'EXAMPLE — TAP TO REPLACE', excluded from QUEUE counts, receipts and Drawer history, and replace it in place on first tap with an empty intention field. A staged showroom (IKEA labels its staged rooms as displays) never lets a visitor mistake the display sofa for their own furniture.

#### [HIGH] The failure slip — the one a witness most needs — is designed blank: no title, one jargon line, no explanation

ReceiptSheet.kt:97-113: if (!receipt.faulted) the 15sp title prints, else an empty Box(modifier.weight(1f)) — the faulted slip is deliberately titleless; its only explanation is ReceiptSheet.kt:158-168 'SHIELD — STILL BLOCKED (SERVICE DIDN'T STOP)' at 12sp, plus 'THE SHIELD WAS OFF FOR PART OF THAT SESSION' with no cause, duration or next step. Opal's Sick Day Pass (apk-re/opal/EVIDENCE.md §10.3) designs the exception first: a reason chosen before release (Feeling sick / Doctor or dentist / Family emergency…) plus a free-text note the school reads — the failure case is the most legible, not the blankest.

Recommendation: Never blank the title on the faulted slip. Keep the intention title and add a witness fault block following the Sick Day Pass pattern: a plain heading 'This session was not fully protected', one sentence of what happened and for how long ('Blocking stopped for part of the session — the service did not restart'), and a pre-written reason field the owner completes before the slip can be shown. Jargon line moves to small mono detail under it.

#### [HIGH] The Drawer archive deletes its own gaps: days and months with nothing stored do not exist, so sporadic use reads as an unbroken run

DrawerScreen.kt:84-107 buildDayGroups() builds its date set ONLY from row dates, day-word dates and (optionally) today — a date with neither is never emitted. drawer.html states it in its own caption: 'A day with no stored rows and no declared word renders NOTHING in the Drawer — no heading, no missed mark.' The ALL MONTHS index likewise lists only storedMonths, so a skipped month never appears either. GitHub's contribution calendar and the Seinfeld chain calendar do the opposite: every day in the range gets a cell, and an empty day is a visible level-0 cell — absence is plotted, not deleted.

Recommendation: Make the month a true calendar: in MONTH and LANDING views render a heading for every date from the 1st to today (future dates omitted), empty days printing the heading plus a hairline and the day-word slot, so a gap reads as a gap. Add the same honesty to ALL MONTHS: months with no records print in onSurfaceVariant between their neighbours instead of vanishing. Keep stored rows visually dominant (ink title vs grey empty heading) so the archive gains a time axis without gaining noise.

#### [HIGH] The Deck breaks the app's own blank-leaf law: with no task cued, the NOW row is deleted outright instead of held as a blank

TactileDeckScreen.kt:783 wraps the entire NOW task row in `if (activeTask != null)` — with no cued task the row, its DONE key and its QUEUE count all vanish and the Deck collapses upward, leaving the wheel and an armable SLIDE TO START with no intention slot and no route to add one. The app's own Tasks screen states the opposite law at FocusSequencerScreen.kt:369-373: 'an empty queue does not collapse the pad… so the address of "what's next" is learned once and kept' — then holds a 112dp blank to honour it.

Recommendation: Hold the NOW address on the Deck exactly as the pad holds its blank leaf: when activeTask is null render the same-height row as a ghost — 'NOW' eyebrow in ink, title slot printing 'NOTHING CUED' in onSurfaceVariant over a 1dp rule, and the QUEUE word replaced by a tappable 'QUEUE A TASK' that opens the sequencer. The slide may still arm a task-less session, but the Deck must show the hole it is arming around instead of pretending the row was never there.

#### [HIGH] Every zero wears the same grey regardless of meaning: 'nothing held' is a victory and 'nothing stored' is a failure, and one frozen digest zero renders as pure silence

AirlockAndDisarmOverlays.kt:385-402: the held-notifications zero prints 'Nothing has been held.' (frozen) or 'Zero notifications intercepted during focus.' (live) in 13sp sentence-case onSurfaceVariant — and if frozenMode is true with frozenAtMillis == null the guard `if (!frozenMode || frozenAtMillis != null)` prints literally nothing at all. The same visual treatment (grey, quiet, easily missed) is used for the Drawer's 'NOTHING STORED YET' (DrawerScreen.kt:709-712), which is a bad zero meaning 'you have no record', while a held-zero is a good zero meaning 'nobody got through'. Apple Mail/Spark-style Inbox Zero treats the good zero as a settled, full-weight state, not as a void.

Recommendation: Give zeros a valence in the type system. Good zeros (held 0, a slip section with NONE, a completed queue) print in onBackground ink at the section's normal weight as a settled fact — e.g. the digest header already prints 'HELD NOTIFICATIONS • 0'; its body should close the thought with one ink line 'NOTHING CAME THROUGH' instead of a grey apology, and the frozen-without-timestamp case must print it too (delete the null guard's silence). Bad/inviting zeros keep the variant tone but gain the action the neighbouring finding specifies. One EmptyFact composable with a QUIET / INVITING variant, used by Drawer, Shield, Tasks and the digest, so valence — not whichever screen you are on — decides how a zero looks.

#### [HIGH] Shield gap is communicated as one flat sentence with no magnitude, no timing and no consequence — the receipt logs the breach but never explains it

A session the shield abandoned mid-run books exactly one extra line on the slip: 'THE SHIELD WAS OFF FOR PART OF THAT SESSION' (ui/components/ReceiptSheet.kt:147), set in the same Atkinson Bold 12sp onBackground as every other line, with no colour, icon, gap start time, gap duration, or statement of what got through during the gap — even though the slip already itemises deflections by timestamp (ReceiptSheet.kt deflections list, receipt.html frame 1). The verdict word itself is a log token appended to the time line: 'ENDED 19:32 · ENDED · SHIELD GAP' (data/MonolithRepository.kt:1688). The only other differentiation is invisible: finishPulses (ReceiptState.kt:111-112) withholds the completion pulse for shield-gap finishes, so the failure's second signal is a sound that does not happen.

Recommendation: Itemise the gap the way the slip already itemises deflections: 'SHIELD OFF 19:04–19:17 · 13 MIN UNGUARDED' as its own ruled section, and promote the verdict from an appended token to the slip's headline treatment. Follow aircraft ECAM/EICAS message design: every fault message names the system, the effect, and the consequence in that order — never a code alone. Here: system (SHIELD), effect (OFF 19:04–19:17), consequence (THOSE MINUTES ARE NOT BOOKED AS HELD). Keep the withheld pulse, but add one visible mark so silence is not the only differentiator.

#### [HIGH] PARK presents every hardware failure as one grey-or-black status word — a dead listener and a user-toggled-off sniper are typographically identical

In PARK, every failure is a single right-aligned status word — GRANTED / MISSING / STALE for permissions, RUNNING / PAUSED / OFF for interceptors (ui/components/ParkDrawer.kt:338-385; park.html board). A lack is distinguished from health only by ink density: wordIsLack swaps the word from onSurfaceVariant grey to full onBackground black (ParkDrawer.kt ParkBoardRow). The drawer's own material law bans the one signal that could carry alarm: 'orange zero' — the only object allowed is the FIX key (ParkDrawer.kt:80-82). So a dead notification listener ('NOTIFICATION LISTENER — MISSING', meaning held notifications silently stop working) reads identically in weight and form to the Shorts sniper being OFF by the user's own choice. No row states a consequence ('notifications will not be held'), a since-when, or a cause; the header Guard line compounds it by naming only the FIRST lack while 'a second rides unnamed in the count' (ui/components/GuardLine.kt:40-45). The FIX key likewise exists only for permission lacks — an interceptor OFF has no remedy affordance on its own row.

Recommendation: Keep the one-tone print discipline but add a consequence clause under any lack row, in the same mono print: 'NOTIFICATION LISTENER — MISSING · HELD NOTIFICATIONS WILL REACH YOU' and a measured-at time. Follow Transport for London line-status design: the word (SEVERE DELAYS) is never printed alone — it is always followed by the plain-language effect on the traveller and the alternative. Also print every lack in the header line ('GUARD 2/4 — LISTENER, BATTERY') instead of hiding all but the first behind a count, and give interceptor lacks the same FIX affordance permission lacks get.

#### [HIGH] The faulted receipt communicates failure by erasing its own title and printing service jargon, with no user action

When the shield service fails to stop at session end, the receipt's response is subtraction: the title is deliberately blanked (ui/components/ReceiptSheet.kt:90-101, 'the faulted sheet has no title'), and the entire failure communication is one line of internal jargon — 'SHIELD — STILL BLOCKED (SERVICE DIDN'T STOP)' (ReceiptSheet.kt:159) — in the same 12sp bold as the shield-gap line. The user is told the machine's service state, not their own situation (apps are still blocked right now), and given no action: the sheet's only interaction is dismissal on any tap (ReceiptSheet.kt clickable scrim/sheet), after which the still-running shield has no surface at all. The most urgent failure state in the app — it is actively blocking the user's phone after the session ended — is presented as a receipt with its headline removed.

Recommendation: Invert it: the faulted sheet should be the ONE receipt with a headline and an action. Title it with the user's situation, not the service's ('STILL BLOCKED'), keep the intention as subtitle, and give the sheet a single ink key — 'STOP THE SHIELD NOW' — wired to the stop path, following Apple HIG / GOV.UK error-page law: state what happened, state what it means for you, provide the next step, in that order. The blank-title rule should apply to no state; a missing headline reads as a rendering bug, not as gravity.

#### [MEDIUM] Airlock demotes a withheld peek from a 42dp chip to a loose sentence — three different blocks share one homeless text style

AirlockAndDisarmOverlays.kt:663-683 composes the available peek as a full-width 42dp BlockitActionChip plus a price line, but AirlockAndDisarmOverlays.kt:690-713 composes all three withheld states — COOLDOWN (peekCooldownPrint at :235, 'PEEK COOLDOWN — AGAIN IN {n} MIN'), ALREADY_ACTIVE (:699) and PEEK_OFF (:705) — as bare 12.5sp Atkinson text at 80% cream with no container. airlock.html frames 1-2 confirm the card is centred with 16dp spacing, so swapping a 42dp chip for a one-line sentence shrinks the card and shifts RETURN TO FOCUS at the moment of maximum temptation; a time-bound block, a running lease and a disabled feature also receive identical visual weight despite needing different responses.

Recommendation: Keep the chip's body for the withheld state, following Material 3's disabled-component rule that the container shape survives at reduced opacity (12% container / 38% content) so layout is learned once: render a non-interactive 42dp chip in Night surfaceVariant printed 'PEEK — AGAIN IN {n} MIN' with a thin progress rule for cooldown, 'PEEK RUNNING' for ALREADY_ACTIVE, and 'PEEK IS OFF' only for PEEK_OFF. Same address, same height, three legibly different prints.

#### [MEDIUM] Cabinet prints unforged curios at full weight — 0/6, 2/6 and 6/6 collections are the same page

DrawerScreen.kt:374-410 lists all six CurioCatalog artifacts unconditionally via items(artifacts); the only partial-state signal is at :398, where a forged row adds the 10.5sp word 'FORGED' — unforged rows print serial, name and subtitle at identical weight, size and ink. drawer.html frame 2 (the Cabinet) shows 2 of 6 forged yet all six rows are visually interchangeable apart from that one small word, and no header anywhere prints a count such as 'FORGED 2 / 6'. A 0/6 first-week cabinet, a 2/6 cabinet and a completed 6/6 cabinet are the same page.

Recommendation: Design the collection's partial state like a Panini sticker album, where uncollected slots are numbered voids rather than full entries: print a Cabinet header 'FORGED {n} / 6', render unforged rows as serial + dot leader + '— — —' in onSurfaceVariant with name and subtitle withheld, and reserve full ink, name and subtitle for forged rows only (detail view already distinguishes them at DrawerScreen.kt:485-488 with 'NOT YET FORGED'). Completion then has a visible shape and each forge visibly changes the page.

#### [MEDIUM] The Cabinet at 0-of-6 spoils and flattens its own collection: unforged curios print at full weight with names and lore revealed, differing from forged ones only by a missing badge

drawer.html Frame 2 (Cabinet, from DrawerScreen.kt cabinet branch): all six curios — Harmonic Loop, Brass Gyroscope, String Prism, Pocket Planetarium, Sand Pendulum, The Monolith Cube — print at identical weight with full name and subtitle whether forged or not; the ONLY state mark is the word FORGED appearing beside two of them, so at 0-of-6 the screen is indistinguishable from 6-of-6 except by absence. There is no count anywhere on the screen (header is just CABINET / BACK), and the detail's entire zero-progress line is 'NOT YET FORGED'. The Pokedex convention — unseen entries shown as silhouettes with names withheld — exists precisely so a collection at zero creates pull and each acquisition is a reveal.

Recommendation: Split the cabinet into two print weights. Forged rows keep today's full treatment. Unforged rows drop to onSurfaceVariant, print serial + a withheld name ('TOY 03 · —————') and no subtitle/lore, so the cabinet at day one reads as six empty mounts, not a finished catalogue. Add the missing tally to the header's right side in the slip's grammar: '0 OF 6 FORGED'. On first forge, the row re-strikes to ink with its name — the reveal the current flat list makes impossible.

#### [MEDIUM] The Drawer's zero state has a different skeleton from its populated state: ALL MONTHS only materialises after the first record, so the first finish rearranges the landing

DrawerScreen.kt:185 defines globallyEmpty, and the LANDING branch at DrawerScreen.kt:709ff renders a different skeleton for it — 'NOTHING STORED YET', today's heading, CURIOS — while the ALL MONTHS nav row exists only in the populated else-branch. The first finished session therefore doesn't just add a row, it inserts a new navigation row above CURIOS and re-lays the landing the user had learned. Stable-chrome systems (Material navigation patterns, Things' fixed sidebar) keep destinations present and merely change their state, so learning survives the first datum.

Recommendation: Freeze the landing skeleton across the zero/populated boundary: in the globallyEmpty branch still render the ALL MONTHS row (in onSurfaceVariant, non-navigating or navigating to an index that prints 'NO EARLIER MONTHS') above CURIOS, and keep 'NOTHING STORED YET' in the content slot where the current month's groups will land. First data should fill addresses, never build them.

#### [MEDIUM] All verdicts share one typographic register — ATTENDED, PARTIAL and SHIELD GAP are the same 11sp mono word in the same slot

receiptOutcomeWord (data/MonolithRepository.kt:1683-1689) maps every publishable ending to a short token — ATTENDED, PARTIAL, SLEPT THROUGH, FLOW ENDED, ENDED, ENDED · SHIELD GAP — and ReceiptSheet.kt:124 prints whichever it is in the identical slot, font and weight: 'ENDED 19:32 · {word}' in 11sp Anonymous Pro tracked 1sp (receipt.html frame 1 shows the clean case). A PARTIAL routine (you showed up for half the window), an ATTENDED one and a shield-gap one differ by one word in a metadata line, under a title that never changes. There is no verdict hierarchy anywhere in the failure vocabulary: the stored tokens (ReceiptState.kt:30-50: ELAPSED_CLEAN, ELAPSED_SHIELD_GAP, VALVE_BROKE, GRACE_CANCEL, ENDED_EARLY) are database dialect lightly respelled, not communication designed per outcome — and VALVE_BROKE, GRACE_CANCEL and ENDED_EARLY endings receive no receipt at all, so breaking a session presents as the session simply vanishing.

Recommendation: Promote the outcome from metadata to message: each publishable kind gets a one-sentence verdict line in Atkinson (the reading voice, not the mono log voice) directly under the title — e.g. PARTIAL: 'YOU WERE THERE FOR PART OF THE WINDOW'; SHIELD GAP: 'THE SESSION RAN, BUT NOT ALL OF IT WAS GUARDED' — with the mono 'ENDED · {word}' demoted to the footer log where tokens belong. Follow Swiss railway departure boards and hospital triage cards: category is carried redundantly by position, wording and weight, never by a single code word the reader must already know. Extend the same treatment to the no-receipt endings: a valve break deserves a one-line un-numbered slip ('BROKE THE HOLD · TOKEN SPENT') instead of disappearance.

### Data visualisation — 30 findings (10 critical, 18 high, 2 medium, 0 low)

#### [CRITICAL] GUARD 4/4 is a completeness badge with a hidden denominator — it counts four of the six permissions the app demands

GuardLine.kt:38-45: the Deck header — the one surface visible in deck.html on every screen — prints 'GUARD 4/4' when WatchItemId.COUNTED (WatchStore.kt:98-101: accessibility, usage, device admin, notification listener) are granted. WatchStore.kt:93-97 defines PERMISSIONS as six, adding OVERLAY and BATTERY, and park.html shows all six as permission rows above three more interceptor rows. A user reading the header fraction at a glance sees a complete score; the two excluded grants simply do not exist in that arithmetic, and the word counted nowhere appears on any surface.

Recommendation: Stop printing a fraction whose denominator is a private subset. Either print the true total — 'GUARD 6/6' derived from PERMISSIONS, with interceptors summarised separately in Park — or rename the header mark to what it is, 'CORE GUARD 4/4', and add the missing two as a second small mark when they lack ('+ OVERLAY MISSING'). Follow the browser-padlock rule: a completeness badge must never be literally true in code and materially false at reading distance; the badge, the board count and the FIX queue must share one denominator everywhere.

#### [CRITICAL] Aggregation deletes everything a letter would quote: DailyFocusStat sums sessions into minutes/blocks/intercepts and throws away intention, named temptations, day words and outcomes at compute time

MonolithModels.kt:473-479 DailyFocusStat holds exactly three fields — totalMinutes, blocks25mCount, interceptionsCount. MonolithRepository.kt:2388-2391 builds them with sumOf { elapsedSeconds } and sumOf { phantomReachesBlocked }: per-session identity is destroyed in the aggregation itself, so no future UI can recover which intention the minutes served, which app was turned away at what hour (data the per-session receipt does keep — ReceiptSheet.kt prints timed deflections), or that a day was declared REST/ILL/FAMILY (DayNoteEntity, MonolithModels.kt day_notes). drawer.html confirms the surviving record: day headings and task rows, no week-level synthesis anywhere. Fitbit's report, built on far dumber data, still selects and names a superlative — one day is labelled 'Best Day!' — because a report a person reads needs a chosen fact, not only totals.

Recommendation: Change the weekly model's shape, not just its surface: DailyFocusStat must retain, per day, the top intention by minutes, the single most-deflected app with its hour, the declared day word, and the day's outcome — aggregates become the letter's appendix table, not its body. The letter's body is then composed from retained facts: one superlative line (longest kept session, named by intention), one resistance line (named app, named hour), one rest line (declared words quoted back verbatim). If a fact was not retained, it is never invented in prose.

#### [CRITICAL] The valve paints spending as earning: breaking the session fills an accent progress bar, and no token is ever drawn emptying

airlock.html frame 3 and ui/views/BlockitSuitcaseAndSwitchesViews.kt Emergency60sValveView (line 532ff): the 68dp valve fills left-to-right in the night accent #F47442, banked quarters solid, in-hand segment at alpha 180, exactly the progress-bar grammar of filling/earning. park.html's own spec plate defines that colour: 'COLOUR IS A VERB: ORANGE = COMMIT' — the same accent as the Deck's slide-to-arm cap (deck.html). Nothing on the valve empties, cracks or is subtracted: no token glyph depletes while the bar grows, so the single most expensive tap in the app is drawn as an achievement filling up. Zario's ScreenBlocker does the opposite with its screen_blocker_xp_slider (apk-re/zario/EVIDENCE.md §4.1): the balance is the slider and spending moves it down.

Recommendation: Invert the valve's valence: open the Disarm overlay with the token drawn full — one filled token cell labelled 1/1 WEEK beside the valve — and drain that cell in step with the hold, the valve track itself staying neutral ink. Accent orange is reserved for the KEEP FOCUSING chip. Spending must look like subtraction everywhere in the app; filling-up is the visual verb for arming and earning only.

#### [CRITICAL] The 7-day series is computed, quantised, then thrown away — minutes, blocks and interceptions never become length

MonolithViewModel.kt:264-265 exposes sevenDayStats and recomputes it at six sites (e.g. :781, :1210, :2453) yet no composable collects it; MonolithRepository.kt:2361-2405 compute7DayHistory() builds a genuinely multivariate record — DailyFocusStat (MonolithModels.kt:473-479) carries totalMinutes, blocks25mCount and interceptionsCount per day — and DrawerScreen.kt:58-62 then declares the only history surface 'not a dashboard: no totals, no streaks, no percentages, no counts'. The aggregation itself destroys shape before any drawing could happen: MonolithRepository.kt:2390 quantises minutes into blocks25 = totalMins/25 with a fudge coerceAtLeast(1) at 15 minutes, and dayLabel is weekday-only ('EEE'), so 14 vs 24 minutes and a spike of interceptions are indistinguishable in the stored series. In drawer.html a 2H 10M day and a 24 MIN day render as identical rows of 10.5sp mono text.

Recommendation: Wire the existing flow into the Drawer landing as one Tufte-style 7-column strip, not a dashboard: seven equal-width columns on a shared zero baseline, bar length = totalMinutes (true minutes, delete the blocks25 quantisation), a single dot per column for interceptionsCount on the same column, weekday + date under each column, direct labels, no axes, no legend, no pie. Keep the Drawer charter's language — label it 'THE WEEK, AS KEPT' — but let length, not prose, carry the comparison, exactly as StayFree's bar system lets length carry usage and Opal's home trend lets one line carry the week.

#### [CRITICAL] The tower is an unhosted pictogram: bricks encode fill order, not dates, amounts or gaps

BlockitTowerFadersAndCatalogViews.kt:24-26 TowerStreakView defaults totalBricksCount to a fabricated 19 and is never instantiated anywhere — AirlockAndDisarmOverlays.kt:62 imports it and no AndroidView ever constructs it, so the app's only accumulation graphic has no host surface. Its encoding in BlockitTowerFadersAndCatalogViews.kt:52-54,111-138 is sequential fill with no temporal mapping: brickNumber = fl*7+col+1, laid bricks all one ink, crown brick accent, the rest ghost — position encodes order of filling, never a date, so a missed week, a light day and a heavy day are visually identical and a gap leaves no hole. Display is also forced: displayFloors = max(totalFloors, 4), so an almost-empty history still draws a 4-floor monument of ghost slots that outweigh the data ink.

Recommendation: Rebuild the tower as a calendar, following GitHub's contribution graph — the reference that proves a grid can be read at a glance: columns = weeks, rows = weekdays, cell position = the actual date, so gaps stay visibly empty. Keep the brick material and 7-wide rhythm, but give each day-brick a 4-step sequential fill (ghost / light taupe / ink / accent for the best day) proportional to that day's focused minutes, print month labels above the columns, and drop the 4-floor minimum so the graphic's size is the history's size. Host it at the top of the Drawer landing, fed by compute7DayHistory extended to per-date minutes, with a tap on a brick opening that date's stored rows.

#### [CRITICAL] The dial has no 12 o'clock: every numeral is the same width and weight, and the scale's origin is an unmarked hole

BlockitCoreViews.kt:793-807 draws every rim numeral (30, 60, 90, 120, 150, 180) with one paintMono, one colour (tokTextSecondary), one 15sp size — no numeral is wider, bolder or brighter than another. The scale's origin gets the opposite of an anchor: :683-690 'Teeth are CUT across FLOW's basin... inside the break there is no grip, no tick, no value', and :748-752 confirms ticks exist only from 10 to 180, so where the dial begins there is a 31.5-degree gap (the Strait, 94.5-126 degrees) with nothing printed at all. Tanaka's first of the nine elements is a double-width index at 12 o'clock precisely so orientation is instant; Monolith's dial must be read, not oriented to — the user hunts for where zero lives and finds a hole.

Recommendation: Cut an orientation anchor into the scale: draw the numeral at the scale's resting position double-width and in the primary ink (the equivalent of the double 12 index), and close the Strait with one wide, flat rectangular marker at the FLOW seat — a single broad plane, wider than any major tick — so 'where the dial starts' is visible from across the room before any numeral is read.

#### [CRITICAL] One rim carries three conflicting division systems: 120 decorative knurl teeth impersonate graduations around 35 real stops and 6 numerals

A dial-maker's chapter ring has exactly one graduation system, and every stroke on a Nomos minute track is a true minute, with the 5-minute stroke merely lengthened. Monolith's rim prints a knurled band of 120 teeth at a 3-degree pitch (BlockitCoreViews.kt:681-715, toothDeg += 3f) that reads at a glance as a 120-division scale — but the wheel can only stop at 35 detents, every 5 minutes at 9 degrees each (BlockitCoreViews.kt:748, minutesToAngle at 516-522), and only 6 of those stops carry numerals. The teeth are admitted decoration ('screen-fixed material', BlockitCoreViews.kt:676-680), and two of them are deliberately printed wrong: toothFlare hand-sets teeth 17 and 83 low at 0.62/0.68 against the 0.84-1.16 field (BlockitCoreViews.kt:557-570) — simulated factory damage on the one surface whose job is to state measurement honestly.

Recommendation: Separate grip from graduation physically: move the knurl to its own band outside the chapter ring, behind the socket hairline, so no tooth sits on the scale's radius; or re-cut the teeth at the true 9-degree detent pitch, phase-locked to minutesToAngle, so every tooth is a stop the wheel can actually make. Delete the two hand-dimmed 'broken' teeth — a measuring surface does not print fake wear.

#### [CRITICAL] The Drawer is a timetable that deletes its empty days and never aligns its times into columns

DrawerScreen.kt:84-110 buildDayGroups() only creates a group for dates present in rows or dayWords — a day with neither renders nothing at all (drawer.html states it verbatim: a day with no stored rows and no word renders NOTHING, no heading, no missed mark). DrawerScreen.kt:886-920 StoredRow() sets category, clockTime() and spentLabel() as three variable-width texts in a Row spacedBy 8dp, so finish times start at a different x on every row; :122-132 spentLabel() itself uses three grammars — '1H 05M', '48 MIN', '45 SEC'. A timetable's contract is the opposite: the grid of days and the columns exist whether or not anything ran, so absence is readable as absence.

Recommendation: Redraw the Drawer as a true timetable: print every calendar day in the month as a fixed row — date in a fixed 92dp left column, word-or-empty in a fixed second column — including blank days with an em-dash, never omitting the row. Give StoredRow three fixed-width columns (category 72dp, finish time 44dp tabular Anonymous Pro, duration 64dp right-aligned) and force one duration grammar everywhere: H:MM above an hour, M MIN below it, no SEC form in the list.

#### [CRITICAL] The panel has no output stage: the summed verdict and the protecting state are computed every shield iteration and printed nowhere on the board

WatchStore.kt:214 documents the shield loop's publication as 'the engine heartbeat (behind the strip, never a board line)'. The Warrant — the one summed verdict, LIVE / OFF / UNPROVEN, derived in WatchStore.deriveWarrant — is printed on the Deck, not in Park. The park.html render shows what the board offers instead: nine component states plus a LAST PROVED timestamp at the top, i.e. the panel's only summary is a clock, not an output. A user can read ACCESSIBILITY GRANTED, USAGE ACCESS GRANTED, NOTIFICATIONS RUNNING and still have no line that answers the only question the panel exists for: is anything actually being held right now — the engineProtecting fact the store already carries in every snapshot and prints nowhere on this surface.

Recommendation: Add the missing OUTPUT stage as the board's final band: one line, VERDICT, printing the derived warrant word (LIVE / UNPROVEN / OFF) beside a second word for the engine state (PROTECTING / IDLE), both derived from the snapshot already passed to ParkDrawer. Set it in the board's largest state type and rule it off with a double hairline, the way an output section is fenced on a panel. LAST PROVED stays as the calibration stamp under it, demoted from headline to footnote.

#### [CRITICAL] Time is never denominated in life: every surface caps its arithmetic at minutes, a session, or a month

The largest unit of time anywhere in the product is the wheel's 180 minutes (ui/views/BlockitCoreViews.kt:367, dial coerced 5..180 at :375). The Deck hero is labelled TOTAL but totals only the next span — breaks included (ui/screens/TactileDeckScreen.kt:618, :632 'The hero states the TOTAL'); the receipt denominates a life-fragment as 'ARMED 18:42 · PLANNED 50 MIN / ENDED 19:32' (ui/components/ReceiptSheet.kt:118) and the Drawer prices days only as task 'ESTIMATE n MIN' / 'SPENT' (ui/screens/DrawerScreen.kt:273, :280). No surface — Deck, Drawer, receipt, Tower — ever converts guarded or lost time into days, a year-fraction, or a share of a life. Seneca's opening charge (De Brevitate Vitae ch.1) is that life is not short but wasted, yet Monolith's arithmetic stops at the session, so a user can 'win' every session for a decade and never once see the decade.

Recommendation: Add a life-denomination, not a score: (1) Receipt gains a final mono line under HELD — '50 MIN · 1/525,600 OF THIS YEAR' computed from planned span; (2) the Drawer's month footer sums the month's guarded time as days ('GUARDED 3.2 DAYS THIS MONTH') in the same Anonymous Pro mono as receipt lines; (3) the Deck hero eyebrow keeps TOTAL for the span but the imprint tenant line gains a cumulative second line once a year total exists: 'THIS YEAR: 11 DAYS HELD'. No points, no percentage-of-goal — the unit changes from minutes to life.

#### [HIGH] The tower has no skyline: identical cells in a labelled grid read as a spreadsheet, never as a structure you built

ui/views/BlockitTowerFadersAndCatalogViews.kt:100-142 — every brick is drawn from one brickW and one floorH (capped at dp(26f)), with an identical dp(4f) corner radius; the only variation in the entire structure is fill state (accent crown :116-120, solid ink :121-131, ghost slot :132-140). Floors are labelled F01, F02 in mono at :95, so the eye reads a spreadsheet with row headers, not a structure. LEGO Architecture skylines work because of representative scaling: in 21028 the Flatiron is deliberately oversized relative to the towers behind it so each element keeps its character and the skyline gains a rhythm of heights; a uniform grid of equal cells produces no profile at any count — 19 bricks and 56 bricks are the same picture at different fill levels. The header even files the structure as data: 'STREAK TOWER • 7 BRICKS / FLOOR' (:60).

Recommendation: Break the grid where the information is: let brick width encode the session that laid it (a 25-minute span a narrow brick, a 3-hour span a wide one, LEGO-style representative scaling with a stated minimum), and give the tower a ground line — a heavier foundation row — and a distinct capstone shape for the newest brick instead of a colour change alone. The result should read as a skyline profile from across the room: irregular, grounded, and taller-feeling than it is wide.

#### [HIGH] The journal is never readable at month scale: ALL MONTHS is a bare list of month names and the words never aggregate into a pattern

DrawerScreen.kt:621-650 (DrawerView.INDEX) renders storedMonths as nothing but monthLabel rows — 'OCTOBER 2026' in Atkinson Medium 14sp with a divider — no word counts, no word marks, no indication that a month contained four ILL days or two FAMILY weeks. The words exist only inline, one heading at a time, inside the month view (DrawerScreen.kt:683-695), so the only way to perceive a pattern is to scroll and memorise. The Hobonichi Techo ships a yearly index — one column per month, every date listed — explicitly used by owners as an at-a-glance record of how the year actually went; Day One likewise offers a calendar view where entry days are marked, making rhythms visible. Monolith already holds exactly the data for this (DayWordStore.all(), DayWordStore.kt:26-29) and renders none of it above day level.

Recommendation: Turn the ALL MONTHS index into the journal's table of contents, Hobonichi yearly-index style: under each month name, print that month's declared words as a compact mono marginalia line in filing order (e.g. 'ILL · ILL · REST · FAMILY') or as a 7-column mini-calendar strip with word-days inked. No totals, no percentages — the app correctly refuses to score words — just the sequence made visible, so a hard month reads as a hard month at one glance.

#### [HIGH] Drawer screenshot reads as a notes / to-do archive: 'STORED' plus task titles and durations, with no visual trace that any of it was focused time

drawer.html: the screen is headed only 'STORED' (DrawerScreen.kt:224) with a search box 'TYPE TO FIND A TASK' (DrawerScreen.kt:546); below, day headings ('FRI 30 OCT · REST') and rows that print just a task title plus category, clock time and duration ('Finish Chapter 4 Problem Set · Study · 09:42 · 1H 05M'). The render caption confirms there is no tower, no streak, no week total and no completed/kept verdict anywhere on the screen, and days with no stored rows render nothing at all. The second view is headed 'CABINET' and lists 'TOY 01 Harmonic Loop', 'TOY 02 Brass Gyroscope — FORGED' with no image of any toy. Nothing in either screenshot says 'focus history', 'you did this', or how much was achieved.

Recommendation: Add the screenshot-level summary Forest's forest view gets for free — accumulated trees make 'past focus' visible without a single label: pin a summary band under 'STORED' reading 'This week: 6 sessions · 7H 20M focused' with a 7-bar day strip (bar height = minutes focused, empty day = flat tick, so vanished days become visibly empty rather than absent), append the plain outcome word 'DONE' to each stored row, and rename the header to 'FOCUS LOG' with 'STORED' kept as a sub-label. Rename 'CABINET' rows to show a drawn 48dp line illustration of each curio beside its name, or a stranger will keep reading them as a toy shop's stock list.

#### [HIGH] MINUTES DIE makes the HORIZON bar a decorative lie: equal taupe blocks for unequal work

FocusSequencerScreen.kt submitTask (~L139-148): 'MINUTES DIE (Sarthak's order): the composer asks NOTHING about duration — 0, no estimate given' — onAddTask(clean, 0, 'Study', '', …). The header then suppresses the total when computedTotalMins == 0 (~L185-195). BlockitTowerFadersAndCatalogViews.kt TaskHorizonBarView.onDraw L194: totalMins = tasks.sumOf { it.estimatedMinutes.coerceAtLeast(10) } — so a queue of name-only tasks, the normal case, is drawn as equal-width taupe segments padded to a fictitious 10 minutes each, differing only in shade. In YPT's 10-minute planner and on a paper timetable grid, segment length IS the information: a 2-hour revision block is visibly four times a 30-minute drill. Here length encodes queue position's shading, nothing about work.

Recommendation: Either kill the bar or make it honest. Following YPT's cell logic: give each leaf a duration by gesture, not by typing minutes — drag the leaf's bottom edge down the 10-minute ruler to lengthen it (10-minute snaps, printed as cell count, not a minute numeral, preserving the no-numbers voice). The Horizon bar then draws true proportions from those cells, segments under ~20 minutes print no label, and a queue with no placed durations draws no bar at all — a thin perforation line with 'NO TIME PLACED' — instead of equal blocks that claim equal work.

#### [HIGH] History rows print unequal times in equal ink — comparison demands arithmetic, not eyesight

DrawerScreen.kt:883-886 defines StoredRow as 'title, category, finish time, time spent. No estimate, no checkbox, no bar, no rank' and DrawerScreen.kt:834-840 defines DayHeading as 'a shelf label only — nothing follows it, no total, no grade'. The durations that ARE printed all get identical visual weight: category, clock time and spentLabel print in the same Anonymous Pro 10.5sp onSurfaceVariant row (DrawerScreen.kt:886-925; drawer.html StoredRow .meta). A 2H 10M row and a 24 MIN row differ only in characters the user must parse and mentally divide — there is no pre-attentive channel (length, position, intensity) anywhere on the screen.

Recommendation: Keep every exact figure, but add the missing length channel per Cleveland & McGill's encoding hierarchy (position/length read accurately, text read slowly): under each day heading draw one hairline bar per stored row, width proportional to actualSecondsSpent against a single shared scale for the visible month (longest row = full width), in ink for the row and hairline-grey for the remainder, with the existing '1H 05M' figure kept at the bar's end as a direct label. This is StayFree's basic move — a bar beside every usage figure — executed in Monolith's own ruled, mono, no-axes idiom, and it requires no total, score or percentage the charter forbids.

#### [HIGH] The only proportional chart in the app draws the plan — no surface ever draws the outcome beside it

The sole proportional graphic in the app visualises intentions, never results: BlockitTowerFadersAndCatalogViews.kt:194,198 TaskHorizonBarView sizes segments from estimatedMinutes (each silently floored: coerceAtLeast(10), so a 2-minute task draws at 5x its true share), hosted in FocusSequencerScreen.kt:169-207 as the pre-session HORIZON strip, and BlockitTowerFadersAndCatalogViews.kt:233 suppresses the minute figure entirely on segments under 38dp. No equivalent strip exists for actualSecondsSpent on the receipt or in the Drawer — outcomes, the data StayFree and Opal chart, get only text rows, while the plan gets the only honest visual channel the app owns (minus its floor distortion).

Recommendation: Mirror the horizon bar at the point of outcome: on the receipt and on each Drawer day, draw the same full-width strip segmented by actualSecondsSpent with a true zero baseline and no 10-minute floor (a 2-minute task gets a 2-minute sliver, labelled outside the segment if it is too narrow, never widened). Put plan and outcome as two stacked strips of identical scale — estimate on top in ghost tone, actual below in ink — so over- and under-running is seen as a length difference, the slopegraph-style before/after comparison Tufte prescribes, instead of two numbers on two different screens.

#### [HIGH] The receipt flattens a timed session into a list — deflection times never take their place on a timeline

ReceiptSheet.kt:116-145 prints ARMED and ENDED as two HH:mm mono lines and then receipt.deflections.forEach as an undifferentiated list of 'HH:mm · AppName' lines at 11sp (ReceiptMonoLine, ReceiptSheet.kt:188-197); receipt.html frame 1 shows the result — three deflections (18:57 Instagram, 19:11 YouTube, 19:26 X) as stacked text. The underlying record has everything a timeline needs — arm wall time, end wall time and each deflection's atWallMillis — yet nothing places an event in proportion: a deflection 2 minutes after arming and one 2 minutes before the end occupy identical lines, and clustering (three reaches in five minutes = a craving wave) is invisible.

Recommendation: Add one 16dp timeline strip to the slip, Tufte sparkline discipline: a single hairline track spanning ARMED to ENDED at true proportional scale, one tick per deflection placed by (atWallMillis - armWallMs) / span, tick height encoding nothing but presence, the existing 'HH:mm · App' lines kept below as the legend/table. A clean session draws an unbroken empty track — the absence becomes the artefact's most eloquent mark, and a clustered session reads instantly as a burst, which no list of times can show.

#### [HIGH] The Drawer archive has no data columns: in StoredRow the clock time starts wherever the category word happens to end

A grid's payoff is comparison down a column. DrawerScreen.kt StoredRow (DrawerScreen.kt:892-936) prints its metadata as one Row with Arrangement.spacedBy(8.dp): categoryTag, then clockTime(completedAtMillis), then spentLabel — three Anonymous Pro texts in sequence. Because the category is content-width, the finish time's x-position shifts row by row with the length of words like STUDY vs DEEP WORK, and the spent figure shifts with both. In drawer.html (.srow) the same drift is visible: no two rows share a time axis, so the one screen whose entire job is reading history comparatively forces the eye to re-find the time on every line. Shield's routine row proves the app knows the cure — it reserves a fixed width(54.dp) time column (ShieldMatrixScreen.kt:668-672) — and applies it nowhere else.

Recommendation: Give StoredRow the routine row's discipline, on the app grid: category in a fixed 80.dp field (column 1), finish time right-aligned in the next 80.dp field, spent duration right-aligned in the last 80.dp field, title above spanning all three. Apply the identical three fields to deflection rows on the receipt and to completed rows in the Sequencer, so a time read in the Drawer sits at the same x as a time read anywhere else in the app.

#### [HIGH] Receipt deflection list uses equal row spacing for unequal time gaps — the ink's position encodes nothing and quietly lies about when urges clustered

ReceiptSheet.kt:139-144 renders each deflection as an identical ReceiptMonoLine ("HH:mm · AppName") in a Column with Arrangement.spacedBy(8.dp) (ReceiptSheet.kt:101): a deflection at 18:57 and one at 19:11 sit exactly the same distance apart as ones at 19:11 and 19:26, and would sit the same distance apart if they were 90 minutes apart. The underlying data is fully temporal — ReceiptState.kt:153 carries deflections with atWallMillis, and the slip itself prints armWallMs/endedAtWallMs (ReceiptState.kt:140-141) — so session position is computable, yet the only channel that could show clustering, escalation or a late-session collapse (vertical position) is spent on uniform text leading. The reader must parse and subtract timestamps to learn the one thing this list exists to show.

Recommendation: Replace the deflection text list with one proportional timeline strip on the slip: a hairline from ARMED to ENDED, one tick per deflection placed at (atWallMillis − armWallMs) / (endedAtWallMs − armWallMs), ticks stacked in two rows when they collide, app names labelled only for the first, last and any repeat offender. Keep the strip the full inner width of the slip so position is readable to the minute.

#### [HIGH] Routines — a 24-hour schedule drawn as isolated text rows, so overlaps, gaps and total daily coverage can never be seen

RoutineEntity stores a pure timetable: startMinutes, endMinutes, daysMask (MonolithModels.kt:549-562), with cross-midnight spans handled arithmetically in RoutineSchedule.durationMinutes (MonolithModels.kt:575-584). ShieldMatrixScreen.kt:328-335 renders each routine as an independent RoutineRow of text (the shield.html render shows '05:00 → 08:00 FASTED BLOCK', '09:00 → 19:30 DAY BLOCKS', '20:00 → 03:30 SLEEP' as three unrelated lines). Nothing anywhere places these spans on a common 24-hour scale: that the three seeded routines tile roughly 21 of 24 hours, where the uncovered gaps fall, and whether two routines collide is computable from the rows but invisible on screen — the user edits ±30-minute steppers (ShieldMatrixScreen.kt:333-334) blind to the collision they may be creating.

Recommendation: Draw one 24-hour timetable strip per routine on a shared scale at the head of the ROUTINES section: horizontal bars from startMinutes to endMinutes (wrapping past 24:00 for SLEEP), stacked as small multiples with a single shared hour axis (00/06/12/18/24) printed once, overlapping regions shown in the accent, and the uncovered remainder left as bare axis. Keep the text rows below for editing; the strip is read-only and updates with every ±30 tap.

#### [HIGH] Per-app usage and limit are measured, reconciled and stored — then never inked: every Shield row spends identical ink regardless of the app's actual behaviour

BlockedAppEntity carries todayUsageMinutes and dailyLimitMinutes per app (MonolithModels.kt:239-240), and AppCatalogReconcile.kt:100-109 continuously rewrites todayUsageMinutes from real UsageStats figures.
