No UI file reads either field (grep across ui/ returns zero usages): the Shield render shows each app as a name, a tier word (SHUT/PEEK/OPEN) and a long dotted leader — an app used 4 minutes and an app used 240 minutes against a 30-minute limit receive byte-identical visual weight. The two numbers that would tell the user which rules are load-bearing and which are decoration exist in the database and reach no surface in any form, not even as numerals.

Recommendation: Add a word-sized sparkbar to each Shield app row: a thin bar whose length is todayUsageMinutes on a scale shared by all rows, with a single tick at dailyLimitMinutes; usage past the tick prints in the accent. Sort the YOUR RULES section by usage descending so ink order follows data magnitude. No new screen, no chart page — the bar lives inside the existing row at the height of the tier word.

#### [HIGH] TowerStreakView is near-pure chartjunk: a card, header, floor labels and up to 56 brick rectangles triple-encode a single integer that is also printed twice as a numeral

TowerStreakView (BlockitTowerFadersAndCatalogViews.kt:26-160) takes exactly one datum, totalBricksCount: Int (line 31), and spends on it: a rounded card fill and hairline, the header 'STREAK TOWER • 7 BRICKS / FLOOR', an 'FL 03' floor readout, an '19 BRICKS' numeral, F01–F08 floor labels, and 7×up-to-8 brick/ghost rectangles — the count is encoded three times (brick glyphs, floor number, brick numeral) while ghost slots ink non-existent future bricks in the same geometry as real ones. The file even imports DailyFocusStat (line 9) — the per-day minutes/interceptions structure that could have given the view real data to draw — and the tower never uses it. Data-ink ratio approaches zero: erase every brick and the two numerals still carry the entire information content.

Recommendation: Cut the card, the header line, the floor labels and all ghost slots. If the tower metaphor stays, draw laid bricks only, one unbordered row, no floor scaffolding, and drop both redundant numerals (keep one small count at the row's end). Better: spend the reclaimed area on the imported-but-unused data — seven day cells sized by DailyFocusStat.totalMinutes with interceptionsCount as a tick count beneath each, so the space the monument occupied becomes a week of actual data.

#### [HIGH] Every routine window must be ATTENDED or be branded MISSED forever — immutable stamps leave no judgement for a deliberately absent day

RoutineDerive.kt:53 defines WindowJudgement { ATTENDED, PARTIAL, MISSED, HELD, LATE_FIRE, NOT_DELIVERED, UNKNOWN } — UNKNOWN is explicitly reserved for the unprovable, never for the chosen — and MonolithModels.kt:313-314 states the resulting routineOutcome stamp is written once and 'Stamps are immutable.' A window the user simply did not live up to is therefore branded MISSED permanently in the record; the app acts as the internalised overseer Han describes, one that never forgets and never forgives, so the user exploits himself against an archive that cannot soften.

Recommendation: Give judgement a half-life in the Drawer: routine verdicts print only for the current week; older windows in DrawerScreen render as plain session rows with the verdict word removed, and MISSED stamps older than 7 days are excluded from every count and summary. The record keeps what happened; it stops keeping the grade forever.

#### [HIGH] Roughness is designed out: a human life must be declared in exactly three words — REST, ILL or FAMILY

DayWordStore.kt:54 closes a life to three words — val WORDS: List<String> = listOf("REST", "ILL", "FAMILY") — and DayWordStore.kt:17-18 states the exclusion as doctrine: 'The word list is closed by construction: REST, ILL, FAMILY — never TEST.' put() silently refuses any other word. In the drawer.html render every day is then filed identically: same 11px heading, same hairline, same row rhythm, whether it was a triumph, a funeral or an exam. Alexander's roughness is not decoration; it is the trace of local circumstance adapting a pattern. Monolith applies its patterns so uniformly that the user's actual, irregular day cannot leave a mark in their own language — the system would rather a day go undeclared than be named inaccurately.

Recommendation: Open the Drawer day heading to authored roughness: allow one free-text day word (up to ~12 characters, stored via the existing DayWordStore.put path alongside the three presets, which remain as quick picks), printed in the same Anonymous Pro heading beside the date. Keep the refusal only for an empty word. A pattern language lives when its users can bend a pattern to their ground; a closed three-word lexicon is a form to fill in, not a language.

#### [HIGH] A missed day renders as nothing: the Drawer deletes the break from the visible history instead of outlining it

design-renders/drawer.html states a day with no stored rows and no declared word 'renders NOTHING in the Drawer — no heading, no missed mark'; DrawerScreen.kt:60-61 enshrines this ('not a dashboard, report card or attendance book: no totals, no streaks…'), and RoutineDerive.kt WindowJudgement MISSED stamps exist in data but buildDayGroups in DrawerScreen.kt groups only completed FocusTaskEntity rows and day words, so a judged MISSED day has no visual existence at all.

Recommendation: Render every judged MISSED/PARTIAL day in the Drawer as a hollow day-group: date heading, an empty ruled row, and a single accent crack-line with the word 'MISSED — [routine name]' or the declared day word joined to it. Absence gets an outline and a seam; the month reads as a continuous vessel with visible repairs, not a history with holes silently removed.

#### [HIGH] The plan-versus-reality smudge is deliberately erased: estimate and spent print as strangers

DrawerScreen.kt:266-267, detail view: 'Estimate and actual as two separate plain facts — never a delta, never a percentage.' ESTIMATE and SPENT print as two unconnected lines in identical type, and StoredRow (DrawerScreen.kt:883-886) omits the estimate from the list entirely ('No estimate, no checkbox, no bar, no rank'). A task estimated at 20 minutes that actually took 2H 10M — the single most honest, weathered fact about that day — reads in the Drawer exactly like a task that landed on its estimate.

Recommendation: In the Drawer detail, join the two facts on one line in words, never numbers-as-grade: 'ESTIMATE 30 MIN — SPENT 1H 20M · RAN LONG' / '· FINISHED EARLY' / '· AS PLANNED', and in StoredRow add the estimate to the meta line only when spent deviates from it by more than half. No percentage, no colour coding, no calibration score — just the deviation named, so the smudge stays in the record where the user can see their own days honestly.

#### [HIGH] Every stored day is ironed to the same perfect grid: 45 seconds and 2 hours wear identical rows

StoredRow (DrawerScreen.kt:886 onwards) gives every stored task the identical treatment — 14sp Medium title, three 10.5sp mono meta items, 6dp padding, 1dp divider — whether spentLabel() returns '45 SEC' or '2H 10M'. The drawer.html render confirms it on screen: a 24-minute draft and a 2H 10M revision are indistinguishable at a glance; a month can only be audited line by line, never apprehended as a shape. Wabi-sabi's fukinsei (irregularity) and its insistence that objects be met by eye and hand are both refused: the one variable that makes a day irregular — how long things actually took — is flattened to one mono string among three.

Recommendation: Give each StoredRow one proportional, non-numeric mark: the divider under the row becomes a duration groove whose length scales with actualSecondsSpent (log-scaled, capped at full width for 2H+), drawn in the existing outlineVariant ink. No bar chart, no axis, no totals — a month then shows its grain at a glance: long grooves for the days that sat deep, hairlines for the days that barely touched, exactly the irregular surface the record currently irons flat.

#### [HIGH] Building is blind: the builder never shows the maker their own attention as material

The app records exactly the grain a maker needs and hides it at the bench. BlockedAppEntity carries interceptCount (MonolithModels.kt:240), incremented on every deflection (MonolithDao.kt:40), plus todayUsageMinutes — yet CatalogueAppRow (ShieldMatrixScreen.kt:1060) passes only appName and currentTier to the sled view, and SlipLineRow (line 968) prints only the app name and its SHUT/PEEK word. The sole consumer of interceptCount is an aggregate sum for a session total (MonolithViewModel.kt:527). Mari's exercise worked because making revealed the structural reasoning of the object; here the user re-tiers apps with no idea which ones they actually reach for, how often, or whether last week's ruling changed anything.

Recommendation: Print the grain on the building surface: each YOUR RULES slip line and catalogue row gains a right-hand mono column — reaches this week, peeks taken, last deflection day (e.g. 'INSTAGRAM ····· SHUT · 14 REACHES / 2 PEEKS'). Sort the catalogue's default order by reaches descending so the material that matters is at the top of the bench, and after a loadout has governed for a week, mark the lines it changed on the slip so revision starts from lived evidence, not memory.

#### [MEDIUM] A month of history and a cabinet of objects are both flattened into a phone list on a tablet

DrawerScreen.kt:511 renders the whole archive as a single LazyColumn of day headings and stored rows, and the Cabinet branch renders the six curios as a single vertical list (drawer.html frames 1-2: one narrow column, void on both sides at any width above phone). A month of study history — dates, day words (REST/ILL/FAMILY), minutes per day — is intrinsically calendar-shaped data, and the Cabinet's own metaphor is a physical shelf of objects; on a tablet both are flattened into a phone feed. Material 3's Feed canonical layout (single column becoming a multi-column grid as width grows) and YPT's tablet bookshelf/folder surface both give peer items spatial arrangement on large screens instead of a longer scroll.

Recommendation: At expanded width, Drawer landing becomes a month grid: 7-column calendar cells, each cell printing the day word, total focused time and a brick-height bar proportional to minutes, with the existing list preserved below 840dp and as the cell's tap-through detail. The Cabinet becomes a 3-column shelf grid — each curio in its own bordered cell at print-catalogue size with serial, name and subtitle — so 'cabinet' reads as furniture, not a menu. Both reuse existing drawerRows/dayWords data; only arrangement changes.

#### [MEDIUM] The Tower's bricks have no coursing, no mortar and no weight: masonry drawn as rounded spreadsheet tiles

A brick wall convinces because of its bond: courses offset by half a brick so no vertical joint runs continuous, mortar recessed between units, each unit sharp-cornered and visibly bearing on the one below. TowerStreakView draws the opposite (BlockitTowerFadersAndCatalogViews.kt:95-140): bricks computed as (area − 6 gaps)/7 identical columns with a uniform 4dp gap on every side, every row aligned to the same x positions (bLeft = brickAreaLeft + col*(brickW+gap), :112), and every unit — laid, ghost and crown alike — drawn with drawRoundRect at 4dp radius (:119, :131, :140). Continuous vertical joints, floating rounded lozenges, no bed, no bearing: it reads as a calendar grid wearing brick colours, and the crown brick in accent hovers in the same grid instead of capping a wall.

Recommendation: Re-lay the tower as masonry: bricks to 0dp corners; offset alternate courses by half a brick width (6 bricks + 2 half-bricks at the ends) so no vertical joint aligns with the course above or below; replace the uniform 4dp outline gap with a 2dp recess joint in the recess token, and give the bottom course a full-width foundation course twice as tall in ink. The crown brick keeps the accent but sits ON the top course with no gap beneath it — weight, visibly transferred.

### The receipt and artifacts — 55 findings (19 critical, 30 high, 6 medium, 0 low)

#### [CRITICAL] The kept artifact is anonymous: the slip never prints its own maker's name

ReceiptSheet.kt:83-110 — the slip's header Row contains only the session intention (Atkinson Bold 15sp) and receipt.numberPrint; the word MONOLITH, a logotype, or any issuer mark appears nowhere in ReceiptSheet.kt. receipt.html Frame 1 confirms it visually: the slip opens 'Revise thermodynamics / № 048' with no masthead, and its only accent-free greys (#2C2A29, #5F5856 on #FAF6F0) could belong to any app. The brand orange used elsewhere in the same render set (launcher #F55314, Deck accent cap #F47442) never touches the slip.

Recommendation: Give the slip a printed masthead as its first line: 'MONOLITH' in Anonymous Pro Bold tracked 2sp at the left, the № at the right on the same baseline, and a single small seal mark — a filled orange square/dot in the existing accent — punched beside the number on every slip, clean or faulted. Same masthead, same position, every issue: that repetition is what turns numbered slips into a recognisable series.

#### [CRITICAL] The slip is anonymous: a friend seeing it cannot tell what made it, so the ritual sells nothing

ReceiptSheet.kt contains no brand text at all: the header row is receipt.title at 15sp (ReceiptSheet.kt:92) opposite receipt.numberPrint '№ 048' (ReceiptSheet.kt:104, ReceiptState.kt:189), and every following line is times, counts or the footer. design-renders/receipt.html Frame 1 confirms visually: the slip reads 'Revise thermodynamics / № 048 / ARMED… / HELD…' with the word MONOLITH nowhere on it. Strava's share sticker, by contrast, closes every shared activity with its logo after distance, elevation and time, so the artefact advertises its maker wherever it lands.

Recommendation: Give the slip a fixed masthead that no session data can displace: top line 'MONOLITH' in Anonymous Pro Bold 10sp tracked 2sp (the Deck header treatment) left, № right, with the intention demoted to the second line. On any exported/shared variant, lock this masthead plus the accent in place, following Strava's sticker rule that the logo is the last, non-removable element of the composition.

#### [CRITICAL] No hero number and a flat 11sp hierarchy: the achievement is illegible at the size a friend actually sees it

ReceiptState.kt:176 stores sealedElapsedSeconds, but ReceiptSheet.kt never renders it — grep confirms zero occurrences in the sheet. Instead title is 15sp (ReceiptSheet.kt:92) and every fact line is the same ReceiptMonoLine at 11sp Anonymous Pro, 1sp tracking (ReceiptSheet.kt:188-193). receipt.html Frame 1 shows the result: five visually identical mono lines, no focal point. Strava's Sticker Stats and Nike Run Club share cards invert this: one metric (distance/time) is set an order of magnitude larger than the supporting stats, legible in a Stories thumbnail.

Recommendation: Promote elapsed time to the slip's hero: set the actual elapsed span (e.g. '50 MIN') in Sora Bold at 44-56sp centred under the masthead, demote ARMED/ENDED/HELD to the existing 11sp mono as supporting lines. Test the composition at 120px wide — the size it appears in a WhatsApp/Instagram feed — and require the hero number and masthead to survive that reduction alone.

#### [CRITICAL] Failure is designed as erasure: a broken session gets no artifact at all, and the machine-faulted slip deletes the user's own title

data/ReceiptState.kt:40-42 — VALVE_BROKE is specified in code as 'the session BROKE. No receipt, no №, ever'; ReceiptState.kt:86 — 'MISSED / LATE_FIRE are never an E0', so a missed routine day also publishes nothing. When the app itself fails, ui/components/ReceiptSheet.kt:86-96 renders an empty Box where the session's title/intention was (the F-W1 rule: the faulted sheet carries NO title) and its only receipt-only line (ReceiptSheet.kt:158-168) is the machine's self-report 'SHIELD — STILL BLOCKED (SERVICE DIDN'T STOP)'. Success gets a numbered, sealed artifact; the two worst outcomes get deletion — of the slip, or of the user's own words on it. Forest does the opposite: a failed session produces its most permanent artifact, a withered tree that stays in the forest forever with its identity intact, so failure is witnessed, named and kept rather than annulled.

Recommendation: Give every terminal outcome a slip. A valve-broken session issues a 'BROKEN' receipt: same numbered slip, title kept, elapsed-before-break printed, stamped with the TokenAlert tone — an artifact the user can look at, not a void. A faulted slip keeps the user's intention as its title and moves the machine's fault to a subordinate line worded as the machine's failure ('WE LOST THE SHIELD AT 19:11'), following Forest's rule that the failed attempt retains its name, date and duration on the permanent record.

#### [CRITICAL] The week never closes, so it can never be an edition: the only weekly computation is a rolling 7-day window ending today, not a sealed Mon–Sun letter

MonolithRepository.kt:2377 compute7DayHistory loops 'for (daysAgo in 6 downTo 0)' from today — the window slides daily, so yesterday's 'week' and today's 'week' are different documents and neither is ever finished, dated as a range, or numbered. A second, incompatible week already exists for the emergency token (MonolithWeek.kt:28 weekAnchorMillis, Monday-anchored), and Monolith already knows how to mint a sealed, numbered edition for a single session (ReceiptState.kt:189 numberPrint = '№ ' + padStart(3); receipt.html Frame 1 prints '№ 048') — the week gets none of that machinery. Fitbit's Weekly Progress Report does the opposite design decision: a closed Monday–Sunday period, a dateline in the greeting ('Hi, [name]! Here are your stats for Mar 2 – Mar 8'), delivered after the week seals.

Recommendation: Make the week a sealed edition on the existing MonolithWeek Monday anchor: at Monday 00:00, close the prior week, mint it the next number from the same sequence family as receipts, and file it in the Drawer under a masthead set in the receipt's own discipline — 'WEEK № 014 · 26 OCT – 1 NOV' (Anonymous Pro 11sp tracked, as ReceiptSheet.kt's mono lines) above an Atkinson title naming the week's main intention. The rolling 6-downTo-0 window stays as an internal stat, never as the presented record.

#### [CRITICAL] Receipt № 100 is typeset identically to № 001 — the app's only longitudinal counter is designed to hide its own milestones

ReceiptState.kt:189 formats every count the same way ('№ ' + number.padStart(3,'0')), and ReceiptSheet.kt:97-109 prints it at a fixed Anonymous Pro Bold 13sp in onSurfaceVariant grey, top-right of the slip. receipt.html frame 1 shows № 048 as a quiet filing mark beside the title — № 007 (day ~7), № 030 and № 100 render byte-identically: same size, weight, colour, position, same 11sp mono ARMED/ENDED lines below, same 9sp footer. The counter that could carry anniversaries is deliberately styled as an invoice number, so crossing a power of ten produces zero typographic event.

Recommendation: Give threshold receipts a variant slip inside Monolith's own language, following Duolingo's streak-milestone redesign (one week / one month / 100 / 365 get a transformed Fire Duo plus a share card, per Duolingo's own design post) and Apple's 10th-anniversary Activity award (same rings badge, but gold-bordered and limited-edition). At № 007, 030, 100 and 365: promote the № to the Deck's hero scale (Sora Bold, ~48sp) at the slip head, add one mono line naming the threshold ('HUNDREDTH SEALED SESSION'), and edge the slip in the existing accent #F55314 instead of outlineVariant. Sessions 1-99 keep today's slip untouched — restraint is what makes the variant read as an anniversary.

#### [CRITICAL] The witness verdict is a tautology in code: ENDED · ENDED tells a teacher nothing she can attest

receipt.html Frame 1 prints 'ENDED 19:32 · ENDED' as the verdict line. ReceiptSheet.kt:124-129 composes 'ENDED ${hhmm} · ${receipt.outcomeWord}'; MonolithRepository.kt:1683-1690 maps the outcome vocabulary to ENDED / ATTENDED / PARTIAL / SLEPT THROUGH / FLOW ENDED / ENDED · SHIELD GAP — all insider tokens, none a sentence a non-user can attest. Opal's school programme (apk-re/opal/EVIDENCE.md §10.3) does the opposite: the mandatory policy states in plain words 'Your school receives a daily report for compliance' and the Sick Day Pass reason is text 'Your school will be able to read this'.

Recommendation: Add a witness verdict line as the slip's largest line, in plain second-person English following Opal's school copy: e.g. 'Focused for 50 minutes, 18:42-19:32. Nothing was unblocked early.' / for PARTIAL: 'Focused for 22 of 50 planned minutes, then ended early.' Keep the coded outcomeWord as the small mono sub-line for the owner; the witness sentence, date and planned-vs-done duration become the attestable headline.

#### [CRITICAL] A proof with no author: the slip carries no masthead, no sender and no addressee, so forwarded it is an anonymous scrap

receipt.html frame 1 shows the slip opening cold on 'Revise thermodynamics / № 048' with no brand, name or addressee. ReceiptSheet.kt:89-115 renders exactly two header elements — the intention title (15sp Atkinson Bold) and numberPrint (13sp mono, onSurfaceVariant grey) — and the word MONOLITH appears nowhere in ReceiptSheet.kt. ReceiptState.kt:166-187 defines the slip's whole content in 18 fields: session facts only, no owner, no sender, no recipient, no witness. hhmm() at ReceiptSheet.kt:190-191 prints bare HH:mm, so the forwarded image does not even carry a calendar date a recipient could place it by.

Recommendation: Give the slip a masthead designed for a second reader, following the printed-receipt and certificate convention (issuer name and date as the trust header, as on any shop receipt, and Strava's share sticker, which leads with the athlete's identity): a top block reading 'MONOLITH — FOCUS PROOF' in the 10sp tracked mono the Deck header already uses, a full date line ('FRI 30 OCT 2026'), and a sender line 'KEPT BY SARTHAK' set at arm time. The mono log stays below as the detail; the header is what makes the object attributable in a chat thread.

#### [CRITICAL] The receipt copies a till slip, not a letter: it has a serial number but no addressee, sender or stamp — so Monolith's one print artifact cannot carry a human connection even if it were sent

receipt.html Frame 1: the slip's complete grammar is title + '№ 048', 'ARMED 18:42 · PLANNED 50 MIN', 'ENDED', 'HELD 12 APPS · 3 SITES', deflection lines, and the 9sp footer. ReceiptSheet.kt:98-119 prints only title and receipt.numberPrint in the header row; ReceiptSheet.kt:176's footer reads 'THE MACHINE KEEPS ITS OWN LOG · YOUR STUDY RECORD LIVES IN YPT' — the one sentence about records directs the user to a different app. There is no TO, FROM, addressee field, stamp box or closing line anywhere in the composable. Slowly does the opposite with the same print vocabulary: every letter carries a collectible stamp, no photos and no real names, and delivery is deliberately delayed by distance (hours to days) so the artifact is correspondence, not a message.

Recommendation: Redesign the slip as a letter, not a till receipt, following Slowly: at ARM time the user names one pair recipient (a single stored name, no contacts graph); the slip gains a 'FOR — {name}' addressee line in the header opposite the №, a stamp box in the top-right corner filled by the session's forged curio, and one free Atkinson line above the footer for a closing sentence written at seal time. The letter is not sendable until the session ends — the delay is the design — and it exports as the slip image exactly as rendered. The YPT footer sentence is deleted; a record that must leave the app should leave as this letter.

#### [CRITICAL] Paper metaphor in name only: the slip is a 24dp-rounded Material bottom sheet wearing a receipt costume

receipt.html Frame 1 shows a full-width card floating on a grey ground, indistinguishable from any Material dialog. ReceiptSheet.kt:71-82: Box padding 12dp, BottomCenter, Column fillMaxWidth(), clip RoundedCornerShape(24.dp), background scheme.surfaceBright, border(1.dp, outlineVariant, RoundedCornerShape(24.dp)), verticalScroll. No masthead, no centred MONOLITH wordmark, no dashed/hairline rule between header, body and footer, no serrated or straight-cut edge, no paper grain or print texture anywhere in the file. Sections are separated only by Arrangement.spacedBy(8.dp) (ReceiptSheet.kt:83).

Recommendation: Rebuild the slip as paper, not a sheet: constrain it to a centred ~300dp column, square corners, a zigzag tear edge clipped along the bottom, a centred 'MONOLITH' masthead in Anonymous Pro bold over a dashed rule, dashed rules again above the deflections and above the footer, and 2dp of off-register ink offset on the №. Keep surfaceBright #FAF6F0 — it is the right paper tint — but stop rounding and floating it like a Material card.

#### [CRITICAL] The verdict has no stamp: the outcome word is a tautological suffix on the ENDED line, in the same 11sp mono as everything else

ReceiptSheet.kt:122-125 prints the verdict as a trailing fragment of a time line: "ENDED ${hhmm(...)} · ${receipt.outcomeWord}" in the same ReceiptMonoLine (11sp Anonymous Pro, letterSpacing 1.sp, ReceiptSheet.kt:188-196) as every other fact — receipt.html Frame 1 renders it literally as 'ENDED 19:32 · ENDED'. The two exceptional verdicts get no more: shieldWasOff (ReceiptSheet.kt:146-155) and faulted (ReceiptSheet.kt:156-166) are 12sp Atkinson Bold paragraphs in onBackground black. The app's single accent, TokenColorPrimaryContainer #F55314 (ui/theme/Color.kt:18, night #F47442 at :39), never appears on the slip at all.

Recommendation: Give the verdict a physical stamp, following the rubber 'PAID' stamp on paper invoices and the rotated entry stamp in a passport: the outcome word alone, Anonymous Pro Bold ~20sp, inside a double-rule rectangular border, rotated -7 degrees, printed in #F55314, overlapping the slip's right edge below the ARMED line. ELAPSED_CLEAN-class outcomes get the orange stamp; ELAPSED_SHIELD_GAP gets the alert tone #D63E06 (Color.kt:29) and the words 'SHIELD GAP'. Delete the outcome word from the ENDED line — the time line keeps the time, the stamp carries the judgement.

#### [CRITICAL] The receipt is a form with no form grid: label and value are fused into single strings, so its proof can never be scanned by column

Müller-Brockmann's form design separates field label from field entry so a document reads down columns. ReceiptSheet.kt does the opposite: every fact is one concatenated Text — ReceiptMonoLine("ARMED ${hhmm(...)} · PLANNED ${longSpan(...)}") at ReceiptSheet.kt:116, "ENDED ... · ${outcomeWord}" at :123, deflections as "${hhmm(...)} · ${appName}" at :140 — rendered by a ReceiptMonoLine that is a bare Text (ReceiptSheet.kt:188-196) inside a Column spacedBy(8.dp) padded 20.dp inside a 12.dp scrim (ReceiptSheet.kt:71,81,83). The position of every value therefore depends on the length of the text before it: PLANNED moves with the ARMED time's digits, the outcome word moves with the ENDED time. receipt.html shows the result — a paragraph wearing a mono font, not a tabulated slip.

Recommendation: Rebuild the slip as a two-field form on the grid: a 80.dp label column (ARMED / ENDED / HELD / BREAK BANKED, Anonymous Pro 10.sp, tracked 2.sp) and a value field spanning columns 2-4, each row exactly 22.dp high (one row unit), rules between sections at field boundaries not at 8.dp gaps. Deflections become three fields — time in the label column, app name in columns 2-3, outcome in column 4 right-aligned — so a reader can scan the time column or the outcome column straight down the slip without reading a single word in between.

#### [CRITICAL] The receipt is filled end-to-end with the machine's account of the session and signed as the machine's property — no part of the slip is left receptive to the user

ReceiptSheet.kt:124 prints 'ENDED {time} · {outcomeWord}', :131 'HELD n APPS · n SITES', :140-143 enumerates every deflection as '{time} · {appName}', and :175-176 closes with 'THE MACHINE KEEPS ITS OWN LOG · YOUR STUDY RECORD LIVES IN YPT'. ReceiptState.kt:13-16 states the contract proudly: 'What persists is exactly a number, a pointer, an outcome word. The slip itself is re-derived from the session row.' The receipt.html render confirms the lived surface: title, № 048, ARMED/PLANNED, ENDED, HELD, three timestamped temptation rows, footer — no blank line, no unprinted space anywhere on the slip.

Recommendation: Redraw the slip as a vessel, not a log: keep only the user's title, the №, and ARMED–ENDED on the printed face. Delete the deflection enumeration and the HELD counts from the slip (leave them one tap away in the Drawer, on demand), delete the footer sentence entirely, and leave the lower half of the card as unprinted surfaceBright white — one faint ruled line and nothing else — so the last thing the session produces is room, not a verdict.

#### [CRITICAL] The receipt's verdict line says the same word twice: 'ENDED 19:32 · ENDED' — a label that reports an event, not a judgement

MonolithRepository.kt:1683-1689 receiptOutcomeWord() returns single-word verdicts ("ATTENDED", "PARTIAL", "FLOW ENDED", "ENDED"); ReceiptSheet.kt:124 prints "ENDED ${hhmm(endedAtWallMs)} · ${receipt.outcomeWord}", so an ordinary clean finish renders literally 'ENDED 19:32 · ENDED' (confirmed in design-renders/receipt.html frame 1). The stored vocabulary underneath is database codes — ReceiptState.kt:28-49 ELAPSED_CLEAN, ELAPSED_SHIELD_GAP, VALVE_BROKE, GRACE_CANCEL — and the slip's whole text is five telegram lines: 'ARMED 18:42 · PLANNED 50 MIN / ENDED 19:32 · ENDED / HELD 12 APPS · 3 SITES'. No line on the app's only keepsake artifact is a sentence addressed to the person who just spent fifty minutes inside it.

Recommendation: Abolish the outcomeWord slot and compose one complete sentence per finish kind from facts the slip already carries (intention, planned vs elapsed, held counts, deflections). Clean: 'You said you would revise thermodynamics for fifty minutes, and you did.' Shield gap: 'The shield was off for part of this session, so this record is incomplete.' Partial: 'You were here for 22 of the window's 50 minutes.' Set the sentence in Atkinson 13sp sentence case as the slip's second line, under the title; keep the mono timetable lines below it as the label's small print.

#### [CRITICAL] The sessions that most need a sentence get no label at all: a broken or early-ended session receives silence instead of a verdict

ReceiptState.kt:40-49 defines VALVE_BROKE ('The 60s valve was held to completion: the token was spent and the session BROKE. No receipt, no №, ever.'), GRACE_CANCEL and ENDED_EARLY, but finishKindOf (ReceiptState.kt:90-107) admits only ELAPSED_CLEAN, ELAPSED_SHIELD_GAP, STOPWATCH_ENDED, ATTENDED and PARTIAL — every failure ending is excluded from publication. The app writes its most careful prose for successes it barely needs to explain, and for the moment the user surrendered, panicked or gave up it prints nothing at all: no slip, no sentence, no record of what happened or when.

Recommendation: Issue an unnumbered slip for VALVE_BROKE and ENDED_EARLY sessions whose entire body is one sentence built from the stored outcomeReason and elapsed span: 'You opened the emergency break at 19:04, twenty-eight minutes in; the session ended there.' No №, no HELD counts, no deflection list — the plainness is the label. Route GRACE_CANCEL to a single Deck sentence ('You changed your mind inside the first minute; nothing was booked.') instead of the current void.

#### [CRITICAL] Rest is booked as capital: breaks are 'banked', priced into the plan total, and even the emergency valve pays out in banked seconds

ReceiptSheet.kt:134-138 prints 'BREAK BANKED {seconds/60} MIN' on the receipt; AirlockAndDisarmOverlays.kt:800-801 instructs the user mid-crisis: 'Every 15 seconds banks. If your hand slips, what isn't banked drains away. The banked part stays.'; TactileDeckScreen.kt:325 and :636-638 price the inter-block breaks into the plan's total span before the session starts ('breaks priced in'). No pause in the product exists that is not denominated in minutes and carried forward as an asset — Han's exact mechanism by which the achievement-subject never rests, because recovery has been reclassified as production.

Recommendation: De-monetise rest: delete the BREAK BANKED line from ReceiptSheet (a break prints as the word 'A BREAK WAS TAKEN' with no duration, or prints nothing), rewrite the valve copy at AirlockAndDisarmOverlays.kt:801 to drop banking entirely ('Hold for 60 seconds. Nothing is kept or lost.'), and stop pricing breaks into the Deck's TOTAL span — show block time and let the gaps be uncounted.

#### [CRITICAL] The emergency break is erased, not mended: VALVE_BROKE is the only ending with no receipt, no number, no record

ReceiptState.kt:40-41 defines VALVE_BROKE as 'the token was spent and the session BROKE. No receipt, no №, ever.'; finishKindOf at ReceiptState.kt:86-101 returns no finish kind for it, so the one session where the user was in genuine distress leaves zero artifact in Drawer or receipt history.

Recommendation: Issue the valve session a numbered MENDED receipt in ReceiptSheet.kt: keep its №, print 'HELD 38 MIN · BROKE FOR [reason]' and minutes held before the break, and draw its top border as a 2dp accent seam line (#F55314 / night #F47442) instead of the 1dp outlineVariant — the break becomes the most decorated slip the app prints, not an unnumbered deletion.

#### [CRITICAL] The second before the receipt is variable dead air filled with knocks, not a held pause: detention lasts 1480-1800ms depending on a shield-stop race

data/ReceiptState.kt:201-213 Detention: HELD_FRAME_MS=1200, RECEIPT_FLOOR_MS=1480, RECEIPT_CEILING_MS=1800, receiptAtMs = min(max(1480, rackStart+280), 1800) where rackStart depends on when MonolithShieldService.instance reads null. ui/MonolithViewModel.kt:1248-1260 fills the wait with scheduled sound: seat knock at E0, completion pulse at E700, knock pair at E880+90ms. ui/screens/TactileDeckScreen.kt:274-275,304-312 heldFinish freezes displaySeconds at the last count (receipt.html frame 3 renders it as hero 00:00). The interval's length is therefore decided by a service-stop race, and its content is three knocks over a corpse frame — neither fixed enough to be felt as rhythm nor empty enough to be rest.

Recommendation: Make detention a fixed, framed threshold on TactileDeckScreen: lock it to exactly 1600ms regardless of pawl-lift timing (engineering confirmation continues invisibly underneath). At E0 fade the hero ghosts and the strip to 40% and clear the slide's 'SLIDE OR TAP TO START' words, leaving one line in 10sp Anonymous Pro: 'HELD'. Remove the E700 pulse and E880 knock pair from MonolithViewModel.kt:1248-1260 — one knock at E0, then silence. The receipt (ReceiptSheet.kt) fades in only after that silence completes, so the second before it reads as a held breath, not a loading stall.

#### [CRITICAL] Monolith publishes the user's attention bill to the minute and its own bill nowhere

ReceiptSheet.kt:120-146 publishes the user's bill in detail — ARMED/PLANNED, ENDED/outcome, 'HELD {n} APPS · {n} SITES' (:131), BREAK BANKED and one line per deflection (:139) — and DrawerScreen prints every stored task, estimate and spent time. No surface anywhere publishes Monolith's own bill: grep of app/src finds no count of Airlocks shown, digest opens, Deck visits, sounds played or seconds spent inside Monolith itself, and the receipt footer at ReceiptSheet.kt:176 even exports the record elsewhere ('YOUR STUDY RECORD LIVES IN YPT'). Simon's allocation problem is unsolvable if the filter's own price is invisible: the user can compare Instagram's cost, never Monolith's.

Recommendation: Add a self-cost line to ReceiptSheet under the HELD line, printed always: 'MONOLITH TOOK {n} INTERRUPTIONS · {m} SEC IN APP' derived from intercepts shown, digest/receipt dwell and Airlock displays for that session, and add the same total as a monthly row at the top of the Drawer landing. If Monolith took more attention than it held, the receipt must say so in the same mono type.

#### [HIGH] The slip has a dialog's body, not a receipt's: full-width, round-cornered, unterminated

ReceiptSheet.kt:66-82 — the slip is a fillMaxWidth Column with RoundedCornerShape(24.dp) on all four corners, a 1dp outlineVariant border, 20dp padding, settled at BottomCenter over a 0.12 black scrim with 12dp screen padding. receipt.html Frame 1 shows the result: a wide, soft-cornered card floating above the screen edge — visually identical in construction to any Material bottom sheet or dialog in the app.

Recommendation: Rebuild the slip as a slip: constrain it to a narrow centred column (~300dp, the on-screen analogue of an 80mm thermal roll), square corners at the top, a straight dashed tear rule directly above the footer, and a zigzag/perforated bottom edge instead of the 24dp radius. Dismissal should follow the metaphor — drag down to tear off — so the object's edges, width and exit all say 'printed strip', not 'dialog'.

#### [HIGH] Monospace without a ledger: no columns, no rules, no alignment for the mono to earn

ReceiptSheet.kt:190-199 — every fact prints through ReceiptMonoLine: Anonymous Pro 11sp with letterSpacing 1.sp, all lines flush-left in one column with uniform 8dp gaps (ReceiptSheet.kt:81). receipt.html Frame 1 shows ARMED, ENDED, HELD and the deflection lines as an undifferentiated text stack: no right-aligned value column, no hairline rule under the header or above the footer, no dot leaders — the 1sp tracking actively breaks the fixed-width alignment that is the entire reason to set a receipt in monospace.

Recommendation: Set the slip as a two-column ledger in the Swiss receipt manner: label flush-left, value flush-right in tabular mono with letterSpacing 0 so columns actually align; a 1dp rule under the masthead, a second above the deflection list, and a double rule above the footer. Drop the 1sp tracking on body lines — keep tracking only on the masthead. The data already arrives as label/value pairs (ARMED/time, HELD/counts, time/app); only the geometry is missing.

#### [HIGH] The verdict has no stamp: clean, gapped, partial and faulted slips wear the same ink

ReceiptSheet.kt:92-103 — on a faulted finish the title is replaced by an empty Box, so the most serious slip in the series has a blank header; ReceiptSheet.kt:150-167 — a shield-gap session and the fault line each print as one ordinary Atkinson Bold 12sp sentence in the same onBackground ink as everything else. receipt.html Frame 1's clean slip and a hypothetical gap/faulted slip are graphically indistinguishable at arm's length: same paper, same ink, same weight, no overstrike, no border stamp, no colour event.

Recommendation: Stamp the verdict like print does: the outcome word set as a bordered stamp — rectangular 1.5dp outline, slight rotation, in accent orange for ENDED and in a warning ink for SHIELD GAP / PARTIAL — placed over the header's right side, overlapping the rule. A faulted slip gets the stamp in place of the missing title, never a blank. A user flipping a stack of kept slips should sort clean from broken by silhouette alone, the way PAID and VOID sort a paper pile.

#### [HIGH] Failure is rendered by erasure, not transformation: the faulted receipt deletes its title and every other outcome reuses the clean slip pixel-for-pixel

ReceiptSheet.kt:50-51 and the faulted branch: the faulted sheet 'carries NO title' — failure is expressed by deleting the session's intention from the slip. receiptOutcomeWord (MonolithRepository.kt:1683-1688) otherwise swaps one word on an otherwise identical slip: 'ENDED' becomes 'ENDED · SHIELD GAP', 'ATTENDED' becomes 'PARTIAL', same #FAF6F0 paper, same 11sp mono, same ink. receipt.html Frame 1 shows the template every outcome shares. Forest expresses failure by transformation, not redaction: the same tree the user grew droops, desaturates and stays recognisably theirs — decay of a specific object. Monolith's failure aesthetic is a censored document: less information, same paper, no visible wound.

Recommendation: Design a withered state for the slip itself, following Forest's transform-don't-delete rule: keep the title (struck through once, in ink, if it must be marked), keep the number, and change the material — slip field drops from #FAF6F0 to the recessed #D8D1CB, the accent edge (per the clean treatment) appears cracked/omitted in segments, and deflections print in full ink instead of dim. A failed session should look like the same artefact, damaged — not like a form with its heading removed.

#### [HIGH] Repair order #5: the receipt is styled as a dismissible card, not a kept document — give it document geometry and one display-size number before building anything on it

receipt.html: the slip is surfaceBright #FAF6F0 with a 24dp radius and 20dp padding — the identical card chrome as the Deck's instrument card in deck.html — its title is 15sp Atkinson Bold (ReceiptSheet.kt:91-95), its serial 13sp mono (ReceiptSheet.kt:103-107), every fact line 11sp Anonymous Pro (ReceiptSheet.kt:190-194) and its footer 9sp (ReceiptSheet.kt:175-179). Nothing in its geometry, edge, rhythm or type says 'document that outlives the app session' rather than 'another card to dismiss'; elapsed time, the one number the slip exists to prove, gets no display tier at all.

Recommendation: Priority 5 — make the receipt a document before adding any share, export or history surface on top of it, following the paper-receipt convention Teenage Engineering and receipt-printer typography use: flat or perforated bottom edge instead of the shared 24dp card radius, tabular mono columns with right-aligned figures, the seal hash set as a colophon, and elapsed time promoted to a 28-32sp Sora hero — the only display-size number on the slip. This is last of the five, not first, because it depends on repairs #1 (a verdict hue) and #3 (a caption tier); but it outranks all new-feature design because the receipt is the sole artifact a user keeps, shows or screenshots — every future proof surface inherits whatever it looks like.

#### [HIGH] Receipt screenshot reads as a parking ticket: no elapsed time, no achievement verdict, and its footer sends the reader to another app

receipt.html frame 1: the slip's title is the task name and '№ 048', followed by three mono lines — 'ARMED 18:42 · PLANNED 50 MIN', 'ENDED 19:32 · ENDED', 'HELD 12 APPS · 3 SITES' (ReceiptSheet.kt:118,124,131) — and a 9sp footer, 'THE MACHINE KEEPS ITS OWN LOG · YOUR STUDY RECORD LIVES IN YPT' (ReceiptSheet.kt:176). The render caption notes the slip prints no elapsed-duration line at all, only wall-clock start/end and the planned span, and the outcome word in the shown clean finish is the tautology 'ENDED'. Screenshotted and sent to a friend, it carries no 'I did it', no big duration earned, no success colour or mark — and its last line directs the reader to a different app, YPT, for the actual record.

Recommendation: Make the slip pass the forwarded-screenshot test the way a race finisher's certificate or a Forest completed-tree card does — verdict first, evidence second: open with a Sora 28sp verdict line ('KEPT · 50 MIN') computed from elapsed time, demote ARMED/ENDED/HELD to the small mono evidence lines they are, and replace the YPT footer with 'MONOLITH · SESSION № 048 · 30 OCT' so the artifact is self-attributing when it leaves the phone. Keep the receipt-paper styling; give it a headline worth screenshotting.

#### [HIGH] Built as a bottom-anchored transient overlay, the slip's composition sabotages the screenshot that is its only exit

The slip is not a standalone canvas: it is a Column inside a full-screen Box with contentAlignment = BottomCenter, a black 0.12 scrim and 12dp padding (ReceiptSheet.kt:68-72), and the whole Box is clickable(onClick = onDismiss) (ReceiptSheet.kt:70) — it vanishes on the next tap anywhere. receipt.html Frame 1 shows the slip hard against the bottom edge, the dimmed Deck showing through above it. A manual screenshot — the only way this artefact can leave the phone — therefore captures a cropped, bottom-weighted overlay fragment floating on someone else's UI, with no top margin, no background of its own and no portrait proportion. Spotify Wrapped and Strava both render a dedicated off-screen share canvas at a fixed social aspect ratio instead of screenshotting the live UI.

Recommendation: Compose a second, dedicated share rendering of the same ReceiptState: a free-standing 4:5 portrait card on the app's own ground colour, 24dp safe margins on all sides, masthead top, hero centre, deflection summary (not the live overlay) bottom. Render it off-screen for export/screenshot so its framing never depends on the Deck behind it or on catching the overlay before a tap dismisses it.

#### [HIGH] Accent-less and genre-less: the 'receipt' reads as a generic Material sheet, not a tear-off artefact worth keeping

ReceiptSheet.kt:77-79 styles the slip with RoundedCornerShape(24.dp), surfaceBright #FAF6F0 and a 1dp outlineVariant border, using only onBackground/onSurfaceVariant text — the brand's single accent, hot orange #F55314 'spent rarely' (ui/theme/Color.kt:18), appears nowhere in the file. receipt.html Frame 1 shows a plain off-white rounded rectangle on a near-matching #E4DFDA ground: no perforated or zigzag tear edge, no barcode/stub line, no accent stripe — none of the visual cues that make a real thermal receipt (or Teenage Engineering's print artefacts) recognisable as a keepable slip, and no silhouette a feed scroller can identify at 100px the way Forest's green tree or Opal's purple gem is identified.

Recommendation: Make the artefact own a silhouette: give the slip a straight-cut body with a perforated/zigzag bottom edge, a dashed tear rule above the footer, and spend the single accent once — an orange seal/stamp block beside the №, echoing a rubber-stamped receipt. Keep the in-app sheet restrained, but the share rendering must carry that stamp at full saturation so the card is recognisable before any text is read.

#### [HIGH] The exam-season receipt stays a shop slip: no mark-sheet treatment, and its own footer outsources the student's record to YPT

design-renders/receipt.html frame 1: the slip prints the intention as a shop title ('Revise thermodynamics'), mono lines 'ARMED 18:42 · PLANNED 50 MIN', 'HELD 12 APPS · 3 SITES', deflection timestamps, and the footer 'THE MACHINE KEEPS ITS OWN LOG · YOUR STUDY RECORD LIVES IN YPT' (ui/components/ReceiptSheet.kt). In exam season — when a student sits three papers in a week and wants one artifact per paper — the receipt stays a generic till slip and even directs the user to a rival for their study record. Nothing on it resembles the one paper artifact every student already reads fluently: the mark sheet.

Recommendation: During exam season, print the receipt as a mark sheet, following the OCR exam-paper cover's 'For Examiner's Use Only' grid: a ruled table with one row per block (block number, subject code, deflections as deductions), dotted leaders like the Shield's own standing-orders slip already uses, and a double-ruled TOTAL box at the foot carrying attended time. Same slip, same mono, same № — re-ruled as an examiner's grid instead of a shop receipt, so a season of receipts reads as a results file.

#### [HIGH] The frozen frame freezes the wrong number: the detention hero is 00:00 remaining, never the elapsed time achieved

MonolithViewModel.kt FinishState: frozenDisplaySeconds for a timed finish = spanTargetSeconds − spanElapsedSeconds (the remaining count), so at a clean finish it is 0. TactileDeckScreen.kt:305-310 renders finishState.frozenDisplaySeconds as the hero through detention, and receipt.html Frame 3 shows the result: the detention portrait is literally '00:00' in 72sp Sora with its print ghosts. ReceiptState.kt PendingReceipt/ReceiptState carries sealedElapsedSeconds, but ReceiptSheet.kt never prints an elapsed line (render Frame 1: ARMED/ENDED wall times and PLANNED only), and the Deck never re-derives the hero from elapsed during the hold.

Recommendation: Flip the hero's tense at E0: at the finish, crossfade/count the readout from remaining 00:00 to the achieved total in the Deck's own span dialect (e.g. '50 MIN' at H2/H3 sizes, as the idle hero already prints totals in TactileDeckScreen.kt), and hold THAT through detention. Following Nike Run Club and Strava post-activity: the finish screen's hero number is the distance/time earned, never the zero that was left; the countdown reaching zero is the trigger, not the portrait.

#### [HIGH] The receipt slip is materially identical for a clean finish and a broken one — success is not made beautiful and failure is not made ugly on the one artifact meant to teach the difference

ReceiptSheet.kt:78 backgrounds every slip in the same scheme.surfaceBright porcelain with the same 24dp radius and hairline border, and line 124 prints the outcome as one more 11sp mono line, 'ENDED {time} · {outcomeWord}', in the same ink as ARMED and HELD. receipt.html frame 1 shows the result: title, three mono lines, three dim deflection lines (Instagram / YouTube / X printed as clean ledger entries in the same style as the totals), and a 9sp footer — no accent seal, no change of material, weight, colour or layout distinguishes this clean slip from a valve-broken or faulted one a user files in the Drawer.

Recommendation: Give the slip an outcome-dependent material, following Forest, whose completed session adds a living tree to a permanent forest while leaving early withers it — the artifact itself carries the reward and the loss. Clean finish: print an orange seal disc overlapping the slip's top edge with the elapsed time in Sora 28sp as the hero line. Broken/valve finish: print the slip in flat grey with a torn/perforated top edge, the outcome word in the orange — spent once, as a warning — and each deflection name struck through rather than listed as a purchase. The Drawer archive then teaches at a glance, without reading a word.

#### [HIGH] CLEAN is purity language and PARTIAL is punished with silence — an all-or-nothing identity that teaches collapse after a lapse

ReceiptState.kt:28-35 names the good outcome ELAPSED_CLEAN and its pair ELAPSED_SHIELD_GAP, commented 'the books are BROKEN'. ReceiptState.kt:110-117 finishPulses(): 'PARTIAL never pulses' and a shield-gap finish never pulses — partial effort gets no completion sound, no pulse, no celebration, by explicit rule. receipt.html Frame 1 shows the consequence: even the clean slip's outcome word is the flat 'ENDED', indistinguishable in weight from a compromised one, while the only emphasised extra lines are accusations: 'THE SHIELD WAS OFF FOR PART OF THAT SESSION' (ReceiptSheet.kt:147).

Recommendation: Kill purity language entirely, following the lapse-not-relapse copy standard in Smoke Free and Fabulous, which never call a day clean or dirty: rename ELAPSED_CLEAN → 'FULL SPAN', ELAPSED_SHIELD_GAP → 'SPAN WITH A GAP — 38 OF 50 MIN HELD', and give PARTIAL a pulse and its own receipt line stating the held fraction as the headline ('YOU HELD 31 OF 50 MIN'). Change finishPulses() so every published finish pulses, with partial pulsing softer rather than not at all — effort must be sonically acknowledged in proportion, not silenced.

#### [HIGH] Paper that isn't paper: a 24dp rounded Material card borrows the word 'receipt' and none of its visual grammar

The slip is a RoundedCornerShape(24.dp) card in surfaceBright with a 1dp outlineVariant border and 20dp padding (ui/components/ReceiptSheet.kt:77-85) — geometrically identical to the Deck's hero card, i.e. a Material bottom sheet wearing a receipt's name. Render receipt.html frame 1 confirms it at phone scale: floating rounded card, left-aligned ragged mono lines, no centred masthead, no columnar right-aligned figures, no dashed perforation rule, no serrated or torn edge, no barcode. Receiptify proved the opposite design decision is the whole product: it mimics a real store receipt faithfully (centred shop header, itemised rows, order number, fictional total, barcode) and that fidelity — not the data — is what millions screenshotted and posted. A thermal receipt is recognisable at thumbnail size from three cues alone (narrow column, perforated tear edge, barcode block); Monolith's slip has zero of the three, so at thumbnail size it reads as a settings dialog, and the one artefact the app produces carries none of the genre's instant legibility.

Recommendation: Re-draw the slip as paper, not as a card: square corners with a single serrated bottom edge (a zigzag Shape clipped along the foot, above the footer), a narrower centred column (~300dp) inside the sheet, a dashed perforation rule separating the deflection list from the footer, and a Code-39-style barcode block at the foot encoding the receipt № (the № already exists as data — ReceiptState.numberPrint, ReceiptSheet.kt:104). Keep the existing type and colours; only the silhouette, column and print furniture change. The test: squint at a screenshot — if it doesn't read 'receipt' in one second, it isn't one yet.

#### [HIGH] The receipt is a single-party slip with no witness column — the session closes unwitnessed and its footer outsources the record to YPT

ReceiptSheet.kt:56-176 composes a strictly single-party slip: one title, one number ('№ 048'), 'ARMED · PLANNED', 'ENDED · {outcomeWord}', 'HELD {n} APPS · {n} SITES', a deflection list of only the user's own lapses, and a footer that literally exports the social record elsewhere — 'THE MACHINE KEEPS ITS OWN LOG · YOUR STUDY RECORD LIVES IN YPT' (ReceiptSheet.kt:176; design-renders/receipt.html frame 1). There is no second name, no partner outcome column, no checkout exchange: the session ends by tapping a slip away, alone. Focusmate ends every session with a spoken checkout where each partner hears what the other accomplished, and a Forest Plant Together room ends with all members looking at the one forest they grew or killed together — closure is a witnessed act in both references.

Recommendation: Re-cut the slip as a perforated two-part receipt for paired sessions: the existing column keeps the user's ARMED/ENDED/HELD lines, and a second ruled column beside the deflections prints the witness's outcome in identical 11sp mono — 'A. · ENDED 19:32 · HELD CLEAN' or 'A. · BROKE 19:11' — so each user's receipt is the other's checkout, delivered as paper instead of speech. Replace the footer for paired slips with 'STRUCK TWICE · № 048 HELD BY A. AND S.' and retire the YPT footer on those slips: a record that was witnessed should say so on its face, not direct the user to a rival for the social half of the proof.

#### [HIGH] Nothing reads at thumbnail size: five equal-weight mono lines and no hero figure, so the proof fails the chat-glance test

receipt.html frame 1: every fact sits at one visual weight — title 15sp, all evidence lines 11sp Anonymous Pro tracked 1sp (ReceiptSheet.kt:195-204, ReceiptMonoLine), footer 9sp. ReceiptState.kt:176 stores sealedElapsedSeconds, yet ReceiptSheet.kt never reads it (zero references in the file): the single figure a recipient would grasp — how long you actually stayed — is not merely small, it is absent from the composition, so a viewer must mentally subtract ARMED 18:42 from ENDED 19:32. In a messaging thread the image renders at roughly 40% of phone width, where 9-11sp mono collapses into grey texture and nothing survives as a headline.

Recommendation: Compose a send-facing hierarchy on the Strava share-sticker model, whose layouts lead with one poster-scale stat (moving time) and demote everything else: elapsed duration as a 56-72sp Sora hero ('50 MIN KEPT') under the intention, outcome as a single plain word beneath it, and the existing 11sp mono lines kept as the fine-print verso. Test the layout at 160dp wide — if the hero and outcome do not read at that size, it is not a social object yet.

#### [HIGH] The slip's geometry cannot be captured: a variable-height, scrollable bottom sheet floating on a scrim is a dialog, not a sendable card

ReceiptSheet.kt:64-84 seats the slip at Alignment.BottomCenter inside a full-screen Box with a 0.12 black scrim over the live Deck, 12dp padding, uniform 24dp rounded corners and a 1dp outlineVariant border — Material bottom-sheet/dialog chrome, not a bounded card. ReceiptSheet.kt:85 attaches verticalScroll to the slip's Column, and ReceiptSheet.kt:154-159 appends one line per deflection, so the slip's height is unbounded and content-dependent: a screenshot either crops the temptation list mid-scroll or captures scrim and Deck around a floating sheet. There is no fixed canvas, no opaque self-contained ground, no margin the image owns.

Recommendation: Design a fixed-format proof card separate from the dismissal sheet, on the fixed-ratio discipline of Strava/Apple Fitness share cards (a locked 4:5 canvas that is identical for every session): opaque surfaceBright ground edge to edge, capped content (hero, outcome, HELD line, at most three deflections then '+ N MORE'), a perforated or double-rule top edge borrowed from real tear-off receipts to mark it as a kept artefact rather than a dialog. The in-app sheet can stay variable; the object that leaves must not.

#### [HIGH] Written by the machine about itself: no first-person line a sender can stand behind, and failure prints as a service error

Every line is the machine reporting on itself in the third person: 'HELD 12 APPS · 3 SITES', outcome vocabulary from MonolithRepository.kt:1683-1689 ('ENDED', 'PARTIAL', 'FLOW ENDED') yielding the tautology 'ENDED 19:32 · ENDED' visible in receipt.html frame 1, and a footer that speaks for the machine — 'THE MACHINE KEEPS ITS OWN LOG' (ReceiptSheet.kt:176-182). On the faulted branch the sender's voice disappears entirely: ReceiptSheet.kt:101-110 deletes the title and the only added line is a service error, 'SHIELD — STILL BLOCKED (SERVICE DIDN'T STOP)' (ReceiptSheet.kt:165-173). No line anywhere lets the human say, in first person, what they set out to do and whether they did it — the exact statement a recipient is being asked to believe.

Recommendation: Add a sender's declaration line in first person directly under the hero, on the Focusmate check-out model — where each partner states aloud what they worked on and reports whether they got through it, and is congratulated in return: e.g. 'I SAID: REVISE THERMODYNAMICS — I KEPT 50 MIN.' generated from intention + outcome, with the faulted variant owning the failure in the sender's voice ('I STOPPED EARLY — THE SHIELD HELD ANYWAY') instead of printing an IT error. Keep the mono machine log below the declaration as supporting evidence, not as the message.

#### [HIGH] No fixed canvas: a variable-height scrolling sheet cannot become an artifact — every screenshot crops it differently

ReceiptSheet.kt:76-82: the slip is fillMaxWidth() with verticalScroll, and ReceiptSheet.kt:139-144 appends one line per deflection with no cap in the composable — so slip height is a function of how often the user reached for Instagram. receipt.html Frame 1: even the short 3-deflection instance sits on a 0.12-alpha scrim (ReceiptSheet.kt:68) with the Deck showing through, so a screenshot captures background clutter, cropped text at the scroll fold, and no brand block. There is no fixed-size off-screen rendering of the slip anywhere in ReceiptSheet.kt or ReceiptState.kt.

Recommendation: Design a second, fixed artifact alongside the interactive sheet, the way Spotify Wrapped builds every card to a fixed Story ratio with bold type and its own colour field, and Strava exports a fixed sticker/card carrying moving time, distance and pace as hero stats: a 1080x1350 (4:5) canvas composited off-screen — paper slip centred on TokenColorBackground #E4DFDA, hero elapsed figure, №, orange outcome stamp, MONOLITH wordmark at the foot, deflections truncated to the top 5 plus a count. The sheet stays for reading; the fixed canvas is the thing that can leave the phone intact.

#### [HIGH] Numbering is minted then demoted: № 048 is set in footer-grey at 13sp with no barcode or serial treatment

ReceiptState.kt:189 carefully formats the number — '№ ' + zero-padded to 3, never truncated (№ 048 … № 1048) — then ReceiptSheet.kt:102-110 renders it at 13sp Anonymous Pro Bold in scheme.onSurfaceVariant, the same muted grey and near-weight as the 9sp footer (ReceiptSheet.kt:172-181). receipt.html Frame 1: the № reads as a page number in a document header, not as a serial. No barcode, bar pattern, check character or any other machine/print rendering of the number exists in ReceiptSheet.kt.

Recommendation: Promote the № into the masthead and give it a printed body, following a railway ticket's PNR block and a retail receipt's Code-39 footer barcode: set '№ 048' centred under the MONOLITH masthead at 15sp in onBackground, and beneath the footer render the number plus sealed elapsed seconds as a Compose-Canvas bar pattern (variable-width black bars, quiet zones at both ends) with the digits repeated in 9sp mono below it. It is a print-authenticity device, not a security claim — but it makes the serial feel issued, checkable and worth keeping.

#### [HIGH] Each earned curio arrives pre-filled with the app's own randomly assigned lore, so the artifact's meaning is occupied before the user's memory can enter it

MonolithModels.kt:811-848 gives each of the six curios a name, a subtitle and a pre-written line of lore ('Two waves of different pitch, drawn against each other until the line closes into a knot of light', 'A heavy brass pendulum over a bed of sand…'). MonolithRepository.kt:2050 chooses which one a finished session earns at random — CurioCatalog.artifacts.shuffled().first() — and DrawerScreen.kt:466-474 prints the subtitle and lore as the cabinet detail. The meaning of the object a user's session created is filled in advance by the app's poetry and assigned by lottery, so it can hold nothing of the session that earned it.

Recommendation: Cut the lore and subtitle fields from the cabinet detail entirely. Print only the artifact's name and form line, then the facts of the session that forged it — its title, date and span — and leave the rest of the detail sheet blank. An earned object should arrive empty so the user's memory of that session is what fills it; replace the app's random poetry with the user's own history and white space.

#### [HIGH] The receipt invites tearing off and filing, but the only gesture it accepts is tap-anywhere-and-it-vanishes

ReceiptSheet.kt:44-51 header comment: the slip 'never re-strikes, never animates its numbers, and dismisses on the next DOWN anywhere or on navigation'; :69-75 the full-screen Box carries .clickable(onClick = onDismiss) behind the slip. receipt.html render shows a paper slip (numbered 'No 048', ARMED/ENDED/HELD lines) presented as a settled sheet with no perforation, edge, handle or filing affordance.

Recommendation: Give the slip the receipt's own acts: print a perforated top edge on the slip, make a downward drag past 120dp tear it off with a single knock and file it into the Drawer where it remains re-openable, and make plain taps on the scrim inert while the slip is up. Remove tap-anywhere dismissal entirely — a record should leave by being filed, not by being brushed.

#### [HIGH] Receipt reveal is desynchronised theatre: the completion sound plays a second before the slip exists, and the slip then fades in silently, already seated

The finish's sounds and the receipt's appearance are scheduled on different clocks that never meet. MonolithViewModel.kt:1253 fires playCompletionPulse() at E700 and seat-knocks at E0/E880, while ReceiptState.kt:195-205 detains the receipt until E1480-E1800 — so the completion music plays to the frozen Deck roughly a second before there is anything to look at. When the slip finally arrives it arrives silently and motionlessly: ReceiptSheet.kt:38-44 states it is 'the slip settled and still: it never re-strikes, never animates its numbers', and ReceiptSheet.kt:61 hardcodes AnimatedVisibility(visible = true) with only a 280ms fadeIn (MonolithCurves.specC). B&O synchronises movement, sound and reveal into one act — the lid's travel IS the sound's duration. Here sound, then silence, then a fade.

Recommendation: Move the E700 completion pulse to the receipt's publication stamp (receiptPublishedMonoMs) and give the slip a mechanical entrance on the same beat: translateY from +32dp to rest over 420ms on Curve B, striking its mono lines in sequence at 60ms intervals synced to two seat-knocks, ending with the tear pulse (currently spent only on task leaves, FocusSequencerScreen.kt:153) as the slip settles. Suppress scrim dismissal until the entrance completes.

#### [HIGH] Incorporation confers no new status: the receipt re-presents the old intention and a machine log number, then outsources the record to YPT

Van Gennep's postliminal rite (agrégation) formally presents the initiate to the community bearing a NEW status, marked by new symbols. Monolith's receipt presents the old identity unchanged: the slip's title is the pre-session intention verbatim ('Revise thermodynamics'), its outcome word is merely ENDED, and its number (№ 048) is a log index, not a status (ReceiptSheet.kt L91-175; receipt.html frame 1). Nothing on the slip states what the bearer now is — no rank, title, tally of standing or mark carried forward — and the footer explicitly exports the meaning elsewhere: 'THE MACHINE KEEPS ITS OWN LOG · YOUR STUDY RECORD LIVES IN YPT'. The rite ends with an audit note addressed to a machine, dismissed on the next DOWN tap anywhere (ReceiptSheet.kt L44-70).

Recommendation: Rewrite the receipt as a presentation, not a log: the slip's head line becomes the new status earned by this passage (e.g. the Tower standing it produces — brick number, streak, day-word filed), the intention moves to a subordinate 'CARRIED IN' line, and dismissal requires a deliberate TAKE UP swipe that returns the user to a light-scheme Deck whose header carries that status until the next session. Delete the YPT footer from the slip; incorporation must happen in the room the user actually returns to.

#### [HIGH] Aggregation confers no status: the user returns from the threshold exactly who they were, and the only witness named is a service that does not exist

Van Gennep's third phase, aggregation, is not an exit — the initiate is reincorporated with a new, publicly legible status. Monolith's receipt (design-renders/receipt.html frame 1; ui/components/ReceiptSheet.kt) confers nothing: verdict word 'ENDED', a serial № 048, wall-clock times, and a footer abdicating witness to elsewhere — 'THE MACHINE KEEPS ITS OWN LOG · YOUR STUDY RECORD LIVES IN YPT', an external app that exists nowhere in the product. Back on the Deck the header still reads the same 'GUARD 4/4' it read before the first session ever run (design-renders/deck.html header band): session № 001 and № 1,000 return to a home screen that registers no change in the person. A passage whose far side looks identical to its near side teaches the user, over weeks, that nothing was crossed.

Recommendation: Make reaggregation visible on the Deck itself: the receipt's final line names the standing the session earned ('KEPT · 12TH THIS MONTH') and that same standing is printed in the Deck header band in place of the static GUARD fraction for the rest of the day, so the ordinary world the user returns to is measurably different from the one they left. Delete the YPT footer line — the witness must be this app, on this screen.

#### [HIGH] The seal certifies elapsed time and calls it CLEAN — a quality verdict the machine never measured

ReceiptState.kt:32 defines ELAPSED_CLEAN as 'a manual session whose span elapsed clean'; ReceiptSheet.kt:124 prints that outcomeWord on the slip beside 'ENDED hh:mm'. The seal's inputs are only elapsed span plus shield continuity (ReceiptState.kt:36-38: ELAPSED_SHIELD_GAP is the same span with the shield gone). Nothing in the outcome computation touches the work itself — yet the printed word is CLEAN, a quality adjective. Pirsig's Quality is the pre-intellectual event of actual engagement, prior to any subject/object measurement; Monolith measures only the measurable shadow (time with the shield up) and then names the shadow with the thing's own name. A session of absorbed work and a session of resentful wall-staring receive the identical signed verdict.

Recommendation: Change the receipt's outcome line in ReceiptSheet.kt to print only what was measured: replace the CLEAN outcome word on the slip with 'SPAN HELD · SHIELD UNBROKEN' (and 'SPAN HELD · SHIELD GAP 04 MIN' for the gap case). Reserve evaluative words for nothing the machine prints; if a quality word is wanted on the slip, it must be the user's own attestation tapped at detention, printed under a separate 'YOUR WORD' line so the machine's facts and the human's judgement never share a typeface or a claim.

#### [HIGH] The shield-gap crack is booked as death and silenced, instead of shown as the day's visible repair

ReceiptState.kt:109-111: 'Death-booked finishes (ELAPSED_SHIELD_GAP) never pulse' — finishPulses returns false for the gap finish while every clean finish sounds the completion pulse. ReceiptState.kt:34-36 defines the outcome as the session where 'the books are BROKEN'. MonolithRepository.kt:1688 reduces the whole event to the slip's stigma word 'ENDED · SHIELD GAP', printing neither when the shield was down nor for how long, even though the session elapsed in full and the user stayed to the end.

Recommendation: On the receipt, print the crack as a seam, not a verdict: replace the outcome word 'ENDED · SHIELD GAP' with a body line in the slip's existing mono voice — 'SHIELD DOWN 14:02–14:09 · YOU RETURNED' — using the gap interval the seal already detects, and change finishPulses so a gap finish sounds one lower, single pulse instead of punitive silence. The finished span stays a finish; its repair becomes the most legible line on the slip.

#### [HIGH] Tetrad reversal: pushed to its limit, the abstinence medium flips into a collectible feed of the user's own non-use

ReceiptSheet.kt:118-176 prints a numbered, filed artefact ('ARMED… PLANNED… HELD 12 APPS · 3 SITES', footer 'THE MACHINE KEEPS ITS OWN LOG'); DrawerScreen.kt:398-431 turns finished spans into collectibles — 'FORGED', 'A FINISHED SPAN FORGES ONE — THE FORGE CHOOSES WHICH' — browsable in a CABINET of serialled TOY 01-06 (drawer.html frame 2). McLuhan's tetrad: a medium pushed to its limit reverses into its opposite — an abstinence tool flips into a content library of one's own non-use, giving the user a new reason to open the phone and browse.

Recommendation: Break the reversal on the Drawer and Receipt surfaces: remove the CABINET index and the FORGED/serial framing — a curio is shown once, on the day it is forged, inside that day's Drawer entry, and is never re-browsable as a collection; drop the receipt number and the 'machine keeps its own log' footer so the slip reads as an ending, not as an instalment in a series to complete.

#### [HIGH] The receipt keeps a meticulous log of the phone's resistance and none of the work's: deflections are timestamped to the minute, but where the material pushed back leaves no trace anywhere

ReceiptSheet.kt:157-162 prints every deflection as 'HH:mm · appName' — a timestamped log of the phone's resistance. The receipt's other lines (ARMED/ENDED/outcome, HELD n APPS · n SITES, BREAK BANKED) are all machine events; the outcome vocabulary itself (ReceiptState.kt:28-30, ELAPSED_CLEAN) is computed from clock and shield only. A session whose Chapter 4 problem set defeated the user for 90 minutes and a session of smooth progress print identically, provided neither touched a LOCKED app. Crawford: attention is educated by the resistance of real things — the stuck point is the most valuable datum a focus practice produces, and Monolith records every push except the work's.

Recommendation: Add a one-tap work-resistance stamp: on the desk clock and the in-session Deck, a single MARK control (no typing, no form) stamps the current substep and elapsed time as a work-deflection. ReceiptSheet prints these interleaved with phone deflections in the same mono list ('14:20 · STUCK — PROBLEM 4'), and the next session's Deck pre-loads that substep as the starting step, so resistance encountered becomes the next session's point of re-entry.

#### [HIGH] The receipt closes the session with a machine verdict and no reflection: the single natural daylight moment in the product is spent on audit, then the record is outsourced to 'YPT'

ReceiptSheet.kt's slip prints only machine facts — ARMED/ENDED times, outcome word, 'HELD n APPS · n SITES', 'BREAK BANKED n MIN' — and then dismisses the user with ReceiptSheet.kt:176 'THE MACHINE KEEPS ITS OWN LOG · YOUR STUDY RECORD LIVES IN YPT'. receipt.html shows the same closed slip. The one moment when the spotlight work is done and reflection is possible is spent issuing a verdict and outsourcing the record elsewhere; the app never asks whether the session served anything, or whether the user still wants what they armed for.

Recommendation: Add a daylight line to the receipt, below the outcome word and above dismissal: the linked Aim, plus one optional free-text sentence — 'Did this move it? What do you want next time?' — skippable with a plain SKIP verb at equal size, stored in the Drawer beside that session and never scored, counted or judged. Remove the YPT deflection line; the reflection lives on the slip the user is already holding.

#### [HIGH] The receipt narrates only resistance: held counts and turned-away apps, never what the attention was for

ReceiptSheet.kt:124-146 prints, in order: ARMED/PLANNED, ENDED · outcome, HELD n APPS · n SITES, BREAK BANKED, then the deflection list (time · app name) — every line records what was kept out or turned away. ReceiptState.kt:138-152 PendingReceipt carries held counts, banked break seconds and deflections, but no field for what the attention was spent on beyond the intention title; there is no prompt, at any point in the flow, asking the user what the session gave them. The feedback loop closes entirely on avoidance, so the artefact the app returns for a life lived attentively is a list of temptations resisted.

Recommendation: Add a closing reflection to the finish flow: when the receipt detention begins, the Deck shows one optional line — 'WHERE DID IT GO?' — with a free-text field; the answer prints on ReceiptSheet as the slip's first line under the title, 'ATTENDED TO — <text>', above HELD and the deflections, which drop to dim mono below it. Sessions where the user skips the line print the intention's completed substeps instead. The receipt's headline fact becomes the good the time bought, not the distractions refused.

#### [MEDIUM] The paper voice is spent on a task leaf while the actual receipt — the app's paper artifact — prints and tears in silence

playTearPulse is documented as 'the counterfoil tear's own voice' — paper language, chord 1.21 against the completion pulse's 1.33, 'near enough to read as paper' (service/TactileSoundEngine.kt:810-817). Its only caller in the app is tearing a task leaf in the Sequencer (ui/screens/FocusSequencerScreen.kt:146-153), where it fires together with task completion. The actual paper artifact, ReceiptSheet, takes no soundEngine parameter at all and dismisses on any DOWN in silence (ui/components/ReceiptSheet.kt:70; see receipt.html render — the slip is purely visual). So the one paper sound is spent where there is no paper, and the slip that prints '№ 048' arrives and leaves mute.

Recommendation: Move the tear to its paper: receipt appearance gets a short print-strike (reuse the seal bolt's filtered-noise renderer at low gain, ~30ms), and receipt dismissal plays playTearPulse. The Sequencer leaf loses the tear and takes a softened completion-pulse variant instead, restoring the engine's own law that the tear 'must not spend the completion pulse' — and vice versa.

#### [MEDIUM] Written in machine-log dialect with no plain-language sentence a friend can understand or repeat

Every line a stranger meets is internal log dialect: 'ARMED 18:42 · PLANNED 50 MIN', 'ENDED 19:32 · ENDED', 'HELD 12 APPS · 3 SITES' (ReceiptSheet.kt:116-131; receipt.html Frame 1, including the tautological 'ENDED · ENDED' produced by ReceiptSheet.kt:124 printing outcomeWord beside the ENDED label). The only sentence-length text is the 9sp footer 'THE MACHINE KEEPS ITS OWN LOG · YOUR STUDY RECORD LIVES IN YPT' (ReceiptSheet.kt:176-178) — a statement about record-keeping, not about what the person did. Duolingo and Nike share surfaces lead with a plain-language verb sentence a non-user can repeat ('I learned Spanish for…', 'I ran 5K'); Monolith gives a friend no sentence they can say back, so the story dies in transmission.

Recommendation: Add one plain-language headline line to the public rendering, generated from the same facts: e.g. '50 minutes with the phone shut — thermodynamics revised.' in Atkinson Bold 15-17sp directly under the masthead, keeping ARMED/HELD mono lines as the forensic detail below it. Ban outcomeWord duplication on that rendering so no line ever prints 'ENDED · ENDED' to an outsider.

#### [MEDIUM] Evening ends on an archive shelf, not a closing artifact: receipts exist per session, never for the day

receipt.html frame 1: the Receipt slip (ReceiptSheet.kt:118-131) prints one session only — 'ARMED 18:42 · PLANNED 50 MIN / ENDED 19:32 · ENDED / HELD 12 APPS · 3 SITES' — numbered per session ('№ 048'). The only day-scale surface, the Drawer, is designed to refuse synthesis: DrawerScreen.kt DayHeading doc comment states 'A date heading: a shelf label only — nothing follows it, no total, no grade.' So the last look of the day is either a per-session slip or an archive shelf of rows; nothing in the app ever composes the day itself into a closing object, even though the receipt grammar (numbered slip, mono lines, seal) already exists to do it with.

Recommendation: Mint a day slip in the receipt's own grammar, following Sunsama's evening shutdown, which presents the finished day as one reviewed record — completed items, unfinished items rolled forward — before closing it: at the SLEEP window start (or on the evening Deck's close-the-day slide), issue a 'DAY №' slip reusing ReceiptSheet's slip stock, 24dp radius and 11sp mono lines, printing the filing date and day-word, the day's sessions with outcomes, total held count, and the first task rolled to tomorrow, sealed with the same imprint treatment as a session receipt. The evening gets an artifact with the same dignity as a single 50-minute session.

#### [MEDIUM] The receipt enters with an opacity fade — the printing machine's one printed object is never printed, struck or fed

ReceiptSheet.kt:43-44 states the design law in its own header: the slip 'never re-strikes, never animates its numbers', and ReceiptSheet.kt:62 enters it with a generic fadeIn(MonolithCurves.specC()) — the standard 280ms opacity fade (MonolithCurves.kt:72). receipt.html Frame 1 shows the result: every line, from the intention title to the footer, materialises simultaneously as translucent paper. For an app whose entire fiction is a machine that prints, stamps and seals, the one printed artefact never prints.
