Papers, Please — the reference this fiction lives next to — makes its stamp slam down with weight, sound and a visible impression; thermal-receipt and ticket-machine interfaces worldwide reveal line by line because the reveal IS the authenticity cue.

Recommendation: Replace the fade with a print: reveal the slip's lines in a top-to-bottom stagger (~45ms per line, ease-out, no bounce), with the № struck last accompanied by the existing seat-knock voice at low amplitude, as if stamped. Keep it under 500ms total and skip it for restored receipts. The numbers never animating can stay as law for the data — it is the paper's arrival that must become physical.

#### [MEDIUM] Credibility theatre with no trust marks: a lone grey '№ 048' and no seal, stamp or countersignature space on the paper

ReceiptState.kt:166-187 contains no witness, partner or countersignatory field, and ReceiptSheet.kt allocates no space for one: the slip's entire credibility apparatus is numberPrint (ReceiptState.kt:189, '№ 048') set in 13sp grey mono at the header's right edge (ReceiptSheet.kt:108-115) — a self-issued serial with no rendered seal, stamp or signature rule anywhere on the card. A recipient sees a typed number anyone could type; the design borrows the receipt's authority while omitting every visual mark — issuer seal, countersignature line, dated stamp overlapping the paper edge — that makes paper proof socially binding, as on an exam-hall attendance slip, which is only valid once the invigilator countersigns the candidate's own signature.

Recommendation: Print the trust marks the metaphor already promises: a circular seal stamp rendered on the slip itself — 'MONOLITH · № 048 · 30 OCT' ringed around the outcome word, set at a slight rotation overlapping the slip's right edge in the night accent — and a ruled countersignature row at the foot ('SEEN BY __________') that a designated partner's co-signed session or a single pre-shared witness name fills at seal time. Even unfilled, the row changes the object's meaning: this is a document meant to be witnessed, not a log the machine kept for itself.

#### [MEDIUM] It fades in like a dialog instead of printing: the one artifact gets the app's most generic entrance

ReceiptSheet.kt:38-48 states the law in its own comment — 'the slip settled and still: it never re-strikes, never animates its numbers' — and ReceiptSheet.kt:60-64 implements exactly that: AnimatedVisibility with a generic fadeIn(MonolithCurves.specC()) / fadeOut(specA()). The user waits out detention (ReceiptState.kt Detention, issuance at 1480-1800ms) and the payoff for that wait is a crossfade identical to any dialog appearing. receipt.html Frame 1 is a static still; nothing in the source gives the slip a feed, rise, or strike.

Recommendation: Stage a print, not a fade: the slip translates up from below the bottom edge behind a hard horizontal clip, as if fed from a slot, over ~350ms; mono lines reveal in sequence at 30ms intervals top to bottom; the new orange outcome stamp lands last, scaling 1.8 to 1.0 in ~120ms with a single short haptic. Total under 650ms after detention. Restored/rehydrated slips (ReceiptState.kt restored flag) skip the sequence and render settled, as they already correctly do in intent.

### Notifications and system surfaces — 39 findings (6 critical, 22 high, 11 medium, 0 low)

#### [CRITICAL] No public face: the Airlock and valve broadcast the owner's app and intention at room scale, and explain nothing to the roommate actually holding the phone

AirlockAndDisarmOverlays.kt:607 prints 'AIRLOCK INTERCEPTION • LOCKED' as the headline, :615 prints the intercepted app name at 24sp, :639 renders the countdown at 88sp, and :648 prints 'ACTIVE INTENTION: {sessionIntention}' — all on a full-screen card (airlock.html frames 1-2). The Disarm overlay (:763-772) likewise opens with 'EMERGENCY BREAK' and 'It is the only break this week.' There is no reduced public layer: whoever holds or glances at the phone in a hostel room or group-study table gets the owner's private facts (which app he was sneaking, what he is studying) at room-readable scale, while a genuine bystander — a roommate handed the phone, someone who finds it mid-session — gets only machine jargon and two owner-priced actions (RETURN TO FOCUS, or a 60-second valve hold that spends the owner's one weekly break). Apple's Focus status makes the opposite decision: people who contact you see only that you have 'notifications silenced' — never which Focus is on (Apple Support, 'Allow or silence notifications for a Focus on iPhone') — because the outward face is a generic availability signal and the details stay behind the owner's unlock.

Recommendation: Split every session surface into a public face and an owner face, following Apple's Focus-status rule (signal, never content). Public face, shown until an owner tap-and-hold or biometric: one plain sentence — 'This phone is in a focus session until 18:30' — plus time remaining, no app name, no intention, no 88sp numeral. Owner face (app name, intention, EMERGENCY PEEK, valve) composes only after that gesture. Add one bystander-safe action on the public face — 'Let a call through / call the owner's emergency contact' — that costs no token and spends no break, so a roommate in a real emergency is never forced to either wait or burn the owner's weekly valve.

#### [CRITICAL] No glance family exists: the widget, tile and shortcut set was never designed as a set, and the surfaces that do exist each speak a different visual language

AndroidManifest.xml:39-137 declares exactly one activity, three services and three receivers — no AppWidgetProvider receiver, no TileService, no shortcuts meta-data anywhere in the app. The glance surfaces that do exist share no visual system: the ongoing notification renders in Android's system type with the launcher foreground as its icon (MonolithShieldService.kt:223-231), the desk clock is cream Anonymous Pro 96sp on true black (receipt.html frame 4; AirlockAndDisarmOverlays.kt:70-223), and the Deck is warm paper #E4DFDA with Sora hero numerals (deck.html). Nothing OS treats its widgets, 1x1 Quick Settings tiles and lock-screen pieces as one family — same monochrome palette, same grid and radii, dot-matrix reserved for small accents — so any Nothing glance reads as Nothing before it reads as data. Monolith has no equivalent family spec, so even a future widget bolted on tomorrow would arrive speaking a fourth language.

Recommendation: Write a one-page Glance Spec before building any surface, and make every glance surface obey it: ground = TokenColorSurfaceVariant #D8D1CB (day) / #100E0C (night), one raised card #FAF6F0, ink #252323, the single orange #F55314 spent only on the armed/active state, Anonymous Pro Bold for numerals, Atkinson Bold for words, 12dp radii, hairline #615B5A at 0x75 alpha. Ship the family as a set designed together — 4x1 strip widget, 2x2 wheel widget, QS tile, three launcher shortcuts — sharing one state vocabulary (IDLE / ARMED / ON BREAK / DONE) so a user who learns one surface has learned all of them, the way Nothing's family teaches itself.

#### [CRITICAL] The Airlock addresses whoever holds the phone as its owner: it broadcasts the owner's private intention and offers the holder the peek escape by name

AirlockAndDisarmOverlays.kt:648 prints 'ACTIVE INTENTION: ${state.sessionIntention}' (the owner's free text) at 12.5sp, :620-630 prints the session end time, and :656-678 offers the holder a full-width EMERGENCY PEEK chip with its price — the surface that appears over another app, i.e. the surface most likely to be read and tapped by a child, parent or stranger who triggered the blocked app (render: airlock.html frames 1-2). Every line is written in owner-voice to whoever holds the phone; no line identifies the session as someone else's property or instructs the holder to return the device.

Recommendation: Split the Airlock into two voices. Default (holder) voice, third person and intention-free: 'THIS PHONE IS IN A FOCUS SESSION UNTIL 18:30 — PLEASE RETURN IT TO ITS OWNER', with the single accent chip RETURN TO FOCUS. The owner's intention, deflection history and the peek offer move behind that return tap (owner is now demonstrably back inside Monolith). This follows iOS Screen Time's limit screen, which addresses the holder as a requester — 'Ask For More Time', with approval held behind a passcode the holder does not have — instead of handing the holder the escape as a labelled, priced chip.

#### [CRITICAL] Nothing about the session is designed for the 96dp status-bar chip — the one text string is written for the shade and would be illegible as a Live Update

MonolithShieldService.kt:142-145 rebuilds one prose string per tick — "Monolith • {intention}" / "42:17 left • Block 2/4 • 3 urges stopped" — and buildNotification (MonolithShieldService.kt:213-231) posts it as a plain NotificationCompat card: no ProgressStyle, no setRequestPromotedOngoing, no setShortCriticalText, no chronometer/setWhen, and AndroidManifest.xml declares no POST_PROMOTED_NOTIFICATIONS despite targetSdk 36 (app/build.gradle.kts:18). Android's Live Update contract gives the chip a maximum width of 96dp and shows critical text whole only under ~7 characters; Monolith's composite string (time + block + scorekeeping) fits none of it. The app already invented the right data model in-app — study blocks separated by Safe Breaks, drawn as a TimelineBar in the desk-clock overlay (AirlockAndDisarmOverlays.kt:120-131) — but exports none of that structure to the system surface.

Recommendation: Design the Live Update as a segmented object, following Google's own ProgressStyle food-delivery codelab pattern: one ProgressStyle segment per study block with a point at each Safe Break, the slab glyph as the progress tracker icon, and the chip carrying exactly one datum — the countdown — via setWhen(session end) so the system renders a live chronometer, or setShortCriticalText("42:17"). Delete 'urges stopped' from every out-of-app surface: scorekeeping is receipt content, not chip content. Request POST_PROMOTED_NOTIFICATIONS and setRequestPromotedOngoing(true); one implementation then renders as the Pixel status-bar chip and, since One UI 8, inside Samsung's Now Bar unchanged.

#### [CRITICAL] Inside a session Monolith refuses to withdraw - it re-asks for attention every two seconds

Weil: school exercises matter only because they train a faculty that then turns away from the exercise to its object; the instrument must withdraw. Monolith never does during a session. MonolithShieldService.kt:85-145,193 runs a 2-second loop (delay(2000L)) and re-posts the ongoing notification every iteration at :142-145 - 'Monolith - {intention}' / '{MM:SS} left - Block i/n - {n} urges stopped' (receipt.html frame 2) - while TactileDeckScreen.kt's running form replaces the wheel with a progress track plus a live '%' readout and keeps the BLOCK/APPS/TIME proof strip and 'N WILL SHUT' imprint pinned. To be protected, the user must keep attending to the protector's clock.

Recommendation: Add a Withdrawn state as the session default: the ongoing notification becomes static text 'Monolith - {intention} - ENDS {HH:mm}' re-posted only at block change, break start/end and finish, with no countdown and no tally; the running Deck collapses to one line - intention and ENDS time - with the progress track, percentage, proof strip and imprint not composed until the user explicitly taps to inspect. Protection should be felt only at the Airlock door.

#### [CRITICAL] The protector is the loudest information source: the shield notification rewrites itself every 2 seconds for the entire session

MonolithShieldService.kt:142-144 calls updateNotification(title='Monolith • {intention}', subtitle='{MM:SS} left • Block {i}/{n} • {phantomReachesBlocked} urges stopped') on every monitor iteration, and MonolithShieldService.kt:193 delays only 2000L — ~1,800 rewrites per hour, ~3,600 in a 2-hour session. buildNotification at :213-228 is ongoing and setOnlyAlertOnce(true), so it cannot be dismissed and sits on the lock screen (receipt.html Frame 2) for the whole session. Simon (1971, Designing Organizations for an Information-Rich World, pp.40-41): information consumes the attention of its recipients — this notification's seconds, block index and running 'urges' tally change constantly yet require no decision between block boundaries.

Recommendation: Throttle the shield notification in MonolithShieldService to decision moments only: update on block change, Safe Break start/end and finish, otherwise post a static 'Monolith • {intention} — session running' with no countdown and no urges tally. Move the live countdown and urges count inside the Deck, where the user has already chosen to spend attention.

#### [HIGH] Blocking state is invisible at the point of temptation: the launcher shows locked apps in full colour with no state, where Digital Wellbeing greys the paused icon itself

AndroidManifest.xml declares exactly one launcher presence — MainActivity with MAIN/LAUNCHER — and no widget provider, TileService or shortcut metadata anywhere in the manifest; blocking state first appears only after the user has already opened the blocked app, when MonolithShieldService.kt:186-201 builds an intercept Intent and launches the Airlock. Digital Wellbeing's Focus mode does the opposite design work: paused apps are greyed out in the launcher/app drawer and a Focus icon sits in the status bar, so the state is visible at the exact surface where the habit fires, before any tap. Monolith's home screen therefore advertises Instagram/YouTube in full colour, full saturation, zero state — the most temptation-dense surface on the phone carries none of the app's information.

Recommendation: Design a 'locked shelf' home-screen surface in the Nothing OS widget idiom (monochrome, one accent, dot/mono type): a 4x1 widget rendering the user's LOCKED and PEEK apps as desaturated icons with a tier dot and the session/end-time word, so state is communicated pre-tap on the launcher within what a third-party app can legally render. Pair it with a long-press launcher shortcut row (Start last session / Start 25m) drawn in the same idiom, so Monolith's state stops beginning only after a failed app launch.

#### [HIGH] The ambient surface demands the screen it exists to replace: desk-clock progress needs foveal reading, where Nothing's Glyph Timer is legible face-down with the screen off

Monolith's only ambient surface is AlwaysOnDeskClockOverlay (ui/components/AirlockAndDisarmOverlays.kt:70-145): an in-app overlay on true black that requires Monolith foregrounded, holds the screen on with FLAG_KEEP_SCREEN_ON (:96), and encodes progress as 96sp numerals plus a 16dp bar (:158-190 in the same file) — information that only exists if you are staring straight at the phone. Worse, it has no end state: MonolithViewModel.kt:1207 sets _isAlwaysOnDeskClockVisible.value = false at the finish edge, so at the moment the session completes the ambient surface simply vanishes. Nothing's Glyph Timer makes the opposite design decision: a light strip depletes segment by segment on the back of a face-down, screen-off phone — progress is peripheral, legible from across a desk, and its completion is the strip emptying, not a screen disappearing.

Recommendation: Rebuild the ambient layer around peripheral legibility, following the Glyph Timer: (1) register the desk clock as a real Daydream/screensaver service so it can own the idle screen instead of borrowing the foreground app; (2) make progress the hero and numerals secondary — a single depleting ring/strip readable at 3 metres, with the MM:SS demoted to a caption; (3) give it a completion frame — when the session ends, hold a 'DONE · 1H 50M' frame for 10 seconds before releasing the screen, instead of the current silent vanish at MonolithViewModel.kt:1207.

#### [HIGH] The Airlock takeover is anonymous — no wordmark, no app icon, no identity on the screen that seizes the phone

airlock.html frames 1-3: the full-screen takeover card carries no MONOLITH wordmark, no app icon and no icon of the intercepted app — only 'AIRLOCK INTERCEPTION • LOCKED' in 11.5sp Atkinson (AirlockAndDisarmOverlays.kt:607), the app's name as bare text, an 88sp countdown and an orange RETURN TO FOCUS chip. The Disarm frame likewise asks for a 60-second hold on an unbranded dark card. Deck.html's identity anchors (MONOLITH header, wheel, orange slide cap) are all absent here except the night palette. This is visually the exact pattern Android security guidance trains users to fear: an anonymous full-screen overlay from an accessibility-powered app demanding a sustained hold. one sec's intervention, by contrast, names itself and phrases the choice as two explicit sentences about the target app ('I don't want to open Instagram' / 'Continue to Instagram').

Recommendation: Give the takeover a verifiable identity, following one sec's self-naming intervention and Android's own branded system dialogs: add a header row to both overlays — the MONOLITH wordmark in the Deck header's exact 10sp tracked style plus the orange slide-cap block as a graphic mark on the left, and the intercepted app's real launcher icon beside its name (Shield already lists these apps; reuse that icon). Add one provenance sentence under the app name: 'Monolith is holding Instagram because you sealed a session ending 18:30.' No new colours or illustration — identity continuity with the Deck is the trust signal.

#### [HIGH] An icon vacuum underneath every glance surface: the app is text-only inside, so a tile or shortcut has no glyph language to inherit — only an off-palette Bauhaus launcher dial

Monolith's entire in-app UI is text-only — the renders show word-labels everywhere and not a single glyph: rail stops are the words DECK/SHIELD/TASKS/LEDGER (deck.html), catalogue state is carried by an 8x8 square margin mark and the words SHUT/PEEK/OPEN (shield.html). A QS tile, a launcher shortcut and a widget's header all demand an icon, and the only icon the app owns is the launcher foreground: a multicolour Bauhaus dial in ultramarine #1E40FF, canary #F5B800 and crimson #E6332A (res/drawable/ic_launcher_foreground.xml) — three colours that appear nowhere in the app's token palette (Color.kt:11-29: warm greys, ink #252323, one orange #F55314). Nothing solved this exact problem by building a dot-matrix glyph language for its widgets and tiles, so its icons are unmistakably its own at 24dp. Monolith at 24dp is either a rainbow sundial or nothing.

Recommendation: Design a three-glyph icon set derived from geometry the app already owns, not from the Bauhaus dial: (1) ARM — the RotaryWheel reader dot seated on its arc; (2) RUNNING — the wheel hub with 2 of 8 wells filled, matching the Deck hub; (3) HELD — the proof-strip seam, a horizontal rule with a centre tick. Draw each at 24dp in single-colour ink, test legibility at QS-tile size, retire the ultramarine/canary/crimson dial from every surface except the launcher, and set the shield notification's small icon to the RUNNING glyph so the most-seen Monolith mark is finally on-palette.

#### [HIGH] The desk clock apes StandBy's job with none of its design decisions: portrait-only, summoned by hand, cream at full brightness instead of a landscape, dock-triggered, red-dimmed ambient face

AlwaysOnDeskClockOverlay (AirlockAndDisarmOverlays.kt:70-223) is a portrait, in-app overlay: 96sp Anonymous Pro time, a 16dp progress bar and a task banner stacked in a centred portrait column on true black, eyebrow 'NIGHTSTAND DESK CLOCK • TAP ANYWHERE TO EXIT', rendered in receipt.html frame 4. It never rotates to landscape, nothing about charging or docking summons it, and its cream NightColorPrimary #FFE4CF (Color.kt:37) burns at full brightness all night. iOS StandBy makes the opposite decision on every axis: it auto-enters when the phone is charging and locked in landscape, lays two glance stacks side by side for across-the-room reading, and in darkness dims to a pale red specifically to protect night vision. Monolith named its surface 'nightstand' and then designed it for a hand, in portrait, at desk distance.

Recommendation: Rebuild the desk clock as a StandBy-class ambient mode: a landscape layout triggered automatically when a session is active and the phone is charging and rotated (portrait keeps the current overlay); in landscape, one hero — remaining time at 160sp+ — on the left and intention plus ENDS time stacked on the right, nothing else; below a low ambient-light threshold, shift the whole palette from cream #FFE4CF to a deep red (~#FF3B30 at 40% luminance) following StandBy's night mode, keeping the existing true-black ground and ±6dp burn-in drift, which are worth keeping.

#### [HIGH] The one persistent glance is the least designed object in the product: a template notification whose icon, type and hierarchy belong to Android, not Monolith

buildNotification() (MonolithShieldService.kt:213-232) sets only a small icon (R.drawable.ic_launcher_foreground — the full-colour Bauhaus dial, illegible and off-palette at notification size), a title, a text line and one PendingIntent to MainActivity. The monitor loop's copy (MonolithShieldService.kt:138-144) crams the session into system-rendered plain text: '24:36 left • Block 1/1 • 3 urges stopped' (receipt.html frame 2). Because NotificationCompat renders in the system's Roboto, the surface a user sees dozens of times per session carries none of Monolith's typography, spacing or colour — it is visually indistinguishable from any template app's alert. Nothing's Glyph Timer makes the contrary choice: session progress is encoded in the hardware light pattern itself, a designed object, not a text string; iOS Live Activities likewise get a designed layout, not the app's leftovers.

Recommendation: Design the notification as an object with a hierarchy, not a string: small icon = the monochrome wheel glyph from the new glance icon set; title slot reserved for the single most glanceable fact — time remaining ('24:36 LEFT') — with the intention demoted to the text line and block position ('BLOCK 1 OF 2 · ENDS 19:32') to a BigTextStyle expansion; drop 'urges stopped' from the collapsed surface entirely, since a temptation count is the one number a locked-out user should not be handed at arm's length. One accent decision: the ongoing notification's chronometer area stays uncoloured — orange appears only when the session ends and the completion notification replaces it.

#### [HIGH] The held-notification digest prints other people's message bodies in full and puts CLEAR ALL / DEL in the same first glance — no masked reading state for a borrowed hand

AirlockAndDisarmOverlays.kt:289-306 defines the digest's LIVE (unsealed) mode as 'live list, live count, CLEAR ALL — plus a per-row delete'; :362-368 renders a CLEAR ALL chip in the header, :420-440 prints each capture as 'appName • senderTitle' plus the full messageBody in 12sp with no masked state, and :436 attaches deletion to a bare 'DEL' text tap. One HELD chip tap from the Deck (TactileDeckScreen.kt:914-915) therefore shows any holder the bodies of other people's messages — the most private data the app touches — and lets that holder destroy the whole archive. The sealed FROZEN mode in the same file proves a no-affordance rendering exists; the live reading surface never uses it (render concept: receipt.html frame 2 shows the same intention-broadcast pattern on the lock screen).

Recommendation: Make masked the digest's default rendering: rows print app + sender + time only, bodies replaced by a ruled 'HELD — TAP AND HOLD TO READ' line; a press-and-hold reveals one body at a time and re-masks on release. Remove CLEAR ALL and DEL from the reading sheet entirely — destruction moves to an explicit EDIT state entered from the header, listing its count before confirming. This is the iOS notification-preview decision (Show Previews: When Unlocked/Never — sender visible, body gated) applied to an archive that currently gives body and delete away together, for free, to any hand.

#### [HIGH] On the lock screen the user's identity is a craving count: '3 urges stopped' is the only live description of who they are

MonolithShieldService.kt:144 builds the lock-screen text as '{MM:SS} left • Block {i}/{n} • {count} urges stopped' — rendered in receipt.html Frame 2 as '24:36 left • Block 1/1 • 3 urges stopped', the one live sentence about the user that a locked phone shows the world. The underlying counter is named phantomReachesBlocked (MonolithModels.kt:298): internally the user is a source of phantom reaches, externally a carrier of urges. No render shows any counter of work done, pages read or problems solved during the session — the temptation count is the only accumulating identity number on a system surface.

Recommendation: Replace the temptation tally with a work tally, following one sec, whose intercept and ongoing surfaces name the chosen activity and the breath taken rather than counting cravings: notification text becomes '{intention} • 24:36 left • 31 min of Chapter 4 done'. Delete 'urges stopped' from MonolithShieldService.kt:144 entirely; if a deflection count survives, move it to the receipt's dim deflection list (where receipt.html already prints per-app lines at 11sp) and label it 'turned away', a verb about the door, not a noun about the user's urges.

#### [HIGH] The only room-visible live surface advertises its own defeat and reports temptation, not commitment

receipt.html Frame 4 / AirlockAndDisarmOverlays.kt:141-160: the desk clock — the only surface meant to be seen across a room — is a full-screen clickable(onClick=onDismiss) whose 11sp eyebrow reads 'NIGHTSTAND DESK CLOCK • TAP ANYWHERE TO EXIT'; it shows only a 96sp countdown and a task banner, no locked state, no end time, no 'do not disturb' signal. Frame 2's ongoing notification instead reports '3 urges stopped' — a temptation count. Opal for Schools (search evidence: Harvard-Westlake deployment) inverts this: officials are notified if a student tries to disable the app, and compliance is verifiable at a glance during the school day.

Recommendation: Split the desk clock into owner and witness readings: remove 'TAP ANYWHERE TO EXIT' from the outward face (exit becomes a long-press with no printed hint), and add a witness line in the banner position: 'FOCUSING UNTIL 19:32 — PLEASE DO NOT DISTURB' in Atkinson Bold 14sp+. Remove the 'urges stopped' count from the lock-screen notification text; replace it with the same ends-at status so anyone glancing at the phone reads commitment, not temptation.

#### [HIGH] Lock-screen privacy is inverted by default: the user's private intention is the public face, the neutral countdown is the hidden one

buildNotification (MonolithShieldService.kt:213-231) calls neither setVisibility nor setPublicVersion, so the notification ships with the platform default split — and the split lands backwards. The content title is "Monolith • {updated.intention}" (MonolithShieldService.kt:143), i.e. the user's own words for what they are working on, which is the element lock-screen and Now Bar surfaces surface most prominently; the content text carrying the countdown and block state is the element that gets redacted on a secure lock screen. No design decision about what a stranger holding the phone — or a colleague glancing at a desk — should see was ever made; the strings.xml channel description (strings.xml:6) even promises 'real-time monotonic focus timer and active app shield telemetry' as the public description of this surface.

Recommendation: Design the two faces explicitly, using Android's publicVersion mechanism the way Google Clock and Maps do (neutral ETA/countdown public, specifics private): the public lock-screen face shows only the slab icon, the chronometer countdown and 'Block 2 of 4' — information with zero personal content. The intention text moves to the private version, visible only after unlock in the shade. The session's most sensitive string should never be the one printed on a locked phone lying face-up in a meeting.

#### [HIGH] Outside the app, a Safe Break is indistinguishable from deep focus — the session's one state change has no surface language

The shield loop computes three distinct states — focus block, Safe Break, stopwatch (MonolithShieldService.kt:124-141) — and renders all three through the identical IMPORTANCE_LOW grey card with only the text string swapped (MonolithShieldService.kt:142-145, 198-211). No icon change, no colour, no chip-text change, no segment state. The Safe Break is the moment the user legitimately picks the phone up; at exactly that moment every out-of-app surface still reads as locked focus, and when focus resumes the reverse transition is equally silent. Compare the render evidence in shield.html: in-app, state changes get full re-composition of the screen; out-of-app, they get a string edit.

Recommendation: Give each state a designed surface identity, as Apple Workout's Live Activity and Samsung's Now Bar do with per-activity pill treatments: during a Safe Break the Live Update's current segment switches to the app's accent (#F55314, the primaryContainer token in Color.kt), the chip text becomes 'BRK 09:32', and the small icon gains its break variant; on return to focus the surface reverts silently. State must be readable at arm's length from colour and icon alone, with the text as confirmation, not the only channel.

#### [HIGH] The title says 'Monolith' twice and spends the lock screen's scarcest characters on the brand, not the intention

MonolithShieldService.kt:142-145 builds the title as "Monolith • ${updated.intention}"; receipt.html Frame 2 (lock-screen render) shows the system header already printing 'Monolith' directly above the title 'Monolith • Revise thermodynamics' — the brand is paid for twice in the ~30 characters a lock-screen title gets. The title is a single-line system template field (buildNotification, MonolithShieldService.kt:223-229 sets only title+text, no style), so it ellipsises from the right: everything after the redundant prefix — the part of the user's intention that actually differs from every other session — is what gets cut. When the intention is boilerplate the title is pure filler: blank intentions default to 'Deep Uninterrupted Study' (MonolithRepository.kt:1348) and routine sessions substitute the routine name (RoutineDerive.kt:169).

Recommendation: Delete the brand prefix entirely — title = the intention alone, nothing else. Put session state where the system gives a free slot: setSubText('SEALED · BLOCK 1/3') or fold state into the text line. Cap the rendered title at the template's visible width by truncating the intention in code with a trailing '…' rather than letting the system shear it mid-word. Follow the Android notification anatomy every mature app obeys (Gmail, Calendar): the system supplies the app name in the header, the title carries content only.

#### [HIGH] The notification re-timestamps itself 'now' every 2 seconds for the entire session — it claims it just arrived, forever

buildNotification (MonolithShieldService.kt:213-231) never calls setWhen, setShowWhen or any chronometer method, and updateNotification (MonolithShieldService.kt:233-235) constructs a brand-new Notification object on every call. The monitor loop calls it every iteration and then delay(2000L) (MonolithShieldService.kt:193), so the notification is reposted roughly every 2 seconds for the whole session — each repost carrying a fresh implicit post-time. receipt.html Frame 2 faithfully renders the result: the header reads '• now' on a session already 25 minutes in. Two consequences: the shade can never tell the user when this session actually began or how long it has been running, and the hand-formatted countdown text (MonolithShieldService.kt:138) decrements in 2-second steps, so odd seconds are never displayed on the one clock the user sees without unlocking.

Recommendation: Anchor the timestamp once at build time: setWhen(session end time) with setUsesChronometer(true) and setChronometerCountDown(true), the pattern Google Clock's timer notification uses — the system then ticks the countdown itself every second and the header time means the session's end, not the latest repaint. Repost only on state changes (block change, break start/end, a deflection milestone), never on a 2-second timer. If a manual repost must happen, reuse the original builder values so 'when' stays pinned to the session, not to the repaint.

#### [HIGH] The sealed session is a live scoreboard, not silence: the lock-screen notification tallies 'urges stopped' while the user is supposed to be feeling the quiet the Throw bought

MonolithShieldService.kt:138 rebuilds the ongoing notification as '%02d:%02d left - Block %d/%d' and :144 appends '${phantomReachesBlocked} urges stopped' on every monitor update; receipt.html frame 2 renders it live on the lock screen ('24:36 left - Block 1/1 - 3 urges stopped'). The desk-clock frame in the same render adds a 96sp countdown and progress bar. After the Throw promises a held, quiet world, the session's ambient surfaces instead run a ticking scoreboard that counts and displays the user's temptations.

Recommendation: Freeze the live notification at seal time to one static line — 'Sealed until 19:32' — with no countdown, no block fraction and no urges tally, updated only when the session ends. Move the urges count to the receipt alone, where it is history. Set the desk clock's default face to wall time only, with session remaining shown only on tap.

#### [HIGH] The intercept names the offender in public: full-screen card broadcasts the blocked app and the private intention to the whole room

AirlockAndDisarmOverlays.kt:607 prints 'AIRLOCK INTERCEPTION • LOCKED', :618-624 prints the intercepted app name at 24sp bold, :648 prints 'ACTIVE INTENTION: {sessionIntention}' — all on a full-screen card the shield launches uninvited via startActivity in MonolithShieldService.kt's monitor loop when it spots a blocked foreground package. airlock.html frames 1-2 confirm the composition: badge, app name, session end, 88sp countdown and intention are all bystander-legible at arm's length. Tokyo Metro's manners posters since 1974 depict a fictional offender (Yorifuji's recurring glasses character) precisely so no real passenger is ever identified in the carriage; the poster shames a drawing, never a person. Monolith inverts this: at the exact moment of lapse, in whatever public place the user happens to be, the phone itself stages the accusation and names both the craved app and the private study intention to anyone within reading distance.

Recommendation: Split the Airlock into a public face and a private face. Public face (default, and the only face until the user taps-and-holds to reveal): no app name, no intention — a single neutral scene line such as 'Not now' over the countdown numeral, in the existing night tokens. App name and intention move behind a deliberate press-and-hold reveal (500ms) that re-covers on release, so the information exists only while the owner's hand is physically on the glass — the poster remains fictional, the passenger stays anonymous.

#### [HIGH] Theft is reported in the past tense: the live notification counts urges already stopped, never the present minute being seized

Mid-session, the one surface a user actually sees — the ongoing lock-screen notification — reads '{MM:SS} left • Block 1/1' with subtitle '{time} • n urges stopped' (service/MonolithShieldService.kt:138, :144; design-renders/receipt.html frame 2). That is a past-tense defence tally plus a future-tense remainder: the present minute, the only portion Seneca says can actually be stolen ('the present is short, the future doubtful, the past certain'), is the one portion never named — the notification never says what this minute is for. The session's intention appears only in the title as a label, never as the price of leaving now.

Recommendation: Rewrite the in-session notification copy in MonolithShieldService.kt:138-144: drop 'urges stopped' from the lock screen entirely (it belongs on the receipt, where HELD already lives) and make the subtitle the present-tense stake — '{intention} · MINUTE 24 OF 50 · THIS MINUTE IS THE SESSION'. Keep title and countdown format unchanged; the change is copy and hierarchy only, on the exact two format strings cited.

#### [HIGH] Communitas inverted: the only other people inside the limen are the ones being held off, and they are rendered as counts and app names, never as persons

Communitas, for Turner, is the direct, unmediated encounter of concrete persons that structure normally keeps apart — it is the social fruit of the liminal state. A solitary blocker cannot manufacture a cohort, but Monolith goes further than solitude: it actively de-persons the user's actual community for the session's duration. People trying to reach the user become a bare integer on the HELD chip (ui/screens/TactileDeckScreen.kt ~L910, monoBadge = capturedNotificationsCount) and, on the receipt, a list of corporations with timestamps — '18:57 · Instagram', '19:11 · YouTube' (design-renders/receipt.html frame 1) — senders nowhere. The social world is admitted into the ritual only as deflection statistics, so re-entry has no one to return to.

Recommendation: Person-first the held world: HELD digest rows lead with the sender's name and app second ('Asha · WhatsApp'), the chip badge stays a count but the receipt's deflection section is retitled 'WAITED' and lists people, and dismissal of the receipt lands on the digest's first waiting person as the act of return — reaggregation staged as coming back to specific people, not to an unlocked phone.

#### [HIGH] The cure re-serves the poison as a readable feed: the held digest is scrollable mid-session, a notification feed with the links removed

CapturedNotificationsDigestSheet (AirlockAndDisarmOverlays.kt:297) renders the full titles and bodies of held notifications in a scrollable sheet, openable mid-session via onOpenNotificationDigest (MainActivity.kt:518). Its own copy concedes the contents are inert — 'Everything here is as of the time above. Nothing here opens' (AirlockAndDisarmOverlays.kt:377) — which makes it pure reading: the exact feed-consumption the session exists to interrupt, re-served inside the cure, concentrated and stripped of the friction of opening each app.

Recommendation: Split the digest into two doses. Mid-session, the sheet shows only the HELD count and one collapsed line per app ('WHATSAPP · 3 HELD') with no titles or bodies rendered. Full text unlocks only after the session's receipt has been shown and dismissed, at which point the sheet is headed 'RELEASED — READ ONCE, THEN IT CLEARS'. Attention captured by the poison should never be re-spendable inside the remedy.

#### [HIGH] Extension as amputation: the live lock-screen ticker outsources vigilance to the machine and numbs the user's own noticing

MonolithShieldService.kt:138-144 builds a per-second-updated, ongoing, non-dismissible lock-screen text: '{MM:SS} left • Block {i}/{n}' plus '{phantomReachesBlocked} urges stopped' under the title 'Monolith • {intention}' (receipt.html frame 2). McLuhan: every extension is also an amputation (Narcissus narcosis) — vigilance is extended onto the lock screen precisely by amputating the user's own noticing; the machine counts his urges so he never has to feel one.

Recommendation: Post the shield notification once at seal time as static ground — 'Monolith • Locked until 19:32' — and never update it during the session: delete the per-second countdown, the Block i/n fraction and the 'urges stopped' counter from MonolithShieldService.kt:138-144. Urge counts, if kept at all, belong only on the end-of-session receipt, after the attention they describe is over.

#### [HIGH] The held-notification digest saves no attention — it defers the entire wealth and re-serves it verbatim

AirlockAndDisarmOverlays.kt:297-455 CapturedNotificationsDigestSheet re-presents everything the listener captured, verbatim and unranked: header 'HELD NOTIFICATIONS • {size}' (:362), a 220dp LazyColumn (:400) of full senderTitle plus full messageBody (:444-446) in capture order, with only DEL/CLEAR ALL as triage. Nothing is summarised, grouped, ranked by sender importance, or auto-discarded as noise — a like, an OTP and a delivery update cost identical reading time. That is deferral, not filtering: Simon's test for an information system in an attention-poor world is how well it filters out the unimportant, and Monolith's digest filters out nothing, it archives perfectly and hands the whole wealth back at session end, the moment attention is most depleted.

Recommendation: Replace the verbatim digest list with a filtered digest: one grouped line per app ('Instagram — 14 held, newest 19:26'), bodies collapsed behind a per-app tap, one-tap 'DISCARD ALL FROM THIS APP NEXT SESSION' on each group, and automatic silent expiry of notification updates/duplicates. The default digest a tired user sees should cost under 10 seconds to clear.

#### [HIGH] The seal encloses the user from the attentional commons without telling the commons: held senders are never informed, so the shared ecology degrades into double-texts and escalation calls

MonolithNotificationListener.kt:49-98: onNotificationPosted only captures; CapturedNotificationEntity (MonolithModels.kt) stores senderTitle and messageBody, and the Detention surface tells the owner 'Everything here is as of the time above. Nothing here opens. Anything newer waits until the session ends.' (AirlockAndDisarmOverlays.kt:377). No code path — no reply action, no status, no share at seal — ever tells a sender the user has withdrawn until a stated time. Crawford's commons is joint attention: a withdrawal nobody can see is not stewardship, it is silent enclosure, and the commons answers rationally — senders double-text, then call, escalating exactly the claims the seal was meant to hold.

Recommendation: Add a seal-time outward notice: on the Deck's arm strip, an optional SESSION NOTICE toggle that, at ARM, fires each held messaging notification's own reply action (or a share-sheet fallback) with 'Sealed in Monolith until 10:40 — messages are held and delivered then.' In the Detention deck, group held items by sender and print under each name 'THEY HAVE NOT BEEN TOLD' until a notice has gone out, so the user can see the state of the commons they have enclosed.

#### [HIGH] Temptation is scored: every blocked reach increments an 'urges stopped' counter, so the most tempted user posts the highest number

MonolithShieldService.kt:144 prints the live shield notification subtitle as '$timeFormatted • ${updated.phantomReachesBlocked} urges stopped', and MonolithRepository.kt:2123 increments phantomReachesBlocked on every recordIntercept. The counter therefore rises fastest for the user who keeps lunging at blocked apps: ten surrendered attempts outscore a session in which the phone was simply left alone and the count stayed zero. The tracking mechanism has been mistaken for the experience — craving, counted, becomes the achievement, and a quiet session reads as an unproductive one on the very surface meant to protect it.

Recommendation: Remove the count from the Shield's ongoing notification entirely — subtitle becomes time remaining only. On the Receipt, keep deflections as a plain timestamped list (as ReceiptSheet.kt already prints them) with no total, no 'urges stopped' wording, and no cumulative counter anywhere in the Drawer, so resisting is recorded as an event, never farmed as a score.

#### [MEDIUM] One notification, three personalities: the only system surface cycles security-shout, telemetry scoreboard and toy joke on a single ID

One notification ID (MonolithShieldService.kt companion, NOTIFICATION_ID = 4096) cycles through three unrelated personalities. It is born as a security shout — buildNotification("Monolith Locked", "Protecting your focus session...") at MonolithShieldService.kt:65. Mid-session it becomes a telemetry ticker — title "Monolith • ${updated.intention}", subtitle "$timeFormatted • ${updated.phantomReachesBlocked} urges stopped" at :142-145, turning the shade into a scoreboard that rewards pulling it down to watch the urge counter climb. At completion it turns whimsical — updateNotification("Session Complete", "Unlocked desk toy ready in your Break tab.") at :116. Nothing OS's system surfaces hold one register everywhere (monochrome dot-matrix, terse, no gamified counters); Monolith's single most-seen surface cannot decide whether it is a guard, a dashboard or a toy, so none of the three readings builds recognition.

Recommendation: Fix one voice for all system surfaces, modelled on Nothing OS's restraint: title is always the session's own word (the intention, nothing else), body is always one clause of state in the same construction — '42 min left · ends 10:40' — with no brand shout, no urge scoreboard and no jokes. Move 'urges stopped' off the shade entirely (it belongs on the receipt); the glance surface's job is calm confirmation, not a counter that pays out for checking it.

#### [MEDIUM] The app's only glance-shaped object speaks proof-jargon to an inspector, not answers to its owner

The one piece of Monolith that is already shaped like a glance — the 53dp ProofStripBand (ui/components/MonolithCustomComponents.kt:644-667), three cells BLOCK / APPS / TIME — spends its seam line, the strip's only sentence, on audit language addressed to an inspector: stamp pairs resolved at MonolithCustomComponents.kt:383-400 print 'BIND HELD · THIS VISIT' / 'PROOF: LIVE BIND', 'PROOF: BIND ONLY', 'PROOF: POSITIVE', 'BIND UNCONFIRMED'. deck.html shows the shipped result: 'BLOCK ON · APPS 12 · TIME ENDS 10:40' over a seam reading 'BIND HELD · THIS VISIT / PROOF: LIVE BIND'. Nothing OS widgets answer the owner's questions in the owner's words (time, date, a toggle's state) — proof grades are never exported to a glance surface. Monolith's glance grammar proves the app to itself instead of informing the user, which is why the strip reads as instrumentation telemetry rather than as the calm one-line status a widget, tile or notification could reuse verbatim.

Recommendation: Split the strip's two jobs. The glance row keeps BLOCK/APPS/TIME but its seam sentence becomes a user-word status line in Nothing's terse register — 'HELD UNTIL 10:40 · 3 APPS CAN PEEK' — and every PROOF/BIND grade moves to a dedicated inspector detail inside PARK where audit language belongs. Design that one sentence as the canonical glance string and reuse it character-for-character as the notification body and any future widget/tile subtitle, so every surface outside the app speaks the same single line.

#### [MEDIUM] Desk clock is sized for distance only in its digits: task banner 14sp and eyebrow 11sp at 60% alpha vanish at arm's length

receipt.html frame 4 and AirlockAndDisarmOverlays.kt:148-182: the desk clock gets the distance problem half right — the session countdown is Anonymous Pro Bold 96sp in cream #FFE4CF on true black — but everything that tells the student WHAT the time means is set for reading in the hand: the eyebrow 'NIGHTSTAND DESK CLOCK - TAP ANYWHERE TO EXIT' is 11sp at 60% alpha, and the task banner is Atkinson Bold 14sp on #362C27. Propped against a stack of books at arm's length or more, the one surface designed to be read without picking the phone up reduces to a bare MM:SS whose task and context are illegible.

Recommendation: Design the clock in two distance tiers, the way Apple StandBy treats a docked phone as a display 'designed to be viewed at a distance': keep the 96sp countdown, promote the task/intention banner to 24-28sp bold cream on black directly under it, and delete or relocate the 11sp eyebrow instruction (exit behaviour belongs in the first-use moment, not permanently printed at reading size on a distance surface). If a line cannot be read from a metre, it should not be on this screen.

#### [MEDIUM] The widget Monolith needs is already composed inside the Deck — proof strip over slide-to-start — but it was designed at reading distance and never transposed to glance scale

The Deck already contains a finished glance composition that was never transposed: the proof strip (deck.html; ProofStripBand) is a 53dp recessed band reading BLOCK ON / APPS 12 / TIME ENDS 10:40 over a seam line 'BIND HELD · THIS VISIT / PROOF: LIVE BIND', and directly beneath it sits the 72dp slide-to-start track with its orange cap — a status readout and a start control, already laid out as a horizontal strip at roughly widget proportions. It exists only inside the app, at in-app reading distance and in-app type sizes (10sp labels, 15sp values). Nothing's all-in-one clock widget shows the transposition discipline Monolith skipped: it consolidates time, date, weather and next event into one placement designed for the home-screen grid first, not shrunk from an in-app screen. iOS StandBy's stacks make the same point — glance layouts are composed at glance scale, with one dominant element per stack.

Recommendation: Transpose, don't shrink: ship the 4x1 widget as the proof strip rebuilt at glance scale — labels up to 11sp, values to 20sp Anonymous Pro, seam line retained, orange reserved for the ARMED state word. Ship the 2x2 as the wheel: hero remaining/total in Sora at Deck proportions with the slide-cap reduced to a single START cap along the bottom edge. Ship a 1x1 as the slide cap alone — orange, unlabelled, one tap arms the last configuration. Ban in-app microcopy that cannot survive the distance ('PROOF: LIVE BIND', 'BIND HELD · THIS VISIT') from every glance surface; each surface gets exactly one hero fact, one secondary fact, one action.

#### [MEDIUM] The glance surface cannot sit still: the notification is rebuilt and reposted by hand every 2 seconds instead of delegating time to the system

The shield loop ends in delay(2000L) (MonolithShieldService.kt:197) and calls updateNotification on every iteration (MonolithShieldService.kt:142-145), re-formatting the countdown string itself with String.format (MonolithShieldService.kt:133-140) and re-posting the whole notification through NotificationManager.notify (MonolithShieldService.kt:233-236). The builder sets no chronometer and no setWhen (MonolithShieldService.kt:223-231), so the system cannot tick the surface for free. The felt result contradicts the product's entire premise: a focus tool whose own ambient surface visibly churns with fresh numbers every couple of seconds, in stepped 2-second jumps, instead of the smooth, silent, system-rendered countdown every native timer shows.

Recommendation: Post once per state change and hand time to the OS: setWhen(block end) with setUsesChronometer(true) and chronometer count-down on the promoted notification, exactly as Google Clock's timer does — the system then animates the chip, lock screen and AOD every second with zero app wake-ups. Repost only on block transitions, Safe Break entry/exit and session end. Stillness is the brand: Monolith's surface should be the calmest thing in the shade, not the busiest.

#### [MEDIUM] Monolith hand-builds a fake always-on display inside the app while the phone's real AOD shows nothing of the session

AirlockAndDisarmOverlays.kt:131-175 implements an in-app desk clock with genuine AOD craft — true-black ground so OLED pixels switch off, and a burn-in pixel-shift that steps the whole composition on a 5×5 grid (dx/dy from burnInStep) — backed by a dedicated 104sp DeskClockTextStyle documented 'H1 - across-the-room time. AOD only.' (Type.kt:73-82). But this object only exists with the app foregrounded and the screen held awake. The real always-on display — the surface a propped-up phone actually presents for the whole session — receives nothing, because the session's only system presence is an unpromoted IMPORTANCE_LOW notification (MonolithShieldService.kt:201-204) that AOD does not render as a live surface.

Recommendation: Stop reimplementing the platform: a promoted Live Update is rendered by the system on the Pixel AOD and in Samsung's Now Bar automatically, with the OS handling burn-in shift itself. Ship the Live Update (segmented progress + chronometer chip, per the design above) and let the real AOD carry the across-the-room time; demote the in-app desk clock to what it actually is — a full-screen in-session view — instead of a workaround compensating for a platform surface the app refuses to use.

#### [MEDIUM] Three modes, three incompatible subtitle grammars — and the stopwatch line prints an internal rule, '(20m floor)', on the lock screen

MonolithShieldService.kt:124-140 defines three unrelated sentence templates switched by mode: timed sessions get '%02d:%02d left • Block %d/%d' (line 138), Safe Break gets 'Safe Break %02d:%02d • Block %d/%d' (line 126) — the word 'left' silently disappears, so the break's remaining time reads as elapsed — and stopwatch gets 'Stopwatch +%02d:%02d (20m floor)' (line 131), a plus-signed count-up followed by the internal rule name '(20m floor)' printed verbatim on the lock screen. All three then get '• N urges stopped' appended (line 144). A user glancing mid-session must first decode which of three grammars they are looking at before the number means anything, and the stopwatch line leaks an unexplained house rule to anyone who picks up the phone.

Recommendation: One template for every mode, in a fixed slot order: '{STATE} · {MM:SS} left · ends {HH:mm}' for timed and break ('BREAK · 04:12 left · ends 19:32'), and '{MM:SS} elapsed · floor passed' / 'floor at 20:00' for stopwatch — the word 'left'/'elapsed' always present, the direction of time never carried by a '+' sign or by an absent word. Delete '(20m floor)' from all system surfaces; internal rule names belong in the app, not on the lock screen. Parkling's iOS timer Live Activity is the model: one card grammar — name, live countdown, and an explicit 'Ends at {time}' — regardless of state.

#### [MEDIUM] Monolith's most-seen surface speaks in three borrowed voices — placeholder boilerplate, telemetry, toy advert — and never in its own

The notification's three lifecycle states are written in three unrelated voices, none of them Monolith's. First post (MonolithShieldService.kt:65) is hardcoded template boilerplate — 'Monolith Locked' / 'Protecting your focus session...' — a sentence any blocker app could ship, shown until the first loop iteration overwrites it. The running state switches to a telemetry register ('24:36 left • Block 1/1 • 3 urges stopped', receipt.html Frame 2). Completion (MonolithShieldService.kt:116) switches again, to a playful register: 'Session Complete' / 'Unlocked desk toy ready in your Break tab.' Inside the app the voice is a disciplined terse ritual register (strings.xml ritual strings: 'SEALED VAULT CHAMBER', 'ONE-WAY RATCHET ENGAGED'; deck.html header/type system). The lock-screen notification is the surface the user sees most often during a session — every glance, for hours — and it is the only surface with no trace of that voice, and no consistency with itself.

Recommendation: Write a one-page notification voice spec in the app's own register and apply it to all three states: kill the hardcoded placeholder by building the first notification from the already-latched session row (the service reads it in the same start path), so the first thing the lock screen ever shows is 'SEALED · {intention}' / '{MM:SS} left · ends {HH:mm}'. Completion uses the receipt's register ('ENDED · {intention}' / '№ {n} · held {x} · deflected {y}'), the same words the Receipt slip prints. Forest is the reference discipline: one metaphor and one voice inside the app and in its notifications — the tree grows in both, the completion notification reports the tree grown.

#### [MEDIUM] In Android Settings — the one place the user judges this channel — its description is developer telemetry-speak: 'real-time monotonic focus timer and active app shield telemetry'

strings.xml:5-6 is the text Android shows verbatim in Settings > Apps > Monolith > Notifications: channel name 'Monolith Active Shield', description 'Displays real-time monotonic focus timer and active app shield telemetry.' 'Monotonic' is the codebase's internal witness vocabulary (the shield loop's comments reason about monotonic stamps); 'telemetry' is engineering language for what the user experiences as 'my countdown'. Android's channel documentation defines the description as 'the user visible description of this channel' that 'the user sees in the system settings' — this is a user decision surface, the place where someone decides whether Monolith may keep speaking, and it is written for a code reviewer. Google's own Clock app names its Settings categories with plain nouns ('Timers', 'Alarms').

Recommendation: Rewrite the channel's Settings prose in outcome language a non-programmer can act on: name 'Focus session', description 'Your running session: time left, which block you are in, and when it ends. Monolith needs this visible while a session is protecting you — turning it off hides your countdown but does not stop the session.' Apply the same rule product-wide: no word may appear on a system surface ('monotonic', 'telemetry', 'shield', 'floor') that does not also appear, explained, inside the app.

#### [MEDIUM] 'Session Complete' wears the live shield's exact uniform — same icon, same channel, no expiry — so finished and still-locked are indistinguishable at a glance

Completion is posted through the identical builder, icon, channel and ID as the live shield: updateNotification('Session Complete', ...) at MonolithShieldService.kt:116, then stopForeground(STOP_FOREGROUND_DETACH) at line 117 leaves it on screen. buildNotification (lines 223-231) offers no state differentiation at all — no alternate small icon, no setColor, no setTimeoutAfter, no auto-cancel — so a finished session and a running one wear exactly the same dress in the shade, distinguishable only by reading the title text word by word. For an app whose whole in-app design language is built on state changes you can feel (sealed vs open, armed vs ended), the moment of release — the emotional payoff — has no visual state of its own outside the app.

Recommendation: Give completion its own designed state: a distinct small-icon glyph (the seal/check mark from the receipt, as a dedicated monochrome stat icon), the brand accent passed via setColor so the app-name tint changes, and a self-expiring lifetime — setTimeoutAfter of ~15 minutes or setAutoCancel(true) so tapping or time clears it. iOS timer Live Activities end by flipping to an explicit 'Done!' state rather than re-dressing the running card; Monolith's shade card should flip just as visibly: running = countdown dress, finished = receipt dress, nothing = nothing.

#### [MEDIUM] The lock-screen notification does three jobs on a half-second surface: countdown, block progress and temptation score compete in one line

MonolithShieldService.kt:142-144 rebuilds the ongoing lock-screen notification on every 2s monitor iteration as title 'Monolith • {intention}' and subtitle '{MM:SS} left • Block {i}/{n} • {n} urges stopped' — three unrelated jobs (a countdown, a curriculum-progress report, and a temptation score) fused into the one surface a rushed person glances at for half a second, hands full, phone face-up on a shared table (receipt.html frame 2 reproduces it verbatim). Tokyo transit design zones its surfaces ruthlessly: platform floor markings answer only 'where do I stand', the door area answers only 'let them out first', the priority-seat sticker answers only 'who sits here' — one surface, one decision, legible at walking speed. A glance surface carrying a score forces the reader to parse, not glance, and the score is the element that lingers in a bystander's memory.

Recommendation: Zone the notification: the ongoing lock-screen body carries exactly one fact — time remaining ('24:36 left') — plus nothing else. Move 'Block i/n' to the Deck proof strip where curriculum progress already lives, and move 'urges stopped' to the receipt, where a count belongs as a record rather than a live public tally. The builder at MonolithShieldService.kt:213-231 takes title+subtitle only, so this is a call-site change at :142-144, not a redesign.

### Accessibility as design — 5 findings (2 critical, 3 high, 0 medium, 0 low)

#### [CRITICAL] Airlock's choice menu is time-gated: assistive navigation speed decides which options exist

AirlockAndDisarmOverlays.kt:562-569 seeds countdownSecs=5 and ticks it down; :636 renders it as an 88sp Anonymous Pro numeral changing every second; :663 composes EMERGENCY PEEK only if countdownSecs==0 && canUse2MinutePeek, :690 composes the withheld reason only at 0. airlock.html shows the same staggered reveal. A TalkBack user swiping linearly, a magnification user panning a zoomed card, or a Switch Access user waiting for scan focus therefore meets a different, incomplete menu for the first seconds and a layout that mutates under their focus — speed of sighted tapping is the eligibility test.

Recommendation: Compose both RETURN TO FOCUS and EMERGENCY PEEK (or its withheld reason) from frame one, visually dimming the peek until the pause ends without removing it from semantics or layout, following one sec: its intervention imposes a pause but never expires or hides the choice from a slow navigator. Announce 'Peek available' once via a live region when the countdown ends instead of forcing the user to watch an 88sp numeral churn.

#### [CRITICAL] SHUT / PEEK / OPEN is a luminance-only code: the app's core ruling vanishes for low-vision and colour-blind users

park.html spec plate states verbatim 'COLOUR IS A VERB: ORANGE = COMMIT · INK = SHUT · GREY = PEEK · PORCELAIN = OPEN'. shield.html:129 gives the day caps as SHUT #252323, PEEK #615B5A, OPEN #FAF6F0 — three warm greys separated only by luminance; shield.html:125 gives the second code as an 8x8dp margin glyph — solid for SHUT, 1.4dp hollow for PEEK, absent for OPEN — invisible at arm's length, under glare, or under magnification panning. Color.kt:44 sets the night muted tier that carries this distinction at 3.5:1. There is no shape, icon, pattern, underline or position code a low-vision or colour-blind user can fall back on.

Recommendation: Add redundant, non-colour coding the way Kinneir and Calvert coded British Rail and road signage — colour plus distinct shape plus word position, so no meaning rides on one channel: e.g. SHUT gets a filled square + double underline, PEEK an eye-slot lozenge + dashed underline, OPEN an open ring + no fill, repeated identically on the rocker, the slip and the Deck imprint. Keep the grey palette; change the shapes, not the brand.

#### [HIGH] Spacer-only rows have no stacked state when both ends expand at once

Every dense row uses the same shock absorber: two expanding texts separated by Spacer(Modifier.weight(1f)) inside a fixed-height Row, with no stacking fallback anywhere in the UI (grep finds zero FlowRow/ViewThatFits-style adaptivity; the only concession is one horizontalScroll for Shield filter words at ShieldMatrixScreen.kt:486). ParkBoardRow (ParkDrawer.kt:653-679) is .height(48.dp) with PillBadge name + Spacer + 15sp state word; ParkSocialSitesRow (:713 .height(48.dp)) must additionally fit a fixed 76x34dp sled — name + RUNNING + sled already totals ~330dp in English in park.html. The FIX key (ParkDrawer.kt:428 .height(48.dp), :458 'FIX — {boardName}' in 15sp Sora) concatenates the longest board name into a button label. The Deck task row (TactileDeckScreen.kt:~788) packs NOW + ellipsised title (maxLines=1 at :805) + DONE keycap + QUEUE count on one line. When both sides expand — German state words plus German board names, or any text at 200% — the spacer collapses to zero and the row has no second state: texts collide, clip, or ellipsise the user's own task title to nothing.

Recommendation: Give every two-text row a designed stacked state, triggered by fontScale or measured overflow — the iOS Dynamic Type pattern of switching horizontal stacks to vertical at accessibility sizes. In Compose: at LocalDensity.fontScale > 1.3 (or when the row's measured width exceeds the container), PARK rows stack state word under the name and move the sled to its own full-width line, the FIX key wraps to two lines with heightIn(min=48.dp), and the Deck task row moves DONE/QUEUE to a second line so the title gets the full width. Test all three rows with the longest real strings — NOTIFICATION LISTENER / FIX — NOTIFICATION LISTENER — at fontScale 2.0 in German pseudo-locale as a merge gate.

#### [HIGH] Font assignment is inverted: Atkinson's disambiguation is wasted on prose, every decision number is set in confusable mono

Type.kt:33-38 registers Atkinson Hyperlegible — the Braille Institute face drawn so 1/l/I, 0/O and b/d/p/q cannot be confused — but Type.kt:85-86 assigns every labelLarge/Medium/Small (Type.kt:149-151) to PillBadgeTextStyle in Anonymous Pro, and AirlockAndDisarmOverlays.kt:636-639 sets the 88sp countdown and the desk clock's 96sp time in Anonymous Pro. deck.html and receipt.html confirm all telemetry, serials, guard counts and session times are mono. The disambiguation Atkinson was bought for is spent on prose, while the digits a stressed, low-vision user must read exactly — 05 vs 00, ENDS 19:32 — get the confusable face.

Recommendation: Invert the assignment following Atkinson's own design intent: set all numerals that carry a decision — countdowns, ENDS times, durations, token counts — in Atkinson Bold (its flagged 1, slashed/distinct 0 and open apertures survive blur), and demote Anonymous Pro to purely decorative serials like the receipt number where a misread costs nothing. Change DialClockTextStyle and DeskClockTextStyle families in Type.kt; keep mono only as a specimen-plate ornament.

#### [HIGH] The hero number is deliberately ghosted into a triple image — letterpress effect that simulates low vision itself

TactileDeckScreen.kt:637 comment admits the treatment: 'two static ghosts at +-1dp behind the glyph, print not rig — it dies on device if it reads as blur (removal trial)'; :655-668 implements it with heroShadowGhost Color(0x99D8D1CB) offset y=-1.dp and heroCatchGhost Color(0xB3FAF6F0) offset y=+1.dp behind the 72sp hero. deck.html renders the result as a triple image of '1H 50M'. For a user with astigmatism, cataracts or dyslexic visual stress this is not a metaphor — it is a simulation of their impairment applied to the one number the screen exists to show, with no setting to remove it.

Recommendation: Kill the ghosts and get the letterpress feeling honestly, as print itself does: one glyph, Sora Bold, with a single 1dp bottom edge in surfaceVariant — depth from a rule, not from duplication. The Braille Institute tests Atkinson under a blur filter to prove legibility survives blur; Monolith should pass that test, not impose the blur. Gate any retained ghost behind the animator-scale/reduced-motion check and default it off when fontScale > 1.3.

### Design system and craft — 39 findings (12 critical, 18 high, 9 medium, 0 low)

#### [CRITICAL] Repair order #1: token governance before screens — role-named tokens and two functional hues, or every later fix is built on lying names

Color.kt:7 declares 'Strictly Zero-Green' as an invariant, Color.kt:18 and Color.kt:29 make the accent #F55314 and TokenAlert #D63E06 steps of the same orange hue, and Color.kt runs to 209 lines because hue-metaphor aliases (SolarAmber, BauhausBlue, BauhausYellow at Color.kt:114-165) all alias the same three tokens — so any new screen built today inherits lying names and a palette where 'celebrate' and 'danger' are pre-collided. Judged in deck.html and shield.html, the accent appears only as the slide cap, with no second hue available for any state a new repair would need to introduce.

Recommendation: Priority 1 — do this before any screen work: (a) delete every hue-metaphor alias and keep only role-named tokens, following IBM Carbon's rule that tokens are named by use ($text-primary, $support-error), never by colour poetry; (b) break Zero-Green for exactly two functional hues — a green success/held hue and a red distinct from the orange accent for failure — following Material 3's separation of primary, tertiary and error roles. Every later repair (state colour, charts, receipt verdicts) is blocked on this; building them on the current tokens re-locks the collision.

#### [CRITICAL] Sequence 1 — Tokens before screens: Theme/Color/Type is the root node, and repainting any screen before replacing it throws the work away

Theme.kt:76-79 defines ObsidianSolar, SunlitPaperLight and WarmIndigoDusk as the identical objects WarmTactileStudioColorScheme / SealedVaultNightColorScheme, and Theme.kt:17-74 never assigns surfaceBright, surfaceContainer or scrim slots that renders rely on (#FAF6F0 raised card in deck.html/receipt.html). Color.kt:97 onwards adds ~87 semantic aliases (ElectricIris = grey at Color.kt:119) over 19 real tokens. Type.kt:139-150 maps bodyLarge to a bold app-title style and labelLarge/Medium/Small all to the same 10sp PillBadge, so Material slots lie. ShieldMatrixScreen.kt:266,318,420,455 then bypasses the ladder with raw 11/12/13sp styles. Every destination in MainActivity.kt:409-470 sits inside this one MaterialTheme, so this layer is literally inherited by all six renders.

Recommendation: Do this first and touch no screen pixels until it lands: collapse Color.kt to Material 3's three tiers — reference palette (the 19 day + 19 night values), system roles (background, raised, recess, ink, accent, alert), and component tokens for chip/sled/slide/strip only; delete all alias names and the three fake schemes; assign every scheme slot including surfaceBright; rebuild Type.kt as a true ladder (72/50 display, 22 title, 15 body, 13 secondary, 10 plate) and forbid raw sp/dp in screens by lint. Material 3 ships ref→sys→comp precisely so a retheme is one layer, not six screen rewrites — Monolith currently has the tiers collapsed into one lying file.

#### [CRITICAL] ON/OFF is three different machines: routine cap, Park sled, and Deck keycap share no body, size or word placement

shield.html + park.html renders: Shield routine ON is a 48dp-wide pill with the word inside it; Park Sound/Shorts ON is an empty 76dp sled with ON printed outside it as a margin word. Source: RoutineRow toggle is a bespoke Box 48x32dp, radius 8dp, ink fill + 'ON' in Anonymous Pro 11sp — ShieldMatrixScreen.kt:710-714. Park's binary is SledSwitchView hosted at 76x34dp, radius 12dp, word rendered separately in Atkinson 15sp — ParkDrawer.kt:513-514 and ParkDrawer.kt:582-583. Deck adds a third body for a binary choice: FLOW/DONE are keycap Boxes, radius 8dp, surfaceVariant fill flipping to inkControlFill() — TactileDeckScreen.kt:719-720. Same thumb, same meaning, three unrelated objects to learn.

Recommendation: Pick ONE binary control and delete the other two bodies. Keep the sled (it is the app's signature hardware) at exactly 76x34dp/r12 with the state word always outside, and rebuild the Routine toggle and the Deck FLOW key as that same SledSwitchView in chrome mode. If a space cannot fit 76dp, shrink the row, not the control. Follow Material 3, which ships exactly one Switch composable for every on/off in the system, and Braun under Rams/Lubs, where by the ET66 every non-circular control had been eliminated so one key shape meant one action everywhere.

#### [CRITICAL] FIX — the most urgent action — wears three bodies: a 48dp Sora bar in Park, an invisible tappable sentence on the Deck, and plain header print

park.html render: FIX is a full-width solid bar. deck.html render: the same repair on the Deck is an unboxed sentence under the slide. Source: Park FIX is a bespoke Box, 48dp high, radius 8dp, inkControlFill(), label 'FIX — {item.boardName}' in PrimaryButtonTextStyle (Sora Bold 15sp) — ParkDrawer.kt:428-458. It does NOT use the app's own button, BlockitActionChip (42dp, radius 12dp, Atkinson 12sp — MonolithCustomComponents.kt:170-201). The Deck's fix is RefusalSentenceSlot: bare Atkinson Bold 15sp text 'BLOCKING IS OFF — TAP TO FIX' with a clickable modifier and no container, fill or border at all — MonolithCustomComponents.kt RefusalSentenceSlot and refusalSentenceFor() (FIX_ACCESSIBILITY/FIX_USAGE). A third door, the header GUARD line, is also tappable print with no affordance.

Recommendation: Make FIX one recognisable object everywhere: the Park bar's form (full-width or chip-width ink bar, 48dp, radius 8dp, Sora 15sp, 'FIX — {NAME}') promoted to a shared FixKey composable, and use that exact bar in the Deck sentence slot's space and in the Airlock/Guard surfaces. Retire the tappable-sentence form entirely — a sentence may explain above the bar, it must never BE the button. Reference: Apple HIG consistency rule that elements with similar functions must look similar, and London Underground wayfinding, where the emergency/help action keeps one colour, one shape and one word at every station so it is found under stress without relearning.

#### [CRITICAL] Equal-width word-hardware only works because English control words are four letters long

The primary controls are sized by English word length, then frozen. ShieldCapSelector.kt hardcodes words = STUDY/WORK/SLEEP and splits the track into equal thirds: cellW = (maxWidth - pad*2)/3, cap .height(30.dp), text 11sp letterSpacing 1.sp. BlockitSuitcaseAndSwitchesViews.kt:427-435 hardcodes stops SHUT/PEEK/OPEN drawn centred in slotW = (168dp - 6dp)/3 = 54dp at sp(10f). MonolithRailView.kt:34 hardcodes WORDS = DECK/SHIELD/TASKS/LEDGER drawn at sp(10f) with letterSpacing 0.2 in equal segments; shield.html and deck.html renders show all three systems as identical equal-width hardware. German breaks the premise: SHUT (4) → GESPERRT (8), PEEK (4) → VORSCHAU (8), TASKS (5) → AUFGABEN (8), SLEEP (5) → SCHLAFEN (8) need ~2x the slot at the same size, and at 200% font scale even English needs 2x. Hindi breaks the other axis: Devanagari in the same 30dp/34dp caps needs ~1.5x line height the caps do not have. There is no measured-width path anywhere — Canvas paints use fixed centres, Compose caps use weight(1f).

Recommendation: Decouple position from word length, the way Material 3 SegmentedButton and iOS UISegmentedControl do: segment widths proportional to measured localized label width (with min/max clamps), track scrolls or wraps when the sum exceeds the screen. If the equal-hardware look must survive, do what Braun/Teenage Engineering hardware does — make the stop language-neutral (detent position + filled/hollow glyph, already present as the 8dp margin glyph in the catalogue row) and print the full localized word once, in a wrapping label beside/below the control that is free to grow. Do not ship a control whose usability depends on a translation being four letters long.

#### [CRITICAL] ShieldCapSelector is a counterfeit sled: it copies the sled family's silhouette with none of its recess, contact shadow or touch-down answer, and only moves after the finger leaves

ShieldCapSelector.kt:106-113 paints the track as one flat surfaceVariant fill and lines 138-157 the cap as one flat inkControlFill fill: no recess shading, no contact shadow, no lit top edge — shield.html shows the cap sitting flush and print-flat in its track. The real Canvas sleds it copies carry exactly that depth kit: BlockitSuitcaseAndSwitchesViews.kt:126-137 pools shadow at the track's top inner edge and light at the bottom, lines 141-155 add a +2dp contact shadow and a 0x59FFFFFF lit top edge to the thumb. Worse, the selector's tap zones (ShieldCapSelector.kt:162-175) are plain clickable{} — they fire on release, play a click and call onSelect — and the cap only then travels via animateDpAsState specA(260) at lines 86-92. There is no DOWN state at all, on the screen's primary selector, in an app whose own rail spec (MonolithRailView.kt:88-91) rules that 'DOWN answers within the frame'.

Recommendation: Stop counterfeiting the sled in Compose: either host the selector in Canvas beside the real sled family, or port the kit exactly — 1.4dp dark top-inner and light bottom-inner recess lines, +2dp contact shadow under the cap, 1.1dp lit top edge — and add a finger-bound press: on DOWN the tapped segment's cap dips 1dp toward the stop (shadow gap closing, per the hub law) before the 260ms throw runs on release. Apple's segmented control and Material 3's segmented button both acknowledge the touch-down before committing the travel; Monolith's rail already demands it of itself.

#### [CRITICAL] The six-size type ladder is a comment, not a system: 141 inline font sizes in 19 values, including fractional half-steps the ladder explicitly forbids

Type.kt:60-63 declares 'six sizes only - 104 / 72 / 50 / 22 / 15 / 10 - no two tiers within 1.4x', yet grep finds 141 inline fontSize assignments outside the theme using 19 distinct sizes: 11.sp x33, 12.sp x20, 13.sp x19, 10.5.sp x12, 12.5.sp x10, 11.5.sp x7, 14.sp, 17.sp, 96.sp, 88.sp, 9.sp, 16.sp, 24.sp. MaterialTheme.typography is consumed at only ~25 sites while screens set fontFamily+fontSize by hand (e.g. DrawerScreen.kt:225-475 repeats AnonymousPro/Atkinson + size per Text). Canvas is a third ladder: BlockitSuitcaseAndSwitchesViews.kt:155 sp(9.5f), BlockitTowerFadersAndCatalogViews.kt:185 sp(10.5f). The fractional 10.5/11.5/12.5 half-steps sit within 1.05-1.1x of their neighbours, exactly the ratio collapse the ladder was written to forbid; deck.html renders the result as a Deck where eyebrow, guard and body copy are visually near-identical weights of small mono.

Recommendation: Enforce the ladder mechanically, following Material 3's role-based type scale (display/headline/title/body/label consumed only via MaterialTheme.typography): delete every inline fontSize/fontFamily in screens, map the 141 sites onto the existing 7 named styles (add at most one Caption style at 12sp if a real need survives), add a detekt/lint rule banning '.sp' literals outside ui/theme, and make Canvas Paints read the same 6 sizes via sp() constants named after the styles. Any size not on the ladder becomes a compile error, not a comment.

#### [CRITICAL] The signature controls cannot be themed: Canvas carries a hand-copied second palette that has already drifted from the Compose tokens, judged by three different night-mode oracles

BlockitCoreViews.kt:56-102 hand-copies all 38 palette values as Int constants (LIGHT_*/NIGHT_*) duplicating Color.kt:12-50, resolved through 20 tok*() functions keyed on a manually-set isNightMode Boolean (BlockitCoreViews.kt:106,128-170) assigned at 6 separate AndroidView sites (MainActivity.kt:708, TactileDeckScreen.kt:691,990, ShieldMatrixScreen.kt:1073, FocusSequencerScreen.kt:194). The copies have already drifted: Color.kt:23 TokenColorOnSurfaceVariant = 0xFF5F5856 with a comment claiming '(R:120, G:113, B:112)' - which is 0xFF787170, the value the Canvas copy actually holds (BlockitCoreViews.kt LIGHT_ON_SURFACE_VARIANT = 0xFF787170). So Compose secondary text and Canvas secondary text on the same Deck are two different greys. A third night oracle compounds it: Theme.kt:113 picks night by 'darkTheme || isFocusSessionActive', Canvas by the passed Boolean, and components by re-deriving luminance()<0.5f at MonolithCustomComponents.kt:315,321,553,846 and ShieldCapSelector.kt:74.
