Recommendation: Single-source the palette the way Material 3 / Nothing OS do - one ColorScheme, every surface reads it: delete the LIGHT_*/NIGHT_* Int table, have BlockitCanvasView resolve colours from the host's MaterialTheme.colorScheme captured in the AndroidView factory (or migrate the wheel/slide/tower to Compose Canvas, which reads the scheme directly), delete all luminance()<0.5f night detection in favour of one LocalNightMode CompositionLocal set by MyApplicationTheme, and add a unit test asserting Canvas-resolved and Compose-resolved values are identical for all 19 roles in both modes.

#### [CRITICAL] One dial, two suns: the wheel rim is lit from azimuth 245.2° while the hub core is lit from 315°

BlockitCoreViews.kt:593-637 grades the socket ring and chamfer catch on a lamp fixed at azimuth 245.2 (alpha 0.16 + 0.66 cos^3(az - 245.2)); the knurl specular uses the same lamp at :693-703. But the hub core at :865-866 is 'REGISTERED at azimuth 315 — deliberately NOT the lamp's 245.2; the Register keeps the two apart'. One physical object is therefore lit from two directions 70 degrees apart: the rim says light falls from lower-left, the hub says upper-right. Tanaka's first discipline is that flat planes under one light produce reflections a viewer can trust and learn; contradictory painted light can never be learned, only noticed as wrongness.

Recommendation: Pick one lamp for the whole app and delete the second register: re-centre the hub core's specular wedge on azimuth 245.2 with the same cos^3 falloff as the rim, and add a single constant (LAMP_AZIMUTH) in BlockitCoreViews.kt that the socket, chamfer, knurl and hub all read, so no future surface can register its own private sun.

#### [CRITICAL] No parameter-lock layer: a hand-set tier and a loadout-written tier are drawn — and stored — as the same object

Elektron marks every deviation from the track's base value: hold a trig and the locked parameter's graphics invert, the trig key blinks, and the PARAMETER page key lights red to show where the lock lives — locked and inherited values are never drawn the same way. Monolith has no lock layer at all. BlockedAppEntity carries exactly one flattened value (MonolithModels.kt:236-247: isBlocked + blockTier, resolvedTier derived from those alone), and applySmartLoadout (MonolithRepository.kt:1126) rewrites every row in place via app.copy(blockTier = tier.name) computed from category/name substrings. On the Shield render every rocker — hand-set, category-guessed, loadout-written, routine-written — is pixel-identical, and the YOUR RULES slip prints only the resolved word. The machine itself cannot answer 'which of these did I decide?' because the distinction was destroyed at write time.

Recommendation: Split the tier into two stored layers: baselineTier (what the loadout/category last wrote) and lockTier (nullable hand override). Render locked rows inverted, Elektron-style: ink-filled name plate, solid margin brick even for PEEK, and a 'LOCK' tick on the rocker. Long-pressing a row prints its source line ('HAND SET · SURVIVES LOADOUT' / 'FROM STUDY LOADOUT · TAP TO LOCK'). Re-applying a loadout rewrites only unlocked rows, and the loadout cap gains a permanent second line: 'N LOCKS HELD'.

#### [CRITICAL] The system's only joint is an untyped string, and a part that doesn't fit is silently swapped for STUDY

The one load-bearing connection between two major parts — which loadout a routine arms — is a free String, not a fitting: RoutineEntity.loadoutName is a raw String column (MonolithModels.kt:556), and it is re-interpreted independently in three places, each with a silent substitution. At materialise time, MonolithRepository.kt:1087-1089 does runCatching { SmartLoadout.valueOf(desired.loadoutName) }.getOrDefault(SmartLoadout.STUDY) and arms that. The editor's cycle verb does the same fallback (MonolithViewModel.kt:1521-1527), and the Shield row's label does it a third time: routineLoadoutLabel is when(loadoutName) { "WORK_SPRINT" -> "WORK"; "SLEEP" -> "SLEEP"; else -> "STUDY" } (ShieldMatrixScreen.kt:636-640). A 606 component either engages the E-profile rail exactly or it visibly does not fit; nothing is ever quietly replaced with a different shelf. Here, any value the joint cannot parse — a renamed loadout, a corrupt row, a future version's new part — is silently seated as STUDY in the label, in the editor and at the moment of arming, so the row can print one intent while a different protection actually runs.

Recommendation: Make the joint a real fitting: replace loadoutName with a typed loadoutId referencing a loadout row, migrate existing strings once, and delete all three fallback interpreters. Where a routine's referenced loadout cannot be resolved, render the routine row in an explicit UNFITTED state (loadout slot shown empty, routine cannot arm, one tap opens the picker to re-seat it) — a visible misfit, never a silent substitution with STUDY.

#### [CRITICAL] No module generates Monolith's sizes — half-point type, off-declaration radii and a second secret Canvas scale prove the 'system' is eyeballing in a mono font

Crouwel's Stedelijk identity ran for two decades on one modular grid that generated every poster and catalogue; a grid's test is that no value exists the module cannot produce. Monolith fails that test everywhere: Type.kt:57-62 declares six sizes, yet call sites use 10.5sp (12 sites), 11.5sp (7) and 12.5sp (10) — half-point nudges no module yields. Theme.kt:80 claims 'Strictly two corner radii across the app: 12.dp and 24.dp', yet call sites draw RoundedCornerShape(8.dp) 7 times, 9.dp 3 times, 3.dp and 2.dp besides. A third, undeclared scale lives in Canvas: sp(9.5f) at BlockitSuitcaseAndSwitchesViews.kt:155 and BlockitTowerFadersAndCatalogViews.kt:106, sizes the Compose ladder has never heard of.

Recommendation: Impose one generative module: a 5sp type module and a 4dp space/radius module. Round every half-point size to the module (10.5→10 or 15, 11.5/12.5→15 for body, 10 for plates), delete the 2/3/8/9dp radii in favour of 12/24, move all Canvas sp() sizes into the same constants file as the Compose ladder, and add a lint check that fails the build on any fontSize or corner radius not in the module table.

#### [HIGH] The same search field is reinvented at two heights, two voices and two edge treatments on adjacent destinations

Shield's app filter is a 40dp recessed box with no border and an Atkinson 13sp sentence-case placeholder, 'Filter apps…' (ShieldMatrixScreen.kt:443-461; shield.html). Drawer's task search is a 48dp box with a 1dp outlineVariant border and an Anonymous Pro 12sp letterspaced uppercase placeholder, 'TYPE TO FIND A TASK' (DrawerScreen.kt:537-556; drawer.html). Same user intent — type to narrow a list — drawn as two different objects at two heights, in two typefaces, with two different edge treatments, on adjacent destinations.

Recommendation: Ship one MonolithSearchField component and use it in both places, the way Material 3 defines search as a single component with one fixed height (56dp) reused across every surface: take the Drawer's bordered 48dp version — the border matches the app's ruled-print language — set the placeholder in Atkinson sentence case on both screens, and delete the Shield's borderless 40dp variant. A user who learns the field on one destination should never meet a stranger wearing its job on the next.

#### [HIGH] Objecthood exists on exactly one screen: leave the Deck and the ritual object collapses into generic admin tables wearing stone colours

deck.html shows real instrument craft on the Deck — knurled wheel rim with alternating light/dark ticks, detent numerals, ghost-embossed 72sp hero. shield.html shows what replaces it one tap away: routines as 42dp chips (ShieldMatrixScreen via MonolithCustomComponents BlockitActionChip), app rulings as a 168x34dp three-stop rocker pill repeated ten times, and 'YOUR RULES' as dot-leader ledger lines — a spreadsheet, not an object. drawer.html is ruled text rows end to end; park.html is a permission checklist (GRANTED/MISSING at 15sp) above sled switches. No wheel geometry, no slab, no seal mark, no material contrast recurs on Shield, Drawer or Park — the tactile language is a Deck-only costume change, and the screens where the user configures the ritual and reviews its history are indistinguishable in kind from any settings app recoloured warm-grey. Teenage Engineering's OP-1 never drops its object language: tape, synth, mixer and settings are all drawn as the same machine's panels, with the same knobs and print discipline throughout.

Recommendation: Extend the Deck's object grammar to the other three rooms instead of inventing new controls: render Shield loadouts as the Deck wheel's detent language (a cap/notch selector drawn like the wheel's rim, not chips), give the Drawer a physical 'shelf' treatment for stored days (the slab's edge as the day divider), and seat Park's board inside the same raised instrument panel as the Deck hero card. Rule for the system: if a control could be pasted into a stock Material settings app unchanged, it fails — redraw it from the wheel, slide and imprint parts kit.

#### [HIGH] One language, one slab: radii and layout are fixed dp constants with no scale, so the identity cannot stretch to any second form factor

ui/theme/Theme.kt:88-95 locks the whole shape language to two constants — 'Strictly two corner radii across the app: 12.dp and 24.dp' — with no spacing scale, no window-size classes (no WindowSizeClass or adaptive layout anywhere in app/src/main/java; the only BoxWithConstraints is ShieldCapSelector.kt:77 dividing one selector into thirds), and every render (deck.html, shield.html, receipt.html) composed for a single 390x844 slab. TE's Field system is the counter-proof: one language stretched across five machines of radically different sizes (TX-6 at 90mm wide, TP-7's reel-dominated face, CM-15 slab) because its rules are proportions and labelling discipline, not fixed dp values. Monolith's rules are values, so a foldable, tablet, watch face or printed receipt card each requires inventing a new language instead of scaling this one.

Recommendation: Convert the constants into ratios before a second form factor forces it: define radius, hairline and cap-height as fractions of the wheel diameter (the product's true module — e.g. large radius = wheel/14, small = wheel/28), add one WindowSizeClass breakpoint where the Deck's pinned strip becomes a side column, and prove the system by shipping the receipt slip at two physical sizes (phone sheet and a 58mm thermal-print width) from the same tokens. A language that has survived one rescale can survive 2030's hardware; one that has never been scaled cannot.

#### [HIGH] 'Selected' is encoded five different ways — fill, fill+marker+tick, bold+underline bar, and rail cap — with no shared signal

shield.html + deck.html renders show all five side by side. (1) ShieldCapSelector: travelling ink cap 30dp/r9 + 10x2dp marker line inside the cap + a 2x8dp tick under the track that darkens — ShieldCapSelector.kt:136 (cap) and its tick row. (2) FilterWord on the same Shield screen: no container at all, selected = Bold + ink colour + an 18x2dp bar 3dp below — ShieldMatrixScreen.kt FilterWord. (3) Routine day letters and loadout word: selected = ink fill via BlockitActionChip(isPrimaryInk=true) — ShieldMatrixScreen.kt:748-756. (4) Tasks KeyCap: selected = ink fill, 36dp/r9 — FocusSequencerScreen.kt:824-836. (5) Bottom rail: selected = a 65x36dp surfaceBright cap, radius 12dp, no marker, no tick — deck.html rail and MonolithRailView.kt:98. Five encodings for one concept, two of them on the same screen.

Recommendation: legislate one selected grammar and apply it without exception: selected = ink fill + on-ink word, nothing else. Strip the cap selector's marker line and under-track ticks, strip FilterWord's underline bar (give filter words the ink-fill chip body instead), and re-cut the rail cap to the same radius (9dp) and fill as the loadout cap. Reference: the Swiss International Style / Müller-Brockmann grid systems and Nothing OS's dot-matrix UI, where a single mark — one filled state — is reused for every selection so the eye never decodes a new signal; Teenage Engineering does the same on the OP-1, where one orange highlight means 'active parameter' across every screen.

#### [HIGH] There is no row system: 40/48/54dp rows ruled by two different hairlines (18% ink in Park, 46% outline elsewhere, none on the slip)

All renders confirm different row pitches and two different hairline inks. Park board rows: 48dp, ruled by ParkHairline() = onBackground at 18% alpha — ParkDrawer.kt:659 and ParkDrawer.kt:776-781. Shield catalogue rows: 54dp, bottom hairline in outlineVariant (#615B5A at ~46%) — ShieldMatrixScreen.kt:1083. Shield slip lines: 40dp, no hairline at all — ShieldMatrixScreen.kt:945. Drawer StoredRows: content-driven height with 6dp vertical padding + HorizontalDivider in outlineVariant — DrawerScreen.kt StoredRow (~line 886). Routine rows: no hairline, separated only by 16dp gaps in shield.html. A list in this app can be 40, 48 or 54dp tall and its rule can be 18% black, 46% grey, or absent, with no semantic difference behind any of it.

Recommendation: Fix a row scale and one rule: data rows 48dp, tappable catalogue rows 56dp, print/ledger lines 40dp — each height reserved for one job and used nowhere else — and a single hairline token (outlineVariant) for every divider on every screen; delete ParkHairline's private 18% ink. Reference: Kinneir & Calvert's Transport alphabet signage and the British Rail corporate identity manual, which held one letterform, one arrow and one rule weight across thousands of different signs, and Josef Müller-Brockmann's grid systems, where row pitch is the system, not a per-page decision.

#### [HIGH] The wheel's knurled rim is 120 simulated metal teeth — with two deliberately faked defects — encoding nothing

BlockitCoreViews.kt:667-722 draws a knurled rim: ~120 radial teeth at a filed 3-degree pitch around the whole 288dp wheel (TactileDeckScreen.kt:705, height 288.dp), each tooth lit by a simulated fixed lamp at azimuth 245.2 with a cos^3 specular curve, and the comment at :671 states teeth 17 and 83 are deliberately given a compile-time 'flare' so they 'sit visibly wrong inside the bright zone'. The same comment block (:673) admits 'the knurl is screen-fixed material' — it does not rotate with the value, marks no minute, and grips nothing, because the surface is glass. In deck.html the wheel SVG carries well over a hundred alternating black/white rim strokes purely as this texture, surrounding the separate, real detent scale drawn at BlockitCoreViews.kt:742.

Recommendation: Delete the knurl layer outright — all ~120 teeth, the lamp simulation and the two manufactured-defect teeth. A physical knurl earns its pixels on a Braun or Teenage Engineering metal shaft because fingers need grip to turn it; Apple's iPod click wheel, the canonical touch-wheel, is dead smooth because texture on a touch surface does no work. Keep the single true detent scale and reader dot; the wheel loses nothing functional and stops lying about being machined metal.

#### [HIGH] Every preset's break number is decorative fiction: breakMinutes is defined in the enum and read nowhere, while the real break is hardcoded 10 minutes

MonolithModels.kt:61-71 gives each StudyModePreset a breakMinutes and a printed badge ('5m Break' for POMODORO_25_5, '10m Break' for DEEP_50_10, 'Full Session' for EXAM_90). A repo-wide search shows breakMinutes has zero readers outside its declaration. The actual break is a separate hardcoded constant: MonolithRepository.kt:110 SAFE_BREAK_DURATION_SECONDS = 10*60, MonolithModels.kt:401 span math uses (blocks-1)*600, and TactileDeckScreen.kt:322-325 hardcodes '(studyBlocksCount - 1) * 10' with the comment calling them 'the 10-minute Safe Breaks'. A user who picks the '25m Sprint · 5m Break' preset is therefore sold a 5-minute break the system will never deliver.

Recommendation: Delete the fiction or make it true: drive Safe Break duration, span math and the hero from preset.breakMinutes as the single source, the way Cirillo's 25/5 cadence and every Pomodoro timer (default 25 focus / 5 short break / 15 long break) keep the printed cadence identical to the enforced cadence. If the break must stay fixed at 10, remove breakMinutes and the '5m Break' badge from the preset vocabulary entirely — a label the engine ignores is worse than no label.

#### [HIGH] The theme never crosses the AndroidView bridge: Canvas views get one Boolean and re-derive colour from their own duplicated palette constants

Compose screens read MaterialTheme.colorScheme (Theme.kt:17-74, built from Color.kt tokens), but every Canvas control receives only `view.isNightMode = groundNight` / `effectiveNight` (MainActivity.kt:708, TactileDeckScreen.kt:691 and :990, ShieldMatrixScreen.kt:1073, FocusSequencerScreen.kt:194). Behind that Boolean, BlockitCanvasView carries a second complete copy of the 19-token palette as raw int constants (BlockitCoreViews.kt:63-70 LIGHT_BG/LIGHT_SURFACE/…, tokBg()/tokAccent() selectors at :128-162) — so the 'single token system' exists only in the Compose minority of the UI, and the majority surface re-implements it by copy. Material You's whole design-system premise is one ColorScheme object consumed by every component; Monolith has the object and then routes around it. Any palette revision must be made in Color.kt, in the Canvas constants, and in the XML copies, and nothing in the build fails when they drift.

Recommendation: Kill the duplicated constants and put one token source under both worlds: pass the resolved light/night token lists from Color.kt into the Canvas views (a setPalette(tokens) call in each AndroidView update block, replacing the isNightMode Boolean), and delete the LIGHT_*/NIGHT_* constant block from BlockitCoreViews.kt. Until the views are migrated to Compose, the bridge should carry the actual scheme — 19 ints — not a Boolean that invites each view to remember its own copy of the palette.

#### [HIGH] MonolithShapes is dead code: zero call sites use the shape token while 40+ literal RoundedCornerShape calls re-type the radius system - and quietly break its two-radius law

Theme.kt:79-86 defines MonolithShapes (12dp/24dp) and passes it to MaterialTheme at Theme.kt:121, but grep finds zero usages of MaterialTheme.shapes anywhere in the app. Instead there are 33+ literal RoundedCornerShape constructions (19 at 12.dp, 14 at 24.dp) re-typed per card, plus law-breaking radii the 'strictly two radii' rule (Theme.kt:79, BlockitCoreViews.kt header) forbids: ParkDrawer.kt:237 RoundedCornerShape(16.dp), ParkDrawer.kt:293 (2.dp) and :430 (8.dp), ShieldCapSelector.kt:135 (9.dp), FocusSequencerScreen.kt:834-836 (9.dp), ShieldMatrixScreen.kt:712 (8.dp), TactileDeckScreen.kt:718,825 (8.dp). Because no call site references the token, changing the radius system means editing 40+ sites, so it will never change - the shape language is frozen by copy-paste, visible in deck.html/shield.html renders where nominally identical cards are rebuilt shape-by-shape.

Recommendation: Follow Material 3's Shapes contract as designed: replace every literal RoundedCornerShape with MaterialTheme.shapes.medium / .large, fold the 8dp and 9dp chips into shapes.small, give ParkDrawer's sheet the 24dp large top-corner treatment (deleting the one-off 16dp), and add a lint ban on RoundedCornerShape( outside Theme.kt. One edit in MonolithShapes should then re-radius the entire app, which is the test of whether a token exists at all.

#### [HIGH] There is no spacing system at all: 328 raw dp literals in ~40 values, no spacing token file, and the renders already show 10dp gaps living beside the claimed universal 12dp unit

ui/theme/ contains Color.kt, Type.kt, MonolithCurves.kt and Theme.kt - colour, type, motion and shape all have token files, spacing has none. Grep counts 328 '.dp' literals across screens/components in ~40 distinct values (12.dp x54, 1.dp x34, 8.dp x30, 24.dp x22, 6.dp x21, 10.dp x17, 16.dp x16, plus off-grid 3.dp, 5.dp, 9.dp, 14.dp, 18.dp, 34.dp, 52.dp, 53.dp, 47.dp one-offs). BlockitCoreViews.kt:122-125 hardcodes its own gapUnit = dp(12f) for Canvas, unconnected to any Compose value. deck.html confirms the drift on screen: the instrument card uses gap:10px and padding 18px/16px against the claimed universal 12dp gap unit, so adjacent Deck sections breathe at 8, 10, 12 and 18dp simultaneously with no rule a new screen could follow.

Recommendation: Create the missing fourth token file, MonolithSpacing, on the 8pt-grid discipline Material Design and Swiss grid systems (Muller-Brockmann) both use: a closed set {2 hairline, 4, 8, 12, 16, 24, 32} exposed as CompositionLocal spacing, migrate padding/Arrangement.spacedBy call sites screen by screen (Deck first), share the same constants into Canvas via dp(MonolithSpacing.M), and lint-ban raw '.dp' literals in screens. Delete the one-off values (47, 52, 53, 34dp) by rounding each layout to the nearest grid step and re-checking against the renders.

#### [HIGH] The 'closed' motion vocabulary leaks at its own call sites: an un-tokenised 650ms duration, an easing curve invented inline, and literal tweens scattered through components

MonolithCurves.kt:10-16 declares durations 'strictly chosen from {180, 260, 280, 420, 520} ms', then its own header admits 140/110/250 were added, the file adds DURATION_1050 (line 29), ReturnHome's comment (lines 44-46) states its '650ms duration is a literal at the animator, never tokenised, no Compose twin', and MonolithKin adds 160/120/240/90/150ms more. Call sites bypass even that expanded set: MonolithCustomComponents.kt:727 tween(90), :826 scale.animateTo with tween(110, easing = CubicBezierEasing(0.9f, 0f, 1f, 0.4f)) - a fourth, unnamed easing curve invented inline that exists in neither the View interpolator set nor the Compose easing set - plus tween(240) at :843. Motion therefore has the same disease as colour: a proclaimed closed vocabulary with sanctioned exceptions accumulating until the vocabulary describes nothing.

Recommendation: Close the set the way Teenage Engineering closes a control layout - nothing unnamed ships: tokenise the 650ms return and the CustomComponents 90/110/240 tweens into MonolithCurves/MonolithKin with names for their joints, promote the inline CubicBezierEasing(0.9,0,1,0.4) to a named curve with both a PathInterpolator and Compose twin or replace it with EasingThrow, rewrite the MonolithCurves header to state the true full vocabulary in one table, and lint-ban tween(<number>) and CubicBezierEasing( outside the theme package.

#### [HIGH] Seven invented control mechanisms where two would do: every screen teaches a new grammar for the same few choices

Binary and few-way choice is re-invented per surface: SledSwitchView (ui/views/BlockitSuitcaseAndSwitchesViews.kt:32) throws a sled for on/off in PARK, AppRowSledToggleView (same file:190) rocks for the 3-tier choice per app, ShieldCapSelector (ui/components/ShieldCapSelector.kt:56) slides a cap for the same 3-tier choice at loadout level, and the routine row uses a fourth mechanism, a 48x32 ink 'ON' cap (design-renders/shield.html). Around them sit RotaryWheelView (ui/views/BlockitCoreViews.kt:371), SlideToStartView (same file:1444), Emergency60sValveView (SuitcaseAndSwitchesViews.kt:532) and MonolithRailView (ui/views/MonolithRailView.kt:98) — seven bespoke gesture grammars (rotate, slide, throw, rock, hold, cap-drag, rail-travel), each with its own affordance, timing and failure modes, none of whose skill transfers to the next screen. Rams' tenth principle — as little design as possible, less but better — and his fourth (a product is understandable when its structure is clarified) fail together: Braun repeated one knob/slider grammar across a whole catalogue precisely so the hand learned the maker once.

Recommendation: Collapse the grammar to two controls and delete the rest: the cap selector becomes the only N-way choice everywhere (loadout, per-app tier, routine state as a 2-stop variant), and the sled becomes the only binary throw (PARK margins, routine on/off). Redraw the Shield app rows with the cap selector at row scale, retire AppRowSledToggleView and the routine ON cap entirely, and keep wheel, slide and valve only because each is a genuinely different verb (set a quantity, commit, endure) — no fourth way of saying 'choose one of these' may be drawn again.

#### [HIGH] No construction grammar: five unrelated mark dialects mean no second hand could ever extend the system — Aicher's extensibility test failed

The marks that do exist share no module, stroke or angle set: catalogue brick = 8dp square, 1.4dp stroke (BlockitSuitcaseAndSwitchesViews.kt:329-340); rail armed marker = 4dp stroked circle with 1.8dp filled centre (MonolithRailView.kt:285-295); valve bank seams = 1.5dp lines (BlockitSuitcaseAndSwitchesViews.kt:666-672); ShieldCapSelector cap marker = a 10x2dp dash (design-renders/shield.html, cap .marker); tower bricks = a 7-per-floor grid unrelated to any of the above (BlockitTowerFadersAndCatalogViews.kt:92-116). Five surfaces, five private geometries, each hand-drawn in its own Canvas code.

Recommendation: Publish one construction sheet before drawing any new sign: a 24-unit square module, stroke fixed at 3 units, angles restricted to 0°/45°/90°, one circle module (the seal ring) and one square module (the brick) as the only primitives, optical sizes at 16/24/48dp derived by stroke scaling, never redrawn. Re-cut the five existing marks onto it — brick first, rail target second (ring + centre dot already wants to be the seal ring), cap dash last. Acceptance test, Aicher's own: hand the sheet, without examples of the new sign, to someone who has never seen the app and have them draw 'cooldown running'; if their drawing matches the team's, the system exists.

#### [HIGH] Joints are drawn lines, not shadow gaps: every panel meeting is a printed hairline pretending to be a recess

In cast concrete, panels never meet at an applied trim line — they meet at a recessed shadow gap, a real void the light falls into, and that void is what articulates one mass from the next. Monolith has no void joints at all: separation is universally a stroked 1dp hairline (Color.kt:23-24, outline and outlineVariant at 0x75 alpha) — the header band's 1px rule (deck.html), the Proof Strip's three 1px cell dividers (deck.html, receipt.html frame 3), the Drawer's row dividers (drawer.html), PARK's hairlines at onBackground 18% (park.html). A line is decoration laid ON a surface; a gap is the surface removed. Because every joint is ink, the screens read as one printed sheet with ruled lines, however heavy the type on it.

Recommendation: Convert the three structural joints to real gaps and delete their strokes: (1) Proof Strip cells separated by 6dp channels of the recess colour (day #D8D1CB, night #100E0C) with no divider line; (2) the header band separated from the Deck by an 8dp ground-coloured slot, the word MONOLITH sitting in the upper mass, GUARD in the lower; (3) Drawer day-groups separated by a 12dp empty band carrying only the day word, replacing the per-row hairlines inside a group. Keep hairlines only inside a single mass (the slip's dot leaders, the valve's bank seams), where a scribed line is honest.

#### [HIGH] The one real geometry system divides by remainder: the rail's module is 73.5dp, its cap 65.5dp, its travel 220.5dp

MonolithRailView.kt:16-23 documents its own arithmetic at the 390dp reference: margins 20, recess 350, track 342, 'segment 73.5 x4 = 294; PARK zone 48 at the track's end; cap 65.5 x 44. Travel DECK->LEDGER = 220.5dp'. The formula at MonolithRailView.kt:38-45 is (recessWidth - 2*INSET_DP - PARK_ZONE_DP)/4 and capWidth = segment - 8: the field is whatever is left after the margins, insets and an appended 48.dp PARK zone (MonolithRailView.kt:30) have taken theirs. A Müller-Brockmann module is chosen, then the format is built from it; here the format was chosen and the module is the residue, landing on half-dp boundaries that no content column, no other screen and no whole-pixel density can share.

Recommendation: Rebuild the rail from the module outward: delete PARK_ZONE_DP from the track division, set segment = 90.dp (one 80.dp column + one 10.dp gutter from the app-wide grid), cap = 80.dp wide x 44.dp high, cap left edges at 20/110/200/290.dp so each stop is literally a column of the page grid and the cap's left edge coincides with the content keyline beneath it. PARK keeps its existing second door — the header guard line already opens it (MainActivity.kt MonolithPullDownHeader onGuardLineTap) — instead of amputating a fifth, unequal field from the rail.

#### [HIGH] The wheel cannot be read from the wheel: 35 stops, only 6 engraved numerals, the real reading lives in a digital hero above it

BlockitCoreViews.kt:748 engraves ticks at every stop from 10 to 180 in 5-minute steps (35 stops), but BlockitCoreViews.kt:793-801 prints rim numerals 'at the majors only' — 30, 60, 90, 120, 150, 180. Stops at 10, 15, 20, 25, 40, 50 and 29 others carry a tick and no number, so the dial's position is illegible on the dial itself; the exact value exists only in the 72sp hero readout in deck.html. A Leica shutter dial engraves every speed it can stop at, because the dial IS the readout — it is set and verified by eye or fingertip with no second display consulted.

Recommendation: Make print and mechanism identical: cut the wheel to the stops it engraves. Keep 15, 30, 45, 60, 90, 120, 150, 180 as the full stop set (8 stops, spacing widened to match), each with its numeral at the reader position, majors at 30-minute intervals in heavier stroke. If 5-minute granularity must survive, engrave a numeral at every stop and delete the hero readout's duration figure, leaving the hero to print only the total span.

#### [HIGH] Withered as costume: the Deck spends its finest craft shading a fake machined socket and ghost-printing its numerals, while the age is only ever depicted, never used

BlockitCoreViews.kt:582-600 draws the wheel's socket as a graded ring computed from a cos^3 lamp curve (s follows 0.16 + 0.66 cos^3(azimuth - 245.2)) in a segmented per-frame pass, purely so the disc appears to sit in a machined recess; deck.html renders the hero total three times with offset ghost copies (g1/g2) to fake letterpress depth. The wheel file alone is 2,416 lines. None of this shading changes a value, a detent or a decision — it depicts aged hardware instead of using aged technology.

Recommendation: Cut the socket's segmented lamp-curve shading pass and the hero numeral's double ghost offset; draw the wheel as one flat disc with its teeth and detent scale only. Reassign that exact craft budget to the detent scale's legibility at arm's length — larger stop numerals, stronger active-stop contrast — the one surface the shading budget should have served.

#### [HIGH] No shared fitting: the same app is tiered by three different private rules depending on which subsystem touched it last

There is no single tier-resolution module that every part hangs from; three subsystems each re-derive an app's tier with different inputs, so the same app is fitted differently depending on which subsystem touched it last. applySmartLoadout decides by package/app-name substrings plus category: STUDY peeks anything whose name contains "youtube" or "chrome" (MonolithRepository.kt:1131-1141), and SLEEP leaves OPEN only names containing dialer/phone/clock/alarm/maps and locks everything else (MonolithRepository.kt:1152-1162). applyProfile ignores names entirely and resolves from the category CSV alone (MonolithRepository.kt:1243-1262). AppCatalogReconcile births a tier from a third rule — a 12-entry factory map by exact package, else a category default (AppCatalogReconcile.kt FACTORY_PRESETS and reconcile()). Chrome is born OPEN by the factory map, becomes PEEK_2M under STUDY's substring rule, and OPEN again under a profile whose CSV lacks its category. On the 606 rail, fit is one mechanical geometry every component shares; here 'fit' is three private opinions, and the user's wall of tiers is whichever opinion ran most recently.

Recommendation: Cut the three resolvers to one: a single TierResolution function (app row + loadout definition -> tier) that the catalogue reconcile, the loadout applier and the profile applier all call, with name-substring exemptions abolished in favour of explicit per-app exception rows stored on the loadout itself. Print the resolving rule on the Shield row's long-press sheet ('PEEK — exception on Deep Study') so a fit can be inspected, not just inherited.

#### [MEDIUM] The signature slide cap breaks concentric-corner geometry its own sibling controls obey

ui/views/BlockitCoreViews.kt:1730 (slide cap inset is 8dp: insetPx() = dp(8f)), :1756 (track drawn at radiusLarge = 24dp), :1777/:1805/:1808 (cap and trail drawn at radiusLarge - dp(4f) = 20dp). Concentric geometry — the rule Apple's design resources formalise and every iOS-native control Opal ships inherits — requires inner radius = outer radius minus inset = 16dp; at 20dp the cap's corners bulge against the track's corners, visible in deck.html's slide zone as a cap that looks swollen at its ends. The app obeys the rule elsewhere, proving it knows it: the rail's cap is 12dp inside a 16dp recess at 4dp inset (ui/views/MonolithRailView.kt:27-29, :247), and Shield's selector cap is 9dp in a 12dp track at 3dp pad (shield.html). The single most-touched control is the one exception.

Recommendation: Change the slide cap, trail and contact-shadow radii from radiusLarge - dp(4f) to radiusLarge - dp(8f) (16dp) in BlockitCoreViews.kt's SlideToStartView.onDraw so cap and track share one centre of curvature, and add the arithmetic as a comment-law next to the rail's correct example so future controls inherit it.

#### [MEDIUM] The background's framed square is designed for a rendering that never ships: every mask amputates it

The background layer's only artwork is an inset square frame at 18,18 to 90,90 in the 108dp canvas (drawable/ic_launcher_background.xml:11-13, commented as a 'Recessed Linen Geometric Grid Frame'). No shipped rendering ever shows it whole: OEM masks (Pixel circle, Samsung rounded square, squircle/teardrop variants) crop the 108dp canvas to a central shape, so the frame survives only as four clipped edge fragments whose lengths differ per device, and adaptive-icon parallax shifts the background against the foreground so the fragments drift out of register with the dial. Per Android's adaptive-icon spec only the central 66dp circle is guaranteed visible; everything outside it is mask-dependent. The icon was composed for the unmasked master file, a rendering no user ever sees.

Recommendation: Design in mask previews, not on the master canvas: delete the inset frame, make the background a flat full-bleed colour field, and keep every meaningful shape inside the central 66dp safe circle. Sign the icon off only against circle, squircle, rounded-square and teardrop mask renders side by side - if a detail does not survive all four, it does not ship.

#### [MEDIUM] Text entry is three heights, two border laws, and a typeface that changes when you start typing

shield.html + drawer.html renders. Shield search: 40dp, radius 12dp, surfaceVariant, NO border — ShieldMatrixScreen.kt:445. Shield add-a-site field on the same screen: 44dp, radius 12dp, surfaceVariant, WITH a 1dp outlineVariant border — ShieldMatrixScreen.kt:576-579. Drawer search: 48dp, radius 12dp, WITH border — DrawerScreen.kt search Box at 48dp (DrawerScreen.kt:537 in source order). Worse, the voice changes inside the field: Shield search placeholder is Atkinson 13sp sentence-case 'Filter apps…' and its typed text is Atkinson Bold 13sp, but the add-site field's typed text is Anonymous Pro 14sp (ShieldMatrixScreen.kt:591 ff.) while its placeholder is Atkinson 13sp — the user's own typing changes typeface mid-field; Drawer placeholder is Anonymous Pro 12sp tracked uppercase 'TYPE TO FIND A TASK' over Atkinson Bold 13sp input.

Recommendation: Ship one TextField component and forbid hand-rolled copies: 44dp, radius 12dp, surfaceVariant, 1dp outlineVariant border always (border = editable, no border = print), placeholder and input in the same family/weight/size (Atkinson 13sp, sentence case) so typing never changes voice, caret always ink. Rebuild all three fields from it and delete the local Boxes. Reference: Braun/Rams ET66 again in reverse — one key profile for digits and functions, distinguished only by colour grouping — and Material 3's single OutlinedTextField spec, where every text entry in an app is recognisably the same hole to type into.

#### [MEDIUM] Every app tier is stated four times per row — glyph, name styling, thumb fill and stop-word colour all say SHUT/PEEK/OPEN

shield.html catalogue row: one tier is encoded four times — margin glyph (solid 8×8 = SHUT, hollow = PEEK, none = OPEN), name weight/colour (bold ink = decided, regular grey = OPEN), rocker thumb position + fill (#252323/#615B5A/#FAF6F0), and the stop word's colour under the thumb. BlockitSuitcaseAndSwitchesViews.kt:324-340 draws the margin glyph ('the margin becomes the display'), :389-417 draws thumb fill and stop words SHUT/PEEK/OPEN. Park repeats the pattern at smaller scale: ParkDrawer.kt:479-530 prints 'SOUND EFFECTS', a margin word 'ON', and a sled thumb position for one boolean.

Recommendation: Keep one encoding per row: the rocker thumb (position + the word printed on it). Delete the margin glyph entirely and print every app name in the same Atkinson Bold 14sp ink — OPEN is shown by the thumb sitting on OPEN, not by demoting the name to grey regular. In Park, delete the margin ON/OFF word; the sled thumb is the state. Reference: the Braun ET66 calculator (Rams/Lubs) — a key's state is its position and label, never a second symbol in the margin restating it.

#### [MEDIUM] Park duplicates SHORTS + REELS as both a board line and a sled row, then parks a 10-line brand spec plate under the repair controls

park.html: SHORTS + REELS appears twice in one drawer — once as a board row ('SHORTS + REELS · OFF') in the interceptor family and again directly below the FIX key as a sled row ('SHORTS + REELS · OFF' + thumb). ParkDrawer.kt:537-610 contains both the board line and the sled row (comment at :537 admits the board line previously 'printed a state whose only source was memory'). Below them, ParkDrawer.kt:105-125 PLATE_HEAD/PLATE_BODY prints a 10-line spec plate — 'MONOLITH ML-01 / UNIT Nº 01 · BUILT FOR ONE USER · NOT FOR SALE' plus a restated manual ('HOLD: 60 SECONDS, BANKED EVERY 15', 'PEEK: 2 MINUTES, THEN SHUT AGAIN', 'COLOUR IS A VERB: …') — inside the drawer whose job is repairing a missing permission.

Recommendation: Two cuts. (1) Merge SHORTS + REELS into a single row: the board row IS the sled row — one row, name left, sled right, no separate interceptor listing above it. (2) Delete the spec plate from Park entirely; if the ML-01 plate is kept anywhere, it belongs on the Receipt or an About screen, never under a FIX key a user opened because something is broken. Reference: Nothing OS and Apple Settings — settings surfaces contain settings; brand plates and manuals live elsewhere, because a repair surface's restraint is its trust.

#### [MEDIUM] The sled deletes its state word as redundant but keeps all four layers of fake shading

SledSwitchView's PARK chrome mode strips the thumb's ARM/OFF word and the armed pip explicitly because 'a fact renders once' (BlockitSuitcaseAndSwitchesViews.kt:60-68) — yet it keeps all four cosmetic layers: top recess shadow line at 0x2E black, bottom light line at 0x2E white, a 2dp-offset contact shadow under the thumb at 0x38 black, and a lit top edge at 0x59 white (BlockitSuitcaseAndSwitchesViews.kt:131-155; visible as the ::before/::after lines and thumb shadow in park.html:85-91). The identical four-layer stack is then copy-pasted into AppRowSledToggleView's rocker (BlockitSuitcaseAndSwitchesViews.kt:383-415). The house's own ruling deletes information as redundant while treating decoration as irreducible — the shading survives every mode, the state word does not. Material 3's switch and Nothing OS's toggles carry state with position, fill and one outline on a flat track: no recess, no contact shadow, no lamp, and nothing is lost.

Recommendation: Apply the 'renders once' law to ornament too: delete the recess light/shadow lines and the thumb contact shadow from both sled views, leaving track fill, one hairline stroke, and the thumb with its colour state. If a depth cue is truly needed at the moment of the throw, keep only the lit top edge, and only while the throw animates — depth as feedback, not as wallpaper.

#### [MEDIUM] The two-radius shape law is written into Material slots that nothing ever reads, while the rendered screens quietly use 8dp and 20dp

Theme.kt:80-88 defines MonolithShapes collapsing all five Material shape categories to 12dp/24dp ('Strictly two corner radii across the app') and installs it in MaterialTheme — but a tree-wide grep finds no consumer of MaterialTheme.shapes outside Theme.kt, and there are no Material components in the app to consume it implicitly. The law survives in the Canvas layer only as another hardcoded copy (radiusSmall/radiusLarge at BlockitCoreViews.kt:122-123), and the faithful renders show it already broken in Compose-land: deck.html renders keycaps at border-radius 8px and the slide-to-arm cap at 20px, neither of which is 12 or 24. Dieter Rams' Braun work and Teenage Engineering's panels hold a radius system because every part is drawn from it; Monolith's exists as a comment and an unread theme slot.

Recommendation: Either enforce the law mechanically or repeal it honestly. Point every custom component at two shared Dp constants (RadiusSmall/RadiusLarge in the theme package) — keycaps and the slide cap included — and add a lint-style test that fails on any other RoundedCornerShape/drawRoundRect radius literal in the tree; the Canvas views already centralise radii in BlockitCoreViews.kt:122-123, so the sweep is small. If 8dp keycaps and the 20dp cap are judged better, amend the law to a named three-step scale (8/12/24) in Theme.kt and the guide — a broken strict law is worse than a kept loose one.

#### [MEDIUM] The Deck's hero numeral is inked three times for a shadow costume — the app's most important figure carries two full non-data copies of itself

TactileDeckScreen.kt:659-671 draws the same heroAnnotated string three times in the same style and size: once in heroShadowGhost (Color 0x99D8D1CB / 0x80000000), once in heroCatchGhost (0xB3FAF6F0 / 0x594A423C), and once in the real heroGlyph colour. Two-thirds of the ink on the single most-read number in the app — the session's total span — encodes no data at all; it is a printed drop-shadow/catch-light effect. At night the shadow copy is literal 50%-alpha black text under the figure, muddying the numeral's edge exactly when the Deck is read in the dark.

Recommendation: Print the hero numeral once, in heroGlyph only. If depth is wanted, achieve it with a single 1dp offset in the surface tone behind the card, not with two ghost copies of the glyphs themselves; reclaim the two erased layers as a flatter, higher-contrast figure at the same size.

#### [MEDIUM] The care is real but sealed in a private liturgy: 244 spec citations in the code point to documents the artifact does not contain

The shipped Kotlin carries 244 '§' citations across 34 files invoking authorities that are not in the app artifact: ReceiptState.kt's header rests the whole receipt contract on 'Zettel, reconciled §10-Z1..Z6; Nocke's discriminator; Reihe's issuance rules', and ReceiptSheet.kt's footer comment litigates a ruling by 'Ren' on 'Voss's wart' down to 0.25sp of letter-tracking. This is lavish care — 5,000+ comment lines — addressed entirely to initiates of an off-artifact scripture. Pirsig's test of care is the machine the next person has to maintain: a mechanic who opens Monolith cannot follow a single citation from inside the repo's app sources, so every design decision is unverifiable and therefore unchangeable with confidence.

Recommendation: Vendor the cited rulings into a docs/ folder inside the repo and add a CI check that every '§' citation in app/src resolves to a heading there; where a ruling governs something the user sees (the valve's banking, the token's weekly limit, the footer's YPT sentence), replace the citation in the composable with the plain-language reason — and reuse that same sentence as the in-app explanation string, so the rationale that currently lives only in comments is printed on the surface it governs.

### Signature moments and delight — 44 findings (12 critical, 24 high, 8 medium, 0 low)

#### [CRITICAL] The seal runs on three clocks that never meet: a 78ms haptic, a 1,000ms sound and a 1,050ms picture, so the moment of commitment has no single instant

TactileSoundEngine.kt:143-144 sets SEAL_THROW_TIMINGS to 0/24/38/16ms (78ms total, amplitudes 255 then 175) while renderSealBuffer (TactileSoundEngine.kt:208) renders a full 44,100-sample / 1,000ms buffer; TactileDeckScreen.kt:247-262 drives a separate 1,050ms shot with phases DEPARTURE <180ms, RECESSION <780ms, SETTLE to 1,050ms, and TactileDeckScreen.kt:588-596 shrinks the whole card to 0.94 scale and blurs it up to 6dp mid-shot. Felt, heard and seen commitment therefore end ~970ms apart; deck.html shows the static before/after but the ceremony itself is this smeared interval.

Recommendation: Collapse the ceremony into one mechanical event, the way the Braun AW10's crown (Lubs/Rams, 1989) engages the movement with a single pushed-in click — one position change, one click, movement started. Land bolt sound, both haptic segments and the cap's dock on the same frame (total event ≤200ms), delete the scale-and-blur recession entirely, and let any 1s reverb tail read as room ring after the clunk, never as the clunk itself. If a settle is kept, it must start after the dock frame, not overlap it.

#### [CRITICAL] Sealing — the app's defining act — leaves a 1dp line at 35% opacity, and the receipt that proves it carries no seal mark and no commit colour at all

MonolithCustomComponents.kt:775-779 states the imprint lip is 'the seal's one light change, a 1dp line present exactly while sealed'; :847-850 sets that line to NightColorSurfaceSheet at 0.35 alpha (day: surfaceBright at 0.5 alpha) and :881-891 draws it 1px tall. deck.html's caption confirms the unsealed imprint has 'no lip' — so sealed vs unsealed differ by one near-invisible hairline. The culminating artefact is worse: ReceiptSheet.kt:56-186 contains no accent/PrimaryContainer colour anywhere — the slip (receipt.html frame 1) is entirely ink and grey mono on porcelain, with no stamp, emblem or seal glyph, only the footer at :175-182. This breaks the app's own law printed in ParkDrawer.kt:113: 'COLOUR IS A VERB: ORANGE = COMMIT' — orange (#F55314, Color.kt:18) is spent on the pre-commitment slide cap and Airlock chip, then vanishes at the moment of proof. A Japanese hanko does the opposite: the vermilion (shuniku) impression IS the binding act, pressed at the climax of the document, in the same vermilion family as Monolith's accent.

Recommendation: Strike a real seal mark at both ends of the act, following the hanko: (1) on seal, stamp a vermilion #F55314 block — receipt number inside a square seal field — onto the Deck imprint zone, replacing the 1dp lip as the sealed state's visible difference; (2) print that same seal block on ReceiptSheet.kt's slip beside the №, as the slip's only colour. One mark, two strikes, nothing else recoloured — orange finally appears where the commitment is completed, not only where it is offered.

#### [CRITICAL] Surprise inventory is zero — and the doctrine that killed the only egg now bans surprise by definition

DrawerScreen.kt:442-448 is a tombstone, not a feature: 'the five-tap egg that toggled a "HARMONIC SYNTH UNLOCKED" line is gone — the synth it named was removed from the app, and an achieved state for a feature that does not exist is not an easter egg, it is a false print.' A full-codebase inventory confirms the count today: easter eggs 0, hidden gestures 0, secret screens 0 (grep for egg/surprise/secret gestures returns only this comment; the renders deck.html, drawer.html, airlock.html, receipt.html show no hidden layer on any surface). The verdict is worse than the absence: the deletion rationale defines any surprise as a truth-claim, so a future egg can only survive if it is literally true — a standard no playful detail in any medium is designed to meet, applied by an app whose own platform has shipped a tap-to-discover egg in every release since Android 2.3 Gingerbread, each one pure fiction (zombie paintings, flingable jelly beans, a cat collector) and none of them a 'false print' to anyone.

Recommendation: Replace the doctrine, not just the egg: adopt a written 'truthful egg' spec — an egg is legal if it actuates real machinery instead of naming fake features. Restore the five-tap on the Cabinet serial plate (DrawerScreen.kt cabinet detail, the exact spot the egg died), but make it run the artifact itself: tapping Toy 01's plate five times draws the Harmonic Loop's actual Lissajous figure in the existing Canvas views and plays a harmonic-seal variant from the existing TactileSoundEngine. The egg is then discoverable like Android's version-tap egg, and passes the app's own truth test because the toy genuinely performs.

#### [CRITICAL] The seal has no downbeat — its haptic, colour, sound, theme and picture climaxes land at five different times across a silent proving prologue and a 1050ms shot, so there is no 'best 2 seconds' to remember

The seal runs on at least four unsynchronised clocks. The proving phase is deliberately silent with the Deck looking idle: jamSentenceFor's own comment states 'PROVING's silence is the machine working' (ui/components/MonolithCustomComponents.kt, jamSentenceFor, ~L560-575), and SessionSealTransition.prove() polls witnesses until t0 = max(lastConfirm, latchMono + DWELL_MS) before executeSeal fires (service/SessionSealTransition.kt:200-245). After t0 the climaxes scatter: the Throw's haptic ends by 78ms (SEAL_THROW_TIMINGS 0/24/38/16 in service/TactileSoundEngine.kt:143-144), the cap's orange is fully shaded out by +150ms (sealExitPhase steps at +50/+100/+150, ui/views/BlockitCoreViews.kt:1567-1575 and tokAccentShaded at L149-165), the audio bolt enters at +30ms (BOLT_START_SAMPLE 1323, TactileSoundEngine.kt:~L106), the ground/theme steps at +400ms (shot.groundStepped at e>=400, ui/screens/TactileDeckScreen.kt:248-262), and the hero only 'lands' at +1050ms (e>=1050 -> heroLanded, same block). Teenage Engineering's OP-1 power-on does the opposite: one slide of the physical power switch and the TE logo is displayed on screen as a single coincident event (TE OP-1 quick guide, step 1). Monolith has no frame where sound, touch, colour and picture agree — a reviewer filming it gets a smear, not a moment.

Recommendation: Re-choreograph the seal around ONE downbeat at ~450ms. Hold every channel until the last proving link confirms, then fire together in a single frame: bolt transient, haptic 255-pulse, cap seat, theme step and imprint strike all at the downbeat; delete the 50/100/150ms colour stepping and move the ground step from +400ms onto the same frame. Compress the shot from 1050ms to ~600ms total (150ms anticipation during proving shown as the cap visibly straining, downbeat, 450ms settle). During proving, replace the silence with a rising ratchet tied to links confirmed (1/2/3) so the wait builds toward the beat instead of preceding it blankly, the way the OP-1's switch travel builds to its logo frame.

#### [CRITICAL] No frame survives as a blog hero image — even a manual screenshot of the Deck fails the thumbnail, crop and caption-free tests

deck.html: the full 390x844 Deck frame splits attention four ways — hero card (TOTAL 1H 50M, Sora 72sp) + 288dp wheel, then a task row, a 53dp proof strip (BLOCK/APPS/TIME), a 72dp slide track and a 52dp rail. TactileDeckScreen.kt:567 hero card and dial are one object, :639-672 hero in DialClockTextStyle, :705 wheel fixed at 288.dp. Color.kt:11 TokenColorBackground #E4DFDA, :15 surfaceBright #FAF6F0, :18 accent #F55314 spent in deck.html only on the 84x56 slide cap. At 200px-wide thumbnail size the greige-on-porcelain contrast collapses to warm grey, the 10sp MONOLITH/GUARD header (deck.html header band) vanishes, and the only saturated pixel cluster is a small orange rectangle with no label in frame.

Recommendation: Build one deliberate Poster Frame and make it the Deck's idle state: full-bleed porcelain ground, wheel centred and enlarged to ~340dp, hero total directly above it in Sora 72sp, task title directly below it in Atkinson 22sp, and nothing else in frame — proof strip, slide and rail move to a second, scrolled layer. Following Forest's single-object rule and Teenage Engineering OP-1 product photography (the whole object fills the photo, no UI chrome competes), test it at 200px wide and in a 1:1 crop: if a stranger cannot say 'a wheel that sets focus time' from the thumbnail alone, it has failed and must be recomposed.

#### [CRITICAL] No shared visual object: two co-focusing users would watch two unrelated dials, never one thing growing or dying together

Every visual object Monolith grows during a session is private and asymmetric: the Deck's wheel hub is 8 wells for the user's own study blocks (design-renders/deck.html caption: 'hub wells 2 of 8 filled'), the imprint tenant counts only the user's own apps — '9 WILL SHUT · 3 PEEK' from imprintTenantText in ui/components/MonolithCustomComponents.kt:430-477 — and the Drawer cabinet curios are forged for one user alone (design-renders/drawer.html). Two people 'focusing together' in Monolith would stare at two unrelated private dials with no common picture: nothing on either screen is the same object, grows the same way, or can fail for both. Forest's Plant Together makes the defining design decision of the category: ONE shared tree rendered on every member's screen, and if any one person leaves, everyone's tree dies — a single joint artifact with joint fate, watched identically by all.

Recommendation: Give a paired session one shared artifact in Monolith's paper idiom instead of copying the tree: a joint imprint. When two users seal together, both Decks strike the identical imprint tenant — same serial, both initials, e.g. '№ 048 · A+S · 1H 50M HELD TOGETHER' — and the imprint's lip is struck in two halves, one per phone. If either user takes the emergency valve, both imprints print the fault line 'BROKEN BY A. 19:11' in the receipt's existing fault style. One object, printed identically on both devices, succeeding or cracking together — Forest's shared-fate tree rebuilt as Monolith's shared-fate seal.

#### [CRITICAL] Willpower itself is the one act with no sensory payoff: every deflection is silent, while turning a dial ticks

Inventory first: every sound in the app is one of 8 synthesized impact voices in service/TactileSoundEngine.kt:629-848 (playRotaryDetent 6ms, playFirmClick 12ms, playMechanicalLatch 16ms, playSeatKnock, playHarmonicSeal 48ms, playSealThrow, playTearPulse 40ms, playCompletionPulse 64ms) — and none of them is wired to a deflection. grep finds zero play* calls and no TactileSoundEngine in service/MonolithAccessibilityService.kt (the service that actually turns the user away) or in the intercept path of service/MonolithShieldService.kt; the only trace of the event is a silent counter in the notification text at MonolithShieldService.kt:144 ('{count} urges stopped'). Renders confirm the visual side: shield.html/airlock.html show the intercept as badge, app name and countdown, nothing that lands. So turning the wheel one detent earns a pitched tick (MonolithViewModel.kt setDialMinutes: pitch = 440 + minutes*2.8), but resisting Instagram at minute 40 — the behaviour the entire product exists to produce — earns literally nothing the senses can register.

Recommendation: Make the deflection the app's conditioned reward, the first of the three delight moments this identity demands. When the accessibility service turns a SHUT/PEEK app away, fire one dedicated voice that exists for nothing else: a deep seat-knock variant (playSeatKnock at ~24ms, pitch falling 320→240Hz) plus a single-frame accent flash on the Airlock badge, and let the 'urges stopped' count tick up visibly/audibly in the Airlock rather than only in the notification. Follow the pinball-bumper / Duolingo correct-answer principle: the rewarded behaviour gets the most distinctive, most repeatable sound in the system, pitched slightly up with each successive deflection in a session so willpower audibly compounds.

#### [CRITICAL] The 10-minute break — the only sanctioned pleasure in the product — is designed as nothing: same ink, same latch sound as locking

The break between blocks is rendered as one line of the same mono text among the Deck's other states — TactileDeckScreen.kt:615-616: 'BREAK · {(safeBreakSecondsRemaining + 59) / 60} MIN' — with the Deck's only break verb an 'END BREAK' keycap at TactileDeckScreen.kt:930-936. Sonically the break is actively anti-delightful: MonolithRepository.kt:1810-1828 documents that crossing into the break plays breakBoundaryKnock(false) = playMechanicalLatch, and re-entering the next block plays the same latch engaged — i.e. release from work is voiced with the identical 16ms locking-machine sound used to shut apps, at TactileSoundEngine.kt:683. No colour temperature change, no slower motion curve, no distinct register exists for the break anywhere in MonolithCurves.kt's duration vocabulary (110-1050ms, all mechanical). deck.html/receipt.html renders show no break state at all — the one sanctioned pleasure in a multi-block day has no designed form.

Recommendation: Design the break as the exhale — the second demanded delight moment. On break entry: swap the latch for a genuinely releasing voice (the harmonic seal's chord played descending and at half gain, sustained ~400ms instead of a 16ms impact), shift the Deck's ground from the night/block tone to the warm cream of the receipt slip (#FAF6F0 family), slow the hero to a breathing-scale pulse using a new 4000ms curve, and print one human line ('BREAK · 10 MIN · NOTHING IS HELD AGAINST YOU HERE' register: a sentence, not a countdown). On re-entry, reverse it. Reference: Apple Watch's Breathe/Mindfulness transitions and Forest's Relax mode both change the whole sensory register for rest; Monolith must stop voicing rest as another lock engaging.

#### [CRITICAL] No consequence-free touch exists: the crank-shaped wheel can only ever set a sentence, never be spun for nothing

RotaryWheelView reports every crossing as a committed value: applyValueFromAngle() ends in onMinutesChanged?.invoke(newValue) (BlockitCoreViews.kt:1176, again at :1240 when the spring seats), and the angle is hard-clamped to the consequential scale, wheelAngleDeg = unwrapped.coerceIn(108f, 432f) (BlockitCoreViews.kt:1147). The deck render (design-renders/deck.html) confirms the wheel is the idle screen's hero object — and turning it is drafting a sentence, not playing. Every other touch in the app likewise writes state: sleds persist settings, the slide arms a session. Playdate's crank can be spun in the launcher, in menus, mid-game, backwards, for nothing; that zero-stakes spinning is what teaches the hand the toy. Monolith offers no gesture whose only product is pleasure.

Recommendation: Add one consequence-free detent: a PLAY stop past the 180 end of the wheel scale (angle beyond 432°) where the wheel spins freely through its pitch ladder and spring physics with onMinutesChanged suppressed, labelled 'SPIN' in the same Anonymous Pro voice as FLOW. Entering it changes no setting, arms nothing, and writes nothing to disk; leaving it returns the dial to its prior value. One free toy, deliberately fenced from every commitment surface.

#### [CRITICAL] The seal's signature clunk is spent on routine edits — a near-identical 'harmonic seal' sounds 13 times for admin, so the real Throw arrives pre-diluted

TactileSoundEngine.kt:139-145 defines the Throw's haptic skeleton as timings (0,24,38,16) amplitudes (0,255,0,175) — the middle zeroed so it 'breathes'. TactileSoundEngine.kt:705-730 playHarmonicSeal(arming) reuses the identical skeleton (0,24,38,16) at (0,255,110,175) plus a 360/480Hz clunk, and MonolithViewModel.kt fires it 13 times for non-seals — e.g. :1799, :1968, :2002, :2099, :2135, :2176 on routine/profile edits and :2244, :2271, :2298 on disarms. The real Throw is deliberately parameter-free and sole-sited (TactileSoundEngine.kt:756-767; SessionSealTransition.kt:142).

Recommendation: Delete playHarmonicSeal entirely. Give every routine/profile edit the quiet 680Hz rotary detent only, and reserve the (0,24,38,16) waveform, the bolt layer and the word 'seal' in sound and copy exclusively for playSealThrow in SessionSealTransition.executeSeal. Add a grep gate mirroring the existing Throw gate: no file outside TactileSoundEngine may reference the Throw timings.

#### [CRITICAL] Every enforced pause is metered, never empty: the 'breathing delay' is an 88sp countdown and the 60s valve hold is a filling gauge with a seconds label

ui/components/AirlockAndDisarmOverlays.kt:545 names the intercept a '5s Breathing Delay Wall', but :562-569 counts it down and :636-639 prints it as an 88sp Anonymous Pro numeral — the largest type in the app (airlock.html frame 1: badge, 24sp app name, session line, giant 03, intention, chip, all centred with 16dp gaps). The Disarm valve does the same to 60 seconds: Emergency60sValveView fills with accent, seams bank every 15s, and its label reads 'KEEP HOLDING VALVE - {remaining}s'. In Ma the pause itself carries the meaning — 'the silence between the notes which make the music'. A breath you must watch being counted is not a breath; it is a queue ticket, and the user spends both pauses staring at the meter instead of feeling the urge pass.

Recommendation: Empty both pauses. AirlockInterceptOverlay: delete the 88sp countdown Text entirely — the card holds only the app name and 'ACTIVE INTENTION: ...' in stillness; the EMERGENCY PEEK chip fades in silently when the 5 seconds elapse, announced by a single soft haptic tick and nothing else. DisarmChallengeOverlay/Emergency60sValveView: remove the '{remaining}s' label and the 15s bank seams; the fill becomes a single unsegmented lightening of the track, so holding is felt in the hand, not read off a gauge.

#### [CRITICAL] 'Kinetic' toys that never move: the curios promise machines you can operate and deliver five lines of text and a FORGED stamp

KineticArtifact (MonolithModels.kt:492-498) is five strings — id, serial, name, subtitle, lore — and nothing else: no state, no motion, no sound, no interaction model. Yet the lore describes operable machines: a gyroscope of 'four brass rings, each free on its own axis' (MonolithModels.kt:815-820), a pendulum whose 'swing decaying into a spiral' (MonolithModels.kt:836-841), a planetarium whose traced line 'blooms into a geometric flower' (MonolithModels.kt:829-834). The Cabinet detail (DrawerScreen.kt cabinet branch) renders serial, name, subtitle, lore and a FORGED/NOT YET FORGED stamp, and its own comment records that the SELECT verb was deleted because 'the detail now ends at the record.' A toy you can only read about is a badge with better prose: the collection checkmark was kept, the play — spinning, swinging, tracing — was never built.

Recommendation: Make each forged curio actually operable in its Cabinet detail, using the wheel's existing physics/sound engine: drag the Gyroscope's rings and hear them settle, flick the Sand Pendulum and watch the spiral decay, scrub the Planetarium's orbits until the flower closes. No scores, no further unlocks inside the toys — operation is the whole point. Until a Toy moves, rename the class honestly in copy: 'RECORD' not 'TOY', and strike 'Kinetic' from the cabinet header.

#### [HIGH] No sonic mark exists: the one crafted sound is a mid-ceremony process noise, never reprised where identity is displayed

The Throw is fired from exactly one place in the codebase — SessionSealTransition.kt:142, inside executeSeal — and never reprised: not on the receipt that displays the session's number and outcome, not at app launch, and not on the ongoing session notification, whose channel is IMPORTANCE_LOW and silent (service/MonolithShieldService.kt:198-209). Every audio track is also routed as USAGE_ASSISTANCE_SONIFICATION in mono (service/TactileSoundEngine.kt:389, 426) — the attributes of private accessibility sonification, not of a public mark. PARK meanwhile advertises the synth in copy instead of sound: its spec plate prints 'SOUND: FLOAT-PCM, 4 PARTIALS · POWER: YOUR PHONE' (ui/components/ParkDrawer.kt:123). Playdate, by contrast, commissioned an actual theme (Panrucker and Cabel Sasser) alongside its UI cues, so the device is recognisable by ear before it is seen.

Recommendation: Promote the Throw's first 400ms (360Hz body + bolt entry at +30ms) into a named two-beat mark and reprise it verbatim at exactly two more moments: receipt appearance (under the print strike) and routine auto-seal. Nowhere else. Put the mark, not the spec text, in PARK: tapping the SOUND EFFECTS row label should audition it. A signature is a repetition discipline, not a waveform.

#### [HIGH] Declaring a word has no filing act: a silent grey-to-black colour swap, no stamp, no sound, no commit moment when it becomes permanent

DrawerScreen.kt:864-878: the declaration control is three bare Text composables (Atkinson Bold 11sp, 16dp apart) whose only state change is colour — active word onBackground, inactive onSurfaceVariant. There is no container, press state, animation, haptic or sound anywhere in DrawerScreen.kt (no haptic/sound references in the file), and MonolithViewModel.kt:1955-1964 declareTodayWord() writes the word with no soundEngine call, unlike session actions elsewhere in the same ViewModel that play harmonic seals. Worse, the one moment that should feel like filing — the 03:30 rollover when the word stops being editable and becomes print (DrawerScreen.kt:835-838: 'While sealed the words are print and answer nothing') — happens with no transition at all; the row simply stops responding. Letterpress, the reference this app's print vocabulary claims, is defined by the impression: pressure, ink transfer, an irreversible mark. A rubber date-stamp on a paper planner page has more ceremony than this.

Recommendation: Build the stamp: on tap, the chosen word animates in as an impression — scales from 1.15 to 1.0 with a fast settle, ink colour deepening from variant grey to full onBackground, paired with one short sound-engine tick and a single light haptic (the app already owns both engines). At the 03:30 seal, if the Drawer is open, the declaration row visibly retires: the three tappable words collapse into the single filed word with a slow fade to print grey — the user should be able to witness the moment a word becomes record.

#### [HIGH] The countdown's climax is a prize reveal: at 00 the only thing that changes on screen is the materialisation of EMERGENCY PEEK, so the wait reads as a loading bar for the craved app

AirlockAndDisarmOverlays.kt:636-642 renders the wait as a zero-padded '0%d' readout at 88sp Anonymous Pro Bold; :663-681 shows the screen's sole state change at countdownSecs == 0 is the appearance of the EMERGENCY PEEK chip plus its price line — airlock.html frame 1 vs frame 2 is a diff of exactly one added reward. Choreographically, five seconds of mounting anticipation terminate in the arrival of the thing the user craves: the design grammar of a download finishing or a loot drop landing. one sec's gradient bar ends on a question, not an unlock — when its wait finishes, nothing new to take appears; a decision is asked. Monolith's wait ends by handing over goods

Recommendation: Re-choreograph the terminal beat: when the delay completes, what should arrive is the decision, not the reward. Compose RETURN TO FOCUS and the peek offer simultaneously at beat two (per the two-beat split), with the peek visually subordinate — smaller, unfilled, below — and let the numeral's final transition be a settle (the pacing element coming to rest), not a zero that triggers a reveal. The peek should never be the only new element a state change delivers.

#### [HIGH] Partial effort leaves no scaled trace: Forest's withered tree keeps the height it grew to, Monolith's PARTIAL is one word, no brick, and no pulse

In Forest, a tree killed at 90% of its timer stands in the forest at 90% of its grown height — partial effort keeps a scaled, visible body. In Monolith, effort has no magnitude in any visual language: receiptOutcomeWord collapses the whole continuum into 'PARTIAL' (MonolithRepository.kt:1685); TowerStreakView (BlockitTowerFadersAndCatalogViews.kt:116-135) has exactly three brick states — crown accent, solid ink, ghost slot — with no half-laid or partial brick; and finishPulses (ReceiptState.kt:109-117) rules 'PARTIAL never pulses', so even the completion vibration is withheld all-or-nothing. 49 of 50 minutes and 5 of 50 minutes receive the identical word, the identical absence of a brick, and the identical silence.

Recommendation: Add a magnitude channel for partial effort, following Forest's grown-height corpse: render a PARTIAL brick in the Tower at fractional height/tint proportional to attended fraction, print the slip's outcome line as 'PARTIAL · 41 OF 50 MIN' in the existing mono (the data is already on the row), and let finishPulses scale one short pulse for any attended fraction above zero. The verdict word can stay; it must stop being the only trace of how much was actually done.

#### [HIGH] Nightfall gets no moment and no warning: the heartbeat seals the SLEEP window in a ≤1500ms proving pass, with no foreshadow surface at any point in the day

The entire onset path is RoutineHeartbeat.kt:131-165: the heartbeat materialises the desired session and launches proveAndSeal off-pass, with the comment at RoutineHeartbeat.kt:158-162 noting the proving window is ≤1500ms — the user mid-conversation at 19:59 gets no countdown, no 'night begins in 30 minutes' line on the Deck, no last-things prompt; the first evidence of evening is the seal Throw and, on the next app open, the airlock. No upcoming-window, warning or countdown surface for routines exists anywhere in the codebase (the only onset code is this heartbeat path). The app lavishes ceremony on session starts the user chooses — a primed seal lane, a golden-hash-pinned Throw, a 1480–1800ms receipt detention (receipt.html frame 3) — and spends none of it on the one transition that happens to the user unchosen, every night. Apple's Wind Down is built entirely as foreshadow: it begins up to 3 hours before bedtime, dims the lock screen, surfaces calming shortcuts, and even fires Sleep Reminders before Wind Down itself starts.

Recommendation: Give nightfall the ceremony the seal already gets: a Deck descent line from T-45 ('NIGHT IN 45 — FEEDS CLOSE, KNOCKS ONLY' updating at T-15 and T-5 in the app's mono voice), a single soft detent (not the Throw) at T-0 minus the final minute so the user can finish a sentence, and the seal itself only at window start. Reuse the receipt detention's held-frame technique in reverse: hold the day's last Deck frame briefly under the first dusk step, so the day visibly ends instead of being replaced.

#### [HIGH] A 1.5-1.8 second anticipation window is spent on a literally frozen frame — duration borrowed from reward reveals, with none of the build

ReceiptState.kt:201-205 sets HELD_FRAME_MS=1200, RECEIPT_FLOOR_MS=1480, RECEIPT_CEILING_MS=1800 — a wait as long as a game loot reveal — but TactileDeckScreen.kt:274 (heldFinish) holds the session's last frame frozen for all of it: receipt.html Frame 3 shows exactly what the user stares at, the wheel composed as a still ghost, hero 00:00, slide seated, utilities absent. There is no progress bar, no racking motion, no tightening detail that tells the user something is being prepared; the seal START, by contrast, gets a named three-phase shot (TactileDeckScreen.kt:1126-1135: DEPARTURE <180ms, RECESSION <780, SETTLE <1050). Zelda: Breath of the Wild's chest opening and Genshin's wish reveal spend their anticipation seconds on escalating light, camera and sound — the wait itself is the show. Monolith's wait is a paused video.

Recommendation: Give the detention a visible build using the app's own machine language: over the 1200ms held frame, rack the receipt in stages — the proof strip's seam prints its final word first, the imprint slot fills, the wheel makes one final detent rotation and locks — each stage landed by the existing E0/E700/E880 sounds, which currently accompany nothing. Name the phases (as the seal shot already does) and derive them from e0Mono so a late observer joins mid-build.

#### [HIGH] The seal sound is engineered so surprise is impossible: identical by law, forever

TactileSoundEngine.kt:756-759, the design comment for playSealThrow(): 'THE THROW (B-5): the one seal voice, zero parameters — no provenance, no duration, no clock can enter it, so two seals cannot differ.' This is an 857-line procedural PCM synthesizer with at least eight distinct voices (playRotaryDetent:629, playFirmClick:644, playSeatKnock:665, playMechanicalLatch:683, playHarmonicSeal:707, playTearPulse:817, playCompletionPulse:833) — the most expressive sound instrument in its category — deliberately tuned so its signature moment is bit-identical on the 1st and the 1,000th hearing. No rare variant, no anniversary voicing, no hidden tone exists anywhere in the engine. Teenage Engineering, the reference this app's hardware aesthetic borrows from, hides whole videogames inside its synthesizers; Monolith hides nothing inside its synthesizer-engine.

Recommendation: Keep the Throw itself canonical (it is the seal's proof-act and should not vary), but add the surprise downstream of it, where variation cannot contaminate the seal: a counterfoil variant — every 25th seal, the tear pulse (TactileSoundEngine.kt:817) plays with its chord ratio shifted from 1.21 to the completion pulse's 1.33 and the receipt slip prints a small variant mark beside its number. One conditional, existing voices only, zero new assets; the user who stays long enough eventually hears the machine do something it has never done before.

#### [HIGH] The only human-voiced copy in the app is never rendered: four finished coaching lines sit orphaned in the data layer

MonolithModels.kt:198-218 defines InterceptReason with the app's only warm, person-voiced sentences — coachingTip: 'Your thumb tapped this on autopilot. Take one slow breath and return to your next micro-step.' (L203), 'Doomscrolling drains working memory faster than resting. Stand up, drink water, or finish this short block.' (L213) — and a grep of the whole ui/ tree finds zero consumers: no composable ever renders coachingTip. What actually ships at the intercept moment (airlock.html, AirlockAndDisarmOverlays.kt) is badge, app name, an 88sp countdown and 'ACTIVE INTENTION:' — ledger voice at the exact second the user is most emotional. The wit inventory of shipped copy is therefore: curio lore (6 lines, quarantined in a Cabinet detail at DrawerScreen.kt:474) and nothing else; every other string in the renders is a label, a count or a verdict.

Recommendation: Ship the voice that is already written: render the matched InterceptReason.coachingTip as a fourth line in AirlockInterceptOverlay under the intention line, Atkinson Hyperlegible italic 12.5sp in the night scheme's cream at 80% — the typeface, size and colour tokens already exist in that composable. This is the Slack-loading-message move (wit placed in a dead moment the user did not choose) at zero writing cost: four finished sentences are sitting in the data layer waiting for one Text() call.

#### [HIGH] The namesake curio can be won by lot in session 2 and re-won forever — no curio is reserved for a milestone, so session 100's forge is a guaranteed anticlimax

CurioCatalog (MonolithModels.kt:799-862) puts all six objects in one flat pool, including Toy 06 'The Monolith Cube — A Cube Within A Cube', the brand's namesake. MonolithRepository.kt:2049-2051 mints on every completed non-routine session via CurioCatalog.artifacts.shuffled().first().id — no memory, no threshold gating — so the Cube can drop on the second session and the 100th session's mint is a repeat of something already owned. The Cabinet records the outcome as a binary tag only: DrawerScreen.kt:375,396-405 prints 'FORGED' at 10.5sp mono (drawer.html frame 2), with no date, no session №, no distinction between a first-week drop and a hundredth-session drop.

Recommendation: Reserve rarity by date, following Forest's milestone logic (a special Streak Tree earnable only at 30 consecutive sessions, permanent once earned) and Apple's limited-edition badges (earnable only on the anniversary day itself). Remove Toy 06 from the shuffled pool and forge it only on the session that claims receipt № 100 (fallback: the first clean session after day 30 for low-frequency users); print its Cabinet row with provenance — 'FORGED · № 100 · <date>' — in place of the bare FORGED tag. The other five toys keep the lottery; the Cube becomes the one object whose arrival is an anniversary, not a dice roll.

#### [HIGH] The seal is a playback, not a performance — the spring seats the cap, a 90ms tap can substitute for the whole gesture, and the shot is coded 'derive-don't-replay' so it skips itself whenever it can

Every path removes the user's hand before the climax. A hand drag is finished by a spring integrator — 'spring accel = 400*(1-x) - 16*v; a hard-stop clamp at x >= 1.00 IS onLatch' (ui/views/BlockitCoreViews.kt:1420-1428) — so the machine seats the cap itself. A tap needs no travel at all: 'a press >=90ms released on a live wire runs the driven mesh (140ms bezier to 0.92)' then the same seat spring (BlockitCoreViews.kt:1429-1436). After the latch the shot is explicitly anti-performance: 'Derive-don't-replay: a shot first observed past a phase boundary starts past it; a pre-existing session (routine-born, restored) is born settled and no shot ever replays for it' (ui/screens/TactileDeckScreen.kt:211-235), and routines seal with no hand present at all via RoutineHeartbeat's transition.proveAndSeal (service/RoutineHeartbeat.kt:162). Playdate's crank — Panic/Teenage Engineering's fold-out crank, read continuously by a Hall-effect sensor (iFixit teardown) — is the inverse contract: the effect exists only while the user keeps cranking, at the user's speed, and stops when they stop. Monolith's user can neither sustain, pace, nor re-perform the seal; they can only trigger it and watch a recording the code is proud to skip.

Recommendation: Make the seal performed, not triggered. Borrow the crank contract: the slide must be held under the finger for the full proving window — finger pressure/travel drives the shot, releasing early decays the attempt back (the existing refusal-retreat machinery already models this). Add three physical detents across the travel mapped to the three proving links, each with its own tick and rising resistance feel, so the user feels the machine confirm link by link in their thumb.
