Demote the 90ms tap from a full order to an accessibility alternative that is visibly the lesser path. Let a routine seal be quiet and shot-less by design, reserving the full performed seal for a present user — a signature moment nobody attends is not a moment.

#### [HIGH] At the Throw nothing new enters the frame — the seated cap still reads 'SLIDE OR TAP TO START', the only seal marks are a 1.04-scale twitch and a 1px lip, and the peak frame is blurred, so the moment cannot be screenshotted

Read the peak frame as a still. In deck.html the track face reads 'SLIDE OR TAP TO START' under the orange cap — and that text is a compile-time constant 'frozen through every drag state' (ui/views/BlockitCoreViews.kt:1430-1436), still printed by onDraw from WORDS_START (BlockitCoreViews.kt:2407) after the cap has seated and the session has started: the hero control keeps announcing an instruction for an act already completed. The only new marks the seal itself strikes are sub-photographic: the Imprint Strike is a 1.04 scale settling in 110ms with ink alpha moving 0.82->0.88 over 400ms (ui/components/MonolithCustomComponents.kt:803-835), plus a 1-physical-pixel lip line (MonolithCustomComponents.kt:~L842-855). Meanwhile the one frame worth capturing is deliberately degraded — the hero card scales to 0.94 and blurs up to 6dp mid-shot (ui/screens/TactileDeckScreen.kt:582-605). The session number that could be the stamp (e.g. 'No 048' in receipt.html) exists only on the receipt, which arrives at session END, not at the seal. A wax seal, the OP-1's boot logo, the Playdate crank swung out — each leaves a new, legible silhouette. Monolith's seal leaves a darker version of the frame you already had.

Recommendation: Give the Throw a stamp that survives in a still. At the downbeat: (1) the track words flip from 'SLIDE OR TAP TO START' to 'SEALED - No 048 - 1H 50M' and stay for the session's first 10 seconds; (2) the Imprint Strike becomes a real strike — the tenant line ('9 HELD - 3 PEEK') plus the session number scales from 1.25 to 1.0 with a hard 2-frame impact and a permanent 1dp lip, modelled on a wax/rubber stamp hit, legible at screenshot size; (3) kill the blur at the downbeat itself — recession blur may build before it, but the landing frame must be tack-sharp, because that is the frame people will capture. Test: a screenshot taken 0.5s after sealing must be unmistakably a sealed Monolith, readable without the theme colour doing all the work.

#### [HIGH] No stamp on the one document that exists to be stamped: the verdict is a suffix in 11sp mono

The session's verdict — the single most stamp-shaped fact in the app — is typeset as a suffix: 'ENDED 19:32 · ENDED' in the same 11sp Anonymous Pro, same weight, same ink as the ARMED line above it (ui/components/ReceiptSheet.kt:124, and the word itself comes from MonolithRepository.kt:1683-1688 where even a shield-gap finish differs only by more of the same text, 'ENDED · SHIELD GAP'). The №, the collectible serial, sits at 13sp in onSurfaceVariant grey (ReceiptSheet.kt:104). Nothing on the slip is rotated, outlined, oversized or struck. This is a vocabulary failure, not a missing feature: the app already owns a stamp gesture — the imprint's Strike, a one-time 1.04-scale settle fired at session START (ui/components/MonolithCustomComponents.kt:777,820) — and spends it on the beginning, leaving the finish unstamped. A passport entry stamp or a Japanese hanko does the opposite: the verdict is the largest, reddest, most rotated object on the page, legible in a photograph before a single line of text is read, and it is the element people photograph.

Recommendation: Give the finish the Strike the start already has: render the outcome word as an actual stamp — double-outline rounded box, rotated -6 degrees, overlapping the slip's top-right corner so it breaks the card edge, in the accent ink for ENDED/ATTENDED, in outlineVariant grey for PARTIAL, struck at issuance with the existing Strike mechanics (snap to 1.04 scale / 0.82 ink alpha, settle 110ms scale + 400ms ink, MonolithCustomComponents.kt:820-830). Move the № directly under the stamp at 15sp in full ink so serial and verdict form one photographed unit. A shield-gap finish gets the same stamp with a cracked/second-line 'SHIELD GAP' — a visibly damaged stamp, not a longer sentence.

#### [HIGH] Nothing transforms in the first 30 seconds — and progress is drawn fading, MISSING in dark ink, GRANTED in grey

park.html's board rows encode the only state changes available in the opening: a word flips MISSING/OFF to GRANTED/RUNNING. The render's own token notes state the inversion — state word 'Lack = onBackground (#2C2A29, darkest ink); granted/running = onSurfaceVariant (#5F5856, grey)'. Success is literally rendered dimmer than failure, each grant visually identical in weight to the last, and the sheet's total entrance motion budget is one 280ms fraction tween (MonolithCurves.kt:90 DRAWER_OPEN_MS; ParkDrawer.kt:152-158). Opal's first gem cracks open — an irreversible before/after the user keeps — and Forest's seed goes into the ground and starts growing; both openings are built around one object changing state for good. Monolith's opening transforms nothing: it annotates.

Recommendation: Make the board a filling instrument, not a list. Render the six grants as segments of one engraved gauge in the Deck's wheel language; each returning FIX trip seats a segment in ink with the seal's sound and a detent haptic, and the sixth grant drives the whole drawer home with the full seal-shot and stamps LAST PROVED in orange — colour the app itself defines as COMMIT (ParkDrawer.kt:114). Progress must get darker, louder and more permanent as it accrues, never greyer.

#### [HIGH] The app's only ownable brand line is typeset as drawer footnotes, below the fold of a settings sheet

ParkDrawer.kt:105-109 defines PLATE_HEAD — 'MONOLITH ML-01' / 'UNIT Nº 01 · BUILT FOR ONE USER · NOT FOR SALE' — the single most screenshot-able, describe-it-to-a-friend line in the product, in the Teenage Engineering tradition of engraving the spec on the object's face. It is then rendered at ParkDrawer.kt:623-645 explicitly as '(7) The spec plate — furniture at the foot': 10sp Anonymous Pro, below six permission rows, the FIX key, two sled rows and the theme row, reachable only by scrolling a drawer most first-run users dismiss in seconds (park.html shows it as the footer's fine print). Opal puts its identity object — the gem — in the centre of the opening, animated; Monolith files its identity as a footnote.

Recommendation: Promote the plate from footnote to title card. PLATE_HEAD becomes the held first frame (see the launch-frame redesign) and is re-struck at full width on the Deck's imprint slot once the first session seals — the engraving the user earns, not the one they scroll past. Keep PLATE_BODY as the drawer's fine print by all means; a spec sheet has footnotes. But 'BUILT FOR ONE USER · NOT FOR SALE' is a headline and must be set like one.

#### [HIGH] The Airlock '03' is the only dramatic frame and it is unphotographable — a 1-second digit floating in 60% empty void

airlock.html frames 1-2: a #362C27 card centred in a full #171412 screen, badge 'AIRLOCK INTERCEPTION • LOCKED' Atkinson Bold 11.5sp, app name 24sp, countdown Anonymous Pro Bold 88sp. AirlockAndDisarmOverlays.kt:562-569 countdownSecs starts at 5 and decrements every second, :636-639 the '03'/'00' numeral at 88.sp — each digit exists for ~1 second, the composed peek state only at 00. Roughly 60% of the 844dp frame in the render is empty night ground above and below the card; at blog-column width the badge, 'SESSION ENDS 18:30' (12.5sp) and intention line are illegible, leaving only a number with no verb, no app icon and no brand mark.

Recommendation: Do not try to screenshot a countdown — design its held poster instead, following the Apple Watch Breathe face and one sec's held pause, both of which hold a single calm composition long enough to be photographed: when the countdown reaches 00, hold a dedicated still for at least 3 seconds — app name at Sora 22sp+, intention at Atkinson 15sp minimum, countdown replaced by a full-width cream rule, card stretched to fill the padded frame so no dead void remains. Remove the 11.5sp badge from that held state; a frame that needs a magnifying glass for its title is not a frame.

#### [HIGH] The Receipt wastes its own screenshot — a bottom slip occupying a quarter of the frame, capped at 15sp, with no elapsed hero number

receipt.html frame 1: the slip sits at BottomCenter over a 0.12 black scrim (ReceiptSheet.kt:65-84), so ~70% of any screenshot is the dimmed Deck behind it, not the receipt. Inside the slip, ReceiptSheet.kt:91-95 title is Atkinson Bold 15.sp, :103-107 number № at 13.sp, :188-193 every fact line (ARMED/ENDED/HELD, deflections) is Anonymous Pro 11.sp with 1.sp tracking, :175-178 footer 9.sp. The render's own caption notes the slip prints no elapsed-duration line at all — only ARMED/ENDED wall times and PLANNED span — so the one number a reader would quote is absent from the one artifact meant to be kept.

Recommendation: Recompose the receipt as a full-frame poster slip, following Strava/Apple Fitness share cards where one result number is the hero: slip anchored to fill the padded viewport, elapsed time promoted to DialClockTextStyle Sora 72sp (Type.kt:63-68) at the top, intention under it at 22sp, HELD/deflection lines kept at 11sp mono as supporting detail, № enlarged to 15sp beside the title. A screenshot of the result should read, top to bottom, as '1H 50M — Revise thermodynamics — № 048' with no cropping and no caption.

#### [HIGH] The signature seal blur does not exist at all on Android 7-11: the defining effect is silently ignored below API 31 with no authored fallback

TactileDeckScreen.kt:589-596 applies Modifier.blur(blurDp) with no Build.VERSION gate anywhere in the file, while app/build.gradle.kts:17 sets minSdk = 24. Android's own API reference for Modifier.blur states the effect 'is only supported on Android 12 and above. Attempts to use this Modifier on older Android versions will be ignored.' So on every Android 7-11 device the app claims to support, the seal shot's named visual event simply does not occur: the card scales 0.94 and rises (TactileDeckScreen.kt:591-595) and nothing else. There is no substitute effect, no stepped-shading fallback, no reduced choreography designed for those devices - the moment was authored exactly once, for one GPU path. The faithful render in design-renders/deck.html can only show the card at rest; the shot itself has no second, portable form.

Recommendation: Author a designed low-path seal instead of silently shipping half of one: on API < 31 (or when the frame budget is missed) replace the blur term with the print vocabulary the app already owns - the slide cap's stepped accent shading (tokAccentShaded's x0.75/x0.50 table in BlockitCoreViews.kt) applied to the hero card's border and eyebrow, plus the existing scale/rise. Playdate is the reference discipline: its 1-bit display is a constraint the whole aesthetic was designed inside, so no Playdate moment exists on one unit and vanishes on another. Gate on Build.VERSION.SDK_INT >= S once, in MonolithCurves/Deck, and test the fallback as a first-class choreography, not a degraded accident.

#### [HIGH] Finishing a task sounds like ripping it up: completion is deliberately denied the completion voice and given a tear

Completing a task in the Sequencer is voiced by playTearPulse: FocusSequencerScreen.kt:147-156 onTearLeaf dispatches onCompleteTask then soundEngine?.playTearPulse(). The engine's own comment at TactileSoundEngine.kt:812-816 defines the semantics: 'The counterfoil tear's own voice… the tear is not a completion and must not spend the completion pulse… a shorter, ripping haptic — near enough to read as paper.' So the most frequent positive micro-act in the app (ticking off work, potentially many times a day) is deliberately forbidden from sounding like an achievement and is instead given the sound of destroying paper, waveform timings (0,8,14,8)ms at TactileSoundEngine.kt:817-831. The completion pulse itself (TactileSoundEngine.kt:833) is rationed to exactly one lawful spend — the session finish's E700 slot per MonolithViewModel.kt:1248-1253.

Recommendation: Re-voice task completion as a small kept thing, not a torn thing. Give onTearLeaf a short two-note rising knock (seat-knock at 320Hz answered 90ms later at 1.33×, reusing the completion chord family at miniature scale) and replace the tear motion with the leaf sliding into a 'done' stack that visibly thickens — the user should accumulate paper, not rip it. Follow Things 3 / Clear, whose check-off is a satisfying settle-and-keep, and Nintendo's item-collect grammar: frequent small wins get a miniature of the big win's voice, so the finish pulse feels like the sum of the day's ticks rather than a stranger to them.

#### [HIGH] The app's finest delight choreography is spent on an error message vanishing: a 500ms stability beat, 90ms fade and 5ms tick for fault recovery

The single most choreographed delight in the codebase is one no user will ever notice or attribute: RefusalSentenceSlot in MonolithCustomComponents.kt:706-745. When a fault sentence clears, the code waits a 500ms 'stability beat', fades the text over 90ms under a tick, and guards against flicker-back — and MonolithViewModel.kt:2185-2189 specifies that tick as 'one 5ms @ 0.4 seat-knock'. This is multi-parameter, named-designer, failure-case choreography spent on an error message disappearing from the setup screen. By contrast the inventory shows no comparable staged sequence anywhere for a user achievement: the Cabinet detail (DrawerScreen.kt:440-490) is static text rows, the desk clock's only motion is an invisible ±6dp/3dp-step burn-in drift (AirlockAndDisarmOverlays.kt:132-133), and the Curio lore in MonolithModels.kt:799-850 is six paragraphs of genuinely good writing locked behind two navigation levels in ruled 10.5sp rows (DrawerScreen.kt:373-420). Delight craftsmanship exists in this codebase — it is allocated to plumbing, not to the user.

Recommendation: Reallocate the choreography budget by rule: no fault-recovery transition may be more elaborately staged than the best user-achievement transition. Port the hand-back recipe — stability beat, timed fade, single tick — to where it belongs: when a Curio is forged, stage its Cabinet arrival with exactly that grammar (the new artifact's row fades in over a beat, one knock, the forge-rule line underneath), and give the desk clock's drift a visible purpose or cut it. Reference: Linear and Raycast spend their famous micro-polish on the core success loop (issue closed, command run), never primarily on error dismissal; Monolith should publish its own polish budget the same way — success first, recovery second.

#### [HIGH] The held world is handed back like a log dump: no reveal, stagger or sound when the digest of everything you missed is returned

Session end returns the user to everything that was held back — messages, mentions, OTPs, news — and that reunion is rendered as an undifferentiated admin list: AirlockAndDisarmOverlays.kt:337-460 shows a 'HELD · AS OF …' header, a flat LazyColumn of 'appName • senderTitle • time' rows, and the two verbs given equal visual weight are 'CLEAR ALL' (line ~370) and 'CLOSE DIGEST' (line ~458). No sound call, no stagger, no ordering ceremony, no per-item reveal exists in the overlay — grep finds no play* or animation spec attached to the digest's appearance. The receipt (receipt.html, ReceiptSheet.kt) likewise prints held apps as three dim 11sp mono lines. The product's narrative promise is 'we held the world back for you'; the moment the world is handed back is designed like clearing a log file, with one-tap total deletion offered as the headline action.

Recommendation: Stage the hand-back as the third demanded delight moment — opening the letterbox. On session end, present the digest with a staggered reveal (items cascade in at 40ms intervals with the seat-knock pitched per item, capped at ~8 ticks), order by person before app, and demote CLEAR ALL behind a hold so the first act offered is opening, not deleting. Add one closing line in the app's own voice — e.g. '12 THINGS WAITED. NONE OF THEM MATTERED AT 19:11.' generated from the real deflection times already on the slip. Reference: Superhuman's triage reveal and the physical pleasure of a held-mail bundle handed over a counter — return should feel like delivery, not disposal.

#### [HIGH] The Airlock — the one literal wall — is the thinnest surface in the app: a bordered card floating on flat ground

Ando's thresholds work because an opening reveals the wall's thickness: you pass through mass, and the depth of the reveal is the proof of it. Monolith's intercept, the moment the app claims to be a wall between the user and Instagram, is rendered as a card: 1dp border in cream at 20% alpha, 24dp radius (AirlockAndDisarmOverlays.kt:599-601), centred with 20dp of flat night ground showing on every side (design-renders/airlock.html). The ground behind it is the identical #171412 as every other night surface, so the 'wall' is a membrane floating in a void — thinner, graphically, than the 88sp countdown numeral it carries. Nothing about the surface says the user has arrived at the outside of a solid thing and is being held at its face.

Recommendation: Demolish the Airlock card. The intercept becomes full-bleed mass: no container, no border, no radius — badge, app name and intention set directly on #171412 edge to edge. The countdown alone sits inside a deep reveal: a full-width recessed well in #100E0C, inset 16dp from the screen edges, with a 12dp inner top band in #000000 so the numeral appears cut into the wall rather than printed on it. When the countdown reaches 00 the well's bottom edge opens by exactly that 12dp band filling accent — the slit widening is the peek being offered, drawn as architecture, not as a new chip appearing.

#### [HIGH] At the moment of temptation the Airlock labels the user's own intention 'ACTIVE INTENTION:' and re-issues it in the machine's voice instead of letting it stand unlabeled

AirlockAndDisarmOverlays.kt:644-648 prints the session intention under a system prefix in tracked capitals: 'ACTIVE INTENTION: ${state.sessionIntention}'. The airlock.html render shows the result at the exact moment of temptation — 'AIRLOCK INTERCEPTION • LOCKED / Instagram / SESSION ENDS 18:30 / ACTIVE INTENTION: Finish Chapter 4 Problem Set / RETURN TO FOCUS' — the user's own resolve filed, labelled and shouted back at them in the app's mono voice, surrounded by the app's other labels.

Recommendation: Strip the airlock to vessel discipline: delete the 'ACTIVE INTENTION:' prefix and the 'AIRLOCK INTERCEPTION •' badge line, and print the intention alone — Atkinson, sentence case, centred, at reading size — with the blocked app's name small beneath it and everything else on the overlay empty. The one sentence the user wrote should be the only full sentence on the screen that is trying to stop them.

#### [HIGH] The seal — the product's signature act — has no glyph: the imprint is a double rule and a line of type, so the one moment that should stamp a mark stamps nothing

MonolithCustomComponents.kt:774-782 documents ImprintSlot, the seal's fixed assembly at the foot of the Deck, as 'a double rule, the count in a fixed 20dp box, and a lip zone'; its composition (lines 890-920) is two hairline Boxes, a Text tenant and a 1px lip line. The Strike animation scales typography, not a symbol. Bass built title sequences so the mark-like gesture carried the meaning before a word was read; here the session is cryptographically signed underneath (HMAC seal) while the user-facing surface of that same act carries no drawable sign at all — the proof has a signature nobody can see.

Recommendation: Give the seal a stamp: draw the slab glyph once (see the mark above) at 14dp, seated left of the imprint count, and let the existing Strike animate it — scale 1.04 settling at 110ms is already timed like a stamp landing. The lip line becomes the stamp's baseline. Same glyph, same size, printed at the head of the receipt so the artefact a user keeps carries the mark the seal struck.

#### [HIGH] The threshold is displaced: the Airlock — the one true doorway — is crossed only in transgression, never on entry or exit

Van Gennep's limen is a threshold that must be crossed and marked as crossed; Monolith builds exactly one threshold space — the Airlock — and the session's own passage never goes through it. Entry is the Deck's slide zone captioned 'SLIDE OR TAP TO START' (deck.html; TactileDeckScreen.kt slide zone ~L946-1115): the tap alternative collapses the one gestural crossing into a button press, followed by a 1050ms seal shot (TactileDeckScreen.kt L248-258). The Airlock's full threshold architecture — 5-second breathing wall, 88sp countdown, intention read back, RETURN TO FOCUS (AirlockAndDisarmOverlays.kt AirlockInterceptOverlay; airlock.html) — is spent exclusively on transgression and peek negotiation, i.e. on failing the rite, never on performing it.

Recommendation: Move the threshold architecture to the passage itself: delete the tap-to-start alternative so the slide is the only crossing; on completion, land the user for one held beat on a true threshold screen — night falling, the intention spoken back, 'YOU ARE LEAVING FOR [duration]' — before the liminal Deck appears. Demote the Airlock to a plain refusal card (app name + return) so the product's one elaborate doorway is the door everyone actually walks through, in the right direction.

#### [MEDIUM] When the session ends the room object vanishes mid-sentence — no held final frame the room can witness as a finish

On session finish the ViewModel simply sets _isAlwaysOnDeskClockVisible.value = false (MonolithViewModel.kt:1204-1207, in onFinishE0), and the overlay's only exit is a generic fadeOut (AirlockAndDisarmOverlays.kt:80-82). The object that has been publicly counting in the room for the whole session therefore cuts straight to the Deck/receipt with no held final state: no settled 00:00/total beat, no receipt number on the clock face, and the reserved orange accent (NightColorPrimaryContainer #F47442, Color.kt:36) is never spent at the one moment the room could witness. The DN40 lineage makes session-end a physical event (tilt-to-cancel body, crescendo alarm on the BC21); Monolith's end is an absence.

Recommendation: Give the clock a closing transformation before it dismisses: hold the final frame for ~8 seconds with the numerals settling to the elapsed total, the bar completing full, the receipt number (e.g. 'No 048') replacing the eyebrow position, and the single orange accent spent once on that number — then crossfade to the Receipt slip. Anyone in the room should be able to see that it finished, and that it finished clean.

#### [MEDIUM] The receipt counter is a surprise machine that never fires: № 001, № 048 and № 500 print identically

receipt.html shows the slip headed '№ 048' — ReceiptSheet.kt:104 prints receipt.numberPrint (Anonymous Pro Bold 13sp) and the repository maintains a real, monotonically increasing receipt sequence. That counter is a ready-made surprise infrastructure and it is used for nothing: the slip for № 048 is typographically and sonically identical to № 001 and will be identical to № 500 — no first-receipt variant, no round-number printing, no milestone mark anywhere in ReceiptSheet.kt. Products that understand this counter use it: Spotify Wrapped and Duolingo's annual report exist entirely to make an accumulated count suddenly visible as an event. Monolith accumulates the count, prints it on every slip, and never once lets it become an occasion.

Recommendation: Make the counter fire three times in a user's life, cheaply: № 001 prints an extra footer line 'FIRST SLIP — THE MACHINE STARTS COUNTING'; № 050 and № 100 (and each hundred after) print on the slip with the number in the accent container colour instead of onSurfaceVariant and add the line 'A ROUND NUMBER — THE FORGE NOTICES'. Pure conditional copy and one colour swap in ReceiptSheet.kt, driven by the sequence value the repository already computes; no new state, no economy, just a number that occasionally means something.

#### [MEDIUM] Zero hidden gestures anywhere — the app's most playful object, the rotary wheel, rewards exploration with nothing

The Deck's rotary wheel (deck.html; BlockitCoreViews.kt RotaryWheelView) is the most toy-like object in the app — a knurled, detented dial spanning 30-180 — and it is the natural home for a hidden gesture, yet spinning it yields detent ticks and nothing else, at any speed, any number of revolutions, landing on any value. A gesture inventory confirms this is global: detectTapGestures appears only at ParkDrawer.kt:279 (the drawer grip press) and ParkDrawer.kt:435 (a FIX-row press) — both purely functional; there is no long-press secret, no double-tap secret, no shake, no repeated-tap handler anywhere outside the deleted Cabinet egg. Android's own eggs reward exactly this kind of manipulation (spin the Android 12 clock hand to 12:00 to unlock the palette screen); Monolith's wheel, spun a thousand times, keeps the secret that there is no secret.

Recommendation: Give the wheel one discoverable behaviour using slots that already exist: three full revolutions while unarmed plays the harmonic-seal arpeggio at low gain through the existing engine and prints 'THE WHEEL REMEMBERS' for one visit in the Deck's RefusalSentenceSlot — the sentence slot deck.html shows reserved and empty in the healthy state. One gesture counter in the wheel view, one existing sound voice, one existing text slot; the dial becomes an object users tell each other about instead of only a control they operate.

#### [MEDIUM] The Throw's one signature detail — the bolt — is mixed -6 dB under a continuous 360Hz body for 55ms, so the seal sound has no exposed event anyone can hear, imitate or describe

The Throw's crafted signature is the bolt layer: filtered xorshift noise starting at +30ms (BOLT_START_SAMPLE 1323), lasting 2426 samples (~55ms), mixed at BOLT_PEAK_GAIN 0.31074 — its own comment prices it at '-6 dB under the body's gain' (service/TactileSoundEngine.kt:95-145) — underneath a continuous 360Hz partial body that decays without any silence gap (renderSealBuffer, TactileSoundEngine.kt:208-270). The haptic twin does have a gap (amplitudes 255, 0, 175 — 'the Throw breathes through it', TactileSoundEngine.kt:139-144), but the audio never mirrors it, so ears receive one undifferentiated thunk in the same family as playHarmonicSeal's clunk. The iPod click made the opposite choice: one exposed click per detent, nothing underneath it, a sound a user can imitate with their tongue and a reviewer can name in one word. Nobody can hum, imitate or describe Monolith's seal sound — its most engineered 55ms are buried by design, protected by a golden-hash test as an artefact for the codebase rather than an earcon for the user.

Recommendation: Promote the bolt from buried layer to the sound itself. Rebuild the Throw as the haptic already is: two exposed mechanical strokes separated by real silence — a foreground latch clack (the bolt noise at full gain, ~40ms), a 60-80ms gap of true silence, then the body thunk at reduced gain as the seat. Drop the continuous 360Hz bed under the first stroke so the transient stands alone like the iPod's click. Success test is social, not spectral: a user who has sealed three times should be able to imitate the sound out loud and have another user recognise it.

#### [MEDIUM] The desk clock is the nearest object-photo and it prints its own exit instructions in the frame

receipt.html frame 4 and AirlockAndDisarmOverlays.kt:70 AlwaysOnDeskClockOverlay: true-black ground, cream #FFE4CF time, 16dp progress bar, task banner — the closest Monolith comes to a Braun DN40-style room object. It sabotages itself in two coded details: :152-158 the eyebrow permanently prints 'NIGHTSTAND DESK CLOCK • TAP ANYWHERE TO EXIT' in Atkinson Bold 11.sp at 60% alpha — instruction-manual language in every photo of it — and :161-166 the time is Anonymous Pro Bold 96.sp, while Type.kt:74-79 defines DeskClockTextStyle as Sora Bold 104.sp for exactly this surface and no call site uses it (grep: DeskClockTextStyle appears only in Type.kt). A reviewer photographing the nightstand would print the exit instruction and the wrong typeface.

Recommendation: Make the desk clock photo-clean, following the Braun DN40 / Nothing Glyph principle that an object surface shows state, never instructions: fade the eyebrow out after the first 5 seconds of each showing (reappear on first touch), and actually use DeskClockTextStyle — Sora Bold 104sp, -3sp tracking from Type.kt:74-79 — for the time, retiring the 96sp Anonymous Pro improvisation. The resulting frame (black, one cream Sora time, one cream bar, one task word) is the single image most likely to be printed; protect that exact composition in a screenshot test.

#### [MEDIUM] CURIOS and TOY give the same reward two opposite value signals — antique treasure vs disposable plaything

The collection is entered under the label 'CURIOS' (ui/screens/DrawerScreen.kt:738,776; design-renders/drawer.html), a word for rare, precious antiques kept in a cabinet. Every object inside then introduces itself in the opposite register: data/MonolithModels.kt:808-850 gives serialCode 'Toy 01' through 'Toy 06' ('Harmonic Loop', 'Brass Gyroscope', 'String Prism'…). A curio is something you preserve; a toy is something you outgrow and discard. The reward — the one thing a finished session earns — is simultaneously priced as heirloom and as trinket, so neither valuation lands and the forge moment feels cheaper than the session that paid for it.

Recommendation: Commit to one register for the reward economy. The TOY register is the stronger one — Playdate and Teenage Engineering's pocket series show playful objects can still feel premium when the naming, serials and materials language are consistent — so rename the Drawer entry and Cabinet header to 'TOYS', keep 'Toy 01' serials, and let the lore keep its object-poet voice. If CURIOS is kept instead, every serial must become 'Curio 01' / 'Artifact 01' and the word Toy must leave the catalogue entirely.

#### [MEDIUM] A four-voice synth that only ever plays door hardware: exhaustive timbre, zero melody — no motif exists anywhere in the app's sound

Every call site in TactileSoundEngine.kt:625-857 is a hardware noise: playRotaryDetent (629), playFirmClick (644), playSeatKnock (665), playMechanicalLatch (683), playSealThrow (767), playTearPulse (817); even playCompletionPulse (833-844) is a single 185 Hz transient with chordRatio 1.33 — timbre, never pitch sequence. The engine already has four weighted partials capable of distinct fundamentals per call, yet no two events in the app are related as notes, so nothing audible can be recognised, anticipated or hummed.

Recommendation: Compose one three-note motif from the existing synth — root, fifth, octave at the seal's own 300 Hz family — and assign it strictly: full motif at session finish, first two notes at seal, first note alone at break end. No new machinery; the same enqueueTransient calls with three scheduled fundamentals. Give the session an audible signature a user can identify from another room.

#### [MEDIUM] Nothing is allowed to decay: even the curio whose subject is a swing narrowing to rest is sealed forever as a binary stamp

Munari built his machines from materials that decay and gave his 1950s a-rhythmic machines movements that discharge excess energy — impermanence and irregular rhythm are the point; nothing is monument or archive. Monolith permits nothing to fade: every finished task is filed permanently in the Drawer, every receipt is HMAC-sealed, day words are persisted in day_notes, and the Sand Pendulum — whose own lore (MonolithModels.kt:838-842) is 'its swing decaying into a spiral that narrows toward rest' — is itself stored as an eternal binary FORGED stamp that never decays. The one object about disappearance is the one thing the app refuses to let disappear.

Recommendation: Let the Sand Pendulum be the app's first unarchived object: when forged, its Cabinet page shows a real spiral that fades a little each day and is gone within a week, leaving no row, no stamp and no record that it was ever there — copy on the page: 'IT FADES. IT IS NOT KEPT.' One deliberately unkept thing teaches the letting-go the rest of the ledger cannot.

### The app as an object — 30 findings (7 critical, 19 high, 4 medium, 0 low)

#### [CRITICAL] ML-01 is a spec plate for hardware that was never designed — the puck must be the Deck made solid, not a Brick clone

ParkDrawer.kt:106-107 prints 'MONOLITH ML-01 / UNIT Nº 01 · BUILT FOR ONE USER · NOT FOR SALE' and ParkDrawer.kt:110-123 specifies wheel, slide, hold, colour and power as if for a manufactured unit, yet AndroidManifest.xml declares no NFC permission and no NFC code exists anywhere in app/src/main. deck.html renders the costume faithfully: a 288dp knurled rotary wheel and a 72dp slide track with an 84x56dp orange cap (#F55314) on a flat touchscreen. Teenage Engineering's OP-1 field is the opposite contract: a real aluminium slab whose labelled encoders and colour-coding are the interface, not a picture of one.

Recommendation: Manufacture the plate's promise as ML-01 Key, not a generic tag: a 72x72x12mm slab (Playdate's 74x76x9mm palm footprint, thickened for weight) in bead-blasted aluminium with a porcelain-white top plate laser-etched with the Park spec plate verbatim, one orange PVD edge as the only colour. NTAG 424 DNA inside for a cryptographic tap the current HMAC seal can verify. Every other focus puck is an anonymous disc; this one must be recognisable across a room as the Deck's wheel housing made solid.

#### [CRITICAL] One tap both ways would delete Monolith's three-verb ritual — the object needs rotate, seat and hold as separate gestures

ParkDrawer.kt:110 states the ritual grammar in one line: 'WHEEL SETS TIME · SLIDE ARMS · THE HOLD BREAKS'. BlockitCoreViews.kt:371-383 RotaryWheelView is a genuine analogue input (5..180 min, detent ticks at minute crossings); BlockitCoreViews.kt:1444 SlideToStartView is a separate commit gesture with its own latch (onSlideCommitted). Brick collapses all of this to one undifferentiated action: tap to block, tap again to unblock, identical in both directions. Playdate's crank works precisely because rotation is not a button — turning it moves through time in Crankin's Time Travel Adventure, direction and speed carrying meaning a tap cannot.

Recommendation: Give the companion three mechanically distinct gestures matching the three verbs: (1) ROTATE a detented bezel on the dock through the same 5-180 minute stops as RotaryWheelView to set duration; (2) SEAT the phone down into the dock's slide-track recess — the physical slide — to arm and seal; (3) LIFT-AND-HOLD the phone against a separate underside pad for the full 60 seconds to break. Never tap-to-toggle. Reversing a session must feel different in the hand from starting one, or the ritual's whole vocabulary is lost in translation to hardware.

#### [CRITICAL] The namesake form never appears: an app called Monolith is built entirely from soft rounded cards, with no slab anywhere

Theme.kt:82-88 enforces 'Strictly two corner radii across the app: 12.dp and 24.dp' (MonolithShapes large/extraLarge = RoundedCornerShape(24.dp)). Every major surface obeys it identically: Deck hero card TactileDeckScreen.kt:574-581 (clip/border 24.dp, surfaceBright #FAF6F0), Airlock and Disarm cards AirlockAndDisarmOverlays.kt:599-601 and :756-758 (24.dp), Receipt slip ReceiptSheet.kt:77-79 (24.dp). In deck.html, shield.html, airlock.html and receipt.html every room is the same horizontal porcelain card on a stone ground. The reference object — Clarke/Kubrick's Monolith — is a matte-black vertical cuboid in exact 1:4:9 proportion with lethally sharp edges and no ornament; its entire power is silhouette and proportion. Monolith-the-app has no vertical slab, no sharp edge, no black mass and no recurring silhouette at any size: the name promises the most recognisable object in cinema and the geometry delivers a pebble.

Recommendation: Give the app one slab geometry and reserve it for the ritual surfaces: introduce a 0-2.dp-radius, full-bleed vertical 'slab' treatment (ink #252323 day / #161311 night, proportioned tall) for the sealed-state Deck face and the Airlock, and keep 24.dp cards only for utility surfaces (Shield, Drawer). Draw the slab once as a shared SlabSurface component so Deck, Airlock and the desk-clock share a silhouette a user can recognise from across the room — following the 1:4:9 slab, not another card.

#### [CRITICAL] Verdict: a form in an object's costume — painted knurling on a slab that has no body

deck.html: RotaryWheelView rendered as ~120 SVG <line> knurl teeth + ghost-offset 72sp hero; shield.html/park.html: same flat #E4DFDA ground, 1dp rgba(97,91,90,.46) borders, 12/24dp radii everywhere. BlockitCoreViews.kt:673 'The knurl is screen-fixed material: it cannot alias' — the rim does not rotate under the finger, the lines are painted light. Theme.kt:80-86 collapses every surface to RoundedCornerShape(12.dp)/24.dp. ParkDrawer.kt:105-107 then stamps the result 'MONOLITH ML-01 / UNIT Nº 01 · BUILT FOR ONE USER · NOT FOR SALE' — a serial plate buried inside a bottom sheet, not on a body.

Recommendation: Stop painting hardware. Either commit to a slab: one continuous edge-to-edge surface with a real top/bottom edge, no Material card chrome, and the ML-01 plate moved to the Deck footer where a maker plate belongs — or drop the metal language and redesign the wheel as honest screen material, like OP-Z dropping its display entirely and letting LEDs be the interface: the wheel becomes pure light/time, no knurl, no specular teeth. Pick one; the current middle state fools no hand.

#### [CRITICAL] Every mass is rounded into a pebble: 24dp corners domesticate the monolith the name promises

Brutalist mass and Ando's walls hold a sharp arris; Ando's only curves are full structural cylinders. Monolith declares just two radii (Theme.kt:82-86: 12dp and 24dp) and spends the large one on architecture itself: the Deck instrument card (TactileDeckScreen.kt:574, 24dp), the Airlock and Disarm cards (AirlockAndDisarmOverlays.kt:323, :599, 24dp), the Receipt slip (ReceiptSheet.kt:77, 24dp), the slide track (24dp with a 20dp cap, deck.html), and the PARK sheet's 16dp top corners (ParkDrawer.kt:237). A stone with every corner sanded to 24dp is not a monolith, it is an appliance. The one true curve the product owns — the rotary wheel's full circle — is visually demoted to the same softness as every card around it, so the building and the machine become indistinguishable.

Recommendation: Split the radius law by kind, not size: architecture goes square — Deck card, Airlock/Disarm containers, Receipt slip, PARK sheet and slide track to 0dp corners (2dp maximum to avoid aliasing shimmer); machinery keeps its radius — wheel and hub stay perfect circles, slide cap and sled thumbs keep 10-12dp as moving parts a finger pushes. Two grammars result: what you pass through is cut stone, what you turn is turned metal.

#### [CRITICAL] Control census: the Deck alone carries ~50 control positions before the session even starts — the taking surface was never cut

deck.html shows, on one idle screen: a wheel with 35 detent stops (BlockitCoreViews.kt:748, 10..180 step 5) plus 8 hub wells plus a centre cycle-press (BlockitCoreViews.kt:916-961, 1008-1043), a FLOW keycap and DONE keycap (TactileDeckScreen.kt:721, 831), a tappable NOW task row with substep toggles (TactileDeckScreen.kt:811, 858), a 3-cell proof strip with 2 seam stamps, a slide cap, and a 5-zone rail — before scrolling to Shield's ~75 further targets. A Leica M3 performs its entire job with shutter dial, aperture ring, advance lever, frame-line selector and rewind: every control that survived was one the photograph cannot be taken without. Monolith's Deck instead carries the whole camera bag on the taking surface, including task editing that already owns a dedicated TASKS rail stop.

Recommendation: Apply the cut to the Deck: it keeps exactly three controls — the wheel, the slide, the rail. Delete DONE, the substep toggles and the tappable task row from the Deck (task editing lives wholly behind the TASKS stop); the NOW row becomes print only, stating the task the slide will seal. Nothing else may be tapped on the surface whose only job is choosing a duration and committing to it.

#### [CRITICAL] The artefact stamps itself 'UNIT Nº 01 · BUILT FOR ONE USER · NOT FOR SALE' — a mass-reproducible app cosplaying a one-off made for its maker

ParkDrawer.kt:105-107 PLATE_HEAD prints 'MONOLITH ML-01' / 'UNIT Nº 01 · BUILT FOR ONE USER · NOT FOR SALE' (rendered verbatim in park.html). Software is the one medium where the best can reach the most for the least — copies cost nothing — yet Monolith's own spec plate declares the opposite ambition: a numbered single unit. The plate is honest about the product: factory presets price twelve named apps with one person's limits (AppCatalogReconcile.kt:52-67, Instagram LOCKED at 20 min/day, WhatsApp PEEK at 45) and the Deck opens pre-filled with a textbook task, so every new guest is seated inside the maker's own configuration and told, in the object's own words, that it was not built for them.

Recommendation: Cut the 'UNIT Nº 01 · BUILT FOR ONE USER · NOT FOR SALE' lines from PLATE_HEAD and replace the serial-number posture with a guest posture: plate line reads 'MONOLITH · MADE TO BE COPIED · YOUR RULES, YOUR PHONE'. Then make the copy true: on first run, present the twelve factory presets as a labelled, one-tap-dismissible 'house suggestions' sheet the guest accepts or clears, instead of silently inheriting them as their own rules.

#### [HIGH] The cap seals nothing in particular: the slide's face is a compile-time constant, so the gesture stamps a payload it never shows

BlockitCoreViews.kt:2407-2408 defines WORDS_START = 'SLIDE OR TAP TO START' and WORDS_UNDO as the only two texts the slide can ever print, and the onDraw comment (~1782) states the words stay 'frozen through every drag state'. Everything the seal actually commits — span 1H 50M, '9 WILL SHUT · 3 PEEK', ENDS 10:40 — lives in separate furniture above and below the slide (deck.html: ProofStripBand and ImprintSlot in the pinned stack, outside the slidezone). The Braun ET66 (Rams/Lubs, 1987) does the opposite: its one accented key, the yellow equals, commits exactly the expression held on the display directly above the keys, on the same object, in the same glance.

Recommendation: Borrow tamper-evident seal tape, whose pull reveals the word it was hiding: as the cap travels, let the trail it uncovers print the payload in mono — '1H 50M · 9 SHUT · 3 PEEK · ENDS 10:40' — revealed left-to-right by the cap's own movement, so a half-slide shows a half-read sentence and only a completed slide has read out the whole commitment. Keep the frozen 'SLIDE OR TAP TO START' only at rest; the instant travel begins, the track face becomes the contract being signed.

#### [HIGH] A centred floating column with no plinth or footing — on a dark desk the phone dissolves and only disembodied numerals remain

The overlay is a vertically centred floating stack: Box with contentAlignment Center and uniform 24dp padding (AirlockAndDisarmOverlays.kt:136-149), Column fillMaxWidth with 18dp gaps (AirlockAndDisarmOverlays.kt:148-152). receipt.html frame 4 shows the consequence — eyebrow, numerals, bar and banner hover mid-screen in a true-black void with equal emptiness above and below, so on a dark desk the phone's body disappears and the session reads as disembodied digits, not a placed object. Teenage Engineering's OB-4 gives its speaker a rotating handle that doubles as a stand, angling the face and giving the object a foot and silhouette; the DN40's slanted wedge face likewise sits on a base. Monolith's composition has no base, no foot, no gravitational anchor.

Recommendation: Recompose the clock as a bottom-weighted object: anchor the intention banner as a full-width 'plinth' plate at the foot of the screen, lock the numerals' baseline a fixed 24dp above it, add a 1dp foot rule aligned to the plinth, and let the upper two-thirds stay true black. The burn-in drift (±6dp, AirlockAndDisarmOverlays.kt:132-133) should move the numeral block only, never the plinth, so the object keeps its footing all night.

#### [HIGH] The companion is state-blind — no doorway-readable physical indicator of shut, peek or open

ParkDrawer.kt:113 already legislates a hardware colour code — 'COLOUR IS A VERB: ORANGE = COMMIT · INK = SHUT · GREY = PEEK · PORCELAIN = OPEN' — but no physical surface exists to speak it; receipt.html frame 4 shows the only room-facing surface, the desk clock, as phone screen text on black. Brick's puck is state-blind: nothing on the object says whether you are blocked, so you must wake the tempting device to check. Teenage Engineering's TP-7 solves this mechanically: its motorised tape reel is visible state — spinning, paused, still — readable without touching a screen.

Recommendation: Put a mechanical state flag on the dock, TP-7-reel logic at Monolith scale: a spring-loaded flip-disc in the dock face that physically snaps to ORANGE (sealed/shut) when the phone is seated, GREY for the 2-minute peek window, and PORCELAIN when open — the exact four verbs from ParkDrawer.kt:113, no LED, no screen, no battery. State must be legible from a doorway and must survive the phone being taken away: the disc stays orange as a room-level accusation that a session is still running elsewhere.

#### [HIGH] Loadouts are a menu index, not objects — STUDY, WORK and SLEEP should be three trapped physical cards

LoadoutStore.kt:48-51 reduces the three loadouts to a software cap index (STUDY 0, WORK_SPRINT 1, SLEEP 2) selected on a touchscreen selector; deck.html's imprint reduces the chosen rule set to one printed line, '9 WILL SHUT · 3 PEEK'. Nothing physical distinguishes one commitment from another, and the selection lives on the same glass the user is trying not to trust. Playdate's season games and Teenage Engineering's Pocket Operators each make a program a distinct physical/graphic object you pick up deliberately; Monolith's loadouts are a menu position.

Recommendation: Issue the three loadouts as three physical NFC cards, credit-card format, anodised in the colour-verb palette: STUDY porcelain, WORK ink-black, SLEEP grey, each etched with its shut/peek counts. The dock is a tray: you slide one card in, then seat the phone on top of it. The trapped card is the design win — the loadout cannot be swapped mid-session without lifting the phone and breaking the seat, so changing your rules requires standing up, handling the object, and choosing a different card, exactly the friction a menu tap was built to avoid.

#### [HIGH] The cabinet files objects like paperwork: no plinth, nameplate or display treatment separates a forged curio from a task-history row

design-renders/drawer.html Frame 2: the cabinet uses the same ruled-row construction as the Drawer's stored-task history in Frame 1 — same 12px side padding, same 1px outlineVariant divider, same type sizes; the only ownership mark, 'FORGED', is set in the same 10.5sp mono as the serial number. ui/screens/DrawerScreen.kt:325-327 states the intent plainly: 'Ruled rows like everything else in the Drawer.' LEGO Architecture separates a model from loose bricks with one repeatable framing device: a black baseplate and a printed nameplate tile ('New York City', 'Dubai') that turn a finished build into a displayed object; Teenage Engineering gives each Pocket Operator a folding bent-wire stand whose only job is to prop the unit up for display. Monolith owns the equivalent parts — a serial ('Toy 01', MonolithModels.kt:810) that could be a nameplate, an accent colour, a surface token — and deploys none of them at the moment of possession.

Recommendation: Build a plinth treatment used nowhere else in the app: forged curios sit on a full-bleed ink (tokPrimary) band — the cabinet's black baseplate — with the serial and name reversed out in cream as a printed nameplate, while unforged curios stay on the plain paper background as empty plinth outlines. One framing device, repeated for all six, converts the list into a shelf without touching the Drawer's paperwork rows.

#### [HIGH] The wheel's simulated machining is capped below visibility — the signature object reads as a flat beige disc where Opal's gem reads as a lit sculpture

ui/views/BlockitCoreViews.kt:667-716: the RotaryWheelView's knurled rim is 1.3dp radial teeth at 3-degree pitch whose specular is deliberately capped — day alpha factor 0.17, night 0.10, peak tooth alpha ~14% (code comment: 'the peak is capped at 14% by day, 8% by night'); the hub's specular core lift is +10% day / +8% night. In deck.html the result is plain to see: the wheel renders as two flat beige circles (#D8D1CB over #E4DFDA) with a tick ring — hundreds of lines of machining simulation produce an object indistinguishable from a placeholder disc. Opal's brand kit shows what the same budget line buys when spent on legibility: its Focus Gems are pre-rendered 3D sculptures, specified 'always on pure black', designed to be read as lit objects at arm's length.

Recommendation: Stop simulating material at alphas nobody can see. Either raise the wheel's lighting model until it survives a screenshot (specular peak at least 35%, a real radial shade across the disc face, the reader dot given a bevel instead of a flat fill), or follow Opal's route for the one hero object: render the wheel's lit states as pre-baked assets with real shading and swap them at runtime. The test is the render test: at 390px wide, a stranger should say 'machined dial', not 'grey circle'.

#### [HIGH] CUT 3 — Delete PARK's spec plate: a 10-line merchandise colophon inside a safety-repair drawer

ParkDrawer.kt:90 calls it 'the spec plate — furniture', ParkDrawer.kt:102-125 defines PLATE_HEAD/PLATE_BODY (10 lines: 'MONOLITH ML-01 / UNIT Nº 01 · BUILT FOR ONE USER · NOT FOR SALE', 'COLOUR IS A VERB: ORANGE = COMMIT…', 'SOUND: FLOAT-PCM, 4 PARTIALS · POWER: YOUR PHONE', 'STUDY HOURS: IN YPT'), and ParkDrawer.kt:623-647 renders it at the foot of the Guard sheet after a 32dp spacer. park.html shows the full block sitting inside the drawer whose actual job is the nine-line permission board and the FIX key above it.

Recommendation: Delete the plate from Park completely — head, body and its hairline/spacer. If the colophon must survive, engrave it where real objects put it: on the back panel, i.e. a single 'ML-01' line on an About/Drawer surface the user visits deliberately, never inside a repair drawer. Reference decision: a Braun rating plate lives on the rear of the housing, not on the operating face; iOS Settings likewise carries no brand manifesto inside Accessibility or Battery. Gain: the Guard sheet ends at THEME, roughly 180dp shorter, and Park reads as an instrument panel instead of merchandise packaging — the brand gets stronger, not weaker, by leaving the work surface.

#### [HIGH] Manners are not a mode: one buried SOUND EFFECTS sled is the whole etiquette system, and the SLEEP routine changes blocklists but never the phone's behaviour in the room

ParkDrawer.kt:479 shows the product's entire manners control set is one sled labelled 'SOUND EFFECTS', buried in the Guard drawer among permission rows (park.html). There is no haptics sled anywhere — TactileSoundEngine.kt:292 hard-codes 'var hapticsEnabled: Boolean = true' with no UI caller — and no luminance or public-face control. The Shield's routines change only app tiers: shield.html shows SLEEP 20:00→03:30 ON as a blocklist swap, so at 20:00 in a shared bedroom the phone gets stricter about apps and not one degree quieter, darker or more private in the room. Apple Watch Theater Mode is the reference decision: one tap bundles Silent Mode ON plus 'keeps the screen dark until you tap it' — sound and light treated as one shared-space behaviour (Apple Watch User Guide, via Control Center masks icon). Android Bedtime mode does the same bundling (Do Not Disturb + grayscale + Keep the screen dark) on a schedule. Monolith has the schedule machinery and the bundle concept (loadouts) and never connects them.

Recommendation: Add a first-class QUIET ROOM manners bundle modelled on Apple Watch Theater Mode's one-tap bundle: speaker transients off, haptics collapsed to a single low-amplitude tick, Airlock/desk-clock luminance capped, public face (finding above) forced on. Put it in three places Monolith already has: as a Deck-level toggle next to the slide, as a per-loadout property so STUDY in a library and SLEEP in a dorm carry it, and auto-applied by the SLEEP routine the way Bedtime mode auto-applies its bundle. Manners become a designed mode with a name, not a side effect of one sled in a drawer.

#### [HIGH] The one authentic ritual-object artefact — the ML-01 numbered-unit plate — is buried at the foot of a settings drawer where the ritual never goes

ParkDrawer.kt:105-107 defines PLATE_HEAD: 'MONOLITH ML-01 / UNIT Nº 01 · BUILT FOR ONE USER · NOT FOR SALE' — the only place the app treats itself as a singular manufactured object rather than software. Its seating, ParkDrawer.kt:623-645, is section (7) 'furniture at the foot' of the Park (Guard) sheet: after the permission board, FIX key, sound/shorts sleds and theme line, below a 32.dp spacer and a hairline, set in Anonymous Pro 10sp/16sp at 1.2sp tracking — body ink for two lines, secondary grey for the rest (park.html spec plate). It appears on no ritual surface: not on the Deck imprint (TactileDeckScreen.kt), not in the Airlock, not on the Receipt (ReceiptSheet.kt:175-182 footer instead exiles the record to YPT). Braun, Leica and Teenage Engineering put the maker's plate and serial on the face of the object, where it is seen at every use; Monolith files its best identity sentence under its permissions.

Recommendation: Promote the plate, verbatim, to the surfaces of the ritual: print 'MONOLITH ML-01 · UNIT Nº 01' as the Deck imprint's standing tenant line (replacing the purely functional count line's monopoly on that slot) and as the Receipt slip's header above the №, demoting the YPT footer. Keep the full PLATE_BODY spec text in Park as the long-form colophon. No copy changes — this is a seating fix: the object should sign its work where the work happens.

#### [HIGH] The wheel's simulated lamp is 300+ arc calls rendering light nobody can see, including two deliberately broken teeth

RotaryWheelView.onDraw simulates one fixed lamp (azimuth 245.2°) three separate times: the socket ring is drawn as ~120 segmented 3.5° arcs, each painted twice with a cos^3 falloff (BlockitCoreViews.kt:586-632), the chamfer catch repeats it as ~90 more segmented arcs in tint #FFF6EC (BlockitCoreViews.kt:640-665), and the knurled rim draws 120 teeth whose specular alpha is modulated by a pseudo-random flare array that deliberately makes teeth 17 and 83 dimmer — 'visibly wrong inside the bright zone' (BlockitCoreViews.kt:557-568, 684-714). After all that arithmetic the peak alpha is capped at 0.17 of the curve by day and 0.10 by night (BlockitCoreViews.kt:704), i.e. a ≤14% white wash on a 3.5dp tooth: in deck.html the wheel reads as a flat disc with ticks — the entire lighting model is below the threshold of perception. Playdate, designed with Teenage Engineering, gets a stronger material identity from a 1-bit black/white screen with no greys at all: identity from constraint, not from simulating photons the display cannot show.

Recommendation: Delete the lamp simulation wholesale: socket shading, chamfer catch and tooth specular become one flat two-tone seam (alternate teeth ink at 18% / paper at 0%, no per-tooth flare, no azimuth math). Keep the genuinely legible parts — the tick scale, the sweep arc, the strait cut. If materiality is wanted, earn it the Playdate way: one bold flat decision (e.g. the whole disc in surfaceBright against the recess) instead of 330 sub-perceptual arc calls per frame.

#### [HIGH] The PARK spec plate — the app's only manual — is unversioned hard-coded text that stays 'UNIT Nº 01' and keeps printing old rules after behaviour changes

ui/components/ParkDrawer.kt:105-107 PLATE_HEAD is hard-coded 'MONOLITH ML-01 / UNIT Nº 01 · BUILT FOR ONE USER · NOT FOR SALE' and PLATE_BODY at ParkDrawer.kt:109-122 is a fixed list of operating rules ('HOLD: 60 SECONDS… PEEK: 2 MINUTES… COLOUR IS A VERB…'). design-renders/park.html renders this plate verbatim as the foot of PARK — the app's only in-app manual. The code comment at ParkDrawer.kt:111-116 already admits one plate clause was 'falsified on his phone' and struck, proving plate text drifts from behaviour with no versioning mechanism to catch it.

Recommendation: Version the plate like a real instrument plate: 'ML-01 · REV <versionName> · PLATE <n>' with PLATE_BODY generated from the same constants that drive behaviour (hold seconds, peek minutes, sniper default) so the printed rule cannot diverge from the shipped rule, and add a 'CHANGED IN THIS REV' line under the plate listing any rule whose text changed since the last plate revision. Follow Braun/Teenage Engineering practice where the spec plate and manual revision move with the firmware revision — the plate is the changelog's permanent home, not a frozen engraving.

#### [HIGH] The icon's frame lives outside the adaptive safe zone, so each launcher brand crops a different icon

ic_launcher_background.xml:14 draws the 'recessed linen frame' as a filled square from 18,18 spanning 72x72dp on the 108dp canvas. Its corners sit ~50.9dp from the centre (54,54), far outside the platform's guaranteed-visible safe zone — a 66dp-diameter circle centred on the canvas; everything outside it may be clipped by the OEM mask (circle on Pixel, squircle on Samsung, teardrop/rounded-square elsewhere). So the frame survives whole on squ squircle/square masks, is cropped into four floating corner arcs on a circular mask, and is cut asymmetrically by a teardrop. Compounding it, res/mipmap-anydpi-v26/ic_launcher.xml and ic_launcher_round.xml are byte-identical (same background and foreground drawables, lines 3-4 of each): the round variant launchers explicitly request gets no round-specific art, so the square frame fights the circular mask it was requested for.

Recommendation: Design to the mask, not to the square: either delete the linen frame or pull all meaningful geometry inside the Ø66dp safe circle (inset the frame to roughly 24-84dp with rounded corners that read as intentional under every mask), and make the background full-bleed colour only, the way Google's own Clock keeps its dial marks inside the safe circle and lets the mask own the silhouette. Then ship a genuinely enlarged, frame-less round variant for ic_launcher_round and verify all four masks (circle, squircle, rounded square, teardrop) in Android Studio's icon preview before calling the icon done.

#### [HIGH] Materials are lied about: porcelain, obsidian and brass are just hex values with heroic names

Color.kt:7 'Strictly Zero-Green: Every single color satisfies green < maxOf(red, blue)' and Color.kt:100-110 aliases PorcelainCanvas=#E4DFDA, ObsidianHeader=#2E2A26, EspressoInk=#252323. deck.html card: background #FAF6F0, 1px border, radius 24px — a flat fill called porcelain, a flat fill called obsidian, slide cap in deck.html with a 1.2px white top line and 1px right line faking a machined edge on #F55314. No grain, weight, temperature or wear behaviour is coded anywhere.

Recommendation: Apply TE's materials honesty literally: rename tokens to what they are on a screen (Ground, Raised, Recess, Ink, Accent) and delete Porcelain/Obsidian/Espresso from code and copy. Then give the one remaining material a real behaviour OP-1's powder-coat has — consequence: e.g. the slide cap dulls/scratches fractionally with each refusal and restores on a clean finish, so surface state is earned history, not a highlight line drawn at draw time.

#### [HIGH] The object has two faces: a primary-colour sundial on the home screen, a stone monolith inside

ic_launcher_foreground.xml:9 fill #1E40FF ultramarine ring, :17 #F5B800 canary sector, :21 #E6332A crimson hub — a Bauhaus sundial. Inside, Color.kt:8-19 allows only warm stone #E4DFDA, ink #252323 and single orange #F55314, 'Zero-Green' verified. deck.html header reads MONOLITH in 10sp mono on stone; no blue, yellow or red sundial geometry appears on any of deck/shield/drawer/park/airlock/receipt renders. The home-screen object and the in-app object share no colour, shape or mark.

Recommendation: Redesign the launcher mark as the object itself, following OP-1's silhouette test (recognisable as a black-and-white outline): a stone slab rectangle, one orange slide cap at its base, MONOLITH cut in mono — drawn only from the in-app tokens #E4DFDA/#252323/#F55314. Retire the sundial entirely; an object cannot have a different face on the shelf than in the hand.

#### [HIGH] Playful-serious collapses to serious-only: the 'Toys' are a text list you cannot play with

MonolithModels.kt:799-850 CurioCatalog: Toy 01 Harmonic Loop, Toy 02 Brass Gyroscope 'Four brass rings... no wider than a palm', Toy 05 Sand Pendulum 'swing decaying into a spiral' — lore describes touchable objects. drawer.html Cabinet frame renders all six as identical text rows: serial, name, subtitle, hairline, no image, no canvas, no interaction. Everywhere else the voice is punitive: airlock.html 'AIRLOCK INTERCEPTION • LOCKED', 'EMERGENCY BREAK', park.html 'GUARD', shield.html SHUT/PEEK. No joke, character or playable surprise exists on any render.

Recommendation: Make the Toys earn the name, as OP-1's tape reels, gorilla drummers and Kraftwerk arpeggiators do — serious engine, funny face: render each forged Curio as a small playable Canvas instrument (spin the gyroscope, drag the pendulum, it decays and draws the spiral from the lore) inside the Cabinet, 30 seconds of purposeless play per toy. Keep the blocking voice severe; reserve all play for the Cabinet so the contrast itself becomes the tone: prison outside, toybox inside.

#### [HIGH] Constraints are merely limits, not OP-Z-style generative engines

BlockitCoreViews.kt:371-385 RotaryWheelView minutesValue coerceIn(5,180) — 176 continuous choices; studyBlocksCount coerceIn(1,8) shown in deck.html only as 8 hub dots, 2 filled, no label. Theme.kt:80 two radii and Color.kt:19 tokens are limits, but they curate nothing. ParkDrawer.kt:109-123 prints the limits afterwards as a spec list ('HOLD: 60 SECONDS... PEEK: 2 MINUTES') rather than designing choices around them. Contrast the Deck's own FLOW keycap in deck.html: a preset word with no distinct behaviour from any other minute count.

Recommendation: Replace the continuous dial with prescriptive engines the way OP-Z labels identical tracks Bass/Lead/Chords so the label steers behaviour: e.g. 3 seats only — SPRINT 25×1, DEEP 50×2, MONOLITH 90×2 — each with a fixed break, peek and sound/haptic character tuned to have no dead spots, and the wheel's detents exist only at those seats. Keep a long-press 'custom' escape, but make the designed path opinionated; a dial that can stop anywhere teaches nothing.

#### [HIGH] No sharp edge exists anywhere in an app named Monolith — every plane is rounded, so edges carry no information

A search of the whole ui/ tree finds zero RectangleShape and zero 0dp corners: every plane terminates in a radius — Theme.kt:80-87 legislates 12dp/24dp, and production adds 20dp (slide cap), 16dp (ParkDrawer.kt:237), 9dp, 8dp, 3dp and 2dp caps and chips. The app is named for a squared slab of stone, yet no surface in it has the sharp edge that is Tanaka's entire legibility device: in the Grammar, the edge is where light breaks and one plane separates from the next; in Monolith every separation is done instead by a 1dp hairline (e.g. TactileDeckScreen.kt:581) while the corners themselves say nothing — a receipt slip, an emergency overlay and a routine chip all round off identically, so edge treatment encodes neither rank, danger nor finality.

Recommendation: Give the edge a grammar: set the terminal surfaces — the Receipt slip and the Airlock wall — to a true 0dp sharp corner, keep 24dp only for the one raised instrument card and 12dp for controls that move (caps, sleds), and delete the 2/3/8/9/16/20dp strays, so a user learns once that sharp means final, round means touchable, and can read any new screen's corners before its words.

#### [HIGH] Painted material, frozen light: the cap's highlight, shadow and the hero's letterpress ghosts never behave like the materials they imitate

B&O's material law is literal: if it looks like aluminium, it is aluminium, and its highlight moves because a real edge turns in real light. Monolith paints its materials and then freezes the paint. BlockitCoreViews.kt:1804-1825 draws the slide cap with a fixed offset shadow (0x4D000000 at +2.5dp), a fixed lit top edge (0x66FFFFFF at top+1.2dp) and a fixed 1dp marker — none of which varies with displayed fraction, travel direction or the seal's exit phase. During the seal shot the room itself is told to recede and re-light (TactileDeckScreen.kt:582-600: scale 0.94, rise -10dp, blur peaking at 6dp, ground stepping at t=400) while the cap's painted light stays glued in place; the hero numeral likewise wears two static ±1dp 'press' ghosts (TactileDeckScreen.kt:655-672) that simulate letterpress depth without ever being pressed.

Recommendation: Make the cap's light obey its motion: fade the top-edge highlight from 0x66 to 0x26 and shift the shadow offset from +2.5dp to +1dp as displayed goes 0→1 (a settling edge catches less light), and at groundStepped (t=400) step both ghosts of the hero numeral to their night values in the same frame as the ground, instead of keying them only to effectiveNight. Cut the catch ghost entirely on the running readout — a live counter wearing fake press-depth is the one surface that must be honest print.

#### [HIGH] Six claimed materials, one material on screen: brass, sand, string and light all arrive as the same ruled prose row

Munari's Prelibri (1945) are twelve pre-books in different materials, sizes and bindings with no words at all — a child who cannot read learns by hand that brass, wood, sponge and mesh are different kinds of knowledge before any text arrives. Monolith's six curios claim six materials — light (Harmonic Loop), brass (Brass Gyroscope), thread (String Prism), orbit, sand (Sand Pendulum), geometry (Monolith Cube, MonolithModels.kt:799-852) — yet KineticArtifact (MonolithModels.kt:487-503) holds only five strings (id, serialCode, name, subtitle, lore), and the Cabinet in DrawerScreen.kt renders every one as the identical ruled row of serial/name/subtitle plus, in detail, one 13sp lore paragraph. In the drawer.html render all six rows are typographically indistinguishable. Material, Munari's first teacher, has been translated into prose and thereby deleted.

Recommendation: Give each Cabinet detail a distinct material behaviour instead of the shared text template: Brass Gyroscope tilts with the device gyro with soft haptic detents per ring, Sand Pendulum draws a granular trace that visibly decays as you watch, String Prism sounds a pitch that rises as its lines are pulled taut. Same cabinet, six different hands-on materials — no scores attached to any of them.

#### [MEDIUM] The desk clock — the surface built to be left in a room with other people — broadcasts the task title to the room and exits on any touch, including a stranger's

AirlockAndDisarmOverlays.kt:141 makes the entire desk-clock Box '.clickable(onClick = onDismiss)', :154 prints the instruction 'NIGHTSTAND DESK CLOCK • TAP ANYWHERE TO EXIT', and :196-226 (deskClockBannerText) prints the owner's raw task title or free-text intention in the 14sp banner (render: receipt.html frame 4). This is the one surface designed to sit unattended in a shared room — nightstand, desk, classroom — yet it is simultaneously the most publicly legible (96sp time plus the owner's task in words) and the easiest surface in the app to destroy: a child's tap, a sleeve, a repair tech's handling all dismiss it into the full app underneath.

Recommendation: Design the clock as a bystander surface, following Apple StandBy's decisions: content redacted to what a room may know — time, progress bar, and 'STUDY · ENDS 19:32' from the loadout category, never the free-text title/intention — and exit removed from the whole-surface tap. Replace it with a single deliberate exit: press-and-hold 2 seconds on a small corner target with a filling ring, labelled 'HOLD TO EXIT'. Taps elsewhere do nothing. A surface whose job is to be left alone with other people must survive being touched by them.

#### [MEDIUM] The collection never composes: six owned curios still look like six isolated rows, and a complete set has no designed state

The Cabinet in DrawerScreen.kt:325-440 is a LazyColumn of ruled text rows plus one footnote rule line — the same list grammar as stored homework tasks. There is no group view, no arrangement, and no state change when forgedArtifactIds reaches all six: the header stays 'CABINET', the layout stays a list, nothing assembles. design-renders/drawer.html Frame 2 shows the ceiling of the design: even a fully imagined cabinet is a ledger page. Contrast Forest, where individual trees are unremarkable but the accumulated forest — an ensemble landscape no single session produces — is the actual collectible, and Opal, where gems fill a shelf whose completeness is itself visible.

Recommendation: Design the whole, not just the parts: give the Cabinet a composed header plate — the six serial plates laid out as a single 2x3 spec-plate strip (forged plates solid, unforged as ghost outlines) that sits above the list and visibly completes. On 6/6, change the cabinet's state once and permanently: the strip becomes a single unbroken plate and the standing rule line is replaced by a completion line. This is buildable in pure Compose text and box work, needs no artwork, and gives the set an ensemble form a list can never have.

#### [MEDIUM] Koko denied: a year of history renders factory-fresh — nothing in Monolith is allowed to weather

Koko — austere sublimity — is beauty that has weathered: age is allowed to show and is honoured for it. Nothing in Monolith is allowed to age. The Drawer keeps months of history, yet drawer.html shows Fri 30 Oct and Sat 24 Oct rendered identically — same row weight, same card, same fresh type — and every receipt issues on the same pristine surfaceBright #FAF6F0 card (ui/components/ReceiptSheet.kt:83-90). A year-old instrument looks factory-new; the past is stored but never weathered, so the Drawer reads as an unchanging database rather than a life accumulating patina.

Recommendation: Let the Drawer weather: render the current month at full row weight, then progressively reduce older months in DrawerScreen — smaller type, no card ground, date + day-word + duration on one bare line — and add one permanent seam notch per completed week to the Deck card's edge, so long use is visible as wear the user earned.

#### [MEDIUM] The Cabinet charges reading time for lore that decides nothing, inside the archive meant to save it

DrawerScreen.kt's Cabinet re-homes six curios whose only content is reading: CurioCatalog in MonolithModels.kt:799-850 gives each artifact a serial, name, subtitle and a lore paragraph (:813 'Two waves of different pitch, drawn against each other until the line closes…', :820, :827, :834, :841, :848), and the Cabinet detail in DrawerScreen.kt prints serial, name, subtitle and full lore before the one decision-relevant fact, FORGED / NOT YET FORGED. The Drawer is the user's history archive — the filtering surface — yet its cabinet section competes with stored tasks by offering six pieces of fiction that inform no choice, cannot be acted on (SELECT was removed as meaningless) and never expire. A finished span 'forges one' at random (DrawerScreen.kt cabinet rule line), so even the reward's arrival is information about nothing the user did.

Recommendation: Invert the Cabinet detail in DrawerScreen: print FORGED / NOT YET FORGED as the headline, keep serial+name as one line, and delete the lore paragraphs from CurioCatalog entirely — or move lore to a single shared cabinet footer shown once. The Cabinet list itself should show forged state only, so scanning six curios costs one glance, not six readings.

### Philosophy and meaning — 34 findings (27 critical, 6 high, 1 medium, 0 low)

#### [CRITICAL] Unguarded time is priced at zero: the idle Deck meters the vault to the second and the hours outside it not at all

The unarmed Deck (design-renders/deck.html) shows the next session's TOTAL, GUARD 4/4 and 'SLIDE OR TAP TO START' — the hours spent unarmed, phone in hand, before that slide are rendered as nothing: no elapsed-unguarded readout exists in TactileDeckScreen.kt, whose eyebrow switches only between TOTAL, SESSION RUNNING and BREAK (ui/screens/TactileDeckScreen.kt:616-618). Seneca's miser paradox — men lock their strongboxes yet let anyone seize their time — is inverted here: the vault door is instrumented to the second, the open field around it is not even priced. The app therefore teaches that time only becomes wealth once Monolith is holding it.

Recommendation: Make waste visible on the idle Deck without adding any blocker: replace the idle hero's empty sentence slot with a live unguarded meter in receipt mono — 'UNGUARDED 02:14 SINCE LAST SESSION' — ticking from the last receipt's ENDED time, resetting silently at arm. On the receipt itself add the reciprocal line 'NEXT SESSION BEGAN n HRS LATER' is wrong scope; keep it Deck-only: one line, no judgement word, no red — the fact alone is the Senecan pressure.

#### [CRITICAL] The emergency exit is a muscular feat - Weil's attention is explicitly not one

Weil, via Stanford Encyclopedia on 'Reflections on the Right Use of School Studies' (Waiting for God 57-65): attention is not a 'muscular effort' but a 'negative effort' (WFG 61), suspending thought, leaving it 'empty, waiting, not seeking anything'. Monolith's only early exit is the opposite: AirlockAndDisarmOverlays.kt:801 prints 'Hold to fill 60 seconds. Every 15 seconds banks. If your hand slips, what isn't banked drains away', implemented by Emergency60sValveView in BlockitSuitcaseAndSwitchesViews.kt:532-564,677-696 (requiredSeconds=60, label 'KEEP HOLDING VALVE'). A tired, cramping hand is the price of leaving - exactly the state in which Weil says attention is scarcely possible.

Recommendation: Replace the grip with waiting on the Disarm overlay: one tap on 'END THIS SESSION' starts a 60-second stillness exit - a blank night card with no fill, no bank seams and no drain - completed by not touching the phone, cancelled by any tap. Delete the 15-second banking/draining rule and the 'KEEP HOLDING VALVE' label; exit is proved by absence of effort, not sustained contraction.

#### [CRITICAL] The limen is the same grey room at night: identical Deck, wheel, strip and rail — only the paint and one eyebrow word change

Van Gennep/Turner: the liminal person is stripped of prior status and ordinary structure is suspended. Monolith's limen suspends almost nothing but the palette. The running Deck is the idle Deck: same instrument card, same rotary wheel, same proof strip, same imprint, same bottom rail (receipt.html frame 3, the frozen running Deck, vs deck.html) — the only changes are the scheme flip (Theme.kt L108) and the eyebrow TOTAL becoming SESSION RUNNING (TactileDeckScreen.kt L617). The wheel that set the session still sits centre-screen as furniture, the rail still offers SHIELD/TASKS/LEDGER citizenship, and the slide zone still prints 'SLIDE OR TAP TO START' under a live session. A different country with the same street plan, same government and same shops is not a different country.

Recommendation: Design the liminal Deck as a stripped room, not a recoloured one: during a session remove the rail entirely, remove the wheel (its work is done), and leave only elapsed presence, the intention, HELD count and the valve — a layout that cannot be mistaken for the ordinary Deck at a glance across the room. Configuration (Shield, Tasks, Ledger) should be unreachable in-limen, not merely ratcheted: in van Gennep's terms the initiate has no status to administer with.

#### [CRITICAL] The limen is never anti-structure: the session is the most audited state in the app, so the user never actually leaves ordinary structure

Turner's liminal phase works only because status, rank and the ordinary accounting of structure are suspended — the initiand is 'betwixt and between the positions assigned and arrayed by law, custom, convention.' Monolith imports the full audit apparatus into the threshold instead: the ongoing notification live-counts compliance ('{MM:SS} left • Block {i}/{n} • {count} urges stopped', service/MonolithShieldService.kt buildNotification ~L223-226, rendered in design-renders/receipt.html frame 2), the running Deck keeps the proof strip stamping 'BIND HELD · THIS VISIT / PROOF: LIVE BIND' and strikes the imprint with the session key (ui/screens/TactileDeckScreen.kt L1097 ImprintSlot strikeKey), and every deflection is logged as evidence for a later grade. The user inside the session is not released from structure into the work; they are structure's most-watched subject. What should feel like seclusion feels like probation, which is why the middle of a long session reads as anxiety rather than absorption.

Recommendation: Strip the running surfaces of accounting: the shield notification shows only remaining time and the intention ('24:36 left • Revise thermodynamics'), the running Deck's proof-strip seam goes blank and the imprint is struck only at finish, and the 'urges stopped' count appears for the first time on the receipt, where judgement belongs. Suspension of the scoreboard is the ritual form that holds the limen.

#### [CRITICAL] GUARD 4/4 prints the tool's health on every screen when nothing is wrong — the one state a working tool should meet with silence

ui/components/GuardLine.kt:39 returns GuardLinePrint("GUARD 4/4") for the whole state, and the header band carries it permanently (deck.html render: the idle home screen's header reads MONOLITH / GUARD 4/4). The only silent state in guardLineFor is UNMEASURED (GuardLine.kt:34-36 returns null) — Monolith goes quiet only when it cannot measure itself, never when it is healthy. The doc comment at GuardLine.kt:22-25 adds that at the seal the print is captured and 'the band holds it for the session's whole life': even mid-work, the header keeps certifying the tool instead of the work. Heidegger's test is exact: ready-to-hand equipment withdraws; a hammer that printed 'HANDLE 4/4' on its grip would force a daily inspection glance at the one moment inspection is pointless.

Recommendation: Make WHOLE print nothing: when warranted == COUNTED.size, guardLineFor returns null and the Deck header's right side collapses to empty. Keep the named-lack print (GUARD 2/4 — OVERLAY) exactly as is — breakdown is when the tool may speak.
