Move the health fact to where inspection belongs: one line in Park, 'LAST PROVED 21:47 · ALL FOUR HELD', shown only when Park is opened.

#### [CRITICAL] The cure keeps no register of its own dose: Monolith's own opens are the one temptation never intercepted, counted or printed

intercept_logs (MonolithModels.kt:451) and BlockedAppEntity.interceptCount (MonolithModels.kt:240) record every other app's temptation, and the receipt prints those deflections by name — but Monolith's own package has no tier, no intercept row and no count anywhere. During a sealed session the user can open Monolith itself unlimited times — checking the Deck clock, re-reading the held digest, visiting the Cabinet — and none of it is logged, printed or priced. The drug exempts its own bottle from the register it keeps on every other substance.

Recommendation: Make Monolith a row in its own register: count Deck opens during a session as deflections and print them on the ReceiptSheet as a mono line 'MONOLITH · n OPENS' alongside the other deflections; on the idle Deck, add a quiet line under the dial, 'TIME IN MONOLITH TODAY · n MIN', computed from its own foreground time, so the cure's dose is as visible as the poison's.

#### [CRITICAL] The sealed Deck sells hyperattention back to the user: a live HELD count and an openable digest inside the session it claims to protect

TactileDeckScreen.kt:947-965 renders, only while a session is running, a HELD chip carrying monoBadge = capturedNotificationsCount.toString() wired to onOpenNotificationDigest, beside a DESK CLOCK chip — the sealed Deck's forward verbs are checking what you are missing. The digest itself (AirlockAndDisarmOverlays.kt:339-362) lists the held notifications' content. The blocker therefore manufactures the rapid switching Han calls hyperattention: focus, glance at the count, open the feed, return — each switch blessed as 'staying informed'.

Recommendation: Seal the lure: during a running session the HELD chip loses its numeric badge and its tap — it prints HELD as inert print only, the digest cannot open until the receipt, and the Deck's only tappable live surface is DESK CLOCK. The count first appears on the Receipt slip, where it is a record, not a temptation.

#### [CRITICAL] The Safe Break has no existence of its own: it is pre-sold as session time, counted as work, and by design law must not be rendered as a break

Pieper's test is whether rest is defined by the work it serves — Monolith's break is, literally, in the price of work before it happens: MonolithModels.kt:400-402 spanTargetSeconds = blocks × target + (n-1) × 600, and TactileDeckScreen.kt:325/632-635 the idle hero sells that TOTAL with 'breaks priced in'. During the break the span keeps counting it as elapsed session (MonolithModels.kt:414-422), and the desk clock is forbidden by an in-code law from showing it as rest at all: MonolithModels.kt:391-392 'the break is not rendered AS a break (Nacht's law holds), session time is' — AirlockAndDisarmOverlays.kt:120-123 repeats that a Safe Break 'earns no special rendering'. Its length is one fixed constant the user never chose (MonolithRepository.kt:110 SAFE_BREAK_DURATION_SECONDS = 10*60), it can only occur between blocks, expiry auto-advances into the next block (MonolithRepository.kt:1846-1888 advancePastBreak), and the Deck's one forward verb during it is END BREAK (TactileDeckScreen.kt:920-939) — i.e. return to work early. Nothing in the break asks what the user wants to receive, look at, or do for its own sake.

Recommendation: Give the break an ontology, not a tariff: (1) Remove breaks from the Deck hero TOTAL — hero prints work time only, with the break shown as a separate unpriced line ' + A BREAK, AS LONG AS IT IS' once breaks become user-lengthened. (2) Repeal the no-rendering law: during a Safe Break the Deck and desk clock switch to a dedicated BREAK state — no session progress bar, no span countdown, no block index ('Block 2 of 3' disappears), just the word BREAK and, if anything, elapsed-not-remaining time. (3) Replace the primary END BREAK chip with two equal verbs, STAY and RETURN, and let a break be extended once by 5 minutes with no ledger entry, no receipt line, and no effect on the session's outcome word.

#### [CRITICAL] There is no Sunday: the week is a Monday-anchored ration ledger and every seeded routine runs ALL_DAYS, so the seventh day is indistinguishable from the first

The app's only definition of a week is accounting: MonolithWeek.kt:9-17 defines it solely so 'the token and any future weekly surface' can count emergency-break spends against a Monday 00:00 anchor. All three seeded routines ship daysMask = ALL_DAYS (MonolithRepository.kt:843-851: FASTED BLOCK, DAY BLOCKS, SLEEP; MonolithModels.kt:574 ALL_DAYS = 127, bit 6 = Sunday treated identically), so a fresh install guards Sunday 05:00-08:00, 09:00-19:30 and 20:00-03:30 exactly as it guards Monday. Even the long-term monument is a work calendar: BlockitTowerFadersAndCatalogViews.kt:20 lays bricks '7 per floor; one brick per focused block/day' — seven identical production slots, no differentiated seventh. Pieper's feast day is time set apart and deliberately unproductive; Monolith has a rollover, not a Sabbath: Monday 00:00 merely stops last week's token rows matching.

Recommendation: Build an actual seventh day: (1) Seed all routines with a Mon-Sat mask and Sunday off by default; enabling a Sunday routine requires an explicit per-routine Sunday toggle in its editor. (2) On Sunday the Deck changes state, not just schedule: no wheel, no TOTAL, no ENDS-AT strip — a single FEAST screen reading 'MONOLITH IS OFF TODAY' with the Drawer and curios reachable and nothing else to arm. (3) Sunday is judgement-exempt in RoutineDerive (no MISSED/PARTIAL can be booked against it) and the Tower renders the seventh cell of each floor as an open gap, not a missing brick, so the monument itself teaches that the week is completed by its empty day.

#### [CRITICAL] SLEEP is not rest but the night shift of total work: sleep itself is renamed 'Full Lockdown' and the guard stays on duty while the user is unconscious

The SLEEP loadout's own copy conflates rest with the strictest work discipline: MonolithModels.kt:54-58 title 'Full Lockdown', subtitle 'Blocks every distracting app except Phone, Clock, and Maps for total focus or wind-down', badge 'Strict Mode' — sleep, focus and wind-down are one product. It is seeded as a 20:00-03:30 routine on ALL_DAYS (MonolithRepository.kt:849-851), i.e. a 7.5-hour blocking session the app actively enforces overnight, and its ending is a bureaucratic 'stand-down' that produces no acknowledgement the user rested (MonolithRepository.kt:1006-1016, 1060-1075: SLEEP rows are 'simply stood down', no booking or stamp; the finish word elsewhere is 'SLEPT THROUGH', MonolithRepository.kt:1686). Pieper's point is that a total-work world colonises even non-work: here the app never itself rests — it works hardest, uninterrupted, precisely when its owner cannot contemplate, choose, or receive anything.

Recommendation: Make SLEEP the one routine where Monolith stands down instead of locking down: (1) Rename the loadout from 'Full Lockdown / Strict Mode' to 'Monolith Sleeps Too' and change its mechanism — at the SLEEP start the app seals nothing, starts no session row, and schedules its own guard to be inert except for user-whitelisted alarms/calls, so the night is unguarded rather than guarded. (2) Add a 20-minute wind-down descent that ends with the app dismissing itself to a black screen reading 'NOTHING IS BEING KEPT. GOOD NIGHT.' — no countdown, no span, no morning receipt for the night. (3) Delete the SLEPT THROUGH outcome: a night produces no receipt, no Drawer entry and no Tower consequence of any kind.

#### [CRITICAL] Challenge is priced only in minutes: no task carries a demand level and no surface knows the user's skill, so challenge-skill matching is impossible by construction

StudyModePreset (MonolithModels.kt:61-72) offers four 'difficulties' that are only durations: 25, 50, 90 minutes and FLOW — workMinutes, breakMinutes, block count, nothing about demand. FocusTaskEntity (MonolithModels.kt:100-125) has title, categoryTag, notes and an estimate the product has deliberately zeroed ('MINUTES DIE'), but no difficulty, familiarity or demand field anywhere in the schema. The wheel's only axis is 5-180 minutes (TactileDeckScreen.kt dial; MonolithViewModel.kt:217 defaults it to 50), so 'challenge' in Monolith literally means 'how long', never 'how hard relative to this person's skill at this task'. Flow's central condition — challenge matched to skill, adjustable as both change — has no representation in the data model, so it cannot be matched, sensed or learned.

Recommendation: Add a demand axis beside the time axis: at arm time, under the wheel, a three-stop cap selector for the bonded task — REVISION (known ground), WORK (at my edge), STRETCH (past it) — stored as a task/session field. Use it concretely: REVISION sessions default the wheel shorter and allow peek, STRETCH sessions pre-split the task via defaultSubStepsForCategory and suggest a shorter first block; the Receipt prints the pair ('50 MIN · STRETCH · CLEARED') so the Drawer history can finally show whether the user's edge is moving, and the next arm pre-selects the demand that last produced a clean finish at that duration.

#### [CRITICAL] Levels of scale collapse above the session: seal, sled and tower are names, not a composing pattern language

TowerStreakView is defined at ui/views/BlockitTowerFadersAndCatalogViews.kt:24 (bricks 7 per floor, capped at ui/views/BlockitTowerFadersAndCatalogViews.kt:52-53 coerceIn(1,8) floors) but is never instantiated anywhere — the only other reference is an unused import at ui/components/AirlockAndDisarmOverlays.kt:62. The Drawer render (design-renders/drawer.html) states it plainly in its own markup: 'There is no tower, no bricks, no streak and no total anywhere on this screen,' and DrawerScreen.kt:61 codifies 'no totals, no streaks.' Below the session, the Deck composes well (wheel detent → block → 10-minute break → span, TactileDeckScreen.kt:325 totalSpanMinutes = dialMinutes*studyBlocksCount + (studyBlocksCount-1)*10). Above the session there is nothing for it to compose into: a day is a text row, a week is a single emergency token, a life is CurioCatalog's closed list of exactly 6 artifacts (data/MonolithModels.kt:799-860).

Recommendation: Build the missing middle and top scales using the session's own brick as the unit: reinstate TowerStreakView in the Drawer as a week/month centre where one brick = one sealed block, floors = weeks, and tapping a brick opens that day's receipt; above it, let the Cabinet hold one object per month rather than stopping at 6 curios for a lifetime. The seal gesture on the Deck, the brick on the Tower and the object in the Cabinet must be the same mark at three scales, not three unrelated vocabularies.

#### [CRITICAL] A broken session is punished by omission: its receipt loses its title and its sound, the exact inverse of a gold seam

ReceiptSheet.kt:50 and :90-101: 'the faulted sheet carries NO title (F-W1)' — a shield-gap/faulted finish renders an empty Box where every other receipt prints its intention. ReceiptState.kt:109-110: death-booked ELAPSED_SHIELD_GAP finishes 'never pulse' and PARTIAL 'never pulses'. MonolithRepository.kt receiptOutcomeWord reduces the event to 'ENDED · SHIELD GAP' in the same 11sp mono as a clean ending.

Recommendation: Restore the title on the faulted slip and print the gap as the slip's seam: a full-width accent rule between ARMED and ENDED lines labelled 'SHIELD OFF 14:02–14:09 · 7 MIN', plus one low completion pulse for PARTIAL and shield-gap finishes in TactileSoundEngine instead of enforced silence — mark the crack in gold and sound, never by blanking and muting.

#### [CRITICAL] Nothing lasts — except Monolith's record: permanent, immutable, and rendered forever in fresh ink

DrawerScreen.kt:58-66 charter: stored rows are 'never auto-deleted, and nothing on this screen can change one'; MonolithDao.kt:193-195: 'There is no archive table and no delete path for stored rows: retention is permanent.' StoredRow (DrawerScreen.kt:886) renders a 3-year-old row in the identical 14sp title / 10.5sp mono meta / 1dp divider as yesterday's, and search (MonolithDao.kt:212) returns all years in the same ink. Sabi is precisely beauty evidenced in patina and wear — an object that shows no age has no sabi, only cryogenics.

Recommendation: Give the Drawer a weathering law and a letting-go rite. (1) Age gradient: rows older than 6 months lose their category/clock meta to title + date only, and month headings older than a year print in the lighter onSurfaceVariant — the record visibly thins as it ages instead of staying factory-fresh. (2) On ALL MONTHS, add a RELEASE verb per month: releasing collapses that month permanently to one line — 'OCTOBER 2025 — LET GO' with its task count — stored, honoured, and unrecoverable by design. Permanence becomes a choice the user renews, not a sentence the app imposes.

#### [CRITICAL] The session itself has no Ma screen: the hours the user bought as emptiness render as a per-second ticking dashboard, and even the desk clock is a 96sp countdown with a progress bar

During a session the Deck stays a live instrument: ui/MonolithViewModel.kt:1020 ticks delay(1000L) and TactileDeckScreen.kt:617 prints eyebrow 'SESSION RUNNING' over a hero MM:SS that changes every second, a 6dp progress track plus a '%'-complete readout (TactileDeckScreen.kt running branch replacing the 288dp wheel). The one alternative, AlwaysOnDeskClockOverlay (AirlockAndDisarmOverlays.kt:70-210, receipt.html frame 4), is true black but fills it with a 96sp ticking clock, a 16dp progress bar and a task banner. Ma is an emptiness that holds attention without demanding it; Monolith sells hours of absence yet offers no screen that can simply be left face-up and ignored — every in-session surface re-summons the eye once per second.

Recommendation: Add a still session face as the Deck's default running form: after the seal, TactileDeckScreen collapses to intention in 15sp Atkinson, end time as 'ENDS 19:32' in the strip's TIME cell, and nothing else — no seconds, no percent, no progress bar. Time updates at minute granularity only. A tap briefly restores the full instrument panel for 5 seconds, then it empties again. Apply the same reduction to AlwaysOnDeskClockOverlay: drop its 16dp progress bar and show wall-clock time of day plus the intention, so the nightstand object is a room, not a readout.

#### [CRITICAL] Fukinsei refused: attention must fit a perfect 5-minute lattice — no irregular session can exist

Fukinsei honours irregularity — the off-centre, the uneven — as the mark of something real. Monolith's time instrument permits no irregularity at all: RotaryWheelView draws stops ONLY every 5 minutes from 10 to 180, '35 stops at 9 degrees each' (ui/views/BlockitCoreViews.kt:742-749, geometry at :503-505), study blocks are 1-8 identical units, and a session's span is computed as n identical blocks plus identical 600-second breaks (data/MonolithModels.kt:399-402 spanTargetSeconds). The week likewise turns on one regular Monday 00:00 anchor (data/MonolithWeek.kt:22-27). A 23-minute, 7-minute or tapering act of attention cannot be expressed — the hand's natural, uneven intention is snapped to the machine's lattice before focus begins. The asymmetry Zen treats as life, Monolith treats as error.

Recommendation: Break the lattice on the Deck wheel: give RotaryWheelView continuous 1-minute detents (fine ticks, no 5-minute snapping), let the hero print odd totals unrounded ('23 MIN'), and allow unequal blocks — a long first block and short last block set by a second hub tap — so a session plan can be asymmetric in shape, not just in length.

#### [CRITICAL] Radical monopoly of legitimate focus: an hour focused without the machine counts as MISSED, or as nothing at all

Illich's radical monopoly: a tool crosses into manipulation when it holds exclusive control over satisfying the need it serves, delegitimising every other way of meeting it. Monolith holds exactly that monopoly over 'focused'. A routine window with no Monolith session row is judged WindowJudgement.MISSED (data/RoutineDerive.kt:224-227, J4), and a finish exists only for inactive rows carrying the machine's own outcome stamps — ELAPSED_CLEAN, STOPWATCH_ENDED, ATTENDED/PARTIAL (data/ReceiptState.kt:28-47, 88-110). There is no honour entry, manual log or self-declaration anywhere in the codebase: a user who leaves the phone in another room and works for three hours — the most convivial focus there is — earns no brick, no receipt, and, if a routine was scheduled, a MISSED verdict. Focus the apparatus did not witness is focus the record says did not happen.

Recommendation: Break the monopoly on the Drawer and the routine judgement: add a 'WITHOUT THE MACHINE' declaration on any past day in the Drawer — the user states the span and what it was, in their own words. Such a day judges a routine window as ATTENDED (SELF-DECLARED), printed on any receipt in a visibly different stamp (unboxed mono text, no receipt number, no brick, no curio — honour without counterfeit proof), and counted in a separate Drawer line, 'HOURS HELD WITHOUT THE MACHINE'. The vernacular route must be first-class, not a correction form.

#### [CRITICAL] No self-obsolescence: success is measured as more sealed time forever, never as needing the seal less

Illich's second watershed: past a threshold a tool becomes counterproductive — it manufactures the need it serves and its success metric becomes its own continued use. Monolith's Deck hero is exactly that metric: the idle eyebrow prints 'TOTAL' and the 72sp hero states cumulative machine-sealed time (ui/screens/TactileDeckScreen.kt:618, 632), and the header demands 'GUARD 4/4' as a permanent whole state (ui/components/GuardLine.kt:13-14, 39). Nothing anywhere in the app fades: no code path reduces friction, retires a routine, relaxes the guard or celebrates an unguarded stretch — grep for taper/graduation/unaided finds only audio fades. A user in month twelve is held to the identical apparatus, identical verdicts and identical 1-token-per-week exit ration as on day one; the design has no answer to 'what does needing this less look like?'

Recommendation: Give the app a deliberate fade arc on the Deck and in PARK: after 8 consecutive ATTENDED routine weeks, the Deck proposes — in print, once — 'RETIRE ONE ROUTINE' and a SHIELD LITE mode (PEEK-tier friction only, no LOCKED tier) for one chosen app; replace the idle hero eyebrow 'TOTAL' with two lines once the user passes 90 days: sealed hours, and beneath it the headline metric 'HOURS HELD UNGUARDED THIS MONTH', computed from declared unaided days. GUARD in PARK gains a fifth lawful whole state, 'GUARD — STOOD DOWN BY CHOICE', so a deliberately relaxed guard reads as mastery, not lack.

#### [CRITICAL] The medium is a dashboard: Monolith's content says focus, its surfaces train self-surveillance and score-keeping

Deck render: hero '1H 50M', ProofStrip 'BLOCK ON · APPS 12 · TIME ENDS 10:40', seam 'BIND HELD · PROOF: LIVE BIND', imprint '9 WILL SHUT · 3 PEEK', header 'GUARD 4/4' (TactileDeckScreen.kt:956 ProofStripBand, :1094 ImprintSlot; MonolithCustomComponents.kt:644,782). Even detention freezes this dashboard as the session's last frame (receipt.html frame 3). McLuhan: a medium's message is the scale/pace/pattern it introduces — here that pattern is continuous self-audit, not attention.

Recommendation: Change the medium during a sealed session, not its content: once sealed, the Deck collapses to the desk-clock ground — time remaining and the intention, nothing else. ProofStrip, ImprintSlot, GUARD fraction and all counts move to the post-session Drawer only, where they are history, not a live feed the user performs for.

#### [CRITICAL] Daylight is not merely absent, it is pre-answered: a blank intention is forged into 'Deep Uninterrupted Study' and the only legitimate reasons to not focus are a closed three-word list

MonolithRepository.kt:1348 startSession writes intention.ifBlank { "Deep Uninterrupted Study" } — silence is filled with the app's purpose, in the user's name. The vocabularies for a legitimate life are likewise closed and authored elsewhere: DayWordStore.kt companion WORDS = listOf("REST","ILL","FAMILY") with the comment 'never TEST. This app does not know test days', and ShieldCapSelector.kt:62 hard-codes the only modes of being as STUDY / WORK / SLEEP. No screen anywhere asks what the user wants, wants to want, or wants to stop wanting; deck.html shows a wheel, a duration and GUARD x/4, and no question at all.

Recommendation: Add a daylight declaration step before first ARM and re-openable from the Deck: one free-text field in the user's own words — 'What is this for, and what would make you stop?' — stored verbatim, never defaulted, never auto-filled. Replace the fabricated fallback: a blank intention must print as NO INTENTION DECLARED on Deck, Airlock and receipt, not as 'Deep Uninterrupted Study'. Open the DayWord list to user-authored words (keep REST/ILL/FAMILY as suggestions) so an exam day, a grief day or a nothing day can be declared without lying.

#### [CRITICAL] Starlight has no data model: nothing in the app can hold a semester-scale aim, so navigation by goals and values is architecturally impossible, not just unshown

There is no object in the schema that can hold an aim longer than a sitting. MonolithModels.kt:268-270 FocusSessionEntity carries only a per-session intention: String, profileName and targetDurationSeconds; MonolithModels.kt:550-569 RoutineEntity carries name, startMinutes, endMinutes, daysMask and loadoutName — a timetable, not a purpose. DayWordStore.kt:5-7 states the Drawer 'prints no totals', and drawer.html confirms it: months of rows with no synthesis, no direction, no 'toward what'. Because no starlight field exists, no surface can render it — not the Deck, not the Drawer, not the moment of temptation.

Recommendation: Introduce a persistent Aim as a first-class entity (name in the user's words, why it matters, target date, linked routines) and render it as starlight on three surfaces: a one-line aim strip under the Deck wheel ('FOR: [aim] · week 6 of 14'), the Airlock card (see next finding), and a Drawer month header that synthesises sessions toward the aim instead of only filing them. Sessions and routines must link to an Aim or be explicitly marked UNATTACHED, so unattributed effort is visible as such.

#### [CRITICAL] At the exact moment of temptation the Airlock can only argue in spotlight: a giant countdown and a clock-out time, with no star to navigate by

AirlockAndDisarmOverlays.kt renders the confrontation in spotlight units only: intercepted app name at 24sp, session-end line at 12.5sp, and an 88sp countdown numeral as the hero; the session's intention appears afterwards at 12.5sp and only 'if (state.sessionIntention.isNotBlank())'. airlock.html shows the same hierarchy. The user is told how long to wait and when the session ends, never what this peek costs the person they are trying to become — there is no self-authored stake on the card because none exists in the data (see Aim absence above), and the generic coaching copy in MonolithModels.kt:198-218 speaks in the app's voice, not the user's.

Recommendation: Rebuild the Airlock card around the user's own starlight: above the countdown, print the linked Aim and one user-authored cost line written at declaration time ('Peeking now trades against: finishing the thermo problem set for the December exam'), in the user's verbatim words. Demote the countdown numeral below that line. If no Aim is linked, the card must say so plainly — 'NO AIM ATTACHED TO THIS SESSION' — instead of letting a timer masquerade as a reason.

#### [CRITICAL] The forge is a lottery: finishing earns a shuffled curio the user never chose, aimed at, or could influence

MonolithRepository.kt:2050 mints the reward as CurioCatalog.artifacts.shuffled().first().id on allBlocksCompleted — pure lot, no input from intention, duration quality, task, or user choice. DrawerScreen.kt:431 prints the rule as a virtue: 'A FINISHED SPAN FORGES ONE — THE FORGE CHOOSES WHICH.' The user performs hours of compliance; the payoff is a dice roll. That is the grifter's structure exactly: a fictional incentive, costless for the house to issue, substituted for anything the user actually chose or did well. A slot pull after homework is not a game about focus; it teaches the user to endure sessions for pulls, and to feel a duplicate or an unwanted Toy as a loss the system manufactured.

Recommendation: Kill the shuffle on the Deck/Cabinet: let the user name the forge before arming — a 'FORGE: —' picker on the Deck beside the intention, listing the six Toys, defaulting to none. No pick, no curio: the session's reward is its receipt. If surprise must stay, print the odds and the full set on the picker ('1 OF 6, BY LOT') so the lottery is honestly labelled a lottery, not dressed as craftsmanship.

#### [CRITICAL] Uselessness is paid as wages: the only useless objects in the app are gated behind a clean productive verdict

Munari's Useless Machines (1933, Design as Art) are useless precisely because they 'do not produce goods for material consumption, do not eliminate labour, nor increase capital' — they hang freely and give spiritual goods to anyone who passes. Monolith inverts this: its only useless objects are wages. MonolithRepository.kt:2049-2051 mints a curio only 'if (allBlocksCompleted && !isRoutineSession)' via CurioCatalog.artifacts.shuffled().first(), and DrawerScreen.kt cabinet rule prints 'A FINISHED SPAN FORGES ONE — THE FORGE CHOOSES WHICH.' Imagination is therefore conditional on a clean verdict; a shield-gap, partial or routine session earns no uselessness at all.

Recommendation: Decouple one object from the ledger entirely: put a live Harmonic Loop (two sine traces closing into a Lissajous knot) on the Deck in its idle, unarmed state — always present, before any session, for forged and unforged users alike, with no counter, no forge event and no Drawer record. Delete its entry from the forge pool so exactly one thing in the app can never be earned.

#### [CRITICAL] There is no plan to build from: the user can only choose among three finished loadouts, never author one

SmartLoadout is a closed enum of exactly three factory designs (MonolithModels.kt:39-60: STUDY/WORK_SPRINT/SLEEP, each with a fixed subtitle recipe). The only loadout gesture in the product is the 3-stop ShieldCapSelector (ShieldMatrixScreen.kt:285-294) and cycleRoutineLoadout, which rotates a routine through the same three names (MonolithViewModel.kt:1521-1526). The one authoring path in code is dead: createCustomProfile (MonolithViewModel.kt:2168) has zero call sites, saveCustomProfile (MonolithRepository.kt:1282) writes a categories CSV no screen can reach, and ShieldMatrixScreen receives profiles/selectedProfileName (lines 93-94) and never renders them. Mari's Autoprogettazione (1974) published plans for 19 pieces in boards and nails precisely so the user performed the design; Monolith publishes finished furniture and lets the user pick a colour.

Recommendation: Give Shield's LOADOUT section a build verb, not just a selector: a SAVE CURRENT RULES AS LOADOUT action that clones the live YOUR RULES state (per-app tiers + blocked sites + sniper/browser toggles) into a named, user-owned loadout, shown as a fourth+ stop on the cap with its name printed, editable and re-appliable, and selectable as a routine payload alongside STUDY/WORK/SLEEP. The factory three become starter plans the user forks, not the whole vocabulary.

#### [CRITICAL] The good life is rationed: one emergency per week, and taking it brands the session BROKE and erases its receipt

ReceiptState.kt:38-41 defines VALVE_BROKE as 'The 60s valve was held to completion: the token was spent and the session BROKE. No receipt, no №, ever.' MonolithRepository.kt completeEmergencyBreak (~L2225-2248) refuses the break outright when the week's single spend exists (emergencyBreaksRemaining, L2178: remaining = 1 − spends), and TactileDeckScreen.kt:1047 labels the only exit 'EMERGENCY BREAK VALVE (60S HOLD)'. A family emergency, a medical call, a child — the reflectively endorsed contents of a good life — are rationed to one per week, and taking one brands the session BROKE and deletes it from the numbered record entirely, while a session spent merely enduring prints a receipt.

Recommendation: Abolish the 1-per-week token and the erasure. In the Airlock valve flow, ask for the reason BEFORE release (one line, typed or picked: 'Family', 'Health', 'Work', free text) and show it back for confirmation — reflection replaces scarcity as the friction. Issue the receipt as normal with outcome word 'ENDED · CALLED AWAY' and the stated reason printed under ENDED on ReceiptSheet; delete the VALVE_BROKE no-receipt branch in ReceiptState.kt so no honest ending is ever unnumbered.

#### [CRITICAL] Moral verdicts (ATTENDED / PARTIAL / MISSED / BROKE) are stamped immutably without ever being endorsed

MonolithModels.kt:313-316 and L565-568: routineOutcome stamps ATTENDED / PARTIAL / MISSED / LATE_FIRE are written once by the finalise funnel and 'Stamps are immutable.' ReceiptSheet.kt:124 prints the verdict word on the slip's ENDED line, and MonolithRepository.kt receiptOutcomeWord (~L1685) maps finishes to ATTENDED / PARTIAL. The user endorsed a schedule and a block list; no surface anywhere shows them the words that will be permanently filed about them, asks whether they accept being graded, or offers a factual alternative. A missed morning becomes a permanent character judgement, not a revisable record.

Recommendation: Add an endorsement sheet to routine creation (and a one-time version for existing routines): show the exact stamp vocabulary — 'This routine will file ATTENDED, PARTIAL or MISSED about you, permanently' — with a factual alternative selected by default, printing 'PRESENT 42 OF 60 MIN' / 'NOT PRESENT' on the receipt and in the Drawer. Stamps become user-editable annotations in the Drawer day view (tap a stamp, reword or clear it), so the record serves the user's own account of the day instead of sentencing it.

#### [HIGH] Liminal time is designed as a countdown to escape: every surface in the limen measures time-left, none suspends ordinary time

Liminality is time out of ordinary time — 'betwixt and between', unmeasured by the profane clock. Monolith's limen is the most clock-saturated state in the app: the hero readout becomes time remaining, the shield notification prints '{MM:SS} left • Block {i}/{n} • {count} urges stopped' (MonolithShieldService.kt L135-137 and updateNotification), the strip's TIME cell prints ENDS HH:mm, and even the one surface built for timelessness — the always-on desk clock — renders the remainder as 96sp Anonymous Pro numerals over a progress bar draining toward incorporation (AirlockAndDisarmOverlays.kt L70-190; receipt.html frame 4). Every liminal surface answers 'how long until this is over' and none answers 'where are you now'.

Recommendation: De-clock the liminal home: the running Deck hero should show elapsed time counting up (time inhabited) or the intention alone — never a remainder; the desk clock should show wall time only, with no session progress bar, so the nightstand reads as a clock, not a sentence being served. Keep the remainder exactly one place — inside the Airlock, where the user is actively negotiating to leave — so countdown becomes the price of exit, not the texture of staying.

#### [HIGH] No time inside Monolith may pass unrecorded: even the 'Open Flow' mode carries a 20-minute minimum floor and exits through a seal, a receipt and a forged reward

The freest mode in the app is still a contract: MonolithModels.kt:68 STOPWATCH_FLOW is labelled 'Open Flow' but badged '20m Min Floor', enforced by MonolithRepository.kt:109 STOPWATCH_MIN_FLOOR_SECONDS = 20*60. Every completed non-routine session, FLOW included, is classified, receipted (ReceiptSheet.kt prints ARMED / ENDED / outcome for every branch, with a dedicated FLOW variant noted at ReceiptSheet.kt:113-121) and paid: MonolithRepository.kt:2049-2051 forges a random curio on all-blocks-completed. There is no surface in the app where a user can simply sit with their attention for an unmeasured while and leave no trace — contemplation in Pieper's sense (receptive, effortless, leaving no artifact) is architecturally impossible because the data model only has timed, sealed, judged sessions. Idleness and leisure are opposites for Pieper; Monolith can only express the timed kind.

Recommendation: Add an unrecorded SIT mode, reachable from the Deck as a plain text verb 'SIT — NOTHING KEPT' beside the wheel: it opens a blank, timerless screen (no numerals, no progress, no intention field), keeps the phone unlocked and unguarded, and on exit writes nothing — no session row, no receipt, no Drawer entry, no curio, no effect on any total or streak. Its settings copy must state the law in one line: 'SIT sessions are never counted, because they are not sessions.' This is the one mode whose success condition is that the database cannot prove it happened.

#### [HIGH] Time-transformation is designed out: every in-session surface is a countdown, so the app forces the clock-watching self-monitoring that flow requires to dissolve

Every live surface is a clock and nothing else: the Deck hero is a 72sp MM:SS (TactileDeckScreen.kt:312-322, 660-690) with a % beside its bar, the strip adds ENDS HH:mm, the shield notification's subtitle updates the countdown and 'urges stopped' (MonolithShieldService.kt:144), and the desk clock is a 96sp session countdown (AirlockAndDisarmOverlays.kt:70-179) whose only other element is another progress bar. There is no setting, gesture or running form that hides time. One of flow's defining marks is transformed time — hours feeling like minutes because self-monitoring has dissolved; Monolith designs the opposite state, continuous clock-surveillance, in which checking 'how long is left' is itself the attentional fragment the app exists to prevent. Even the mode named FLOW (STOPWATCH_FLOW, MonolithModels.kt:68) leads with an ever-growing elapsed readout.

Recommendation: Add a TIME BLIND running form to the Deck: a long-press on the hero (or a PARK sled) collapses the running Deck to task title, NEXT sub-step and the HELD chip — no numerals, no bar, no ENDS line — with time returning only at block boundaries, on a deliberate tap of the blank hero, or in the last 60 seconds of a block. The desk clock gets the same treatment as its default: task name and a slow-breathing progress wash instead of 96sp digits, digits on tap. Market it in the surface's own voice: the strip's TIME cell prints 'UNCOUNTED' while blind, a state the receipt honours rather than faults.

#### [HIGH] Gradients fail: every mercy is a cliff — 120 seconds of peek, then a flat 20-minute wall, at any point in the session

Access is stepped, never graded. MonolithRepository.kt:106-108 fixes the whole economy in three constants: PEEK_DURATION_SECONDS = 120, PEEK_DURATION_MILLIS = 120*1000L, PEEK_COOLDOWN_MILLIS = 20*60*1000L — a locked app is fully shut, then fully open for exactly 120 seconds, then fully shut again under a flat 20-minute cooldown, whether the session has 90 minutes or 90 seconds left. The same cliff shape repeats at every scale: app tiers are the discrete SHUT / PEEK / OPEN, the emergency break is one token per week (spent or unspent), and the session end in the airlock.html render is a single line 'SESSION ENDS 18:30' with no softening as that moment approaches. The one true gradient in the product — the valve banking every 15 seconds — proves the team can build one; it was built only for exit, never for approach.

Recommendation: Introduce gradients where the cliffs are: on the Airlock, scale the peek offer to distance from session end (e.g. in the final 10 minutes the peek lengthens and the cooldown copy shortens, printed as 'TAKING THE PEEK STARTS A 5 MINUTES COOLDOWN'); on the Deck's sealed state, fade the proof strip's density as ENDS approaches so the session visibly thins toward release instead of ending at full strength; and make the Shield tier control a three-stop gradient with a genuine middle weight rather than three equal discrete stops.

#### [HIGH] Routines are a starlight counterfeit: they automate the spotlight on a schedule and grade obedience (ATTENDED/MISSED), never whether the aim they serve is still alive

RoutineDerive.kt:33 and MonolithModels.kt:550-569: a routine is judged ATTENDED / PARTIAL / MISSED from elapsed time and an evidenceMask, and RoutineEntity has no aim link, no start/end date and no review state. A user can be ATTENDED every weekday for a year while the aim the routine was built for died months ago, and Monolith will keep certifying obedience and marking absences MISSED. That is a spotlight machine wearing starlight's clothes: automation of the immediate task, presented as fidelity to a life direction.

Recommendation: Give every routine a mandatory Aim link and a review cadence: every 4 weeks the Deck presents a starlight review card for each routine — sessions attended, aim progress in the user's words, and three verbs: KEEP, CHANGE, RETIRE — with RETIRE rendered at equal weight, not as failure. An unreviewed routine pauses instead of silently rolling into a new month, and its Drawer verdict changes from MISSED to UNREVIEWED until the user re-endorses it.

#### [HIGH] Completion pays out a lottery curio: a variable-ratio collectible reward the user never asked to play for

MonolithRepository.kt:2049-2051: on allBlocksCompleted a non-routine session forges a collectible — CurioCatalog.artifacts.shuffled().first().id — a random KineticArtifact drawn by lot. MonolithModels.kt:799-840 CurioCatalog lists the toys (Harmonic Loop, Brass Gyroscope, String Prism…) that fill the Drawer cabinet. A variable-ratio lottery is the exact reinforcement schedule of the slot machine, bolted onto the moment of completion: the user endorsed two hours of study, not a draw. Extrinsic collectibles crowd out the intrinsic worth of the attended work and give the next session an acquisitive motive the user never chose.

Recommendation: Remove the lottery forge from the completion path in MonolithRepository. Convert the cabinet from winnings into dedication: at arm time, the Deck offers 'DEDICATE THIS SESSION' — the user may attach one chosen curio (or none) to the intention, and that chosen object, not a random one, is printed on the receipt slip. The collection stops growing by chance and becomes a shelf of self-chosen meanings; sessions completed without a dedication mint nothing.

#### [MEDIUM] Fake machined-metal shading on every row is pure style — it encodes nothing and will date the whole system

BlockitSuitcaseAndSwitchesViews.kt:126-147 and :370-389 spend canvas work on 'recess shading', 'contact shadow under the moving sled' and a 'lit top edge' — a simulated machined-metal object — repeated for every one of dozens of app rows in shield.html (rocker ::before/::after inner shadows). This is style in Vignelli's exact sense: a fashionable material fiction applied uniformly regardless of content, which will date the app to its skeuomorphic moment while encoding zero information — SHUT, PEEK and OPEN get identical shadows. 'Good design is a language, not a style' and the fight is against ugliness understood as gratuitous visual noise; a flat diagram needs no pooled shadows to be believed.

Recommendation: Delete the depth pass entirely: remove recess shading, contact shadows and lit top edges from AppRowSledToggleView and the sled switch, and render track and thumb as flat fills separated by the existing 1dp hairline. Spend the freed canvas budget on the one graphic distinction that carries meaning — the tier glyph in the left margin — drawn at a fixed 10dp module on the same grid as the slip's dot leaders.

---

## Design wins — protect these — 72 findings

### Visual identity and brand — 5 wins

#### [WIN] Shield's dot-leader rules slip is real print craft Opal's generic list rows never attempt

ui/screens/ShieldMatrixScreen.kt:960-968 (SlipLineRow: 'One line of the book: the app's name, a dot leader, its ruling word. The leader is the ledger's mechanism for binding an entry'), rendered in shield.html's YOUR RULES section: INSTAGRAM · · · · PEEK, CHROME · · · · SHUT — a printed-ledger slip with a tally header (4 SHUT · 3 PEEK · 3 OPEN). Opal presents the equivalent rule list as standard rounded iOS rows with switches; nothing in its brand kit or screenshots attempts a print artifact. Monolith's slip is a genuine, ownable piece of print craft — the one surface where its paper-and-ledger identity is executed better than the category leader's generic list.

Recommendation: Protect the dot-leader slip in any redesign: keep the leader, the tally header and the ruling-word column exactly as the Shield's rules summary, and extend the same ledger grammar to the Drawer history rows rather than letting a future cleanup 'modernise' it into generic cards.

#### [WIN] Protect the seal chain: ARM → BIND → SEALED → IMPRINT → numbered RECEIPT is the one place the vocabulary is a system, and no rival has it

Across the Deck and Receipt the session lifecycle speaks a single, internally consistent language of binding and proof: the proof strip prints 'BIND HELD · THIS VISIT' / 'PROOF: LIVE BIND' (ui/components/MonolithCustomComponents.kt:383), finished spans are suffixed ' · AS SEALED' (MonolithCustomComponents.kt:447,461), the Deck reserves an ImprintSlot (MonolithCustomComponents.kt:782), and the session ends as a numbered paper artifact — '№ 048', 'THE MACHINE KEEPS ITS OWN LOG' (render receipt.html; ui/components/ReceiptSheet.kt). Every term predicts the next: you arm, the bind holds, the seal sets, the imprint lands, the receipt prints. Neither Forest's tree (which dies but certifies nothing) nor Opal's gem score gives a finished session the feeling of an executed document; this chain does, and it is the strongest identity asset in the app.

Recommendation: Freeze this chain as the constitutional vocabulary and judge every future noun against it: a new term is admitted only if it belongs to the bind/seal/print family or names a literal part of the ML-01 machine. In any redesign, the receipt's numbering, the 'AS SEALED' suffix and the imprint moment are non-negotiable keepers — extend them (let shared proof be the receipt itself, shown as the sealed slip) rather than inventing parallel reward language elsewhere in the app.

#### [WIN] Palette-as-state — arming a session inverts the whole colour world, a grammar no rival owns and the seed of the 2030 identity

ui/theme/Theme.kt:110-114 selects SealedVaultNightColorScheme when 'darkTheme || isFocusSessionActive' — the entire palette inverts (Color.kt night set: ground #171412, ink flipped to cream #FFE4CF, accent warmed to #F47442) because a session started, not because the user picked a theme. receipt.html frames 1 vs 3 show the same Deck in warm stone by day and sealed-vault night under session, so colour carries a state no words need to explain: you can read commitment from across the room. Rival focus apps and Nothing OS both treat dark mode as a user preference setting; none makes palette itself the lock engaging. This is the one Monolith decision already operating at TE's level, where orange-always-means-recording turns colour into grammar.

Recommendation: Protect and codify this as the identity's first law in the in-repo DESIGN.md: palette = state, never preference — remove any future settings toggle for theme, and extend the flip to the two surfaces that currently lag it (launcher icon badge and the ongoing notification's accent) so every Monolith surface in the OS tells the same armed/unarmed truth. In any redesign, this inversion is non-negotiable heritage, ahead of the wheel itself.

#### [WIN] The orange slide cap is a genuine brand asset — one colour, reserved for one action, that the user physically performs

ui/theme/Color.kt:18 declares "THE single accent — hot orange, spent rarely" (#F55314), and its one physical embodiment is the slide cap: deck.html shows an 84x56 orange block on an ink track that the user must drag to commit a session. ParkDrawer.kt:113 codifies the rule in words: "ORANGE = COMMIT". Nothing's red dot, by contrast, is a passive signifier — printed, never operated. Monolith's orange is a verb you perform with a thumb, which makes the cap a more ownable brand object than a logo: the brand is an action, not a decoration.

Recommendation: Protect this in any redesign: never let #F55314 appear on anything that is not a commitment (no badges, no highlights, no marketing surfaces), and make the redrawn launcher mark and desk-clock progress edge quote the orange cap/block shape so the one ownable asset becomes the identity system.

#### [WIN] The header nameplate is treated as print, not chrome: 48dp, invariant across theme, session state and seal — the one piece of identity discipline in the app

MonolithCustomComponents.kt:230-248 specifies the header band as 'a printed nameplate, not a console. 48dp, invariant in both modes and both session states; it never grows, never wraps, never changes height', and the implementation holds it: a 47dp row over a 1dp hairline (lines 259-310), the brand as pure print with its click deliberately dead, the session's facts banished to the Deck's own strip. deck.html's render confirms the band sits identical over the unarmed Deck. Most apps let branding flex, badge and animate with state; this one files the name like a plate riveted to a machine — Rand's identity-program instinct, present exactly once.

Recommendation: Protect it by extending it: keep the band's dimensions and print-only rule untouched, and when the drawn wordmark and slab glyph land, seat them in this band at its existing left margin — the plate is already the right home; do not let any future state (armed suffix, held pill, theme toggle) buy space in it.

### Typography — 1 wins

#### [WIN] True monospace telemetry keeps every count and clock aligned across Deck, Shield and Receipt

deck.html proof strip and shield.html tally set counts and times in Anonymous Pro Bold 15sp (APPS 12, ENDS 10:40; '4 SHUT · 3 PEEK · 3 OPEN'), and receipt.html Frame 1 sets ARMED/ENDED times in mono 11sp — because the face is truly monospace, columns of values align digit-for-digit across screens with no layout code. Material 3's default Roboto/proportional labelling would let 11:11 and 10:40 drift; Monolith's telemetry never does. Type.kt:40-46 documents Anonymous Pro explicitly as 'Telemetry & Numbers', and that discipline holds at small sizes throughout.

Recommendation: Protect this in any redesign: keep a genuine monospace (not a proportional face with tnum switched on) for all telemetry ≤15sp, and extend the same face to the Drawer history times so the whole record-keeping layer shares one aligned figure grid. Do not let a future 'modernisation' swap telemetry to Sora or Atkinson for style reasons.

### Colour — 4 wins

#### [WIN] The tower's colour discipline — one accent brick, ink for the rest, and a hard night-fill ceiling — is genuine display-object restraint

ui/views/BlockitTowerFadersAndCatalogViews.kt:116-140 — of the tower's three brick states, exactly one, the newest, may use the accent #F55314; laid bricks are solid ink and unlaid slots are surface-variant with a hairline. At night the laid fill is deliberately capped at #A79587 (the 38% cream blend ceiling, comment :122-127) so a tall tower never becomes a wall of light, with the single crown brick filed as the standing exception. Gamified streak art normally pays out in rainbow rarity tiers and full-saturation fills; LEGO Architecture's adult display models hold the same discipline — muted, office-desk-safe palettes where colour is spent on one landmark at a time. This rationing is why the tower, alone among the app's reward surfaces, would survive being printed on paper unchanged.

Recommendation: Protect this in any tower redesign: keep the three-state fill system and the one-accent rule as fixed constraints — silhouette and brick-width variation (the missing profile) must be achieved with geometry and ink, never by adding per-brick colours, rarity tints or a fourth fill state. Write the night cap (#A79587 ceiling, crown excepted) into the design tokens as a named rule so a future theme pass cannot quietly repeal it.

#### [WIN] The fixed zero-green palette makes Monolith recognisable on any phone — the one Material You refusal worth protecting in any redesign

Color.kt:1-19 fixes a 19-token, strictly zero-green palette (warm stone #E4DFDA ground, single hot-orange accent #F55314 spent rarely) with a fully specified night inversion (cream ink #FFE4CF on #171412), and the renders confirm the result: deck.html and shield.html are built entirely from those hexes, so a screenshot of the Deck is identical on a Pixel, a Samsung and a Xiaomi. Material You's dynamic colour deliberately dissolves app identity into each user's wallpaper — Google's own apps are unrecognisable from one phone to the next — while Nothing and Teenage Engineering both hold fixed palettes precisely so the object reads as itself everywhere. Monolith's fixed ink-and-accent core achieves that object-identity by accident of refusal, but it is real and it is the brand.

Recommendation: Protect the core while fixing the silence around it: in any dynamic-colour adoption (including the FOLLOW PHONE sled proposed for PARK), lock primary ink, on-primary and the #F55314/#F47442 accent slots to the fixed tokens and let only background/surface neutrals breathe with the wallpaper. Write that rule into Theme.kt where the scheme is assembled — 'neutrals may follow the phone; ink and accent never do' — so a future contributor cannot trade the recognisability away for stock dynamicColor = true.

#### [WIN] Night text is voiced in cream tiers, not shouted in white — a calmer dark hierarchy than Nothing OS's stark white-on-black

Color.kt:37 flips the night primary to cream #FFE4CF instead of white, and Color.kt:49 deliberately steps night body text #D2C6BB down to a measured 11:1 tier with the comment that the previous ~16.8:1 'everything shouted'; night glyph tone #EDE3D8 (:46) sits at 14.5:1 for the elements that must shout. That is a three-tier luminance voicing — whisper/body/shout — executed in warm off-whites. Nothing OS, the obvious reference, puts stark white on pure black at maximum contrast everywhere, which on OLED causes halation for astigmatic users and makes a long lockdown screen glare; Monolith's cream tiers are measurably calmer while every tier still clears WCAG AA by a wide margin (secondary #9C8E84 = 5.78:1).

Recommendation: Protect this in any redesign: keep the cream-not-white primary and the stepped 5.8 / 11 / 14.5:1 night text tiers as fixed, tested token values, and document them as the night voicing spec so a future 'increase contrast' pass does not flatten them back to maximum white. If the ground moves to true black per the OLED fix, re-measure and re-tune the creams against #000000 rather than swapping them for #FFFFFF.

#### [WIN] One saturated colour in the whole product, spent only where the hand commits: the single-accent discipline holds

ui/theme/Color.kt:10 documents the light scheme as 19 tokens of warm neutrals with a 'Single Accent #F55314', and :18 names it 'THE single accent — hot orange, spent rarely'. The renders confirm the discipline holds on screen: across deck.html, shield.html, park.html and airlock.html every surface is stone, ink or cream, and the one saturated colour appears only where the hand commits or the record crowns — the slide-to-arm cap (deck), the valve fill and RETURN TO FOCUS chip (airlock), the sled's armed pip (ui/views/BlockitSuitcaseAndSwitchesViews.kt:153) and the newest tower brick (ui/views/BlockitTowerFadersAndCatalogViews.kt:117). This is Rams' third and tenth principles genuinely met — aesthetic restraint in service of use, colour as information about where action lives, in the Braun manner of a single red operative point — and it survives in an app that elsewhere invents without limit.

Recommendation: Protect this as a hard rule in the token file: keep exactly one saturated token, and add a lint-style test that fails any new Color literal outside the neutral ramp and #F55314/#F47442 pair. When new surfaces are drawn, spend the accent only on the element that commits, spends or seals — never on headers, badges or decoration — so the colour keeps meaning 'your hand changes something here'.

### Layout and spacing — 2 wins

#### [WIN] One raised mass in an empty field: the ground is flat by default and exactly one card is allowed to rise

Color.kt:10-14 encodes a discipline most products never attempt: background, default surface and sheet are all the same #E4DFDA ('flat by default'), and there is exactly one raised tone, #FAF6F0, reserved in the token's own words for 'The ONE raised card (timer card, nav capsule)'. The Deck render honours it (design-renders/deck.html): a single pale mass holding wheel and hero numeral, everything else — task row, proof strip, rail — flush with the ground or recessed below it (#D8D1CB). This is Ando's field condition: one wall in emptiness, its singularity doing the compositional work a dozen elevated cards do elsewhere.

Recommendation: Protect this as law and extend it by one clause: audit every future surface against a 'one rise per screen' budget — Shield, Drawer and PARK currently spend the raised tone only on thumbs and caps (moving parts), which is compliant; any proposal adding a second raised card must name which existing rise it demolishes. Keep surface == background in both schemes permanently; the moment the ground itself gets a second level, the monolith becomes a dashboard.

#### [WIN] RailGeometry is a grid in embryo: one named object, every dimension derived by formula and unit-testable

MonolithRailView.kt:16-46 concentrates the entire chrome band in object RailGeometry: HEIGHT_DP 52f, MARGIN_DP 20f, INSET_DP 4f, CAP_HEIGHT_DP 44f (:26-31), with recessWidthDp, segmentDp, capWidthDp, capLeftDp, stopForX and nearestStop as pure functions of screen width (:36-65) rather than literals scattered through draw code. Its header comment states the reference width and shows its working. Almost no product UI does this — geometry is normally buried as magic numbers per view — and it is exactly the Müller-Brockmann instinct: the order of a surface stated once, as arithmetic, where it can be argued with and tested.

Recommendation: Protect this pattern and promote it to the whole app: extract the screens' geometry into a sibling MonolithGrid object with the same discipline (named constants, pure span functions, reference-width arithmetic in the header comment), and require new screens to consume spans from it rather than declaring padding and heights locally. The rail's numbers themselves should change (see the fractional-module finding) — its method should become the law.

### Iconography and illustration — 3 wins

#### [WIN] The legacy power-ring mark has real silhouette discipline - flat, two-colour, readable at 48px

The legacy PNG mark (mipmap-xxxhdpi/ic_launcher.png and its densities) is genuinely shelf-strong: pixel analysis shows essentially two dominant colours - a near-black field (13,14,18) and one orange-red (#FF4F18) - plus the cream frame, so at 48x48 mdpi it still resolves as a single glyph where multi-part marks dissolve. Its cream octagonal frame is an ownable container shape none of the focus rivals use, and its ink/paper/orange palette is the only launcher palette that matches the product inside (deck.html: #252323 ink, #FAF6F0 paper, #F55314 orange). It out-disciplines Opal's launcher mark, a photographic 3D gem (Opal brand kit: gems are rendered sculptures, 'always on pure black') that collapses toward a shiny blob at home-screen size, while the flat ring survives the shrink intact.

Recommendation: Protect this mark in any redesign: keep the dark field, the octagonal cream frame and the single flat orange ring untouched, and promote exactly this composition to be the adaptive icon and every density - do not let a redesign 'modernise' it into a gradient, a multi-part diagram or a lighter tile.

#### [WIN] The rocker stops spell SHUT / PEEK / OPEN instead of using lock-and-eye glyphs

BlockitSuitcaseAndSwitchesViews.kt:406-409: 'The stops print WORDS (Ren's ruling, Oct 29 — one word for one fact): SHUT / PEEK / OPEN' with stops = arrayOf(SHUT, PEEK, OPEN) drawn on every rocker cap; shield.html shows the same on the LOADOUT selector (STUDY/WORK/SLEEP spelled on the cap). Rival blockers conventionally mark these states with lock / eye / unlock glyphs — an eye that can mean viewable, watched, or time-limited, and a padlock that cannot distinguish hard-blocked from peekable.

Recommendation: Protect this in any redesign: on controls where the three states are verbs with different consequences, the spelled word on the moving cap is clearer than any pictogram, self-teaching (the lexicon SHUT/PEEK/OPEN is learned by using the control, not from a legend), and immune to icon-font ambiguity. Extend the principle rather than diluting it — add symbols only where they carry recognition or state at a glance (app identity, tier margin, navigation anchors, guard health), and never let a glyph replace a consequential verb on a control cap.

#### [WIN] The emergency valve already speaks Aicher: banked time is solid, in-hand time is translucent, and the seam is the grammar

Emergency60sValveView.onDraw (BlockitSuitcaseAndSwitchesViews.kt:654-672): the in-hand chamber is drawn at alpha 180 ('The chamber still in the hand: translucent', line 654), the banked chamber at alpha 255 ('What is banked is solid — it does not drain', line 659), with 1.5dp seams appearing at each crossed 15-second bank line (lines 666-672). design-renders/airlock.html frame 3 confirms the effect reads on screen: solid orange up to the bank seam, translucent beyond it. The distinction the user most needs mid-hold — what is safe versus what a slip will cost — is carried entirely by the fill, before a single word is read.

Recommendation: Protect this exactly as built and make it the seed grammar of the wider sign system: in every future sign and progress surface, solid fill = banked/permanent fact, translucent fill = provisional/at-risk state, a seam = the moment one becomes the other. Apply it first to the peek countdown (solid arc for elapsed wait, translucent for remaining) and forbid any new surface from inventing a second encoding for permanence.

### Motion and animation — 1 wins

#### [WIN] The wheel gets heavier as the commitment grows: load-scaled inertia and coast are motion design as meaning, and worth protecting

The duration wheel's physics are weighted by the session the user is building: loadInertia() = 1 + 0.14 per study block beyond the first, coastTau() rises from 0.34s with the square root of that load (BlockitCoreViews.kt:535-539), and the well spring scales stiffness and damping per unit mass so zeta holds 0.38 at every load (BlockitCoreViews.kt:1222-1229). The slide's seat spring is equally considered: omega0=20, zeta=0.40, substepped, with the latch knock fired in-step at 0.97 travel before the latch lands (BlockitCoreViews.kt:1420-1427). No canned slide-to-confirm or time-picker wheel in the reference set does this: a standard slide control (and the Playdate-crank-style direct manipulation it imitates) has one fixed feel regardless of what the gesture commits you to. Here, choosing 8 blocks over 1 makes the wheel measurably heavier to fling and slower to coast — the commitment's weight is felt in the hand before it is read on screen. deck.html's static wheel gives no hint of this; it is the one piece of motion design in the app that could not be captured in a screenshot, and it is genuinely Monolith's own.

Recommendation: Protect this in any redesign: keep loadInertia/coastTau and the per-mass spring scaling exactly as tuned, and resist any refactor that replaces the wheel or slide integrators with Compose tweens or off-the-shelf pickers for convenience. If the Compose surfaces are ever rebuilt, port the physics, don't approximate it — and use this as the template for the speed law the rest of the app lacks: motion parameters derived from the meaning of the gesture, stated as constants with names.

### Sound design — 5 wins

#### [WIN] The seat knock is played like an instrument, not triggered like a sample: pitch, length and force all track the physical mass being seated

playSeatKnock (TactileSoundEngine.kt:665) takes duration, amplitude and pitch as continuous parameters of one voice - 16 ms at 0.85 gain unloaded rising to 24 ms at 1.0 with pitch dropping as blocks are added - and MonolithViewModel.kt drives it expressively: 24 ms/1.0f/320 Hz for a full seat (line 1248), 12 ms/0.5f for a light one (line 1260), 6 ms/0.2f for a glancing contact (line 1411), with the haptic amplitude derived from the same 0-1 value (TactileSoundEngine.kt:666-672). Stock Android and iOS control sounds are one fixed sample at one fixed loudness regardless of what the control is carrying; here the ear can judge how loaded the wheel is without looking.

Recommendation: Protect this mapping in any sound redesign and extend it into the stated grammar of the whole engine: every voice should expose one continuous physical parameter (mass, tension, distance) driven by the state it reports, the way the knock already does, rather than collapsing back to discrete named effects with fixed constants.

#### [WIN] The completion voice is integrity-gated: a death-booked session gets an audibly empty E700 slot instead of borrowed celebration

MonolithViewModel.kt:1245 rules 'Death-booked: the E700 slot stands EMPTY', and ReceiptState.kt:111-117 (finishPulses) returns false for every non-clean finish kind — so a session whose shield died or was breached receives the knocks of a machine stopping but is pointedly denied the completion voice, while clean MANUAL_FINISH, FLOW_FINISH and ROUTINE_ATTENDED finishes earn it. The celebration is gated by the integrity of the session itself, in the score, before any visual verdict. Duolingo does the reverse: a failed-then-retried lesson still gets the full fanfare, and its streak freeze exists precisely to sell absolution after a lapse. Forest plants its tree and pays coins on completion regardless of how the session felt. Monolith's withheld pulse is a rarer and more honest piece of reward craft: silence as a verdict the user can hear.

Recommendation: Protect this in any redesign of the finish: whatever crescendo or print choreography is added at issuance must inherit the same gate — the celebratory layer (pulse, stamp, colour) fires only on finishes finishPulses already blesses, and death-booked finishes keep an audibly emptier score. Do not let a future 'delight pass' uniform-ise the celebration across outcomes.

#### [WIN] The seal Throw is pre-rendered at latch into its own AudioTrack, so the app's most important sound costs one play() call at the moment it must land

TactileSoundEngine.kt:301-312 and 343-375: the Throw - a fully procedural 44,100-sample render (SEAL_SAMPLES, line 95; renderSealBuffer at line 356) - is rendered and written whole into its own dedicated, pre-stopped AudioTrack at prime time, at the latch, inside the latch-to-t=0 window that has nothing else to do. At t=0 the entire audio cost is one play() call, and preemption is designed in three layers (queue purge, sequence-barrier drop, legacy-track pause+flush under a lane epoch). Rival focus apps trigger sound files through media players at the event itself, paying decode and player latency at the exact frame that must feel instantaneous; Monolith pays everything early, in dead time, on a lane nothing else may enter.

Recommendation: Protect this architecture in any redesign: the prime-at-latch render, the dedicated seal track sized 5% over the render (TactileSoundEngine.kt:404-406), and the rule that the Throw never enters the serial command queue should be treated as load-bearing design, not optimisation trivia. If the visual shot is ever reworked, extend the same contract to it - pre-stage the seal shot's expensive layers at latch, not at t=0.

#### [WIN] The Seal Throw is a composed foley event, not a click: body, bolt and room in sequence, with a haptic twin that breathes — protect it exactly as built

renderSealBuffer (TactileSoundEngine.kt:208-260) builds the one-second seal from three narratively ordered layers: the 360 Hz pitched body at sample 0, a filtered-noise bolt entering at exactly +30 ms (BOLT_START_SAMPLE = 1323, line 104) and decaying over 55 ms, then a two-comb-plus-allpass room whose tail is still audible to ~900 ms before a linear fade to exact silence (lines 231-260). Its haptic twin deliberately zeroes the middle segment — timings {0, 24, 38, 16} with amplitudes {0, 255, 0, 175} (line 143) — so the hand feels strike, gap, seat: cause, travel, consequence. The render is pinned by a golden SHA-256 (line 151) so it cannot drift in a refactor. Against the field this is genuinely ahead: iOS's lock sound is a single flat sample with no room and no sequence, Android's stock lock feedback is a generic click, and no rival focus app ships a designed signature sound at all. The Park spec plate even prints the engine as a product credential — 'SOUND: FLOAT-PCM, 4 PARTIALS' (design-renders/park.html:174).

Recommendation: Protect the Throw as the brand's sonic logo in any redesign: keep the 30 ms bolt delay, the room tail and the haptic gap as untouchable constants alongside the golden hash, and build all future voices (including the refusal voice and any completion redesign) as relatives of its material — same noise generator, same room — rather than new recipes, so the kit grows from the one sound that already sounds like the product.

#### [WIN] The muted seal is a composed score, not an absence — muting loses timbre, never the event

TactileSoundEngine.kt:765 documents the law 'With sound off: haptic only (S0 — muting loses timbre, never the event)', and playSealThrow (:769) still fires SEAL_THROW_TIMINGS/AMPLITUDES (:143-144) — a separately composed haptic score whose middle segment is zeroed (110 -> 0) versus the audible seal's, so the muted seal breathes through a true gap the sounding one does not have. The mute path is authored, not merely the sound path with the volume removed, as it is in Forest and Opal where muting simply deletes the event.

Recommendation: Protect this in any redesign: keep a named, separately-scored haptic twin for every voice (not just the seal), specified alongside the PCM recipe in the same constants block, so 'sound off' remains a complete rendering of the interface rather than a degraded one.

### Haptics and feel — 3 wins

#### [WIN] The FLOW strait's 9 degrees of withheld sound is a negative-space earcon no rival ships — silence used as a detent

Crossing into FLOW under the finger is '9 degrees of haptic silence, and the landing speaks on the far shore': the strait crossing deliberately fires nothing, then FLOW takes a weighted gate knock (14ms @ 0.8, 300Hz) while the 10-minute shore takes the ordinary detent (ui/views/BlockitCoreViews.kt:1154-1170). In free motion the knock is withheld again — 'a coast that falls back from the gate has landed nowhere' (same passage). Playdate's crank and the OP-1's encoders click continuously and uniformly; neither uses withheld sound to mark a threshold. Monolith already owns the rarer device: silence as a detent.

Recommendation: Protect this in any sound redesign: keep the strait crossing silent and the gate knock exclusive to a true FLOW landing under contact. Extend the same negative-space grammar once — the emergency valve's final 5 seconds should drop its ticks rather than add a warning sound — and document the rule in the engine header so a future 'add feedback everywhere' pass cannot fill the silence in.

#### [WIN] The wheel's detent feel is genuinely toy-grade: a rising pitch ladder, a two-overshoot spring, and a knock spent only on real arrivals

RotaryWheelView's feel is composed, not defaulted: detent pitch climbs a continuous ladder with value, freq = 340f + ((newValue - 5) / 175f) * 540f (BlockitCoreViews.kt:1172), so spinning up the scale literally plays up a scale; the seat spring is tuned per load so 'zeta holds 0.38 (exactly two overshoots) and the seat lands inside 520ms at every count' (BlockitCoreViews.kt:1223-1224); and the seat knock is spent only on a real arrival — 'if (travelled >= 2f) fireSeatKnockForCount()' (BlockitCoreViews.kt:1244) — so a release already seated in its well is correctly not an event. One mechanical input, continuous pitch feedback, a spring with a chosen number of overshoots, and silence where nothing happened: that is the crank discipline, executed in full, in exactly one control.

Recommendation: Protect this verbatim: pin the pitch-ladder formula, the zeta-0.38 two-overshoot spring and the travelled>=2° knock gate with golden tests at the same rank as the seal-throw hash, and forbid any future wheel work (granularity, presets, tappable fallback) from flattening them. When other controls are rebuilt, copy these three numbers as the house feel standard rather than inventing new ones.

#### [WIN] The Throw itself is genuinely Balmuda-grade — one bit-identical 1000ms voice, zero parameters, the same seal on every device forever

TactileSoundEngine.kt:86-157: SEAL_SAMPLES=44_100 (exactly 1000ms), bolt entering at sample 1323 (+30ms) for 2426 samples through a 900Hz one-pole (alpha 0.1203), room combs at COMB_G=0.836 fading -46dB at 900ms, all as decimal literals with 'ZERO transcendental calls' so the grain is 'bit-exact on every device', pinned by SEAL_BUFFER_GOLDEN_SHA256 (d204b95a...). TactileSoundEngine.kt:756-767: 'THE THROW (B-5): the one seal voice, zero parameters — no provenance, no duration, no clock can enter it, so two seals cannot differ', fired only as executeSeal's last statement (SessionSealTransition.kt:142), primed in advance so it never queues or degrades silently.

Recommendation: Protect it as the product's 5cc: freeze the constants under the golden-hash test permanently, never parameterise the Throw for routine vs manual seals, and build the missing release counterpart from the same recipe (bolt reversed, tail first) rather than inventing a new finish sound — the pair, Throw and Release, becomes the only named sounds in the app.

### Interaction and gestures — 3 wins

#### [WIN] The slide's geared resistance and velocity-seeded seat out-engineer Slide to Unlock — past the gate the cap fights back, and a thrown seal lands faster than a pushed one

BlockitCoreViews.kt:1309-1356 (SlideGestureMath): drag is free 1:1 only to the 0.68 gate, then geared at 2/3 gain so the finger must travel to 0.92 to display the 0.84 catch — resistance you feel in the wrist before commitment. The gate is a Schmitt latch (0.680 arm / 0.660 release) with pitched detents both ways (:1990-2010), and crossing the catch hands the cap to the seat integrator seeded with the crossing MOVE's measured velocity, floored at 0 and capped at +6.0 frac/s (:2030-2050), so a thrown seal lands faster than a pushed one. iOS's original Slide to Unlock was linear 1:1 to the end with a canned unlock animation; Android's stock slide-to-confirm components are linear with a tween back. Monolith's geared, velocity-seeded commit is the more considered mechanism of the three.

Recommendation: Protect this in any redesign: keep the 2/3 post-gate gearing, the Schmitt dead-band and the velocity-seeded seat exactly as tuned. If the slide is ever rebuilt in Compose, port the integrator and gear function numerically rather than re-expressing them as animate*AsState tweens, which would silently delete the resistance and the throw-feel that make the seal feel earned.

#### [WIN] One bounded 324-degree turn maps the whole commitment - position itself reads as proportion, which endless encoders and drum pickers cannot do

BlockitCoreViews.kt:500-503 files the whole range as one unwrapped turn: FLOW at 108, numeric stops 10..180 at 9 degrees per 5 minutes from 126 to 432, total travel 324 degrees; the sweep arc is drawn proportionally from wheelAngleDeg (sweepNormalized, ~730-740 in onDraw) and ticks exist only where the wheel can stop (748). deck.html shows the payoff: at the 50-minute detent the reader's position and the filled arc make 'about a third of the maximum' pre-attentively obvious before any numeral is read.

Recommendation: Protect this in any redesign: do not replace the wheel with an iOS-style drum picker or an endless TE-style encoder for duration, both of which give a value no spatial home and force the user to read digits to know whether they chose a little or a lot. A finite, serious commitment deserves a finite dial with visible ends. Keep the single-turn absolute scale and the proportional sweep even if the drag model becomes relative - decouple the input mechanics from this display, which is the part that is right.

#### [WIN] PARK's grip is a genuine without-thought fit: press, pull and throw all behave as the hand already expects

ParkDrawer.kt:241-291: the grab strip is 32dp visual on a 48dp touch area, the grip visibly grows 24dp to 28dp on DOWN (gripPressed), onVerticalDrag moves the sheet by exactly dragAmount/sheetHeightPx clamped 0..1 — the sheet is under the finger, not animated toward it — and release past the dismissal fraction throws it shut. No instruction text is printed anywhere on the sheet; none is needed.

Recommendation: Protect this exactly as built: keep the grip's press-growth, the 1:1 fraction mapping and the threshold throw unchanged, and use this grip — not the rail's blank PARK zone — as the template when the Drawer archive is given its pull-to-open grammar. Do not add a 'drag to close' hint label; the handle already teaches it.

### Information architecture — 3 wins

#### [WIN] The day is filed from the user's 03:30 waking, not calendar midnight — the one day-boundary drawn around a life instead of a clock

DrawerDay.kt:8-31: 'his day starts at 03:30 (he wakes at 03:30), not at midnight… a task finished at 00:02 files under the next day AND the next month, and a phantom month appears' without the rule; filingDate subtracts the 210-minute offset and every Drawer derivation — DAO months index, repository month bounds, screen grouping — goes through it (DrawerDay.kt:22-31, monthBoundsMillis anchored at 03:30 local). Calendar-day ledgers such as Android Digital Wellbeing's and Apple Screen Time's daily views cut the day at midnight, so the 00:30 session belongs to a day the user never experienced as separate. Monolith's 03:30 boundary files the small hours with the evening that produced them — the day is drawn around the user's sleep, not the clock's zero.

Recommendation: Protect this in any redesign: keep 03:30 as the single filing boundary for every day-scale surface (including the proposed morning masthead and day slip, which should both key off filingDate), and never let a new surface quietly revert to calendar-midnight grouping — the internal stats code that still buckets by midnight (MonolithRepository.kt day windows) should be migrated to DrawerDay, not the other way round.

#### [WIN] A hard four-destination ceiling with zero overflow — no hamburger, no 'More', no hidden fifth place

MainActivity.kt MonolithRootApp: the entire app is one when(destination) over exactly four MonolithDestination values, switched from MonolithRailView's single 52dp band (MonolithRailView.kt:33 WORDS) — no hamburger, no overflow menu, no second tab bar, no FAB hiding a fifth place. Every top-level job is one tap from every screen, including mid-scroll, because the rail is Scaffold chrome, not screen content.

Recommendation: Protect this in any redesign: cap the destination count at four and resist the standard growth path (a fifth 'More' stop, a settings cog exiled to a corner, feature tabs inside tabs). If new top-level jobs arrive, they must displace or absorb an existing stop — the way Teenage Engineering's OP-1 keeps four modes and deepens within them — rather than widen the rail. The one sanctioned exception already exists and should stay the pattern: PARK's wordless zone for machine-state, not user destinations.

#### [WIN] The Social Sites channel strip — measured state and its own switch co-located on the one line they govern

ParkSocialSitesRow (ParkDrawer.kt:685-760, header comment 685-698): 'the SOCIAL SITES board line, carrying its own sled — the setting's switch, seated on the line it governs... Two facts share the line and neither impersonates the other: the WORD still prints the measured interceptor state, and the SLED prints and writes the setting itself.' park.html shows the result: one 48dp ruled line carrying name, live RUNNING word and its own sled together. This is exactly a mixing-console channel strip (name, meter/status and fader/mute co-located on one strip) — and it beats the standard Android pattern, used across Monolith's rival focus apps, where a blocking status is reported on one screen and its toggle lives in a separate settings list.

Recommendation: Protect this row as the panel's template and extend it: give SHORTS + REELS and NOTIFICATIONS the same channel-strip treatment (measured word + own sled on the governed line), and delete the duplicate standalone Shorts sled row below the board so each interceptor has exactly one strip. Do not let a redesign separate status from switch again for tidiness.

### Flows and friction — 1 wins

#### [WIN] The FIX key stays physically dipped for the entire Settings absence and only releases once the return has been proved

ParkDrawer.kt:181-184 and 425-447: the FIX key dips 1dp on finger-DOWN and the dip is deliberately held 'for the whole absence' — it does not spring back when the finger leaves or when Settings opens. It releases only after the return-proving effect (ParkDrawer.kt:192-212) waits out the host's re-sweep (800ms stability beat) and reads the store live. The control the user pressed is thus treated as a held commitment whose state is resolved by evidence on return, not by the press ending — a small, precise piece of interaction design that neither one sec's tap-and-go permission buttons nor Opal's auto-return service attempts: in both rivals the launching control resets instantly and remembers nothing about the trip.

Recommendation: Protect this in any redesign of the permission flow: whatever replaces the serial FIX key (departure cards, arrival stamps, a six-denominator count), keep the grammar that a control which sends the user away stays physically depressed until the app has proved what happened on the trip. It is the one moment where the expedition feels like a machine that knows you left — extend the same held-until-proved treatment to the arrival stamp rather than discarding the dip as a quirk.

### Microcopy and voice — 5 wins

#### [WIN] The peek offer prints its full price in plain words before the tap — a stated consequence on the temptation itself that one sec's decision screen never gives its 'Continue' option
