AirlockAndDisarmOverlays.kt:674-681 — directly under the EMERGENCY PEEK chip, before any tap, the overlay prints peekPriceText(PEEK_COOLDOWN_MILLIS): 'TAKING THE PEEK STARTS A 20 MINUTES COOLDOWN ON THIS APP' (airlock.html frame 2), and the withheld states at :690-714 likewise print their reason rather than silently omitting the chip. one sec's 'Continue to Instagram' carries no stated cost at the moment of choice — its awareness cue is a retrospective attempt count, not a price. Monolith's lapse is honestly labelled at the exact second it is being considered

Recommendation: Keep the price-on-the-offer rule inviolable in any redesign of this screen: every escape the Airlock offers must carry its full consequence in plain words, adjacent to the control, before the tap — including in the proposed first-person rewrite ('OPEN INSTAGRAM ANYWAY — 2 MIN, THEN 20 MIN LOCKED'). Do not let a cleaner two-beat layout relocate the price to a later confirmation step.

#### [WIN] The emergency valve banks partial progress in 15-second increments and says so in plain words — 'The banked part stays'

ui/components/AirlockAndDisarmOverlays.kt:796-801 — the disarm overlay's rule line reads 'Hold to fill 60 seconds. Every 15 seconds banks. If your hand slips, what isn't banked drains away. The banked part stays.', and its consequence line (lines 770-776) is equally plain: 'This ends the session early. It is the only break this week.' The user mid-quit is told exactly what they keep, in increments, before they commit. Forest's give-up is total by contrast: leave and the tree dies whole, nothing of the elapsed growth is banked or acknowledged in the moment. Monolith's valve treats even the act of quitting as partly honourable and prices it honestly — a humane microcopy decision worth protecting verbatim in any redesign of the failure surfaces.

Recommendation: Protect this copy and its banking mechanic unchanged; extend the same voice to the broken session's record — the receipt recommended above should print the banked figure ('BANKED 45 OF 60 SECONDS') in this same plain dialect, so the honesty of the valve moment survives into the artifact.

#### [WIN] Sleep is 'SLEPT THROUGH', never MISSED, and the faulted receipt prints no title at all — two refusals to shame worth locking in

MonolithRepository.kt:1686 maps FinishKind.ROUTINE_SLEEP_STANDDOWN to 'SLEPT THROUGH' instead of routing sleep routines through MISSED; ReceiptSheet.kt:40-52 documents and implements the rule that 'the faulted sheet carries NO title (F-W1 — ENDED-FAULT never prints anywhere)': the title composable at ReceiptSheet.kt:113-125 renders an empty Box when receipt.faulted is true. In a vocabulary otherwise built from stamps, these are two deliberate refusals to shame: sleeping is described, not failed, and a broken finish gets silence where a failure headline would go.

Recommendation: Protect both decisions verbatim in any redesign and extend the principle, don't dilute it: keep 'SLEPT THROUGH' as the model for a descriptive (not verdict) outcome lexicon — rewrite MISSED/PARTIAL in its image rather than the reverse — and keep the faulted slip title-less; if a future design adds a heading there, it must name the app's fault ('MONOLITH FAULT'), never the session's. Add both strings to a locked copy register so a later tone pass cannot 'clarify' them into FAILED / ENDED-FAULT.

#### [WIN] Each curio's lore gives the object an intrinsic mechanical identity, where Opal's gems are interchangeable labels for grind thresholds

Every lore line in CurioCatalog (MonolithModels.kt:810-850) is a precise one-sentence mechanical specification of a distinct object: 'Two waves of different pitch, drawn against each other until the line closes into a knot of light' (Harmonic Loop), 'Four brass rings nested one inside the next, each free on its own axis' (Brass Gyroscope), 'Nothing in it is curved. Straight threads under tension borrow the shape of a prism' (String Prism). The objects are worth wanting for what they are. Opal's catalogue, by contrast, names gems after the threshold that dispenses them — Driven Gem 'Focus for 10 hours', Devoted Gem 'Focus for 1,000 hours' — the gem's identity is the grind, and any gem shape could carry any label.

Recommendation: Protect this in any redesign: do not rename curios after achievements, durations or streaks, and do not let future lore drift into motivational copy. The Braun / Teenage Engineering tradition Monolith is closest to names objects by their construction, not by the effort that bought them. If visuals are ever built, derive each one strictly from its lore sentence — the lore is already a buildable spec — rather than commissioning generic gem-style artwork the text never described.

#### [WIN] The frozen digest's three-sentence honesty — 'Nothing here opens. Anything newer waits until the session ends.' — is the best explanatory copy in the app

AirlockAndDisarmOverlays.kt:377, frozen held-digest: 'Everything here is as of the time above. Nothing here opens. Anything newer waits until the session ends.' — three short declarative sentences that state the snapshot's age, its inertness and the fate of new arrivals, with zero jargon. Its empty state (:394) is equally plain: 'Nothing has been held.' design-renders/airlock.html / receipt.html confirm this is the rare place the sentence-case register survived into composition.

Recommendation: Protect this exact register as the template for all state-explaining copy: timestamp + what is true + what happens next, in plain sentences. It beats mainstream messaging apps' vague 'last seen' / disappearing-message notices, which never state as-of or consequence this cleanly. When the Airlock's dead coaching voice is restored (and in the emergency recourse line), write them in this voice — it is the one Monolith already owns.

### Onboarding and teaching — 2 wins

#### [WIN] The reseed/prune notes announce change inline, at the exact rows changed, and dismiss when the user acts — no modal takeover

ui/screens/ShieldMatrixScreen.kt:313-326 places the reseed note directly above the routine rows it describes, in the app's normal 11sp mono voice, and ui/MonolithViewModel.kt:506-510 dismisses it when the user edits any routine — the note ends when the user has demonstrably absorbed the change by acting on it. ShieldMatrixScreen.kt:412-430 reuses the same quiet inline grammar for the catalogue prune note ('the reseed note is the precedent'), tap-to-dismiss, never a modal, never blocking the Deck or an arm.

Recommendation: Protect this pattern in any redesign and make it the mandatory template for all update communication (see the UpdateNote component above): inline, at the site of the change, in instrument voice, dismissed by acting on the change. Do not replace it with a full-screen What's New carousel or a blocking modal — the restraint is the design. Extend, don't replace: keep the placement and dismissal law, add only the missing before→after content and version keying.

#### [WIN] The manual is engraved on the machine forever — the spec plate is permanent furniture, not a disposable onboarding carousel

ParkDrawer.kt:102-124 labels the plate 'furniture, byte-identical in day and night' and ParkDrawer.kt:623-646 seats it permanently at PARK's foot: model, unit number and operating clauses stay printed on the device for its whole life, re-readable in the exact drawer where permissions are re-proved. Opal's teaching is a one-pass chat flow and one sec's is a one-pass tutorial sequence (apk-re/opal/EVIDENCE.md:190; apk-re/onesec/EVIDENCE.md:167-168) — once completed, neither app leaves its instructions engraved anywhere in the product; Monolith, like a Braun appliance or a Teenage Engineering panel, carries its manual on its body.

Recommendation: Protect this in any onboarding redesign: whatever staged first-run flow is added must remain a layer over the plate, never a replacement for it — the plate stays byte-identical, permanently resident at PARK's foot, so the instructions a user learned on day one are still printed on the machine on day one hundred. Do not migrate the plate's content into dismissible cards, a help web page or a settings screen.

### States: empty error loading — 2 wins

#### [WIN] The Tasks blank leaf — a 112dp perforated, ruled blank that holds the pad's shape at zero instead of collapsing or decorating the void

FocusSequencerScreen.kt:369-410: an empty queue renders a PerforationRow plus a 112dp ruled blank — 'NOTHING QUEUED' in Atkinson 15sp onSurfaceVariant over a single 1dp rule at 18% alpha — holding the pad at full height so the list's geometry, and the composer's position above it, never move. drawer/deck/shield empties elsewhere collapse or apologise; this one behaves like a tear-off paper pad (the Abriss block the code's own comments invoke), which keeps its block shape down to the last leaf. Mainstream task apps (Todoist's centred empty-state illustration and slogan) spend the zero on decoration and teach nothing about the list's structure.

Recommendation: Protect this exactly as built in any redesign: the 112dp height, the perforation, the single rule and the absence of illustration or CTA on the leaf itself. It is the app's correct empty-state instinct — extend its geometry-holding behaviour to the Deck's NOW row and the Drawer's month (per the losses above) rather than replacing it with a generic illustrated empty state.

#### [WIN] Unmeasured is printed as nothing — Monolith refuses to fabricate a failure or a clean bill it has not earned

When a permission has never been measured, Monolith prints nothing rather than a verdict: guardLineFor returns null if any counted item is UNMEASURED (ui/components/GuardLine.kt:36-37), so the header band carries no GUARD line at all instead of a fabricated 'GUARD 0/4' — the file's own comment names the failure this refuses: 'the seeded all-false guard status that used to print a day-one 0/4 is exactly the claim this state exists to prevent' (GuardLine.kt:18-22). PARK does the same: a never-measured board prints its nine names with blank right sides and no invented words (ParkDrawer.kt snapshot==null branch; ParkBoardRow prints the name only when word is null). Unknown is presented as honest blank space, never dressed as failure or as health.

Recommendation: Protect this in any redesign: keep UNMEASURED as typographic silence — no skeleton verdicts, no default-red or default-green fills, no 'checking…' theatre that resolves into an assumed state. It matches the Airbus 'dark cockpit' philosophy, where an unlit annunciator means 'not reported', never 'OK', and it is the one failure-adjacent state Monolith presents more honestly than the typical Android permission dashboard, which renders unmeasured permissions as red warnings or green ticks by default. If a loading treatment is ever added, it should be a timed 'MEASURING' print with the LAST PROVED instant beside it — never a state word.

### Data visualisation — 1 wins

#### [WIN] Exact-figure tables with zero chartjunk beat the rivals' pie charts for reading a value

Where Monolith does show numbers it refuses every low-accuracy chart form: there is no pie, donut, gauge or 3-D chart anywhere in the UI, and both history and receipt print exact values as direct text labels — StoredRow's spentLabel gives '1H 05M / 48 MIN / 45 SEC' in tabular mono (DrawerScreen.kt:122-131, :886-925) and the receipt prints exact counts and times as mono lines (ReceiptSheet.kt:116-145). StayFree's MPAndroidChart system, by contrast, spends part of its surface on device-breakdown and per-app pie charts, where shares must be judged by angle and area — the least accurate encodings in Cleveland & McGill's hierarchy — so a user can read Monolith's 24 MIN exactly while StayFree's user estimates a slice.

Recommendation: Protect this in any redesign: keep the exact-figure table as the primary record and add length/timeline encodings ALONGSIDE the figures as direct-labelled bars and strips (findings above), never INSTEAD of them. Explicitly ban pie, donut and gauge forms from the design system — if a part-to-whole view is ever needed, use a single stacked bar on a common scale, preserving the current system's one genuine data-viz virtue: nothing in Monolith ever asks the eye to judge an angle.

### The receipt and artifacts — 5 wins

#### [WIN] The receipt headlines the user's own intention, not the app's verdict — the one place identity is the person's work

receipt.html Frame 1: the slip's largest, boldest line is the user's own intention — 'Revise thermodynamics' in Atkinson Bold 15sp (ReceiptSheet.kt title slot) — above the serial '№ 048', while the machine's outcome word is demoted to the end of an 11sp mono line, 'ENDED 19:32 · ENDED'. MonolithRepository.kt:1683 comment states the intent: the outcome is 'the long-form dialect — in words a man reads, never the stored token', so ELAPSED_CLEAN never prints on the artifact at all. Forest's and Opal's shareable end-cards headline the app's own tree/score artwork and brand first; Monolith's artifact headlines the work the person chose, numbered like an edition of their own record.

Recommendation: Protect this hierarchy in any redesign: the intention stays the slip's title at 15sp bold, the № stays, and no score, streak, brand mark or outcome stamp may be promoted above it. If a verdict line is humanised per the other findings, keep it in the existing 11sp mono line — never as a headline, badge or colour-coded stamp over the title.

#### [WIN] The slip never prints a fact it did not witness — FLOW receipts omit PLANNED entirely rather than dress a floor up as a plan

ReceiptSheet.kt and MonolithRepository.kt:1640-1648 enforce an omission law most products fail: a FLOW (stopwatch) session's stored target is a 20-minute floor, so plannedSeconds is set null and the sheet prints 'ARMED 18:42' with no PLANNED segment at all, rather than the false 'PLANNED 20 MIN' an earlier build produced for a 3h50m span; held counts are likewise omitted whole when uncaptured (-1 never prints as a figure), and a zero deflection list prints nothing. The label states only what is in the bottle.

Recommendation: Protect this law explicitly when the receipt's verdict becomes a sentence: the composed sentence may only use witnessed fields, and where a fact is absent the sentence must omit that clause rather than substitute a default — e.g. a FLOW verdict reads 'You worked until 19:32.' with no duration claim the session never made. Add a unit test per finish kind asserting no unwitnessed figure or clause appears in the rendered sentence.

#### [WIN] The receipt slip is a tool that recedes: still, unanimated, dismissible on any tap, and its footer deliberately sends the study record elsewhere instead of retaining the user

ReceiptSheet.kt:44-51 documents the discipline in code — slip settled and still, 'it never re-strikes, never animates its numbers, and dismisses on the next DOWN anywhere' — and the slip closes with 'THE MACHINE KEEPS ITS OWN LOG · YOUR STUDY RECORD LIVES IN YPT' (line 186), explicitly handing the user's record to another tool instead of farming it in-app. In a category built on re-engagement surfaces, Monolith's terminal artifact refuses to compete for the attention it just protected: it prints, it ends, it releases the user back to the world beyond the phone.

Recommendation: Protect this exactly as built: keep the receipt unanimated, single-gesture-dismissible and free of any streak, share or 'next session' prompt in future revisions — if a follow-on action is ever added, it belongs on the Deck after dismissal, never on the slip itself.

#### [WIN] YOUR RULES is a real maker's ledger — hand-set sled rulings printed back as a balanced book of the user's own decisions

The per-app rule book is genuinely made by hand: each ruling is set app-by-app on a physical 3-stop sled (CatalogueAppRow, ShieldMatrixScreen.kt:1060) and then read back in YOUR RULES as a printed ledger the user authored — dot-leader lines binding each app to its ruling (SlipLineRow, line 968), with a tally whose three numbers sum to the whole phone (tallyText/StandingTallyLine), so the book provably covers every app on it. Most rivals configure by category toggle or cloud preset and never hand the user a complete, balanced, self-made artefact of their own decisions. This is the one surface where the user performs the design instead of consuming it — Mari's test, passed.

Recommendation: Protect this surface as the product's centre of making: keep the slip complete (all three tiers listed), keep the tally balancing to the phone's total, and route every future building feature — named loadouts, drafts, test-fits — through the slip as its printed record, rather than adding a separate settings-style editor that would demote the maker's book to a side effect.

#### [WIN] The slip lists deflections and never sums them: no score, no total, no grade — eudaimonic restraint most focus apps fail

ReceiptState.kt:124-128 states the discipline in the contract itself: 'There is deliberately NO total/count field anywhere in this contract (Zettel): the slip lists; it never sums.' ReceiptSheet.kt:141-146 accordingly prints each deflection as a bare time-and-app line with no header count, no score, no percentage, and the app computes no Focus Score from the rich session record it keeps. Where rival products convert attention into a grade that manufactures its own appetite, Monolith's slip remains testimony rather than a scoreboard.

Recommendation: Protect this in the receipt contract: add a standing rule beside the no-total clause in ReceiptState.kt that no aggregate score, grade or summed deflection count may be derived from ReceiptState/PendingReceipt fields for any surface, and keep future Drawer summaries to listed days and sessions in the same unsummed form.

### Notifications and system surfaces — 1 wins

#### [WIN] The hours-long session notification is engineered to never make a sound — IMPORTANCE_LOW, badge off, onlyAlertOnce — the one surface a roommate will never hear

MonolithShieldService.kt:201-207 creates the session channel at NotificationManager.IMPORTANCE_LOW with setShowBadge(false), and :224-231 builds the ongoing notification with setOngoing(true) and setOnlyAlertOnce(true) — so the one surface that lives for the entire session, updating its countdown roughly every minute (receipt.html frame 2), never rings, never buzzes and never re-alerts the room on any update; it simply sits silently on the lock screen. Against the category norm of timer and focus apps whose foreground notifications arrive as alerting heads-ups, this is the correct shared-room instinct, applied exactly where the exposure is longest.

Recommendation: Protect this in any redesign: keep the shield channel at IMPORTANCE_LOW with onlyAlertOnce and no badge as a written invariant (guard it with a test or a spec-plate line), and resist any future 'session ended — celebrate loudly' notification on this channel; finish fanfare, if it ever exists, belongs on a separate, user-opted-in channel so the hours-long surface stays silent by construction.

### Accessibility as design — 1 wins

#### [WIN] Task prose is genuinely set in Atkinson Hyperlegible at full body size — protect it

Type.kt:115-131 sets AppTitleTextStyle, BodyTextStyle and TaskActiveTitleTextStyle in AtkinsonHyperlegibleFamily at a genuine 15sp/22sp and 22sp/27sp — not a token caption size. drawer.html and deck.html confirm task titles the user actually reads and writes ('Finish Chapter 4 Problem Set', stored history rows) are set in it, so b/d, p/q and 1/l distinctions hold in the user's own words. Most focus rivals set everything in a generic system grotesque with uniform, confusable letterforms.

Recommendation: Protect this in any redesign: keep Atkinson as the mandatory face for all user-authored and user-read prose at 15sp minimum, and extend it to the mono-assigned surfaces in the finding above rather than letting a future visual refresh swap it for a fashionable grotesque. It is the one accessibility decision in the app that is ahead of its references — do not trade it for brand novelty.

### Design system and craft — 10 wins

#### [WIN] Monolith's trust print expires and labels itself — STALE after 45 seconds, SELF-REPORT on the timestamp, silence when unmeasured

GuardLine.kt:35-37 returns null — the header prints nothing at all — when any counted permission is UNMEASURED, rather than a reassuring default. WatchStore.kt:150 sets STALE_AFTER_MS to 45,000 and permPrintAt (WatchStore.kt:359-362) demotes an old GRANTED to STALE instead of letting it stand. ParkDrawer.kt:315-324 prints 'LAST PROVED … · SELF-REPORT', explicitly labelling the timestamp as the app's own claim. MonolithCustomComponents.kt:406-421 degrades the Deck proof strip's right mark to 'PROOF: STALE' when the warrant read ages, and seamMarksFor (383-400) distinguishes 'PROOF: LIVE BIND', 'PROOF: BIND ONLY' and 'PROOF: NONE'. park.html and deck.html both show this vocabulary in place.

Recommendation: Protect this in any redesign: keep the three laws — unmeasured prints nothing, granted expires visibly to STALE on a short clock, and self-measured facts are labelled SELF-REPORT — and resist any request to replace them with a persistent green shield or checkmark. If the board is rebuilt with scope lines (per the other findings), carry the same ageing into them: each row's state word should stale on the same 45-second rule, so the honesty survives the richer layout.

#### [WIN] The Deck's pinned stack never moves — proof strip, 72dp verb zone and rail hold one fixed thumb address across idle, grace, running and finish

TactileDeckScreen.kt Section 5 (pinned stack, ~lines 944-975): the proof strip keeps its 53dp address in every state and the 72dp zone beneath it is deliberately held constant (Delta-y = 0) across tenancies — the slide sits there when idle, the GRACE WINDOW ABORT chip (58dp) in the first 10 seconds, and the EMERGENCY BREAK VALVE chip for a settled running session. deck.html (idle) and receipt.html frame 3 (frozen detention Deck) show the same strip, zone and imprint in identical positions in opposite states. The eye and the thumb learn one bottom address for 'what is shut, when it ends, and the session verb', and it never moves.

Recommendation: Protect this in any redesign: freeze the pinned stack's geometry as a hard invariant (53dp strip + 72dp verb zone + rail, same y in idle, running, grace, break and finish states) and resist adding banners or cards that push it. It is the app's Teenage Engineering trait — a fixed control layout the hand learns once — and it is worth more at a study desk than any new surface that would reflow it.

#### [WIN] The motion curves are genuinely defined once and mirrored exactly across both toolkits - same control points, one name, both engines

MonolithCurves.kt defines each core curve twice with byte-identical control points in both toolkits: CurveA PathInterpolator(0.2,0,0,1) at line 33 and EasingA CubicBezierEasing(0.2f,0.0f,0.0f,1.0f) at line 57; likewise CurveB/EasingB (0.05,0.7,0.1,1) and CurveC/EasingC (0.3,0,0.8,0.15). MonolithKin then names the semantics once (EasingSeat = EasingA, EasingThrow) and ParkDrawer.kt:154-156,262,417-420 actually consumes those names for both its Compose animations. Most two-toolkit apps let View and Compose motion drift into different feels per surface; here a Canvas sled and a Compose drawer landing on Curve A land identically.

Recommendation: Protect this in any redesign: keep the dual-representation rule (no curve exists in one toolkit without its exact twin in the other, same control points, one shared name) and extend it to the exceptions found elsewhere - the seal Vertigo easings and ReturnHome currently have no View/Compose twins, so give them paired definitions in MonolithCurves rather than letting the next surface invent its own.

#### [WIN] The ripple is purged and surfaces are flat by default — planes answer with position and fill, never a decorative wash

Color.kt:12 'Default surface — same as ground, flat by default' (TokenColorSurface is literally the background value, repeated for night at :33), and Theme.kt:94-122 installs NoRippleIndication app-wide with the note 'Ripple is purged app-wide... controls in this app answer with position, fill and sound — never a wash'. A ripple is a travelling distortion drawn across a flat plane for decoration; refusing it, and refusing elevation shadows in the Compose layer, is exactly Tanaka's demand that a surface stay geometrically honest and answer through its planes. Most Android apps fail this on every tap; Monolith holds it as a system rule, not a per-screen choice.

Recommendation: Protect this in the token file itself: add a lint/check rule that fails the build on any Modifier.shadow, elevation or default ripple indication introduced under ui/, so the flat-plane discipline survives future contributors the way the Grammar survived by being written down as rules, not taste.

#### [WIN] The wheel's engraved scale is honest: ticks exist only where the wheel can actually stop, and FLOW is refused a numeral

BlockitCoreViews.kt:742-748: 'ticks exist ONLY where the wheel can actually stop — every 5 minutes from 10 to 180, 35 stops at 9 degrees each... Inside the strait there is no tick at all: the break in the scale is a break in the print too. FLOW prints as a word in the hero, never as a tick or a number here.' The drawn scale, the snap physics (nearestStopAngle, BlockitCoreViews.kt:1179) and the haptic detents all derive from the same stop set, so the instrument never promises a position it cannot hold — the engraving discipline of a shutter dial, which most digital dials (continuous scroll wheels with decorative tick rings) fail outright.

Recommendation: Protect this invariant in code review: any future stop added to valueForAngle must appear as a tick in the same commit, and no decorative tick, numeral or arc segment may be drawn at a non-stopping angle. Extend the same law to the hub: when block counts change, their wells are already drawn from the same 1..8 set the hub can commit — keep that coupling and name it in the file header alongside the existing scale comment.

#### [WIN] Additions honour the existing installation: catalogue sync never re-prices a hand-set tier

The catalogue reconcile obeys the core 606 discipline: additions join the existing installation without disturbing what is already hung. AppCatalogReconcile.kt states the law in its header — 'an installed package with a row keeps its row untouched — the man's own tier is never re-priced by a sync' — and the code honours it: reconcile() inserts newly discovered packages with a birth tier and factory preset where one exists, prunes only packages that are gone, and for every existing row changes nothing but the real usage figure (AppCatalogReconcile.kt reconcile(), the existing-row branch copies only todayUsageMinutes). In a product whose other appliers bulk-rewrite the tier wall, this one part treats the owner's accumulated arrangement as permanent furniture and only adds or removes pieces around it.

Recommendation: Protect this law by name: keep the reconcile's never-re-price rule as a stated invariant in the Shield's catalogue header copy ('Your tiers are never changed by a sync'), and extend the same contract to the two appliers that violate it — a loadout or profile application should list which existing hand-set tiers it will override before it runs, the way a new 606 component is planned against the drawing of what's already on the wall.

#### [WIN] The Shield app-row sled is a true panel switch — three labelled stops printed on the track, state readable from position, lit word and margin glyph at once

In the shield.html render, every catalogue row is a single-function three-position sled (AppRowSledToggleView, ShieldMatrixScreen.kt:505): the three stops SHUT / PEEK / OPEN are printed on the track itself, the selected stop's word is lit in its cap colour, and a margin glyph redundantly encodes the same state (solid square = SHUT, hollow = PEEK, none = OPEN). State can be read three ways — thumb position, lit word, glyph — without touching the control, and the control does exactly one thing. That is genuine panel discipline: labelled stops, no hidden modes, no menu behind the switch.

Recommendation: Protect this exactly as built: keep the stop words printed on the track (never replace them with colour alone or icons), keep the margin glyph, and use this row as the template when the Park board's interceptor lines gain their sleds — same track, same stop typography, same glyph grammar, so the whole app reads as one instrument built by one hand.

#### [WIN] The rotary wheel's scale is genuinely generated, not drawn — the one surface that thinks the way Crouwel's grids did

The Deck's wheel (deck.html render of BlockitCoreViews.kt RotaryWheelView) carries a full generated tick ring: minor ticks at every step, longer 1.8-weight majors at the hour stations, station numerals placed by the same rotation math that drives the detents, and a progress arc derived from the selected value. Nothing is positioned by eye; change the range and the scale redraws itself correctly. That is parametric form — a rule producing an instrument — and it is the standard the rest of the app's hand-nudged half-point type fails to meet.

Recommendation: Protect and generalise it: extract the wheel's tick-generation parameters (step, major interval, weight ratio) into the theme as the seed of the missing module system, and require new dials, faders and tower scales to be generated from those parameters rather than hand-placed.

#### [WIN] The Deck instrument practises real economy: preset tiles deleted, one value with one control, and every fact given exactly one rendering

TactileDeckScreen.kt:571-575 documents the discipline in the code itself — 'the readout lives in the same panel as the wheel that sets it. The preset tiles are gone: one value, one control — the wheel'; lines 628-632: 'The hero states the TOTAL, once (one fact, one rendering)' with the span honestly priced including breaks; lines 626-630 record the eyebrow's app count being deliberately evicted because the count already lives in the strip and imprint. Where most focus apps multiply chips, preset grids and duplicate totals across hero, strip and summary, Monolith's instrument panel removes parts until each number appears exactly once, in the panel that sets it — the best, arranged for the least.

Recommendation: Protect this in writing: add the rule 'one fact, one rendering; one value, one control' to the Deck's section header comment as a binding constraint on future edits, and apply the same eviction audit to the Shield header, where loadout counts and rule counts still restate the matrix the guest can already see below them.

#### [WIN] The refusal sentence slot and imprint lip are true designed emptiness — 22dp reserved when healthy, vacated by a 500ms stability beat and a fade, never by a swap

ui/components/MonolithCustomComponents.kt:715-760 RefusalSentenceSlot reserves 22dp always — 'Healthy = nothing stands here' — and on recovery the sentence does not swap or snap: after a 500ms stability beat it fades over 90ms under one tick and 'the slot returns to its reserved emptiness'. ImprintSlot in the same file reserves its 20dp tenant box and 4dp lip zone in every state so the pinned stack 'never changes height by one pixel across the seal'. This is Ma practised as engineering: emptiness given fixed dimensions, a designed exit, and a rule against being filled with a reassuring substitute line.

Recommendation: Protect this pattern and promote it to the design system's stated rule: every transient surface (receipt fault line in ReceiptSheet.kt, detention frame on TactileDeckScreen, Airlock withheld-peek line) must reserve its box while empty and exit by the same 500ms stability beat plus fade, never by layout collapse or a replacement 'ALL CLEAR' line. Name the 22dp slot and the reserved-lip assembly as the reference implementation in MonolithCustomComponents.kt so future surfaces copy the emptiness, not just the components.

### Signature moments and delight — 7 wins

#### [WIN] Monolith's restraint beats Forest's guilt engine: failure is a neutral log line, never a dead pet left on display

Forest's core emotional device is a guilt corpse: a tree you killed stays withered in your forest permanently, engineering loss aversion on every return visit. Monolith refuses this everywhere: the UI's outcome vocabulary tops out at the neutral 'ENDED' (MonolithRepository.kt:1688), the internal VALVE_BROKE token never prints on any surface (ReceiptState.kt:38-40: 'No receipt, no №, ever'), the faulted slip's one line is factual — 'THE SHIELD WAS OFF FOR PART OF THAT SESSION' (ReceiptSheet.kt) — and an ILL day in the Drawer (drawer.html Frame 1, 'WED 28 OCT · ILL') is just a word beside a date, with no dead organism, scar or shaming mark attached to being sick.

Recommendation: Protect this in any emotional redesign: if growth/death imagery is borrowed from Forest, borrow the growth, not the corpse-as-guilt. Keep failure language factual and corpse-free — no withered mascots for ILL/FAMILY days, no permanent shame objects. Monolith's stone register can carry feeling through material and colour (per the slip treatments above) without ever making the user look at something they killed.

#### [WIN] The imprint line is a receipt printed before the act — '9 WILL SHUT · 3 PEEK' stamped under the slide, flipping to HELD once sealed

MonolithCustomComponents.kt:450-477: imprintTenantText composes a single future-tense line — '{n} WILL SHUT · {m} PEEK' — printed in the ImprintSlot directly beneath the slide-to-start control, and the same line flips tense to '{n} HELD · {m} PEEK' once sealed (deck.html renders it: '9 WILL SHUT · 3 PEEK' set as a letterpress imprint under double rules below the slide track). No setup screen, no dialog: the consequence of the gesture you are about to make is stamped, in counts, fused to the control itself, before you make it — and it is honest about the split (shut vs peek are never merged into one flattering number). Opal and Forest both show app lists and durations across setup screens, but neither prints a one-line, tense-aware consequence manifest at the point of commitment.

Recommendation: Protect verbatim in any redesign: keep the imprint line physically attached to the start control, keep the WILL SHUT → HELD tense flip, and keep shut and peek as separate counts. If the Deck is ever re-laid-out, this line — not the wheel — is the element whose removal would most damage the app's honesty; treat it as a signature, on the level of a colophon in a printed book.

#### [WIN] Tear-off completion beats YPT's checkbox: the perforated counterfoil leaf makes finishing a task physical and final

FocusSequencerScreen.kt TaskLeafItem + PerforationRow (~L470-720): each leaf is topped by a real perforation (3dp dash / 3dp gap in the hairline token), completion is 'DONE — TEAR' — booking at the tap, then a 260ms ghost tear (drops 10dp, fades, dashes halve), the pad edge draws one tone-stepped line per leaf behind (capped at 3) so queue depth is felt as stack thickness, and while a session is sealed the perforation is overprinted solid and the tear verb is absent, not greyed. YPT's Planner, by contrast, completes a to-do with a conventional checkbox state change — the item stays in place, visually identical in weight to an unchecked one. Monolith's completion has finality, sound (playTearPulse) and a physical object metaphor a student understands from a paper counterfoil book.

Recommendation: Protect this in any planner redesign: keep the perforation, the sealed-overprint rule and the tear as the only completion gesture when the queue moves onto a time grid — each timetable row tears off its time cell when done, leaving the cell's outline in the day as the record of time actually spent. Do not replace it with checkboxes, swipe-to-complete or a DONE button, and do not add an un-tear animation; REOPEN as the single quiet text verb (already on the last-finished line) is the correct, proportionate undo.

#### [WIN] The wheel hub's press is genuinely best-in-class and must be protected: anchored shadow closing 2dp→1dp, 45ms dip against a 160ms return, and a specular core that travels 2dp under the depression — real light physics no flat state-layer (Material 3) or dim-on-press (iOS) default attempts

BlockitCoreViews.kt:847-854 anchors the hub's contact shadow while the hub seats 1dp into it; lines 461-495 give the dip an asymmetric 45ms attack and 160ms seat-return on dedicated curves (HubPressDip / HubSeatReturn); and lines 868-905 move the specular core's origin by hubPressDepth*2dp toward bearing 135 while the depression lasts — the light source stays fixed in the room and the highlight travels across the metal, which is how a real dished key (Braun ET66 calculator keys, Teenage Engineering's machined buttons) behaves under a finger. Material 3's pressed state, by contrast, is a flat 10-12% state-layer wash and iOS's default button press is a uniform dim/scale: neither moves light or closes a shadow gap. deck.html's wheel render shows the resulting object: a hub that sits ON its wheel in a way no other element in the app — and few in any app — matches.

Recommendation: Protect this exact mechanism in any redesign: anchored shadow, 45/160ms asymmetric dip/return, and the 2dp specular-core travel gated by CORE_TRAVEL_GATE must survive untouched, and it should be the reference implementation the slide cap, sleds and FIX key are ported toward (per the losses above), not be flattened toward their simpler treatments for consistency's sake.

#### [WIN] A real instrument, not a sample pack: every sound is synthesized live and married to its haptic at one call site

Monolith has no audio assets at all: TactileSoundEngine.kt:20-39 documents a procedural Float-PCM synthesizer in which 'every haptic pulse and acoustic transient fire together from the same call site', and the eight voices (TactileSoundEngine.kt:629-848) are all parameterised synthesis — fundamental Hz, duration, chord ratio (1.21 tear vs 1.33 completion), gain — so the detent genuinely changes pitch with the value it sets (MonolithViewModel.kt setDialMinutes: 440 + minutes×2.8Hz) and the whole sound identity weighs zero bytes, can never be a stale licensed sample, and is perfectly consistent across devices. This is the Teenage Engineering OP-1/OP-Z principle — synthesize the instrument, don't sample it — executed in a focus app whose rivals ship recorded or system-stock effects.

Recommendation: Protect this in any redesign: keep the zero-asset synthesized engine and its sound+haptic single-call-site rule as a non-negotiable identity asset, and extend its parameter space (pitch ladders, chord ratios) to the new deflection, break and hand-back voices recommended above rather than ever introducing audio files. Document the eight voices as the brand's sonic logo set, the way Teenage Engineering documents its synth engines.

#### [WIN] The Airlock's 5-second wall is the genuine article: a timer and one huge numeral — the cheapest possible parts — doing the job rivals buy with feeds, scores and friction systems

AirlockAndDisarmOverlays.kt:562-569 implements the wall as a plain 1-second countdown loop from 5; lines 636-639 render it as a single 88sp Anonymous Pro numeral ('0%d'); airlock.html frame 1 shows the whole composition — blocked app named, session end time, one numeral, one RETURN TO FOCUS chip, nothing else on screen. No classifier, no feed, no persuasion copy: the cheapest mechanism in the entire app carries its most consequential moment.

Recommendation: Protect this exactly as built: resist any addition of reason pickers, streak warnings or explanatory copy to the countdown state, and hold the 88sp single-numeral composition as the fixed template any future intercept surface must match before it ships.

#### [WIN] The Airlock and the desk-clock banner pass the disappearance test: at the intercept they name the work, not the tool — and print nothing when there is no work to name

ui/components/AirlockAndDisarmOverlays.kt:648 prints 'ACTIVE INTENTION: {sessionIntention}' on the intercept card, with 'SESSION ENDS 18:30' and the single accent chip 'RETURN TO FOCUS' (:656) — the surface the user meets at the moment of temptation speaks in terms of the task and the return, and imposes a 5-second breathing delay rather than a score or a warning. The desk clock goes further: deskClockBannerText (:225-226) returns the task title, else the declared intention, else null — and when null, NO banner is composed at all (:196-215), the code comment noting the old fabricated default 'Deep Focus Session' was removed because it 'fabricated a name for a session nobody named'. Equipment that appears only at breakdown, points past itself to the work, and falls silent when it has nothing true to say is ready-to-hand design most focus apps never achieve.

Recommendation: Protect both behaviours as the house rule and extend them: adopt 'name the work, never the mechanism; print nothing rather than a default' as the written standard for the Deck header and the session notification, and add a regression test asserting the Airlock composes no banner, badge or brand line beyond the intention, the end time and RETURN TO FOCUS.

### The app as an object — 5 wins

#### [WIN] True-black ground, one cream value, orange withheld — a desk object more disciplined than Apple StandBy's photo-and-notification billboard

The clock's ground is true Color.Black with the explicit intent 'OLED pixels off, not the block-bar tone' (AirlockAndDisarmOverlays.kt:140-143), and every lit element — numerals, progress fill, banner text — uses the single NightColorPrimary cream #FFE4CF (Color.kt:33; fill choice commented 'Session progress in cream — orange is the arm commit only', AirlockAndDisarmOverlays.kt:186-188). receipt.html frame 4 shows the whole face is just three elements. Apple StandBy, the category's desk-object benchmark, fills the same nightstand role with photo slideshows, widget stacks and large notification previews — a glowing billboard that leaks the distractions a focus session exists to hold. Monolith's face leaks nothing and spends nothing.

Recommendation: Protect this discipline in any redesign: keep true-black ground, the single cream value for all sustained elements, and orange reserved exclusively for arm/finish instants. If new information is ever proposed for the clock face, it must displace an existing element, not add a fourth.

#### [WIN] Monolith already out-designs Brick's puck on paper — its virtual hardware grammar is a complete manufacturing brief

deck.html and park.html show a complete, transferable hardware design language already specified to manufacturing tolerance: sled tracks 76x34dp with recess shading lines and 37.8x28dp thumbs, a slide cap with a 1.2px top highlight and a single vertical marker line, a wheel with knurl ticks and detent numerals in Anonymous Pro 15sp, and the colour-verb law at ParkDrawer.kt:113. Brick ships a featureless puck with no input grammar, no state language and no identity beyond a logo; Playdate needed Teenage Engineering to invent its crank language from scratch.

Recommendation: Protect this in any hardware programme: do not commission a fresh industrial design. Hand the manufacturer the existing geometry as the brief — sled, slide cap, wheel knurling and the four colour verbs scale 1:1 from dp drawings to machined parts. Monolith is the rare focus app whose companion object is already designed; it is only unbuilt. Any redesign that softens the recess shading, marker line or detent numerals destroys the one asset Brick cannot copy retroactively.

#### [WIN] The Park spec plate is a genuine object identity — a manufacturer's data plate no rival attempts

ParkDrawer.kt:90-122 defines a manufacturer's spec plate for the whole product: 'MONOLITH ML-01 / UNIT Nº 01 · BUILT FOR ONE USER · NOT FOR SALE' followed by operating facts as plate print ('WHEEL SETS TIME · SLIDE ARMS · THE HOLD BREAKS', 'COLOUR IS A VERB: ORANGE = COMMIT · INK = SHUT · GREY = PEEK · PORCELAIN = OPEN'), with the code comment at ParkDrawer.kt:90 specifying it is 'furniture, byte-identical in day and night' — it does not theme, adapt or apologise. No rival focus app gives its settings surface an object identity: Opal's and Forest's settings are generic grouped lists indistinguishable from any utility app. Seen in park.html: the drawer reads as the data plate riveted inside a machine's lid, which is exactly what a product named Monolith should feel like.

Recommendation: Protect this verbatim in any redesign: keep the plate's fixed ink, fixed wording and foot-of-drawer placement, and extend the conceit rather than diluting it — add the build/version line and the dial glyph stamped as a maker's mark at the plate's corner, in the manner of Braun and Teenage Engineering data plates. Do not let a future theming pass recolour it, and do not move it into a scrollable settings list.

#### [WIN] The Deck's wheel-and-slide instrument genuinely is an object — knurled, detented and embossed — and out-crafts every rival's duration picker

BlockitCoreViews.kt:371 RotaryWheelView and :1444 SlideToStartView render what deck.html shows faithfully: a 288dp wheel whose rim carries individual knurl ticks alternating dark/light, detent numerals (30/60/90/120/150/180) in Anonymous Pro 15sp, a reader dot seated at the chosen detent, and a hub with filled/empty wells; the hero numerals carry two ghost offsets (rgba(216,209,203,.6) at -1px, rgba(250,246,240,.7) at +1px) that read as embossing; the slide cap (#F55314, 84x56dp, 20.dp radius) has a top highlight line, a vertical marker line and a 2.5px contact shadow against the #2E2A26 track. No focus rival builds its picker as a physical instrument: Opal and one sec set duration with flat stock sliders/steppers, and Forest replaces the control with a cartoon sapling. This is Teenage Engineering-grade skeuomorphic restraint — one machine part, fully committed.

Recommendation: Protect this in any redesign: freeze RotaryWheelView's rim ticks, detent numerals, reader dot and ghost-emboss treatment and SlideToStartView's cap highlights/marker as untouchable assets, and judge every new surface against them (per the Shield/Drawer/Park finding) rather than flattening the Deck toward the other screens. If cuts are needed, cut copy and rooms before touching the wheel's physical rendering.

#### [WIN] No account, no server, no INTERNET permission — the tool works entirely without the toolmaker's system

Illich's convivial test — a tool anyone can use 'as often or as seldom as desired, for the accomplishment of a purpose chosen by the user', without dependence on the maker's apparatus — is one most focus apps fail with accounts, clouds and subscription gates, and Monolith passes it outright. AndroidManifest.xml declares no INTERNET permission (permissions at lines 6-12 are VIBRATE, FOREGROUND_SERVICE, POST_NOTIFICATIONS, RECEIVE_BOOT_COMPLETED, SYSTEM_ALERT_WINDOW and package/usage access), and there is no account, sign-in, Retrofit or HTTP client anywhere in main source. Every seal, receipt, brick and verdict is computed and kept on the device; if the maker vanished tomorrow the tool would work unchanged. This is the convivial core the rest of the design should be judged against — and must not be traded away for sync or social features.

Recommendation: Protect it in print: add one line to PARK's spec plate — 'NO ACCOUNT · NO NETWORK · NOTHING LEAVES THIS PHONE' — in the existing mono footer voice, and treat any future network feature as opt-in and off by default so this property survives. No surface change is needed beyond making the fact visible where the user inspects the machine.

### Philosophy and meaning — 2 wins

#### [WIN] The declared day word is a word, never a number — the one surface that refuses to price a life-day

DayWordStore's governing comment states the declared day word 'is a word, never a number, and it is never folded into any total (the Drawer prints no totals for it to be folded into)' (data/DayWordStore.kt:5-7), and the closed list is REST / ILL / FAMILY — 'never TEST. This app does not know test days' (DayWordStore.kt:54 and class doc). In a product that numbers receipts, counts urges and bricks a tower, the days of sickness, rest and family are deliberately refused quantification — the one place Monolith treats a portion of life as wealth that must not be converted into a score, which is exactly Seneca's demand.

Recommendation: Protect and extend this refusal in design, not just in the store: (1) when the planned stats/report surfaces are built, add an explicit design rule beside DayWordStore.kt:5 — day words never feed streaks, totals or tower bricks; (2) give the word one more dignified surface: on a day declared REST/ILL/FAMILY, the Deck eyebrow prints the word in place of TOTAL for that filing day, so the refusal is visible at the moment of arming, not only retrospectively in the Drawer.

#### [WIN] The Drawer's refusal to judge is genuine: no totals, no streaks, no percentages — a record kept, not graded

DrawerScreen.kt:58-66 charter, kept in the shipped code and visible in drawer.html: 'It is not a dashboard, report card or attendance book: no totals, no streaks, no percentages, no counts, no summons.' A declared day word prints 'as his authored word — never a number' (REST / ILL / FAMILY beside the date heading, DayWordStore.kt:54), and a day with no rows and no word renders nothing at all. Against an industry of streaks, scores and red missed-day marks, the kept record simply stores and stays silent — austerity and modesty as built behaviour, not styling.

Recommendation: Protect this exactly as-is while fixing the findings above: any weathering, groove or partial-row change to the Drawer must introduce no total, streak, percentage or count anywhere on the screen, and the day word must remain a word beside the date, never a factor in any judgement. If a future change needs a number to justify itself, it does not belong in the Drawer.
